pack.name: bridge-common-conventions
pack.description: bridge-craftwork's conventions, card settings and bidding rules

bidding_conventions/bart.name: BART
bidding_conventions/bart.summary:
After 1♥ or 1♠, a forcing 1NT and opener's 2♣, responder's 2♦ is artificial,
covering several stronger hands (a good club raise, a good preference,
diamonds) that need room.

bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d.name: Benjamin 2♦
bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d.summary:
Openings in which 2♣ shows a strong two in any suit, 2♦ is the game-forcing
hand, and 2♥ and 2♠ are weak twos, so there is no weak 2♦.

bidding_conventions/bergen_raises.name: Bergen raises
bidding_conventions/bergen_raises.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's jumps to 3♣ and 3♦ show four-card
raises of different strength (usually 3♣ constructive, 3♦ limit) and 3M is
preemptive, so opener knows the fit and strength at once.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/blackwood.name: Blackwood
bidding_conventions/blackwood.label: Standard Blackwood
bidding_conventions/blackwood.summary:
Once a trump suit is agreed, 4NT asks how many aces partner holds: 5♣ none
or four, 5♦ one, 5♥ two, 5♠ three. 5NT then asks for kings the same way.

bidding_conventions/checkback.name: Checkback
bidding_conventions/checkback.summary:
Played instead of NMF: after opener's notrump rebid, a fixed suit (usually
2♣) asks about support and majors, whichever minor was bid.

bidding_conventions/control_bids.name: Control (Cue) Bids
bidding_conventions/control_bids.brief: With a trump suit agreed, bid a control below game on the way to slam
bidding_conventions/control_bids.label: Control (cue) bids
bidding_conventions/control_bids.desc: BBA's 'Cue bid'. With a trump suit agreed and slam in the air, bid a control below game instead of asking straight away
bidding_conventions/control_bids.summary:
With a trump suit agreed and slam possible, bidding a new suit below game
shows a control there (an ace or void, and in many styles a king or
singleton), so the partnership can find out whether a suit is unguarded
before asking for keycards. Control bids once showed first-round controls
only; Italian champion teams found first or second round more effective, and
that is now the most prevalent treatment.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

style.label: Control bids show
style.desc: first_round: the ace or a void only, the historical style. first_or_second_round: king and singleton too, as Italian champion teams showed to be more effective; the most prevalent treatment today

bidding_conventions/depo.name: DEPO
bidding_conventions/depo.label: DEPO
bidding_conventions/depo.summary:
Played instead of DOPI: when they interfere over a keycard ask, double shows
an even number of keycards and pass an odd number.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi.name: DOPI and ROPI
bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi.summary:
When the opponents interfere over a keycard ask, double shows no keycards
(or none of the first step) and pass shows one (DOPI); after they double,
redouble shows none and pass one (ROPI). The next steps continue.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Slam Bidding: Dealing with Interference Over Ace-Asking Bids

bidding_conventions/drury.name: Drury
bidding_conventions/drury.summary:
By a passed hand over partner's third- or fourth-seat 1♥ or 1♠, 2♣ asks
whether opener has a full opening, with a fit for the major. In the original
form opener's 2♦ shows a light opening; Reverse Drury swaps opener's
replies.

bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.name: Exclusion Blackwood
bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.brief: Jump in a void suit asks for keycards excluding that suit
bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.summary:
A jump to the five level in a new suit after agreeing trumps shows a void
there and asks for keycards outside it, so the ace in the void suit does not
count.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/flannery.name: Flannery 2♦
bidding_conventions/flannery.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a minimum opening with five hearts and four spades, so
responder can find a spade fit without opener having to reverse or rebid
awkwardly.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/forcing_1nt.name: Forcing 1NT
bidding_conventions/forcing_1nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 1NT is forcing for one round, covering
a wide range of hands including invitational ones; opener must bid again, on
a three-card minor if need be.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.name: Fourth Suit Forcing
bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.label: Fourth suit forcing
bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.desc: We play fourth suit forcing (Bridge-Classroom's card); one_round / game_force say how far it forces. Turns off responder's natural two-level fourth suit (1♦–1♥–1♠–2♣)
bidding_conventions/fourth_suit_forcing.summary:
When three suits have been bid, responder's bid of the fourth suit is
artificial and forcing (for one round, or to game by agreement), asking
opener to describe the hand further.

bidding_conventions/french_2d.name: French 2♦
bidding_conventions/french_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ with an artificial meaning in the French style; details vary
by partnership, so the card's notes say which.

bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt.name: Gambling 3NT
bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt.summary:
An opening 3NT showing a long, solid minor with little outside. Partner
passes with stoppers in the other suits, and otherwise runs to four or five
of the minor.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
NT Auctions: Trick-Showing NT Bids - Gambling 3NT and More

bidding_conventions/gazzilli.name: Gazzilli
bidding_conventions/gazzilli.summary:
After 1♥ or 1♠ and a 1NT response, opener's 2♣ is artificial: either natural
clubs or any strong hand. Responder's 2♦ asks, letting opener show strong
hands at the two level.

bidding_conventions/gerber.name: Gerber
bidding_conventions/gerber.summary:
A jump to 4♣ over partner's notrump asks for aces, with steps answering as
for Blackwood (4♦ none or four, 4♥ one, and so on), leaving 4NT as a natural
raise.

bidding_conventions/grand_slam_force.name: Grand slam force
bidding_conventions/grand_slam_force.summary:
A jump to 5NT (not after a keycard ask) asks partner to bid the grand slam
in the agreed suit holding two of the top three trump honours.

bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.name: Help Suit Game Try
bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.brief: Sub-game bid asks help in that suit
bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.label: Help suit game tries
bidding_conventions/help_suit_game_try.summary:
After a major-suit raise, opener's new suit is a game try asking for help
there: responder bids game with honours or shortness in that suit and signs
off without.

bidding_conventions/impossible_2s.name: Impossible 2♠
bidding_conventions/impossible_2s.desc: 1♥–1NT–2m–2♠: artificial, a good raise of opener's minor (4+, the top of the 1NT response), forcing to three of the minor
bidding_conventions/impossible_2s.summary:
After 1♥–1NT–2♣ or 2♦, responder's 2♠ cannot be natural, so it shows a good
raise of opener's minor, forcing to three of it.

bidding_conventions/ingberman.name: Ingberman 2NT
bidding_conventions/ingberman.summary:
After opener reverses, responder's 2NT relays to 3♣ to show a weak hand, so
other bids by responder show values.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/intermediate_twos.name: Intermediate two-bids
bidding_conventions/intermediate_twos.summary:
An opening 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠ shows a six-card suit and a sound minimum opening,
about 10 to 13 points: stronger than a weak two, and not forcing.

bidding_conventions/inverted_minors.name: Inverted Minor Raises
bidding_conventions/inverted_minors.label: Inverted minors
bidding_conventions/inverted_minors.summary:
Over partner's 1♣ or 1♦, the single raise is strong (invitational or better,
forcing one round) and the jump raise is weak, the reverse of the natural
meanings. It usually denies a four-card major.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Inverted Minors and 1D-2C Auctions with Structure

bidding_conventions/jacoby_2nt.name: Jacoby 2NT
bidding_conventions/jacoby_2nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 2NT shows four or more trumps and game-
forcing values. Opener's rebid describes the hand: a short suit at the three
level, a good second suit at the four level, or strength by 3M, 3NT or 4M.

bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers.name: Jacoby Transfers
bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers.label: Jacoby transfers

see.title: NT Auctions: Opponents' Doubles of Our Stayman and Transfers

super_accept_doubleton.label: Super-accept by bidding a doubleton
super_accept_doubleton.desc: With 4+ trumps and a maximum, bid the doubleton suit (or 2NT when it cannot be shown below it). BBA: Extended acceptance after NT

vs_2c.label: Transfers on if RHO bids clubs

over_2c_3nt.label: Transfers over 2♣–2♦–3NT
over_2c_3nt.desc: After 2♣–2♦–3NT, responder transfers at the four level: 4♦ shows five or more hearts and 4♥ five or more spades, opener completing in the major. Off, 4♦ and 4♥ are natural

bidding_conventions/kickback.name: Kickback
bidding_conventions/kickback.summary:
A keycard ask in the suit above trumps instead of 4NT: 4♦ with clubs as
trumps, 4♥ with diamonds, 4♠ with hearts, and 4NT with spades. The answers
then never take the auction past five of the trump suit.

bidding_conventions/kokish.name: Kokish relay
bidding_conventions/kokish.summary:
After 2♣–2♦, opener's 2♥ is a relay: either hearts or a strong balanced
hand. Responder must bid 2♠, and opener's next bid says which, which keeps
the strong 2NT rebid out of the way.

bidding_conventions/kokish_game_tries.name: Kokish game tries
bidding_conventions/kokish_game_tries.summary:
A structure of game tries after a major-suit raise that uses the next step
as a relay, so opener can make several kinds of try.

bidding_conventions/lars_multi.name: Lars Multi 2♦
bidding_conventions/lars_multi.summary: A Multi 2♦ that shows a weak two in either major or a 20–21 balanced hand.

bidding_conventions/last_train.name: Last Train
bidding_conventions/last_train.summary:
When the only bid left between a fit and game in the agreed major is one
step below it, that bid is a general slam try rather than showing anything
in its suit.

see.title: Slam Bidding: Last Train Slam Try

bidding_conventions/mccabe.name: McCabe adjunct
bidding_conventions/mccabe.brief: After weak two doubled: 2NT = lead-directing raise
bidding_conventions/mccabe.summary:
After partner's weak two is doubled, responder's new suits and 2NT say what
to lead rather than show length, so the partnership can compete and direct
the defence at once.

bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d.name: Mini-Roman 2♦
bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d.brief: 3-suited hand, short in a specified suit
bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a three-suited hand (4-4-4-1 or 5-4-4-0) of opening
strength; responder bids the cheapest suit to play or 2NT to ask for the
short suit.

see.title: Mini Roman
see.note: The slam continuations in our rules are Rick Wilson's additions

maxi.label: Mini-Roman 2♦: Mini-Maxi (also 19+)
maxi.desc: The Mini-Roman 2♦ is either the three-suiter of opening strength (Mini) or a 19+ three-suiter (Maxi), which bids again after responder's sign-off. Off: Mini only

bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman.name: Minor Suit Stayman
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman.label: Minor Suit Stayman (1NT–2♠)
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT (or 2NT), a bid, usually 2♠, asks opener for a four-card
minor, for responder with both minors and slam interest or a hand looking
for a minor-suit game.

bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.name: Minor-Suit Transfers over 1NT
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.label: Minor-suit transfers
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.desc: Minor-suit transfers over 1NT; style says which structure
bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, responder's 2♠ and 2NT (or 3♣) are transfers or relays
to the minors, so a long minor can be shown weak to play or strong with slam
interest.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

over_1nt.label: Minor-suit transfers
over_1nt.desc: Minor-suit transfers over 1NT; style says which structure

style.label: Minor-suit transfers: style
style.desc: relay: 2♠ relays to 3♣, pass or correct to 3♦. four_way: 2♠ clubs, 2NT diamonds; the step below the suit shows good support. four_way_reversed: the suit itself shows good support. bba: 2♠ clubs, 3♣ diamonds, always completed (BBA). two_nt_three_c: 2NT clubs, 3♣ diamonds, leaving 2♠ free (for minor-suit Stayman); BBA's 21GF-MSTandMSS.

two_s.label: 1NT–2♠ transfer
two_s.desc: The card's 2♠ transfer box, as Bridgodex marks it; what it transfers to is in the card's notes

two_nt.label: 1NT–2NT transfer
two_nt.desc: The card's 2NT transfer box, as Bridgodex marks it

bidding_conventions/minorwood.name: Minorwood
bidding_conventions/minorwood.summary:
With a minor agreed, four of that minor asks for keycards instead of 4NT,
keeping the answers low enough to stop in five of the minor.

bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt.name: Modified Jacoby 2NT
bidding_conventions/modified_jacoby_2nt.summary:
Played instead of standard Jacoby 2NT: responder's 2NT is the same raise,
but opener's rebids are rearranged, usually so that 3♣ shows a minimum and
responder can then ask for shortness.

bidding_conventions/muiderberg.name: Muiderberg twos
bidding_conventions/muiderberg.summary:
Openings of 2♥ and 2♠ that show five cards in the major and four or more in
a minor, with less than an opening bid.

bidding_conventions/multi_2d.name: Multi 2♦
bidding_conventions/multi_2d.brief: Weak 2 in a major (or strong variants)
bidding_conventions/multi_2d.summary:
An opening 2♦ that shows a weak two in either major, or one of a few strong
hands. Responder bids to cater for either major, and opener's rebid resolves
which.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

strong_option.label: Multi 2♦: strong option
strong_option.desc: The strong hand the Multi 2♦ may hold besides a weak two in either major. none: weak twos only. balanced_20_21: 20-21 balanced (Lars Multi). balanced_22_23: 22-23 balanced. three_suiter: a strong 4-4-4-1. strong_minor: a strong (Acol) two in a minor. other: written in the card's notes

bidding_conventions/namyats.name: Namyats
bidding_conventions/namyats.summary:
Openings of 4♣ and 4♦ show a strong four-level preempt in hearts and spades
respectively, so a direct 4♥ or 4♠ opening is weaker.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.name: New Minor Forcing
bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.brief: After 1m-1M-1NT, 2 of other minor = forcing inquiry
bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.label: New minor forcing
bidding_conventions/new_minor_forcing.summary:
After opener's 1NT rebid, responder's bid of the unbid minor is artificial
and forcing, asking opener about three-card support for responder's major or
a four-card other major.

bidding_conventions/ogust.name: Ogust
bidding_conventions/ogust.brief: 2NT over weak two asks suit + hand quality
bidding_conventions/ogust.summary:
After partner's weak two, responder's 2NT asks about the hand in steps: 3♣
bad hand bad suit, 3♦ bad hand good suit, 3♥ good hand bad suit, 3♠ good
hand good suit, 3NT a solid suit.

bidding_conventions/over_splinters.name: Over-splinters
bidding_conventions/over_splinters.summary:
A jump one level beyond a normal splinter, used when the normal splinter bid
has another meaning, to show shortness and a fit.

bidding_conventions/parrish_relay.name: Parrish relay
bidding_conventions/parrish_relay.summary:
A treatment of the 2♥ bust over a 2♣ opening: a relay that follows the bust
bid, so a partnership plays it only with that convention.

bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt.name: Pick-a-slam 5NT
bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt.brief: 5NT after a fit suggests slam, lets partner pick the strain
bidding_conventions/pick_a_slam_5nt.summary:
A 5NT bid, not after a keycard ask, asks partner to choose among several
possible slams, usually in notrump or in a suit partner prefers.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

bidding_conventions/picture_3nt.name: 1M–3NT picture raise
bidding_conventions/picture_3nt.summary:
Over partner's 1♥ or 1♠, responder's 3NT is a game-forcing raise with a
balanced hand and good trumps, better than a direct raise to four.

bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters.name: Polish two-suiters
bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters.summary:
Weak openings at the two level that show two-suited hands, with the second
suit unknown or limited, as used in Polish Club.

bidding_conventions/precision_2d.name: Precision 2♦
bidding_conventions/precision_2d.summary:
In Precision, an opening 2♦ shows a limited opening short in diamonds,
usually 4-4-1-4 or 4-4-0-5 with 11-15 points.

bidding_conventions/preempt_keycard.name: Keycard over preempts
bidding_conventions/preempt_keycard.summary:
After partner's preempt, an agreed bid (often 4♣) asks for keycards in
partner's suit, since 4NT would take the auction too high.

bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman.name: Puppet Stayman
bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman.summary:
A form of Stayman, usually over 2NT, that finds five-card majors as well as
four-card ones: 3♣ asks, opener shows a five-card major directly or bids 3♦
with a four-card major, and responder then bids the major responder does
not hold.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
NT Auctions: Puppet Stayman and 5-Card Stayman

over_1nt.label: Puppet Stayman over 1NT (3♣)
over_1nt.desc: Bridge Classroom's editor, its PDFs and the BBO and Bridgodex importers write notrump.stayman.puppet for this (BBO's 1NPuppet, the Classic card's 1NT box)

over_2nt.label: 2NT: Puppet Stayman (3♣)
over_2nt.desc: Over 2NT (and 2♣–2♦–2NT), 3♣ asks for a four- or five-card major

bidding_conventions/range_stayman.name: Range Stayman
bidding_conventions/range_stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, a bid (often 2♠, or 2♣ then 2♠) asks whether opener is
minimum or maximum, for responder with an invitation to 2NT or a minor-suit
hand.

see.title: NT and Balancing Auctions: Range Stayman

bidding_conventions/reverse_bergen_raise.name: Reverse Bergen raises
bidding_conventions/reverse_bergen_raise.summary:
Played instead of Bergen raises: the same four-card raises with the meanings
of 3♣ and 3♦ swapped.

bidding_conventions/reverse_bids.name: Reverse Bids
bidding_conventions/reverse_bids.summary:
Opener's rebid in a new suit higher than the first, at the two level, shows
extra strength and a longer first suit; it is forcing for one round in most
styles.

bidding_conventions/reverse_drury.name: Reverse Drury
bidding_conventions/reverse_drury.summary:
By a passed hand over partner's third- or fourth-seat 1♥ or 1♠, 2♣ shows a
limit raise with three or more trumps. Opener rebids two of the major with a
light opening; other bids show a full one.

bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery.name: Reverse Flannery
bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery.desc: Responder's jump to 2♥ or 2♠ over partner's 1♣ or 1♦, showing five spades and four or more hearts, below a game try; which jumps: two_h, two_s
bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery.summary:
Over partner's 1♣ or 1♦, responder's jump to 2♥ shows five spades and four
or five hearts in a weak hand, and the jump to 2♠ the same shape with
invitational values. Opener can place the contract in a major at once.

bidding_conventions/roman_keycard.name: Roman Keycard
bidding_conventions/roman_keycard.label: Roman Keycard Blackwood
bidding_conventions/roman_keycard.summary:
4NT asks for five keycards, the four aces and the trump king. 1430 answers
5♣ one or four, 5♦ three or none, 5♥ two without the trump queen, 5♠ two
with it; 0314 swaps 5♣ and 5♦. The next step asks for the trump queen.
5NT then confirms every keycard and the trump queen and asks for side
kings, by number or, with specific kings, the cheapest one held.

style.label: RKCB responses
style.desc: 1430: the first step shows one or four keycards, the second none or three. 0314: the first step none or three, the second one or four

minor_0314.label: RKCB 0314 with a minor as trumps (1430 in the majors)

king_ask_specific.label: King ask: specific kings
king_ask_specific.desc: The king ask is answered by the cheapest side king below six of trumps (six of trumps with none) instead of the number of kings. A new suit below trumps then asks for that king: seven of trumps with it, six of a higher suit below trumps with that king instead, six of trumps with neither. The asker places the grand

bidding_conventions/roudi.name: Roudi
bidding_conventions/roudi.summary:
A checkback used in Acol and similar systems after opener's 1NT rebid, with
2♣ asking about support and strength.

bidding_conventions/schuler_shift.name: Schuler shift
bidding_conventions/schuler_shift.summary:
A style for opener's rebid after a 2/1 game-forcing response, one of the three
the card's 2/1 rebid style offers.

bidding_conventions/semi_forcing_1nt.name: Semi-forcing 1NT
bidding_conventions/semi_forcing_1nt.summary:
Played instead of the forcing 1NT: responder's 1NT over a major is forcing
only if opener has more than a minimum, so opener may pass with a balanced
minimum.

see.title: 2 over 1 Game Forcing: Responder's Rebids after 1NT Semi-Forcing Response

bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.name: Serious 3NT
bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.brief: In a 2/1 auction, 3NT denies slam interest
bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.label: Non-serious 3NT
bidding_conventions/serious_3nt.summary:
In a game-forcing auction with a major agreed at the three level, 3NT is
artificial and says whether the bidder is serious about slam (serious or
non-serious by agreement), before control bids begin.

bidding_conventions/six_key_rkcb.name: Six-key Roman Keycard
bidding_conventions/six_key_rkcb.summary:
Roman Keycard with two trump suits: six keycards, the four aces and both
trump kings, plus both trump queens, when the partnership has a fit in two
suits.

bidding_conventions/smolen.name: Smolen
bidding_conventions/smolen.summary:
After 1NT–2♣–2♦, responder with five cards in one major, four in the other
and game values jumps to three of the four-card major, so the strong hand
becomes declarer in a 5-3 fit.

see.title: Smolen and 5/5 Majors After a 2NT Opening

bidding_conventions/soloway.name: Soloway jump shifts
bidding_conventions/soloway.summary:
Responder's jump shifts are strong and describe the hand by type: a one-
suiter, a fit for opener, or a balanced hand, as GIB plays them.

bidding_conventions/spiral.name: Spiral
bidding_conventions/spiral.brief: Step-wise control showing (1st-round controls in order)
bidding_conventions/spiral.label: Spiral cuebids
bidding_conventions/spiral.summary:
A relay that asks about trump length and quality in steps once a fit is
found, so the asker can judge game or slam from how good the trumps are.

see.title: Fits and More: 2NT Trump Suit Game Try - Spiral

bidding_conventions/splinters.name: Splinters
bidding_conventions/splinters.summary:
A double jump in a new suit, by responder or by opener, shows a singleton or
void there and a fit with game values, so partner can judge slam by how well
the hands fit.

see.title: Slam Bidding: Splinter Bids by Responder

bidding_conventions/stayman.name: Stayman
bidding_conventions/stayman.summary:
Over partner's 1NT, 2♣ asks opener for a four-card major: 2♦ denies one, 2♥
or 2♠ shows it. Responder uses it to find a 4-4 major fit with invitational
or better values; Garbage Stayman uses it weak, planning to pass any reply.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

over_2nt_both_majors.label: 2NT–3♣–3NT shows both majors
over_2nt_both_majors.desc: Stayman-style 3♣ over 2NT; opener's 3NT shows 4-4 in the majors

bidding_conventions/strong_2c.name: Strong 2♣
bidding_conventions/strong_2c.summary:
An opening 2♣, artificial and forcing, for the strongest hands: game-forcing
or nearly so, balanced or not. Responder usually bids 2♦ to wait, and opener
then describes the hand.

bidding_conventions/strong_jump_shifts.name: Strong jump shifts
bidding_conventions/strong_jump_shifts.summary:
Responder's jump in a new suit over partner's opening shows a strong hand
with a good suit or a fit, forcing to game and looking at slam.

bidding_conventions/strong_twos.name: Strong two-bids
bidding_conventions/strong_twos.summary:
An opening 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠ shows a strong hand with a long, good suit: about
eight playing tricks, forcing for one round. The weak two gives way to it.

bidding_conventions/super_accept.name: Super-Accepting a Transfer
bidding_conventions/super_accept.summary:
After partner's transfer over 1NT, opener with four-card support and a
maximum bids above the two-level completion to say so, and responder can bid
a thin game.

bid_4c.label: 4♣ is a transfer
bid_4c.desc: The bid: 4♣ over 1NT transfers (South African Texas: to ♥, with 4♦ to ♠)

bid_4s.label: 4♠ is a transfer
bid_4s.desc: The bid: 4♠ over 1NT transfers (to a minor); no printed card has a box for it

two_under.label: 2-under Texas
two_under.desc: Texas one step lower: 4♣ transfers to ♥ and 4♦ to ♠. Opener's bid of the suit in between (4♦ over 4♣, 4♥ over 4♦) is a super-accept; four of the major is a plain completion

range_min_plus.label: 3NT artificial raise: minimum has a plus
range_min_plus.desc: A good hand at that end: the range written with a plus ("14+-17" is a good 14 to 17)

range_min_minus.label: 3NT artificial raise: minimum has a minus
range_min_minus.desc: A poor hand at that end: the range written with a minus ("15-17-" is 15 to a poor 17)

range_max_plus.label: 3NT artificial raise: maximum has a plus
range_max_plus.desc: A good hand at that end: the range written with a plus ("14+-17" is a good 14 to 17)

range_max_minus.label: 3NT artificial raise: maximum has a minus
range_max_minus.desc: A poor hand at that end: the range written with a minus ("15-17-" is 15 to a poor 17)

bidding_conventions/tislevoll.name: Tislevoll slam try
bidding_conventions/tislevoll.summary:
After partner opens a major and the opponents preempt, responder's 4♣ and 4♦
are slam tries in partner's major that show or deny a control in the
opponents' suit.

bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.name: Transfer Walsh
bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.label: Transfer responses to 1♣
bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.summary:
Over partner's 1♣, responder's 1♦ and 1♥ are transfers to the next suit,
showing four or more cards in it, and 1♠ denies a four-card major. Opener
can accept the transfer, so the 1♣ hand often declares.

bidding_conventions/transfers_after_doub.name: Transfers after a takeout double
bidding_conventions/transfers_after_doub.label: Vs takeout double: transfer responses
bidding_conventions/transfers_after_doub.summary:
After partner's opening is doubled for takeout, responder's new-suit bids
are transfers to the next suit, so opener can accept or show a fit and
responder can describe more hands.

bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust.name: 2♥ bust over 2♣
bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust.label: Parrish 2♥ bust
bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust.summary:
After 2♣–2♦ and opener's natural rebid, a cheapest-suit reply shows a very
weak hand, so opener knows when to stop short of game. The Parrish form uses
2♥ as the bust in some auctions.

relay.label: Parrish relay
relay.desc: A relay that follows the 2♥ bust, so it depends on it

bidding_conventions/two_over_one.name: 2/1 Game Force
bidding_conventions/two_over_one.label: 2/1 game force
bidding_conventions/two_over_one.summary:
After a one-level opening, responder's new suit at the two level, without
jumping and by an unpassed hand, forces to game. The auction can then go
slowly, with room to describe both hands.

see.title: 2 over 1 Game Forcing: Modern Bridge Standard
Vic's Views: Building a new partnership – part 1

rebid_style.label: 2/1 opener's rebid style
rebid_style.desc: Opener's rebid after a 2/1 game force (1♥–2♦). bergen (Bergen style): 2NT is the default bid and says nothing; rebidding the major shows six; a new suit (2♠, 3♣) shows no extras. lawrence (Lawrence style): rebidding the major is the default, 5+; a new suit shows extras; 2NT shows stoppers. schuler (Schuler Shift): rebidding the major is the default, exactly five; a new suit shows extras; 2NT shows six or more in the major (Vic Quiros, ACBL Bridge Bulletin, September 2026)

game_forcing_except.label: 2/1 game forcing except when suit rebid

bidding_conventions/two_way_drury.name: Two-way Drury
bidding_conventions/two_way_drury.summary:
Played instead of Drury: a passed hand's 2♣ and 2♦ over partner's third- or
fourth-seat major both show limit raises, split by trump length (usually 2♣
three trumps, 2♦ four).

bidding_conventions/two_way_game_tries.name: Two-way game tries
bidding_conventions/two_way_game_tries.summary:
After a major raise, opener's 2NT (or the next step) is a relay for one kind
of game try and new suits are another, so opener can make short-suit and
long-suit tries.

bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.name: Two-way new minor forcing
bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.label: Two-way new minor forcing
bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.summary:
Played instead of NMF: after opener's 1NT rebid, responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦
(to sign off or invite) and 2♦ is game forcing.

see.title: Two-Way New Minor Forcing aka xyNT
2-Way New Minor Forcing and Wolff Signoff

by_passed_hand.label: Two-way NMF by a passed hand

bidding_conventions/walsh.name: Walsh
bidding_conventions/walsh.label: Walsh responses (BBA's switch)
bidding_conventions/walsh.desc: BBA's 'Walsh style'. With it on BBA still bids 1♦ over 1♣ with four diamonds and a four-card major, so our rules read one_club_responses instead
bidding_conventions/walsh.summary:
Over partner's 1♣, responder with a weak or moderate hand bids a four-card
major ahead of longer diamonds, so opener can rebid 1NT with any balanced
hand knowing no 4-4 major fit is lost.

see.title: Thinking and Responding: Walsh and Extended Walsh

bidding_conventions/weak_2s.name: Weak Twos
bidding_conventions/weak_2s.summary:
An opening 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠ shows a good six-card suit and less than an opening
bid, as a preempt. Responder's 2NT usually asks for more, and a raise
continues the preempt.

bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts.name: Weak jump shifts
bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts.summary:
Responder's jump in a new suit over partner's one-level opening shows a long
suit and a weak hand, rather than a strong one.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Thinking and Responding: Jump Shifts After 1-Level Openings - Weak and Invitational

bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.name: Western cue bid
bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.brief: 4 of an opponent's suit asks for a stopper for 3NT
bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.label: Western cuebid
bidding_conventions/western_cuebid.summary:
A cue bid of the opponents' suit when looking for 3NT asks partner to bid
notrump with a stopper in that suit.

bidding_conventions/wilkosz.name: Wilkosz 2♦
bidding_conventions/wilkosz.summary:
An opening 2♦ showing a weak two-suited hand with at least five cards in
each of two suits, one of them a major.

bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.name: Wolff signoff
bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.label: Wolff sign-off
bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.desc: After 1x–1y–2NT, responder's 3♣ asks opener to bid 3♦, to pass or sign off in a suit; every other call but pass forces to game. No .bbsa key (BBA does not play it)
bidding_conventions/wolff_signoff.summary:
After opener's 2NT rebid (1m–1M–2NT), responder's 3♣ forces opener to bid
3♦, so responder can sign off in a suit or show weaker hands; other three-
level bids force.

see.title: 2-Way New Minor Forcing and Wolff Signoff

bidding_conventions/xyz.name: XYZ
bidding_conventions/xyz.label: XYZ
bidding_conventions/xyz.summary:
After any three one-level bids, responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦ and 2♦ is game
forcing, extending two-way checkback to every such auction.

competitive_bidding/anti_lead_directing_.name: Anti-lead-directing doubles
competitive_bidding/anti_lead_directing_.summary:
When a lead-directing double of an artificial bid is expected, a double asks
partner not to lead that suit, and a pass says nothing.

competitive_bidding/bromad.name: BROMAD
competitive_bidding/bromad.summary:
Bergen raises used over the opponents' takeout double of partner's major
(Bergen Raises Over Major Doubles), with the structure adjusted for the
double.

competitive_bidding/cappelletti.name: Cappelletti over 1NT
competitive_bidding/cappelletti.summary:
Over their 1NT: double is for penalty, 2♣ shows a one-suited hand, 2♦ both
majors, 2♥ and 2♠ that major and a minor, 2NT both minors.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/collante.name: Collante
competitive_bidding/collante.summary:
After partner's 1♣ and their 1♦ (or 1♦ and 1♥), a double shows four cards in
the next suit up and a bid of it shows five or more.

competitive_bidding/crash.name: CRASH
competitive_bidding/crash.summary:
A defence to a strong 1♣ opening: overcalls show two-suited hands by colour,
rank and shape (CRASH: Colour, RAnk, SHape).

competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt.name: Defending against 1NT
competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt.summary:
An agreement on what overcalls and doubles of the opponents' 1NT mean,
usually a system that shows two-suited hands at the two level. The card
names which one, against strong and weak notrumps.

competitive_bidding/dont.name: DONT
competitive_bidding/dont.desc: Bridge-Classroom's DONT switch: plays DONT when vs_1nt_strong.system is unset or other
competitive_bidding/dont.summary:
Over their strong 1NT: double shows one long suit (partner relays 2♣); 2♣
and 2♦ show that suit and a higher one; 2♥ both majors; 2♠ six or more
spades.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/equal_level_conversi.name: Equal level conversion
competitive_bidding/equal_level_conversi.summary:
After a takeout double and partner's forced response, the doubler's bid of
another suit at the same level shows a two-suited hand without extra
strength, rather than a strong one.

competitive_bidding/exit_transfers.name: Exit transfers
competitive_bidding/exit_transfers.summary:
When the opponents double partner's 1NT, redouble and suit bids are
transfers to the next suit to escape, and pass forces a redouble for two-
suited runouts.

competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps.name: Fit-showing jumps
competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps.summary:
In competition, a jump in a new suit shows a good suit there and a fit for
partner, so partner can judge how the hands fit.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/forcing_pass.name: Forcing pass
competitive_bidding/forcing_pass.summary:
When the partnership has shown game-invitational or better values and an
opponent bids, a pass is forcing: it asks partner to double or bid, and
shows interest in continuing.

competitive_bidding/ghestem.name: Ghestem
competitive_bidding/ghestem.summary:
Played instead of Michaels and the Unusual 2NT: 2NT, a cue bid and a jump
cue bid each show a specific pair of suits.

competitive_bidding/good_bad_2nt.name: Good/bad 2NT
competitive_bidding/good_bad_2nt.summary:
In a competitive auction where the opponents have just bid at the two level,
2NT is artificial and shows a weak hand that wants to compete to the three
level; bidding the three level directly is stronger.

competitive_bidding/jordan_2nt.name: Jordan 2NT
competitive_bidding/jordan_2nt.label: Jordan (Truscott) 2NT
competitive_bidding/jordan_2nt.summary:
After partner's opening is doubled for takeout, responder's 2NT shows a
limit raise or better in partner's suit, leaving the direct raises weak.

competitive_bidding/landy.name: Landy
competitive_bidding/landy.summary: Over their 1NT, 2♣ shows both majors; other overcalls are natural.

competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubl.name: Lead-directing doubles
competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubl.brief: Double of artificial bid suggests opening lead
competitive_bidding/lead_directing_doubl.summary:
A double of an artificial bid (a cue bid, Stayman, a transfer, a response to
an ace ask) or of a slam asks partner to lead that suit, or a specific
unusual suit.

competitive_bidding/leaping_michaels.name: Leaping Michaels
competitive_bidding/leaping_michaels.brief: 4♣/4♦ over weak two = good 5+ in that minor + 5+ major
competitive_bidding/leaping_michaels.summary:
Over their weak two, a jump to four of a minor shows that minor and the
other major (or both majors over a minor), five-five with game values.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/lebensohl.name: Lebensohl
competitive_bidding/lebensohl.summary:
When they overcall partner's 1NT, responder's 2NT is a relay to 3♣: the two-
step route shows a weaker or different hand from a direct bid, and whether
responder cue-bids fast or slow tells whether a stopper is held.

see.title: NT Bidding: Responding to 1NT in Competition - Lebensohl

after_weak_two_double.brief: 2NT relay after partner doubles a weak two
after_weak_two_double.label: Lebensohl after doubling a weak two

competitive_bidding/mathe.name: Mathe
competitive_bidding/mathe.summary:
A defence to a strong 1♣ opening: double shows the majors, 1NT the minors,
and suit bids are natural.

see.title: Competitive Bidding: Bidding Over Strong 2C (and 1C) Openings - Mathe

competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles.name: Maximal doubles
competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles.label: Maximal doubles
competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles.summary:
When the opponents have competed to the three level just below your suit, a
double is a game try rather than penalty, since there is no room for another
try.

see.title: Non-Takeout Doubles: Card-Showing, Maximal, Penalty, Lead-Directing

competitive_bidding/meckwell.name: Meckwell over 1NT
competitive_bidding/meckwell.summary:
Over their 1NT: double shows a one-suited minor or both majors; 2♣ and 2♦
show that minor and a major; 2♥ and 2♠ are natural; 2NT shows both minors.

strength.label: Michaels strength
strength.desc: wide_range: any strength from about 7 HCP with five-five (BBA: 8+ total points, 12+ vulnerable). weak_or_strong (mini-maxi): weak, or 16+ and bids again; an intermediate hand overcalls instead. Bridge-Classroom's seed card writes weak_or_strong

minor_advance.label: Advancing Michaels over a major: which minor
minor_advance.desc: After a Michaels cue bid of a major (the other major and a minor). ask_2nt: advancer bids 2NT to ask for the minor, at any strength; 3♣ and 3♦ are natural, a long suit of advancer's own (Bridge Bum). pass_or_correct: 3♣ is pass or correct to partner's minor, and 2NT a stronger ask (Larry Cohen)

over_minor.label: Cue of a natural 1♣/1♦: Michaels (both majors)

over_major.label: Cue of 1♥/1♠: Michaels (the other major and a minor)

over_short_minor.label: Cue of a possibly short 1♣/1♦: Michaels

competitive_bidding/michaels_unusual.name: Michaels & Unusual 2NT

competitive_bidding/mitchell_stayman.name: Mitchell Stayman
competitive_bidding/mitchell_stayman.summary:
After partner's minor opening and their 1NT overcall, responder's 2♣ shows
both majors (five-four) with modest values, and opener chooses.

competitive_bidding/mixed_raise.name: Mixed raise
competitive_bidding/mixed_raise.label: Jump cuebid: mixed raise
competitive_bidding/mixed_raise.desc: Advancer's jump cuebid of their suit shows a mixed raise of partner's overcall: four-card support, between a preemptive jump raise and a limit raise
competitive_bidding/mixed_raise.summary:
After partner's overcall, advancer's jump cuebid of the opponents' suit
shows a mixed raise: four-card support with values between a preemptive jump
raise and a limit raise. The plain cuebid is then a limit raise or better.

competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti.name: Modified Cappelletti
competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti.summary:
Played instead of Cappelletti: over their 1NT, 2♣ shows a one-suited minor
or a major and a minor, and 2♥ and 2♠ are natural one-suiters.

competitive_bidding/multi_landy.name: Landy and Multi-Landy over 1NT
competitive_bidding/multi_landy.summary:
Over their 1NT: double shows a four-card major and a longer minor, 2♣ both
majors, 2♦ one long major, and 2♥ and 2♠ that major with a minor.

competitive_bidding/negative_doubles.name: Negative Doubles
competitive_bidding/negative_doubles.label: Negative doubles
competitive_bidding/negative_doubles.summary:
After partner opens and the next player overcalls, responder's double is for
takeout, usually showing the unbid major or majors, so responder can compete
without a long suit or a fit.

through.label: Negative doubles through
through.desc: The highest overcall a double of is negative (4♥: a double of 4♠ or higher is not)

competitive_bidding/non_leaping_michaels.name: Non-leaping Michaels
competitive_bidding/non_leaping_michaels.summary:
Played instead of Leaping Michaels: over their preempt, a non-jump bid of a
new suit at the next level shows that suit and a major.

competitive_bidding/raptor.name: Raptor 1NT
competitive_bidding/raptor.summary:
An overcall of 1NT that shows a four-card major and a longer minor, rather
than a strong balanced hand.

competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.name: Responsive Doubles
competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.brief: Double after partner double + opp raise = takeout
competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.label: Responsive doubles
competitive_bidding/responsive_doubles.summary:
After partner doubles for takeout and the next player raises, advancer's
double is for takeout too, showing values and usually both unbid suits of a
kind (the majors or the minors).

through.label: Responsive doubles through
through.desc: The highest raise of their suit, after partner's takeout double or overcall, that a double of is responsive (3♠: a double of 4♣ or higher is not)

competitive_bidding/rodrigue.name: Rodrigue
competitive_bidding/rodrigue.summary:
After partner's minor and their 1♠, a double shows four hearts, and five or
more hearts are shown by 2m with 8–10 points or 2♥ with 11 or more.

competitive_bidding/rosenkranz.name: Rosenkranz double
competitive_bidding/rosenkranz.summary:
When the opponents overcall partner's opening and advancer raises partner's
overcall, a double or redouble shows a top honour in partner's suit, and a
raise denies one.

competitive_bidding/rubensohl.name: Rubensohl
competitive_bidding/rubensohl.summary:
A transfer version of Lebensohl: after they overcall partner's 1NT,
responder's bids from 2NT up are transfers to the next suit, which lets
responder show a suit, a stopper or values at a lower level.

see.title: NT Bidding: Modern, Transfer, and Modern Transfer Lebensohl

after_double.label: Rubensohl after doubling a weak two

competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.name: Sandwich 1NT
competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.brief: 1NT in 4th seat after two suits bid = unusual NT
competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.label: Sandwich NT
competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt.summary:
In the sandwich seat, after the opponents have bid two suits, a 1NT overcall
shows the two unbid suits rather than a strong balanced hand.

competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt.name: Scrambling 2NT
competitive_bidding/scrambling_2nt.summary:
In a competitive auction where a takeout double would be natural, advancer's
2NT asks partner to pick a minor or a two-suited contract, rather than
showing values.

competitive_bidding/snapdragon.name: Snapdragon doubles
competitive_bidding/snapdragon.brief: After 3 suits bid, double = 4+ in 4th suit + tolerance for partner
competitive_bidding/snapdragon.summary:
When three suits have been bid, one by each of three players, fourth hand's
double shows the unbid suit and tolerance for partner's.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/sos_redouble.name: SOS redouble
competitive_bidding/sos_redouble.brief: Redouble asking partner to pick another suit
competitive_bidding/sos_redouble.summary:
When a low-level contract is doubled for penalty, a redouble asks partner to
choose another suit, rather than showing strength.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

competitive_bidding/spear.name: Spear
competitive_bidding/spear.summary:
How to intervene after the opponents' 1♣ or 1♦ opening and 1NT response:
suit bids and double describe both-majors, one-major and strong hands.

competitive_bidding/suction.name: Suction
competitive_bidding/suction.summary:
Over their 1NT, each two-level suit bid shows either the next suit up or the
other two suits, so the overcall is ambiguous by design and partner bids the
next suit to find out.

competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.name: Support Cuebids
competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.brief: Cue of opp's suit = 3+ card limit raise
competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.label: Cue-bid raise
competitive_bidding/support_cuebids.summary:
A cue bid of the opponents' suit in response to partner's opening or
overcall shows a raise of partner's suit with limit-raise values or better,
leaving direct raises weaker.

see.title: Constructive Bidding Opposite 3rd Hand Openings: Cuebid as Limit Raise+ by a Passed Hand

competitive_bidding/support_doubles.name: Support Doubles and Redoubles
competitive_bidding/support_doubles.label: Support doubles
competitive_bidding/support_doubles.summary:
After opener's one-level opening and responder's one-level suit, when the
next player bids, opener's double shows exactly three-card support for
responder (a redouble after their double), and a raise shows four.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know

through.label: Support doubles through
through.desc: The highest call by RHO over which the double still shows three-card support (2♥). Unset: two of responder's major

competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles.name: Takeout Doubles
competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles.summary:
A double of an opening bid, when partner has not bid, asks partner to bid:
it shows opening values, shortness in their suit and support for the unbid
suits, or a hand too strong to overcall.

competitive_bidding/thrump_double.name: Thrump double
competitive_bidding/thrump_double.summary:
After partner opens and the opponents preempt at the three level,
responder's double asks opener to bid 3NT with a stopper, for a hand with
values and no fit or long suit.

competitive_bidding/transfer_advances.name: Transfer advances
competitive_bidding/transfer_advances.summary:
After partner's overcall, advancer's bids are transfers to the next suit, so
the overcaller can accept or show more, and advancer can describe more
hands.

competitive_bidding/unusual_vs_unusual.name: Unusual vs Unusual
competitive_bidding/unusual_vs_unusual.summary:
After they show two suits with Michaels or the Unusual 2NT, cue bids of
their suits show hands in the other two suits: one cue bid a raise of
partner, the other a strong hand in the fourth suit.

see.title: 25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know
Unusual vs. Unusual and Unusual vs. Michaels

defense/defensive_signals.name: Defensive Signals
defense/defensive_signals.summary:
Defenders' agreements on what their cards say: attitude (like this suit or
not), count (odd or even length) and suit preference (which other suit to
play), and which applies when.

defense/lavinthal.name: Lavinthal
defense/lavinthal.label: First discard: Lavinthal
defense/lavinthal.summary:
A discard is suit preference: a high card asks for the higher of the other
two suits, a low card for the lower.

defense/odd_even_discards.name: Odd-even discards
defense/odd_even_discards.label: First discard: odd/even
defense/odd_even_discards.summary:
A defender's first discard says something by being odd or even: an odd card
encourages that suit, an even card discourages and its size points to
another suit.

defense/opening_leads.name: Opening Leads
defense/opening_leads.summary:
The partnership's choice of card from each kind of holding on opening lead,
such as fourth best from length and the top of a sequence, so partner can
read the lead.

see.title: Fundamentals of Trick Taking – 4th Best Leads (Attitude)

defense/reverse_smith_echo.name: Reverse Smith echo
defense/reverse_smith_echo.summary:
Played instead of the Smith echo: on declarer's first suit, a defender's
high-low says they did not like partner's opening lead.

defense/rusinow_leads.name: Rusinow leads
defense/rusinow_leads.summary:
Played instead of standard honour leads: from touching honours lead the
second highest (the king from KQ, the queen from QJ), usually only at trick
one against suit contracts.

defense/smith_echo.name: Smith echo
defense/smith_echo.label: Smith echo
defense/smith_echo.summary:
On declarer's first suit, a defender's high-low says whether they liked
partner's opening lead, rather than giving count.

defense/trump_suit_preference.name: Trump suit preference
defense/trump_suit_preference.label: Trump suit preference
defense/trump_suit_preference.desc: A defender's spot cards in trumps show suit preference (high for the higher side suit), not count
defense/trump_suit_preference.summary:
A defender's spot cards in the trump suit show suit preference, not count:
a high trump asks for the higher of the side suits, a low one for the lower.

defense/upside_down_signals.name: Upside-down signals
defense/upside_down_signals.summary:
Played instead of standard signals: a low card encourages and a high one
discourages, and count is shown upside down too, so the defenders keep their
high cards.

see.title: Defensive Carding: Upside-Down Count and Attitude (UDCA)

declarer_lead.suit_preference.label: Signal on declarer's lead: suit preference

partner_lead.attitude.label: Primary signal to partner's lead: attitude

partner_lead.count.label: Primary signal to partner's lead: count

partner_lead.suit_preference.label: Primary signal to partner's lead: suit preference

vs_1nt_strong_includes.label: Their 1NT is strong if its range includes
vs_1nt_strong_includes.desc: Which defense to play: a 1NT whose range includes this point count gets vs_1nt_strong, any other vs_1nt_weak. BBO cards write 16 as Strong 16+ and Weak No 16

direct_jump_cuebid_major.label: Direct jump cuebid over a major

direct_jump_cuebid_minor.label: Direct jump cuebid over a minor

quasi_natural.label: Cue of a possibly short 1♣/1♦: natural

quasi_other.label: Cue of a possibly short 1♣/1♦: other

style.label: Bidding style
style.desc: Unset: our default (modern where we have one, else standard). standard: the textbook treatment where the default is modern. bba: what BBA does, as far as probes and the corpus show; for A/B tests

forcing_opening.label: Forcing opening (as written)
forcing_opening.desc: The card's forcing-opening line as an importer wrote it ("2C"); forcing_opening_1c/2c/other are the structured form

vs_suits.length.fourth_best.label: Length leads vs suits: fourth best

strong.label: Defense vs strong 1NT
strong.desc: Bridge-Classroom's system name (its editor's list: Cappelletti, DONT, Meckwell, Multi-Landy, Penalty...). Unset, natural or other: natural overcalls. cappelletti (Hamilton): X penalty, 2♣ one suit, 2♦ majors, 2♥/2♠ that major and a minor, 2NT minors. modified_cappelletti: 2♣ a minor one-suiter or a major and a minor, 2♥/2♠ one-suited. dont: X one suit, 2♣/2♦/2♥ that suit and a higher one, 2♠ spades. meckwell: X a minor or the majors, 2♣/2♦ that minor and a major, 2♥/2♠ natural, 2NT minors. multi_landy: X a four-card major and a longer minor, 2♣ majors, 2♦ one major, 2♥/2♠ that major and a minor. landy: 2♣ majors, the rest natural. Played against every 1NT range. See conventions/competitive/vs-1nt.notes.md

acbl.name: ACBL
acbl.summary: Natural calls are not alerted and artificial calls are, apart from a list of exemptions such as Stayman, 4NT ace asks and a very strong 2♣. A few calls are announced instead: the 1NT opening range, a minor opening that may be short, transfers and other bids showing one named suit, and a forcing or semi-forcing 1NT response. A conventional call at 3NT or higher from opener's rebid on, and any control bid, gets a delayed alert after the auction; passes, doubles and redoubles are never delayed.

source.version: Effective February 16, 2026 (PDF titled "Alert Procedures Update February 2026"; supersedes April 15, 2024 and January 1, 2021 editions)

ebu.name: EBU
ebu.summary: The bidder's partner alerts any call that is not natural, or natural with a meaning the opponents would not expect. On the first round a fixed set of calls is announced instead, among them the 1NT range, short minors, natural two-level openings, Stayman and transfers. Above 3NT after the first round nothing is alerted except artificial first-round suit bids and some doubles and passes, and there is no delayed alert.

source.title: EBU Blue Book: EBU Player Handbook (chapter 4, Alerting and Announcing)
source.version: Revised 2024, effective 1 August 2024 (current edition per ebu.co.uk/blue-book as of Oct 2026)

wbf.name: WBF
wbf.summary: Artificial calls, and any call resting on a special partnership understanding, are alerted; natural calls are not. There are no announcements, no delayed alerts and no level cut-off, so conventional calls at the four level and above are alerted too. Non-forcing new-suit and jump-shift responses must be alerted, and behind screens each player alerts both their own calls and partner's.

source.title: WBF Alerting Policy
source.version: Adopted July 1997, revised August 2002 and August 2022; published by the WBF Systems Committee March 2023. Screen procedure from WBF General Conditions of Contest §16 and §33.2 (2022) and 'Using Bidding Boxes with Screens' §2.2 (February 2024)

alert.note: Asks for a four-card major. Exempt from alerting in the ACBL; the EBU announces it as "Stayman" and the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Stayman over 2NT, treated like 2♣ over 1NT: exempt in the ACBL, announced in the EBU. The WBF does not list it; it alerts every artificial call.
Denies a four-card major. Exempt in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Natural major reply. The EBU alerts a 2♠ that does not deny four hearts.
Natural notrump rebid. The EBU alerts it when the 2♣ did not promise a major; the ACBL and WBF do not mention it and it reads as natural.
Transfer to the next suit up: partner names the suit ("Hearts", "Spades") in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF has no announcements and alerts it.
Transfer over a 2NT opening, announced like the 1NT ones. The WBF alerts it as artificial.
Plain completion of the transfer. The WBF alerts it as a call resting on a partnership understanding.
Super-accept: a jump completion promising four-card support. The EBU and WBF alert the specific holding; the ACBL does not mention it and it reads as a natural raise.

alert.when: responder's rebid has an agreed artificial meaning
alert.note: Alerted only when responder's rebid carries an agreed artificial meaning (for example a game force with long spades); a natural second suit is not.
Four-level transfer to a major, announced by naming the suit even above 3NT. The WBF alerts it as artificial.
Completion of the transfer. The WBF alerts it as a call based on an understanding.
Shows four cards in the major bid and five in the other.
Natural choice of game. The WBF does not mention it; natural calls are not alerted there.
Puppet Stayman over 1NT. The ACBL exempts any major-suit ask over notrump; the EBU alerts Puppet rather than announcing it, and the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Asks for a four- or five-card major. Exempt in the ACBL as a major-suit ask; alerted in the EBU and WBF.
Shows at least one four-card major and no five-card major.
Shows a five-card major. The ACBL lists it as a natural reply that is still alerted; the EBU treats it as natural, and the WBF does not mention it.
Natural: no four- or five-card major.
Responder bids the major he does not hold. The ACBL treats it as a one-suit showing call to announce (uncertain: some directors want an alert); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Shows both majors. The EBU does not alert it because it is above 3NT after the first round.
Relay forcing opener to bid 3♣.
Forced completion of the relay.
Stayman-like cuebid, with the route showing or denying a stopper. The ACBL exempts bids in the overcaller's suit after a notrump opening; the EBU and WBF alert it.
To play, but its route shows or denies a stopper. The ACBL treats it as natural; the EBU alerts the stopper message, and the WBF's rule for special understandings points the same way.
Stayman that may be weak. Still exempt in the ACBL and still announced "Stayman" in the EBU; the WBF alerts it as artificial.
Passing opener's reply is natural.

alert.when: playing crawling Stayman (2♥ shows both majors, weak)
alert.note: Crawling variant: weak with both majors. The ACBL alerts it; the EBU and WBF do not mention it, but its extra message is alertable under their general rules.
Natural game-forcing new suit (2♥ only over 1♠). The EBU announces it as "natural, game-forcing"; the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: the 2♣ response may hold fewer than three clubs
alert.note: Alerted when the 2♣ response may hold fewer than three clubs, since it is then not natural.
Artificial game-forcing raise.
Shows shortness in the suit bid.
Shows extras without shortness. The ACBL reads it as natural; the EBU and WBF alert it as a coded strength message.
Coded hand description, not an offer to play. The ACBL gives a delayed alert because it is at 3NT on opener's rebid.
Shows a good second suit. Natural in the ACBL and above 3NT after the first round in the EBU; the WBF alerts the reply.
Minimum sign-off. The WBF does not list it separately; it reads as natural.
Artificial game-forcing raise.
Step replies showing strength or controls.
Step reply at 3NT. The ACBL delays the alert to the end of the auction.
Step reply above 3NT. The ACBL gives a delayed alert, the EBU none after the first round; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Responder's artificial follow-up asks (ACBL uncertain: depends on the scheme, and those at 3NT or above are delayed).
Artificial raises showing four-card support.
Preemptive jump raise, alerted in the ACBL and EBU when the next hand passed. The WBF does not list it and reads a jump raise as natural (uncertain).
Artificial re-ask or game try after the artificial raise.
Jump raise weaker than a limit raise; the ACBL does not alert it after a double. The WBF reads it as a natural raise (uncertain).
A mixed raise shown by an artificial bid (such as 3♣). The ACBL does not alert a jump cuebid after an overcall.
Double jump showing shortness. Alerted at once even at the four level, as responder's first call.
Opener's jump showing shortness below 3NT.
Opener's splinter above 3NT. The ACBL delays the alert; the EBU does not alert it after the first round; the WBF alerts it.
Artificial raise by a passed hand.
Artificial reply about opener's strength.
Return to the major. Natural in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts opener's replies as artificial (it groups them, so this is our reading).
Artificial raise by a passed hand.
Artificial: a full opening with game interest.
Sign-off showing a light opening. Natural in the ACBL and EBU; the WBF alerts it as a step reply.
Partner announces "Semi-forcing" in the ACBL and the upper limit ("Up to 12") in the EBU. The WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Not announced in the ACBL after a third- or fourth-seat opening. The EBU has no seat rule, so the announcement still applies; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Rebid in a three-card minor: natural in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF alerts a rebid that may be that short.

alert.when: opener's minor may be a doubleton
alert.note: Rebid in a minor that may be a doubleton is not natural (EBU uncertain).
Partner announces "Forcing" (ACBL: add "could have four spades" if 1♠ may be bypassed). The WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Not announced in the ACBL after a third- or fourth-seat opening. The EBU has no seat rule, so it still announces; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Rebid in a three-card minor: natural in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF alerts a rebid that may be that short.

alert.when: opener's minor may be a doubleton
alert.note: Rebid in a minor that may be a doubleton is not natural (EBU uncertain).
Strong, forcing single raise.
Weak jump raise, alerted when the next hand passed (WBF uncertain).
Opener's bid showing a stopper rather than length. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert artificial calls below 3NT.
Natural four-card major response.
Natural, but denies a four-card major unless strong. The ACBL and EBU (uncertain) leave the inference to questions; the WBF alerts it as a special understanding (uncertain).
Natural rebid that may bypass a major.
Transfer: partner names the suit shown ("Hearts", "Spades"). The WBF alerts it.
Denies a four-card major. Alerted in the ACBL and WBF; the EBU announces "No major".
Accepting the transfer. Natural in the ACBL (uncertain) and EBU unless it promises a holding; the WBF alerts it.
Artificial strong opening. The ACBL exempts a very strong 2♣ (alert one that may be merely strong); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Waiting or negative reply. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU and WBF.
Natural positive reply.
Natural balanced rebid.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Natural weak two. The EBU announces the strength ("Weak"); the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.

alert.when: a new-suit response is not forcing
alert.note: Alerted when a new-suit response is not forcing. The EBU and WBF do not cover it directly; an unexpected meaning is alertable under both.

alert.when: a raise is invitational or forcing, not preemptive
alert.note: Alerted in the ACBL when a raise is not preemptive. The EBU and WBF do not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
Asking bid. The ACBL exempts any forcing 2NT over a two-level preempt; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Coded replies about strength and suit quality.
Coded reply (such as a solid suit). The ACBL delays the alert as a 3NT call on opener's rebid.
Weak two in an unknown major or other options; also pre-alerted in the ACBL.
Pass-or-correct response (ACBL uncertain).
Enquiry. The ACBL exempts a forcing 2NT over a two-level preempt (uncertain, as Multi may hold strong hands); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Coded replies to the enquiry.
Three-suited opening.
Asks for the short suit; not a preempt, so the ACBL 2NT exemption does not apply.
Show the short suit.
Pass-or-correct response. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert a call that does not promise the suit.
Five spades and four or five hearts in a weak hand: the jump shows a suit it does not name, so every regulator alerts it.
Five spades and four hearts with invitational values: the hearts are an agreement the opponents would not expect.
Asks responder for shape and strength.
Relay: hearts or a big balanced hand.
Forced relay.
Balanced, stronger than a direct 2NT. The EBU alerts the unexpected strength; the ACBL treats it as natural, and the WBF does not mention it.
Natural heart rebid after the relay (EBU uncertain).
Very weak reply, says nothing about hearts.
Relay to 3♣. The ACBL exempts a forcing 2NT after a two-level preempt (uncertain); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Forced reply to the relay.
Lead-directing, with support for partner, not a suit to play.
Ace or keycard ask. Exempt in the ACBL and above 3NT in the EBU; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Replies to the ask. The ACBL gives a delayed alert; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
King ask and its replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Ace or keycard ask. Exempt in the ACBL and above 3NT in the EBU; the WBF has no level cut-off.
Replies to the ask. The ACBL gives a delayed alert; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
King ask and its replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Asks for the trump queen. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Show or deny the queen (and kings). Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Ace ask directly over notrump. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU alerts it as an artificial first-round suit bid above 3NT, and the WBF alerts it.
Ace replies. Delayed in the ACBL (opener's rebid), not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
King ask and replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Gerber outside a direct notrump auction. Not exempt in the ACBL, so delayed; not alerted in the EBU; alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask. Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU does not alert it after the first round; the WBF alerts it.
Keycard step replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask in the agreed minor. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted above 3NT in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard step replies. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Keycard ask excluding the void. Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU alerts it only as a first-round jump; the WBF alerts it.
Keycard replies ignoring that suit. Delayed in the ACBL, not alerted in the EBU, alerted in the WBF.
Asks partner to choose a slam, not a notrump offer. Delayed in the ACBL; not alerted in the EBU; alerted in the WBF.
Natural choice of strain.
Asks for a stopper for 3NT. The ACBL exempts cuebids after an opening and overcall; the EBU (below 3NT or on the first round) and WBF alert it.
Asks for a stopper in a suit the partnership has bid (ACBL uncertain; delayed at 3NT or above after opener's rebid).
The ACBL always delays control bids, even below 3NT; the EBU and WBF alert them at once.
Trump-quality asks and step replies (ACBL uncertain).

alert.call: Asks, replies and control bids above 3NT
alert.note: Delayed in the ACBL; the EBU does not alert above 3NT after the first round; the WBF alerts them.
Shows or denies slam interest rather than offering to play. The ACBL delays the alert; the EBU (3NT is not above 3NT) and WBF alert it at once.
The ACBL delays all control bids; the EBU does not alert above 3NT; the WBF alerts them.
Takeout double of a natural suit opening. The WBF has no explicit exemption but treats it as generally understood (uncertain).

alert.when: the double of 1NT is not for penalty
alert.note: Takeout or conventional double of a 1NT opening. Listed by the EBU; the ACBL and WBF alert a double of notrump that is not for penalty or values.
Negative double. Exempt in the ACBL (announce the major if it usually holds five); the EBU announces it when it shows just four of the other major; the WBF alerts it (uncertain).
Negative double after other one-level openings. The WBF alerts a double that is not for penalty (uncertain).
Negative double after a preempt. The ACBL exempts only a penalty double here; the EBU does not alert a takeout-style double; the WBF alerts it.
Negative, penalty or card-showing double after a notrump opening. Exempt in the ACBL and not alerted in the EBU; the WBF alerts a non-penalty double.
Takeout double by advancer after they raise. Not alerted in the ACBL or EBU; the WBF alerts it as a special understanding.
Shows exactly three-card support. The ACBL exempts all doubles from opener's rebid on; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Support redouble. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Cuebid showing both majors. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU (overcalls are never announced) and WBF alert it.
Cuebid showing the other major and a minor. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU and WBF.

alert.when: the cuebid shows a pair of suits other than the usual one
alert.note: A cuebid showing a non-standard pair of suits.
Asks for overcaller's minor.
Two lowest unbid suits. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU and WBF alert it as two-suited.

alert.when: 2NT shows suits other than the two lowest unbid
alert.note: A 2NT overcall showing two suits other than the lowest two.
Two-suited 2NT after an opening and a response; exempt in the ACBL since 2026. The EBU and WBF do not list it; both alert a two-suited 2NT.
Shows a one-suiter.
The suit bid plus a higher one.
Natural spade one-suiter.
Relay or pass-or-correct bid.
Limit raise or better. Exempt in the ACBL after an opening and overcall; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Raise of the overcall, limit or better. Exempt in the ACBL; alerted in the EBU, and by the WBF's rule for artificial calls.
Double of an artificial bid asking for that suit. Not alerted in the ACBL or EBU; the WBF alerts it.
Double of an artificial bid asking for a different lead or against that suit.
Lead-directing double such as Lightner. The ACBL does not alert doubles of 3NT or higher; the EBU alerts the lead message even above 3NT, and so does the WBF's special-meaning rule.
Relay to 3♣ (ACBL uncertain: its forcing-2NT exemption may reach advancer).
Forced completion of the relay.
Artificial cuebid by advancer (ACBL uncertain); not listed by the EBU or WBF, but artificial.
Shows the two unbid suits, not a notrump hand.
Shows the fourth suit with tolerance for partner. The ACBL announces the suit (uncertain); the EBU (uncertain) and WBF alert it.
Game try, not penalty. The ACBL exempts all doubles from opener's rebid on; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Cuebids of the shown suits. Exempt in the ACBL as raises or good hands; the EBU and WBF alert them.
Shows values or penalty interest. Exempt in the ACBL and not listed by the EBU (uncertain); the WBF alerts it.
Natural and non-forcing. The ACBL and WBF alert a non-forcing new suit by an unpassed hand; the EBU's "natural, non-forcing" announcement fits it.
The minor plus the other major; a direct overcall, so not delayed.
Cuebid of the weak two. Exempt in the ACBL; the EBU (first-round artificial bid) and WBF alert it.
Two-suited jump over a weak 2♦. The ACBL does not mention it; it alerts natural bids that also show another suit.
Artificial and forcing (one round); does not promise the suit.
Natural rebids: raise, notrump with a stopper, preference.
Artificial and forcing (game force); does not promise the suit.
Natural rebids: raise, notrump with a stopper, preference.
Natural try promising three or more cards in the suit (WBF uncertain).

alert.when: the try may be a doubleton or shorter
alert.note: A try that may be a doubleton or shorter.
Natural; the extra strength is standard.
Artificial forcing enquiry.
Natural replies; an artificial reply is alerted.
Relay to 2♦.
Artificial game force.
Forced completion of the relay.
Relay to 2♦ (also after a 1NT rebid).
Artificial game force.
Forced completion of the relay.
Asks partner to pick another suit. Exempt in the ACBL in the balancing seat or after a balancing double; the EBU and WBF alert it.
Asks partner to pick another suit.
Artificial relay or enquiry, not a natural notrump.
Forced or coded reply to the relay.
Partner states the range ("15 to 17") in the ACBL and EBU. The WBF does not alert a natural notrump opening of any range.
Natural; only the 1NT range is announced.
Partner announces the minimum length ("Could be two"). The WBF has no rule for it but alerts a 1♣ that may be short (uncertain).
Partner announces the minimum length. The WBF alerts a 1♦ that can hold fewer than three cards as artificial.
Strong, forcing, artificial 1♣; the ACBL also wants a pre-alert.
When 2♣ is natural. The ACBL alerts any natural 2♣; the EBU announces its strength band; the WBF does not alert a natural opening.
A natural two-level opening that may hold 12+ HCP (not 4th seat). The ACBL alerts it; the EBU announces the band ("Intermediate"); the WBF does not cover it, and natural openings are not alerted.
Based on a long running suit, not a natural notrump. The WBF does not list it; it is not natural, so it is alerted.
Transfer to a major. The ACBL announces the suit shown (and wants a pre-alert); the EBU and WBF alert it.
Natural 1NT overcall in the usual range.
Alerted in the ACBL below 14 HCP and in the EBU when well under 15. The WBF does not cover it; this follows the ACBL.
A weak jump overcall is natural and expected, treated like a weak two opening: no regulator alerts it.

alert.when: jump overcalls are intermediate or strong, not weak
alert.note: Natural but not weak, so not what opponents expect: the ACBL and the EBU alert it; the WBF does not cover it, so this follows the ACBL.
A natural cuebid of a natural one-level opening. The ACBL alerts it; the EBU and WBF do not list it, but a natural cuebid is unexpected.
Invitational double raise: natural and expected.
Preemptive jump raise, alerted in the ACBL and EBU when the next hand passed. The WBF reads a raise as natural (uncertain).

A weak jump shift by responder with no interference. Strong is the default, so the ACBL and the WBF alert the weak version; the EBU announces it as natural and non-forcing. Not to be read as a preempt like a weak two or a weak jump overcall.
After a double or an overcall the weak jump shift is standard: no alert in the ACBL, and none in the EBU (uncertain). The WBF alerts every non-forcing jump shift.
Natural and forcing. The EBU announces "natural, game-forcing"; the ACBL and WBF do not alert it.
Shows a control in the suit bid. The ACBL always delays it; the EBU does not alert it above 3NT after the first round (it does below); the WBF alerts it.
