# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Benjamin twos (Wikipedia, "Benjamin Twos"; the PBS scenario
# `Benjamin_2D`): 2♣ is a strong two that is not forcing to game, 2♦ is
# the game-forcing opening, and there is no weak 2♦ (preempts.bid,
# `weak_2d_open`). The 2♣ openings of strong-openings.bid are off.
#
#   2♣  22-23, or an unbalanced 20+ with a good six-card suit or a
#       strong two-suiter and at most four losers
#   2♦  24+, or 23 without a five-card suit, or 22+ with one loser
#
# The ranges are BBA's (Benjamin_2D: 2♣ 20-23 and every distributional
# powerhouse, 2♦ 24+ and some 23s without a long suit); Wikipedia and
# the PBS chat put game-in-hand hands in 2♦.
#
# Responses to 2♣ are those of strong-openings.bid (2♦ waiting, the
# positives, the second negative). Responses to 2♦ (PBS): 2NT negative
# (0-6), 2♥/2♠ five or more, 3♣/3♦ six or more, any strength, 3NT 7+
# without a long suit. See benjamin.notes.md.

module benjamin "Benjamin 2♣ and 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d
  needs  strong-openings
  skill  bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d

when opening
# The strong two: about nine tricks.
  2C  "Benjamin 2♣: 22-23, or a strong two"   alert
      shows hcp=22..23 | (!balanced, hcp=20..23, losers<=4, (S>=6, quality(S)>=good) | (H>=6, quality(H)>=good) | (D>=6, quality(D)>=good) | (C>=6, quality(C)>=good) | shape 5-5-x-x | shape 6-5-x-x)
      sets  forcing=game, ask=strong_2c
      artificial
      priority 1
  2D  "Benjamin 2♦: game forcing, 24+"   alert
      shows hcp>=24 | (hcp=23, longest<=4)
      sets  forcing=game, ask=benjamin
      artificial
      priority 1
  # Game in hand (Wikipedia: 2♦ is the game force on playing tricks):
  # BBA opens 2♦ with 22-23 and at most one loser (Benjamin_2D: 4 of 4).
  2D  "Benjamin 2♦: game in hand, 22+ and at most one loser"   alert
      shows hcp>=22, losers<=1
      sets  forcing=game, ask=benjamin
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Responder to 2♣ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Benjamin's 2♣ is forcing for one round, and passable after opener's
# rebid. We keep the strong 2♣'s game force and its second negative
# (strong-openings.bid) for now: written as passable, half of the
# continuations had no rule (benjamin.notes.md). A raise of opener's
# major after the waiting 2♦ agrees it.
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2M (P)
  3M  "Three or more {M}: a raise with some values"   shows M>=3, hcp>=4
      sets  trump=M
      priority 1

# ── Responder to 2♦ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PBS chat (Benjamin_2D.btn): 2NT is the negative, "5- HCP, no 5-card
# major"; 2♥/2♠ five or more, 3♣/3♦ six or more, with no strength
# floor (the 5+ HCP is the chat's 2♣ responses; until 2026-10-07 we read
# it into 2♦ too and bid 2NT with a weak five-card major, notes). BBA
# (Benjamin_2D corpus): every five-card major bids it, 0-13 HCP; a
# six-card minor bids it from 1 HCP; without either 2NT up to 6 and 3NT
# from 7.
when asked benjamin
  2S  "Five or more spades, any strength"         shows S>=5, S>=H
  2H  "Five or more hearts, any strength"         shows H>=5, H>S
  3C  "Six or more clubs, no five-card major"      shows C>=6, C>=D, H<=4, S<=4
  3D  "Six or more diamonds, no five-card major"   shows D>=6, D>C, H<=4, S<=4
  3N  "Positive: 7+ HCP, no five-card major or six-card minor"   shows hcp>=7, H<=4, S<=4, D<=5, C<=5
  2N  "Negative: 0-6, no five-card major or six-card minor"      artificial
      priority -1

# ── Opener after a positive suit ─────────────────────────────────────
# Game is forced; opener has 24+, so the questions are the fit and the
# strain (BBA raises with three, else shows a suit or bids notrump). The
# raise agrees the suit, and the slam modules take over (keycards).
# Until 2026-10-07 opener had no rule here and the base 3NT ended the
# auction (Benjamin_2D: 2♦-2♥-3NT-pass on boards with a grand slam).
after 2D (P) 2y (P) | 2D (P) 3y (P) when y is not N
  cheapest(y) "Raise: three or more {y}"   shows y>=3   sets trump=y
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"        shows S>=5   when y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"        shows H>=5   when y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"      shows D>=5   when y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"         shows C>=5   when y is not C
  cheapest(N) "No fit, no suit to show"
      priority -1

# Responder after opener's raise of the major: with 0-5 the fast arrival
# to game (BBA: 4 of 4 with 0-6 there, two of them 3NT); more cue-bids
# (control-bids.bid) or asks.
after 2D (P) 2M (P) 3M (P)
  4M  "Weak: 0-5, game"    shows hcp<=5
      priority 2

# Opener over responder's game in the agreed major (0-5 after the raise,
# 0-6 after the negative): slam needs the playing tricks, at most two
# losers (BBA: asked on 4 of 4 with two or fewer, passed 5 of 6 with
# three or more, Benjamin_2D). With fewer the generic keycard ask
# (rkcb-1430.bid, 18 of my own) asks anyway.
after 2D (P) 2M (P) 3M (P) 4M (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 3M (P) 4M (P)
  P   "No slam interest"   shows losers>=3
      priority 1

# Responder after opener's suit: raise with three (agreeing it), rebid a
# six-card major or a seven-card minor, else notrump. (A six-card minor
# rebid at the four level left opener without a rule: four boards.)
after 2D (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) | 2D (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) | 2D (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) when y is not N, z is not N, z is not y
  cheapest(z) "Three or more {z}: agrees it"   shows z>=3   sets trump=z
      priority 1
  cheapest(y) "Six or more {y}"                shows y>=6
      when  y is H | y is S
  cheapest(y) "Seven or more {y}"              shows y>=7
      when  y is C | y is D
  cheapest(N) "No fit"
      priority -1

# ── Opener over the 3NT positive ─────────────────────────────────────
# 24+ facing 7+: slam is there. BBA (Benjamin_2D, 41 boards) bids slam
# on every one: mostly 5NT, which responder answers 6NT, or 7NT with a
# maximum; 6NT or 7NT directly with more.
after 2D (P) 3N (P)
  # 37 or more between us.
  7N  "Grand slam"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 37
      priority 3
  5N  "Slam: 6NT, or 7NT with a maximum"    shows hcp>=23
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
after 2D (P) 3N (P) 5N (P)
  7N  "A maximum: 12+ HCP"    shows hcp>=12
      priority 1
  6N  "6NT"

# ── Opener after the negative 2NT: natural ───────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2N (P)
  3C  "Five or more clubs"       shows C>=5
  3D  "Five or more diamonds"    shows D>=5
  3H  "Five or more hearts"      shows H>=5
  3S  "Five or more spades"      shows S>=5
  3N  "Balanced"                 shows balanced
      priority 1
  4N  "Balanced 28+: invites 6NT"   shows balanced, hcp>=28
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 2

# Responder after opener's suit over the negative: raise with three
# (agreeing it: opener's 24+ then asks for keycards), else 3NT.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3z (P) when z is not N
  4z  "Three or more {z}"    shows z>=3   sets trump=z
      when  z is H | z is S
      priority 1
  3N  "No fit"

# Benjamin twos: notes

## Decisions

- 2♣ = 22-23 (any shape), or unbalanced 20-23 with a good six-card suit
  or a 5-5/6-5 two-suiter and at most four losers. 2♦ = 24+, or 23
  without a five-card suit. These are BBA's ranges (Benjamin_2D corpus);
  Wikipedia and the PBS chat put game-in-hand hands (fewer HCP, a long
  solid suit) in 2♦, BBA opens them 2♣. We follow BBA here because the
  source gives no number for "game in hand".
- The strong 2♣ openings of strong-openings.bid are off (`!benjamin`).
- 2♣ keeps the strong 2♣'s machinery: game forcing, 2♦ waiting, the
  positives and the second negative. Benjamin's 2♣ is really forcing for
  one round and passable after opener's rebid; written that way, half of
  the continuations had no rule (no generic non-forcing structure after
  2♣–2♦–2M). Open: write the passable version.
- Responses to 2♦ (PBS chat, BBA): 2NT negative (0-6, no five-card
  major or six-card minor), 2♥/2♠ five+ and 3♣/3♦ six+ at any strength,
  3NT 7+ without them. After 2♦–2NT opener bids naturally (3NT
  balanced, 4NT 28+ quantitative).
- 2♦ also opens 22-23 with at most one loser (game in hand; BBA 4 of 4).
- Weak 2♦ off (preempts.bid).

## BBA (compare Benjamin_2D --limit 50, 2026-10-05: 76% of calls agree)

- Opening 1♠/1♣ vs our 2♣ (5 boards): BBA opens some 20-21 two-suiters
  at the one level; don't care.
- 2♦–P: BBA's thresholds for the positives differ a little: don't care.
- The scenario's card (21GF-PolishTwoSuiters) also plays Polish
  two-suiters and Namyats.

## Convention score (2026-10-07)

`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only benjamin` (Benjamin_2D, NS with Benjamin
on and off, BBA and us): poor before, Rusty's gain -215, BBA's +52, net
-0.68 per changed board (393 boards). Our 2♦ auctions lost the slams
(and some games) that the strong 2♣ structure finds:

- **No rules after a positive.** Opener had nothing after 2♦–2♥/2♠/3♣/3♦
  and the base fallback bid 3NT, passed (2♦-2♥-3NT on boards with a
  grand slam). Now opener raises with three (agreeing the suit, so the
  keycard ask follows), shows a five-card suit, or bids notrump;
  responder raises opener's suit with three, rebids a six-card major or
  a seven-card minor, else notrump.
- **2♦–3NT was passed** with 24+ facing 7+. BBA bids slam on all 41
  corpus boards, mostly 5NT ("6NT, or 7NT with a maximum"). Now: 7NT
  with 37 between us, else 5NT; responder bids 7NT with 12+.
- **The positives had a 5 HCP floor** read from the chat's 2♣
  responses. The chat gives none for 2♦ ("2♥/♠ 5+♥/♠", "2NT 5- HCP, no
  5-card major"), and BBA bids every five-card major from 0 HCP. So a
  weak five-card major bid 2NT and the fit was lost.
- **Weak raises.** After 2♦–2M–3M responder with 0-5 bids 4M (fast
  arrival); opener over 4M (and over 2♦–2NT–3M–4M) passes with three
  losers or more (BBA: asked on 4 of 4 with two or fewer, passed 5 of 6
  with three or more), else the keycard ask.
- Game-in-hand 22-23s (one loser) open 2♦, as BBA does.

| | Rusty's gain | BBA's gain | net / changed board | halves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | -215 | +52 | -0.68 (393) | agree |
| after | +109 | +52 | +0.14 (393) | agree (+47/+10) |

Background (Benjamin_2D, vs BBA by par): -726 -> -402 IMPs (-1.45 ->
-0.80 a board). What is left is slam bidding after the 2♦ positives
(responder's cue-bids on weak hands, keycard answers with five
keycards) and the opening split between 2♣ and 2♦.

## Open questions

- Should 2♣ be passable after 2♣–2♦–2M / 2NT (true Benjamin)? We keep
  the game force for now.
- Game-in-hand hands with fewer than 24 HCP: 2♦ (Wikipedia) or 2♣ (BBA)?
  We follow BBA: 2♣, except 22-23 with one loser or none, which BBA
  opens 2♦ too (2026-10-07).

## Sources

- Wikipedia, "Benjamin Twos", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Twos:
  the meanings of 2♣ and 2♦.
- Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `btn/Benjamin_2D.btn` (the responses to
  2♦: no strength floor for the suit positives) and
  `bba/Benjamin_2D.pbn` (ranges; BBA's 3NT positive from 7, the 5NT
  slam after it, the loser count over a weak game raise: corpus counts
  above, 2026-10-07).
- Where we differ: the 2♦ continuations after a positive are our own
  (natural, the slam modules decide); BBA cue-bids more.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Standard Blackwood: 4NT asks for aces once a trump suit is agreed. The
# answers count aces only; keycards(N) is aces without a trump king.

module blackwood "Blackwood (standard)"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/blackwood
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/blackwood
  skill  partnership_bidding/blackwood
  param  style = bidding_conventions/control_bids:style default first_or_second_round
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Rick's ruling:
#
#   Slam asks isn't about 18 -- what has partner shown? It's more about
#   33+ combined points, where in a suit contract the player with fewer
#   trumps gets to switch to short-suit points -- 1 for a doubleton, 3
#   for a singleton, 5 for a void, capped by number of trumps held. When
#   the slam asker has unprotected suits, we will normally use control
#   bids before keycard, and stop in game if there is a suit unprotected
#   in both hands.
#
# So the test is **33 combined support points with the agreed suit as
# trump**, `we.tp(trump)`: my exact count plus the range a raise recorded
# for partner. It replaces `tp(trump) + partner.hcp.max`, which was a
# workaround from before raises showed support points. The evidence
# behind the boundaries is in slam-catch.notes.md.
#
# Two branches, because partner's range is read from a different end.
#
# 1. **Partner is limited** (a raise, a limit raise) and nothing has
#    forced us to game. Partner has shown a top as well as a bottom, and
#    the only other call on offer is game, so the ask carries the whole
#    decision and 33 is measured against partner's maximum:
#    `we.tp(trump).max >= 33`. With it, the hand must play for twelve
#    tricks opposite a minimum (`losers <= 4`) and must not have **two
#    bare side suits** -- two or more cards with neither the ace nor the
#    king, where the first two tricks can go. That last test replaces
#    `controls >= 7`: it says which suit is the problem rather than
#    counting. One bare suit is allowed, because a raise facing it will
#    usually hold something there; two is where partner cannot cover
#    both. BBA draws the same line: over `1S P 2S P` and `1S P 3S P` on
#    the Basic-Bridge card it asks with none or one bare suit (272
#    boards) and never with two.
#
# 2. **We are already forced to game.** Partner's range has no top, so
#    `we.tp(trump).max` says nothing; what is known is partner's floor.
#    33 between us on that floor is the test, and where the trump
#    agreement recorded no support points for partner the fallback is my
#    own 18, a game force being worth about 13 (`slam_values`, named in
#    slam-entry.bid with the other shared conditions). Here the
#    ask ranks *behind* the system's descriptive calls: shortness, a
#    second suit and a control bid all say more than 4NT does, and the
#    ask is what is left when they are used up.
#
# When the card plays control bids (`slam.cue_bids.play`), a hand with a
# bare suit goes to `control-bids.bid` first and comes back here only
# once partner has shown a control.

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  slam_values_limited     # 33 facing partner's maximum
      when  !two_bare_suits  # and no two bare side suits
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control   # after a control dialogue its own rules decide
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  slam_values  # 33 on partner's floor, or 18 of my own
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1                      # after any natural 4NT

# A fit known but not agreed (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 1): partner's
# game raise, his preempt, a transfer completed. No rule set `trump`, so
# the asks above never saw it. The ask agrees the major on the way.
# Majors only for now: the sign-offs after an answer are awkward in a
# minor.
when we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid   # uncontested for now: in competition it cost
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  shown_fit(S), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

# The keycard suit when no rule has set the one we play in (Rick,
# 2026-10-03; `kc_open`, slam-entry.bid): a suit agreed by what we have
# shown, else, with no notrump bid by us, the last suit we bid
# (1H-1S-2H-4NT asks for aces with hearts agreed). The ask sets it as
# trump. As in rkcb-1430.bid.
when we.trump is none, !asked, !they.bid
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(S), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(S).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(H), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(H).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♦: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(D), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(D).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(D), !two_bare_beside(D)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=D, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♣: how many aces?"
      when  kc_open(C), !shown_fit(S), !shown_fit(H), we.fit(C).min >= 8, fit_slam_values(C), !two_bare_beside(C)
      when  hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30   # a minor slam needs the high cards (rebids.test: 17 facing a preference)
      sets  trump=C, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority -1

# A minor set as trump, and a major agreed since (Rick, 2026-10-03): the
# major is trump.
when minor_given_way, !asked
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♠: how many aces?"
      when  major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(S), !two_bare_beside(S)
      sets  trump=S, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1
  4N  "Blackwood, agreeing ♥: how many aces?"
      when  major_over_minor(H), !major_over_minor(S), fit_slam_values(H), !two_bare_beside(H)
      sets  trump=H, ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 1

# After a control-bid exchange (`control-bids.bid`, when the card plays
# them). `asked control(t)` is partner's control bid; `answered control(u)`
# says partner was answering mine, so I am the hand that opened the
# dialogue and the one that takes charge. Above it, the stop-in-game rule
# at priority 20 has already ruled out a suit bare in both hands; below
# it, any control still to show outranks the ask.

# In a control-bid dialogue (control-bids.bid): ask once every side suit
# is covered -- a control of mine, one partner has cued, or one I denied
# that partner has promised by bidding on. A control bid below game still
# comes first (priority 12), the ask before one past game (10).
when we.trump is suit, asked control(t)
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  all_covered
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 11

when we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4{trump}
  4N  "Blackwood: how many aces?"
      when  all_covered_by_us
      sets  ask=aces
      artificial
      priority 15

when asked aces
  5C  "0 or 4 aces"                    shows keycards(N) in 0|4  artificial
  5D  "1 ace"                          shows keycards(N)=1       artificial
  5H  "2 aces"                         shows keycards(N)=2       artificial
  5S  "3 aces"                         shows keycards(N)=3       artificial

# The asker places the contract: slam with at most one ace missing,
# otherwise five of the trump suit (or pass when that is the answer).
when answered aces
  # The king ask (`slam.king_ask.style = five_nt`, 2026-10-05): all four aces
  # are ours and the grand turns on the kings.
  5N        "King ask: all the aces held"
            when kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(N)=4
            sets ask=kings(N)
            artificial
            priority 1
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when we.keycards(N)>=3
  P         "To play"
            when partner.last=5{trump}, we.keycards(N).max<=2
  5{trump}  "Signoff"
            when we.keycards(N).max<=2
  # "0 or 4" facing no ace of my own is four.
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when maybe we.keycards(N)>=3
            priority -1

# The king ask by 5NT: the number of kings by steps from 6♣ (6NT four),
# as ACBL's SAYC booklet. Kings are controls less two for each ace.
define bw_kings = controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N)

when kstyle is five_nt, asked kings(N)
  6C  "No king"       shows bw_kings = 0   artificial
  6D  "One king"      shows bw_kings = 1   artificial
  6H  "Two kings"     shows bw_kings = 2   artificial
  6S  "Three kings"   shows bw_kings = 3   artificial
  6N  "Four kings"    shows bw_kings = 4   artificial

# The asker: the grand with every king between us, or with three and 33
# HCP on partner's floor; else six, or 6NT when the answer has passed six
# of our suit.
define partner_kings = (partner.last = 6D) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6H) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6S) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N) + (partner.last = 6N)

when kstyle is five_nt, answered kings(N)
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when bw_kings + partner_kings >= 4
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when bw_kings + partner_kings >= 3, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
  P         "To play"
            when partner.last = 6{trump}
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
  6N        "Small slam"

# blackwood (`blackwood.bid`): notes

Standard Blackwood (card `slam.blackwood.play`, the Basic-Bridge card):
4NT asks for aces once a trump suit is agreed; 5♣ 0 or 4, 5♦ 1, 5♥ 2, 5♠ 3.
The asker bids six with at most one ace missing, else signs off in five
(passing an answer in the trump suit). Cases: `blackwood.test`.

Added because BBA asks with 4NT on the Basic card and our side used to pass
the ask. Aces are `keycards(N)`: keycards with no trump king, four in the
deck, so "0 or 4" resolves against the asker's own aces.

## When to ask

The two-branch test in the `# The ask` block is shared with
`rkcb-1430.bid` and is written up once in **`slam-catch.notes.md`**, with
the BBA evidence behind the boundaries. It is Rick's rule: **33 combined
support points** with the agreed suit as trump, read against partner's
maximum when partner is limited and against partner's floor in a game
force, plus at most four losers and **no two bare side suits**.

`we.tp(trump)` is what makes the combined count sayable at all; before a
raise recorded support points the rule had to use `partner.hcp.max`. The
bare-suit test replaced `controls >= 7`, which counted top cards without
knowing which suit could lose the first two tricks; on the Basic-Bridge
card BBA draws the same line (272 boards asked with none or one bare
suit, none with two).

Basic-Bridge has `Cue bid = 0`, so `control-bids.bid` is not loaded and
4NT is still the whole of the slam machinery on this card. The
`asked control(t), answered control(u)` rule is there for a card that
plays standard Blackwood *and* control bids; no corpus card does.

## Gaps

- The 5NT king ask (card `slam.king_ask.five_nt`) and grand slams.
- **The queen ask.** After 4NT-5C ("0 or 4") BBA asks for the trump queen
  with the next step (5D, alerted "spades queen ask"), and the answer
  names a king as well ("!S queen and !C king"); it then places the
  contract. We bid six directly on the ace count. 55 boards, -30 IMPs
  against par. `slam.rkcb.queen_ask` exists in the field registry but
  no `.bbsa` key is mapped to it, so it cannot be switched on from a
  corpus card yet.

## Shared conditions named in slam-entry.bid (2026-09-30)

The long conditions of blackwood.bid (up to 1,300 characters a line) are now
named conditions in `slam/slam-entry.bid`: `slam_values`,
`slam_values_limited`, `controlled(x)`, `first_round(x)`,
`side_suit_uncontrolled`, `two_bare_suits`, `denials_promised`,
`all_covered` and their variants. Each is exactly the condition it
replaced; a definition reads `style` from slam-entry.bid, which names the
same card field and default (`slam.cue_bids.style`,
`first_or_second_round`). The full corpus bids identically
(docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 0). `two_bare_suits` uses the new
`bare(x)` (a side suit of 2+ cards without the ace or king), which, like
`has`, is not recorded when a call is read, so the ask's negative
inference is unchanged; `bare_suits <= 1` would say the same but would
add that denial, a change to measure on its own.

## A fit known but not agreed (2026-09-30)

With no trump suit set, a public fit in a major (eight shown between us,
or partner's six-card suit) and slam values on partner's floor (or his
top when he has limited his hand, as a preempt does), 4NT agrees the
major and asks (`sets trump=x`). Uncontested only. Evidence and figures:
slam-entry.notes.md, "Phase 1".

## The keycard suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)

The same rulings as rkcb-1430.notes.md, "The keycard suit": with no
notrump bid by us 4NT asks for aces with the agreed suit, else the last
suit our side bid, agreed by the ask (1H-1S-2C-4NT on the Basic-Bridge
card: aces, clubs agreed; it was quantitative); a major agreed after a
minor was set replaces it. The rules mirror rkcb-1430.bid's.

## The 5NT king ask (2026-10-05)

With `slam.king_ask.five_nt`, 5NT after the answer promises all four
aces and asks for kings by number: 6♣ none up to 6NT four. Seven with
every king between us, or three and 33 HCP on partner's floor.

## Sources

- **The convention:** standard (plain) Blackwood with the usual ace
  answers, as the Basic-Bridge card plays it. Standard practice, not yet
  cited to a book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** when to ask (33 combined support points, the
  two-branch test, no two bare side suits), 2026-09-23; written up in
  `slam-catch.notes.md` and quoted in `control-bids.notes.md`.
- **BBA evidence:** BBA's asks on the Basic-Bridge card (272 boards asked
  with none or one bare side suit, none with two), re-bid with
  `bba-cli --all-meanings`, and the `rbb probe` boundary hands, all in
  `slam-catch.notes.md` "Evidence". No `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** the queen-ask gap (55 boards, -30 IMPs).
- **Where we differ:** no queen ask after 4NT-5♣, where BBA asks for the
  trump queen with the next step (Gaps).
- **Rick's rulings, 2026-10-03:** the keycard suit, as rkcb-1430.notes.md.
- **The king ask, 2026-10-05:** ACBL SAYC booklet (5NT asks for kings,
  promising all the aces; answers by number). Grand thresholds ours,
  standard practice not yet cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Checkback Stayman: after opener's 1NT rebid, responder's 2C is
# artificial, invitational or better, and asks about three-card support
# for responder's major and four cards in an unbid major, whichever minor
# was opened. Opener: 2D denies both, two of responder's major shows
# three, two of the other major shows four. Played instead of NMF
# (new-minor-forcing.bid switches off when this is on). See
# checkback.notes.md.

module checkback "Checkback Stayman"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/checkback
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/checkback

after 1x (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) when !tw(x)
  2C  "Checkback: invitational or better, asks about the majors"   alert
      shows M>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4), points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=checkback
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P) when !tw(C)
  2C  "Checkback: invitational+, asks for a 4-card major"   alert
      shows H>=4 | S>=4, points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=checkback
      artificial
      priority 1

# Opener's answers. Over a minor opening: three of responder's major
# first, then four hearts after a 1S response (1NT over 1H denies four
# spades). After 1H-1S-1NT: three spades or 2D.
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) when !tw(m)
  2M  "Three {M}"                          shows M=3
  2H  "Four hearts, not three spades"      shows H>=4, S<=2
      when  M is S
  2D  "No three {M}, no four-card major to show"   artificial
      priority -1
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 1N (P) 2C (P)
  2S  "Three spades"                       shows S=3
  2D  "Not three spades"                   artificial
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) when !tw(C)
  2H  "Four hearts"                        shows H>=4
  2S  "Four spades, not four hearts"       shows S>=4, H<=3
  2D  "No four-card major"                 shows H<=3, S<=3   artificial
      priority -1

# Responder places the contract: with a fit (five opposite three, or
# four-four), invite with 3M or bid game; without one 2NT invites and 3NT
# is game.
when answered checkback
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"              shows points>=13, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets trump=H
  3H  "Invitational, heart fit"            shows points=11..12, H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets trump=H, ask=invite(H)
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"              shows points>=13, S>=5 | (S>=4, partner.S.min>=4)   when partner.S>=3   sets trump=S
  3S  "Invitational, spade fit"            shows points=11..12, S>=5 | (S>=4, partner.S.min>=4)   when partner.S>=3   sets trump=S, ask=invite(S)
  3N  "Game, no fit"                       shows points>=13
      priority -1
  2N  "Invitational, no fit"               shows points=11..12   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1

# checkback (`checkback.bid`): notes

Checkback Stayman, card field `other_conventions.checkback.play` (on in
21GF-GIB-Bergen and 21GF-PolishTwoSuiters, both without NMF). Cases:
`checkback.test`.

## Structure

- After 1x-1y-1NT, 2♣ is artificial, invitational or better (11+ total
  points): five of responder's major, or both majors; after 1♣-1♦-1NT, a
  four-card major. Ranked ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT, as NMF.
- Opener: two of responder's major with three; after a 1♠ response four
  hearts (2♥); after 1♣-1♦ either four-card major; else 2♦.
- Responder: with a fit (5-3, 4-4) 3M invites and 4M is game; without one
  2NT invites and 3NT is game. Opener answers the invitations in
  rebids.bid.
- On, it switches off NMF and the natural 2♣ after 1NT
  (responder-rebids.bid).

## Open questions

- No minimum/maximum split in opener's answers (Bridge Bum has none at
  this step); some partnerships play 2♦ = minimum. Not built.
- No PBS scenario plays Checkback on the NS card, so there is no corpus
  check; cases only.

## Sources

- **Bridge Bum, "Checkback Stayman"**
  (https://www.bridgebum.com/checkback_stayman.php): 2♣ after the 1NT
  rebid, invitational or better; 2♦ denies, 2M shows three, the other
  major four.
- **Where we differ:** responder's 2♣ needs five of the major or both
  majors (a four-card major alone bids notrump); Bridge Bum allows any
  invitational hand. Standard practice, not yet cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Control bids: with a trump suit agreed and slam in the air, name a suit
# you can control instead of asking for keycards straight away. Rick's
# rulings:
#
#   When the slam asker has unprotected suits, we will normally use
#   control bids before keycard, and stop in game if there is a suit
#   unprotected in both hands.
#
# So this is the branch that runs *before* the ask in `blackwood.bid` /
# `rkcb-1430.bid`, whenever the card plays control bids and the asker has
# a suit it cannot control on its own. It is gated on the card:
# `slam.cue_bids.play` is BBA's own `Cue bid` key, off on Basic-Bridge
# (which is why BBA blasts 4NT there) and on for the 21GF cards.
#
# No auction patterns: like the rest of slam/, the rules key on
# `we.trump`, `we.forcing` and the control-bid dialogue itself.

module control-bids "Control bids before the keycard ask"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/control_bids
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/control_bids
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding
  param  style = style default first_or_second_round

# ── The treatment (Rick, 2026-09-25) ─────────────────────────────────
#
#   In a game force with a suit agreed, new non-jump bids below game are
#   control bids. You bid the cheapest control you can show; any suit you
#   skip over you are denying. Partner then shows the cheapest control
#   they have. If either player skips (denies) a suit and the other
#   continues control bidding, they are promising a control in the
#   skipped suit. Standard control bids are aces and voids; the
#   first-and-second-round treatment, more common now, shows an ace, king,
#   singleton or void. Control bidding past game shows first-round
#   control. A singleton or void in partner's own suit is not shown.
#
# `style` is the card's choice: `first_round` (aces and voids) or
# `first_or_second_round` (the default). "Partner's own suit" is one
# partner has shown four or more of.
#
# The engine keeps the dialogue: each ladder call (`sets ladder=control`)
# records the suits it skipped as denied by its bidder
# (`partner.denied(x)`, `me.denied(x)`) and the suit it names as cued
# (`partner.cued(x)`). `cheapest(x)` is the non-jump bid; `under_game(x)`
# says whether it is still below game; `prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(x)`
# picks the cheapest of the controls I hold.
#
# Majors only (Rick, 2026-09-25): "we don't usually use control bids for
# minors". With a minor agreed, new suits show stoppers on the way to 3NT
# (responder-rebids.bid).
#
# ── Opening the dialogue ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The values are the ask's own (slam-catch.notes.md): 33 support points
# between us, or 18 of my own facing a game force. What sends the hand
# here rather than straight to 4NT is a side suit I cannot control.

when we.trump is suit, !asked, !answered control, (trump is H | trump is S), we.forcing = game
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  slam_values, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12

# Over a limited raise: partner has shown a top as well as a bottom, so
# 33 is measured against partner's maximum, and the control bid forces
# to game itself.

when we.trump is suit, !asked, !answered control, (trump is H | trump is S), (we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  slam_values_limited, side_suit_uncontrolled, controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control, forcing=game
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12

# ── Answering a control bid ───────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Show the cheapest control I have, promising every suit partner has
# denied; past game, first-round controls only. With no such call, sign
# off in game: that is also where a suit denied by both hands leaves us.
# When every side suit is covered the keycard ask comes first
# (blackwood.bid, rkcb-1430.bid).

when we.trump is suit, asked control(t), (trump is H | trump is S)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), under_game(C)
      when  controlled(C), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 12
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), under_game(D)
      when  controlled(D), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 12
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), under_game(H)
      when  controlled(H), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 12
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), under_game(S)
      when  controlled(S), denials_promised
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 12
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), !under_game(C), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(C) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(C) < 28)
      when  first_round(C), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 10
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), !under_game(D), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(D) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(D) < 28)
      when  first_round(D), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 10
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), !under_game(H), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(H) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(H) < 28)
      when  first_round(H), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 10
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), !under_game(S), !kb_spade_ask, (trump is H, cheapest_rank(S) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(S) < 28)
      when  first_round(S), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 10
  4{trump}  "Signoff: no further control"
      sets  ladder=control
      priority -5
  5{trump}  "Signoff: no further control"
      priority -6

# ── Partner signed off in game ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Partner bid game over my control bid, denying what it skipped. I may
# still go on past game with first-round controls, promising every suit
# partner has denied; otherwise pass.

# Not when I bypassed a suit myself: partner's sign-off says he cannot
# cover it, and no control of mine past game can (2026-09-30; the case
# surfaced when slam_values moved to 32).
when we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4{trump}, (trump is H | trump is S), !me.denied(C), !me.denied(D), !me.denied(H), !me.denied(S)
  cheapest(C)  "Control bid in ♣: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not C, !partner.cued(C), !me.cued(C), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(C) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(C) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(C), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 10
  cheapest(D)  "Control bid in ♦: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not D, !partner.cued(D), !me.cued(D), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(D) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(D) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(D), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 10
  cheapest(H)  "Control bid in ♥: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not H, !partner.cued(H), !me.cued(H), (trump is H, cheapest_rank(H) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(H) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(H), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 10
  cheapest(S)  "Control bid in ♠: first-round control"  alert
      when  trump is not S, !partner.cued(S), !me.cued(S), !kb_spade_ask, (trump is H, cheapest_rank(S) < 27) | (trump is S, cheapest_rank(S) < 28)
      when  slam_values, first_round(S), denials_promised_first
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 10
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2

# control-bids (`control-bids.bid`): notes

Control bids: with a trump suit agreed and slam in the air, name a suit
you can control instead of asking for keycards straight away. Cases:
`control-bids.test`. The decision to start the dialogue at all is the
ask's own decision, written up in `slam-catch.notes.md`.

## Rick's rulings (2026-09-23)

- **A singleton is a control and protects the suit.** What a control bid
  guards against is the defenders cashing the ace and king of a side
  suit; keycard makes sure they cannot cash two aces, and controls check
  for the top two in one suit. So "bare" means two or more cards with
  neither the ace nor the king — a singleton or void is not bare.
- **Control-bid when there is room and we have an open suit**, rather
  than asking straight away.
- **The answerer keeps showing controls** for now, with no extra values
  required. Serious and Non-Serious 3NT will divide those hands later.

## Guidance

Rick's ruling, which this module and the ask both implement:

> Slam asks isn't about 18 — what has partner shown? It's more about
> **33+ combined points**, where in a suit contract the player with
> **fewer trumps** gets to switch to short-suit points — 1 for a
> doubleton, 3 for a singleton, 5 for a void, **capped by number of
> trumps held**. When the slam asker has **unprotected suits**, we will
> normally use **control bids before keycard**, and **stop in game if
> there is a suit unprotected in both hands**.

Three things follow, and this file holds the second and the third.

## The card

`slam.cue_bids.play` is BBA's own `Cue bid` key: **0 on Basic-Bridge, 1
on the 21GF cards**. That is why BBA blasts 4NT on the basic card and
cue-bids on the others, and it is why the whole module is `card
slam.cue_bids.play` — on Basic-Bridge nothing here is loaded and the ask
behaves exactly as before.

`slam.cue_bids.style` chooses what a control bid promises:

| Option | Promises |
|---|---|
| `first_round` | the ace or a void |
| `first_or_second_round` (default) | also the king or a singleton |

No `.bbsa` key maps to `style`, so every corpus card gets the default.
That default is right for BBA: of **1024 control bids** in
`Slam_After_Major_Fit`, `Jacoby_2N` and `Splinters` (21GF-DEFAULT,
`bba-cli --all-meanings`), every one held the ace, the king, a singleton
or a void of the suit named. Two held three small cards and **none held
a bare doubleton**, which is why a doubleton is not a control here
either, even under `first_or_second_round`.

## A bare suit

A side suit is **bare** when I hold two or more cards in it and neither
the ace nor the king: the first two tricks can go there. It is the same
test everywhere in `slam/` — it gates the ask (no two bare suits), it
sends a hand here rather than to 4NT (one bare suit), and it is what
"unprotected in both hands" is measured with.

## The ladder

The cheapest suit I can control, above the last bid: **3♠** (hearts
agreed, over partner's 3♥), then **4♣, 4♦, 4♥, 4♠**, skipping the trump
suit, whose four level is the sign-off. The priorities (14 down to 10)
put the calls in bidding order, so skipping a suit denies a control in
it, and the engine's ranking does the rest.

That is BBA's structure. From `1S P 2N P 3S P` it cue-bids 4♣ 23, 4♦ 9,
4♥ 6, 4♠ 2 and bids 3NT 9 times; from `1H P 2N P 3H P` it bids 3♠ 36
times; and with hearts agreed it goes on **past game** — `1H P 2N P 3C P
3H P` → 4♦, then → 4♠ — treating 4♥ as the sign-off rather than a step
on the ladder.

`4S` carries `!game_reached`. Without it, hearts agreed and partner
having already bid 4♥, we bid 4♠ as a "control bid" over partner's game:
107 passed-out artificial contracts on the slam scenarios before that
guard went in.

## Stop in game when a suit is unprotected in both hands

The rule at priority 20, above everything else in the dialogue.

Partner's control bid in `t` is partner's *cheapest* control, so partner
has denied every side suit below `t` that was available, and will never
bid one of them again. Two cases, and they are not symmetric:

- **Partner opened the dialogue** (`!answered control`): everything
  below `t` was available. A bare suit of mine below `t` is bare in both
  hands, so game is the limit.
- **Partner is answering my own control bid in `u`**: only the suits
  *between* `u` and `t` were available to partner, and those are the
  ones now known to be bare in both. My own bare suits below `u` are
  **not**: partner bid on knowing I had denied them, which promises
  cover there. Reading it symmetrically would make every dialogue I open
  end in game, since I bid my cheapest control and therefore always have
  a bare suit below it.

When the dialogue has already gone past 4{trump} the sign-off is
5{trump}, at priority 19, so the four level is taken whenever it is
still legal.

`P` at priority 2 closes the other side of it: partner bid game in the
agreed suit over my control bid, which is the sign-off, so I pass.

## What we could not express

- **A suit below the first control bid of the whole dialogue.** Nobody
  can name it — it was never available — so neither the stop rule nor
  anything else can tell whether it is covered. The keycard ask has to
  settle it, and it only counts aces. This is the real hole, and it is
  the same hole a human cue-bidding pair has.
- **Partner's holdings.** `partner.has(A,x)` and `partner.stop(x)` are
  always *unknown*: the knowledge store keeps `has` and `stop` as
  constraints but answers no questions about them (LANGUAGE §12). So
  everything partner knows about controls has to travel as the
  control-bid state (`ask=control(x)`), not as knowledge, and only
  partner's **latest** control bid is remembered, not the whole history.
  A dialogue longer than two rounds loses its earlier steps.
- **"The cheapest control"** is written as five calls with descending
  priorities rather than `cheapest(x)` with a suit variable, because
  `cheapest(x)` needs `x` bound and an unbound suit variable in a call
  expands to four *candidates* whose order is then decided by
  descriptiveness — which for four near-identical `shows` is sample
  noise, not bidding order.
- **Minors.** The module is majors only (`trump is H | trump is S`), like
  the sign-off in `slam-catch.bid`: five of a minor is a different
  conversation and "3NT or five of the minor" was never settled.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- **BBA control-bids on far more hands than we do.** After `1S P 2N P 3S
  P` it cue-bids on 40 of 49 boards — essentially whenever a Jacoby 2NT
  auction reaches the three level, whatever the values. We control-bid
  only with the ask's own values (33 combined support points) *and* a
  bare suit, which is Rick's ruling. On the slam scenarios this is worth
  about 0.3 points of call agreement and nothing measurable in IMPs.
- **BBA continues the ladder where we sign off, and the reverse.** After
  `1H P 2N P 3N P 4C P` BBA bids 4♥ with a minimum balanced hand; we bid
  the next control if we hold one. Gating the *answering* ladder on the
  same values made the whole thing worse (contract agreement 40.0% →
  39.5%, −330 IMPs on the slam scenarios), so it is left alone.
- **BBA does not always read game in the agreed suit as a sign-off.**
  `Jacoby_2N` board 394: 1♥ – 2NT – 3♥ – 3♠ – 4♥, and BBA's next call is
  4NT, reaching 6♥. Our `P` rule treats 4♥ there as the stop. That is
  Rick's rule, and the cost is real but small.

## Open questions for Rick

1. **Does a singleton count as unprotected?** Here it does not: a small
   singleton is one fast loser, and under `first_or_second_round` it is
   a control. So `AKQ952.A.AQ865.5` has no bare suit and goes straight
   to 4NT where BBA cue-bids 4♣.
2. **Is one bare suit facing a limited raise really enough to ask?** The
   ask allows one, and BBA's Basic-Bridge behaviour agrees (272 boards
   asked with none or one, never with two), but it is the loosest of the
   three tests.
3. **Should the answerer need values to continue the ladder?** BBA's
   answerer signs off in game with a minimum; ours shows any control it
   holds. Measuring says leave it, bridge says otherwise.

## For Rick: control bids stop in game too often (2026-09-25)

A removal screen of the convention modules found control-bids.bid net
negative: without it, +427 by distance and +890 IMPs to the bidding side
(451 boards). Almost all of it is game against slam:

| With control bids | Without | Boards | IMPs, for the version without |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4H | 6H | 65 | +559 |
| 4S | 6S | 45 | +307 |
| 5H | 6H | 17 | +164 |

Some of these stops are right, e.g. 1N_5M_and_6m 84, where 6H goes
down on the club lead. The rest stop in game with slam making, which
points at "stop in game if a suit is unprotected in both hands" firing
too often. Suspects: what counts as bare, and whether a control bid by
partner is read as covering the suit. Not changed, as it is your
ruling; worth a look with the examples.

## Fixed: denial by bypassing (2026-09-25, Rick: "that is the actual bridge meaning")

**The cause.** The stop-in-game rule read partner's control bid in `t` as
denying every side suit below `t`. A control bid denies only the suits
it bypassed: those a control bid was available in, between the previous
bid and partner's, on the ladder. Two failures:
- Over our 3H, partner's 3S denies nothing. We read it as denying both
  minors (1NT-2D-2H-3C-3H-3S-4H on 18 boards; responder held the
  minors).
- After 1S-2NT-3C, 4C bypasses nothing: the ladder starts at 4C when
  spades are trumps.

**The engine.** New terms: `partner.bypassed(x)`, optionally with the
ladder's start, `partner.bypassed(x, 3S)`; and `me.last`
(docs/LANGUAGE.md). The stop rule now asks whether I am bare in a suit
partner bypassed. 3S is on the ladder only directly over our 3H.

**Two follow-ons:**
- **Going past game** with a control bid (4S over hearts) needs my own
  cover in each minor partner has not shown. Without it, 4H lets
  partner continue. Test 37 keeps its 4H for this reason.
- **Asking when everything is covered:** when partner opened the
  dialogue and every side suit is covered, by me or by partner's
  control bid, ask for keycards (blackwood.bid, rkcb-1430.bid). Before,
  that hand signed off in game after Jacoby 2NT.

**Results against the rules before** (146 boards):
- Distance from par: +460.
- IMPs to the bidding side: +739.
- Corpus par: -156,610 -> -156,150.

Against no control bids at all, the gap fell from +427 / +890 to +45 /
+279 (distance / to the side). What is left is the ladder's own limit:
a suit below the first control bid of the dialogue can't be shown, so a
hand that holds it may still stop in game.

## Rewritten to Rick's description (2026-09-25)

Rick: "In a GF and a suit agreed on, new non-jump bids below game are
control bids. You bid the cheapest control you can show; any you skip
over you are denying. Partner then shows the cheapest control they
have. If either player skips (denies) a control in a suit and the other
continues control bidding, they are promising a control in the skipped
suit. Standard control bids are aces and voids; first- and second-round
controls (A, K, singleton, void) are more common now. Control bidding
past game shows first-round control. We don't normally show a singleton
or void in partner's suit." Also: control bids start only once a suit is
agreed.

What the module does now:
- **Every non-jump new suit below game is on the ladder** (`cheapest(x)`,
  `under_game(x)`). It no longer starts above three of the trump suit.
  The cheapest control held is chosen (`prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(x)`).
- **The engine keeps the dialogue.** Each ladder call records what it
  skipped (`denied`) and named (`cued`). Continuing promises a control
  in every suit partner has denied; with no call that keeps the
  promise, the hand signs off in game. That replaces the old "bare in
  both hands" rule.
- **Past game, first-round controls only.**
- **No shortness control in a suit partner has shown** (four or more).
- **`style`:** `first_round` or `first_or_second_round` (default), as
  before.
- **Order:** a control bid below game; the keycard ask once every side
  suit is covered (mine, cued by partner, or denied by me and promised
  by partner); a control bid past game; the sign-off.

Test 25 changed: KJ.AJ864.Q7.AJ72 after 1H-2NT-3H-4D now asks with
4NT. 4S past game would promise first-round control, and every suit is
covered.

**Results:**

| Against | Distance from par | IMPs to the bidding side |
|---|---|---|
| The bypassed fix (earlier today) | +159 | +236 |
| No control bids at all | control bids now ahead by 114 | 41 behind (was 427 / 890 behind this morning) |

What is left is mostly spade Jacoby auctions (1S-2NT, 118 boards).

## Shared conditions named in slam-entry.bid (2026-09-30)

The long conditions of control-bids.bid (up to 1,300 characters a line) are now
named conditions in `slam/slam-entry.bid`: `slam_values`,
`slam_values_limited`, `controlled(x)`, `first_round(x)`,
`side_suit_uncontrolled`, `two_bare_suits`, `denials_promised`,
`all_covered` and their variants. Each is exactly the condition it
replaced; a definition reads `style` from slam-entry.bid, which names the
same card field and default (`slam.cue_bids.style`,
`first_or_second_round`). The full corpus bids identically
(docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 0). `two_bare_suits` uses the new
`bare(x)` (a side suit of 2+ cards without the ace or king), which, like
`has`, is not recorded when a call is read, so the ask's negative
inference is unchanged; `bare_suits <= 1` would say the same but would
add that denial, a change to measure on its own.

## Sources

- **The convention:** control (cue) bids once a suit is agreed in a game
  force, as Rick described them on 2026-09-25 ("Rewritten to Rick's
  description": the cheapest control first, skipping denies, past game
  shows first-round control). Beyond that description, standard practice,
  not yet cited to a book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** 2026-09-23 (a singleton is a control; control-bid
  when there is room and an open suit; the answerer keeps showing
  controls; 33+ combined points; stop in game when a suit is unprotected
  in both hands); 2026-09-25 (denial by bypassing is "the actual bridge
  meaning", and the description quoted above).
- **BBA evidence:** 1,024 control bids in Slam_After_Major_Fit, Jacoby_2N
  and Splinters on 21GF-DEFAULT, read with `bba-cli --all-meanings` (what
  a control promises); BBA's ladder after `1S P 2N P 3S P` and
  `1H P 2N P 3H P` ("The ladder"). No `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** the removal screen, the bypass fix and the
  rewrite (2026-09-25).
- **Where we differ:** BBA control-bids on far more hands, continues the
  ladder with a minimum, and sometimes bids on over game in the agreed
  suit ("Accepted differences from BBA").

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Exclusion Blackwood: with a suit agreed, a jump to the five level in a
# new suit shows a void there and asks for keycards outside it (the ace
# of the void suit does not count, so there are four). The answers are
# steps above the ask, 1430 style: first step 1 or 4, second 0 or 3,
# third 2 without the trump queen, fourth 2 with it. With
# `general.style=bba` the steps count 0, 1, 2, 3 and the ask need not be
# a jump (BBA's own treatment). Notes: exclusion.notes.md.

module exclusion "Exclusion Blackwood: a jump to five in a void asks for keycards outside it"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood
  param  gstyle = general.style
  param  dopi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:dopi default false
  param  ropi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:ropi default false

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A void in v (not the trump suit), the slam values of the keycard ask
# (`slam_values`, `slam_values_limited`: slam-entry.bid), and keycards
# enough that every answer leaves room: three of my own, or two when the
# answer "none" is still at or below five of our suit. Above the 4NT ask
# (priority 1); control bids, when the card plays them, come first.

# A jump: the cheapest bid in v is at the four level or lower. In BBA's
# style any five-level bid in v asks.
define ex_jump(v) = (v is C, cheapest_rank(C) <= 20) | (v is D, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21) | (v is H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 22) | (v is S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 23)
define ex_level(v) = ex_jump(v) | gstyle is bba

# The answer "no keycard" is at or below five of the trump suit: 1430's
# second step, BBA's first.
define ex_zero_room(v) = (gstyle is not bba, (v is C, trump is H | trump is S) | (v is D, trump is S)) | (gstyle is bba, (v is C, trump is not C) | (v is D, trump is H | trump is S) | (v is H, trump is S))
define ex_room(v) = keycards(trump) >= 3 | (keycards(trump) >= 2, ex_zero_room(v))

define ex_values = slam_values | slam_values_limited

when we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked
  5C  "Exclusion: ♣ void, how many keycards outside ♣?"  alert
      shows C=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not C, ex_level(C), ex_room(C)
      sets  ask=exclusion(C)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5D  "Exclusion: ♦ void, how many keycards outside ♦?"  alert
      shows D=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not D, ex_level(D), ex_room(D)
      sets  ask=exclusion(D)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5H  "Exclusion: ♥ void, how many keycards outside ♥?"  alert
      shows H=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not H, ex_level(H), ex_room(H)
      sets  ask=exclusion(H)
      artificial
      priority 12
  5S  "Exclusion: ♠ void, how many keycards outside ♠?"  alert
      shows S=0, ex_values
      when  trump is not S, ex_level(S), ex_room(S)
      sets  ask=exclusion(S)
      artificial
      priority 12

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Keycards outside the void suit: the trump king and the other three aces.
define ex_keys(v) = keycards(trump) - has(A,v)

when asked exclusion(v), rho.last = P, gstyle is not bba
  5D  "1 or 4 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "0 or 3 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is C
  5S  "2 keycards outside clubs, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is C
  5N  "2 keycards outside clubs and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "1 or 4 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is D
  5S  "0 or 3 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is D
  5N  "2 keycards outside diamonds, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is D
  6C  "2 keycards outside diamonds and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is D
  5S  "1 or 4 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "0 or 3 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is H
  6C  "2 keycards outside hearts, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is H
  6D  "2 keycards outside hearts and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "1 or 4 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when v is S
  6C  "0 or 3 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when v is S
  6D  "2 keycards outside spades, no {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, !has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is S
  6H  "2 keycards outside spades and the {trump} queen"   shows ex_keys(v) = 2, has(Q,trump)   artificial   when v is S

when asked exclusion(v), rho.last = P, gstyle is bba
  5D  "0 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is C
  5H  "1 keycard outside clubs"       shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is C
  5S  "2 keycards outside clubs"      shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is C

  6C  "3 keycards outside diamonds"   shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is D
  5S  "0 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is H
  5N  "1 keycard outside hearts"      shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is H
  6C  "2 keycards outside hearts"     shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is H

  5N  "0 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) = 0   artificial   when v is S
  6C  "1 keycard outside spades"      shows ex_keys(v) = 1   artificial   when v is S
  6D  "2 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) = 2   artificial   when v is S
  6H  "3 keycards outside spades"     shows ex_keys(v) >= 3  artificial   when v is S

# Over interference, DOPI and ROPI as for the keycard ask (dopi-ropi.bid):
# double or redouble the first step, pass the second; with two keycards
# or more, partner's and mine make a slam, so bid it.
when asked exclusion(v), dopi, rho_bid, rho.last <= 6S
  X   "DOPI: first step"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  P   "DOPI: second step"  shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  X   "DOPI: no keycard"   shows ex_keys(v) = 0      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
  P   "DOPI: one keycard"  shows ex_keys(v) = 1      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
when asked exclusion(v), ropi, rho.last = X
  XX  "ROPI: first step"   shows ex_keys(v) in 1|4   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  P   "ROPI: second step"  shows ex_keys(v) in 0|3   artificial   when gstyle is not bba   priority 5
  XX  "ROPI: no keycard"   shows ex_keys(v) = 0      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
  P   "ROPI: one keycard"  shows ex_keys(v) = 1      artificial   when gstyle is bba       priority 5
when asked exclusion(v), !rho.last = P
  6{trump}  "Small slam: two keycards outside the void"
      shows ex_keys(v) = 2
      priority 4

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The step partner answered with, by the ask's suit.
define ex_s1(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5D) | (v is D, partner.last = 5H) | (v is H, partner.last = 5S) | (v is S, partner.last = 5N)
define ex_s2(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5H) | (v is D, partner.last = 5S) | (v is H, partner.last = 5N) | (v is S, partner.last = 6C)
define ex_s3(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5S) | (v is D, partner.last = 5N) | (v is H, partner.last = 6C) | (v is S, partner.last = 6D)
define ex_s4(v) = (v is C, partner.last = 5N) | (v is D, partner.last = 6C) | (v is H, partner.last = 6D) | (v is S, partner.last = 6H)

# Partner's keycards outside the void, the low count where the step
# leaves two open (1430 "1 or 4" facing none of mine, "0 or 3" facing
# one: read low, as the keycard sign-off is). Over DOPI and ROPI the
# double (redouble) is the first step and the pass the second.
define ex_d1 = partner.last = X | partner.last = XX
define ex_d2 = partner.last = P
define ex_partner(v) = (gstyle is not bba, ex_s1(v) | ex_d1) + (gstyle is not bba, ex_s3(v) | ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is not bba, ex_s3(v) | ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s2(v) | ex_d2) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s3(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s3(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v)) + (gstyle is bba, ex_s4(v))
define ex_total(v) = keycards(trump) + ex_partner(v)

# The trump queen: mine, or 1430's fourth step.
define ex_queen(v) = has(Q,trump) | (gstyle is not bba, ex_s4(v))

when answered exclusion(v)
  7{trump}  "Grand slam"
            when  ex_total(v) >= 4, ex_queen(v)
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            when  ex_total(v) >= 3
  P         "Defend doubled: two keycards missing"
            when  ex_d1, partner.last = X, ex_total(v) <= 2
  X         "Penalty: two keycards missing"
            when  ex_d2, rho.last = P, lho_bid, lho.last >= 5C, lho.last <= 6S, ex_total(v) <= 2
  P         "To play"
            when  partner.last = 5{trump}, ex_total(v) <= 2
  5{trump}  "Signoff"
            when  ex_total(v) <= 2
  6{trump}  "Small slam"
            priority -1

# exclusion (`exclusion.bid`): notes

Exclusion Blackwood (2026-10-05), gated on `slam.exclusion_blackwood.play`
(on in 21GF-GIB, -GIB-Bergen, -SPECIALS2, -WJS-MSS, -PolishTwoSuiters,
Precision).

## What the rules do

- **The ask:** trumps agreed, a void in v (not trumps), the keycard ask's
  slam values (`slam_values | slam_values_limited`), and a **jump** to
  five in v (the cheapest bid in v was at the four level or lower).
  Priority 12: it outranks the 4NT ask and the splinter's own 4NT, and
  ties control bids, where it wins as the more descriptive call.
- **Room:** three keycards of my own, or two when the answer "none" is
  still at or below five of our suit, so a bad answer leaves a sign-off.
- **Answers:** 1430 steps excluding the void ace (four keycards: three
  aces and the trump king): 1 or 4, 0 or 3, 2 without the queen, 2 with.
  Over interference, DOPI/ROPI's first two steps (double/redouble,
  pass); with two keycards, bid six.
- **The asker:** seven with all four keycards and the queen, six with
  three, else five of our suit (pass when that was the answer); a
  double or a pass of partner's double when they interfered. An open
  count ("1 or 4" facing none, "0 or 3" facing one) is read low.
- **`general.style=bba`:** BBA's treatment, steps counting 0, 1, 2, 3
  ("1 out of 4" in its notes) and any five-level bid in the void suit
  asks, jump or not.

## Corpus (Exclusion_After_1M, Exclusion_After_Sta_Jac, --limit 50)

BBA asks 66 times on these 100 boards; we make the same call 9 times.
Almost all the misses are **BBA style**: BBA's ask is a non-jump five-level
bid over a game in our suit (1S-2NT-3C-4S-5C, 1H-(3S)-4H-5D) or over a
splinter (1S-4D-5C), where by the cited definition 5♣ is a control bid,
not Exclusion; we ask 4NT. A few are our room rule (two keycards, the
"none" answer past five of our suit: we ask 4NT). Where we do ask, the
answers and the slam level agree with BBA's reading; the grand is
sometimes missed (we need the queen shown).

## Open questions (for Rick)

- **Jump or not:** we follow the sources (an unusual jump). BBA, and the
  scenarios, treat 5 of a new suit over our game as Exclusion. Should
  the default follow BBA here? (Then control bids past game lose 5♣/5♦.)
- **Responses:** 1430 steps by default (Bridge Bum, Todd's first
  option); Todd prefers 0-1-1-2-2 for the four keycards, BBA 0-1-2-3.
- No queen ask or king ask after an Exclusion answer.

## Sources

- **The convention:** Bridge Bum, "Exclusion Blackwood"
  (https://www.bridgebum.com/exclusion_blackwood.php): a jump to the 4-
  or 5-level in a new suit shows a void, 1430 step answers excluding
  that ace. Robert S. Todd, "Exclusion Keycard", Adventures in Bridge
  #584 (an unusual jump at the five level; 1430 or 0-1-1-2-2 answers).
  Convention-card `bidding_conventions/exclusion_blackwood.toml` (Kantar,
  *25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know*, ch. 10).
- **Where we differ:** we leave the four-level jump out (it is a
  splinter in our system), and use only five-level jumps.
- **BBA:** its corpus notes ("Exclusion, for !S", "1 out of 4") give the
  `bba` treatment.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Flannery 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Flannery 2D"): an opening 2♦ shows 11-15 HCP
# with exactly four spades and five hearts, so the 1♥ opener never has to
# reverse or rebid awkwardly with the 4-5 majors. The natural weak 2♦ is
# off (preempts.bid, `weak_2d_open`). Responder:
#
#   Pass  6+ diamonds, weak          2♥/2♠  to play
#   2NT   asks (forcing)             3♣  6+ clubs, to play
#   3♦    6+ diamonds, invitational  3♥/3♠  invitational, 10-12
#   3NT   to play                    4♣/4♦  transfer to 4♥/4♠
#
# Opener's answers to 2NT: 3♣ 4-5-1-3, 3♦ 4-5-3-1, 3♥ 4-5-2-2 minimum,
# 3♠ 4-5-2-2 maximum, 3NT 4-5-2-2 maximum with the minors stopped, 4♣
# 4-5-0-4, 4♦ 4-5-4-0. See flannery.notes.md.

module flannery "Flannery 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/flannery
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/flannery

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ahead of 1♥ and 1NT (both would describe it less well).
when opening
  2D  "Flannery: 11-15 HCP, four spades and five hearts"   alert
      shows S=4, H=5, hcp=11..15
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Over a double the same calls (the double is usually a strong hand or
# diamonds; nothing is lost by playing the system on).
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  P   "Six or more diamonds, weak: to play"
      shows D>=6, hcp<=9, H<=2, S<=3
      priority 1
  2S  "To play: no game interest"
      shows hcp<=9, S>=4 | (S=3, H<=1)
  2H  "To play: no game interest"
      shows hcp<=10
      priority -1
  3C  "Six or more clubs: to play"
      shows C>=6, hcp<=9, H<=2, S<=3
      priority 1
  3D  "Six or more diamonds, invitational"
      shows D>=6, hcp=10..12, H<=2, S<=3
  3H  "Invitational: three or more hearts, 10-12"
      shows H>=3, tp(H)=10..12, S<=3
  3S  "Invitational: four or more spades, 10-12"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=10..12
  # Game in a major: the transfer, so that opener declares.
  4C  "Transfer to 4♥: game, no slam interest"   alert
      shows H>=3, tp(H)>=13, tp(H)<=18, S<=3
      sets  trump=H
      artificial
  4D  "Transfer to 4♠: game, no slam interest"   alert
      shows S>=4, tp(S)>=13, tp(S)<=18
      sets  trump=S
      artificial
  3N  "To play: the minors held, no major fit"
      shows hcp=13..17, H<=2, S<=3, stop(C), stop(D)
  2N  "Asks opener's shape: game interest"   alert
      shows hcp>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=flannery
      artificial
      priority -1

# ── Opener after a sign-off or a natural game ────────────────────────
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3N (P)
  P   "No further bid"

after 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Accepts the invitation: 14-15"   shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines: a minimum"
after 2D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Accepts the invitation: 14-15"   shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines: a minimum"
after 2D (P) 3D (P)
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum with the clubs stopped"   shows hcp>=14, stop(C)
  P   "Declines"

after 2D (P) 4C (P)
  4H  "Completes the transfer"
after 2D (P) 4D (P)
  4S  "Completes the transfer"

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked flannery
  3C  "Three clubs: 4-5-1-3"              shows D=1, C=3   artificial
  3D  "Three diamonds: 4-5-3-1"           shows D=3, C=1   artificial
  3H  "4-5-2-2, minimum, 11-13"           shows D=2, C=2, hcp<=13
  3S  "4-5-2-2, maximum, 14-15"           shows D=2, C=2, hcp>=14   artificial
  3N  "4-5-2-2, maximum, the minors held"  shows D=2, C=2, hcp>=14, stop(C), stop(D)
  4C  "Four clubs: 4-5-0-4"                shows D=0, C=4   artificial
  4D  "Four diamonds: 4-5-4-0"             shows D=4, C=0   artificial

# ── The asker places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
# 3NT with the short suit held, else game in the 5-2 heart fit; a
# fit in the minor that opener holds as a side suit is left to the
# natural rules.
when answered flannery
  P   "3NT is the contract"
      when  partner.last=3N
      priority 1
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"                shows S>=4
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"                shows H>=2
      when  !partner.last=3N
  3N  "To play: the short suit held"
      shows stop(C) | partner.C.min>=2, stop(D) | partner.D.min>=2
      when  partner.last <= 3S
      priority 1

# Flannery 2♦: notes

## Decisions

- Opening: exactly 4-5 in the majors, 11-15 HCP, any seat, ahead of 1♥
  and 1NT (priority 1). The weak 2♦ is off (preempts.bid, `weak_2d_open`).
- Responder's weak calls follow BBA (Flannery scenario): pass with six
  diamonds and at most two hearts, 2♥ with up to 10 HCP and no better
  call, 2♠ with four spades (or three and a singleton heart). 2NT from 11.
- Game in a major goes through the 4♣/4♦ transfer; the direct 4♥/4♠ of
  Bridge Bum are not written.
- Over a double the same responses (system on).
- After the 2NT answer the asker bids 3NT when the short suit is covered
  (his stopper or opener's doubleton), else 4♥ in the 5-2 fit.

## BBA (compare Flannery --limit 50, 2026-10-05: 87% of calls agree)

- BBA super-accepts the transfer with a maximum (2♦–4♣–4♦ "surplus",
  2♦–4♦–4♥): BBA style, not written.
- Invitation versus game thresholds differ by a point either way at
  2♦–P (3♠ vs our 4♦ transfer, 4♣ vs our 3♥): don't care.
- 2♦ passed out by responder with long diamonds is reported as "contract
  is an artificial call": intended, Bridge Bum's pass.

## Open questions

- Does Rick want the super-accept (BBA) or the plain completion (Bridge
  Bum)? We complete.

## Sources

- Bridge Bum, "Flannery 2D", https://www.bridgebum.com/flannery_2d.php:
  the opening, the responses, the answers to 2NT. Deviations: direct 4M
  not written; responder's weak ranges from BBA.
- BBA corpus, Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `bba/Flannery.pbn`.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The 4NT opening: asks for specific aces. A hand whose only losers are
# aces (a long, solid suit and kings with queens or short) needs to know
# which aces partner holds, not how many. Answers: 5♣ no ace, 5♦ 5♥ 5♠
# the ace of that suit, 6♣ the club ace, 5NT two aces. The opener then
# places the contract in his long suit. Notes: four-nt-opening.notes.md.

module four-nt-opening "4NT opening: asks for specific aces"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/four_nt_opening
  needs  base

# ── The opening ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every loser is an ace: each suit without the ace is a singleton, K-x,
# K-Q-x, or the long suit headed by the K-Q-J (partner's ace there is a
# winner; a longer side suit could lose its small cards too), the suits
# with the ace lose nothing (`losers` equals the aces missing), and no
# void, where partner's ace would be wasted. One to three aces missing,
# and a suit of six or more to play in, the longest (spades first on a
# tie). One rule, which sets no trump: partner's answer does not depend
# on the suit, and the opener places the contract in his own.
define fna_ace_only(x) = has(A,x) | x = 1 | (has(K,x), x = 2) | (has(K,x), has(Q,x), x = 3) | (has(K,x), has(Q,x), has(J,x), x >= 6)
define fna_hand = C>=1, D>=1, H>=1, S>=1, fna_ace_only(C), fna_ace_only(D), fna_ace_only(H), fna_ace_only(S), keycards(N) >= 1, keycards(N) <= 3, losers + keycards(N) = 4
define fna_suit(x) = x>=6, x>=S, x>=H, x>=D, x>=C

when opening
  4N  "Asks for specific aces: a long suit, every loser an ace"  alert
      shows fna_hand, S>=6 | H>=6 | D>=6 | C>=6
      sets  ask=specific_aces
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked specific_aces
  5C  "No ace"                    shows keycards(N)=0                 artificial   priority 5
  5D  "The diamond ace"           shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,D)       artificial   priority 5
  5H  "The heart ace"             shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,H)       artificial   priority 5
  5S  "The spade ace"             shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,S)       artificial   priority 5
  6C  "The club ace"              shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,C)       artificial   priority 5
  5N  "Two aces"    shows keycards(N) in 2|3            artificial   priority 5

# ── The opener places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
#
# Every ace partner holds is one I lack, so each covers a loser: seven
# with none left, six with one, else five of the suit (pass when that
# was the answer).
define fna_left = losers - (we.keycards(N).min - keycards(N))

when answered specific_aces
  7S  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(S), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6S  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(S), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(S), partner.last = 5S
        priority 5
  5S  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(S)
        priority 5
  6S  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(S)
        priority 4
  7H  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(H), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6H  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(H), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(H), partner.last = 5H
        priority 5
  5H  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(H)
        priority 5
  6H  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(H)
        priority 4
  7D  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(D), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6D  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(D), fna_left <= 1
        priority 5
  P   "To play"
        when fna_suit(D), partner.last = 5D
        priority 5
  5D  "Signoff"
        when fna_suit(D)
        priority 5
  6D  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(D)
        priority 4
  7C  "Grand slam"
        when fna_suit(C), fna_left <= 0
        priority 5
  6C  "Small slam"
        when fna_suit(C), fna_left <= 1
