# four-nt-opening (`four-nt-opening.bid`): notes

The 4NT opening asking for specific aces (2026-10-05), gated on
`slam.four_nt_opening.play` (on in most 21GF cards; off in Basic-Bridge
and Precision).

## What the rules do

- **The opening:** a hand whose only losers are aces: no void, each suit
  without the ace a singleton, K-x, K-Q-x, or the long suit headed by the
  K-Q-J (a longer K-Q side suit can lose its small cards), the suits with
  the ace losing nothing (`losers` = aces missing), one to three aces
  missing, and a suit of six or more. Priority 2, over the strong 2♣.
  One rule, setting no trump: with one rule per suit, partner read the
  first (hearts) and every 4NT opener played in hearts (tripwire,
  2026-10-05). The opener places the contract in his longest suit.
- **Answers:** 5♣ no ace, 5♦/5♥/5♠ that ace, 6♣ the club ace, 5NT two
  aces (three, which cannot happen often, the same).
- **Opener:** each ace partner shows covers one loser (all my losers
  are aces), so seven with none left, six with one, else five of the
  suit, or pass when partner's answer was five of it. An answer past
  five of the suit (6♣, or 5NT over 5♠-and-up) forces six.

Rare: no PBS scenario deals it. On the --limit 50 tripwire it opened 7
boards (Benjamin_2D, Kokish_Relay, We_Overcall_Their_2C and others):
contract errors 52 before, 36 after.

## Open questions

- The opener does not play 6NT/7NT, even when the long suit is solid and
  the aces make the tricks.
- Three aces opposite is answered 5NT (two), as there is no step for it.

## Sources

- **The convention:** the 4NT opening for specific aces, standard
  practice (Culbertson's), as Bridge Guys' "Four Notrump Opening" and
  ACBL's convention charts describe it: 5♣ none, 5♦/5♥/5♠ that ace, 6♣
  the club ace, 5NT two aces. Not yet checked against a book; the
  opening condition (every loser an ace) is ours.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# French 2♦ (the French standard system, SEF: "2♦ forcing de manche";
# BBA's `French 2D`, probes/b2-French-*.toml): 2♦ is the artificial
# game-forcing opening, 24+ HCP of any shape, and 2♣ keeps the strong
# hands below it (strong-openings.bid caps it at 23 when this is on).
# There is no weak 2♦ (preempts.bid, `weak_2d_open`).
#
# Responder answers in aces (BBA):
#
#   2♥   no ace, 0-7, no five-card major
#   2♠   one ace, the ♥A or the ♠A
#   2NT  no ace, 8+
#   3♣   one ace, the ♣A          3♦   one ace, the ♦A
#   3♥/3♠  no ace, 0-7, a five-card suit
#   3NT  two aces or more
#
# Opener then bids naturally. See french-2d.notes.md.

module french-2d "French 2♦ (game forcing)"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/french_2d
  needs  strong-openings
  skill  bidding_conventions/french_2d

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Above every 2♣ opening and the 3NT opening (BBA opens 2♦ with a
# balanced 26 too).
when opening
  2D  "French 2♦: game forcing, 24+ HCP"   alert
      shows hcp>=24
      sets  forcing=game, ask=french_2d
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Responder: aces ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked french_2d
  3N  "Two aces or more"                 shows keycards(N)>=2
      artificial
      priority 2
  2S  "One ace: the ♥A or the ♠A"        shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,H) | has(A,S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3C  "One ace: the ♣A"                  shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,C)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3D  "One ace: the ♦A"                  shows keycards(N)=1, has(A,D)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3H  "No ace, 0-7: five or more hearts"   shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7, H>=5, H>=S
  3S  "No ace, 0-7: five or more spades"   shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7, S>=5, S>H
  2N  "No ace, 8+"                       shows keycards(N)=0, hcp>=8
      artificial
  2H  "No ace, 0-7"                      shows keycards(N)=0, hcp<=7
      artificial
      priority -1

# ── Opener: natural ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The auction is forced to game; opener shows his suit or his balanced
# hand, and the slam modules take over once a suit is agreed.
after 2D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Three or more hearts: agrees hearts"   shows H>=3
      sets  trump=H
      priority 2
after 2D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Three or more spades: agrees spades"   shows S>=3
      sets  trump=S
      priority 2
# Two aces opposite 24+: a balanced 25 bids the slam (32+ between us).
after 2D (P) 3N (P)
  6N  "Balanced: slam opposite two aces"    shows balanced, hcp>=25
      priority 1
  P   "Balanced 24: game"                    shows balanced
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3D (P) | 2D (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 3S (P) | 2D (P) 3N (P)
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"       shows S>=5
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"       shows H>=5
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"     shows D>=5
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"        shows C>=5
  cheapest(N) "Balanced"                  shows balanced
      priority -1

# French 2♦: notes

## Decisions

- The convention-card entry leaves the meaning to the partnership. We
  take the French standard (SEF) meaning, which is also BBA's `French 2D`
  (probes/b2-French-openings.toml, b2-French-openings-strong.toml): 2♦ is
  the artificial game force, 24+ HCP of any shape, balanced 26-27
  included (BBA opens 2♦, not 3NT). 2♣ stays the strong opening of
  strong-openings.bid, capped at 23.
- Responses are BBA's ace answers (probes/b2-French-resp-2D*.toml):
  2♥ no ace 0-7, 2♠ one major ace, 2NT no ace 8+, 3♣/3♦ the ace of that
  suit, 3♥/3♠ no ace 0-7 and a five-card suit, 3NT two aces or more.
  BBA bids 2♥ with a long minor and no ace; so do we.
- Opener rebids naturally (five-card suits, notrump balanced); over 3♥/3♠
  he agrees with three; over 3NT a balanced 25+ bids 6NT.
- The weak 2♦ is off (preempts.bid). Responses to 2♣ are unchanged:
  BBA's French 2♣ (19-24 by its alert) answers 2♦ waiting, and our ladder
  already does.

## Open questions (decision taken)

- After 2♠ (a major ace) BBA may ask which; we let opener bid naturally.
- No interference structure over 2♦.
- 2♣–2♦–2NT is passable in BBA's French scheme; ours stays game forcing
  as strong-openings.bid plays it.

## Sources

- Système d'Enseignement Français (FFB), "2♦ forcing de manche": the
  meaning of the opening; not quoted from a page.
- BBA as a black box: probes/b2-French-openings.toml,
  b2-French-openings-strong.toml, b2-French-resp-2D.toml,
  b2-French-resp-2D-aces.toml, b2-French-resp-2C.toml (2026-10-05).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gambling 3NT (ACBL SAYC booklet; Bridge Bum, "Gambling 3NT";
# convention-card bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt): a solid seven- or
# eight-card minor (AKQ at least) and no outside ace or king. The
# balanced 26-27 then opens 2♣ (strong-openings.bid reads the same field).
#
# The pass-or-correct calls are not marked artificial: a pass plays
# them. Responder: pass to play (the other suits stopped), 4♣ and 5♣ pass or
# correct to opener's minor, 4♥/4♠ to play, 6♣ pass or correct with slam
# values. See gambling-3nt.notes.md.

module gambling-3nt "Gambling 3NT: a solid minor"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ahead of a one-level or three-level opening of the minor.
when opening, seat<=3
  3N  "Gambling: a solid seven-card minor, no outside ace or king"   alert
      shows C>=7, has(A,C), has(K,C), has(Q,C), D<=3, S<=4, H<=4
      shows !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(A,D), !has(K,D)
      priority 2
  3N  "Gambling: a solid seven-card minor, no outside ace or king"   alert
      shows D>=7, has(A,D), has(K,D), has(Q,D), C<=3, S<=4, H<=4
      shows !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(A,C), !has(K,C)
      priority 2

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Opener brings seven tricks: pass with the other three suits covered.
after 3N (P)
  P   "To play: the other suits stopped"
      shows stop(S), stop(H), stop(C) | stop(D)
      shows hcp>=10
  4C  "Pass or correct: to play in your minor"   alert
      priority -5
  5C  "Pass or correct: game in your minor"   alert
      shows S<=1 | H<=1, C>=3, D>=3
      priority -4
  6C  "Pass or correct: slam in your minor"   alert
      shows hcp>=16, quick_tricks>=4
  4H  "To play: a long heart suit"            shows H>=7 | (H>=6, hcp>=10)
  4S  "To play: a long spade suit"            shows S>=7 | (S>=6, hcp>=10)

after 3N (P) 4C (P) | 3N (P) 5C (P) | 3N (P) 6C (P)
  P   "My minor is clubs"                     shows C>=7
  cheapest(D)  "My minor is diamonds"         shows D>=7

after 3N (P) 4H (P) | 3N (P) 4S (P)
  P   "Partner's suit: to play"

# Responder after the correction: the contract is placed.
after 3N (P) 4C (P) 4D (P) | 3N (P) 5C (P) 5D (P) | 3N (P) 6C (P) 6D (P)
  P   "To play in opener's diamonds"

# gambling-3nt (`gambling-3nt.bid`): notes

Gambling 3NT (`notrump.gambling_3nt.play`): a solid seven-card minor
(AKQ at least, eight allowed) and no outside ace or king, first to third
seat. strong-openings.bid already read the field (the balanced 26-27
opens 2♣ when 3NT is Gambling) but nothing opened the Gambling 3NT. Every
21GF stock card has the field on, so this changes the 21GF scenarios
wherever such a hand turns up (it opened 3♣/3♦ or one of the minor
before). Cases: `gambling-3nt.test`.

## Structure

- Responder: pass with spades, hearts and a minor stopped and 10+ HCP;
  4♣ pass or correct (the default); 5♣ pass or correct with shortness in
  a major and three cards in each minor; 6♣ pass or correct with 16+ and
  four quick tricks; 4♥/4♠ to play with seven, or six and 10+.
- Opener passes clubs or corrects to diamonds at the same level.
- The pass-or-correct calls are alerted but not `artificial`: a pass
  plays them.

## Corpus (Gambling_3N, 50 boards, 2026-10-05)

87.3% of calls agree, no problems in our auctions. Remaining
divergences:

- The opponents' overcalls over 3NT (BBA 4♥/4♠/X, we pass): competitive/,
  not this module. **Don't care here** (reported to the competitive
  owner).
- BBA passes 3NT on some hands where we bid 4♣ (3 boards) and bids 7♦
  once where we bid 6♣: **BBA style**, left.

## Questions for Rick

- 4♦ as an asking bid (shortness, some play it) is not built: 4♦ has no
  meaning. Decision: leave it out, as the SAYC booklet.
- Fourth seat: no Gambling 3NT (seat<=3), as Namyats. Decision taken.

## Sources

- **ACBL SAYC booklet** (Gambling 3NT: a solid seven-card minor, no
  outside ace or king; 4♣/5♣ pass or correct) and **Bridge Bum,
  "Gambling 3NT"** (https://www.bridgebum.com/gambling_3nt.php), which
  the Gambling_3N scenario cites; the scenario's script allows a queen or
  two jacks outside (9-11 HCP).
- **Where we differ:** responder's pass, 5♣ and 6♣ thresholds are ours
  (standard practice, not yet cited).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gazzilli: after 1♥/1♠ and a 1NT response (or 1♥-1♠), opener's 2♣ is
# artificial: either natural, 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any
# strong hand (16+). Responder's 2♦ says 8+ and asks; anything else is
# 5-7 and natural.
#
#   1M-1NT-2♣-2♦:  2M the natural minimum with clubs (NF); 2NT 16-17
#                  balanced; 3♣/3♦ 16+ with the minor, 3M 16+ with six or
#                  more, the other major 16+ with four (all game forcing)
#
# The classic form (Wikipedia, "Gazzilli"; BBA plays it: every 2♣ in the
# PBS scenario Gazzilli holds clubs or 16+). Todd's modern form ("Modern
# Gazzilli", Adventures in Bridge TWiB 488) moves the minimum six-card
# one-suiter into 2♣ and the 5-4 with clubs into 2M; not played. Partial:
# the artificial relays after 2♦ and opener's 5-5 jumps are not played;
# see gazzilli.notes.md.

module gazzilli "Gazzilli 2♣ after 1M-1NT and 1♥-1♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gazzilli
  needs  rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/gazzilli

# A strong hand for the relay: 16+, but not 18-19 balanced (2NT at once)
# or six of the major and 16-18 (the jump rebid, as BBA).
define gazzilli_strong(M) = hcp>=16, !(balanced, hcp=18..19), !(M>=6, hcp<=18)

# ── Opener ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1M (P) 1N (P)
  2C  "Gazzilli: 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any 16+"  alert
      shows gazzilli_strong(M) | (hcp<=15, C>=4)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=gazzilli(M)
      artificial
      priority 2                       # ahead of the natural rebids (rebids.bid)
  3x  "Five-five, 13-15: {M} and {x}"
      shows M>=5, x>=5, hcp=13..15
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S
      priority 3                       # the jump in a new suit (PBS Gazzilli; Todd)
after 1H (P) 1S (P)
  3x  "Five-five, 13-15: hearts and {x}"
      shows H>=5, x>=5, hcp=13..15, S<=3
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority 3
  2C  "Gazzilli: 11-15 with four or more clubs, or any 16+"  alert
      shows gazzilli_strong(H) | (hcp<=15, C>=4), S<=3
      sets  forcing=round, ask=gazzilli(H)
      artificial
      priority 2                       # a spade fit raises (rebids.bid)

# Responder after the 5-5 jump (13-15, not forcing).
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) when x is not M, M is S | x is not S
  4M  "Game in {M}: two or more and 9+"
      shows M>=2, points>=9
      priority 3
  3M  "Preference for {M}"
      shows M>=2
      priority 2
  3N  "No fit for {M}, 10+"
      shows points>=10
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: plays {x}"
      priority 1
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) when x is C | x is D
  4H  "Game in hearts: two or more and 9+"
      shows H>=2, points>=9
      priority 3
  3H  "Preference for hearts"
      shows H>=2
      priority 2
  3N  "No fit for hearts, 10+"
      shows points>=10
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: plays {x}"
      priority 1

after 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) 3M (P) | 1M (P) 1N (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is not M
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) 3H (P) | 1H (P) 1S (P) 3x (P) 3N (P) when x is C | x is D
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 2

# ── Responder after 2♣ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked gazzilli(M), rho.last=P, partner.last=2C
  2D  "Gazzilli: 8+, asks"  alert
      shows hcp>=8
      sets  forcing=round
      artificial
      priority 3                       # ahead of responder's natural rebids
  2M  "5-7, two or more {M}"
      shows hcp<=7, M>=2
      priority 3
  2H  "5-7, five or more hearts, no spade fit"
      shows hcp<=7, H>=5, S<=1
      when  M is S
      priority 2
  2S  "5-7, five or more spades, no heart fit"
      shows hcp<=7, S>=5, H<=1
      when  M is H, me.last=1S
      priority 2
  3C  "5-7, six or more clubs"
      shows hcp<=7, C>=6, M<=1
      priority 2
  3D  "5-7, six or more diamonds"
      shows hcp<=7, D>=6, M<=1
      priority 2
  2N  "5-7, no fit for {M}"
      shows hcp<=7, M<=1
      priority 1

# ── Opener after 2♦ (8+) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
when answered gazzilli(M), rho.last=P, partner.last=2D
  2M  "Gazzilli: the natural minimum, four or more clubs"
      shows hcp<=15
      priority 3                       # ahead of opener's natural rebids
  2N  "Gazzilli: 16-17, balanced"
      shows hcp=16..17, balanced
      priority 3
  3N  "Gazzilli: 20-21, balanced"
      shows hcp>=20, balanced
      priority 3
  3M  "Gazzilli: 16+, six or more {M}"
      shows hcp>=16, M>=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3C  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more clubs"
      shows hcp>=16, C>=4, C>=D, M<=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3D  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more diamonds"
      shows hcp>=16, D>=4, D>C, M<=6
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  3H  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more hearts"
      shows hcp>=16, H>=4
      when  M is S
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
  # Anything else strong: game in the major.
  4M  "Gazzilli: 16+, game"
      shows hcp>=16
      priority 1

after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2S  "Gazzilli: 16+, four or more spades"
      shows hcp>=16, S>=4
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2S  "Gazzilli: 16+, three spades"
      shows hcp>=16, S=3
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 3

# ── Responder after opener's minimum (2M, not forcing) ───────────────
after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2M (P)
  4M  "Game opposite a minimum: 12+ with two or more {M}"
      shows points>=12, M>=2
      priority 3
  3M  "Invites opposite a minimum: 10-11"

  3N  "No fit for {M}, 11+"

      priority 2

  2S  "Five or more spades, no heart fit: to play"
      shows S>=5, H<=1, points<=10
      priority 3
  2N  "No fit for hearts, 8-10"
      shows H<=1, S<=4, points<=10
      priority 3
  3N  "No fit for hearts, 11+"
      shows H<=1, points>=11

  4H  "Game opposite a minimum: 12+ with two or more hearts"
      shows points>=12, H>=2
      priority 3
  3H  "Invites opposite a minimum: 10-11"
      shows points=10..11, H>=2
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite a minimum"
      priority 2

  3N  "Game opposite 16-17: 9+"
      shows points>=9
      priority 3
  P   "No game opposite 16-17"
      priority 2

  4M  "Game in the six-card major"

  4M  "Game in the major: three of them"

  3N  "Game: no fit for {M}"
      priority 2
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2N (P)

  P   "No game opposite 16-17"
      priority 2

      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)

      priority 3
after 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 3x (P) when x is C | x is D

      shows H>=3

  3N  "Game: no fit for hearts"

after 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2M (P) 2N (P) | 1H (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2N (P)

      shows hcp<=18

      when  !partner.last=2D

      when  !partner.last=2D

# gazzilli (`gazzilli.bid`): notes

Gazzilli after 1♥/1♠ - 1NT and 1♥ - 1♠. Partial (2026-10-05). Cases:
`gazzilli.test`.

## What the card says

`major_openings.gazzilli.play` (`.bbsa` `Gazzilli`; 21GF-Gazzilli sets it).

## The structure played

- Opener's 2♣: 11-15 with four or more clubs, or 16+ (classic form).
  Not 18-19 balanced (2NT at once, as Todd), and not six of the major
  with 16-18 (the jump rebid, as BBA). After 1♥-1♠ only without four
  spades: a fit raises. A minimum six-card one-suiter rebids 2M; 5-5
  with 13-15 jumps in the second suit (PBS summary, Todd).
- Responder: 2♦ with 8+ HCP; with less, 2M with two or more, else a
  five-card major of his own (2♥ over 1♠; 2♠ over 1♥-1♠), a six-card
  minor at the three level, or 2NT (no fit).
- After 2♦: 2M the natural minimum with clubs (not forcing); 2NT 16-17
  balanced; 3NT 20-21 balanced; 3♣/3♦ 16+ with the minor, 3M 16+ with
  six, the other major 16+ with four, 2♠ after 1♥-1♠ with three spades
  (all game forcing); otherwise 4M.
- Responder after the minimum: game with 12, invite with 10-11, 2NT/3NT
  without a fit (2♠ with five spades after 1♥-1♠), else pass. After a
  game force: 4M with three, else 3NT; opener corrects 3NT to 4M with six.
- Opener after a weak answer: pass up to 18; 3M with six and 19-20; game
  above.

## Deviations

- From Todd's "modern" Gazzilli: there the minimum six-card one-suiter
  goes through 2♣ and the minimum 5-4 with clubs rebids 2M. BBA plays the
  classic form (every 2♣ in the Gazzilli corpus holds clubs or 16+), and so
  do we. The PBS scenario's summary mixes the two.
- Not played: the artificial rebids after 2♦ (2oM "some four-card suit"
  with its relay, 2NT "six and a four-card side suit"), and any defence
  to interference (the convention is off in competition).
- BBA starts 18-19 balanced with 2♣ too (then 2NT); we bid 2NT at once.

## Sources

- Robert S. Todd, "Constructive Bidding: Modern Gazzilli", Advancing in
  Bridge TWiB 488, https://www.advinbridge.com/this-week-in-bridge/488
  (responses to 2♣, opener's rebids after 2♦, 2NT 17-19 at once).
- Wikipedia, "Gazzilli" (the classic 2♣: natural 11-15 with clubs or any
  16+).
- The PBS scenario Gazzilli (`btn/Gazzilli.btn`) summary.
- Responder's and opener's game thresholds: standard practice, not yet
  cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Gerber: 4♣ asks for aces over partner's natural notrump, where no suit
# has been agreed. Answers by steps (4♦ 0 or 4, 4♥ 1, 4♠ 2, 4NT 3); 5♣
# then asks for kings the same way. The asker places the contract; 4NT
# after an answer is a sign-off. Notes: gerber.notes.md.
#
# Where it applies (card `slam.gerber.*`):
# - directly over partner's 1NT or 2NT where systems are on (2NT opening,
#   2♣–2♦–2NT, Kokish's 2NT ...: one-nt.bid, `systems on`);
# - over interference to our 1NT opening (a double, a two-level overcall);
# - after 1NT–2♣–2♦ (Stayman, no major; not with the bba treatment);
# - over partner's 1NT or 2NT rebid after 1x–1y, and by opener over a
#   natural 2NT response (1m–2NT, 2♣–2NT), unless the card says
#   `gerber.only_over_nt_openings` (BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings")
#   or not `gerber.over_nt_seq`;
# - brill: over a 3NT opening and opener's 3NT rebid after 2♣.
# Never where clubs are natural or a suit is agreed: after a transfer, a
# major Stayman answer, or a minor raise, 4♣ keeps its other meanings.
#
# 4♣ over 1NT is a transfer to diamonds with `transfers.texas_4c`, and
# then Gerber is off there. Over 2NT the 4♣ slam try in clubs
# (two-nt-responses.bid) is off when Gerber is on: those hands ask for
# aces and bid 6♣ (gerber.notes.md, "Decisions").

module gerber "Gerber: 4♣ asks for aces over partner's notrump"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/gerber
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/gerber
  param  only_openings = only_over_nt_openings default false
  param  nt_seq = over_nt_seq default true   # not in the .bbsa map: true unless a card JSON says no
  param  texas_4c = bidding_conventions/texas:bid_4c default false
  param  tu = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false   # 2-under Texas: 4C transfers
  param  style = general.style
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (over 3NT)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The hands that would bid 6NT directly (one-nt.bid, two-nt-responses.bid)
# check the aces first; priority 1 puts the ask ahead of 6NT. BBA asks a
# point lower, 31 HCP between the hands (probes/gerber-resp-1N.toml,
# gerber-resp-2N.toml), and then bids 6NT only with three aces between
# the hands: that is the bba treatment. Our default keeps Rick's 4NT
# invitation with 16 opposite 15-17 (one-nt.bid).
after 1N (P) when !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # a major goes through Stayman or a transfer
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1                         # ahead of 6NT: check the aces first
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over 2NT a long club suit asks too, and plays in 6♣ (BBA from 9 HCP
# with six clubs; our threshold is the old 4♣ slam try's).
after nt2 when !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (balanced, strength>=slam) | (C>=6 | (C>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite)
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min) | (C>=6, hcp>=29-partner.hcp.min)
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# brill (the Brill card): Gerber over a 3NT opening too (25-27), where
# our default reads 4C as a club slam try (over-3nt.bid). Brill /explain,
# 2026-10-15, after 3N P: "Gerber" `slammish`. Slam values: 31 between
# the hands, as over-3nt.bid counts.
after 3N (P) when system is brill
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Brill: also over opener's 3NT rebid after 2♣ (2♣–2♦–3NT, and after
# their overcall, 2♣ (2♥) P (P) 3NT, 2♣ P 2♦ (2♥) 3NT). Our default reads
# 4♣ after 2♣–2♦–3NT as the club slam try, as over the 3NT opening
# (over-3nt.bid), and has no rule after interference (notes, "Gaps").
after 2C (*) P (P) 3N (P) | 2C (P) 2D (*) 3N (P) when system is brill
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over interference to our 1NT opening (a double or a suit overcall at
# the two level) the jump to 4♣ is still Gerber, the same hands as
# without it: 4♣ is not a sensible cue-bid or natural call there.
after 1N (X) when !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
after 1N (2y) when y is not N, !texas_4c, !tu
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, hcp>=31-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# After Stayman's 2♦ (no major) the jump to 4♣ is Gerber: no suit is
# agreed and clubs are not natural. The hands that bid 6NT there
# (stayman.bid) check the aces first. The bba treatment keeps BBA's 4♣
# minor slam try (stayman.bid).
after 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when style is not bba
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Over a notrump rebid or response (the card's "over NT sequence";
# BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings" turns it off).
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1N (P) | 1x (P) 1y (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# Gerber by opener over responder's natural 2NT: 1♣–2NT and 1♦–2NT
# (Bridge Bum: 4♣ over any natural notrump; PBS Gerber_By_Opener), and
# 2♣–2NT, the balanced positive. After 1♣ too: clubs are not agreed, and
# opener with long clubs shows them at the three level first. Slam
# values against responder's minimum; over 2♣–2NT the balanced hands
# that bid 6NT (strong-openings.bid) ask first.
after 1m (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows H<=4, S<=4, strength>=slam
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1
after 2C (P) 2N (P) when !only_openings, nt_seq
  4C  "Gerber: how many aces?"  alert
      shows balanced, points>=33-partner.hcp.min
      sets  ask=gerber
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked gerber
  4D  "0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
  4H  "1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
  4S  "2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2        artificial
  4N  "3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3        artificial

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
# we.keycards(N) is my aces plus partner's answer, four in the deck, so
# "0 or 4" resolves against my own. Rules without `shows` rank by
# priority, then file order: the grand before the king ask before six.
# The thresholds (my points plus opener's minimum) were set on the
# corpus: 7NT from 35 with all the aces, the king ask at 33-34
# (gerber.notes.md, "Grand slam and the king ask"; the textbook 37 for
# 7NT scored 400 IMPs worse).
when answered gerber
  7N  "Grand slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)=4, points + partner.hcp.min >= 35
      priority 3
  5C  "Gerber: how many kings?"  alert
      when  we.keycards(N)=4, points + partner.hcp.min >= 33, points + partner.hcp.min <= 34
      when  C<=5                         # a long club suit settles for six
      sets  ask=gerber_kings
      artificial
      priority 2
  6C  "Small slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)>=3, C>=6, imps       # at matchpoints 6NT scored better (notes)
      priority 1
  6N  "Small slam"
      when  we.keycards(N)>=3
  4N  "Signoff"
      when  we.keycards(N).max<=2
  # "0 or 4" facing no ace of my own is four.
  6N  "Small slam"
      when  maybe we.keycards(N)>=3
      priority -1

when asked gerber_kings
  5D  "0 or 4 kings"  shows (controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 0) | (controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 4)   artificial
  5H  "1 king"        shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 1   artificial
  5S  "2 kings"       shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 2   artificial
  5N  "3 kings"       shows controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) = 3   artificial

# All four aces are ours (the king ask needs them): seven with all four
# kings as well, else six. Kings are controls less two for each ace.
when answered gerber_kings
  7N  "Grand slam"
      when  (partner.last=5N, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 1) | (partner.last=5S, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 2) | (partner.last=5H, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 3) | (partner.last=5D, controls - keycards(N) - keycards(N) >= 4)
      priority 1
  6N  "Small slam"

# gerber (`gerber.bid`): notes

Gerber (card `slam.gerber.play`, alias `other_conventions.gerber.play`;
BBA's `Gerber`, on 17 of the 18 corpus cards, and on Rick's card). 4♣
over partner's natural notrump asks for aces: 4♦ 0 or 4, 4♥ 1, 4♠ 2,
4NT 3. 5♣ then asks for kings on the same steps. The asker places the
contract; 4NT after an answer is a sign-off. Cases: `gerber.test`.
Built 2026-09-28.

## Where 4♣ is Gerber

- **Directly over partner's 1NT or 2NT opening**, and over 2♣–2♦–2NT.
- **Over partner's 1NT or 2NT rebid** after 1x–1y, unless the card has
  `gerber.only_over_nt_openings` (BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings",
  set on 21GF-MSS, 21GF-Multi and 21GF-NoInvertedMinor). BBA uses it
  there (Gerber_By_Responder: 1♦–1♠–1NT–4♣, 1♣–1♥–2NT–4♣).
- **Over interference to our 1NT opening** (2026-10-30): after their
  double or a suit overcall at the two level (1NT (2♣) 4♣, 1NT (2♥) 4♣,
  1NT (X) 4♣) the jump to 4♣ is still Gerber, on the same hands as
  without it (`bba` treatment: BBA's 31 HCP). 4♣ is neither a useful
  cue-bid nor natural there. Off with a 4♣ Texas (`texas_4c`, 2-under).
- **After Stayman's 2♦** (1NT–2♣–2♦–4♣, 2026-10-30): no suit agreed and
  clubs not natural, so the jump is Gerber (Bridge Bum: "a jump to 4♣
  after Stayman"). The hands that bid 6NT there (stayman.bid, 32 between
  the hands) ask first. Not with `general.style = bba`: BBA's 4♣ there
  is its minor slam try (stayman.bid, probed). Not after 2♥/2♠: a fit
  may exist and 4♣ stays free for cue-bids/splinters.
- **Gerber by opener over a natural 2NT response** (2026-10-30):
  1♣–2NT–4♣, 1♦–2NT–4♣ (slam values against responder's range, no
  five-card major) and 2♣–2NT–4♣ (balanced, 33 between the hands: the
  hands that bid 6NT there ask first). PBS Gerber_By_Opener defines
  exactly these sequences, citing Bridge Bum. **Decision: 1♣–2NT–4♣ is
  Gerber, not a club slam try.** Opener's 1♣ is not agreement (it may be
  three cards, or two on some cards), and opener with real clubs can
  show them at the three level, still forcing over a natural 2NT.
  Wikipedia's "not when a natural club suit has been bid" would make it
  natural; we read that as "after clubs are bid and supported"
  (1♣–2♣–2NT–4♣ stays off). These and the 1x–1y–NT contexts follow the
  card's "over NT sequence" (`slam.gerber.over_nt_seq`, default true:
  the field is not in the `.bbsa` map, so only a card JSON can switch it
  off; SAYC.json sets it true) and BBA's "Gerber only for NT openings"
  (`only_over_nt_openings`, which turns them off).
- **Brill: over opener's 3NT rebid after 2♣** (2♣–2♦–3NT, 2♣ (2♥) P (P)
  3NT, 2♣ P 2♦ (2♥) 3NT, any overcall), as over Brill's 3NT opening
  (`general.system = brill`). The Brill card needs its JSON
  (`-c Brill`); `cards/bbsa/Brill.bbsa` imports without
  `general.system`, so with it these stay the default.
- **Nowhere else.** Not after a transfer, a Stayman major answer, over a
  minor raise, or when clubs have been bid and supported: 1♣–2♣–2NT–4♣ is
  whatever it was before (27 corpus boards, in minor-raise scenarios).
  Not over our 1NT overcall either: no corpus evidence
  (We_Overcall_1N_then_Gerber has no BBA file). Default (non-Brill):
  after 2♣–2♦–3NT 4♣ stays over-3nt.bid's club slam try (as over the 3NT
  opening), and after 2♣ (overcall) … 3NT it is the club slam try too
  (over-3nt.bid; Rick's rulings below).
- The card's other Gerber fields: `gerber.over_nt_seq` is read (above);
  `gerber.over` is free text (Bridge-Classroom's seed card says
  `1nt_2nt_only`, which is what the opening context does);
  `gerber.directly_over_nt` (covered by `play`) and `non_nt_seq` (4♣
  ace-ask in suit auctions: not played) are read by no rule. Rick's card
  sets only `other_conventions.gerber.play`.

## Decisions

- **Texas.** Gerber is 4♣ only; Texas is 4♦/4♥, so they coexist over
  1NT, and after a Texas completion 4NT stays keycard (texas-transfers).
  With `transfers.texas_4c` (4♣ a transfer to diamonds; no rule reads it
  yet) Gerber is off directly over 1NT.
- **The 4♣ minor slam try over 2NT** (two-nt-responses.bid, 2026-09-27)
  is off when Gerber is on: the same hands (six clubs, or five
  unbalanced, slam-invite values) ask for aces instead, then bid 6NT
  with three aces between the hands (6♣ at IMPs; at matchpoints 6NT
  scored better on par: 19 boards, -50 for 6♣), or sign off in 4NT. The
  4♦ diamond try stays. BBA does the same: 2NT–4♣ then 6♣/6♦/6NT, from 9
  HCP with six clubs (`probes/gerber-resp-2N.toml`). Its follow-ups
  (`after 2N (P) 4x (P)`) are restricted to diamonds when Gerber is on,
  so opener never reads Gerber as the try.
- **Who asks.** The hands that used to bid 6NT directly: balanced, 32
  points between the hands on opener's minimum over 1NT (17 opposite
  15-17), `strength>=slam` over 2NT. 16 opposite 15-17 keeps Rick's
  quantitative 4NT. BBA asks a point lower (31 HCP: 16 over 1NT, 11 over
  2NT, `probes/gerber-resp-1N.toml`, `gerber-resp-2N.toml`) and then bids
  6NT only with three aces between the hands; that is the `bba`
  treatment. A four-card major does not stop the ask (see "Corpus":
  2♣ → 4♣ is +647).
- **Grand slam and the king ask** (thresholds by corpus A/B, below):
  7NT with all four aces and 35 between the hands (my points plus
  opener's minimum); with 33-34, ask for kings and bid 7NT when all four
  are there, else 6NT. A long club suit does not ask for kings. Corpus
  A/B (all scenarios, vs BBA with par as the yardstick, both modules in):

  | 7NT from | king ask | vs BBA |
  |---:|---|---:|
  | 37 | none | -108,591 |
  | 37 | 34-36 | -106,518 |
  | 36 | 33-35 | -106,262 |
  | 36 | 32-35 | -106,572 |
  | 35 | none | -106,396 |
  | 35 | 34 | -106,004 |
  | **35** | **33-34** | **-105,913** |

  The textbook grand needs 37. Caution for Rick: the slam scenarios that
  carry most of this (Gerber_By_Responder, Grand_Slam_Invite) deal
  slam-rich hands by design, so the corpus may favour bold grands; the
  king ask at 33 alone lost (6NT → 5♣: -78 on 155 boards after 4♠) and
  the gain is in 7NT at 35-36.

the 4-4 fit is not looked for. Par likes it (+807 and +828 above),

## Rick's rulings (2026-10-31)

- **Gerber needs a jump**: where 4♣ is a jump it is Gerber, where it is
  not it is a slam try. So 1♣–2NT–4♣ is Gerber (a jump over 2NT), and
  on the default cards 2♣–2♦–3NT–4♣ stays the club slam try; after
  their overcall (2♣ (2♥) P P 3NT) 4♣ is now the club slam try too
  (over-3nt.bid).
- Over interference to 1NT (a double or any two-level overcall,
  including 2♣) 4♣ stays Gerber.
- The Brill card keeps Gerber over 3NT (the 3NT opening and opener's
  3NT rebid after 2♣): there Rusty's partner is a Brill robot, which
  reads 4♣ as Gerber by its own rules. A partnership treatment, not
  the general principle.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The Impossible 2♠ (Robert Todd, "The Impossible ♠ Bid", Adventures in
# Bridge TWiB 269; GIB's "Impossible spade"): after 1♥–1NT, responder has
# denied four spades, so a later 2♠ over opener's 2♣ or 2♦ cannot be
# natural. It shows a good raise of opener's minor: four or more, the top
# of the 1NT response, and forcing to three of the minor. The plain raise
# to 3m stays the lesser raise (responder-rebids.bid). Only after a 1♥
# opening (over 1♠, 2♠ is a preference) and only over a minor rebid: our
# 1NT denies three hearts, so Todd's 1♥–1NT–2♥–2♠ (a three-card limit
# raise) has no hand here. See impossible-2s.notes.md.

module impossible-2s "Impossible 2♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/impossible_2s
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/impossible_2s

# ── Responder: the good raise ────────────────────────────────────────
# Our 1NT is 6-10 HCP, so the raise to 3m (9-10 points) is the courtesy
# raise and 2♠ takes the 11+ hands (10 HCP and a fifth trump, or a
# sixth). Without the convention they raise to 3m (responder-rebids.bid).
# Priority 1: the 6-12 1NT of the 2/1 cards brought a natural 11-12 HCP
# raise to 3m (responder-rebids.bid, 2026-09-30) that outranked 2♠ on
# description and took every hand, so switching the convention off
# changed nothing (convention score, 2026-10-07).
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P)
  2S  "Impossible 2♠: good raise of {m}, 4+ {m}, 11+ points"  alert
      shows m>=4, H<=2, points>=11
      sets  trump=m, forcing=round
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Opener answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Responder has 11-13 with the fit, so opener goes to game with 15+
# support points (HCP and shortness: a 5-4-3-1 twelve-count, a 5-4-2-2
# thirteen; GIB's minimum is 12-13 total points): 3NT with both unbid suits stopped, otherwise the
# stopper he has (up the line, looking for 3NT, with the minor as the
# fallback; responder answers in responder-rebids.bid), otherwise five
# of the minor. With a minimum he signs off in three of the minor.
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2S (P)
  3C  "Minimum: no game opposite the good raise"
      shows tp(C)<=14
      sets  ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 15+, spades and diamonds stopped"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(S), stop(D)
  3D  "Diamond stopper, not spades: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(D), !stop(S)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  3S  "Spade stopper, not diamonds: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(C)>=15, stop(S), !stop(D)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  5C  "Game in clubs: 15+, neither suit stopped"
      shows tp(C)>=15
      priority -1
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)
  3D  "Minimum: no game opposite the good raise"
      shows tp(D)<=14
      sets  ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 15+, spades and clubs stopped"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(S), stop(C)
  3C  "Club stopper, not spades: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(C), !stop(S)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  3S  "Spade stopper, not clubs: looking for 3NT"
      shows tp(D)>=15, stop(S), !stop(C)
      sets  ask=stoppers, ladder=stopper, forcing=game
  5D  "Game in diamonds: 15+, neither suit stopped"
      shows tp(D)>=15
      priority -1

# ── Responder after opener's minimum ─────────────────────────────────
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 3m (P)
  P   "Opener is minimum: play three of {m}"

# ── Responder after opener's game ────────────────────────────────────
after 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 3N (P) | 1H (P) 1N (P) 2m (P) 2S (P) 5m (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# Impossible 2♠ — notes

After 1♥–1NT responder has denied four spades, so 2♠ over opener's 2♣ or
2♦ cannot be natural: it is a good raise of opener's minor. Card field
`major_openings.impossible_2s.play`; BBA's `.bbsa` key `Imposible 2S`
(sic) maps to it (on in 9 of the PBS cards, 21GF-DEFAULT among them).

## Sources

Rick (2026-09-28) pointed to two sources; the key was mapped on their
authority.

- **Robert S. Todd, "The Impossible ♠ Bid"**, Adventures in Bridge, This
  Week in Bridge (269), level 3
  (<https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5127d3d2e4b0b304f0b6db24/t/5c8e551f104c7b066eb43ac8/1552831776048/3+%28269%29+The+Impossilbe+Spade+Bid+.pdf>).
  After 1♥–1NT (forcing or semi-forcing) – 2♣: "3♣ Courtesy Raise, 4+card
  ♣, 8-9 pts"; "2♠ Limit Raise, 4+card ♣, 10-11 pts (Impossible ♠)". The
  same over 2♦. Over opener's 2♥ (11-14, six hearts) the two raises
  describe the fit instead: 3♥ invitational with two hearts, 2♠ a limit
  raise with three, both 10-11. "In all of these auctions the impossible
  ♠ shows the best raise possible, given the context of the auction!"
  No follow-ups are given, and nothing after a 1♠ opening.
- **GIB** (BBO's bidding database, read through
  <https://netbridge.dk/gib.html>, which queries
  `gibrest.bridgebase.com/u_bm/u_bm.php`; fetched 2026-09-28):
  - 1♥–1NT–2♣–2♠: "Impossible spade -- 4+ ♣; 2- ♥; 3- ♠; 11-12 total
    points; forcing to 3C". The same over 2♦ ("forcing to 3D"). 3m there
    is "5+, 8-12 total points"; 2NT a balanced invitation, 10+ HCP.
  - Opener's answers: 3m minimum (12-13 total points); 3♥ six hearts,
    12-13; 2NT 15-17 HCP, partial stoppers, forcing to 3m; 3NT 16+ HCP;
    the other minor natural and forcing; 3♠ "4+ ♠".
  - Responder then: pass 3m; over 2NT, 3NT with 10+ HCP, 3m with five.
  - Not over 1♠ (1♠–1NT–2m–2♠ is "2-3 ♠, 6-9 HCP") and not over 1♥–1NT–2♥
    (2♠ there is natural-ish: "3 ♠, 8-12 total points").

**Where they differ.** Todd's 2♠ is 10-11 with four trumps and his 3m the
8-9 courtesy raise; GIB's 2♠ is 11-12 total points and its 3m is a
five-card raise over the whole 8-12 range. Todd also plays 2♠ over 2♥
(three-card limit raise); GIB does not. GIB defines opener's answers,
Todd gives none. Neither uses it after 1♠.

The PBS scenario (`btn/Impossible_2S.btn`) cites a third source, a Kiva
Bridge Club PDF, whose 2♠ over 1♥–1NT–2♥ shows 6-5 or better in the
minors. Not implemented.

## What we play

- Responder, after 1♥–1NT–2♣/2♦: 2♠ with 4+ of opener's minor and 11+
  total points (our 1NT is 6-10 HCP, so this is 10 HCP and a fifth trump,
  or 9 with a sixth). Forcing one round, the minor agreed. The raise to 3m
  stays at 9-10: Todd's courtesy raise, one point up because our points
  count length. Before this, 11+ hands had no call and passed 2m.
- Opener: 3m with 14 or fewer support points (HCP plus shortness);
  with 15+, 3NT holding both unbid suits, else the stopper he has (up the
  line, `ask=stoppers`), else five of the minor. Responder answers a
  stopper bid in responder-rebids.bid (`when asked stoppers`), with
  3NT, the next stopper or 5m.
- Responder passes 3m, 3NT and 5m.
- Only after 1♥, only over a minor rebid. Todd's 2♠ over 2♥ has no hand
  here: our 1NT over 1♥ denies three hearts (the three-card raises go
  through 2♥ or 3♥).
- When the opponents play it, their 2♠ is read with their card: over
  1♥–1NT–2♣ it shows 4+ clubs and ≤2 hearts, not spades (checked with
  `rbb call ... --ew-card 21GF-DEFAULT`; with Basic-Bridge for EW the
  same 2♠ has no rule).

## BBA (probes, 21GF-DEFAULT, 2026-09-28)

BBA's note on the call is "limit raise or better in !C" (142 corpus
boards in Impossible_2S) or "!D" (12).

- `probes/imp2s-resp-1H-1N-2C.toml` (200 responders, 6-12 HCP, ≤2 hearts,
  4+ clubs): BBA bids 2♠ from about 11 points with five clubs, and from 12
  with four; with four clubs and two hearts it prefers 2♥ up to 11; 3♣ is
  five clubs and 10-11. Every one of BBA's 79 2♠ calls is ours too;
  agreement 24/200 before, 100/200 after. The rest are the existing
  raise/preference rules (BBA 2♥ or pass where we raise to 3♣ with four
  clubs), untouched here.
- `probes/imp2s-opener-1H-1N-2C-2S.toml` (200 openers, 11-18, 5♥ 4+♣):
  BBA treats 2♠ as nearly forcing to game. 3♣ only with a poor 11; then
  3♥ ("biddable suit", 87), 4NT keycard (39), 3♠/3♦ ("en passant"), 5♣,
  3NT. Agreement 54/200. **Accepted difference**: we sign off in 3♣ with
  up to 14 support points (39 hands where BBA goes on), following GIB's
  12-13 minimum; responder has at most 10 HCP. For Rick: the corpus cannot
  settle this (see below); a par study on dealt hands could.

## Corpus (2026-09-28)

Full corpus, `--pbs` Practice-Bidding-Scenarios: vs BBA −114,604 →
−114,581 (+23 IMPs); 18 boards change, all at 1♥–1NT; sideimps.py
+12 IMPs to the side that changed its call. Calls agreeing +337.
Impossible_2S itself: calls agreeing 72.1% → 75.8% (NS 44.2% → 51.6%),
contracts unchanged: the scenario's responder has 11-12 HCP and BBA's
forcing 1NT, where ours bids 2♣/2♦ at once (the 1NT response is 6-10), so
our auctions seldom reach the position.

## Convention score (2026-10-07)

The first run (`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only impossible-2s`) found our
auctions identical with the card field on and off: on the 2/1 cards the
6-12 1NT had brought a natural "3m: 4+, 11-12 HCP" raise into
responder-rebids.bid (2026-09-30) that outranked 2♠ on description and
took all its hands. 2♠ now has priority 1. Without the convention the
11+ hands raise to 3m (responder-rebids.bid: "4+, 11+ points", for any
card, so the old gap where they passed is closed). After the fix the
switch changes 463 of 500 boards (BBA's 154): Rusty +250, BBA +6, net
+244 = +0.53 a changed board, both halves positive ("good").

## Gaps

- On the 2/1 cards the 1NT is 6-12 and the scenario's 11-12 responders
  now reach 2♠; the "6-10" in "What we play" is the standard card's 1NT.
- Todd's 2♥ variant and Kiva's 6-5 variant: not built.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Ingberman 2NT (Lebensohl over opener's reverse; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/ingberman; Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge #417,
# "Lebensohl over Reverses"): after 1x-1y-2z, a reverse (17+, forcing one
# round), responder's 2NT is artificial and weak and asks opener for 3♣;
# responder then passes with clubs or signs off in three of a suit. Every
# other call above 2NT is natural and game forcing; responder's rebid of
# his own suit at the two level is five or more and forcing one round.
# Not played over interference. See ingberman.notes.md.

module ingberman "Ingberman 2NT after opener's reverse"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/ingberman
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/ingberman

# A reverse is the one two-level new suit that forces one round: a jump
# shift forces to game, and a new suit below the first does not force.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y, we.forcing = round, !tw(x)
  2N  "Ingberman: weak, relay to 3♣"   alert
      shows points<=8
      sets  ask=ingberman
      artificial
      priority 2
  2y  "Five or more {y}, forcing one round"
      shows y>=5, points>=6
      sets  forcing=round, ask=ing_suit
      priority 3
  3x  "Three or more {x}: game forcing"
      shows x>=3, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3z  "Four or more {z}: game forcing"
      shows z>=4, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game, trump=z
      priority 3
  3y  "Six or more {y}: game forcing"
      shows y>=6, points>=9
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3N  "Game: no fit, 9+"
      shows points>=9, z<=3
      priority 1

when asked ingberman
  3C  "Forced: 3♣ as asked"   alert
      artificial

# Responder signs off: pass with clubs, else three of a suit.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when answered ingberman
  3z  "Weak, four or more {z}: invitational"   shows z>=4   sets trump=z, ask=invite(z)
      priority 3
  3y  "Weak, six or more {y}: to play"         shows y>=6   sets ask=signoff
      priority 2
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                 shows C>=2
      when  x is C
      priority 1
  3x  "Weak: to play in {x}"                   shows x>=2   sets ask=signoff
      when  x is not C
      priority 1
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                 shows C>=5
      when  x is not C
      priority 2

# Opener over the forcing 2y: support, a longer suit, or 2NT without.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) when asked ing_suit
  3y  "Three-card support for {y}"         shows y>=3
      sets  trump=y
      priority 2
  3x  "Six or more {x}"                    shows x>=6, y<=2
      priority 1
  3z  "Five or more {z}"                   shows z>=5, y<=2
      priority 1
  3N  "19+, no fit"                        shows hcp>=19, y<=2
  2N  "No fit for {y}"       shows y<=2
      priority -1
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=8
      priority -5
  3y  "Six or more {y}: to play"           shows y>=6, points<=8   sets ask=signoff
  3N  "Game: 9+"                           shows points>=9
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3y (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=7
      priority -5
  4y  "Game"                               shows points>=8
      when  y is H | y is S
  3N  "Game"                               shows points>=8
      when  y is C | y is D
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) when answered ing_suit
  P   "Weak: no game"                      shows points<=7
      priority -5
  3N  "Game"                               shows points>=8

# ingberman (`ingberman.bid`): notes

Ingberman 2NT (`other_conventions.ingberman_2nt.play`): after opener's
reverse (1x-1y-2z, 17+, forcing one round), responder's 2NT is weak
(up to 8 total points) and asks for 3♣. Cases: `ingberman.test`. No PBS
scenario, and no stock card switches it on.

## Structure

- A reverse is recognised as the two-level new suit that leaves the
  auction forcing one round (`we.forcing = round`): jump shifts force to
  game, lower new suits do not force.
- After 2NT-3♣ responder passes with clubs (opener's first suit, or five
  of them), signs off in three of opener's first suit, bids three of the
  reverse suit with four (invitational: opener passes a minimum reverse),
  or three of his own six-card suit.
- 2y (his own suit): five or more, forcing one round; opener raises with
  three, shows six of his first suit or five of the reverse suit, 3NT
  with 19+, else 2NT, which responder passes with 8 or less.
- 3x, 3z, 3y and 3NT: natural and game forcing, 9+.
- Off over interference (field definition is silent; Todd describes the
  uncontested reverse).

## Questions for Rick

- The weak threshold: Todd's "5 to 7-" points. We use up to 8 total
  points (opener's 17 plus 8 is game). Decision taken: 8.
- Opener always bids 3♣ over 2NT, even with a game-forcing reverse
  (19+); some play that opener may then bid on. Decision: always 3♣;
  responder's invitational 3z lets a strong opener bid game.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only ingberman`.
IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer;
"actor" is the side that made the first differing call. There is a
scenario after all: Reverse_By_Opener and Reverse_After_Two_Over_One:
301 boards changed; actor contract +116, double-dummy +138, halves
+30/+86 (z +1.5): leans gain.

## Sources

- **Robert S. Todd, "Lebensohl over Reverses", Adventures in Bridge #417**
  (https://www.advinbridge.com/this-week-in-bridge/417): 2NT relay with a
  bad hand, sign-offs after 3♣, everything above 2NT game forcing, the
  two-level rebid of responder's suit forcing one round.
- **"25 More Bridge Conventions You Should Know"**, chapter 11 (cited by
  convention-card `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/ingberman.toml`);
  not consulted directly.

# inverted-minors (`inverted-minors.bid`): notes

## Why (2026-09-25)

The card field `minor_openings.inverted_minors.play` was mapped from
`.bbsa` but read by nothing. On 21GF-DEFAULT (inverted minors on),
responder had no rule with a long fit and game values: about 600
corpus boards after 1C-P and 1D-P where BBA bid.

## BBA's treatment (probes/minor-resp-inv-1C.toml, 1D; inv-opener-1C, 1D)

**Responder:**
- 2m: 10+ HCP, four or more of the minor, no four-card major, forcing.
- 3m: weak, 5-9 with five or more.
- With four diamonds over 1C, 1D comes first.
- 1NT over 1m gives way to the raise with five of the minor.

**Opener after 1m-2m** (BBA's meanings):

| Call | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 2D/2H/2S | "stopper", up the line; the usual call with 15-17 |
| 2NT | balanced, 11-15 (12-14 in practice) |
| 3m | minimum, five or more |
| 3 of a new suit | shortness (splinter), four trumps |
| 3NT | 18-19 balanced |
| 4m | slam try, 16+ |

**Ours:** the same frame, with simpler stopper bids: the cheapest
stopper when opener has 15+ or is unbalanced. Responder then bids 2NT
(10-12 balanced), 3NT (13+) or 3m. Agreement with BBA: responder
65-78%, opener ~42% (BBA's stopper choice is finer).

Corpus, together with the Basic-Bridge fixes below: -163,528 ->
-162,699 (+829).

## Without inverted minors (Basic-Bridge, probes/minor-resp-std-1C.toml)

- **3m limit raise:** now 10-12 HCP. Total points passed six clubs with
  10-12.
- **3NT:** the fallback with 13+, a fit and no major, as BBA. We had no
  call.

## Convention score (2026-10-07)

`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only inverted-minors` (Inverted_Minors, 500
boards): -1.11 IMPs per changed board before (Rusty -323, BBA +208, 479
boards), -0.14 after (Rusty +142, BBA +208; halves +24/-90, differ),
fair. What was wrong:

- **Responder stopped short of game.** Over opener's 2NT (12-14
  balanced) responder bid 3NT only from 13; the 11-12 counts the scenario
  deals passed 2NT, where 3NT makes about half the time with the
  nine-card minor fit (corpus DD: 11 HCP 49%, 12 HCP 54%), and our own
  off run (2NT invitation, opener accepts from 13) reached it. Now 3NT
  from 12, or 11 with a fifth trump; over opener's 3m (minimum,
  unbalanced) 3NT from 12 with both majors held.
- **Opener's 4m slam try was passed**: responder had no rule there and
  played 4m with 26-29 HCP between the hands (5m made on 14 of 15). Now
  5m declines; the keycard rules take a hand with more.
- **Opener bid 3NT over the weak 3m with 14** (rebids.bid's acceptance
  of the standard limit raise). Opposite 5-9 game now needs 18: 3NT
  balanced, 5m otherwise, else pass.
- Opener had no rule after 2NT-3m or a splinter-4m: pass.
- The off run (no inverted minors) had no response with 11-12, four
  diamonds and five clubs over 1♦ on a 2/1 card: a limit raise 3♦ now
  (responses.bid). That made our off run better, so it lowered our gain
  (from +192 to +142) without changing any inverted auction.

Tripwire (`compare --limit 50`, all scenarios): the 3NT-from-12 changes
other inverted-minor scenarios (1m-2N 17 boards -28 errors,
Vics_Bal_Resp_to_1m 7 boards -30): a coin flip on those deals. Kept,
as par on the Inverted_Minors deals favours it; a question for Rick.

## The plain raise blocks stay out (2026-10-29)

rebids.bid's `after 1x (P) 2x (P)` and `after 1m (P) 2m (P)`, and
responder-rebids.bid's `after 1m (P) 2m (P) 3m (P)`, were written for the
plain raise and also read the inverted one: `1D P 2D P 2N` was read as
12-14 here and 18-19 there (the table heard "11-19 HCP"), and `1D P 2D P
3D` as a minimum and as a game try. They now need `!inverted`
(`minor_openings.inverted_minors.play`). Found by the description pass
(sibling rules telling the table nothing). Compare --limit 50 with the two
other fixes of that day: 51 boards, errors +74 IMPs to us.

## Sources

- **The convention:** inverted minor raises. The structure is modelled on
  BBA's treatment, learned by probing; otherwise standard practice, not
  yet cited to a book or article. The game thresholds after opener's
  rebid (12 opposite 2NT, 18 opposite the weak raise) are par on the
  Inverted_Minors corpus deals (2026-10-07), not a cited source.
- **Rick's rulings:** none recorded for this module.
- **BBA probes:** `probes/minor-resp-inv-1C.toml`,
  `probes/minor-resp-inv-1D.toml`, `probes/inv-opener-1C.toml`,
  `probes/inv-opener-1D.toml`; without inverted minors (Basic-Bridge),
  `probes/minor-resp-std-1C.toml`. Opener's meanings are BBA's alerts.
- **Corpus measurements:** 2026-09-25, with the Basic-Bridge fixes
  (+829).
- **Where we differ:** opener's stopper bids are simpler than BBA's (the
  cheapest stopper with 15+ or an unbalanced hand), so opener agrees
  about 42% of the time.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module jacoby-transfers "Jacoby Transfers"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers
  skill  partnership_bidding/stayman_transfers
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_double = vs_double default false
  param  vs_2c = vs_2c default false
  param  style = general.style
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments

# The transfer is a question: "bid my suit". Opener's next call answers it,
# whether a plain completion or a super-accept.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2H  "Transfer to spades, 5-5 in the majors"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5, H>=5
      when  style is bba                  # BBA transfers to spades first with 5-5
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)
      artificial

# Opener completes the transfer. Super-accepts are separate modules
# (super-accept.bid, superaccept-doubleton.bid), switched on by the card.
after nt1 2D (P)
  2H  "Completes transfer"
      when  system is not brill
after nt1 2H (P)
  2S  "Completes transfer"
      when  system is not brill

# brill (the Brill card): the plain completion denies four trumps, except
# with 4-3-3-3 and a minimum. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "No superaccept":
# `hearts < 4 or (not max and ExplicitShape == '3=4=3=3')` (spades:
# `spades < 4 or (not max and ExplicitShape == '4=3=3=3')`). The other
# four-trump hands super-accept: super-accept.bid, superaccept-doubleton.bid.
after nt1 2D (P) when system is brill
  2H  "Completes transfer: 2-3 ♥, or a minimum 3=4=3=3"
      shows H<=3 | (H=4, shortest=3, hcp<=15)
after nt1 2H (P) when system is brill
  2S  "Completes transfer: 2-3 ♠, or a minimum 4=3=3=3"
      shows S<=3 | (S=4, shortest=3, hcp<=15)

# Responder's second call, once opener has answered. There is no auction
# pattern: `answered transfer(M)` holds after any auction where partner
# answered my transfer, and binds M to the major.
#
# `strength` bands are measured against what opener has shown: after a
# 15-17 1NT, invite is 8-9 and game 10-15; after a maximum super-accept the
# invitational band shrinks, so invitational hands bid game. Notrump
# decisions use `strength`, total points (HCP + ½ per ten + 1 per card
# beyond four, so the fifth card of the major counts); playing in the major
# uses `suit_strength` (HCP + ½ per card beyond four).
when answered transfer(M)
  3M  "Sign off in the known fit"              shows suit_strength=signoff
      when partner.M>=4, !(partner.last=2{M})  # after a 2S or 2NT super-accept, not Brill's plain 4-card completion
  4M  "Game: in the fit, opposite a super-accept"  shows suit_strength=invite
      when partner.M>=4                        # the super-accept is for thin games
  P   "Weak: to play, {signoff} total points"  shows strength=signoff
      when maybe partner.M<=3 | partner.last=3{M}   # never pass an artificial super-accept (2S, 2NT)
      when !passes_out_artificial                   # nor my own transfer, doubled and passed back (base.bid)
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points, exactly 5 {M}"  shows M=5, balanced | shortest>=2, strength=invite
      sets ask=invite(M)
  3M  "Invitational: {invite} total points, 6+ {M}"  shows M>=6, suit_strength=invite
      when partner.last=2{M}                   # after a super-accept 3M is the sign-off
      sets ask=invite(M)
  # Six cards and a count between the two measures: too much to pass in
  # total points (the sixth card counts two), too little to invite in
  # suit points (it counts one). J85.KJ9754.6.J52 (6 HCP) had no call at all
  # (convention score, 2026-10-07: 6 no-rule boards with Texas, 26
  # without; 13 without super-accepts, whose plain completion is then
  # the whole 1NT range). HCP decide, as for the five-card hands below.
  3M  "Invitational: 6+ {M}"                   shows M>=6, strength>=invite, suit_strength=signoff, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      when partner.last=2{M}
      sets ask=invite(M)
      priority -1
  P   "Weak in HCP: play here"                 shows M>=6, strength>=invite, suit_strength=signoff, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      when partner.last=2{M}
      priority -1
  3N  "Choice of games: 5 {M}, {game} total points"  shows M=5, balanced, strength=game
      when maybe partner.M<=2                  # only while the fit is unknown
      sets ask=choice                          # opener corrects with 3+ {M}
  4M  "Game: {game} total points, 6+ {M}"      shows M>=6, suit_strength=game
      when !texas_1nt                              # with Texas, game-only hands use it
  4M  "Game: 6+ {M}, mild slam interest"             shows M>=6, suit_points>=31-partner.points.max, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when texas_1nt                               # 14-17 opposite 15-17: slam if opener has
                                               # the right hand; Texas is for 18+
      sets ask=slam_try(M)
  4M  "Game: {game} total points, 6+ {M}"      shows M>=6, suit_strength=game
      when texas_1nt                               # game-only hands normally use Texas
      priority -1                              # a fallback: 4M still reads as the slam try
  4M  "Game: in the known fit"                  shows suit_strength=game
      when partner.M>=3                        # known, e.g. after a super-accept
  # Without Texas the slam hands with six come through the transfer too
  # (convention score, 2026-10-07: 39 had no rule). Five of the major
  # invites six; six bids it.
  5M  "Slam invitation: 6+ {M}"                shows M>=6, suit_strength=slam_invite
      when !texas_1nt, partner.last=2{M}
      sets ask=major_slam_invite(M)
  6M  "Slam: 6+ {M}"                           shows M>=6, suit_strength>=slam
      when !texas_1nt, partner.last=2{M}
  3m  "Second suit, game forcing"              shows m>=4, strength>=game
      sets forcing=game, ask=new_suit(M)
  4N  "Quantitative, 5 {M}"                    shows M=5, balanced, strength=slam_invite
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets ask=quant_major(M)
  6N  "Slam: {slam} total points, 5 {M}"       shows M=5, balanced, strength=slam
  # Invitational in total points only through length (5-5 with a
  # singleton, 6 HCP): no natural invitation fits. BBA passes.
  P   "Weak in HCP: play here"                 shows M=5, strength=invite, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
      when maybe partner.M<=3 | partner.last=3{M}
      priority -1
  # With a singleton and a real invitation in HCP, BBA bids 2NT anyway
  # (Basic_Openers_Rebid 172, KT432.Q32.2.QJ93).
  2N  "Invitational, exactly 5 {M}, a singleton"   shows M=5, strength=invite, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
      sets ask=invite(M)
      priority -1

# Opener's answer to the invitation (`when asked invite(M)`) is a base
# rule in rebids.bid: it answers any invitation in a major, transfers or
# not.

# Opener answers the quantitative 4NT with five in the major: slam with
# 32 combined. Double dummy on dealt hands (probes/dd/quant-4nt-hearts.toml,
# jacoby-transfers.notes.md, 2026-10-03): the doubleton is what makes the
# major worth playing. A fit and a doubleton count the doubleton (`tp`),
# so a minimum with one accepts in the major; 4-3-3-3 has no ruffing value
# and plays notrump, or passes with a minimum. At IMPs the major with
# four trumps, or three below a maximum; 6NT otherwise and at matchpoints.
# 5M (to play, a minimum) never beat the better of pass and slam.
when asked quant_major(M)
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: four trumps, a doubleton"
      shows M>=4, shortest=2, points>=32-partner.points.min
      when  imps
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: three trumps, a doubleton, not a maximum"
      shows M=3, shortest=2, points>=32-partner.points.min, hcp<=shown.hcp.max-1
      when  imps
  6M  "Accepts in {M}: a fit and a doubleton"
      shows M>=3, shortest=2, points<=31-partner.points.min, tp(M)>=32-partner.points.min
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows points>=32-partner.points.min
  P   "Declines"                        shows points<=31-partner.points.min

# Opener after responder's second suit (game forcing): rebid the major with
# three-card support, which agrees it below game so that responder can look
# for slam; otherwise 3NT.
when asked new_suit(M)
  3M  "3+ {M}: support"             shows M>=3   sets trump=M
  3N  "No fit: 2 {M}"               shows M<=2

# Responder over opener's 3NT, with the 5-4 shown (Rick, 2026-11-06,
# bridge-classroom #85: AKT76.A95.9.AJ94 passed 3NT opposite 17 and
# 6NT made; "Rusty should invite slam here"). over-3nt.bid counts HCP
# for a balanced hand; this hand has shown its shape, and its fifth
# major card is a trick in notrump too, so it counts total points:
# 32 on opener's floor invites with a quantitative 4NT, 34 bids six.
# This 4NT takes over over-3nt.bid's (which counts HCP) in this auction,
# so opener reads one meaning. He accepts in points, one more than the
# textbook 32 on responder's floor (17 shown: a 16-count with two tens
# or a fifth card accepts, a flat 15 declines), in the minor with four
# of it (a 4-4 fit takes a ruff), else 6NT.
when answered new_suit(M), partner.last=3N, !they.bid
  6N  "Small slam: 5-4 shown, {slam} total points"
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 34
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT, 5-4 shown"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 32, points + partner.hcp.min <= 33
      sets  ask=quant_two_suits

when asked quant_two_suits
  6C  "Accepts, in clubs: four clubs"     shows C>=4, points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.C>=4
      priority 1
  6D  "Accepts, in diamonds: four diamonds"  shows D>=4, points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.D>=4
      priority 1
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"       shows points>=33-partner.points.min
  P   "Declines"                          shows points<=32-partner.points.min

# Opener after the jump to game with mild slam interest: bid on with a good
# fit and a maximum, even without having super-accepted.
when asked slam_try(M)
  4N  "Keycard ask: good fit and a maximum"   shows M>=3, points>=31-partner.suit_points.min
      sets ask=keycards(M)
      artificial
  P   "No slam: plays game"

# Opener answers five of the major: six unless minimum.
when asked major_slam_invite(M)
  6M  "Accepts the slam invitation: not a minimum"   shows hcp>=shown.hcp.max-1
  P   "Declines: a minimum"           shows hcp<=shown.hcp.max-2

# BBA's treatment (probed 2026-09-24, jacoby-transfers.notes.md), our
# default since Rick's ruling the same day: with five hearts, four spades
# and 7-9 HCP transfer rather than bid Stayman, then show the spades. The 2S is not forcing: opener passes
# with three spades and two hearts. He prefers hearts: game with four,
# or with three and 17; with four spades (two hearts) game from 16.
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P)
  2S  "5 hearts and 4 spades, invitational, not forcing"
      shows H=5, S=4, hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min

after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P)
  4H  "Accepts, in the heart fit"      shows H>=4 | (H=3, points>=24-partner.hcp.min)
  3H  "Declines, in the heart fit"     shows H=3, points<=23-partner.hcp.min
  4S  "Accepts, in the spade fit"      shows S>=4, H<=2, points>=23-partner.hcp.min
  3S  "Declines, in the spade fit"     shows S>=4, H<=2, points<=22-partner.hcp.min
  P   "No eight-card fit: play 2S"     shows H<=2, S<=3

# Responder bids game over the decline with the top of the range.
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Game: the top of the invitation"  shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
  P   "Minimum: play 3H"                 shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max
after 1N (P) 2D (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Game: the top of the invitation"  shows hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max
  P   "Minimum: play 3S"                 shows hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max

# ── Under interference ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# `transfers.vs_double` and `transfers.vs_2c` say the transfers survive
# RHO's double or 2♣ overcall. They keep their own calls in both cases:
# 2♦ for hearts and 2♥ for spades. Opener completes as usual; the
# super-accepts are not written for these auctions, so he simply bids
# the major. One `after` line takes one `when`, so the double and the
# 2♣ overcall are two contexts.

# With both majors, transfer to the longer, and to spades when they are
# equal: that is what BBA does under interference, and the higher suit
# leaves us better placed if they bid again. (Uncontested, Stayman comes
# first with 5-4 for Smolen; here it does not.)
after 1N (X) when vs_double
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5  when S>=H  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5  when H>S   sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial

# Over the 2♣ overcall the transfer has a floor of five HCP: below that
# BBA leaves the auction alone rather than push to the two level with
# nothing. (Over the double there is no floor — running is the point.)
after 1N (2C) when vs_2c
  2H  "Transfer to spades"  announce "Transfer"  shows S>=5, hcp>=5  when S>=H  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(S)  artificial
  2D  "Transfer to hearts"  announce "Transfer"  shows H>=5, hcp>=5  when H>S   sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(H)  artificial

after 1N (X) 2D (P) when vs_double
  2H  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (X) 2H (P) when vs_double
  2S  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (2C) 2D (P) when vs_2c
  2H  "Completes transfer"
after 1N (2C) 2H (P) when vs_2c
  2S  "Completes transfer"

# jacoby-transfers (`jacoby-transfers.bid`): notes

2D/2H transfers over 1NT, the completion, responder's second call, and
opener's answers to invitations and to the mild slam try. The
super-accepts are separate modules. Cases: `jacoby-transfers.test`.

## Guidance

- The transfer is forcing; opener completes (or super-accepts).
- Responder's second call is one `when answered transfer(M)` block, with
  no auction patterns. Notrump decisions (2NT, 3NT) use total points (HCP
  + ½ per ten + 1 per card beyond four, since 2026-09-23). Decisions to
  play in the major use **suit points: HCP + ½ per card beyond four**.
- **8 HCP with a six-card major invites** (transfer, then 3M): 8 HCP + 1 for
  length is 9 suit points.
- 3NT with exactly five offers a choice; opener corrects to 4M with three
  (`choice-of-games.bid`).
- **Mild slam interest** (six-card major, 14–17 suit points): transfer,
  then jump to 4M. Opener bids on (4NT keycard) with 3+ trumps and a
  maximum. Game-only hands and slam hands (18+: Texas needs 33 even opposite
  a 15 minimum) use Texas (`texas-transfers.bid`).
- **Responder's new suit (3m) is game forcing** (Rick, 2026-09-21). Opener
  rebids the major with three-card support, which agrees it below game so
  responder can look for slam; otherwise 3NT.
- Opener plays in the major with an eight-card fit: three opposite five,
  two opposite six. Without a fit he accepts only when game is certain
  (17 opposite 8–9); with the fit, 16 is enough (2026-09-23, below).
- After a super-accept (a known fit of nine or more) responder counts suit
  points. Opposite that maximum, invitational values bid game: the
  super-accept exists to reach thin games.

## Evidence from BBA

Probes (21GF-DEFAULT), `--prefix "1NT Pass 2D Pass 2H Pass" --dealer S`:

| Hand (then 1–4 more tens) | BBA | Agree |
|---|---|---|
| `82.KJ973.K94.Q83` (9, five hearts) | 2NT with 0–1 tens, 3NT with 2+: tens count at notrump | 5/5 |
| `82.QJ9732.K94.Q8` (8, six hearts) | 3H however many tens: length counts, tens do not | 5/5 |
| `82.Q97532.K94.Q8` (7, six hearts) | 3H, the same | 5/5 |
| `82.K9732.K94.Q83` (8, five hearts) | 2NT with 0–1 tens, **pass** with 2+ | 2/5 |

Jacoby_Transfer (500 boards): 85.9% of calls agree, 29.2% identical
auctions, 39.2% the same contract. Jacoby_Super-Accept: 81.7%, 30.8%, 33.8%.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- **A ten in the trump suit.** `82.KT973.K94.Q83`: BBA passes. With the ten
  in diamonds instead (`82.K9732.KT9.Q83`), BBA invites. It is the same on
  every layout. That looks like an internal quirk of BBA, not a principle,
  so we do not model it.
- With a six-card major, BBA's choice between Jacoby and Texas differs from
  ours at 8 and at 10–17 (see `texas-transfers.notes.md`).
- **Opener after the new suit**: BBA jumps to 4M with three trumps (106
  Jacoby_Transfer boards); we bid 3M, as Rick plays it. Once 3M agrees the
  suit, BBA's responder sometimes bids 3NT, offering a choice; we bid 4M in the
  known fit.
- After a plain 3M super-accept, which may be a minimum, BBA passes some
  invitational hands where we bid game (8 boards; 24 others go our way).

## Gaps (not built yet)

- **5-4 invitations.** 9 HCP with five spades and four of a minor bids 3m
  for BBA (for example `A6543.7.K43.QT63`). Our 3m is game forcing, so these
  hands need another route (2NT with an unbalanced hand?). For now they
  have no rule and pass the completion (76 boards in Jacoby_Transfer and
  Texas_or_Jacoby).
- **Five-four with game values after a super-accept.** BBA bids 4M; our
  game-forcing 3m ranks higher (17 boards).
- **Opener after 6NT with five**: no correction to 6M yet.

## Under interference (2026-09-23)

`after 1N (X) when vs_double` and `after 1N (2C) when vs_2c` keep the
transfers on their own calls, 2♦ for hearts and 2♥ for spades, with the
completions written for each. Two differences from the uncontested
rules:

- **the longer major wins, and spades when they are equal**
  (`when S>=H` / `when H>S`). Uncontested there is no such tie-break and
  5-5 hands go through Stayman; under interference BBA transfers, and to
  the higher suit. Note that a `prefer S` / `prefer H` pair did **not**
  break the 5-5 tie — the two calls score the same — so the choice is a
  `when` on each rule.
- **over a 2♣ overcall the transfer has a five-HCP floor.** Below that
  BBA leaves their 2♣ alone rather than push to the two level with
  nothing; over a double there is no floor, because running is the
  point.

The super-accepts are not written for these auctions: opener simply
completes. Evidence and numbers: `nt-interference.notes.md`.

and a doubleton −0.8 at 15, −0.1/−0.2 at 16 (a tie), +0.25/+0.5 at 17;

What it says:

- **5♥ never wins.** It beats pass only with four hearts and a doubleton
  (+0.6), and there 6♥ beats it by a further 0.9. Over a 4-3-3-3 it
  loses to 4NT (−0.4 to −0.7 at 15): Rick's instinct about 4-3-3-3 is
  right, and it extends to 4-3-3-3 with four hearts, which is the worst
  slam hand of all (no side four-card suit either).
- **The doubleton is a point.** With a fit and a doubleton a 15-count
  plays slam in hearts (+1.1 to +1.8 against pass); a 4-3-3-3 15-count
  passes. That is opener's support points (`tp(H)`: HCP + 1 for the
  doubleton) reaching the 32 the rule already asks of `points`.
- **The strain:** four trumps and a doubleton play hearts; three trumps
  and a doubleton hearts below a maximum, notrump with 17; 4-3-3-3 and
  two hearts notrump. At matchpoints 6NT outscores 6♥ on 54-88 % of the
  boards in every class, so the major is an IMP choice; the 15-count's
  slam on the doubleton stays in hearts (6♥ beats pass on 57-60 %, 6NT
  only 42-52 %).
- **Opposite responder's 16 or 17** (`--by N.h --by S.pts`): 15 + a
  doubleton opposite 16 is close to even (+0.05 to +0.34), opposite 17
  +2.6 to +4.1; 32 combined in `tp` is the right line. 4-3-3-3 with four
  hearts and 16 opposite 16 loses even in 6NT (−1.0 ±0.4); not split
  out, since opener cannot tell 16 from 17.

The rule (`when asked quant_major(M)`): at IMPs 6M with four trumps and a
doubleton, or three and a doubleton below opener's maximum; 6M with a fit,
a doubleton and a minimum that the doubleton lifts to 32 (`tp(M)`), at
either scoring; 6NT on any other acceptance; pass otherwise. No 5M.
Spades: the same test (`probes/dd/quant-4nt-spades.toml`), below.

**Spades** (1NT-2♥-2♠-4NT, 1,000 deals per class at 15, 300-650 at 16
and 17): the same picture. 5♠ never best (+0.61 ±0.10 with four spades
and a doubleton at 15, where 6♠ is +1.76); the 15-count with a fit and a
doubleton +1.55 to +1.76 in 6♠ against pass; 4-3-3-3 passes at 15
(−1.3 / −3.1 in slam) and plays 6NT or 6♠ alike above it (6NT − 6♠ +0.1
/ −0.1 ±0.1-0.2); four spades and a doubleton prefer 6♠ at every
strength (6NT − 6♠ −2.3, −1.8, −1.0); three and a doubleton 6♠ at 15-16,
6NT at 17 (+0.3 / +0.6).
