# Polish two-suiters: notes

## Decisions

- 2♥ = five hearts and another five-card suit (spades possible), 2♠ =
  five spades and a five-card minor; 5-11 HCP, seats 1-3, ahead of the
  one-level opening (BBA: 5 HCP opens, 12 opens 1♥;
  probes/polish-openings.toml). Wikipedia says 6-11.
- No weak twos in the majors with this on (preempts.bid); BBA passes a
  weak six-card major (probe).
- Responder (BBA, probes/polish-resp-2H.toml, -2S.toml): pass with
  three hearts / two spades (BBA passes 2♥ even with 13 HCP and three
  hearts); with a misfit 2♠ (over 2♥) or 3♣ (over 2♠) pass-or-correct;
  2NT asks from 15. Wikipedia: over 2♥, 2♠ is pass or correct and 2NT
  asks (3♥ = spades, others natural).
- The 3♥/3♠ preemptive raises and the asker's placements are ours.

## Partial

- No scenario plays these openings as such (Benjamin_2D's card turns
  them on, but its hands are strong). Interference beyond a double, and
  opener's strength after the 2NT ask, are not written.

## Open questions

- Does the 2NT ask also want opener's strength (minimum/maximum)? Not
  in our source; not written.

## Sources

- Wikipedia, "Polish Club", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Club:
  the openings, 2♠ pass-or-correct and the 2NT ask over 2♥.
- BBA probes (21GF-PolishTwoSuiters): probes/polish-openings.toml,
  probes/polish-resp-2H.toml, probes/polish-resp-2S.toml.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Precision 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Precision 2D"): 11-15 HCP, short in
# diamonds, 4-4-1-4 or 4-4-0-5; 4-3-1-5 or 3-4-1-5 when the clubs are
# too weak for a Precision 2♣ (here: fewer than two of the top three).
# Written as an opening on its own; it does not need the forcing 1♣.
# The weak 2♦ is off (preempts.bid).
#
# Responder:
#
#   Pass        six or more diamonds, no interest in the other suits
#   2♥ 2♠ 3♣    natural, sign-off
#   2NT         11+, game forcing, asks:
#               3♣ 3-4-1-5   3♦ 4-3-1-5
#               3♥ 4-4-1-4 11-13   3♠ 4-4-1-4 14-15
#               3NT 4-4-1-4 14-15 with the ♦A or ♦K
#               4♣ 4-4-0-5 11-13   4♦ 4-4-0-5 14-15
#   3♦          six or more diamonds, invites 3NT
#   3♥ 3♠       preemptive
#
# Responder's rebids are natural. See precision-2d.notes.md.

module precision-2d "Precision 2♦"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/precision_2d
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/precision_2d

define prec_2d_shape = (S=4, H=4, D=1, C=4) | (S=4, H=4, D=0, C=5) | (S=4, H=3, D=1, C=5, quality(C)<=fair) | (S=3, H=4, D=1, C=5, quality(C)<=fair)

# ── The opening ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Priority 1: it takes these hands from the one-level openings.
when opening
  2D  "Precision 2♦: 11-15, short diamonds"   alert
      shows hcp=11..15, prec_2d_shape
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2D (P) | 2D (X)
  2N  "Asks for shape and strength: 11+, game forcing"   alert
      shows hcp>=11
      sets  forcing=game, ask=precision_2d
      artificial
  P   "Six or more diamonds: to play"     shows D>=6, hcp<=10
      priority 1
  3D  "Six or more diamonds: invites 3NT"   shows D>=6, hcp=9..10, quality(D)>=good
      priority 1
  3H  "Preemptive: six or more hearts"    shows H>=6, hcp<=8
  3S  "Preemptive: six or more spades"    shows S>=6, hcp<=8
  2S  "Sign-off"                          shows S>=3, S>H, hcp<=10
  2H  "Sign-off"                          shows H>=3, hcp<=10
  3C  "Sign-off"                          shows C>=4, hcp<=10, S<=2, H<=2
  # The best of a bad lot.
  2H  "Sign-off"   shows hcp<=10
      priority -2

# Opener passes the sign-offs.
after 2D (P) 2H (P) | 2D (P) 2S (P) | 2D (P) 3C (P) | 2D (P) 3H (P) | 2D (P) 3S (P) | 2D (X) 2H (P) | 2D (X) 2S (P) | 2D (X) 3C (P)
  P   "No further bid"
# The invitation: 3NT with a maximum and the diamond singleton an honour.
after 2D (P) 3D (P)
  3N  "Accepts: 14-15"     shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines"
      priority -1

# ── Opener answers 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────────
when asked precision_2d
  3C  "3-4-1-5"                       shows S=3, H=4, C=5
  3D  "4-3-1-5"                       shows S=4, H=3, C=5
  3H  "4-4-1-4, 11-13"                shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp<=13
  3S  "4-4-1-4, 14-15"                shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp>=14
  3N  "4-4-1-4, 14-15, the ♦A or ♦K"  shows S=4, H=4, D=1, hcp>=14, has(A,D) | has(K,D)
      priority 1
  4C  "4-4-0-5, 11-13"                shows S=4, H=4, D=0, hcp<=13
  4D  "4-4-0-5, 14-15"                shows S=4, H=4, D=0, hcp>=14

# ── Responder places the contract ────────────────────────────────────
# Opener's shape is known: game in a major with a 4-4 fit (or five
# opposite three), 3NT with diamonds held, else five clubs.
after 2D (P) 2N (P) 3x (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 4x (P) | 2D (P) 2N (P) 3N (P)
  4S  "Game in spades"    shows S>=4 | (S>=5, partner.S>=3)
      when  partner.S>=4 | (partner.S>=3, S>=5)
      priority 2
  4H  "Game in hearts"    shows H>=4 | (H>=5, partner.H>=3)
      when  partner.H>=4 | (partner.H>=3, H>=5)
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: diamonds held"   shows stop(D), D>=3
  5C  "Game in clubs"     shows C>=3
      priority -1
  P   "Partner's 3NT"
      when  partner.last=3N
      priority -1
  3N  "Game in notrump"
      priority -2

# They come in over the sign-off: opener passes (responder may act).
after 2D (P) 2H (*) | 2D (P) 2S (*) | 2D (P) 3C (*)
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5

# Precision 2♦: notes

## Decisions

- 11-15 HCP; 4-4-1-4 or 4-4-0-5; 4-3-1-5 or 3-4-1-5 when the clubs hold
  fewer than two of the top three honours (Bridge Bum: "too weak for a
  Precision 2♣"; we have no Precision 2♣ yet, so this stands in).
  Written as an opening of its own: it does not depend on the forcing
  1♣, and any card with `Precision 2D` turns it on (Precision.bbsa,
  Precision-14-16.bbsa).
- Responses as Bridge Bum: pass with six diamonds; 2♥/2♠/3♣ sign-offs
  (2♥ with equal majors, opener's 3-4-1-5 is as likely as 4-3-1-5); 2NT
  game-forcing ask with Bridge Bum's answers; 3♦ six diamonds inviting
  3NT (opener accepts with 14-15); 3♥/3♠ preemptive.
- After the answer responder places the contract: a known 4-4 major fit
  (or five opposite three), 3NT with diamonds stopped, else 5♣.

## BBA (probes/b2-Precision-openings.toml, 2026-10-05)

- With the Precision card BBA opens 2♦ on 4-4-1-4 and 4-4-0-5 14, as we
  do. With `Precision 2D = 1` set on 21GF-DEFAULT it ignores the key and
  opens 1♣; we honour the field on any card.
- Tripwire (batch-1 baseline): 4 boards in SCS_* now open 2♦ (expected).
  On the Precision card the weak 2♦ is now off (`Weak natural 2D = 0`
  there; before, the default kept it on): five third-seat boards in
  Weak_NT_* that opened a weak 2♦ on a six-card ten-count now pass, where
  BBA opens 3♦. Our three-level preempt wants seven cards (preempts.bid).

## Open questions (decision taken)

- Invitational hands with a major (10-ish and four cards) have no
  natural invite in Bridge Bum's scheme; they sign off at two or use 2NT.
- No defence to interference beyond opener passing.

## Sources

- Bridge Bum, "Precision 2D", https://www.bridgebum.com/precision_2d.php:
  shapes, range, every response and the 2NT answers.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Roudi: after 1m-1M-1NT, responder's 2C is artificial, invitational or
# better, and asks about support and strength. Opener (WB5_Roudi's
# definition, which BBA's corpus follows): 2D minimum without three of
# responder's major, 2H minimum with three, 2S maximum with three, 2NT
# maximum without, three of opener's minor maximum with three and five
# of the minor. Played instead of NMF. See roudi.notes.md.

module roudi "Roudi"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/roudi
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/roudi

after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) when !tw(m)
  2C  "Roudi: invitational or better, asks for support and strength"   alert
      shows M>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4), points>=11
      sets  forcing=round, ask=roudi
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a natural 2NT or 3NT

# Minimum is 12-13 HCP, maximum 14 (the 1NT rebid's range).
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) when !tw(m)
  2D  "Minimum, at most two {M}"           alert   shows hcp<=13, M<=2   artificial
  2H  "Minimum with three {M}"             alert   shows hcp<=13, M=3    artificial
  2S  "Maximum with three {M}"             alert   shows hcp>=14, M=3    artificial
  2N  "Maximum, at most two {M}"           alert   shows hcp>=14, M<=2
  3m  "Maximum with three {M} and five {m}"  alert shows hcp>=14, M=3, m>=5

# Responder. After a minimum: with a fit invite or bid game; without one
# 2NT invites and 3NT is game. After a maximum: game.
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when !tw(m)
  2N  "Invitational, no fit"               shows points=11..12, M<=5   sets ask=nt_invite
  3M  "Invitational: six {M}"              shows M>=6, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(M)
  3N  "Game"                               shows points>=13, M<=5
  4M  "Game: six {M}"                      shows M>=6, points>=13
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2H (P) when !tw(m)
  3M  "Invitational, in the fit"           shows M>=5, points=11..12   sets trump=M, ask=invite(M)
  4M  "Game in the fit"                    shows M>=5, points>=13      sets trump=M
  2N  "Invitational, four {M}"             shows M=4, points=11..12    sets ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game, four {M}"                     shows M=4, points>=13
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2S (P) | 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 3m (P) when !tw(m)
  4M  "Game in the fit"                    shows M>=5                  sets trump=M
  3N  "Game, four {M}"                     shows M=4
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2N (P) when !tw(m)
  4M  "Game: six {M}"                      shows M>=6
  3N  "Game"                               shows M<=5

# roudi (`roudi.bid`): notes

Roudi, card field `other_conventions.roudi.play` (21GF-SPECIALS2).
Cases: `roudi.test`. Scenario: WB5_Roudi.

## Structure

- After 1m-1M-1NT, 2♣ is artificial, invitational or better (11+ total
  points), with five of the major or both majors; ahead of a natural
  2NT/3NT.
- Opener (12-13 minimum, 14 maximum): 2♦ minimum, at most two of
  responder's major; 2♥ minimum with three (whichever major); 2♠ maximum
  with three; 2NT maximum, at most two; 3m maximum with three and five of
  the minor.
- Responder: after a minimum, invite (2NT, or 3M with a fit or six) or bid
  game; after a maximum, game (4M with a fit, else 3NT).
- On, it switches off NMF and the natural 2♣ (responder-rebids.bid).
- Only after a minor opening: on 21GF-SPECIALS2 BBA's 2♣ after
  1♥-1♠-1NT is natural (no alert), so ours is too.

## Corpus (WB5_Roudi, 2026-10-05)

NS calls agreeing 76.2% (all calls 88.1%). The opener's answers match
BBA's alerts on the boards checked. Divergences at the convention's
calls:

- **BBA style:** BBA passes 1NT with 11 total points where we invite
  (2NT or Roudi), and bids Roudi on some 10-counts; it is the existing
  invitation threshold, not Roudi.
- **BBA style:** after 2♥ (minimum, three) BBA's responder bids 2♠, a
  further try, where we invite with 3M or bid game. Not modelled.
- BBA sometimes passes 2♦ with a weak Roudi bid; ours always invites.

## Sources

- **WB5_Roudi scenario** (Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `btn/WB5_Roudi.btn`,
  its chat text): opener's five answers. The BBA corpus agrees with it.
- convention-card `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/roudi.toml` (no
  structure given).
- **Where we differ:** responder's continuations are standard practice,
  not yet cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Smolen. With five cards in one major, four in the other and game values,
# responder bids Stayman (stayman.bid gives 5-4 hands priority for it);
# when opener denies a major, responder bids three of the FOUR-card major,
# showing five of the other. Opener, who has two or three of that suit,
# bids 3NT or game in the 5-3 fit, so the notrump opener declares either
# way. With three spades and a maximum, after 3♥ opener has room to agree
# spades below game (3♠): a slam try. Once a suit is agreed the keycard
# and control-bid modules take over; nothing here names them.
#
# Written against the Stayman question, not the auction: `answered
# majors` with opener's answer denying both majors covers 1NT–2♣–2♦,
# 2NT–3♣–3♦ (Smolen_after_2N) and the same with systems on after
# interference, as BBA plays it. Notes: smolen.notes.md.

module smolen "Smolen: 5-4 in the majors after Stayman's denial"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/smolen
  needs  stayman
  skill  bidding_conventions/smolen
  param  style = general.style

when answered majors, partner.H<=3, partner.S<=3
  3H  "Smolen: four hearts, five spades, game forcing"  alert
      shows H=4, S=5, strength>=game
      when  style is not bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=smolen(S)
      artificial
      priority 1                          # ahead of 3NT, which now denies 5-4
  3S  "Smolen: four spades, five hearts, game forcing"  alert
      shows S=4, H=5, strength>=game
      when  style is not bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=smolen(H)
      artificial
      priority 1
  # BBA (probes/smolen-resp-1N.toml): from 10 HCP opposite 15-17, in
  # HCP; with 8-9 it bids two of the five-card major.
  3H  "Smolen: four hearts, five spades, game forcing"  alert
      shows H=4, S=5, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=smolen(S)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3S  "Smolen: four spades, five hearts, game forcing"  alert
      shows S=4, H=5, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba
      sets  forcing=game, ask=smolen(H)
      artificial
      priority 1

# Opener: two or three cards in responder's five-card major (the 2♦ or
# 3♦ answer denied four). BBA (probes/smolen-opener-3H.toml, 3S): game
# with three, 3NT with two, whatever the strength; after 3♥, 3♠ with
# three spades and a maximum (17 opposite 15-17, every time).
when asked smolen(M)
  3S    "Three spades and a maximum: slam interest"
        shows S>=3, hcp>=shown.hcp.max
        when  M is S
        sets  trump=S
        priority 1                        # ahead of 4S
  4{M}  "Three {M}: game in the five-three fit"
        shows M>=3
        sets  trump=M
  3N    "Two {M}: no fit, play 3NT"
        shows M<=2

# Responder after 3NT: no fit. The slam counts after Stayman apply
# (stayman.bid): 6NT with 32 between us, else pass.
when answered smolen(M), partner.last=3N
  6N  "No fit, but slam values"           shows points>=32-partner.hcp.min
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -5

# smolen (`smolen.bid`): notes

Smolen (card `notrump.smolen.play`; BBA's `SMOLEN`, on 17 of the 18
corpus cards, and on Rick's card). With 5-4 in the majors and game
values responder bids Stayman (`stayman.bid` gives those hands priority
1 for it); over opener's denial he bids three of his **four**-card
major, showing five of the other and forcing to game. Opener bids four
of that major with three, 3NT with two. Opener declares either way.
Cases: `smolen.test`. Built 2026-09-28.

## What the module does

- **Written against the question, not the auction.** The jumps sit
  under `when answered majors, partner.H<=3, partner.S<=3`, so the same
  rules serve 1NT–2♣–2♦, 2NT–3♣–3♦ (Smolen_after_2N) and the same
  auctions with systems on over our 1NT overcall or their double, as BBA
  plays them. The jump sets `forcing=game, ask=smolen(M)` with M the
  five-card major.
- **Opener** (`when asked smolen(M)`): 4M with three, 3NT with two.
  After 3♥ (five spades) there is room for **3♠: three spades and a
  maximum** (`hcp>=shown.hcp.max`), a slam try that agrees spades below
  game. BBA does exactly this (below).
- **Responder** after 3NT passes, or bids 6NT with 32 between the hands
  (the no-fit count after Stayman). After a fit the agreed suit and the
  game force are enough: keycard (`rkcb-1430.bid`), control bids and
  the base game fallback read state, and nothing here names them.
- **Strength.** The default counts total points (`strength>=game`: 10
  opposite 15-17, the fifth card of the major counting), as everywhere
  after 1NT (Rick, 2026-09-23). The `bba` treatment uses HCP, 10
  opposite 15-17, which is what BBA does.
- **Five spades, four hearts, invitational** now bids 2♠ over the 2♦
  denial (`stayman.bid`, `when asked spades_invite`): opener bids game
  with 16-17 (4♠ with three, 3NT with two) and passes a minimum. Not
  Smolen, but the invitational half of the same structure
  (Smolen_Invitational); it used to bid 2NT. With five hearts and four
  spades an invitation still transfers first (jacoby-transfers.bid).

## Evidence from BBA

- `probes/smolen-resp-1N.toml` (21GF-DEFAULT, 200 hands 5-4 in the
  majors, 8-18 HCP, after 1NT–2♣–2♦): BBA bids Smolen from **10 HCP**
  up to 18 (never a direct slam), and with 8-9 HCP two of the five-card
  major.
- `probes/smolen-opener-3H.toml`, `smolen-opener-3S.toml` (opener 15-17,
  no four-card major): with two cards in responder's suit 3NT, with
  three 4M, every time, except that after 3♥ with three spades and **17**
  BBA bids **3♠** (26 of 26 hands; 15-16 bid 4♠). After 3♠ (five hearts)
  there is no such room: 4♥ (a few 6♥ with 17).
- Corpus (Smolen, Smolen_after_2N): 1NT–2♣–2♦–3♠–4♥ 133, –3♥–4♠ 122,
  –3♠–3NT 88, –3♥–3NT 82, –3♥–3♠ 38; the same shapes after 2NT.

## Corpus (2026-09-28, all 343 scenarios, with Gerber)

The Smolen part of the change, by the first call that changed:

| Where | Boards | vs BBA (par) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1NT–2♣–2♦: 3NT → 3♠ | 446 | +608 |
| 1NT–2♣–2♦: 3NT → 3♥ | 443 | +251 |
| 2NT–3♣–3♦: 3NT → 3♥ / 3♠ | 409 | +398 |
| 1NT–2♣–2♦: 2NT → 2♠ (invitational) | 117 | +167 |
| 1NT–2♣–2♦: pass → 3♠ / 3♥ | 40 | +263 |
| 6NT → Smolen (1NT and 2NT) | 306 | +18 |
| after our 1NT overcall (1♣/1♦/1♥/1♠ 1NT) | 461 | +34 (over 1♥: -47) |

Scenario totals: Smolen +542 (500 boards changed), Smolen_Invitational
+420, Smolen_after_2N +384. The whole change (Smolen and Gerber) is in
`gerber.notes.md`, "Corpus".

## Differences from BBA

- **Invitational hands with a fifth card.** 9 HCP with 5-4 in the
  majors is 10 total points to us, so it bids Smolen where BBA bids 2♠
  (117 boards in Smolen_Invitational). The `bba` treatment agrees with
  BBA. The par total for the scenario is positive either way.
- **After a fit** BBA cue-bids or asks for keycards more often (4♣ over
  opener's 3♠; 4NT over 4M with 11+ extra); we sign off in 4M unless the
  keycard modules' 33-point test fires. Not examined further.
- **After 2NT–3♣–3♦–3♠–3NT BBA sometimes bids 4♥** (23 boards):
  apparently with a strong or long heart suit. We pass; not yet probed.
- Over our 1NT overcall of 1♥, Smolen's 3♥ names their suit (-47 on 24
  boards). Left alone for now: too few boards to judge.

## Gaps

- 6-4 in the majors: some play 4♦/4♥ over 2♦ as a transfer showing six
  (Texas-style Smolen). Not built; 6-4 hands take their existing route.
- Responder's slam tries after 3NT other than 6NT (a quantitative 4NT).

## Sources

- **The convention:** Bridge Bum, "Smolen"
  (https://www.bridgebum.com/smolen.php), read 2026-09-28: game-forcing
  5-4 in the majors; after 2♦ "responder now jumps to the three-level in
  his shorter major, thereby showing five cards in the other major";
  opener bids 3NT with a doubleton, four of the major with three. Where we
  differ: the page says nothing about 2NT, opener's 3♠ slam try or 6-4
  hands; the 2NT version and the 3♠ try come from BBA (above).
- **Rick's rulings:** Smolen is on his card (`notrump.smolen.play`); total
  points include length (2026-09-23); 5-4 hands go through Stayman first
  (stayman.notes.md, 2026-09-24).
- **BBA probes:** `probes/smolen-resp-1N.toml`,
  `probes/smolen-opener-3H.toml`, `probes/smolen-opener-3S.toml`
  (21GF-DEFAULT, matchpoints, none vulnerable).
- **Corpus:** Smolen, Smolen_after_2N, Smolen_Invitational (BBA's
  auctions), and the compare runs above.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Splinters over a major opening: responder's double jump in a new suit
# (1♥–3♠, 4♣, 4♦; 1♠–4♣, 4♦, 4♥) agrees opener's major with four or more
# trumps, game values, and a singleton or void in the suit bid; opener's
# double jump after a one-level major response (1♦–1♠–4♣) agrees
# responder's major with 17-21. Also: responder's double jump in the
# overcaller's suit (1♥ (2♣) 4♣), opener's jump over a two-over-one
# (1♠–2♥–4♣, 1♥–2♣–3♠), responder's over opener's raise (1♣–1♥–2♥–3♠)
# and over opener's second suit (1♣–1♥–1♠–4♦), at the end of the file.
# The splinterer's partner counts honours
# in the short suit as wasted (the ace is not) and bids game, or makes a
# slam try that the slam machinery (slam/) carries on. Wikipedia,
# "Splinter bid"; BBA probes probes/splinter-*.toml. See
# splinters.notes.md. The slam-or-game sections count support points
# less the honours wasted opposite the shortness (`tp(M) - wasted_hcp`, the
# engine's term since 2026-11-07: K 3, Q 2, J 1 opposite a singleton;
# it was eight spelled-out combinations before).
#
# A double jump is never a jump shift here: strong jump shifts are single
# jumps (1♥–2♠), invitational ones single jumps to the three level
# (1♠–3♣); the double jumps had no meaning before.

module splinters "Splinters over 1♥ / 1♠"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/splinters
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/jacoby_2nt_splinters
  skill  bidding_conventions/splinters
  param  by_resp = by_responder default true
  param  by_open = by_opener default true
  param  cue     = bidding_conventions/control_bids default false
  param  style   = bidding_conventions/control_bids:style default first_or_second_round
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  # Under Transfer Walsh 1C-1D/1H are transfers: opener's splinters
  # read them as natural and agreed the wrong major (self A/B, 2026-10-05).
  param  twalsh  = bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh default false

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 12-15 HCP with a small singleton, 11 with a void (BBA, both probes);
# above that, Jacoby 2NT. A singleton honour, the ace included, is not
# shortness to show: those hands bid Jacoby 2NT too (BBA). A passed hand
# splinters with a maximum, 10-11 and four trumps.
after 1H (P) when by_resp
  3S  "Splinter: 4+ hearts, game values, at most one spade"  alert
      shows H>=4, S<=1, !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S), tp(H)>=15
      shows hcp=12..15 | (hcp=11, S=0)
      when  !passed_hand
      sets  trump=H, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2                       # ahead of Jacoby 2NT
  3S  "Splinter: 4+ hearts, 10-11, at most one spade"  alert
      shows H>=4, S<=1, !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S), hcp=10..11, tp(H)>=13
      when  passed_hand
      sets  trump=H, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2                       # ahead of Drury

after 1M (P) when by_resp
  4x  "Splinter: 4+ {M}, game values, at most one {x}"  alert
      shows M>=4, x<=1, !has(A,x), !has(K,x), !has(Q,x), !has(J,x), tp(M)>=15
      shows hcp=12..15 | (hcp=11, x=0)
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S, !passed_hand
      sets  trump=M, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2
  4x  "Splinter: 4+ {M}, 10-11, at most one {x}"  alert
      shows M>=4, x<=1, !has(A,x), !has(K,x), !has(Q,x), !has(J,x), hcp=10..11, tp(M)>=13
      when  x is not M, M is S | x is not S, passed_hand
      sets  trump=M, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2

# Over a two-level overcall, the double jump in their suit (1♥ (2♣) 4♣,
# 1♠ (2♦) 4♦, 1♠ (2♥) 4♥) is the splinter: the same hand, short in the
# suit they bid. The simple cue bid stays the limit raise or better
# (after-interference.bid), so the jump has no other meaning. Not by a
# passed hand: Drury and the cue bid cover those.
after 1M (2x) when by_resp, x is not M, M is S | x is not S, !passed_hand
  4x  "Splinter: 4+ {M}, game values, at most one {x} (their suit)"  alert
      shows M>=4, spl_short(x), tp(M)>=15
      shows hcp=12..15 | (hcp=11, x=0)
      sets  trump=M, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Opener's splinters ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Over a one-level major response, opener's double jump in a new suit
# (1♣/1♦–1♥–3♠; 1x–1M–4y below 4M) agrees the major with four, a
# singleton or void and 17-21 HCP (16 with a void): BBA's own range,
# probes/splinter-by-opener-1D-1S.toml. Without a singleton or void the
# same hands raise to game (rebids.bid).
after 1m (P) 1H (P) when by_open, !(twalsh, m is C)
  3S  "Splinter: 4 hearts, 17-21, at most one spade"  alert
      shows H>=4, S<=1, !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S), tp(H)>=19
      shows hcp=17..21 | (hcp=16, S=0)
      sets  trump=H, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2                       # ahead of the raise to game
after 1x (P) 1M (P) when by_open, !(twalsh, x is C)
  4y  "Splinter: 4 {M}, 17-21, at most one {y}"  alert
      shows M>=4, y<=1, !has(A,y), !has(K,y), !has(Q,y), !has(J,y), tp(M)>=19
      shows hcp=17..21 | (hcp=16, y=0)
      when  y is not M, y is not x, M is S | y is not S
      sets  trump=M, forcing=game
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── Opener ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Honours in partner's short suit other than the ace are wasted. Count
# support points (tp: HCP and shortness) less the wasted honours (K 3,
# Q 2, J 1: `wasted_hcp`). With 14 or more, a slam try: the cheapest control below
# game when a side suit is bare (two or more cards, neither ace nor
# king), else the keycard ask; with fewer, game. Corpus (splinters.notes.md):
# 14 on support points beat 13 and 15, and beat BBA's own line, which
# is about 13 HCP less wasted honours (probes/splinter-opener-*.toml).
# The same over their double of the splinter (lead-directing, it takes
# no room): 4M is still the sign-off. Without it 4M read as a Law-of-
# total-tricks raise or a 19+ game bid (Brill daily 2026-10-11 board 1,
# 1S P 4D X 4S; 2026-10-15).
after 1H (P) 3S (P) | 1H (P) 3S (X) | 1H (P) 3S (X)
  4H  "Game: no slam interest"
      shows !(tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14)
      priority 13                      # ahead of the control bids (12) and any natural reading
  cheapest(C)  "Slam try: control bid in ♣"  alert
      shows tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, H is not C, S is not C, under_game(C), has(A,C) | C<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,C) | C<=1)
      when  (H is not C, S is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (H is not D, S is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (H is not H, S is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (H is not S, S is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 14
  cheapest(D)  "Slam try: control bid in ♦"  alert
      shows tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, H is not D, S is not D, under_game(D), has(A,D) | D<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,D) | D<=1)
      when  (H is not C, S is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (H is not D, S is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (H is not H, S is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (H is not S, S is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 14
  cheapest(H)  "Slam try: control bid in ♥"  alert
      shows tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, H is not H, S is not H, under_game(H), has(A,H) | H<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,H) | H<=1)
      when  (H is not C, S is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (H is not D, S is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (H is not H, S is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (H is not S, S is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(H)
      priority 14
  cheapest(S)  "Slam try: control bid in ♠"  alert
      shows tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, H is not S, S is not S, under_game(S), has(A,S) | S<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,S) | S<=1)
      when  (H is not C, S is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (H is not D, S is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (H is not H, S is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (H is not S, S is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(S), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(S)
      priority 14
  4N  "Keycard ask in {trump}"
      shows tp(H) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  rkcb
      sets  ask=keycards(trump)
      artificial
      priority 12
after 1M (P) 4x (P) | 1M (P) 4x (X) | 1M (2x) 4x (P) when x is not M, M is S | x is not S
  4M  "Game: no slam interest"
      shows !(tp(M) - wasted_hcp >= 14)
      priority 13                      # ahead of the control bids (12) and any natural reading
  cheapest(C)  "Slam try: control bid in ♣"  alert
      shows tp(M) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, M is not C, x is not C, under_game(C), has(A,C) | C<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,C) | C<=1)
      when  (M is not C, x is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (M is not D, x is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (M is not H, x is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (M is not S, x is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(C), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(C)
      priority 14
  cheapest(D)  "Slam try: control bid in ♦"  alert
      shows tp(M) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, M is not D, x is not D, under_game(D), has(A,D) | D<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,D) | D<=1)
      when  (M is not C, x is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (M is not D, x is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (M is not H, x is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (M is not S, x is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(D), ladder=control
      artificial
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(D)
      priority 14
  cheapest(H)  "Slam try: control bid in ♥"  alert
      shows tp(M) - wasted_hcp >= 14
      when  cue, M is not H, x is not H, under_game(H), has(A,H) | H<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,H) | H<=1)
      when  (M is not C, x is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (M is not D, x is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (M is not H, x is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (M is not S, x is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))
      sets  ask=control(H), ladder=control

  cheapest(S)  "Slam try: control bid in ♠"  alert

      when  cue, M is not S, x is not S, under_game(S), has(A,S) | S<=0 | (style is first_or_second_round, has(K,S) | S<=1)
      when  (M is not C, x is not C, C>=2, !has(A,C), !has(K,C)) | (M is not D, x is not D, D>=2, !has(A,D), !has(K,D)) | (M is not H, x is not H, H>=2, !has(A,H), !has(K,H)) | (M is not S, x is not S, S>=2, !has(A,S), !has(K,S))

# splinters (`splinters.bid`): notes

Splinters over a major opening, by responder and by opener, and the
slam-or-game decision over them. Cases: `splinters.test`.

## What the card says

`major_openings.splinters.play` (BBA's `Splinter`; on Rick's card, on
21GF-DEFAULT and 21GF-GIB) switches the module on.
`splinters.by_responder` and `splinters.by_opener` default to on: a card
that says only "Splinters" plays both, as BBA does with its one switch.
`mini_splinters.play` (BBA's `Mini Splinter`, set by no corpus card) is
not played.

## The structure

- **Responder's splinter**: a double jump in a new suit over 1♥ (3♠, 4♣,
  4♦) or 1♠ (4♣, 4♦, 4♥): four or more trumps, 12-15 HCP (11 with a void)
  and a singleton or void that is not an honour. It agrees the suit and
  forces to game (`trump=M, forcing=game`), so the slam machinery
  (slam/) runs from there. Above 15, and with a singleton honour, Jacoby
  2NT. A passed hand splinters with 10-11 and four trumps (ahead of
  Drury).
- **Opener's splinter**: after 1x–1M (a one-level major response), a
  double jump in a new suit (1♣/1♦–1♥–3♠; 1x–1M–4y below 4M): four
  trumps, 17-21 HCP (16 with a void), a singleton or void that is not an
  honour.
- **The partner of the splinterer** counts support points less the
  honours wasted in the short suit (K 3, Q 2, J 1; the ace is not
  wasted). Over responder's splinter: 14 or more make a slam try; over
  opener's: 11 or more. The try is the cheapest control bid below game
  when a side suit is bare (two or more cards, neither ace nor king) and
  the card plays control bids, otherwise the keycard ask (Rick's rule in
  control-bids.bid: control bids before keycard when a suit is
  unprotected). With less, game.

Not a jump shift: strong jump shifts are single jumps (1♥–2♠),
invitational ones single jumps to three (1♠–3♣); the double jumps had no
meaning before. `rebids.bid`'s answers to an invitational jump shift
(`after 1x (P) 3y (P)`) now require no agreed trump, so they no longer
read 1♥–3♠ as natural spades (opener used to raise to 4♠).

## Evidence

**BBA's responder** (`probes/splinter-resp-1H.toml`, `-1S.toml`, 1000
hands each with four trumps and shortness, 21GF-DEFAULT): its splinter
is "12 to 20 total points", but it splinters only with 12-15 HCP (11
with a void) and a small singleton; a singleton honour, the ace
included, goes through Jacoby 2NT, as does 16+. 8-9 HCP bid 4M
(preemptive), 10-11 Jacoby 2NT. Agreement 685/1000 and 658/1000.

**Opener over the splinter** (`probes/splinter-opener-1S-4D.toml`,
`-1H-4C.toml`, 800 hands each): BBA's line is about 13 HCP outside
wasted honours (mixed at 11-13, always a try from 14), and its try is
always a control bid. Ours: 355/800 and 380/800; the difference is
mostly that we ask 4NT when no side suit is bare.

**The slam line, on the corpus** (Exclusion_After_1M, Gavin_Strong_Splinter,
Splinters, the four Jacoby_2N scenarios, Gavin_Weak_Splinter,
Slam_After_Major_Fit, Splinters_By_Opener; −3,506 before):

| Opener's slam try from | vs BBA |
|---|---|
| 13 HCP less waste (BBA's line) | −3,860 |
| 12 support points less waste | −3,118 |
| 13 support points less waste | −3,014 |
| **14 support points less waste** | **−3,001** |
| 15 support points less waste | −3,256 |

Counting HCP alone missed the hands whose value is shape: a void and a
seventh trump. The splinter's range: 12-16 −2,984 and 11-15 about equal
(noise); 12-15 kept, BBA's and the books' range.

**Opener's splinter** (`probes/splinter-by-opener-1D-1S.toml`, 800
hands): BBA splinters from 17 HCP (16 with a void), about half the time
(the rest raise to 4♠). Splinters_By_Opener −1,107 → −859; the
responder's threshold (9, 11, 13) changed nothing measurable.

**Corpus, the whole change** (with Drury, same commit): Splinters −33 →
−13, Gavin_Strong_Splinter −23 → +138, Jacoby_2N +33 → +126,
Jacoby_2N_4x_void −57 → +19, its Leveled form −129 → −2,
Splinters_By_Opener −1,107 → −859.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- Over a splinter with every side suit protected we ask for keycards;
  BBA cue-bids (Rick's control-bid rule, control-bids.bid).
- The slam line is on support points (shape counts); BBA's is on HCP.
- Opener splinters every time the hand qualifies; BBA sometimes raises
  to game instead.
- A passed hand's splinter needs four trumps; BBA's takes three at 11.

## Gaps

- **Minor-suit splinters**: responder's splinters in support of a minor
  live in `inverted-minors.bid` (13+ HCP, only with inverted minors) and
  are not gated on this field. Splinters_after_Minor is −1,242; BBA
  splinters there with less (1♦–3♠ and 1♦–3♥ are its two costliest
  divergences). Left for a separate change.
- Mini-splinters (the field exists, no corpus card sets it).
- Splinters after a jump or a 2/1 rebid (1♠–2♣–2♦–4♥), and Rick's
  card's `slam.control_bids` text is not read. Opener's splinter over the
  2/1 itself and responder's over opener's raise or second suit are
  written ("Later splinters", below).
- Splinters in competition: only responder's in their suit over a
  two-level overcall (below); the rest need the opponents to pass.
- **Transfer Walsh** (2026-10-05): opener's splinters stand aside after
  1♣-1♦/1♥ when the card plays transfer responses
  (`minor_openings.one_club.transfer_resp`): they read the transfer as
  the natural suit and agreed the wrong major (Transfer Walsh self A/B,
  transfer-walsh.notes.md). Opener's splinters in the transfer's major
  are not written.

## Their double of the splinter (2026-10-15)

Brill daily 2026-10-11 board 1 (MP): 1♠ (P) 4♦ (X) 4♠ (P), Rusty South
the splinterer with AKT87.KQT62.3.64 (12 HCP). On the day it bid 4NT and
reached 6♠ (12 tricks double dummy, one off at the table); the replay
passed 4♠ under rebids.bid's "Nothing to add: partner's rebid was a
minimum". Not a regression in the slam rules: on the day opener's 4♠
over the double was read by rebids.bid as "Game: six or more spades,
19+" (no rule here covered the doubled splinter), which made South's
keycard ask look right; since 2026-10-09 it was read as total-tricks'
"ten trumps, 10-12". Both are misreadings: opener's 4M is the sign-off
whether or not they double the artificial splinter (it takes no room).
The opener's block now covers `1M (P) 4x (X)` and `1H (P) 3S (X)`, so 4♠
reads "Game: no slam interest", and the splinterer with no extras passes
it, as he does uncontested (`1S P 4D P 4S P` passes too). 12 HCP
opposite a sign-off is no slam try by any count here; the slam on the
day was the misreading's luck. Opener's redouble or pass over the
double (control-showing) is not written.

## Later splinters (2026-10-30)

Gaps found by comparing Brill's convention files with our rules (calls
we had no rule for; brill_probe/brill_cases, the "Splinter" and
"Overcall1HSplinter" groups). Brill's definitions were the hint, not the
spec; the ranges are ours.

- **In their suit over a two-level overcall**: 1♥ (2♣) 4♣, 1♥ (2♦) 4♦,
  1♠ (2♣/2♦/2♥) 4 of their suit: the responder's splinter (4+ trumps,
  12-15 HCP or 11 with a void, a small singleton or void in their suit),
  not by a passed hand. The simple cue bid stays the limit raise or
  better. Opener answers as over the uncontested splinter (the opener's
  block takes `1M (2x) 4x (P)` too). BBA plays it: the corpus boards
  where we now bid it (After_Opp_Overcalls 176, Dealing_with_Overcalls_Weak
  240, Transfer_Advances 23) are BBA's own call.
- **Opener over a two-over-one** (seat 1 or 2 only: a passed hand's 2♣ is
  Drury): 1♠–2♥–4♣/4♦, four hearts, a small singleton or void, 14+ HCP:
  the fast 4♥ (1♠–2♥–4♥, rebids.bid 14-17) is the other hand, so the
  splinter carries slam interest. Responder counts support points less
  waste from 16 (4♥ or a control bid / keycard, as above).
- **Natural for now** (Rick, 2026-10-31: "advanced splinters deserve
  research as a whole"): opener's splinters raising a two-over-one minor
  (1♥–2♣/2♦–3♠, 1♠–2♣–4♦) and 1♠–2m–3♥. The 1♥–2m–3♠ splinter was
  written and taken out again; BBA bids it (Two_Over_One 380, Serious
  15, Slam_After_Major_Fit 445), so those boards go back to differing.
- **Responder over opener's single raise**: 1m–1♥–2♥–3♠ and
  1x–1M–2M–4y (y a new suit below 4M): 4+ trumps, a small singleton or
  void, 18+ support points (slam interest: the raise is 12-15 and plain
  game values bid 4M). Opener tries for slam from 15 less waste.
- **Responder over opener's second suit**: 1♣–1♥–1♠–4♦ and
  1♦–1♥–1♠–4♣ agree spades as a splinter over 1♠ would (12-15, 11 with
  a void); opener counts from 14 as over the splinter of his opening.

The shared conditions are named once (`spl_short(s)`, `spl_bare(t, s)`,
defined in splinters.bid). Every count is `tp(t) - wasted_hcp` since
2026-11-07 ("Working HCP", below).

Measured: `compare` on Splinters, Splinters_By_Opener, the Gavin
splinters, Slam_After_Major_Fit, Two_Over_One, Reverse_After_Two_Over_One,
After_Opp_Overcalls, Dealing_with_Overcalls_Strong/Weak and
Mixed_Raise_In_Comp (500 boards each): 6 boards changed, every new
splinter BBA's own call; errors +11 on one board (Slam_After_Major_Fit
86, 7♥ for 6♥), 0 on the rest. The all-scenario tripwire (`--limit 50`,
17,100 boards): 2 boards changed (Serious 15, Transfer_Advances 23), both
to BBA's call; totals unchanged.

Accepted difference: Dealing_with_Overcalls_Weak 203, 1♠ (2♥) with a
heart void and 13 HCP: we splinter 4♥, BBA cue-bids 3♥; both reach 5♠.
Slam_After_Major_Fit 86: opener with seven hearts and four clubs
splinters 1♥–2♣–3♠ (void); showing the hearts first may be better, but
it reached the grand that par wants.

**Left out**:
- **Advancer's splinter** (Brill's Overcall1HSplinter: (1♣) P (1♦) 1♥
  (1NT/P/1♠/2♣/2♦) 3♣/3♦/3♠/4♣/4♦, a passed hand's jump in their suit
  raising the overcall). No card field covers it, so it cannot be self
  A/B'd, and the position (both opponents bid, advancer passed) is rare
  enough that 500 random boards would not show it. Our rules have no
  meaning for those jumps, so nothing conflicts (fit-showing jumps are
  in new suits; the mixed-raise jump cue is direct-seat `(1x) 1y (P)`).
  Rick, 2026-10-31: not now.
- **After Stayman** (1NT–2♣–2♥–4♣/4♦): 4♣ there is Gerber on many cards;
  left to the notrump modules.
- 1♥ 1♠ 2♠ (P) 4♣ (the task excluded it) and the splinters over 1NT
  interference.

## Working HCP (2026-11-07)

Rick, 2026-11-07, of modified Jacoby, Jacoby 2NT and splinters alike:

> "keycard should be the stronger hand. the idea of the relays is it
> will allow us to find low HCP slams when there is a good fit. one of
> the hands had 4-5 weak spades in responder's hand, and opener had a
> spade void, i think, which means all the combined HCP are 'working',
> which is the goal of this system (and the standard jacoby 2nt, and
> splinter bids). this may be a concept we haven't introduced yet."

The splinter rules already counted that way (support points less K 3,
Q 2, J 1 in the short suit); the eight spelled-out combinations per
call are now the engine's term, `tp(M) - wasted_hcp`
(slam-entry.notes.md, "Working values"). Same thresholds, so a pure
rewrite: compare on the matching set (5,000 boards, standard card)
changed 0 boards from it.

## Sources

- **Convention description**: Wikipedia, "Splinter bid" (double jump in
  a side suit; four-card support, a singleton or void, game values,
  "typically 10-15 HCP"; opener re-values, "Axxx is ideal whereas KJ9x is
  almost worthless" in the short suit; opener's splinter with 15-18). We
  take the lower end from BBA (12, or 11 with a void) and opener's range
  from BBA (17-21), and we exclude singleton honours as BBA does.
- **Bridge-Classroom** `conventionCatalog.js`: `splinters.play` ("double
  jump shows shortness").
- **BBA probes** (2026-09-28): `probes/splinter-resp-1H.toml`,
  `probes/splinter-resp-1S.toml`, `probes/splinter-opener-1S-4D.toml`,
  `probes/splinter-opener-1H-4C.toml`,
  `probes/splinter-by-opener-1D-1S.toml`.
- **Corpus measurements** (2026-09-28): the slam line and the ranges,
  the tables above.
- **Later splinters** (2026-10-30): the splinter in the overcaller's
  suit, opener's over a two-over-one and responder's over a raise or
  opener's second suit follow the Wikipedia definition (double jump, or
  a jump past a reverse, in a side suit; four trumps; shortness) applied
  one round later; the ranges are ours (above), standard practice, not
  yet cited beyond that. BBA bids the same calls on the corpus boards
  named above. Brill's convention files pointed at the gaps (no text
  taken from them).
- **Rick's rulings**: control bids before keycard when a suit is
  unprotected, and the 33-support-point slam count (control-bids.bid,
  rkcb-1430.bid, 2026-09-25/27); the wasted-honour count here is a
  refinement of that count, not a ruling.
- **The doubled splinter** (2026-10-15): opener's game bid stays the
  sign-off over a lead-directing double, standard practice, not yet
  cited; the Brill daily 2026-10-11 board 1 for the motive.
- **Working HCP** (Rick, 2026-11-07, quoted above): the wasted-honour
  count is the engine's `wasted_hcp` since then.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module stayman "Stayman"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/stayman default true
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/stayman
  skill  partnership_bidding/stayman_transfers
  param  minors = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:style default relay
  param  mtp    = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:over_1nt default true
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_double = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_double default false
  param  vs_2c = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_2c default false
  param  style = general.style
  param  jacoby = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  param  smolen = bidding_conventions/smolen default false

after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  2C  "Stayman: asks for a 4-card major"  alert
      shows strength>=invite, H=4 | S=4 | ((mtp, minors is four_way | minors is four_way_reversed), strength=invite, C<=5, D<=5), H<=4 | S<=3 | strength>=game
      when  !shape 4333 | ((mtp, minors is four_way | minors is four_way_reversed), strength=invite)
      when  style is not bba
      # 5 hearts and 4 spades below game transfers, then bids 2S
      # (jacoby-transfers.bid; BBA's treatment, Rick 2026-09-24).
      # Other 5-4 in the majors included (Smolen). 4-3-3-3 just bids notrump, except
      # with four-way transfers, where 2NT is not natural: invitational hands
      # go through Stayman, with or without a major, and bid 2NT next. A
      # six-card minor transfers instead (minor-transfers.bid): opposite
      # good support it bids 3NT.
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial
      priority 1                           # ahead of transfers with 5-4 majors
  2C  "Stayman: asks for a 4-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max, (H=4 | S=4, H<=5, S<=5, H<=4 | hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min) | ((mtp, minors is four_way | minors is four_way_reversed), strength=invite, C<=5, D<=5)
      when  style is bba
      # BBA (probed 2026-09-24): a four-card major and 7 HCP, whatever the
      # shape (4-3-3-3 too) or the tens; 2NT next shows 7-9. A six-card
      # major transfers, and so does 5 hearts and 4 spades below game
      # values (2D, then 2S: jacoby-transfers.bid). stayman.notes.md.
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial
      priority 1

  # Without transfers an invitational hand with a five-card major starts
  # with Stayman and bids two of the major over 2♦ (BBA, bare SAYC: 7-8
  # HCP with five, probes/nt-van-5m-resp.toml). Below the 4-card-major
  # rule, which partner reads 2♣ by: the answer is the same.
  2C  "Stayman: invitational with a five-card major"  alert
      shows H>=5 | S>=5, strength=invite, hcp>=7
      when  !jacoby, style is not bba
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial

# Opener. With both majors the first rule that fits (2H) wins.
after nt1 2C (P)
  2H  "4+ hearts"                 shows H>=4
  2S  "4 spades, not 4 hearts"    shows S>=4, H<=3
  2D  "No 4-card major"           shows H<=3, S<=3

# Responder's second call. No auction patterns: a fit is whatever opener's
# answer has shown. Without a fit, 2NT and 3NT imply the other major, and
# opener corrects with four of it (choice-of-games.bid).
#
# Once the fit is found, responder also counts support points, tp(x) (HCP
# plus shortness, capped by the trumps held): they can raise an invitation
# to game or a game to slam. Those rules come as extras beside the
# total-point ones, which stay the ones partner reads the negative
# inferences from (3NT here denies the fit only through them).
when answered majors
  # Five spades and four hearts, invitational: 2♠ over the 2♦ denial
  # (Smolen_Invitational; BBA bids it with 8-9 HCP,
  # probes/smolen-resp-1N.toml). With five hearts and four spades an
  # invitation transfers instead (jacoby-transfers.bid). Game-forcing
  # 5-4 hands use Smolen (smolen.bid).
  2S  "Five spades, four hearts, invitational"   shows S=5, H=4, strength=invite
      when  partner.last=2D, style is not bba
      sets  ask=spades_invite
  2S  "Five spades, four hearts, invitational"   shows S=5, H=4, hcp>=23-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min
      when  partner.last=2D, style is bba
      sets  ask=spades_invite
  # Without transfers: an invitation with five (or more) in a major,
  # after 2C with that hand (above). Over 2♥ the spades are new; over a
  # 4-card answer in the five-card major responder raises instead.
  2H  "Five or more hearts, invitational"   shows H>=5, H>S, strength=invite
      when  partner.last=2D, !jacoby, style is not bba
      sets  ask=invite(H)
  2S  "Five or more spades, invitational"   shows S>=5, strength=invite
      when  partner.last=2D | partner.last=2H, !jacoby, style is not bba
      when  H<=3                    # with four hearts: Smolen's 2S over 2D, a raise over 2H
      sets  ask=invite(S)
  # Without transfers or Smolen, 5-4 in the majors with game values bids
  # the five-card major over the denial, forcing: opener chooses 4M or
  # 3NT as over 1NT-3M (one-nt.bid, `choose_game`).
  3S  "Five spades, game forcing"   shows S>=5, S>=H, strength>=game
      when  partner.last=2D, !jacoby, !smolen
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(S)
  3H  "Five hearts, game forcing"   shows H>=5, H>S, strength>=game
      when  partner.last=2D, !jacoby, !smolen
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(H)
  6H  "Slam in the heart fit"                     shows H>=4, strength=slam   when partner.H>=4
      sets  trump=H
  6S  "Slam in the spade fit"                     shows S>=4, strength=slam   when partner.S>=4
      sets  trump=S
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"                     shows H>=4, strength>=game  when partner.H>=4, style is not bba
      sets  trump=H
  3H  "Invitational raise in hearts"              shows H>=4, strength=invite when partner.H>=4, style is not bba
      sets ask=invite(H), trump=H
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"                     shows S>=4, strength>=game  when partner.S>=4, style is not bba
      sets  trump=S
  3S  "Invitational raise in spades"              shows S>=4, strength=invite when partner.S>=4, style is not bba
      sets ask=invite(S), trump=S
  6H  "Slam in the heart fit"  shows H>=4, tp(H)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.H>=4
      sets  trump=H
  6S  "Slam in the spade fit"  shows S>=4, tp(S)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  partner.S>=4
      sets  trump=S
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"  shows H>=4, tp(H)>=25-partner.points.min
      when  partner.H>=4, strength<=invite
      when  style is not bba
      sets  trump=H
      priority 1                                  # support points raise an invitation to game
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"  shows S>=4, tp(S)>=25-partner.points.min
      when  partner.S>=4, strength<=invite
      when  style is not bba
      sets  trump=S
      priority 1
  # Rick, 2026-09-24: balanced 16-17 with no fit, as over 1NT: 4NT with
  # 16, 6NT with 17 (32 combined opposite a minimum).
  # After a stronger opening (2NT: 20-21) the counts, fitted opposite
  # 15-17, do not apply: the earlier rules, measured against partner's range.
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"  shows H>=4, (hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, !shape 4333) | hcp>=26-partner.hcp.min | (hcp>=24-partner.hcp.min, shortest<=0)
      when  partner.H>=4, matchpoints, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      when  style is bba

# BBA: opener answers the raise in the fit with a maximum (17 counting
# tens opposite 15-17), or one less with a fifth trump. Partner's range
# is no guide: the raise is in HCP by shape.

  4M  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows points>=shown.hcp.max | (M>=5, points>=shown.hcp.max-1)
  P   "Declines: not a maximum"        shows points<=shown.hcp.max-1, M<=4 | points<=shown.hcp.max-2

# Opener over the invitational 2♠ (five spades, four hearts): game with
# the top of the range, in spades with three, else 3NT; a minimum passes.
when asked spades_invite
  4S  "Accepts, three spades"          shows S>=3, hcp>=shown.hcp.max-1
  3N  "Accepts, two spades"            shows S<=2, hcp>=shown.hcp.max-1
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=shown.hcp.max-2

# responder, who has them too, bids game with 9 (probed 2026-09-24).
after 1N (P) 2C (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) 3S (P) when style is bba
  4S  "Game in the spade fit: the top of the invitation"  shows S>=4, hcp>=26-partner.hcp.max
  P   "Minimum: play 3S"                                  shows hcp<=25-partner.hcp.max

# ── Under interference ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two card switches say the 1NT structure survives RHO's action:
# `transfers.vs_double` keeps it over a double, and `transfers.vs_2c`
# over a 2♣ overcall. Over the double 2♣ is still Stayman; over 2♣ the
# call is gone and the double takes its place, which is what BBA plays
# on every card in the corpus that sets the switch.

# Over the double Stayman starts a point below the invitational floor
# (7 opposite 15-17): finding the 4-4 fit is also somewhere to run to.
# It denies a five-card major, unlike the uncontested 2C: with 5-4 BBA
# transfers rather than looking for the other major first.
after 1N (X) when vs_double
  2C  "Stayman: asks for a 4-card major"  alert
      shows hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max, H=4 | S=4
      when  H<=4, S<=4
      sets  forcing=round, ask=majors
      artificial
      priority 1

after 1N (2C) when vs_2c
  X   "Stayman: asks for a 4-card major"  alert
      shows strength>=invite, H=4 | S=4
      when  H<=4, S<=4

# stayman (`stayman.bid`): notes

2C Stayman over 1NT, opener's answer, and responder's second call.
Cases: `stayman.test`.

## Guidance

- Stayman promises a four-card major and invitational values or better.
  With 5-4 in the majors, Stayman comes first (priority 1), ahead of the
  transfer, as the start of Smolen (`smolen.bid`, `smolen.notes.md`).
- **Five spades and four hearts, invitational** (2026-09-28): 2♠ over the
  2♦ denial, and opener bids game with 16-17 (4♠ with three spades, 3NT
  with two) or passes (`when asked spades_invite`). BBA bids 2♠ with 8-9
  HCP (`probes/smolen-resp-1N.toml`); it used to bid 2NT here. +167 IMPs
  against BBA on 117 boards (smolen.notes.md, "Corpus").
- **4-3-3-3 hands bid notrump and skip Stayman** (Rick, 2026-09-21), though
  BBA uses Stayman with them.
- Responder's second call: raise with a fit (3M invites, 4M is game, 6M is
  slam); without one, 2NT, 3NT or 6NT. Opener corrects 3NT to four of the
  other major with four cards (`choice-of-games.bid`).
- Opener's answer to 2NT uses a 4-4 fit when one is known
  (`one-nt.bid`, `asked nt_invite`).

## Evidence from BBA

Stayman scenario (21GF-DEFAULT, 500 boards): 92.4% of calls agree, 57.2%
identical auctions, 75.0% the same contract.

Choice of games after `1NT P 2C P 2M P 3NT P`: 210 of 211 corpus boards agree.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- **4-3-3-3 with a four-card major**: BBA uses Stayman on 755 corpus deals
  (21GF-DEFAULT) where we bid 2NT, 3NT, 4NT or 6NT. Rick: keep our rule.
- **2NT after Stayman**: BBA's shows about 7–8. With 7 HCP BBA bids 2C and
  then 2NT (for example `J543.964.J32.AJ3`), and BBA's opener passes it
  holding 17 (24 Stayman boards, for example `K64.KJ3.AK85.K32`). Ours
  shows 8–9, as after 1NT–2NT, and opener accepts with 17. Rick: our way is
  fine.

## Gaps (not built yet)

- **5-4 with a minor after 2D**: BBA bids 3C or 3D (for example
  `A82.QJ98.7.KJ973` bids 3C, then 4C). The bba style now does too
  ("BBA's 3C/3D after Stayman"); the default bids 3NT, which par prefers.
- **Garbage Stayman** (weak hands that pass the answer), and Stayman with
  interference. (Smolen is built: `smolen.bid`.)
- **Slam after a fit**: with 18+ and a fit we jump to 6M. Keycard first
  would be better.

## Questions

- **Weak hands.** Of the corpus deals where BBA bids Stayman and we do not,
  176 are under 8 HCP and not 4-3-3-3: Garbage Stayman, or the lighter
  invitation above. Build Garbage Stayman as its own card option?

## Under interference (2026-09-23)

Two contexts at the foot of `stayman.bid` keep Stayman alive when RHO
acts, gated by the card switches `notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_double` and
`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c`:

- over a **double** it is still 2♣, from a point below the invitational
  floor (`hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max`, so 7 opposite 15-17: finding the
  4-4 fit is also somewhere to run to);
- over a **2♣ overcall** the call is gone and **the double takes its
  place**, 8+ as usual.

Both **deny a five-card major**, unlike the uncontested 2♣: under
interference BBA transfers with 5-4 rather than looking for the other
major first, so Smolen's priority does not apply here. Opener's answers
are the same three calls, written once per context.

Evidence and numbers: `nt-interference.notes.md`.

## Support points and length points (2026-09-23)

Rick: "our rules should have HCP, total points and support points, and
decide which to use under which circumstances". Once opener's answer
shows the fit, responder also counts **support points**, `tp(x)`: HCP
plus shortness (doubleton 1, singleton 3, void 5, capped by the trumps).

- **6M with 33 support points** opposite opener's minimum
  (`AQ82.K.KQ943.J83`, 15 HCP + 3 = 18 opposite 15–17). This is most of
  the gain: 1NT–2♣–2♥ → 6♥ and 1NT–2♣–2♠ → 6♠ (and the same after
  2NT–3♣) where we bid game.
- **4M with 25 support points** when the total-point count says invite
  (`KJ82.Q7.Q943.J83`: 9 HCP + 1 = 10, game).

These are **extra** rules beside the total-point ones, not replacements.
Replacing the bands with `tp` outright gained less (+1,896) because
partner can no longer read a negative inference from a `tp` rule: after
1NT–2♣–2♥–3NT opener stopped knowing that responder has four spades
(157 boards of 1N lost the 4♠ correction, −392 IMPs). Kept as extras,
corpus par **+2,478 IMPs**, Basic_* +2, uncontested −3 (noise).

Also: opener's answer to the raise (`when asked invite(M)` in
`jacoby-transfers.bid`) accepts with 16 in the fit, see its notes.

card, all four hands fixed (`rbb probe`):

**Measured as our default and rejected on par** (corpus, net IMPs vs BBA):
Stayman from 7 with a major, 2NT 7-9, pass with 7 once the fit is found:

invitations once 2NT can be 7 (1NT-2C-2D-2NT alone: -446 on 232 boards).
Without the pass once the fit is found: -1,078.

Also rejected: passing 2M after the fit is found with any invitational
hand (-113; pass better on 135 boards, the invitation on 123, but the
invitation's wins are games), or with 8 and inviting with 9 (-227).

**Kept as the BBA treatment** (`general.style = bba`): the light Stayman,
2NT 7-9 and the pass with the fit. Our default stays Stayman from 8 total
points with 2NT 8-9, because par prefers it.

  shape; not with a six-card major; with 5♥-4♠ only from 10 HCP.
- In the fit, fit points in HCP by shape against opener's range: game 10
  (9 with a void; 11 with 4-3-3-3), invite from 8 (7 with a singleton, 9
  with 4-3-3-3), pass below. At IMPs game from 9, the singleton counting
  1. Opener answers with a maximum (points ≥ `shown.hcp.max`, 17), or
  16 with a fifth trump (`ask=fit_invite(M)`).
- No fit: 2NT 7–9, 3NT game, **each rule for one answer** so that it
  denies the major it did not raise (the knowledge the default gets from
  negative inference). 4NT 16 HCP, 6NT 17 (before, 16–17 had no rule
  after 2♦ and passed: `K842.KQ5.AQ.QJ82`, Basic_What_To_Open 204; our
  default has the same gap).
- `1NT P 2C P 2H P 2NT P 3S P`: 4♠ with 9, else pass.

**Engine note: a `when` with a hand term leaks, on its own line too.**
The engine ANDs every `when` line of a rule into one condition, and in
interpretation keeps the rule possible whenever any part of it depends on
the caller's hand (`hand_dependent` in `eval.rs`). So `when !shape 4333
| ...` on one line and `when style is bba` on the next still made the
old bba 2♣ part of what 2♣ means under the default style: the default's
2♣ read as `(points>=8, ...) | (points>=8 | (hcp>=7, H=4 | S=4), ...)`.
It changed no call (the whole corpus is identical with and without the
rule), but the knowledge was wrong. The new rule has only `when style is
bba`, and the default 2♣ now reads as before. The reverse still holds:
default rules with hand terms in `when` (2♣'s `!shape 4333`, the 3♣ over
2NT, the support-point 4M's `strength<=invite`) widen what those calls
mean under `bba`: after 2♣ the bba side does not know responder has 7+
HCP. The fit answers are therefore keyed to opener's own maximum, not to
responder's range.

## BBA's counts after Stayman (2026-09-24)

The `bba` style's continuations after 1NT-2C now use counts fitted to BBA's
answers on random hands, as with pass/2NT/3NT directly over 1NT
(one-nt.notes.md):

- **After 2D (no major fit):** pass vs 2NT, then 2NT vs 3NT. The measures are
  `bba_stay_nt_points` and `bba_stay_nt_imp_points`.
- **After 2H, responder with four hearts:** pass vs 3H, then 3H vs 4H. The
  measures are `bba_stay_raise_points`, `bba_stay_game_points`, and their
  `_imp` versions.
- **After 2S, responder with four spades:** the same, with the
  `bba_stay_sraise_*` and `bba_stay_sgame_*` measures. Spades need their own
  weights: the ♠/♥ asymmetry in BBA's 1NT (5-4-2-2 with four hearts, never
  four spades) carries through.

Each measure is linear, fitted by logistic regression on random hands that
include singletons and voids. The features are the honour counts, tens, a
charge for a doubleton ♠ or ♥ without A/K, shape class (4333, 4432, 5332,
5422), a five-card minor, and doubletons, singletons and voids. The counts
are scaled so the higher call starts at 8 (invite) or 10 (game).
Agreement on held-out hands:

| Decision | Agreement |
|---|---|
| No fit after 2D | about 91-92% |
| Heart fit | about 93-94% |
| Spade fit | 88-95% |

**Known miss:** K876.5.K862.Q652 after 2S at IMPs. BBA bids 4S; the count
says 3S (stayman.test).

**Gated to 15-17 openers.** The counts were fitted opposite BBA's 15-17
1NT. Applied elsewhere, they lost boards: after 2NT openings, after our 1NT
overcall, and after Precision's weaker 1NT. The count rules are therefore
gated `partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17`, and the earlier rules
stay in force for any other range (`partner.hcp.min<=14 |
partner.hcp.max>=18`). The first-response counts in one-nt.bid get the
same gate. No-fit continuations after 2H/2S keep the earlier rules, because
the counts were fitted after 2D only.

**Corpus (bba style):**
- Corpus: calls 76.1%, auction/contract 18.3% / 33.0% (unchanged), par
  -181,410 -> -181,330.
- Basic_*: 44.7% / 52.0%.
- Basic_* NS: 63.6% / 69.4%.
- Replay against the rules before: better on 127 boards, worse on 114.
- The default is unchanged (-167,558).

**Not modelled yet:** the losses after 2D on the other cards (21GF).
3C/3D: next section.

## BBA's 3C/3D after Stayman (2026-09-24)

Probed with random hands (`probes/stay-3m-*.toml`, 400-2,500 hands each;
`probes/grid_tally.py <name>` tallies a run). The grid now keeps BBA's
continuation and the meaning of its call (bba-cli `--all-meanings`), which
is how the meanings below were read.

**Responder, after 2D.** With a five-card minor and a four-card major,
BBA's 3C/3D ("9 to 25 total points, 5+ cards") is the game-going call
unless the hand wants 3NT:
- **Below 12 HCP:** 3NT with a diamond stopper (A, Kx, Qxx, Jxxx), 3m
  without one, from 9 HCP. It is the diamond stopper for both minors: five
  diamonds without an honour bid 3D, and a spade stopper changes nothing.
  Clubs: 99% of 1,050 hands; diamonds: 96% of 946.
- **From 12 HCP:** 3m whatever the stoppers (a slam try in effect).
- **Level:** below the 3m line, pass, 2NT or 3NT come from the counts
  already fitted (`bba_stay_nt_points`).
- **Six-card minors:** 4m from about 12 ("slam try"). Not modelled.

**Responder, after 2H/2S without the fit.** 3m from 10 HCP whatever the
stoppers; 2NT at 8, 9 split. 3NT almost never with a five-card minor.

**Opener over 3m.** A suit is *open* when:
- the other minor is unstopped; or
- after 2D only, a major doubleton is unstopped (responder's major is
  unknown).

An open three-card major is no reason. Opener:
- raises to 4m with a fit (four clubs, or three at 16+; three diamonds)
  and a suit open, or with a flat 4-3-3-3 minimum;
- bids 5m instead with 17;
- otherwise bids 3NT.

A minimum is 15 counting half a point per ten (two tens make it 3NT).
With a minimum:
- after 2D, bid 3D over 3C without four clubs, and 4C over 3D with five
  clubs;
- after 2H/2S, bid 3D over 3C with four diamonds;
- after 2S, bid 3H with a flat hand and three hearts, the 4-3 fit, since
  responder has four.

Agreement: 83% after 2D, 80-84% after 2H/2S.

**Responder again.**
- After the raise: 5m from 11 HCP (half the 11s pass), 4NT from about 15.
  Our rule is 5m from 11, with no Blackwood.
- After a minimum: 3NT up to 14, and a quantitative 4NT with 15.
- After 3D-4C (opener's five clubs): BBA bids its four-card major at the
  four level, into a 4-3 fit at best. Modelled as it stands.

**Agreement on the random hands, bba style, before -> after:**

| Probe | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Responder after 2D (MP) | 36% | 89% |
| Responder after 2H (MP) | — | 94% |
| Responder after 2S (MP) | — | 93% |
| Opener over 3C/3D | 0% | 83% |

"0%" means we passed 3m. The IMP columns are lower after 2H/2S: at IMPs
BBA bids 3NT with 8-9 where the earlier no-fit rules bid 2NT. That is a
gap in the no-fit level line, not in 3m.

**Corpus (bba style):** replayed calls closer to BBA on 399 boards and
further on 1. 127 auctions became identical to BBA's and none stopped
being identical. Par: -181,330 -> -181,678 (-348 IMPs). The loss is on
boards where our 3NT used to beat BBA's 3m auction and now copies it.

**Default: keeps 3NT (par decides).** On the corpus, where BBA bid 3m at
game level and we bid 3NT (99 boards on all cards), 3NT came out +72 IMPs
ahead. BBA's gains came on slam hands, where the default passes 2D or
bids 2NT on the 21GF cards. That is worth a look separately: a 3m slam
try from 12+ opposite 15-17 may pay.

## Six-card minors and the no-fit line after 2H/2S (2026-09-25)

**Six-card minors** (`probes/stay-4m-*.toml`, 1,200 hands per answer):
- **4m, BBA's slam try:** from 13 HCP at matchpoints, 12 at IMPs, after
  all three answers. Some 10-12 after 2D bid 4m as well; nothing I tried
  separates them.
- **3m below that:** from 9 HCP, even with a diamond stopper after 2D.
- **Weak, 7-8:** BBA plays the answer. It passes 2D with six diamonds,
  and passes 2H/2S with three of the major.
- **Opener over 4m:** 5m, or the other minor with five of it and two of
  responder's minor (4D over 4C, 5C over 4D). Some 16-17s with a
  four-card fit ask with 4NT; the 4NT is not modelled.
- **Responder over 5m:** 6m from 14. The decision fits only ~70% on
  HCP, shape and controls.

## Without transfers (2026-09-30)

With `notrump.jacoby_transfers.play` off (BBA's bare SAYC card) two hands
that would transfer use Stayman instead (one-nt.notes.md, "Natural
majors without transfers"):

- **Invitational with a five-card major** (7+ HCP and invitational by
  our count): 2♣, then 2M over 2♦ (five or more, `ask=invite(M)`,
  answered by the base rule in rebids.bid), or 2♠ over 2♥ with at most
  three hearts. Over an answer in the five-card major responder raises.
  BBA bids 2♣ with every 7-8 HCP five-card major in
  `probes/nt-van-5m-resp.toml` and then two of the major. The new 2♣
  rule sits below the four-card-major one, so partner reads 2♣ the
  usual way; the answer does not change. Over 2♦, 2♠ with five spades
  and four hearts is still the Smolen-style invitation above.
- **5-4 in the majors with game values** (no Smolen): 2♣, then three of
  the five-card major over 2♦, forcing; opener bids 4M with three, 3NT
  with two (`choose_game`, one-nt.bid). Before, responder bid 3NT and
  lost the 5-3 fit. BBA bids 3M directly with these hands.


## A raise of the answer agrees the major (2026-10-03)

1NT-2♣-2♥-4♥ set no trump suit, though both hands had shown four hearts
(fit.bid's `agreed_fit` held). The knowledge review showed it. Every
raise of opener's major after the Stayman answer (invitation, game,
slam; both treatments) now `sets trump`, so 4NT later asks for
keycards in it and the review shows the agreement. Measured with the
engine's knowledge change of the same day. With the two other rule
changes of that day (nt-interference.bid's answer to 2NT, fit.bid over
3NT) it moved the vanilla SAYC set by -56 IMPs in distance from par and
-139 in errors against the engine change alone: small, and not measured
apart.

## Sources

- **The convention:** 2♣ Stayman over 1NT, non-forcing, with the usual
  answers. Standard practice, not yet cited to a book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** 4-3-3-3 hands skip Stayman (2026-09-21); keep our
  2NT (8-9) after Stayman; "HCP, total points and support points, and
  decide which to use under which circumstances" (2026-09-23); 16-17 with
  no fit bids 4NT or 6NT, and 5♥-4♠ below game transfers then bids a
  non-forcing 2♠ (2026-09-24).
- **BBA probes:** `rbb probe` on Basic_Openers_Rebid board 47 and
  variants, and the 2026-09-24 sandbox runs (`fit`, `fitS`, `acc`, `nf`,
  `st`, `t54`), which were not kept in the repo; `rbb grid` specs
  `probes/stay-3m-*.toml`, `probes/stay-4m-*.toml`,
  `probes/stay-nofit-2H.toml` and `probes/stay-nofit-2S.toml`, tallied
  with `probes/grid_tally.py`.
- **BBA evidence:** the Stayman scenario and the Basic-Bridge,
  21GF-DEFAULT and 21GF-GIB corpora; BBA's meanings of its 3♣/3♦ read
  with `bba-cli --all-meanings`.
- **Corpus measurements:** support and length points (+2,478), the
  2026-09-24 rulings (+4,518), the `bba` style's fitted counts; the
  routes without transfers on the vanilla SAYC random set (2026-09-30,
  one-nt.notes.md).
- **Without transfers:** 1NT-2♣-2♦-3M as five cards and forcing is
  standard practice (SAYC), not yet cited to the page; the invitational
  route is BBA's (`probes/nt-van-5m-resp.toml`).
- **Where we differ:** 4-3-3-3 with a four-card major, 2NT after Stayman
  ("Accepted differences from BBA"); the default bids 3NT with 5-4 and a
  minor after 2♦, which par prefers, where BBA and the `bba` style bid
  3m.
- **2026-10-03:** trump set by the raises; standard practice (a
  raise of partner's shown major agrees it), not yet cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module texas-transfers "Texas Transfers"
  kind   convention
  convention  bidding_conventions/texas
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers
  param  tu = two_under default false
  param  tex1 = over_1nt default false
  param  tex2 = over_2nt default false
  param  o23 = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:over_2c_3nt default true

# Texas shows a six-card major and one of two hands: game with no slam
# interest (pass the completion), or slam values (keycard after it): 33 total
# points or more even opposite opener's minimum, so 18+ opposite 15-17,
# in suit points or in support points (HCP + shortness, the fit being
# certain with six trumps). With
# mild slam interest responder transfers at the two level and jumps to game
# instead (jacoby-transfers.bid), which lets opener bid on. Game values
# count HCP and length points (8 + 2 for six cards = 10 opposite 15-17:
# Rick, 2026-10-29); the top of game-only and the slam band are in suit
# points.
#
# Where (Rick, 2026-10-29): every notrump of ours where the system is on
# (`systems`, one-nt.bid): the 1NT and 2NT openings, our notrump overcall
# and balancing notrump as the card says, 2♣–2♦–2NT, Kokish's
# 2♣–2♦–2♥–2♠–2NT, 2♣ and a positive then 2NT. The strength bands are
# measured against opener's range, so the same rules serve every one.
# Over interference Texas stays on as long as it is a jump: a double, or
# any bid that leaves three of the transfer suit available (4♦ over
# 2-level bids and 3♣, 4♥ also over 3♦), and never into their suit.
# `notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c` is a different question (2♦/2♥ transfers over
# their 2♣, nt-interference.bid) and does not switch Texas.
define texas_room_d = !tu, !me.named(H), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | (they.level<=2, they.strain is not H) | (they.level=3, they.strain is C)
# 2-under Texas (`notrump.texas.two_under`, Rick 2026-10-29): one
# step lower, 4♣ for hearts and 4♦ for spades, with the same hands; opener
# bids the suit in between to super-accept (four trumps, the top of his
# range) or four of the major. 4♥ is then natural (Rick, 2026-10-29).
define texas2_room_c = tu, !me.named(H), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | (they.level<=2, they.strain is not H)
define texas2_room_d = tu, !me.named(S), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | (they.level<=2, they.strain is not S) | (they.level=3, they.strain is C)
define texas_room_h = !tu, !me.named(S), rho.last=P | rho.last=X | (they.level<=2, they.strain is not S) | (they.level=3, they.strain is C | they.strain is D)

# Over 2♣–2♦–3NT only with `notrump.jacoby_transfers.over_2c_3nt` (Rick,
# 2026-11-07: "i would make this a treatment on the Jacoby Transfer card";
# "default to on"). Off, 4♦ and 4♥ there are natural.
# The card says where it plays Texas: over 1NT (and our 1NT overcalls),
# over 2NT (and the 2♣ auctions that reach 2NT or 3NT). A card that plays
# it over 1NT plays it over 2NT too, whatever its 2NT box says: most cards
# have one Texas box. Other modules read these two.
define texas_1nt = tex1
define texas_2nt = tex1 | tex2
define auction texas_entry = systems 1N (*)   when tex1
  systems 2N (*)   when tex1 | tex2
  2C (*) 2D (*) 3N (P)   when o23, tex1 | tex2

after texas_entry
  4D  "Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=30-partner.points.max
      when  texas_room_d
      sets  ask=texas(H)
      artificial
  4D  "Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, suit_points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas_room_d
      sets  ask=texas(H)
      artificial
  4D  "Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, tp(H)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas_room_d
      sets  ask=texas(H)
      artificial
  4H  "Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=30-partner.points.max
      when  texas_room_h
      sets  ask=texas(S)
      artificial
  4H  "Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, suit_points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas_room_h
      sets  ask=texas(S)
      artificial
  4H  "Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, tp(S)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas_room_h
      sets  ask=texas(S)
      artificial
  # Over interference Texas doubles as a preempt: with seven cards and
  # no values BBA transfers straight to game rather than to the two
  # level, and takes the auction away from them.
  4D  "Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=7, hcp>=4, suit_strength=signoff
      when  !(rho.last=P | rho.last=X), texas_room_d
      sets  ask=texas(H)
      artificial
  4H  "Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=7, hcp>=4, suit_strength=signoff
      when  !(rho.last=P | rho.last=X), texas_room_h
      sets  ask=texas(S)
      artificial

  # 2-under Texas: the same hands, one step lower.
  4C  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=30-partner.points.max
      when  texas2_room_c
      sets  ask=texas2(H)
      artificial
  4C  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, suit_points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas2_room_c
      sets  ask=texas2(H)
      artificial
  4C  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, tp(H)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas2_room_c
      sets  ask=texas2(H)
      artificial
  4D  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=30-partner.points.max
      when  texas2_room_d
      sets  ask=texas2(S)
      artificial
  4D  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, suit_points>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas2_room_d
      sets  ask=texas2(S)
      artificial
  4D  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=6, tp(S)>=33-partner.points.min
      when  texas2_room_d
      sets  ask=texas2(S)
      artificial
  4C  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♥, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=7, hcp>=4, suit_strength=signoff
      when  !(rho.last=P | rho.last=X), texas2_room_c
      sets  ask=texas2(H)
      artificial
  4D  "2-under Texas: 6+ ♠, game only or slam values"  announce "Transfer"
      shows S>=7, hcp>=4, suit_strength=signoff
      when  !(rho.last=P | rho.last=X), texas2_room_d
      sets  ask=texas2(S)
      artificial

# After 2♣–2♦–3NT there is no Jacoby route for the mild slam hands
# between the two bands (31-32 combined): opposite Kokish's 26-27 (strong-
# openings.bid) that is a 4-5 count with six hearts, which passed 3NT
# (base fallback). They bid game through Texas (2026-11-07).
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 3N (P) when o23
  4D  "Texas: 6+ ♥, game"  announce "Transfer"
      shows H>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when  texas_room_d
      sets  ask=texas(H)
