# nmf-after-2nt (`nmf-after-2nt.bid`): notes

New Minor Forcing after opener's 2NT rebid (18-19), card field
`other_conventions.new_minor_forcing.after_2nt_rebid` (BBA's "NMF after
2NT rebid"; most 21GF cards). Cases: `nmf-after-2nt.test`.

## Structure

- 1♣-1M-2NT-3♦ and 1♦-1M-2NT-3♣: five of the major (or both majors), any
  game-going values; 1♥-1♠-2NT-3♣: five spades.
- Opener: three of responder's major, else four of the other major, else
  3NT. Responder: four of the major with a fit (5-3, 4-4), else 3NT.
- Independent of `new_minor_forcing.play`: 21GF-SPECIALS2 plays NMF after
  2NT without NMF after 1NT, and BBA's corpus on it shows the 3♣ ask.
- Responder's 4M does not set `trump`: with trump set, slam-entry.bid's
  `slam_values` ("18 of my own") sent every 18-19 opener into keycard
  after 4M (tripwire, 2026-10-05: about 15 boards reached slam from what
  was 3NT). Left as a known fit, the keycard path for a fit not agreed
  judges with `fit_slam_values` instead. A question for the slam layer.
- With Wolff on (`wolff_signoff.play`), 3♣ after 1♦-1M-2NT stays Wolff's,
  and there is no ask there.

## BBA (corpus, 2026-10-05)

On 21GF-DEFAULT BBA alerts 3 of the unbid minor after 1m-1M-2NT, and
after 1♥-1♠-2NT both 3♣ and 3♦ ("NMF after 2NT rebid"). We take 3♣ there
and leave 3♦ natural. After a 1♦ response (1♣-1♦-2NT) 3♦ is natural, as
in BBA. Opener's jump to 4M with three and a maximum (seen once) is not
modelled.

## Open questions

- 1♥-1♠-2NT: which minor asks? We use 3♣; BBA labels both.

## Sources

- **The convention:** New Minor Forcing as extended to the 2NT rebid;
  standard practice (Bridge Bum, "New Minor Forcing", mentions the 2NT
  rebid variant), not yet cited further.
- **BBA evidence:** the PBS corpus, auctions 1x-1M-2NT-3m with the alert
  (about 100 boards on 21GF-DEFAULT, a few on 21GF-SPECIALS2).

files.rules/base/preempts.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Weak two-bids and higher preempts (Rick, 2026-09-22):
#
# - a weak two is 4-9 HCP with a six-card suit, a major 4-10 (2026-09-23);
#   vulnerable it needs two of the top three or three of the top five
#   honours;
# - third seat is looser: a five-card suit will do, and no suit-quality
#   requirement;
# - fourth seat has no weak two: 2 of a suit there shows a six-card suit
#   and the values of a minimum opening bid;
# - with a seven-card suit open at the three level, not the two;
# - the same guidelines apply to a weak jump overcall (competitive.bid,
#   not written yet).

module preempts "Weak two-bids and preempts"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/weak_2s
  skill  bidding_conventions/preemptive_bids
  skill  partnership_bidding/weak_twos
  param  two_d = opening.2d default bidding_conventions/weak_2s
  param  two_h = opening.2h default bidding_conventions/weak_2s
  param  two_s = opening.2s default bidding_conventions/weak_2s
  param  style = general.style
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (below)
  param  flannery = bidding_conventions/flannery default false
  param  multi    = bidding_conventions/multi_2d default false
  param  benjamin = bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d default false
  param  polish   = bidding_conventions/polish_two_suiters default false
  param  mini_roman = bidding_conventions/mini_roman_2d default false
  param  french   = bidding_conventions/french_2d default false
  param  wilkosz  = bidding_conventions/wilkosz default false
  param  prec_2d  = bidding_conventions/precision_2d default false

# The natural weak twos give way when a convention takes the call
# (conventions/openings/): Flannery, Multi, Benjamin, Mini-Roman, French,
# Wilkosz and Precision 2♦ take 2♦; Multi
# shows the weak twos in a major through 2♦ (BBA opens every such hand
# 2♦, probes/multi-openings.toml), and Polish two-suiters take 2♥ and 2♠.
define weak_2d_open = !flannery, !multi, !benjamin, !mini_roman, !french, !wilkosz, !prec_2d
define weak_2h_open = !multi, !polish
define weak_2s_open = !multi, !polish
# For the responses (weak-two-responses.bid): a 2x opening that is a natural weak two.
define weak_two_suit(x) = x is not D | (!flannery, !multi, !benjamin, !mini_roman, !french, !wilkosz, !prec_2d), x is not H | (!multi, !polish), x is not S | (!multi, !polish)

# ── Weak two-bids, first and second seat ─────────────────────────────
when opening, seat<=2
# standard: 4-9 (a major 4-10), no side four-card major; vulnerable, a
# good suit. The default follows BBA (below; Rick, 2026-09-24).
  2D  "Weak two: six diamonds, 4-9"    shows D=6, hcp=4..9, H<=3, S<=3
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, style is standard, !vul
  2D  "Weak two: six diamonds, 4-9, a good suit"   shows D=6, hcp=4..9, H<=3, S<=3, quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, style is standard, vul
  2H  "Weak two: six hearts, 4-10"     shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, style is standard, !vul
  2H  "Weak two: six hearts, 4-10, a good suit"    shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3, quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, style is standard, vul
  2S  "Weak two: six spades, 4-10"     shows S=6, hcp=4..10
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, style is standard, !vul
  2S  "Weak two: six spades, 4-10, a good suit"    shows S=6, hcp=4..10, quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, style is standard, vul

# The default and bba (probed 2026-09-24, preempts.notes.md): every weak two goes to 10
# HCP. A side four-card major stops it only when it holds the jack or
# better. A ten-count with two aces opens at the one level, and so does a
# major with the ace-king (base.bid decides between one and pass). The
# hand conditions are in `shows` and `when` stays public, so that these
# rules never widen what a weak two shows under the default style.
  2D  "Weak two: six diamonds, 4-10"   shows D=6, hcp=4..10, H<=3 | (!has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), !has(J,H)), S<=3 | (!has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,D) | (!has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,C))
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, !vul
  2D  "Weak two: six diamonds, 4-10, a good suit"   shows D=6, hcp=4..10, quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3, H<=3 | (!has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), !has(J,H)), S<=3 | (!has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,D) | (!has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,C))
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, vul
  2H  "Weak two: six hearts, 4-10"     shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3 | (!has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,H) | (!has(K,H), !has(A,S), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, !vul
  2H  "Weak two: six hearts, 4-10, a good suit"     shows H=6, hcp=4..10, quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3, S<=3 | (!has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), !has(J,S)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,H) | (!has(K,H), !has(A,S), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, vul
  2S  "Weak two: six spades, 4-10"     shows S=6, hcp=4..10, H<=3 | (!has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), !has(J,H)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,S) | (!has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, !vul
  2S  "Weak two: six spades, 4-10, a good suit"     shows S=6, hcp=4..10, quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3, H<=3 | (!has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), !has(J,H)), hcp<=9 | !has(A,S) | (!has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, style is not standard, system is not brill, vul

# brill (the Brill card, general.system = brill): Brill's weak two is
# six cards, 5-11 HCP, with no five-card side major; a four-card one is
# allowed. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15: "Weak 2 S" requires `hcp<= 11 and
# S == 6 and hcp> 4 and bestsuit('S') and loserlevel >= 2 and S_points >= 6
# and H <= 4 and not shapeopenings` (2D: `S <= 4 and H <= 4`). No
# vulnerability condition. The top stays at 10 and the ace clause stays,
# so the choice against a one-level opening is the default's.
  2D  "Weak two: six diamonds, 5-10, no five-card major"   shows D=6, hcp=5..10, H<=4, S<=4, hcp<=9 | !has(A,D) | (!has(A,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,C))
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, system is brill
  2H  "Weak two: six hearts, 5-10, no five spades"         shows H=6, hcp=5..10, S<=4, hcp<=9 | !has(A,H) | (!has(K,H), !has(A,S), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, system is brill
  2S  "Weak two: six spades, 5-10, no five hearts"         shows S=6, hcp=5..10, H<=4, hcp<=9 | !has(A,S) | (!has(K,S), !has(A,H), !has(A,D), !has(A,C))
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, system is brill

# ── Third seat: five cards will do, and no quality requirement ───────
when opening, seat=3
  2D  "Weak two: five or six diamonds, 4-9"  shows D>=5, D<=6, hcp=4..9, H<=3, S<=3
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open, D>=6 | quality(D)>=good
  2H  "Weak two: five or six hearts, 4-9"  shows H>=5, H<=6, hcp=4..9, S<=3
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open, H>=6 | quality(H)>=good
  2S  "Weak two: five or six spades, 4-9"  shows S>=5, S<=6, hcp=4..9
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open, S>=6 | quality(S)>=good

# ── Fourth seat: no weak two; 2 of a suit is a sound minimum opening ─
# The hand that would open one and rebid two of the suit: a six-card suit
# and 12-15 total points (Rick, 2026-11-09). Stronger hands open one.
when opening, seat=4
  2D  "Fourth seat: six diamonds, 12-15"  shows D>=6, points>=12, points<=15
      when two_d is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2d_open
  2H  "Fourth seat: six hearts, 12-15"    shows H>=6, points>=12, points<=15
      when two_h is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2h_open
  2S  "Fourth seat: six spades, 12-15"    shows S>=6, points>=12, points<=15
      when two_s is bidding_conventions/weak_2s, weak_2s_open

# ── Three- and four-level preempts (not in fourth seat) ─────────────
when opening, seat<=3
  3C  "Preempt: seven clubs, 4-9"      shows C=7, hcp=4..9, H<=3, S<=3
      when !vul | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3, system is not brill
  3D  "Preempt: seven diamonds, 4-9"   shows D=7, hcp=4..9, H<=3, S<=3
      when !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3, system is not brill
  3H  "Preempt: seven hearts, 4-9"     shows H=7, hcp=4..9, S<=3
      when !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3, system is not brill
  3S  "Preempt: seven spades, 4-9"     shows S=7, hcp=4..9
      when !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3, system is not brill
  # brill: a side major may be four cards, never five (Brill /explain,
  # 2026-10-15, "Preempt": `clubs >= 7 and hcp>= 5 and hcp<= 11 and
  # totalpoints >= 6 and not shapeopenings and H <= 4 and S <= 4`; 3H
  # `S <= 4`, 3S `H <= 4`).
  3C  "Preempt: seven clubs, 4-9, no five-card major"     shows C=7, hcp=4..9, H<=4, S<=4
      when !vul | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3, system is brill
  3D  "Preempt: seven diamonds, 4-9, no five-card major"  shows D=7, hcp=4..9, H<=4, S<=4
      when !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3, system is brill
  3H  "Preempt: seven hearts, 4-9, no five spades"        shows H=7, hcp=4..9, S<=4
      when !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3, system is brill
  3S  "Preempt: seven spades, 4-9, no five hearts"        shows S=7, hcp=4..9, H<=4
      when !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3, system is brill
  4H  "Preempt: eight hearts"          shows H>=8, hcp=4..10, S<=3
  4S  "Preempt: eight spades"          shows S>=8, hcp=4..10
  5C  "Preempt: eight clubs"           shows C>=8, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  system is not brill
  5D  "Preempt: eight diamonds"        shows D>=8, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  system is not brill
  # brill (the Brill card, no Namyats): four of a minor is a natural
  # preempt with eight, five with nine. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15,
  # "Preemptive_4_Level_Openings": `C >= 8 and hcp>= 5 and hcp<= 11 and
  # loserlevel >= 3 and H <= 4 and S <= 4 and not shapeopenings` (and
  # `C >= 7 ... loserlevel >= 4`); "Preemptive_5_Level_Openings" `C >= 8
  # ... loserlevel >= 5`. Seen at the table: 2026-10-14 IMP board 5,
  # Brill opened 4C with KJT8763 in clubs. Brill's seven-card 4m wants
  # `loserlevel >= 4`; we take a void as that shape (an approximation).
  4C  "Preempt: seven or eight clubs, no five-card major"  shows C=8 | (C=7, shortest=0), hcp=4..10, H<=4, S<=4
      when  system is brill
      priority 1                         # a seven-card suit with a void: ahead of 3C
  4D  "Preempt: seven or eight diamonds, no five-card major"  shows D=8 | (D=7, shortest=0), hcp=4..10, H<=4, S<=4
      when  system is brill
      priority 1
  5C  "Preempt: nine or more clubs"                   shows C>=9, hcp=4..10, H<=4, S<=4
      when  system is brill
  5D  "Preempt: nine or more diamonds"                shows D>=9, hcp=4..10, H<=4, S<=4
      when  system is brill

# bba: not vulnerable, six-four in the minors opens at the three level
# with 4-8 (9-10 open 2D, and six clubs have no weak two).
  3D  "Preempt: six diamonds and four clubs, 4-8"  shows D=6, C=4, hcp=4..8
      when !vul, seat<=2, style is bba
  3C  "Preempt: six clubs and four diamonds, 4-8"  shows C=6, D=4, hcp=4..8
      when !vul, seat<=2, style is bba

# ── Responder to a three-level preempt ────────────────────────────────
# Before these rules responder had no call at all after 3x-(P): ~700
# corpus boards where BBA bid (probes/preempt-resp-3S.toml, 3C). BBA,
# 2026-09-25:
# - over 3M, game with four trumps whatever the strength, with three and
#   9 support points (HCP and shortness), with two and 15 HCP;
# - over 3m, a preemptive 4m with three trumps and less than 12, and 5m
#   with four and a singleton or 12+ (15+ with three and a singleton);
#   strong hands without a fit pass (3NT and a long major: 2026-09-30,
#   below and preempts.notes.md). Vulnerable, 4m is
#   invitational (9-14, two trumps will do), weak hands pass, and 5m wants
#   15, or 12 with four trumps and a singleton. (BBA follows relative
#   vulnerability, and is mixed at equal; keying on ours alone scores
#   best against par: preempts.notes.md.)
after 3H (P)
  4H  "Raise to game"  shows H>=4 | (H=3, tp(H)>=9) | (H=2, hcp>=15)
after 3S (P)
  4S  "Raise to game"  shows S>=4 | (S=3, tp(S)>=9) | (S=2, hcp>=15)
after 3C (P)
  3N  "To play: 16+, A or K of clubs, side suits stopped"
      shows hcp>=16, has(A,C) | has(K,C), stop(S), stop(H), stop(D)
      priority 2
  4H  "To play: seven hearts"    shows H>=7, hcp>=12
      priority 2
  4S  "To play: seven spades"    shows S>=7, hcp>=12
      priority 2
  5C  "Game in clubs: 17+ and a doubleton"  shows C>=2, hcp>=17
      priority 1
  5C  "Game in clubs"  shows C>=4, shortest<=1 | hcp>=12 | (C>=3, hcp>=15, shortest<=1)
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  4C  "Preemptive raise"  shows C>=3, hcp<=11
      when  !vul
  5C  "Game in clubs"  shows C>=3, hcp>=15 | (C>=4, hcp>=12, shortest<=1)
      when  vul
      priority 1
  4C  "Invitational raise"  shows C>=2, hcp=9..14
      when  vul
after 3D (P)
  3N  "To play: 16+, A or K of diamonds, side suits stopped"
      shows hcp>=16, has(A,D) | has(K,D), stop(S), stop(H), stop(C)
      priority 2
  4H  "To play: seven hearts"    shows H>=7, hcp>=12
      priority 2
  4S  "To play: seven spades"    shows S>=7, hcp>=12
      priority 2
  5D  "Game in diamonds: 17+ and a doubleton"  shows D>=2, hcp>=17
      priority 1
  5D  "Game in diamonds"  shows D>=4, shortest<=1 | hcp>=12 | (D>=3, hcp>=15, shortest<=1)
      when  !vul
      priority 1
  4D  "Preemptive raise"  shows D>=3, hcp<=11
      when  !vul
  5D  "Game in diamonds"  shows D>=3, hcp>=15 | (D>=4, hcp>=12, shortest<=1)
      when  vul
      priority 1
  4D  "Invitational raise"  shows D>=2, hcp=9..14
      when  vul

# Responder passes everything else (2026-09-30): a misfit, a weak hand,
# or a strong one without a fit and without 3NT. Before this rule the
# pass was the engine's "no rule" (vanilla SAYC: ~490 boards).
after 3x (P) when x is not N
  P   "No game: no fit, or not enough"
      priority -10

# The preempter after partner's raise to four of the minor: pass. BBA
# passed all 45 times on the vanilla SAYC set, 6-10 HCP.
after 3x (P) 4x (P) when x is C | x is D
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -10
files.rules/base/preempts.notes.md:
# preempts (`preempts.bid`) and the opening rules: notes

Weak two-bids, three- and four-level preempts, and the seat rules in
`base.bid`. Cases: `preempts.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **A weak two is 4-9 HCP with a six-card suit.** Vulnerable it needs two
  of the top three or three of the top five honours.
- **Third seat is looser**: a five-card suit will do (we ask for a good one:
  BBA passes those hands, so an unqualified five-card weak two costs about
  200 calls).
- **Fourth seat has no weak two**: two of a suit there shows a six-card
  suit and the values of a minimum opening.
  Rick, 2026-11-09: the hand that would open one and rebid two of the
  suit, **12-15 total points**; 18 with a six-card suit is too strong.
  The rule allowed 12-21 HCP until then.
- **With a seven-card suit, open at the three level**, not the two.
- **Third seat may open one of a good four-card major** with 10-11.
- **Fourth seat opens by the rule of 15**: HCP plus spade length, 15+.
- **A one-level opening needs 12 total points** — HCP plus one for each
  card beyond four in every suit — not 12 HCP, so nothing falls between a
  weak two and an opening bid.
- The same guidelines apply to a weak jump overcall (not written yet).

## Evidence

Basic_Weak_2: calls 61.9% → 76.0%, identical auctions 0.2% → 13.2%.
Basic_What_To_Open: 68.4% → 76.6%. Whole corpus: calls agreeing 70.3% →
71.9%, first-call divergences 37,868 → 15,699.

**The rule of 20 was measured** as an extra requirement for hands without a
six-card suit (it rules out 11 HCP with 5-3-3-2). BBA opens those hands far
more often than it passes them: 2,939 calls lost against 225 gained, so the
12 total points stand alone.

**Rick, 2026-09-23: a major weak two goes up to 10 HCP** (preemptive
value), where a 10-count with six cards used to open at the one level (12
total points). BBA does the same (about 70 Basic_Weak_2 boards). Measured
against par it costs: −243 IMPs on the corpus over 1,106 changed boards,
−42 on Basic_*. Most of the first measurement (−515) was a bug it exposed:
"no feature" over the 2NT ask was capped at 9 HCP, so a 10-count passed a
forcing 2NT (fixed in weak-two-responses.bid). What remains is the
preempt's own price: partner passes 2M with hands that would reach game
after 1M, and par does not reward the preemption here. Kept as Rick's
ruling; the trade is his to revisit. Diamonds stay 4-9 (par favoured our
1♦ on those boards, +29).

**A side four-card major** (Rick: modern style allows it, depending on
the relative suit quality) was tried as "the six-card suit holds more of
the top five honours than the major": −51 IMPs on the corpus, −26 on
Basic (−75/−33 with the 2NT fix). Not adopted; **question for Rick**
whether a different quality test is worth trying.

Responder had no rule at all after 3x-(P): about 700 corpus boards where

|---|---|

| 3♦ | P 264, 4♦ 31, 5♦ 31, 3NT 15, 3♥ 12, 3♠ 7, 6♦ 3, 4♥ 3, 4♠ 1 |

BBA's passes run from 1 to 20 HCP: misfits and strong hands without a
fit alike. So:

- **Pass** is a rule now, the lowest of the responses: "no game: no fit,
  or not enough".
- **3NT over a minor** (BBA 15-26 HCP, nearly always with the ace or
  king of partner's suit and the side suits held): from 16 with the ace
  or king of the minor and a stopper in each side suit, ahead of 5m.

  bidding 5♦ 21/13; it bid 3NT on 6/17 hands we do not (some with three

## Brill (general.system = brill, 2026-10-15)

Brill's treatment, played on the Brill card only (`cards/json/Brill.json`, `general.system = brill`: a stand-in until convention-card's `general.style` takes a `brill` value; cards/README.md "Brill"). Every other card is unchanged (a `.test` line on 21GF-GIB beside each Brill line; `compare --limit 50` tripwire against main: no board changed).

Weak twos: six cards, 5-10 HCP (Brill 5-11; our top stays at 10 so that
the choice against a one-level opening is the default's), with no five-card
side major; a four-card one is allowed whatever its honours. Brill's "Weak 2
S": `hcp<= 11 and S == 6 and hcp> 4 and bestsuit('S') and loserlevel >= 2
and S_points >= 6 and H <= 4 and not shapeopenings` (its second rule:

shapeopenings and H <= 4 and S <= 4`; 3H `S <= 4`, 3S `H <= 4`).

Four of a minor (the Brill card has no Namyats): a natural preempt,
eight cards or seven and a void, no five-card major; five of a minor

shapeopenings`, and `C >= 7 ... loserlevel >= 4`;
"Preemptive_5_Level_Openings" `C >= 8 ... loserlevel >= 5`). A void
stands in for Brill's `loserlevel >= 4` with seven (we have no loser
level term). Seen at the table: 2026-10-14 IMP board 5, Brill opened 4C
with KJT8763 in clubs, which 21GF-GIB (Namyats) reads as a strong heart

The Brill dailies showed our fourth-seat 2♦/2♥ on 14-19 HCP. Every other
