# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Opener's rebid after a one-level suit opening and an uncontested response
# (Standard American). Rick's rulings: 1NT rebid 12-14 HCP; a jump rebid of
# opener's suit or a jump raise of responder's suit 16-18 total points; a
# reverse 17+ with the first suit longer; a jump in a new suit 19+. The rest
# follows BBA's own meanings (see rebids.notes.md).
#
# Strength: notrump rebids in HCP; suit rebids in suit points (HCP + ½ per
# card beyond four); raises of partner's suit in support points, tp(y).
# Minimum rebids have no lower bound: the opening already showed it, and
# light openings (rule of 20) must still answer a forcing response.

module rebids "Opener's rebid"
  kind   system
  needs  responses
  skill  partnership_bidding/rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/reverse_bids
  param  style = general.style
  param  new_suit_forcing = competitive.new_suit_after_overcall_forcing default true
  param  support_x = competitive_bidding/support_doubles default false
  param  support_through = competitive_bidding/support_doubles:through
  param  walsh = bidding_conventions/walsh default true
  param  inverted = bidding_conventions/inverted_minors default false
  param  weak_js3 = bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts:three_level default false
  param  gf21 = bidding_conventions/two_over_one default false
  param  style21 = bidding_conventions/two_over_one:rebid_style default bergen
  param  semi = major_openings.one_nt_response.semi_forcing default false
  param  twalsh = bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh default false
  param  rkcb = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false

# A notrump jump reaches 3NT at most: the last bid is below 2NT, so the
# cheapest notrump bid is 2NT or lower. In a suit's terms: the cheapest
# spade bid is 2S or lower, or the last bid was 2S. Above that a jump in
# notrump is 4NT, which with no notrump bid by us is keycard (Rick,
# 2026-10-03; slam-entry.bid, "The keycard suit"). Used by every natural
# `jump(N)`.
define nt_jump_to_game = cheapest_rank(S) <= 13 | partner.last=2S | rho.last=2S

# Transfer Walsh (`minor_openings.one_club.transfer_resp`): after 1C the
# one-level responses are transfers, so the natural rules for the opener
# and responder that read the response as a suit stand aside there
# (transfer-walsh.bid has the auction instead). Used across base/.
define tw(x) = twalsh, x is C

# Opener's rebid after 1M-2x in a 2/1 game force, by the card's style
# (`major_openings.two_over_one.rebid_style`; Vic Quiros, ACBL Bridge
# Bulletin, September 2026, p. 70; Rick, 2026-10-16: Bergen the
# default). Outside the game force (a round-forcing 2/1, a passed hand)
# none applies: 2M is six or more there (d24a9f6).
define bergen21 = gf21, we.gf, style21 is bergen
define lawrence21 = gf21, we.gf, style21 is lawrence
define schuler21 = gf21, we.gf, style21 is schuler

# ── After a one-level new-suit response ───────────────────────────────
after 1x (P) 1y (P) when !tw(x)
  2y  "Raise: 4+ {y}, minimum"             shows y>=4, tp(y)<=15   sets trump=y
      when  style is not bba
  3y  "Jump raise: 4+ {y}, 16-18"          shows y>=4, tp(y)=16..18   sets trump=y
      when  y is H | y is S, style is not bba   # a major: 19+ jumps to game
  # BBA raises a major on HCP and length, not shortness: 2y up to 14,
  # 3y 15-17 (HCP + a point a card beyond four), game with 18 HCP or 17
  # and 19 support points (rebids.notes.md, "BBA treatment").
  2y  "Raise: 4+ {y}, minimum"       shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=14   sets trump=y
      when  style is bba
  3y  "Jump raise: 4+ {y}, 15-17"    shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=15, hcp<=17, hcp<=16 | tp(y)<=18   sets trump=y
      when  y is H | y is S, style is bba
  3y  "Jump raise: 4+ {y}, 16+"             shows y>=4, tp(y)>=16   sets trump=y
      when  y is C | y is D                  # a minor: there is no four-level game
  2x  "Rebids {x}: 6+, minimum"            shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      when  x is H | x is S
      priority -1                          # a new suit first
  # A minor's rebid is read as five or more (2026-10-09): 5-4 too weak to
  # reverse rebids it too (below). Six-card hands bid it here.
  2x  "Rebids {x}: 5+, minimum"   shows x>=5, suit_points<=15
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  x>=6
      priority -1                          # a new suit first
  3x  "Jump rebid: 6+ {x}, 16-18"          shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      when  style is not bba
      priority -1                          # a new suit first
  3x  "Jump rebid: 6+ {x}, 15-18"    shows x>=6, hcp=15..18
      when  style is bba
      priority -1
  2x  "Rebids {x}: 5+"
      shows x>=5, suit_points<=18
      when  x is C | x is D                 # 5-4-2-2 with 15-18: no other rebid
      priority -4
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14, y<=3
      when  !weak_nt
  2N  "18+ HCP, balanced"                  shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp>=18, y<=3
  2N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=18..19, y<=3
      priority 1                           # ahead of a jump shift or reverse, as BBA
  1N  "Minimum, no fit"           shows hcp<=14, y<=3
      priority -3                          # e.g. 5-4 with a singleton: no suit to rebid
  3x  "Jump rebid: 6+ {x}, 16+"
      shows x>=6, suit_points>=16
      priority -4                          # a long suit with 19+ and no 3NT or 4M
  2N  "15-17 HCP, balanced"     shows balanced, hcp=15..17, y<=3
      when  !weak_nt
      priority -4                          # 1NT would be a lie: the rebid is 12-14
  # With a weak notrump (Rick, 2026-11-07: "3 yes"): the balanced hands
  # too strong for the 1NT opening rebid 1NT, from the top of the range
  # in force up to 17 (15-17 opposite 11+-14); 2NT stays 18-19.
  # Responder counts against opener's shown range (responder-rebids.bid).
  1N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt, y<=3
      when  weak_nt
after 1x (P) 1M (P) when !tw(x)
  4M  "Game raise: 4+ {M}, 19+"            shows M>=4, tp(M)>=19   sets trump=M
      when  style is not bba
      priority 1                           # support first, ahead of a jump shift (BBA)
  4M  "Game raise: 4+ {M}"
      shows M>=4, hcp>=18 | (hcp>=17, tp(M)>=19)   sets trump=M
      when  style is bba

# A new suit: at the one level 4+ and up to 18; at the two level below the
# first suit 4+, not a reverse; a reverse (two level, above the first suit)
# 17+ with the first suit longer; a jump in a new suit 19+, game forcing.
after 1C (P) 1D (P) when !tw(C)
  # Walsh (Rick, 2026-09-24; the modern default): balanced 12-14 rebids
  # 1NT even with one or both four-card majors. Standard, and any card
  # with the Walsh switch off (minor_openings.walsh.play, as BBA reads
  # it), bids a four-card major up the line, balanced or not.
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced, may hold a 4-card major"   shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14
      when  style is not bba, style is not standard, walsh, !weak_nt
      priority 2
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced, no four-card major"   shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14, H<=3, S<=3
      when  style is standard | !walsh
      when  !weak_nt
      priority 2
  # With a weak notrump the same rebids show the hands above it, up to
  # 17 (above, after a one-level response).
  1N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP, may hold a 4-card major"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt
      when  style is not bba, style is not standard, walsh, weak_nt
      priority 2
  1N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP, no four-card major"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt, H<=3, S<=3
      when  style is standard | !walsh
      when  weak_nt
      priority 2
  1H  "4+ hearts, up to 18"                shows H>=4, suit_points<=18, H>=S
      when  style is not bba | S>=4 | !walsh
  1S  "4+ spades, up to 18"                shows S>=4, suit_points<=18, S>H
      when  style is not bba | !walsh
  2H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 19+"         shows H>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(H, C, D)
      when  style is not bba
  2S  "Jump shift: 4+ spades, 19+"         shows S>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(S, C, D)
      when  style is not bba
  # BBA (Walsh style: responder bypasses diamonds with a weak hand and a
  # major) rebids 1NT with 12-17 and one four-card major, even 5-4 with a
  # singleton; 1H only with both majors; a jump shift from 18.
  1N  "12-17 HCP, not both majors"
      shows hcp=12..17, H<=4, S<=4, H<=3 | S<=3, C<=5, D<=4, shortest>=2 | C=5
      when  style is bba, walsh               # Walsh off: up the line, as above
      priority 2
  2H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 18+"   shows H>=4, hcp>=18, H>=S   sets forcing=game, ask=js(H, C, D)
      when  style is bba
  2S  "Jump shift: 4+ spades, 18+"   shows S>=4, hcp>=18, S>H   sets forcing=game, ask=js(S, C, D)
      when  style is bba
after 1C (P) 1H (P) when !tw(C)
  1S  "4+ spades, up to 18"                shows S>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  H<=3                           # four hearts: raise first
      priority 2                           # four spades: 1S before 1NT
  2D  "Reverse: 4+ diamonds, longer clubs, 17+"  shows D>=4, C>D, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  2S  "Jump shift: 4+ spades, 19+"         shows S>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(S, C, H)
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 19+"       shows D>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(D, C, H)
after 1C (P) 1S (P) when !tw(C)
  2D  "Reverse: 4+ diamonds, longer clubs, 17+"  shows D>=4, C>D, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  2H  "Reverse: 4+ hearts, longer clubs, 17+"    shows H>=4, C>H, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 19+"       shows D>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(D, C, S)
  3H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 19+"         shows H>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(H, C, S)
after 1D (P) 1H (P)
  1S  "4+ spades, up to 18"                shows S>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  H<=3                           # four hearts: raise first
      priority 2                           # four spades: 1S before 1NT
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=12..14, H<=3
      when  style is not bba, !weak_nt     # Rick: balanced rebids 1NT, not 2C
      priority 1
  1N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP"
      shows balanced, above_weak_nt, H<=3
      when  style is not bba, weak_nt
      priority 1
  1N  "12-13 HCP, balanced"   shows balanced, hcp=12..13, H<=3, C=4
      when  style is bba
      priority 1                           # BBA: 1NT before 2C, but 2C with 14
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18, D>=C
  2S  "Jump shift: 4+ spades, 19+"         shows S>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(S, D, H)
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 19+"          shows C>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(C, D, H)
after 1D (P) 1S (P)
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18, D>=C
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=12..14, S<=3
      when  style is not bba, !weak_nt     # Rick: balanced rebids 1NT, not 2C
      priority 1
  1N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP"
      shows balanced, above_weak_nt, S<=3
      when  style is not bba, weak_nt
      priority 1
  1N  "12-13 HCP, balanced"   shows balanced, hcp=12..13, S<=3, C=4
      when  style is bba
      priority 1                           # BBA: 1NT before 2C, but 2C with 14
  2H  "Reverse: 4+ hearts, longer diamonds, 17+"  shows H>=4, D>H, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 19+"          shows C>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(C, D, S)
  3H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 19+"         shows H>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game, ask=js(H, D, S)
after 1H (P) 1S (P)
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18
  2D  "4+ diamonds, up to 18"              shows D>=4, suit_points<=18, D>=C | C<=3
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 19+"          shows C>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 19+"       shows D>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game

# ── After 1NT (not forcing) ──────────────────────────────────────────
after 1x (P) 1N (P)
  P   "Minimum, to play"      shows suit_points<=15
      when  !semi_1nt(x)
      priority -5
  P   "Balanced, no game"    shows balanced, hcp<=17
      when  !semi_1nt(x)
      priority -1                          # BBA passes 5-3-3-2 with 16-17 (major-rebid-1S-1N.toml)
  2x  "Rebids {x}: 5+, 16-18"
      shows x>=5, suit_points=16..18
      priority -2                          # 5-4 with 16-18: a reverse needs 17
  2x  "Rebids {x}: 6+, minimum"            shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      priority -1
  3x  "Jump rebid: 6+ {x}, 16-18"          shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      when  style is not bba
      priority -1
  2N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=18..19
  # 4-4-4-1 with 18+ and no suit to reverse into or jump in had no call
  # (Basic_Minor 78, AQJT.K765.AK72.Q: BBA 3NT).
  3N  "Game: 18+"   shows hcp>=18
      priority -3
  3x  "Jump rebid: 6+ {x}, 15-18"    shows x>=6, hcp=15..18
      when  style is bba
      priority -1
after 1S (P) 1N (P)
  # Over a forcing 1NT the minor may be three cards (below): read as such.
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  !(we.forcing = round | semi_1nt(S))
  2D  "4+ diamonds, up to 18"              shows D>=4, suit_points<=18, D>=C | C<=3
      when  !(we.forcing = round | semi_1nt(S))
  2H  "4+ hearts, up to 18"                shows H>=4, suit_points<=18
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 19+"          shows C>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 19+"       shows D>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  3H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 19+"         shows H>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  # BBA jumps sooner: 17 suit points in hearts, 18 in a minor; 5-5 with
  # 16 bids game in hearts.
  3H  "Jump shift: 4+ hearts, 17+"   shows H>=4, suit_points>=17   sets forcing=game
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 18+"    shows C>=4, suit_points>=18   sets forcing=game
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 18+"  shows D>=4, suit_points>=18   sets forcing=game
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
  4H  "5-5 in the majors, 16+"       shows H>=5, hcp>=16   sets trump=H
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
after 1H (P) 1N (P)
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  !(we.forcing = round | semi_1nt(H))
  2D  "4+ diamonds, up to 18"              shows D>=4, suit_points<=18, D>=C | C<=3
      when  !(we.forcing = round | semi_1nt(H))
  2S  "Reverse: 4+ spades, longer hearts, 17+"   shows S>=4, H>S, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 19+"          shows C>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 19+"       shows D>=4, suit_points>=19   sets forcing=game
  3C  "Jump shift: 4+ clubs, 18+"    shows C>=4, suit_points>=18   sets forcing=game
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
  3D  "Jump shift: 4+ diamonds, 18+"  shows D>=4, suit_points>=18   sets forcing=game
      when  style is bba
      priority 1
after 1D (P) 1N (P)
  2C  "4+ clubs, up to 18"                 shows C>=4, suit_points<=18
  2H  "Reverse: 4+ hearts, longer diamonds, 17+"  shows H>=4, D>H, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  2S  "Reverse: 4+ spades, longer diamonds, 17+"  shows S>=4, D>S, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
after 1C (P) 1N (P)
  2D  "Reverse: 4+ diamonds, longer clubs, 17+"  shows D>=4, C>D, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  2H  "Reverse: 4+ hearts, longer clubs, 17+"    shows H>=4, C>H, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1
  2S  "Reverse: 4+ spades, longer clubs, 17+"    shows S>=4, C>S, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      priority 1

# ── Too strong for a jump rebid ──────────────────────────────────────
# A jump rebid of our own suit is 16-18, so 19+ with a one-suiter had no
# rebid at all and passed a forcing response. BBA plays these as 3NT with
# a long minor ("calculated bid: 18 to 21 total points, 6+ clubs"), and
# game in a long major.
#
# A major's jump to game is not made once the response forced to game (a
# two-over-one, a strong jump shift): there the jump to game is the
# minimum (fast arrival), and with 19+ opposite a game force slam is in
# the air (2026-09-30, random deals: 1H 2S 4H with 20 HCP facing 15,
# where responder passed 35 between us). The minor's 3NT stays: its
# 18-21 is what over-3nt.bid counts to 6NT, and without it opener had
# only base.bid's bare 3NT (corpus: -1,027 on 465 boards).
after 1m (P) 1y (P) | 1m (P) 2y (P)
  3N  "18-21 with six or more {m}: to play"
      shows m>=6, hcp=18..21
      when  y is not m, !wjs_on | !partner.jumped   # opposite a weak jump shift: weak-jump-shifts.bid
      when  !(weak_nt, partner.last=2C)      # with a weak notrump 1D-2C-3NT is 15-17 balanced (below)
after 1M (P) 1y (P) | 1M (P) 2y (P)
  4M  "19+ with six or more {M}: game"
      shows M>=6, hcp+length_points>=19
      when  y is not M, style is not bba, !we.gf
  4M  "Game: seven {M} and 13+, or six and 19+"
      shows M>=6, (M>=7, hcp>=13) | hcp>=19
      when  y is not M, style is bba, !we.gf
# The same two rules after a 1NT response. They cannot share the context
# above: `y` is bound by the other alternatives only, and a `when` that
# names it can never be decided after 1NT, so the rules never fired.
after 1m (P) 1N (P)
  3N  "18-21 with six or more {m}: to play"
      shows m>=6, hcp=18..21
# A semi-forcing 1NT (2/1 cards with `one_nt_response.semi_forcing`,
# 6-12; Todd, Adventures in Bridge #375): opener passes only a balanced
# minimum and otherwise rebids as over the forcing 1NT below.
define semi_1nt(x) = semi, gf21, x is H | x is S
after 1M (P) 1N (P) when semi_1nt(M)
  P   "Semi-forcing 1NT: balanced minimum, to play"   shows balanced, hcp<=14

# A forcing 1NT (2/1 cards with `one_nt_response.forcing`, 6-12): opener
# may not pass, so a balanced hand bids its longer minor, three cards if
# need be, and 18-19 bids 2NT (2026-09-30, 2/1 game force).
after 1M (P) 1N (P) when we.forcing = round | semi_1nt(M)
  # A minor over the forcing 1NT is three or more (standard 2/1): the
  # four-card rebid is read with the three-card one (2026-10-09; it read
  # as "4+", which the three-card rebid below does not hold).
  2C  "Forcing 1NT: clubs, three or more, up to 18"   shows C>=3, suit_points<=18
      when  C>=4
  2D  "Forcing 1NT: diamonds, three or more, up to 18"   shows D>=3, suit_points<=18
      when  D>=4, D>=C | C<=3
  2C  "Forcing 1NT: three or more clubs"   shows C>=3, C>=D, suit_points<=18, M<=5
      priority -1
  2D  "Forcing 1NT: three or more diamonds"  shows D>=3, D>C, suit_points<=18, M<=5
      priority -1
  2N  "Forcing 1NT: 18-19, balanced"       shows balanced, hcp=18..19
  # Six, or five when the hand has no three-card minor to bid (5-4-2-2
  # with the other major). Read as six (Rick, 2026-10-16: a major rebid
  # is six or more in any context); the five-card one is the least lie.
  2M  "Rebids {M}: six or more, minimum"
      shows M>=6, suit_points<=15
  2M  "Rebids {M}: six or more, minimum"
      shows M>=5, suit_points<=15, C<=2, D<=2
      priority -1
after 1M (P) 1N (P)
  4M  "19+ with six or more {M}: game"
      shows M>=6, hcp+length_points>=19
      when  style is not bba
  4M  "Game: seven {M} and 13+, or six and 19+"
      shows M>=6, (M>=7, hcp>=13) | hcp>=19
      when  style is bba

# ── After a raise ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# With a fit found, opener counts support points tp(x): BBA bids game over a
# simple raise with 16-18 and a singleton, but passes 14-15 with doubletons.
# A raise that can hold 11-12 (a card without the limit raise:
# responses.bid) is invited from 15 (responses.notes.md, 2026-09-30).
# Not over an inverted raise: inverted-minors.bid has opener's rebids.
after 1x (P) 2x (P) when !inverted | x is H | x is S
  P   "Minimum: no game"                   shows tp(x)<=16, tp(x)<=14 | x is C | x is D | partner.tp(x).max<=10
      when  style is not bba | x is C | x is D
      priority -5
  3x  "Invitation: game try in {x}"
      shows tp(x)=17..18 | (tp(x)=15..16, x is H | x is S, partner.tp(x).max>=11)
      when  style is not bba | x is C | x is D
after 1M (P) 2M (P)
  4M  "Game: 19+ with the fit"             shows tp(M)>=19
      when  style is not bba
  # BBA opposite a raise: pass up to 15 HCP whatever the shape (13 with
  # six trumps), invite with 16 (14-15 with six), bid game with 17, or 16
  # and six trumps or a singleton.
  P   "Minimum: no game"        shows hcp<=15, M<=5 | hcp<=13
      when  style is bba
      priority -5
  3M  "Invitation: game try in {M}"
      shows (hcp=16, M<=5, tp(M)<=18) | (hcp=14..15, M>=6)
      when  style is bba
  4M  "Game: 17+, or 16 with shape"
      shows hcp>=17 | (hcp=16, M>=6 | tp(M)>=19)
      when  style is bba
after 1m (P) 2m (P) when !inverted
  2N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=18..19
  3N  "20-21 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp>=20
  # Counting tricks (Rick, 2026-09-27, ticket b469: K2.A9.AT.AKJ9742
  # passed 1C P 2C): with partner's support a long minor headed by two
  # top honours runs, and stoppers in the other three suits make up the
  # nine tricks in notrump.
  3N  "Nine tricks: a running {m}, the other suits stopped"
      shows m>=6, quality(m)>=2, hcp>=16
      shows stop(C) | m is C, stop(D) | m is D, stop(H), stop(S)
  5{m} "Game: 19+ support points, no notrump"   shows tp(m)>=19
      priority -1

after 1M (P) 3M (P)
  4M  "Accepts the limit raise"            shows tp(M)>=15
  P   "Declines: minimum"                  shows tp(M)<=14
after 1m (P) 3m (P)
  3N  "Accepts, balanced: 14+"             shows hcp>=14, balanced | semibalanced
  5m  "Accepts, unbalanced: game in the minor"   shows hcp>=14
      priority -1
  P   "Declines: minimum"                  shows hcp<=13
      priority -5

after 1m (P) 2N (P)
  3N  "Accepts: 14+"                       shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines: 12-13"                    shows hcp<=13
      priority -5

# Responder's game-forcing 2NT after a two-over-one and opener's rebid
# (12-14 or 18+, no fit: responder-rebids.bid, Rick 2026-11-06): it is
# forcing, and opener counts slam on its minimum with over-3nt.bid's
# numbers for this shape (2026-09-30); responder's strong branch then
# invites over the 3NT.
after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 2N (P) when x is not y, we.gf
  6N  "Slam in notrump"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
  3N  "Game: no extras"                    shows points + partner.points.min <= 30
# A self-sufficient major plays in game, as over-3nt.bid does over
# partner's 3NT (ticket b194): before 2026-11-06 responder's minimum
# bid 3NT and opener answered 4M there; now the minimum bids 2NT, and
# opener's "no extras" 3NT lost the game in the suit (corpus, Namyats
# and Misfit boards, -10 IMPs each).
after 1S (P) 2x (P) 2S (P) 2N (P) when x is not S, we.gf
  4S  "To play: a self-sufficient ♠ suit"
      shows (S>=6, quality(S)=3, top5(S)>=4) | (S>=7, quality(S)=3)
      shows (H<=2, !stop(H)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      priority 1
after 1H (P) 2x (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) when x is not H, we.gf
  4H  "To play: a self-sufficient ♥ suit"
      shows (H>=6, quality(H)=3, top5(H)>=4) | (H>=7, quality(H)=3)
      shows (S<=2, !stop(S)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      priority 1
# In the Lawrence style opener's 2M was the default rebid, five or more
# (Rick, 2026-10-16), so over responder's 2NT (12-14 or 18+, two or fewer of the
# major) a sixth card is news: it makes the doubleton an eight-card fit.
# Only without extras: with them opener counts slam in notrump as above
# (measured: 3M first with every hand lost the 4NT/6NT count, -51 by
# errors on 22 boards at --limit 50). Bergen's 2M was six already, and
# Schuler's exactly five (six bid 2NT).
after 1M (P) 2x (P) 2M (P) 2N (P) when x is not M, lawrence21
  3M  "Six or more {M}, no extras"
      shows M>=6, points + partner.points.min <= 30
      priority 2                           # the fit before 3NT

# ── After the jump rebid of a minor, responder's continuation ───────
# (2026-10-20, Brill daily board 7: 1D 1S 3D 4D, opener had no rule.)
# Responder's 4m invites (3+, 8 points; responder-rebids.bid): accept with a
# maximum (17+ HCP) unless two side suits are bare (no ace or king), the
# notrump game's tricks are not there for five of a minor either; a
# minimum passes. Responder's 3M (five, forcing): 4M with three, else
# 3NT.
after 1m (P) 1y (P) 3m (P) 4m (P)
  5{m} "Accepts: a maximum, 17+"            shows hcp>=17
      when  !two_bare_suits
  P    "Declines: minimum, or two bare side suits"
      priority -5
after 1m (P) 1M (P) 3m (P) 3M (P)
  4{M} "Three-card support"                 shows M>=3
  3N   "No three-card support"              shows M<=2
      priority -1

# ── After a two-over-one response (forcing one round) ────────────────
# In a 2/1 game force the rebid follows one of three styles, the card's
# `major_openings.two_over_one.rebid_style` (Vic Quiros, "Vic's Views:
# Building a new partnership - part 1", ACBL Bridge Bulletin, September
# 2026, p. 70; Rick, 2026-10-16: rules for all three, Bergen the
# default):
#
#                       Bergen     Lawrence    Schuler
#   default (nothing)   2NT        2M          2M
#   2M shows            six+       five+       exactly five
#   new suit: extras?   no         yes         yes
#   2NT shows           nothing    stoppers    six+ in M
#
# "New suit" is a reverse (1H-2m-2S) or a new suit at the three level
# (1H-2D-3C, 1S-2H-3m); a lower suit at the two level (1S-2C-2D/2H,
# 1S-2D-2H, 1H-2C-2D) is natural with no extras in every style. Raises
# of responder's suit and the jumps (3M six 16-18, 3NT 18-19) are the
# same in all three.
after 1M (P) 2x (P) when x is not M, !wjs_on | !partner.jumped   # a weak jump shift: weak-jump-shifts.bid
  # Bergen: 2NT says nothing: any hand without a better call, a 5-3-3-2
  # of any strength below the 3NT rebid, no stopper promised. 2M is six
  # or more, any strength; a new suit is shape, not strength.
  2N  "Waiting: 5+ {M}"
      shows M>=5
      when  bergen21
      priority -1                          # a new suit, 2M with six, a raise, a jump first
  # The six-card suit comes before a four-card side suit (6-4: 2M, not
  # the new suit; BBA and Brill alike, probes/rebid-style-*.toml), and
  # the jump keeps its 16-18 above it.
  2M  "Rebids {M}: 6+, any strength"
      shows M>=6, x<=2 | x is C | x is D    # 1S-2H: a heart fit raises first
      when  bergen21
      priority 1
  3M  "Jump rebid: 6+ {M}, 16-18"          shows M>=6, suit_points=16..18
      when  bergen21
      priority 1
  # Lawrence: 2M is the default, waiting rebid, five or more and any
  # strength (Rick, 2026-10-16: "for 2-over-1 sequences, 1M - 2x - 2M is
  # the default response, not promising 6+", 481e3ad). 2NT is balanced
  # with the unbid suits stopped and no fit for a major 2/1.
  2M  "Rebids {M}: 5+, any strength"
      shows M>=5
      when  lawrence21
      priority -1                          # a new suit, a raise, a jump first
  2N  "Balanced, the unbid suits stopped"
      shows balanced, hcp<=17, x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      shows stop(C) | x is C, stop(D) | x is D, stop(H) | x is H | M is H, stop(S) | x is S | M is S
      when  lawrence21
  # Schuler shift: 2M is the default with exactly five, 2NT shows six or
  # more (any strength below the jump), so the six-card fit opposite a
  # doubleton is known at once.
  2M  "Rebids {M}: exactly five"
      shows M=5
      when  schuler21
      priority -1
  2N  "Schuler shift: six or more {M}"
      shows M>=6
      when  schuler21
  # Otherwise (forcing one round, or "game forcing except" a suit rebid)
  # it reads six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16: a major rebid is six or more
  # in any context). A five-card hand with nothing better still rebids
  # it, the least lie, read by the six-card rule (a read-as call by
  # design); until then it was read as 5+.
  2M  "Rebids {M}: 6+, minimum"            shows M>=6, suit_points<=15
      when  !(gf21, we.gf)
      priority -1                          # the default minimum rebid
  2M  "Rebids {M}: 6+, minimum"
      shows M>=5, suit_points<=18
      when  !(gf21, we.gf)
      priority -2
  3M  "Jump rebid: 6+ {M}, 16-18"          shows M>=6, suit_points=16..18
      when  !bergen21
  3x  "Raise: 4+ {x}"                      shows x>=4
      sets  trump=x                        # agreed: keycard and the fit follow (ticket b173)
  2N  "15-17 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=15..17
      when  !(gf21, we.gf)
      priority -3                          # a 5-3-3-2 rebids its major (below every 2M)
  3N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=18..19
after 1S (P) 2C (P)
  2D  "4+ diamonds"                        shows D>=4
  2H  "4+ hearts"                          shows H>=4
# A reverse or a new suit at the three level shows extras, except in the
# Bergen style, where it is shape alone (the table above).
after 1S (P) 2D (P)
  2H  "4+ hearts"                          shows H>=4
  3C  "4+ clubs, extras"                   shows C>=4, suit_points>=16
      when  !bergen21
  3C  "4+ clubs, no extras promised"   shows C>=4
      when  bergen21
after 1S (P) 2H (P)
  3H  "Raise: 3+ hearts"                   shows H>=3
  4H  "Game raise: 3+ hearts, 14-17"       shows H>=3, suit_points=14..17
  3C  "4+ clubs, extras"                   shows C>=4, suit_points>=16
      when  !bergen21
  3D  "4+ diamonds, extras"                shows D>=4, suit_points>=16
      when  !bergen21
  3C  "4+ clubs, no extras promised"   shows C>=4
      when  bergen21
  3D  "4+ diamonds, no extras promised"   shows D>=4
      when  bergen21
after 1H (P) 2C (P)
  2D  "4+ diamonds"                        shows D>=4
  2S  "Reverse: 4+ spades, longer hearts, 17+"   shows S>=4, H>S, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      when  !bergen21
      priority 1
  2S  "4+ spades, no extras promised"   shows S>=4
      when  bergen21
after 1H (P) 2D (P)
  2S  "Reverse: 4+ spades, longer hearts, 17+"   shows S>=4, H>S, suit_points>=17  sets forcing=round
      when  !bergen21
      priority 1
  2S  "4+ spades, no extras promised"   shows S>=4
      when  bergen21
  3C  "4+ clubs, extras"                   shows C>=4, suit_points>=16
      when  !bergen21
  3C  "4+ clubs, no extras promised"   shows C>=4
      when  bergen21
after 1D (P) 2C (P)
  2D  "Rebids diamonds: minimum"           shows D>=5, suit_points<=15
      priority -1
  3D  "Jump rebid: 6+ diamonds, 16-18"     shows D>=6, suit_points=16..18
      priority -1
  2D  "Rebids diamonds: 5+"
      shows D>=5, suit_points<=18
      priority -2
  3C  "Raise: 4+ clubs"                    shows C>=4
  2H  "4+ hearts"                          shows H>=4
  2S  "4+ spades"                          shows S>=4
  2N  "12-14 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=12..14
      when  !weak_nt
  3N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  !weak_nt
  # With a weak notrump (Rick, 2026-11-07: "after 2/1 a jump to 3NT
  # shows 15-17, 2NT shows 12-14 or 18-19, same as for opening strong
  # 1NT"): responder's scheme after a 2/1 game force mirrored
  # (responder-rebids.bid, #91). 2NT forces to game; opposite it
  # responder counts slam on the minimum, and opener's strong branch
  # invites over responder's 3NT (below).
  3N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP"
      shows balanced, above_weak_nt, !weak_nt_top_out
      when  weak_nt
  # The good 14 jumps too, read as the rule above (15-17): the slam
  # counts over 3NT need its floor (a 17 opposite it invites).
  3N  "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17 HCP"
      shows balanced, weak_nt_top_out
      when  weak_nt
      priority -1
  2N  "Balanced: 12-14 or 18+ HCP, game forcing"
      shows balanced, (hcp<=14, !weak_nt_top_out) | hcp>=18
      when  weak_nt
      sets  forcing=game
after 1D (P) 2C (P) 2N (P) 3N (P) when weak_nt, shown.hcp.max >= 18
  4N  "Quantitative: 18-19, invites 6NT"   shows hcp>=18
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1

# ── After a reverse over 1NT and responder's preference at three ─────
# Responder has 6-10 and two or more of opener's first suit; opener had
# no third call (Basic_Major 270, 1D-1NT-2S-3D with 20 and 6-5).
after 1x (P) 1N (P) 2z (P) 3x (P) when z is not x
  4x  "Game in the fit: 19+"               shows suit_points>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
  5x  "Game in {x}: 19+ with six"          shows x>=6, suit_points>=20
      when  x is C | x is D
  3N  "Game in notrump: 19+"               shows hcp>=19
      when  x is C | x is D
  P   "Minimum: to play" shows suit_points<=19
      priority -5

# ── After a reverse and responder's forced 2NT ───────────────────────
# Responder's 2NT after a reverse is the forced minimum, 6-10 with no fit
# (responder-rebids.bid; until 2026-10-09 it was read as 11-12 and opener
# accepted the "invitation"). Opposite the reverse's 17+ that is still
# game: 23-27 between us, and the corpus (Reverse_By_Opener, 2026-10-09)
# lost 96 IMPs by errors on 27 boards where opener passed it.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) 2N (P) when z is not x, z is not y, partner.points <= 10, shown.suit_points >= 17
  3N  "Game: 16+"   shows hcp>=16

# ── After an invitational jump shift (10-12, six cards) ──────────────
after 1x (P) 3y (P) when y is not x, we.trump is none, !weak_js3   # not a splinter (splinters.bid); weak ones: weak-jump-shifts.bid
  P   "Minimum, no fit"                    shows hcp<=13
      priority -5
  # With a fit for a minor 3NT is still the game (Basic_Major 44 and 121,
  # and 1H-3D with four diamonds, had no call).
  3N  "Accepts: 14+, to play notrump"      shows hcp>=14, y<=2 | y is C | y is D
  4y  "Accepts in the fit: 14+"            shows y>=2, suit_points>=14
      when  y is H | y is S
  4x  "Accepts in {x}: seven, or six strong"
      shows x>=7 | (x>=6, top5(x)>=4), hcp>=14, y<=1 | y is C | y is D
      when  x is H | x is S

# ── Responder bid a fourth suit at the one level ─────────────────────
# 1♣-1♦-1♥-1♠ is natural on this card, and opener had no third call at
# all. He raises with four, and otherwise shows his shape once more. The
# fourth suit at the one level is always a major, so it binds to `M`.
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) 1M (P) when !tw(x)
  2M  "Raise: 4+ {M}, minimum"             shows M>=4, tp(M)<=15   sets trump=M, ask=signoff
  3M  "Jump raise: 4+ {M}, 16-18"          shows M>=4, tp(M)=16..18   sets trump=M, ask=invite(M)
  4M  "Game raise: 4+ {M}, 19+"            shows M>=4, tp(M)>=19   sets trump=M
  1N  "Minimum, no fit for {M}"            shows M<=3, hcp<=15   sets ask=signoff
  2N  "16-18, no fit for {M}"              shows M<=3, hcp=16..18   sets ask=nt_invite
  2x  "Six or more {x}"                    shows x>=6, suit_points<=15   sets ask=signoff
      priority -1

# ── Partner has signed off ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Responder's weak second calls — a preference, a weak rebid of his own
# suit, a raise of opener's second suit, 1NT — say "play here", and set
# `ask=signoff` (responder-rebids.bid). Opener's answer is the same
# whatever the auction was, so it is written once against the ask rather
# than as the dozen eight-call patterns it would otherwise take: pass
# with a minimum, one more try with 16-18, game with 19+.
when asked signoff, !partner.opened
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5
  2x  "Six or more {x}: to play"        shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      when  maybe partner.x<=2
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  3x  "Invitation: six or more {x}, 16-18"  shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      sets  ask=invite(x)
  3x  "Invitation: 3+ {x}, 16-18"             shows x>=3, suit_points=16..18
      when  partner.x>=5
      sets  ask=invite(x)
  2y  "Preference: three or more {y}"         shows y>=3
      when  partner.y>=5
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -2
  4M  "Game: 6+ {M}, 19+"                     shows M>=6, suit_points>=19
  4M  "Game: 3+ {M}, 19+"                  shows M>=3, suit_points>=19
      when  partner.M>=4

# The same question put to responder, by opener's minimum rebid in a
# contested auction. The rules above are opener's: read as responder's,
# their 3x ("six or more, one more try") took over responder's cue bid
# and opener raised their suit (2026-09-25). Responder's own
# continuations are in responder-rebids.bid; this is the pass under them.
when asked signoff, partner.opened
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5

# ── Answering an invitation in a major ───────────────────────────────
# Any invitation in a major sets `ask=invite(M)`: responder's invitational
# raise or jump in a suit auction, 2NT or 3M after a transfer, a raise
# after Stayman. Play in the major with an eight-card fit, which is 3+
# cards opposite five and 2+ opposite six. Without a fit accept only when
# game is certain (17 opposite 8-9); with the fit one point less is
# enough (16), which par prefers by 1,300 IMPs over the corpus. Until
# 2026-09-30 this lived in jacoby-transfers.bid, so a card without
# transfers had no answer to 1♦-1♥-2♥-3♥ and its relatives
# (rebids.notes.md, "The major invitation without transfers").
when asked invite(M)
  4M  "Accepts, in the fit"             shows M>=8-partner.M.min, points>=24-partner.points.min
  3N  "Accepts, no fit"                 shows M<8-partner.M.min, strength>=game
  3M  "Declines, in the fit"            shows M>=8-partner.M.min, points<=23-partner.points.min
  P   "Declines"                        shows strength<=invite, (M<8-partner.M.min | points<=23-partner.points.min)

# When the invitation was a raise it showed support points, not total
# points, so `partner.points` above stays at the one-level response's 6
# and opener never accepted (1♣-1♠-2♠-3♠ with 14). Opposite a raise
# showing 10+ support points opener counts his own the same way: game
# from 25 between them, 14 opposite 11-12, as BBA (rebids.notes.md).
when asked invite(M), partner.tp(M).min>=10
  4M  "Accepts, in the fit"   shows M>=8-partner.M.min, tp(M)>=25-partner.tp(M).min
      priority 1
  P   "Declines: a minimum"                     shows M>=8-partner.M.min, tp(M)<=24-partner.tp(M).min
      priority 1

# Responder after opener declines in three of the major: pass.
when answered invite(M), partner.last=3{M}
  P   "No further bid"

# ── Answering an invitation in a minor ───────────────────────────────
# Responder's invitational raise or jump sets `ask=invite(x)`. A minor
# invitation had no answer anywhere, so opener passed a live auction.
# Opposite 10-12, opener needs 14 to go on, and there is no game below 5 of a
# minor: 3NT with the values and a shape for it, 5 of the minor with
# real extras, otherwise pass.
when asked invite(m)
  P   "Declines: minimum"
      priority -5
  3N  "Accepts, in notrump: 14+"
      shows hcp>=14, balanced | semibalanced
  5m  "Accepts in {m}: 18+ with the fit"      shows hcp>=18, m>=5

# ══ Opener's rebid once they come in ═════════════════════════════════
#
# Everything above is keyed on `after 1x (P) 1y (P)` and its relatives,
# so none of it fires once the opponents act: opener had no second call
# in any contested auction. That was the largest cluster of dead
# auctions left in the corpus (about 20,000 boards) and, wherever our
# own rules made partner's free bid forcing, the largest source of
# `passed a forcing auction` too.
#
# What opener does with his own hand — raise partner, rebid his suit,
# bid the game — does not depend on what they bid, so these blocks are
# written with `(*)` for their calls and with relative calls
# (`cheapest`, `jump`) so the level takes care of itself. The two things
# that do depend on their call are handled without naming it:
#
#   - **never bid a suit they have shown.** `maybe lho.x<=4` is "LHO has
#     not shown five", which is false after an overcall in that suit and
#     true after a takeout double. Knowledge does the work a pattern
#     variable would have done, and it is right over a double, an
#     overcall, a cue bid or a jump alike.
#   - **notrump needs a stopper**, and a stopper needs their suit bound.
#     Those rules are the one place a pattern names it, in blocks of
#     their own below; over a takeout double there is no suit to stop.
#
# Strength is measured as it is uncontested — notrump in HCP, suit
# rebids in suit points, raises in support points — and Rick's ladder is
# unchanged: 1NT 12-14, a jump rebid or jump raise 16-18, a reverse 17+,
# a jump in a new suit 19+. Partner's free bid is worth about what an
# uncontested response is worth, so the same numbers apply.

# ── Partner made a free bid in a new suit at the one level ───────────
# BBA never passes here, over an overcall or over a double (49 of 49
# positions in the Basic-Bridge scenarios), so the block ends with a
# rebid of opener's own suit rather than a pass when RHO has passed.
after 1x (*) 1z (*) when they.bid, z is not x
  cheapest(z) "Raise: four or more {z}, minimum"
      shows z>=4, tp(z)<=15
      when  partner.z>=4
      sets  trump=z, ask=signoff
  jump(z) "Jump raise: four or more {z}, 16-18"
      shows z>=4, tp(z)=16..18
      when  partner.z>=4, z is H | z is S
      sets  trump=z, ask=invite(z)
  jump(z) "Jump raise: four or more {z}, 16+"
      shows z>=4, tp(z)>=16
      when  partner.z>=4, z is C | z is D
      sets  trump=z
  4{z} "Game raise: four or more {z}, 19+"
      shows z>=4, tp(z)>=19
      when  partner.z>=4, z is H | z is S
      sets  trump=z
  # A major rebid is read as six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16): the
  # five-card rebid with nothing better to say, below, is the least lie
  # and is read by this rule. A minor's stays five or more (2026-10-09):
  # six-card hands bid it here.
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, minimum"
      shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      when  x is H | x is S
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: 5+, minimum"
      shows x>=5, suit_points<=15
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  x>=6
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  jump(x) "Jump rebid: six or more {x}, 16-18"
      shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      sets  ask=invite(x)
      priority -1
  4{x} "Game: six or more {x}, 19+"
      shows x>=6, suit_points>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10
# Their pass leaves partner's free bid unanswered, and it is not a call
# opener may leave: with nothing else, he repeats his own suit.
after 1x (*) 1z (P) when they.bid, z is not x
  # A second suit, when neither opponent has shown it: at the one level
  # four cards, at the two level four cards below opener's first suit,
  # and above it a reverse, 17+ with the first suit longer.
  1H  "Four or more hearts, up to 18"
      shows H>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not H, z is not H
      when  maybe lho.H<=4, maybe rho.H<=4
  1S  "Four or more spades, up to 18"
      shows S>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not S, z is not S
      when  maybe lho.S<=4, maybe rho.S<=4
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs, up to 18"
      shows C>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not C, z is not C
      when  maybe lho.C<=4, maybe rho.C<=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds, up to 18"
      shows D>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is H | x is S
      when  z is not D
      when  maybe lho.D<=4, maybe rho.D<=4
      priority -2
  2H  "Reverse: four or more hearts, longer {x}, 17+"
      shows H>=4, x>H, suit_points>=17
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  z is not H
      when  maybe lho.H<=4, maybe rho.H<=4
      sets  forcing=round
  2S  "Reverse: four or more spades, longer {x}, 17+"
      shows S>=4, x>S, suit_points>=17
      when  x is not S, z is not S
      when  maybe lho.S<=4, maybe rho.S<=4
      sets  forcing=round
  2D  "Reverse: four or more diamonds, longer clubs, 17+"
      shows D>=4, C>D, suit_points>=17
      when  x is C, z is not D
      when  maybe lho.D<=4, maybe rho.D<=4
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: 5+"
      shows x>=5, suit_points<=18
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -4
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}"
      priority -6

# Notrump is the one rebid that has to know which suit they bid, so it
# is written with their call bound. Over a takeout double there is no
# suit to stop and the range is the same. When they overcall partner's
# response instead, the ranges are BBA's (below).
after 1x (1y) 1z (P) | 1x (2y) 1z (P) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y
  cheapest(N) "12-14 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14, z<=3
      when  stop(y), !weak_nt
      sets  ask=signoff
  # With a weak notrump: the hands above it, up to 17 (Rick, 2026-11-07,
  # as uncontested).
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt, z<=3
      when  stop(y), weak_nt
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19, z<=3
      when  stop(y)
  # Strong hands with nothing else to bid (2026-09-25: 19-counts repeated
  # a five-card suit and were passed): 3NT with their suit held, else a
  # cue bid of their suit, forcing to game.
  3N  "Game: 19+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=19, stop(y), z<=3
      priority -1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 19+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows suit_points>=19
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -3

# They overcalled partner's response at the one level (1C P 1H (1S);
# it had no rule, bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #93). BBA's ranges
# (Rick 2026-11-07: "we can follow BBA's lead"; probes/opnt-1C-1H-1S.toml,
# opnt-1C-1D-1S.toml): 1NT 13-16 (a balanced 12 passes), the jump to
# 2NT 17-18, 3NT 19+. In practice 13-14, 18 and 19: a balanced 15-17
# opened 1NT.
after 1x (P) 1z (1y) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y
  cheapest(N) "13-16 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=13..16, z<=3
      when  stop(y), !weak_nt
      sets  ask=signoff
  jump(N) "17-18 with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp=17..18, z<=3, longest<=6       # BBA: unbalanced too
      when  stop(y), !weak_nt
  # With a weak notrump the 12-14 hands opened 1NT and the 15-17 ones
  # did not: 1NT shows those (up to 17), the jump 18-19 (Rick,
  # 2026-11-07, as uncontested).
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt, z<=3
      when  stop(y), weak_nt
  jump(N) "18-19 with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp=18..19, z<=3, longest<=6
      when  stop(y), weak_nt
  3N  "Game: 19+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=19, stop(y), z<=3
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 19+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows suit_points>=19
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -3
after 1x (X) 1z (P) when z is not x
  cheapest(N) "12-14 balanced"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14, z<=3
      when  !weak_nt
      sets  ask=signoff
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, above_weak_nt, z<=3
      when  weak_nt
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19, z<=3

# Opener with 18+ after 1x (X) 1z (1w): double, the strong hand, as BBA
# (2026-09-27, ticket b6: 18 balanced passed 1C X 1D 1S). Responder's
# answers are in responder-rebids.bid.
# Where the double is a support double (support-doubles.bid: partner's
# major, their call no higher than the card's `through`), it is not
# this one: with support doubles on BBA doubles with three of partner's
# major at any strength and never with 18+ otherwise
# (probes/support-x-1C-X-1H-1S.toml).
after 1x (X) 1z (1y) when z is not x, y is not x, y is not z
  X   "Strong hand: 18+"
      shows hcp>=18
      when  !support_x | z is C | z is D | !((support_through is none, rho.last <= 2{z}) | rho.last <= support_through)
      priority -2
after 1x (X) 1z (1y) X (P) * (P) when z is not x, y is not x, y is not z, !answered support
  cheapest(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19, stop(y)
  3N  "20+ balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=20, stop(y)
  cheapest(x) "Six or more {x}, the strong hand"
      shows x>=6
      priority -1
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -5

# ── Partner made a free bid in a new suit at the two level or higher ─
# Partner has 8-10 or more and five cards, and on the cards where a new
# suit over interference is forcing (`competitive.new_suit_after_
# overcall_forcing`, on by default and off on Basic-Bridge) opener must
# bid: those auctions were 1,438 of the corpus's 1,838 broken forces.
# Where it is not forcing, BBA passes a minimum with no fit about a
# third of the time, and that is the `P` at the foot of the block — the
# engine drops it of its own accord when the auction is forcing.
# Natural free bids only (2026-10-09): a cue bid of their suit (a limit
# raise or better, after-interference.bid) or another artificial call is
# answered where it is defined; here opener's 3x read as "six or more"
# where the cue-bid answer bids it on any minimum.
after 1x (*) 2z (*) | 1x (*) 3z (*) | 1x (*) 4z (*) when they.bid, z is not x, partner.named(z)
  cheapest(z) "Raise: three or more {z}"
      shows z>=3, tp(z)<=17
      when  partner.z>=5
      sets  trump=z, ask=signoff
  cheapest(z) "Raise: four or more {z}, minimum"
      shows z>=4, tp(z)<=17
      when  partner.z>=4, maybe partner.z<=4
      sets  trump=z, ask=signoff
  4{z} "Game raise: 18+ with the fit"
      shows z>=3, tp(z)>=18
      when  partner.z>=4, z is H | z is S
      sets  trump=z
  # A major rebid is read as six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16): the
  # five-card rebid with nothing better to say, below, is the least lie
  # and is read by this rule. A minor's stays five or more (2026-10-09):
  # six-card hands bid it here.
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, minimum"
      shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      when  x is H | x is S
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: 5+, minimum"
      shows x>=5, suit_points<=15
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  x>=6
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  jump(x) "Jump rebid: six or more {x}, 16-18"
      shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      sets  ask=invite(x)
      priority -1
  4{x} "Game: six or more {x}, 19+"
      shows x>=6, suit_points>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
  P   "Minimum, no fit"
      shows suit_points<=15
      priority -4                          # BBA passes these ahead of 2NT
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: 5+"
      shows x>=5
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -6
  # Where the free bid is forcing, opener had no call with a four-card
  # major, a raise with extras, or nothing at all (2026-09-25: 80
  # no-rule positions such as 1D (1H) 2C (P) on K643.K.KQ32.AJ62).
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not S, z is not S
      when  maybe lho.S<=4, maybe rho.S<=4
      when  we.forcing = round, partner.z>=5   # a free bid, not a cue bid of their suit
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not H, z is not H
      when  maybe lho.H<=4, maybe rho.H<=4
      when  we.forcing = round, partner.z>=5   # a free bid, not a cue bid of their suit
      priority -2
  cheapest(z) "Raise with extras: 18+, forcing to game"
      shows z>=3, tp(z)>=18
      sets  trump=z, forcing=game
      when  partner.z>=5, new_suit_forcing   # a forcing free bid, even if they bid over it
      priority -1
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}"
      when  we.forcing = round, partner.z>=5   # a free bid, not a cue bid of their suit
      priority -8
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10
after 1x (1y) 2z (P) | 1x (2y) 2z (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) | 1x (3y) 3z (P) when y is not x, z is not x, z is not y
  cheapest(N) "Balanced with a stopper in {y}, minimum"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp<=15, z<=3
      when  stop(y)
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -5                          # below the pass: only when forced
  jump(N) "16-18 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=16..18, z<=3
      when  stop(y)
  # Strong hands (2026-09-25): 3NT with their suit held, else a cue bid.
  3N  "Game: 17+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=17, stop(y)
      priority -1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 18+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows suit_points>=18
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -3
after 1x (X) 2z (P) when z is not x
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, minimum"
      shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp<=15, z<=3
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -5                          # below the pass: only when forced

# ── Partner raised opener's suit ─────────────────────────────────────
# The raise is 6-9 over an overcall and 4-9 over a double, close enough
# to the uncontested 6-10 that the same ladder applies: pass up to 16
# support points, invite with 17-18, bid the game with 19. BBA passes
# these hands about two thirds of the time.
after 1x (*) 2x (*) when they.bid
  P   "Minimum: no game"
      shows tp(x)<=16
      priority -5
  cheapest(x) "Invitation: 17-18 with the fit"
      shows tp(x)=17..18
      sets  trump=x, ask=invite(x)
  4{x} "Game: 19+ with the fit"
      shows tp(x)>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
      sets  trump=x
  # Their suit stopped (Rick, 2026-10-16: no stopper prohibits 3NT).
  3N  "Game: 19+, balanced"
      shows balanced, hcp>=19, stop(they.strain)
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  they.strain is not none, they.strain is not N
  3N  "Game: 19+, balanced"
      shows balanced, hcp>=19
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  they.strain is none | they.strain is N
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10
# A jump raise over their call is preemptive, so opener bids the game or
# lets it alone.
after 1x (*) 3x (*) when they.bid
  4{x} "Game: 19+"
      shows tp(x)>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
      sets  trump=x
  5{x} "Game: 19+"
      shows tp(x)>=19
      when  x is C | x is D
      sets  trump=x
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10
# Over a two-level overcall three of opener's suit is often the cheapest
# raise, 7-10, not a jump; it was read as preemptive, so 16-21 passed
# (2026-09-26: 51 corpus boards with 25+ HCP and game on).
after 1x (2y) 3x (P) when y is not x, !partner.jumped
  3N  "Game: 16+ with a stopper in {y}"   shows hcp>=16, stop(y)
      when  x is C | x is D
  4{x} "Game: 17+ support points"          shows tp(x)>=17
      when  x is H | x is S
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 18+"            shows hcp>=18
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority -1
# Partner raised a minor to four over their preempt (7-10, three-card
# support): game with 16+ (2026-09-25: no rule; 1C (3S) 4C with 18).
after 1x (*) 4x (*) when they.bid, x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Game: 16+ with the fit"             shows hcp>=16
      sets  trump=x
  P   "No game"                            shows hcp<=15
      priority -10

# ── Partner bid notrump over their call ──────────────────────────────
# 1NT here is 6-10 with a stopper in their suit, so opener passes a
# minimum, repeats a six-card suit, and jumps with 16-18.
after 1x (*) 1N (*) when they.bid
  P   "Minimum"
      shows suit_points<=15
      priority -5
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, minimum"
      shows x>=6, suit_points<=15
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  jump(x) "Jump rebid: six or more {x}, 16-18"
      shows x>=6, suit_points=16..18
      sets  ask=invite(x)
      priority -1
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
  4{x} "Game: six or more {x}, 19+"
      shows x>=6, suit_points>=19
      when  x is H | x is S
  # Partner's 1NT promised their suit stopped, so opener raises notrump
  # with any shape (2026-09-26: 17-20 counts passed 1NT, 35 corpus boards
  # with 25+ HCP and game on).
  cheapest(N) "16-17: invites 3NT"
      shows hcp=16..17
      when  !lho.last=X                    # over an overcall: partner holds their suit
      sets  ask=nt_invite
      priority -2
  jump(N) "Game: 18+"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows hcp>=18
      when  !lho.last=X                    # over an overcall: partner holds their suit
      priority -2
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# ── Partner redoubled ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redouble is 10+ and says we own the hand, so opener has nothing to
# prove: he repeats a six-card suit, shows a second suit with extras,
# and otherwise passes and leaves the next decision to partner, who has
# the values. BBA never doubles them here on these cards.
after 1x (X) XX (*)
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more"
      shows x>=6, suit_points<=18
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -1
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not S
      when  maybe lho.S<=4, maybe rho.S<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not H
      when  maybe lho.H<=4, maybe rho.H<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -2
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not D
      when  maybe lho.D<=4, maybe rho.D<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -2
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, suit_points<=18
      when  x is not C
      when  maybe lho.C<=4, maybe rho.C<=4
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -2
  P   "No further bid"  priority -5

# ── Partner passed and they kept bidding ─────────────────────────────
# Partner has nothing (0-5 over a double, or nothing to say over an
# overcall), so opener needs a real reason to bid again. BBA passes
# about two thirds of these.
# `maybe lho.hcp<=14` is "they have not shown a strong hand": after a
# 1NT overcall they own the balance of the pack, partner has nothing,
# and BBA passes every one of these. Without the guard opener kept
# rebidding his six-card suit over their Stayman and lost 157 calls in
# the five We_Overcall_NT_* scenarios.
# Opener is not forced here, so bidding again at all shows extras, and
# there is no need to jump (Rick, 2026-09-27): 1H (X) P (2H) 3H with
# 16, where a 16-18 jump to 4H was for when partner's forcing response
# obliges opener to bid. The free rebid is 13-18 suit points; tried
# (full corpus, par / side): up to 18 -35 / +746, 13-18 +191 / +119,
# 14-18 +529 / -1,504.
after 1x (*) P (*) when they.bid, maybe lho.hcp<=14, maybe rho.hcp<=14
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, extras"
      shows x>=6, suit_points=13..18
      priority -1
after 1x (*) P (*) when they.bid
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# ── They bought it and partner passed: opener reopens ────────────────
# `1x (1y) P (P)` and `1x (2y) P (P)` were 2,725 dead boards in the
# corpus. Partner may hold a trap pass or 5 points with no bid, so BBA
# reopens more often than it passes: a takeout double short in their
# suit, a second suit of five, a rebid of a six-card suit, or 2NT with
# 18-19 and a stopper.
after 1x (1y) P (P) | 1x (2y) P (P) | 1x (3y) P (P) when y is not x
  X   "Reopening double: short in {y}, support for the other suits"
      shows y<=2, hcp>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S | y is S), (H>=3 | x is H | y is H), (D>=3 | x is D | y is D), (C>=3 | x is C | y is C)) | hcp>=16
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades, 14+"
      shows S>=5, suit_points>=14
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts, 14+"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, suit_points>=14
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds, 14+"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, suit_points>=14
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, 14+"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, D<=4, suit_points>=14
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)

# ── Partner passed and they reopened: opener's notrump ───────────────
# 1D P P (1H) 1NT is the same bid as 1D (1H) P (P) 1NT above: 18-19
# balanced with their suit stopped (Rick, 2026-11-06, bridge-classroom-
# bug-artifacts #90; it had no rule). 15-17 would have opened 1NT and a
# balanced 12-14 passes. Only the notrump is here; the six-card rebid
# and the pass are `1x (*) P (*)` above.
after 1x (P) P (1y) | 1x (P) P (2y) when y is not x
  cheapest(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)
# Partner's two of a suit over it is 0-5 and six cards, to play: opener
# has shown his hand and passes (the generic sign-off answer would
# invite with 16-18, which 18-19 opposite 0-5 never is).
after 1x (P) P (1y) 1N (P) 2z (P) when y is not x, z is not y
  P   "Partner's sign-off: pass"
      priority 1

# ── They overcalled partner's response at the two level ──────────────
# 1D P 1H (2S): BBA's style (Rick 2026-11-07, bridge-classroom-bug-
# artifacts #93: "we can follow BBA's lead"; probes/opnt-*.toml on
# 21GF-GIB). A minimum balanced opener passes, or makes a support double
# where the card has one. 2NT is 17-18 balanced with their suit stopped,
# not forcing, and 3NT 19-21 (in practice 18 and 19: 15-17 opened 1NT).
# Where the double is not a support double (their call above the card's
# `through`, two of partner's major when unset: 1H (2S)), opener's
# double shows values: 15-18 balanced, at most three of partner's major
# and of their suit; BBA doubles there with 15+ and three of partner's
# major, 17+ with two, and bids 2NT with four of their suit (#93's
# K6.AK4.Q985.AQ82 doubles). Responder's answers: responder-rebids.bid.
after 1x (P) 1z (2y) when y is not x, y is not z, z is not x
  X   "Values: 15-18 balanced, at most three {z} and three {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp=15..18, z<=3, y<=3
      shows z=3 | hcp>=17
      when  z is H | z is S
      when  !support_x | (support_through is none, rho.last > 2{z}) | (support_through is not none, rho.last > support_through)
      sets  ask=values(z, x, y)
      priority 1
  2N  "17-18 with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp=17..18, z<=3, longest<=6       # BBA: unbalanced too
      when  stop(y)
  3N  "19-21 with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp=19..21, z<=3, longest<=6
      when  stop(y)
# Responder's cue bid over the values double: 10+, nothing in their
# suit. Notrump with it held, else the major with three, else four of
# the minor.
when asked values_cue(M, x, y)
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                   shows stop(y)
      priority 1                       # what the cue bid asked
  4M  "Three or more {M}, no stopper in {y}"   shows M>=3
      sets  trump=M
  4x  "No stopper, two {M}"                priority -2
      when  x is C | x is D

# Responder's cue bid over the double after 1C P 1D (overcall): 10+, no
# stopper, and not four of my major (he would have bid it up to 11).
when asked minor_x_cue(M, y)
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                   shows stop(y)
      priority 1
  cheapest(M) "No stopper in {y}"
      sets  forcing=game

# ── They overcalled partner's 1D response to 1C: the double ──────────
# 1C P 1D (1S) X: three or four hearts, 14-18 balanced; over a two-
# level overcall (2H, 2S) 15-18; over 1H three spades (with four opener
# bids 1S, below). BBA, 21GF-GIB (Rick 2026-11-07:
# "yes" to playing it; probes/opnt-1C-1D-1S.toml, -1H, -2H, -2S; 26 to
# 46 doubles per 160 hands, from 14 at the one level, 15 at the two).
# 17-18 doubles with or without a stopper, as BBA (Rick 2026-11-07: "yes
# to 1 and 2"), and bids on over a weak answer (below).
# No card field speaks to this double. Responder: responder-rebids.bid.
after 1C (P) 1D (1y) | 1C (P) 1D (2y) when y is H | y is S
  X   "Three or four hearts, 14-18 balanced"
      shows balanced, H=3..4, D<=3, hcp=14..18
      shows H=4 | hcp>=15                    # BBA: 1NT with 14 and three
      when  rho.last=1S
      sets  ask=minor_x(H, C, S)
      priority 1
  X   "Three or four hearts, 15-18 balanced"
      shows balanced, H=3..4, D<=3, hcp=15..18
      shows H=4 | hcp>=17                    # BBA mostly passes 15-16 with three
      when  rho.last=2S
      sets  ask=minor_x(H, C, S)
      priority 1
  X   "Three spades, 14-18 balanced"
      shows balanced, S=3, D<=3, hcp=14..18
      when  rho.last=1H
      sets  ask=minor_x(S, C, H)
      priority 1
  X   "Three or four spades, 15-18 balanced"
      shows balanced, S=3..4, D<=3, hcp=15..18
      when  rho.last=2H
      sets  ask=minor_x(S, C, H)
      priority 1
  # Unbalanced too (Rick 2026-11-07, "4: yes"; BBA "15 to 21 total
  # points", probes/opnj-1C-1D-1S.toml, -2H.toml: 13 and 34 of 120 strong
  # hands, all 17-18 HCP with four of the major and five clubs; 19+
  # reverses): 15-18 HCP, three or four of the major, longer clubs.
  X   "Three or four hearts, 15-18, longer clubs"
      shows !balanced, H=3..4, D<=3, C>H, C<=5, hcp=15..18
      when  rho.last=1S
      sets  ask=minor_x(H, C, S)
      priority 1
  X   "Three or four spades, 15-18, longer clubs"
      shows !balanced, S=3..4, D<=3, C>S, C<=5, hcp=15..18
      when  rho.last=2H
      sets  ask=minor_x(S, C, H)
      priority 1
# Opener's third call after the double and responder's weak answer
# (back to clubs, five diamonds, four of the major; all `ask=signoff`):
# 14-16 passes, 17-18 bids on (Rick 2026-11-07: "yes to 1 and 2"). BBA
# (probes/opnt-o-1C-1D-*.toml, 18 HCP): mostly the cue bid of their
# suit, "17+, raise or better" in clubs; 3NT with three of the major
# and their suit held. Ours, more natural: game in the major with four
# opposite four; with their suit held 2NT inviting over 2C / 2D (0-9),
# 3NT over the major (to 11, BBA's 3NT) or a three-level answer; else the
# cue bid, forcing.
after 1C (P) 1D (1y) X (P) * (P) | 1C (P) 1D (2y) X (P) * (P) when y is H | y is S, asked signoff
  4S  "Game: four spades opposite four, 17-18"   shows S>=4, hcp>=17
      when  y is H, partner.last=1S | partner.last=2S
      priority 2
  4H  "Game: four hearts opposite four, 17-18"   shows H>=4, hcp>=17
      when  y is S, partner.last=2H | partner.last=3H
      priority 2
  2N  "17-18 with a stopper in {y}: invites"     shows hcp>=17, stop(y)
      when  partner.last=2C | partner.last=2D
      sets  ask=nt_invite
      priority 1
  3N  "17-18 with a stopper in {y}"              shows hcp>=17, stop(y)
      when  partner.last!=2C, partner.last!=2D
      priority 1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 17-18, no stopper in {y}, forcing"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=17
      sets  forcing=round, ask=x_cue(y)
      priority 1
  # 14-16 bids on with a fit or a stopper (Rick 2026-11-07, "3: yes";
  # BBA, the same grids): three diamonds and four hearts over the club
  # answer (2D, or 3D over 3C), the raise of the major with four (invites: responder's
  # answer was up to 11), 1NT / 2NT over the major with three of it and
  # their suit held. Otherwise pass.
  cheapest(D) "14-16, four hearts and three diamonds: competes"   shows hcp<=16, D=3, H=4
      when  y is S, partner.last=2C | partner.last=3C   # BBA: with three hearts it passes
  cheapest(D) "14-16, four spades and three diamonds: competes"   shows hcp<=16, D=3, S=4
      when  y is H, partner.last=2C | partner.last=3C
      sets  ask=signoff
  3H  "14-16, four hearts opposite four: invites"     shows hcp<=16, H>=4
      when  y is S, partner.last=2H
      sets  trump=H, ask=invite(H)
  1N  "14-16 with a stopper in {y}"                   shows hcp<=16, stop(y)
      when  partner.last=1S
      sets  ask=signoff
  2N  "14-16, three hearts, a stopper in {y}: invites"   shows hcp<=16, stop(y), H=3
      when  y is S, partner.last=2H
      sets  ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
# ── Strong new suits over their overcall of the response ─────────────
# Rick 2026-11-07, "5: yes". BBA (probes/opnj-*.toml, 120 hands each,
# 17-21 unbalanced with a new suit): a reverse into a major at the two
# level with 19+ (1C P 1D (2H) 2S, 1C P 1D (1S) 2H, 1D P 1S (2C) 2H:
# "19 to 21 total points", the minor five or longer); diamonds over
# clubs at the three level with 18+ (1C P 1H (1S) 3D, a jump; 1C P 1S
# (2H) 3D, 1C P 1H (2S) 3D); clubs over diamonds with a jump over a
# one-level overcall, 18+ (1D P 1H (1S) 3C). Forcing to game.
after 1m (P) 1z (1y) | 1m (P) 1z (2y) when y is not m, z is not m, z is not y
  2H  "Reverse: four or more hearts, longer {m}, 19+, forcing to game"
      shows H>=4, m>H, !balanced, hcp>=19 | (points>=19, m>=6 | H>=5)   # balanced: notrump; 17-18 with 5-4: the double
      when  z is D, y is not H
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(H, m, y, z)
      priority 1
  2H  "Reverse: four or more hearts, longer {m}, 19+, forcing to game"
      shows H>=4, m>H, S<=2, !balanced, hcp>=19 | (points>=19, m>=6 | H>=5)
      when  z is S, y is not H
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(H, m, y, z)
      priority 1
  2S  "Reverse: four or more spades, longer {m}, 19+, forcing to game"
      shows S>=4, m>S, !balanced, hcp>=19 | (points>=19, m>=6 | S>=5)
      when  z is D, y is not S, cheapest_rank(S)>=13   # 1S is natural (1C P 1D (1H), below)
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(S, m, y, z)
      priority 1
  2S  "Reverse: four or more spades, longer {m}, 19+, forcing to game"
      shows S>=4, m>S, H<=2, !balanced, hcp>=19 | (points>=19, m>=6 | S>=5)
      when  z is H, y is not S
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(S, m, y, z)
      priority 1
  3D  "Strong: four or more diamonds, longer clubs, 18+, forcing to game"
      shows D>=4, C>D, points>=18, z<=2, !balanced, !stop(y)   # support first; notrump with a stopper (BBA)
      when  m is C, z is not D, y is not D
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(D, m, y, z)
      priority 1
  3C  "Strong: four or more clubs, 18+, forcing to game"
      shows C>=4, D>=C, points>=18, z<=2, !balanced, !stop(y)
      when  m is D, z is not C, y is not C, rho.last<=1S
      sets  forcing=game, ask=rev(C, m, y, z)
      priority 1
# Opener after responder's answer to the strong new suit (game forced):
# game in the fit responder raised, 3NT with their suit held, else game
# in the minor (BBA, probes/opns-r-1C-1D-2H-2S.toml and relatives).
when answered rev(w, m, y, z), partner.last!=3N, partner.last!=4H, partner.last!=4S, partner.last!=5C, partner.last!=5D
  # Slam: the keycard ask in the agreed suit with 30 between us on
  # partner's floor (Rick 2026-11-07: "5: yes"; BBA asks after the raise
  # and the minor try). Without it, game. Responder's 4m is forcing
  # (Rick: "for our default, let's make it forcing").
  4N  "Keycard ask in {w}"
      when  rkcb, w is H | w is S, we.trump is w, partner.last=3{w}
      shows tp(w) + partner.hcp.min >= 29     # support points: shortness counts in the fit
      sets  ask=keycards(w)
      artificial
      priority 3
  4N  "Keycard ask in {m}"
      when  rkcb, we.trump is m, partner.last=4{m}
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 30
      sets  ask=keycards(m)
      artificial
      priority 3
  4{w} "Game in {w}"                        shows w>=4
      when  w is H | w is S, we.trump is w
      priority 2
  5{w} "Game in {w}"
      when  w is C | w is D, we.trump is w
      priority 2
  3N  "A stopper in {y}: 3NT"               shows stop(y)
      when  we.trump is none | we.trump is m | we.trump is z
      priority 1
  4{z} "Three {z}: game in the fit"         shows z>=3
      when  z is H | z is S, partner.last=3{z}
      priority 1
  5{m} "Game in {m}: a minimum for slam"
      when  partner.last=3{m} | partner.last=4{m}
  5{m} "No stopper: game in {m}"
      priority -3
# Opener after responder's answer to his uncontested jump shift: as
# after the strong new suit in competition (above), without a suit of
# theirs to stop.
when answered js(w, m, z), partner.last!=3N, partner.last!=4H, partner.last!=4S, partner.last!=5C, partner.last!=5D
  4N  "Keycard ask in {w}"
      when  rkcb, w is H | w is S, we.trump is w, partner.last=3{w}
      shows tp(w) + partner.hcp.min >= 29     # support points: shortness counts in the fit
      sets  ask=keycards(w)
      artificial
      priority 3
  4N  "Keycard ask in {m}"
      when  rkcb, we.trump is m, partner.last=4{m}
      shows points + partner.hcp.min >= 30
      sets  ask=keycards(m)
      artificial
      priority 3
  4{w} "Game in {w}"
      when  w is H | w is S, we.trump is w
      priority 2
  5{w} "Game in {w}"
      when  w is C | w is D, we.trump is w
      priority 2
  4{z} "Three {z}: game in the fit"         shows z>=3
      when  z is H | z is S, partner.last=3{z} | partner.last=2{z}
      priority 2
  3N  "No fit for {z}: 3NT"
      when  we.trump is none | we.trump is m | we.trump is z
      priority 1
  5{m} "Game in {m}: a minimum for slam"
      when  partner.last=3{m} | partner.last=4{m}
      priority 1
  5{m} "Game in {m}"
      priority -3

# 1D P 1H (1S) 2C: five-five in the minors, 13-17 (Rick 2026-11-07, "6:
# yes"; BBA "13 to 17 total points", 7 of 120 strong hands and 9 of 160
# others, probes/opns-1D-1H-1S.toml, opnj-1D-1H-1S.toml). Not forcing.
# Over a two-level overcall of 1D P 1M, BBA's 3C is natural and wide,
# "13 to 19", four or more clubs (probes/opnj-1D-1H-2S.toml,
# opnj-1D-1S-2H.toml).
after 1D (P) 1z (1y) | 1D (P) 1z (2y) when y is not D, z is not D, z is not y, z is H | z is S, y is not C
  2C  "Five or more clubs and diamonds, 13-17"
      shows C>=5, D>=5, points=13..17, z<=2       # three of partner's major: support first
      when  rho.last=1S
      priority 1
  3C  "Four or more clubs, five or more diamonds, 13-19"
      shows C>=4, D>=C, D>=5, points=13..19, z<=2
      when  rho.last>=2H
      priority 1
# They competed over the 3C and partner raised to 4C (compare
# 2026-11-07, GIB_1N5422 13: no rule): the decision was partner's.
after 1D (P) 1z (2y) 3C (*) 4C (*) when z is H | z is S, y is not z, y is not C, y is not D
  P   "Partner competed: no more"
      priority -5
# Responder's invitational 3D over the five-five 2C (10-11, three
# diamonds): game with 15+.
after 1D (P) 1H (1S) 2C (P) 3D (P)
  5D  "Accepts: 15+"                       shows points>=15
  P   "Declines"
      priority -5
# ── 1C P 1D (1H): opener's natural spades ────────────────────────────
# BBA (Rick 2026-11-07: "yes to 1 and 2"; probes/opns-1C-1D-1H.toml,
# 160 hands): 1S with four spades, 11-15 total points, before 1NT and
# the double (which then shows three); the jump to 2S with four spades
# and 15+ (five clubs) or 18 balanced, forcing one round (BBA's
# responder passes it only with a misfit and 6-9). Responder:
# responder-rebids.bid.
after 1C (P) 1D (1H)
  1S  "Four spades, 11-15"
      shows S=4, points<=15
      priority 1                             # four spades: 1S before 1NT, as BBA
  2S  "Jump: four spades, 16+, forcing"
      shows S=4, points>=16
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1                             # ahead of 2NT and 3NT, as BBA
# Responder's cue bid over 1S or 2S: game values, no heart stopper.
# Notrump with one, else a fifth club, else three diamonds, else spades.
when asked ns_cue(y)
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                   shows stop(y)
      priority 1
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, no stopper in {y}"   shows C>=5
  cheapest(D) "Three diamonds, no stopper in {y}"      shows D>=3
      priority -1
  cheapest(S) "No stopper in {y}"
      priority -2
# Responder's minimum preference over the forcing 2S: game only with
# the top of the jump and their suit held.
after 1C (P) 1D (1H) 2S (P) 3C (P)
  3N  "18+ with a heart stopper"           shows points>=18, stop(H)
  P   "No game opposite a minimum"
      priority -5

# Responder bid five of his major over 2NT: choose the game.
after 1x (P) 1z (2y) 2N (P) 3z (P) | 1x (P) 1z (1y) 2N (P) 3z (P) when y is not x, y is not z, z is not x, z is H | z is S
  4{z} "Three-card support"                shows z>=3
      sets  trump=z
  3N  "Two {z}: notrump"                   shows z<=2
# They competed over opener's strong notrump and partner doubled: opener
# has described his hand and leaves the decision with partner (compare
# 2026-11-07: six no-rule positions such as 1C P 1H 2S 2N 3S X 4S).
after 1x (P) 1z (2y) 2N (*) X (*) | 1x (P) 1z (1y) 2N (*) X (*) | 1x (P) P (1y) 1N (*) X (*) | 1x (P) P (2y) 2N (*) X (*) when y is not x
  P   "Described: partner's double decides"   priority -10

# Opener answering responder's 2NT invitation with a six-card major
# (2026-09-27, ticket b220: 1S 2C 2H 2NT, AQ6542.JT65.97.K passed): the
# sixth card plays better than notrump opposite partner's doubleton.
# Three declines, four accepts; BBA bids 3S and responder raises.
when asked nt_invite, !partner.opened
  3S  "Six or more spades: not a maximum"   shows S>=6, strength<=invite
      priority 1
  4S  "Six or more spades: accepts"         shows S>=6, strength>=game
      priority 1
  3H  "Six or more hearts: not a maximum"   shows H>=6, S<=3, strength<=invite
      priority 1
  4H  "Six or more hearts: accepts"         shows H>=6, S<=3, strength>=game
      priority 1
