## Responder's second call once they have come in (2026-09-23)

Written alongside the contested opener rebids (`rebids.notes.md`),
because opener's new calls need an answer and because responder's own
second call was the next dead turn in every one of those auctions.

Opener's contested rebids set `ask=signoff` or `ask=invite(suit)`
wherever they are limited, and the state blocks in `rebids.bid` answer
those whatever the auction was. Four things set no ask, and each has a
block here:

- **opener's answer to our negative double** (`1x (*) X (*) 1z/2z/3z`,
  and a separate one for his notrump answer). The double showed 6+ and
  four cards in each unbid major, so responder is usually done: BBA
  passes 16 of the 24 positions in the Basic-Bridge scenarios with 6-10.
  We pass to 10, raise his suit with four and 11-12, bid the game with
  13, and put notrump below the fit (`priority -1`) because opener's
  answer may be a three-card major — `partner.z>=3`, not `>=4`, is what
  lets the raise fire at all.
- **opener's rebids after our redouble**, and the auctions where he
  passes them back: responder doubles with four of their suit, goes back
  to opener's suit with three, or bids his own five-card major. BBA bids
  2x/3x on these with 10-11 and never doubles; we keep the penalty
  double, because the redouble said we own the hand and somebody has to
  be able to collect.
- **opener's reopening double** (`1x (2y) P (P) X`): responder takes it
  out in his longest suit, passes it with four of theirs, or returns to
  opener's suit. From 2026-10-02 four poor ones (not two of the top
  three or three of the top five) need 8 HCP to pass: with 7 or fewer,
  43 of 58 one-level passes let them make it; doubling errors +317
  vanilla, +217 corpus, +282 21GF (penalty-doubles.notes.md, "Doubling
  more").
- **opener's second suit over their call** (`1x (*) 1y (*) 1z/2z`), the
  mirror of the uncontested blocks above. Our own rules make a contested
  reverse forcing, and 58 corpus broken forces were responder with no
  answer to one.

Two blocks are pass-by-rule rather than pass-by-accident: when both
partners have passed and they have stopped (`1x (*) P (*) P (P)`, which
BBA passes 6 of 6 with 3-9), and when they bid over our negative double
and opener passed it out — there responder needs 11+ to bid again.

## Notrump rebids after a 2/1: 2NT 12-14 or 18+, 3NT 15-17 (Rick, 2026-11-06)

bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #91 (board 29, NT Ladder, Rick South):
1♦-2♣-2♥ and North, 12 HCP, jumped to 3NT, read as "Game, no fit:
13-15". Rick: "In a 2/1 auction responder's jump to 3NT shows 15-17.
2NT here shows 12-14 or 18-19." So in a game-forcing 2/1, after any
two-level rebid by opener (his suit again, a new suit, a reverse; 2NT
is always available there), responder without a fit bids:

- **2NT: 12-14 or 18+**, forcing. Opener may not pass. He counts slam
  on the minimum (rebids.bid: 6NT, quantitative 4NT, otherwise 3NT).
  Over opener's 3NT the strong branch invites with a quantitative 4NT
  (18-20) and bids 6NT with 21+. The minimum passes. Four cards in
  opener's second suit, when it is a major, raise it instead.
- **3NT: 15-17**, the jump. Opener counts slam with over-3nt.bid (18
  opposite 15 bids a quantitative 4NT).

The ranges are now in HCP, as notrump ranges are. Since 2026-09-30
they had been notrump points, 3NT 13-15 and 2NT 16+ ("Fast arrival in
notrump" above). In HCP, over-3nt.bid's HCP count reads the 3NT. When
opener's rebid is 2NT or higher the scheme does not apply, and those
blocks are unchanged. A 2/1 that forces only one round (`!we.gf`) keeps
2NT as 11-12 invitational and 3NT as game.

Board 29 now goes 1♦-2♣-2♥-2NT-3NT: the same contract, read right.

**Source:** Rick's ruling. Robert Todd, "Using NT Rebids in 2/1
Auctions", Adventures in Bridge #425 (2022), gives no ranges for
responder but points the same way: responder's jump to 3NT "shows
extra values", and his 2NT does not promise them. The same article
gives opener's 2NT as 12-14 or 18-19 and his 3NT as 15-17, the scheme
Rick applies to responder. No book with responder's ranges is cited
yet (Hardy's and Lawrence's 2/1 books were not checked).

**Measured** with compare --limit 50, `--par-all` and errors_diff.py,
counting the bidding side's contract errors. Both issues' changes ran
together; the boards are split by the first differing call. Over all

- The 12-14 2NT lost 12 on 42 boards. That is after adding opener's

### Support points, not HCP (Rick, 2026-11-07)

Rick answered the question above: "support points. with 9 support
points a direct, constructive raise is correct." So:

- the weak three-card raise through 1NT is **5-7 support points** with
  the major as trump (`tp(M)<=7`; the 1NT's 6 HCP floor stays, so in
  practice 6-7), and the 1NT and the preference are read that way;
- the direct single raise with three trumps is **constructive, 8-10
  support points** (responses.bid already bid it so; its reading
  `tp(M)=6..10` with `tp(M)>=8` on the 2/1 cards is 8-10);
- Rick's board-14 hand Q72.97.AT8742.J2 (7 HCP, two doubletons: 9
  support points) raises 1♠-2♠ at once.

The 6-7 HCP reading had let hands with 8-9 support points into the
1NT, and over 1♥ the 1NT had won the tie with 2♥ on such hands
(descriptiveness). Now they raise, as Rick rules. When a hand with 8+
support points has bid 1NT anyway (Rick's own 1NT on board 14), a
fallback "Preference: three {M}" (priority -3) still takes the major;
partner reads the main rule.

The narrower 1NT also became more descriptive than the 2/1 2♣ over
1♥ with 12 HCP and a long minor and won that tie (descriptiveness),
undoing last round's flip the other way: -53 IMPs on 28 boards in the
tripwire. The 1NT on the 2/1 cards now also says `hcp<=11 |
points<=12`: a 12-count with a long suit has 13 points and bids its

## Counting against opener's shown range: the weak notrump (Rick, 2026-11-07)

With a weak notrump in force opener's 1NT rebid is a good 14 to 17 (rebids.notes.md,
"With a weak notrump"), so the counts after it are written against his
shown HCP minimum instead of as fixed numbers, for a three-point range:
`nt_rebid_signoff` (my points plus his minimum at most 22),
`nt_rebid_invite` (23-24), `nt_rebid_game` (25 or more). Counting on
his maximum as well was tried first: it changed a Precision board
(Weak_NT_11-16 30, where 1♦ caps the 1NT rebid below 14) in the
tripwire, so the counts read the minimum only. Opposite 12-14 they are
the old 10 / 11-12 / 13; opposite the weak-notrump card's 1NT, read as a
good 14 to 17, 8 / 9-10 / 11. They serve the natural block
after 1NT, two-way NMF / XYZ and NMF (NMF's continuations count on his
minimum, which the 2♥/2♠/2NT answers leave unchanged). The contested 1NT
(`1x (1z) 1y P 1N`, `1x P 1y (1z) 1N`) and the 1NT answer to a negative
double keep their fixed numbers and have weak-notrump blocks of their
own (opener's range 14+ to 17 or more), since their stock ranges (13-16,
10-14) are not 12-14. After 1♦–2♣–2NT with a weak notrump (12-14 or 18+)
responder counts slam on the minimum, as opener does over responder's
2NT (#91): 6NT with 33, a quantitative 4NT with 31.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responses to a one-level suit opening, uncontested: Standard American
# (SAYC), as BBA's Basic-Bridge card plays it. Ranges come from BBA's own
# meanings (bba-cli --all-meanings) and the Basic_* corpus; see
# responses.notes.md.
#
# Which suit to bid first at the one level: the longest; with two four-card
# suits the cheaper (up the line); with two five-card suits the higher.

module responses "Responses to one-level suit openings"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  partnership_bidding/basic_bidding
  skill  partnership_bidding/basic_major
  skill  bidding_conventions/walsh
  skill  bidding_conventions/forcing_1nt
  skill  bidding_conventions/semi_forcing_1nt
  param  limit_raise = major_openings.jump_raise.inv default true
  param  bergen      = bidding_conventions/bergen_raises default false
  param  rbergen     = bidding_conventions/bergen_raises:reverse default false
  param  strong_js   = bidding_conventions/strong_jump_shifts:two_level default true
  param  inv_js      = bidding_conventions/strong_jump_shifts:invitational default false
  param  weak_js3    = bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts:three_level default false
  param  soloway     = bidding_conventions/soloway default false
  param  over_1c     = minor_openings.one_club_responses default up_the_line
  param  nt2         = minor_openings.two_nt_response default invitational
  param  style       = general.style
  param  system      = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (limit raises)
  param  inverted    = bidding_conventions/inverted_minors default false
  param  drury       = bidding_conventions/drury default false
  param  drury_rev   = bidding_conventions/drury:reverse default false
  param  gf21        = bidding_conventions/two_over_one default false
  param  f1n         = major_openings.one_nt_response.forcing default false
  param  twalsh      = bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh default false
  param  semi        = major_openings.one_nt_response.semi_forcing default false   # opener's pass: rebids.bid

# The invitational 1M-3M, unless Bergen raises (majors/bergen.bid) take
# the jump to 3M for a preemptive raise: a three-card limit raise then
# goes through 2M, as on a card without the limit raise.
define inv_jump_raise = limit_raise, !bergen, !rbergen

# ── Over 1♣ / 1♦ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1C (P) when over_1c is up_the_line, !twalsh   # Transfer Walsh: transfer-walsh.bid
  1D  "4+ diamonds, 6+ HCP"         shows D>=4, hcp>=6, D>=H, D>H | D=4, D>=S, D>S | D=4
      sets forcing=round
  1H  "4+ hearts, 6+ HCP"           shows H>=4, hcp>=6, H>=D, H>D | H>=5, H>=S, H>S | H=4
      sets forcing=round
  1S  "4+ spades, 6+ HCP"           shows S>=4, hcp>=6, S>=D, S>D | S>=5, S>H | S>=5, S>=H
      sets forcing=round

# Walsh: with a four-card major, bypass diamonds unless game forcing (12+ HCP).
after 1C (P) when over_1c is walsh, !twalsh
  1D  "Walsh: 4+ diamonds, no 4-card major unless 12+ HCP"
      shows D>=4, hcp>=6, (H<=3, S<=3) | hcp>=12, D>=H, D>=S
      sets forcing=round
  1H  "4+ hearts, 6+ HCP"           shows H>=4, hcp>=6, H>=S, H>S | H=4, hcp<=11 | H>D
      sets forcing=round
  1S  "4+ spades, 6+ HCP"           shows S>=4, hcp>=6, S>H | S>=5, S>=H, hcp<=11 | S>D
      sets forcing=round

after 1C (P)
  1N  "6-10 HCP, balanced, no 4-card major or diamonds"   shows hcp=6..10, H<=3, S<=3, D<=3
      when  !inverted | C<=4           # with inverted minors five clubs raise, weak or strong
  2D  "Strong jump shift: 15+, 5+ diamonds"  shows D>=5, hcp>=15  when strong_js, !wjs_on, !soloway, !passed_hand
      sets forcing=game

after 1D (P)
  1H  "4+ hearts, 6+ HCP"           shows H>=4, hcp>=6, H>=S, H>S | H=4
      when  hcp<=10 | H>=C | (gf21, hcp<=11 | points<=12)   # 11+ HCP with longer clubs: 2C first (a 2/1 card: only with game values)
      sets forcing=round
  1S  "4+ spades, 6+ HCP"           shows S>=4, hcp>=6, S>H | S>=5, S>=H
      when  hcp<=10 | S>=C | (gf21, hcp<=11 | points<=12)
      sets forcing=round
  1N  "6-10 HCP, no 4-card major"          shows hcp=6..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  !inverted | D<=4           # with inverted minors five diamonds raise
  2C  "11+ points, 4+ clubs"           shows C>=4, points>=11 | C>=6, suit_points>=10, H<=3 | C>H, S<=3 | C>S
      when  !gf21
      sets forcing=round
  2C  "Two over one, game forcing: 4+ clubs"           shows C>=4, (style is not bba, hcp>=12, points>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13), H<=3 | C>H, S<=3 | C>S
      when  gf21, !passed_hand
      sets forcing=game
  3C  "Invitational jump shift: 10-12 points, 6+ clubs"  shows C>=6, points=10..12, H<=3, S<=3  when inv_js, !weak_js3

after 1m (P)
  2m  "Raise: 6-9, 5+ {m}, no 4-card major"     shows m>=5, hcp>=6, points<=9, H<=3, S<=3
      when  !inverted
  3m  "Limit raise: 10-12 HCP, 5+ {m}, no 4-card major"  shows m>=5, hcp=10..12, H<=3, S<=3
      when  !inverted                  # HCP: six clubs and 10-12 passed on 10-12 total points
  # With inverted minors the raises are in inverted-minors.bid.
  # Game values, a fit and no major, without inverted minors: 3NT, as BBA
  # (probes/minor-resp-std-1C.toml). A fallback below the natural calls.
  3N  "Game values, no 4-card major"            shows hcp>=13, H<=3, S<=3
      when  !inverted
      priority -1
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12, balanced, no 4-card major"        shows balanced, points=11..12, H<=3, S<=3
      when  nt2 is invitational
      priority -1                      # a one-level suit first when there is one
  3N  "13-15, balanced, no 4-card major"        shows balanced, points=13..15, H<=3, S<=3
      when  nt2 is invitational
      priority -1
  2N  "13-15, balanced, no 4-card major: game forcing"  shows balanced, points=13..15, H<=3, S<=3
      when  nt2 is game_forcing
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -1
  3N  "16-17, balanced, no 4-card major"        shows balanced, points=16..17, H<=3, S<=3
      when  nt2 is game_forcing
      priority -1
  2H  "Strong jump shift: 15+, 5+ hearts"       shows H>=5, hcp>=15  when strong_js, !wjs_on, !soloway, !passed_hand, !rf_2h_on
      sets forcing=game
  2S  "Strong jump shift: 15+, 5+ spades"       shows S>=5, hcp>=15  when strong_js, !wjs_on, !soloway, !passed_hand, !rf_2s_on
      sets forcing=game

# 2/1 cards: 2C over 1D is game forcing (13+), so 11-12 with clubs and
# no major bids the invitational 2NT, as BBA (probe 2026-09-30:
# 72.K84.K73.AQ952 bids 2NT). Same priority as the balanced 2NT: partner
# reads them together.
after 1D (P) when gf21, nt2 is invitational
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12, 4+ clubs, no 4-card major"   shows points=11..12, C>=4, H<=3, S<=3, D<=3
      priority -1
#
# 11-12 and unbalanced with four diamonds and a longer club suit (no
# major, too weak for a 2/1 2C, too long in diamonds for the 2NT above)
# had no call without inverted minors (the conv-ab off run, 2026-10-07):
# 1D promises four or more but for 4-4-3-2, so the limit raise.
after 1D (P) when !inverted
  3D  "Limit raise: 10-12 HCP, four diamonds, no 4-card major"  shows D=4, hcp=10..12, H<=3, S<=3, !balanced
      priority -2
after 1D (P) when gf21
  3C  "Invitational jump shift: 10-12 points, 6+ clubs"   shows C>=6, hcp>=10, hcp<=11 | points<=12, H<=3, S<=3
      when  !weak_js3                  # with weak jump shifts 3C is weak (weak-jump-shifts.bid)
      priority -1

# With 2NT game forcing, 11-12 balanced bids a new minor first (2NT next).
after 1D (P) when nt2 is game_forcing
  2C  "11-12, balanced, no 4-card major"   shows balanced, points=11..12, C>=3, H<=3, S<=3
      sets forcing=round
      priority -1
after 1C (P) when nt2 is game_forcing, !twalsh
  1D  "11-12, balanced, no 4-card major"   shows balanced, points=11..12, D>=3, H<=3, S<=3
      sets forcing=round
      priority -1

# ── Over 1♥ / 1♠ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1H (P)
  1S  "4+ spades, 6+ HCP"           shows S>=4, hcp>=6
      when  H<=2 | (style is not bba, (H=3, tp(H)>=11) | tp(H)>=13 | !inv_jump_raise) | (style is bba, H=3, hcp>=11 | S>=6 | (hcp>=10, S>=5 | shortest<=2)), hcp<=10 | (S>=C, S>=D) | (hcp<=12, C<=5, D<=5) | (gf21, hcp<=11 | points<=12)
      # 6-10 with 3+ hearts: raise; 11-12 with 4+: limit raise; 11+ with a longer minor: 2m first
      # (bba: with three hearts 1S from 11 HCP, or 10 with five spades or a doubleton; never with four hearts)
      sets forcing=round
  1N  "6-10 HCP, no heart fit, no 4 spades"   shows hcp=6..10, H<=2, S<=3
      when  !gf21
  # 2/1 cards: a weak three-card raise (5-7 support points) may bid
  # 1NT; a 12-count with 13 points bids its 2/1 (Rick, 2026-11-07, #87;
  # responder-rebids.notes.md).
  1N  "Forcing 1NT: 6-12 HCP, no heart fit or a weak three-card raise, no 4 spades"   shows hcp=6..12, H<=2 | (H=3, tp(H)<=7, !passed_hand, style is not bba, system is not brill), S<=3, hcp<=11 | points<=12
      when  gf21, f1n
      sets forcing=round
  1N  "6-12 HCP, no heart fit or a weak three-card raise, no 4 spades"   shows hcp=6..12, H<=2 | (system is brill, H=3, tp(H)>=10) | (H=3, tp(H)<=7, !passed_hand, style is not bba, system is not brill), S<=3, hcp<=11 | points<=12
      when  gf21, !f1n, !semi             # brill: a three-card limit raise starts here (3H below)
  1N  "Semi-forcing 1NT: 6-12 HCP, no heart fit or a weak three-card raise, no 4 spades"   shows hcp=6..12, H<=2 | (H=3, tp(H)<=7, !passed_hand, style is not bba, system is not brill), S<=3, hcp<=11 | points<=12
      when  gf21, !f1n, semi
  2S  "Strong jump shift: 15+, 5+ spades"  shows S>=5, hcp>=15  when strong_js, !wjs_on, !soloway, !passed_hand
      sets forcing=game
  2C  "11+ points, 4+ clubs"           shows C>=4, points>=11 | C>=6 | (H>=3, tp(H)>=11), suit_points>=10, C>=D, S<=3 | (C>S, hcp>=13 | C>=6)
      when  !gf21
      when  !passed_hand | (!drury, !drury_rev)   # Drury (drury.bid) takes a passed hand's 2♣
      when  H<=2 | (style is not bba, H=3 | tp(H)>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13 | (hcp>=12, shortest<=2) | (hcp>=11, H>=4))   # limit values and a fit: raise first
      sets forcing=round               # with 4 spades and no longer minor: 1S first
  2C  "Two over one, game forcing: 4+ clubs"           shows C>=4, (style is not bba, hcp>=12, points>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13), C>=D, S<=3 | (C>S, hcp>=13 | C>=6)
      when  gf21, !passed_hand
      when  !passed_hand | (!drury, !drury_rev)   # Drury (drury.bid) takes a passed hand's 2♣
      when  H<=2 | (style is not bba, H=3 | tp(H)>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13 | (hcp>=12, shortest<=2) | (hcp>=11, H>=4))   # limit values and a fit: raise first
      sets forcing=game               # with 4 spades and no longer minor: 1S first
  2D  "11+ points, 4+ diamonds"        shows D>=4, points>=11 | D>=6 | (H>=3, tp(H)>=11), suit_points>=10, D>C, S<=3 | (D>S, hcp>=13 | D>=6)
      when  !gf21
      when  H<=2 | (style is not bba, H=3 | tp(H)>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13 | (hcp>=12, shortest<=2) | (hcp>=11, H>=4))
      sets forcing=round
  2D  "Two over one, game forcing: 4+ diamonds"        shows D>=4, (style is not bba, hcp>=12, points>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13), D>C, S<=3 | (D>S, hcp>=13 | D>=6)
      when  gf21, !passed_hand
      when  H<=2 | (style is not bba, H=3 | tp(H)>=13) | (style is bba, hcp>=13 | (hcp>=12, shortest<=2) | (hcp>=11, H>=4))
      sets forcing=game
  3H  "Limit raise: 11-12 support points, 3+ hearts"  shows H>=3, tp(H)=11..12 | (H>=4, tp(H)=10, shortest<=2), hcp<=12
      when  !passed_hand | (!drury, !drury_rev)
      when inv_jump_raise, H>=4 | S<=3, style is not bba, system is not brill
      priority -1                      # 3 hearts: a new suit, then a jump raise, when there is one
      sets trump=H
  # brill (the Brill card): the limit raise promises four trumps; with
  # three, 1NT and then 3H (responder-rebids.bid). Brill /explain,
  # 2026-10-15, "Nat, Inv, 10-12": `hcp >= 9 and hcp< 12 and H >= 4`.

# responses (`responses.bid`): notes

Responses to a one-level suit opening, uncontested. Standard American as BBA's
Basic-Bridge card plays it; the Basic_* scenarios use that card. Cases:
`responses.test` (one corpus hand per response, all agreeing with BBA).

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **Treatments**, one card field each:
  - `minor_openings.one_club_responses`: `up_the_line` (default, as BBA:
    1♦ with four diamonds and a four-card major) or `walsh` (bypass
    diamonds for a four-card major unless game forcing, 12+).
  - `minor_openings.two_nt_response`: `invitational` (default, as BBA:
    1m-2NT 11-12, 1m-3NT 13-15) or `game_forcing` (1m-2NT 13-15, 1m-3NT
    16-17; with 11-12 bid a new minor, then 2NT).
- **Strong jump shift: 15+**, matching BBA for now.
- **Two-level new suit: as BBA**, 11+, or a six-card suit with 10.
- **Game values with a fit and no four-card side suit: a three-card minor
  first**, as BBA (4M only when there is no three-card minor).
- BBA's own "Walsh style" switch stays on the card as
  `minor_openings.walsh.play`, but the rules read `one_club_responses`:
  with the switch on, BBA still bids up the line.

## How the rules were set

BBA was asked for its meaning of every call: the Basic_* deals re-bid through
`bba-cli --all-meanings` (auctions identical to the corpus, 4000 of 4000).
Its meanings for responder's first call, with the hands that made them:

| Call | BBA's meaning | Hands in the corpus |
|---|---|---|
| New suit at the one level | 6+ total points, 4+ cards | 3-19 HCP, median 9 |
| 1NT | 6-11, no support (over 1♥: no 4 spades) | 6-10 HCP |
| 2M | "7 to 9 total points", 3+ | 6-12 HCP |
| 3M | "1M-3M inviting", 10-12, 3+ | 9-12 HCP |
| 4M | "preemptive", 4-8, 4+ | 4-11 HCP |
| Two-level new suit | "10+ HCP if fit or 6+; 12+ F" | 8-20 HCP, median 12 |
| Jump to 2 of a higher suit | 15+, 5+ cards | 14-22 HCP |
| Jump to 3 of a lower suit | "Inviting jump shifts", 10-12, 6+ | 10-12 HCP |
| 1♣-2♣, 1♦-2♦ | 6-10, 5+, no four-card major | |
| 1♣-3♣, 1♦-3♦ | 9-13, 5+ | |
| 2NT | 11-13, balanced (rare: BBA bids a new suit) | |
| Pass | 0-5 | |

**Raises count support points.** BBA's choice between 2M, 3M and a new suit
(the way to game) follows HCP plus shortness plus a fourth trump. At 9 HCP,
for example, it bids 2M with a flat three-card fit, but 3M with a doubleton
or four trumps. We use `tp(M)`: HCP plus void 5, singleton 3, doubleton 1,
and with only three trumps void 3, singleton 2, doubleton 1. Bands: 2M 6-9,
3M 10-12, and game (a new suit, 3NT, or 4M) 13+. With a fit and limit
values responder raises before bidding a new suit.

**Rick's raise structure over 1M (2026-09-23)**, replacing the bands above:

- 6-10 support points and 3+ trumps: raise to 2M, ahead of any new suit
  (not 1♠ then a heart preference, not 1♠ then notrump).
- 11-12 with four trumps: 3M at once.
- 11-12 with three trumps: a new suit, then a jump raise
  (1♥-1♠-1NT-3♥, 1♥-1♠-2♣-3♥). Read "then jump to 2H" in his message as
  the jump raise to 3M; **to confirm**.
- Where three trumps and 11-12 leave no new suit to bid (over 1♠: 3♠-4♥
  with 3-3 minors; or 11 support points from shortness with a suit too
  weak for the two level), 3M stays as a fallback (`priority -1`). Without
  it 445 hands passed 1♠ (−2,404 IMPs).
- A 2-level new suit counts support points: with three trumps and 11+
  support points it is allowed below 11 notrump points (`932.854.62.AKQJ2`).

Measured against the previous bands, whole corpus: calls agreeing 75.6%
unchanged, same contract 30.5%, −116 IMPs vs par (of −196,305). Basic_*
uncontested NS: roughly flat. The costs are what the ruling asks for:
10-point raises to 2♠ where BBA bids 3♠ (1,120 boards, −223), and the new
suit before a three-card limit raise (about −500 over 1♥ and 1♠). Taken
as Rick's ruling. Follow-up: after 1M-2M, opener with 23+ now blasts
4NT because the raise can hold 10 (130 boards, −140); that belongs to a
slam try, not keycard.

Which suit to bid first at the one level: the longest; with two four-card
suits the cheaper, up the line (1♦ over 1♣ with four diamonds and a
four-card major: BBA always does, 76 of 76); with two five-card suits the
higher. Over 1♥ a weak hand with three hearts raises rather than bid 1♠.
With 11+ and a longer minor, 2m comes before a four-card major.

## Total points count length (2026-09-23)

`points` now adds 1 for each card beyond four (Rick: "total points should
include length points"). Each band here was re-chosen for the measure that
fits its decision, and measured against par (net IMPs vs BBA; less negative
is better). Baseline after the engine change, before these rules moved:
corpus −182,498, Basic_* −2,153, Basic_* uncontested NS −1,030.

- **1NT response: 6-10 HCP** (was total points). A five-card minor is not a
  reason to leave 1NT: `K3.Q84.KJ852.J62` bids 1♠-1NT. With total points,
  10 HCP and a five-card suit could not bid 1NT at all.
- **1♦-1M "11+ with longer clubs: 2♣ first"** and **1♥-1♠ "11+ with a
  longer minor: 2m first"**: the threshold is HCP. With 10 HCP and 5-4 the
  major comes first (previously some such hands passed 1♦).
- **Walsh 1♣-1♦ "game forcing"**: 12+ HCP (Rick's "12+"). With total
  points 11 HCP and 5-4 (`KQ2.JT63.KQ742.8`) became game forcing and bid
  1♦ over the major. Not in the corpus (no card plays Walsh), so unmeasured.
- **Kept on total points**: the two-level new suit (11+) and the
  invitational jump shift (10-12). Moving the two-level new suit to HCP
  cost 930 IMPs over the corpus on its own; moving the jump shift to HCP
  cost 701 (11-12 HCP six-card suits are worth forcing, and 9-10 HCP ones
  inviting, which total points gets right on both sides). So four `.test`
  cases now differ from BBA, taken on par: `A8.94.532.AK8632` 1♦-2♣ (BBA
  3♣), `AK85.8.QT9862.K3` 1♥-2♦ (BBA 3♦), `T.AKT542.87.A953` 1♠-2♥ (BBA
  3♥), `.KT9763.AQ98.432` 1♠-3♥ (BBA 2♥).

| Variant | corpus | Basic_* | Basic_* NS |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (all bands on total points) | −182,498 | −2,153 | −1,030 |
| jump shifts on HCP | −183,199 | −2,204 | −1,081 |
| two-level new suit on HCP | −183,428 | −2,224 | −1,087 |
| 1NT and two-level on HCP, 1♦-1M guard on HCP | −181,766 | −2,138 | −1,014 |
| 1NT on HCP | −182,051 | −2,097 | −983 |
| 1NT and 1♦-1M guard on HCP | −181,903 | −2,073 | −959 |
| **+ 1♥-1♠ guard on HCP (kept)** | **−181,873** | **−2,066** | **−952** |

Question for Rick: with 10 HCP and a five-card suit both 1NT (6-10 HCP) and
a two-level new suit (11+ total) are allowed; 1NT wins over 1M, but over 1♦
`K843.Q3.J6.KJ852` bids 2♣ rather than 1♠. Should a two-level new suit
need 11 HCP when a one-level major or 1NT is available? Moving the whole
two-level band to HCP measured worse (−930), so it stays on total points
until you rule.

## Evidence

Basic_* responses (2,069 positions after `1x P`): 89.3% agree with BBA.
Before this module we passed every one. Whole corpus: calls agreeing 66.4%
→ 68.5%, same contract 11.7% → 14.9%.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- Where exactly 2M becomes 3M: BBA makes a limit raise with some 10
  support points; we raise to 2M (Rick: 6-10).
- BBA's preemptive 4M with 8-10 HCP, four trumps and a singleton (it counts
  these as game hands); we make a limit raise.
- Some 6-counts BBA passes (for example `65.K8654.KT43.86`).

## Gaps (not built yet)

- **Opener's rebid**: the largest gap in the whole corpus now (1♣-1♦,
  1♦-1♥, 1♦-1♠ each pass on thousands of boards).
- Responses by a passed hand beyond switching off jump shifts. Drury is
  its own module (`majors/drury.bid`, 2026-09-28): with it on, a passed
  hand's limit raise, natural 2♣ and game-values 2♣/2♦ are switched off
  here.
- Responses after interference.
- 2/1 game force and forcing 1NT: built 2026-09-30 (below).

## Questions

- 2026-09-23: two-level new suit on 10 HCP and a five-card suit when a
  one-level major is available (see "Total points count length").

## BBA treatment (2026-09-24)

The default is Rick's raise structure (above) and stays. `general.style =
bba` now plays a probed model of BBA's responses to 1M; it replaces the
first `bba` treatment, which was the pre-ruling structure tuned for
agreement and never probed (BBA raised to 2♥ with 10 on Basic_Major 45 and
65, which that model bid 1♠).

**Probes** (`rbb probe`, Basic-Bridge both sides, dealer S, None, MP;
responder North after `1S Pass` or `1H Pass`; honours placed as A♣, K♥,
Q♦, K♠, ... so each row adds one honour; no tens):

| Shape (♠-♥-♦-♣) over 1♠ | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-3-3-4 (3 trumps, flat) | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ |
| 3-4-2-4 (doubleton Qx) | Pass | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 2♣ |
| 3-4-1-5 | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 2♣ |
| 4-3-3-3 | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 2♣ |
| 4-3-2-4 | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 2♣ |
| 4-4-1-4 | 2♠ | 2♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 2♣ |
| 5-3-3-2 | 2♠ | 2♠ | 2♠ | 3♠ | 3♠ | 2♦ | |
| 5-3-4-1 | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 2♦ | |
| 5-4-4-0 (from 4) | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 4♠ | 2♦ | |

Over 1♥ the same shapes give the same answers (3-4-1-5: 4♥ from 7 with
the five-card club suit). With three hearts and four spades: 2♥ up to 9-10,
3♥ on 10 with a doubleton, 1♠ from 11 (from 10 with five spades); with
four hearts BBA never bids 1♠, and with 12 it bids a three-card minor.

- **Tens count for nothing** in a raise: `432.K32.QJ2.AT32` and the same
  hand with three tens both bid 2♠; 8-counts with one to three tens all 2♠.
- **Honour placement matters** and is not modelled: a queen or jack in
  trumps upgrades (`J432.K32.Q2.A432` 10 → 4♠, `Q432.K32.Q2.A432` 11 →
  2♣, but `K432.Q32.Q2.A432` 11 → 3♠); an ace in a short side suit
  upgrades (`K972.86.A65.K874` 4♠, `K972.86.K65.A874` 3♠); an honour in
  the doubleton does not count as shortness (`432.K432.Q2.A432` 9 → 2♠,
  where the corpus hands with a small doubleton and 9 bid 3♠).
- BBA's 4♠ is labelled "preemptive, 4 to 8 total points" by
  `--all-meanings`, but it is bid on 8-10 HCP with four trumps and a
  singleton: a hand worth game that is short of the HCP to force.

**Corpus** (Basic_*, raises with 3+ trumps, 10-12 HCP): with four trumps
and 11 HCP BBA bids a new suit (5 of 5 over 1♠, 7 of 12 over 1♥), not the
limit raise the probes gave for honour-light hands; with three trumps and
11 it is half and half (7 new suit, 7 3♠).

**The model** (`responses.bid`, rules under `when style is bba`):

- 2M: three trumps and 6-10 HCP flat, or 6-8 with a doubleton or
  shorter; four trumps and 5-8 HCP (without the shortness that makes 4M).
- 3M: three trumps and 11-12 flat, or 9-11 with a doubleton or shorter;
  four trumps and 9-10 (not the 4M hands below).
- 4M: four trumps and a singleton or void with at most 10 HCP (`tp(M) +
  M >= 15`: 8 HCP with four trumps, 7 with five); or 9-10 with a doubleton
  and four controls or a five-card suit.
- A new suit, forcing: 11 HCP with four trumps, 12 with three and a
  doubleton or shorter, else 13 (the three-card minor as before). Over
  1♥ with three hearts and four spades: 1♠ from 11, from 10 with five
  spades or a doubleton, and with six spades; 3♥ below that.
- 1♠-2♥ on 10 HCP and five hearts (probes: 10 HCP five hearts bids 2♥
  over 1♠ whatever the shape; a minor needs 11, `2.KJ2.K5432.K432` 1NT).
- The default's preemptive 4M (5+ trumps, 5-9) is off under `bba`.

**Measured** (`--set general.style=bba`; before = the old `bba`
treatment, after = this one plus the rebid treatments in rebids.bid and
responder-rebids.bid):

| corpus, before | 75.7% | 16.0% | 31.2% | −185,676 |
| corpus, after | 75.8% | 16.8% | 31.8% | −187,508 |
| Basic_*, before | 84.1% | 37.3% | 46.8% | −2,298 |
| Basic_*, after | 84.6% | 40.4% | 48.6% | −2,193 |
| Basic_* NS, before | 90.5% | 52.6% | 61.6% | −1,243 |
| Basic_* NS, after | 91.2% | 57.1% | 64.4% | −1,162 |

Responder's first call on Basic_* uncontested NS: after 1♠ 462 → 496 of
538 agree (85.9% → 92.2%), after 1♥ 334 → 356 of 396 (84.3% → 89.9%).
The divergences named for this work: 1♠-2♠/3♠ 14 → 2, 1♠-4♠/3♠ 11 → 1,
1♥-2♥/1♠ 8 → 0, 1♥-4♥/3♥ 7 → 2, 1♠-2♥/1NT 5 → 0. The default is
unchanged: every one of the 170,161 corpus boards bids the same with and

**Where BBA still differs under `bba`** (each a handful of boards):
three trumps and 9 with an honour doubleton (`AJT94.K62.863.J6`, Basic_Major

**Where our default differs and why**: Rick's ruling of 2026-09-23 (2M

BBA's 3♠ with a flat 9 and four trumps, and its 4♠ on 8-10 with a

## Strong jump shifts count HCP (2026-09-25)

The strong jump shifts said `points>=15`. Total points count half a
point a ten and a point a card beyond four, so 12 HCP with four tens and
five spades jumped (AJT74.JT4.QT.AT5 over 1H). BBA
(`probes/sjs-1H.toml`, 800 hands with 5+ spades over 1H, Basic-Bridge):

| HCP | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jump to 2S | never | ~1% | ~25% | ~94% |

The rules now say `hcp>=15`. Corpus: par -167,558 -> -167,342 (+216 IMPs);
the 1H P 1S / 2S divergence alone cost 453 IMPs over 261 boards.

## The fourth trump with shortness makes a limit raise (2026-09-25)

Corpus, Basic-Bridge, 1S P: BBA's 3S against our 2S cost 276 IMPs (184
boards); our 3S against BBA's 2S won 435 (138). By responder's hand:

| Trumps | HCP | Shortness | Boards | BBA's call | Ours | IMPs to us |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 9 | doubleton | 59 | 3S | 2S | -179 |
| 3 | 9 | doubleton | 99 | 3S | 2S | -98 |
| 3 | 8 | singleton | 106 | 2S | 3S | +316 |
| 4 | 8 | singleton | 25 | 2S | 3S | +115 |

So our shortness count is right, and a fourth trump is worth a point
when there is shortness to ruff. With four trumps, 10 support points and
a doubleton or shorter, we now make the limit raise.
- Corpus: -167,342 -> -167,152.
- Flat 10s still raise to 2M (Rick: 2M is 6-10; the corpus agrees, +4
  over 11 boards).
- The same for three trumps with a doubleton lost 636 IMPs overall: not
  adopted.

## Invitational jump shifts: BBA's 10-12 HCP loses to ours (2026-09-25)

BBA's invitational jump shift over 1S (Basic-Bridge, `probes/ijs-1S.toml`,
800 hands with a six-card minor and no spade fit) is 10-12 HCP. With
7-9 it bids 1NT; with 13+ it bids 2m. Ours counts total points (10-12,
so 8-10 HCP with six cards) and bids 2m with 11-12: 26% agreement.
- BBA's HCP range: 90% agreement but -483 IMPs against par.
- Widening ours to 10+ points and up to 12 HCP: -409.

Par decides: ours stays. Tests 24, 41, 48 and 52 are Rick's cases for it.

## Drury, tried (2026-09-25)

21GF-DEFAULT plays Reverse Drury and 21GF-GIB plays Drury; we play
neither. BBA's opener answers (`probes/drury-opener-*.toml`): minimum
2M/2D, 12-14 the other, and 2NT, 3NT, new suits, splinters or game
above that. A simple version was tried: 2C with three trumps and 10-12
support points; opener's minimum, 12-14 or game; responder signs off.
It lost to our passed-hand limit raise on both measures: -237 by
distance, -354 to the side (536 boards). Not adopted. A fuller version
(opener's strong answers, responder's game tries) would be needed to
beat it.

Built 2026-09-28 as `majors/drury.bid`, with opener's game answer and
responder's follow-ups and 2♣ from 10 support points: adopted
(drury.notes.md).

## Over 1H, 1S before a five-card minor with 11-12 (2026-09-25)

With four spades, a five-card minor and 11-12, BBA responds 1S; we bid
the minor at the two level. Now 1S, and 2m with four spades needs 13 or
a six-card minor (test 41 keeps 2D with six). +52 by distance, +71 to
the bidding side.

## 2/1 game force and the forcing 1NT (Rick, 2026-09-30: "definitely fix 2/1")

On cards with `major_openings.two_over_one.play` (the 21GF cards;
derived from the system type) the two-over-one is **game forcing**
(`sets forcing=game`) with opening values: 13+ total points with 12+ HCP
by default (length counts, Rick 2026-09-23), 13+ HCP under
`general.style = bba`. BBA (probe 2026-09-30, 21GF-DEFAULT, over 1S, 1H
and 1D): 2/1 from 13 HCP; 12 HCP with a five-card suit bids 1NT over a
major and the invitational 2NT over 1D. The 1NT response over a major is
6-12, forcing (`sets forcing=round`) when the card plays
`one_nt_response.forcing` (21GF-DEFAULT; not 21GF-GIB). Standard American
cards keep the 11+ one-round force.

Around it: over 1D, 11-12 with clubs bids 2NT and 10-12 with six clubs
3C (short of a game force); the "11+ with a longer minor: 2m first" gate
on the one-level majors lets 11-12 bid the major on 2/1 cards. Opener's
rebids over a forcing 1NT and responder's continuations: rebids.notes.md,
responder-rebids.notes.md.

Measured (IMPs vs BBA, par as the yardstick): random deals (20,000,
21GF) +96, corpus +115; calls agreeing with BBA 80.4% -> 80.6% random,
78.1% -> 78.3% corpus; "no rule in a live auction" 324 -> 316 random,
2,669 -> 2,605 corpus; broken forces unchanged. Measuring responder's new
11-12 minor raise in points instead of HCP scored +375 more on the corpus
but overrode impossible-2s.bid's tested choices, so it counts HCP.

Not measured yet: BBA's plain 13 HCP threshold as the default.

## A card without the limit raise: 2M takes 6-12 (2026-09-30)

On the vanilla SAYC random set (95,558 deals BBA bid with a bare SAYC
card) responder had no call after 1♠ on 355 boards and after 1♥ on 149.
The card's `.bbsa` (SAYC-bare: `System type = 1`, every toggle off)
says "1M-3M inviting = 0", "1M-3M blocking = 0", "Mixed raise = 0" and
"Bergen = 0", and the import reads that literally: no jump raise of any
kind, so the limit raise is off. BBA itself plays Bergen raises on that
card all the same (`.rbb-cache/random/README.md`). With the limit raise
off nothing else took 10-12 support points with a fit
(`983.AJT2.KT742.4` over 1♠: 2♠ stopped at 10, no 3♠, no new suit).
The same hole was open on every card without the limit raise: the
corpus cards Precision, Precision-14-16, 21GF-GIB-Bergen and
21GF-WJS-MSS (weak or mixed jump raises and Bergen, none of which the
rules play yet).

What BBA does on that card (its own auctions, `ref.py` on the vanilla
set): it never bids 1♠-3♠; with three trumps it raises to 2♠ up to
11-12 HCP (2♠ by HCP: 5:50 6:377 7:336 8:400 9:412 10:371 11:254 12:42)
and bids a new suit with 11-12 and shortness. Its four-trump limit raises
went to Bergen 3♦ and were filtered out of the set, so it says nothing
about four trumps.

The rules, when the card plays no limit raise (`!limit_raise`):

- **2M is 6-12 support points** (the default's 2M rule, widened in the
  same rule so partner reads one range; BBA style: 6-12 HCP). Three
  trumps with 11-12 and a four-card side suit still bid the new suit
  first (then 4M, responder-rebids.bid), as with the limit raise: on
  the vanilla set those boards scored +357 against BBA's 2♠ (2♣/2♦ then
  game, 326 boards). Four trumps and 10-12 raise to 2M too: no evidence
  either way (BBA's boards were filtered), and the opener's game try
  below catches the 12s.
- **Opener invites from 15** (rebids.bid): opposite a raise whose
  `partner.tp(M).max` is 11 or more, 3M is 15-18 (17-18 otherwise) and
  the pass up to 14. Measured on the vanilla set against the plain
  widened raise (−41,490; before the rebase onto 1199c40): invite
  15-18 −41,131; 16-18 with responder
  accepting from 10 −41,375; 15-18 accepting from 10 −41,357; 14-18
  −41,224. Responder keeps accepting from 9.
- Over 1♥ with four spades, a heart fit and 11-12 support points
  (`KJ43.K82.Q93.Q54`) the widened 2♥ now outranks 1♠ (by
  descriptiveness), where the 1♠ rule's `!limit_raise` clause had let
  1♠ in: +296 on 98 corpus boards on the no-limit-raise cards. Over 1♠
  the two-level new suit still comes first (`K92.A82.KQ93.854` 2♦).

**Rick, 2026-09-30:** vanilla SAYC plays the limit raise (the
comparison adds `--set major_openings.jump_raise.inv=true`); the rules
keep this fallback, because the engine must not leave a hole on any card
without the limit raise.

Measured (IMPs vs BBA, double-dummy par as the yardstick; on main
1199c40, with the 1♠-1NT-2m-2♥ rule of responder-rebids.bid, which is
all that moves on cards with the limit raise):

| set | before | after | change | no-rule boards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla SAYC with the limit raise (Rick's card) | −36,747 | −36,678 | +69 | 371 → 362 |
| vanilla SAYC as imported (no limit raise) | −37,952 | −36,806 | **+1,146** | 876 → 362 |
| corpus (342 scenarios) | −92,854 | −91,712 | **+1,142** | 1,694 → 1,442 |
| 21GF random, 100,000 boards | −43,589 | −43,518 | +71 | 835 → 827 |

Without the limit raise the fallback comes within 128 IMPs of playing
it (−36,806 against −36,678). Calls agreeing with BBA on the imported
card 82.5% → 82.4%, mostly the invitation from 15, where BBA passes. On the corpus the widened raise moved only
the four cards above; 21GF moved only by the 2♥ rule.

Not built: weak and mixed jump raises (`major_openings.jump_raise.weak`,
`.mixed`) and Bergen. A card that plays one of them without the limit
raise gets this widened 2M for the invitational hands.

## Brill (general.system = brill, 2026-10-15)

Brill's treatment, played on the Brill card only (`cards/json/Brill.json`, `general.system = brill`: a stand-in until convention-card's `general.style` takes a `brill` value; cards/README.md "Brill"). Rusty plays the Brill dailies as South with three Brill robots, so it should read and bid what they do. Every other card is unchanged (a `.test` line on 21GF-GIB beside each Brill line; `compare --limit 50` tripwire against main: no board changed).

The limit raise 1M-3M promises four trumps ("Nat, Inv, 10-12": `hcp >= 9
and hcp< 12 and S >= 4`); a three-card limit raise bids 1NT (Brill's 1NT:
`hcp <= 12 and S < 4 and hcp>= 6`) and then 3M (responder-rebids.bid,
"Limit raise: three-card support, 10-12"). Soloway (the card turns it on)
has 16+ HCP in every type under brill (Brill "Soloway": `hcp >= 16 and
(solid('H') or semisolid('H') or H >= 7) and singlesuited and controls >=
4`, `H >= 5 and D >= 4 and hcp> 17 and controls >= 4`, `H >= 6 and balish
and hcp>= 17 and controls >= 4`).

Brill labels the 1NT response "Forcing", and its opener bids a three-card
minor over it; `major_openings.one_nt_response.forcing = true` on the Brill
card measured slightly worse in the probe (bids 66.0% -> 65.8%: our forcing
1NT rebids read differently), so the card keeps 21GF-GIB's non-forcing 1NT.
Question for Rick.

Measured with `probes/tools/brill_probe.py report --card Brill` over the top 2000 corpus auctions (calls of this group, board-weighted, our reading against Brill's): 1M-3M 0% -> 100% of 2,678 boards; 1M-1NT stays 100% of 3,409; Soloway 92% ignoring the artificial flag, as before the card turned it on (0% without the 16+ floor).

## The weak three-card raise goes through 1NT on 2/1 cards (Rick, 2026-11-06)

bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #87: Rick bid 1♠-1NT-2♥-2♠ with
Q72.97.AT8742.J2 (7 HCP) and wants the preference read as "2S or 3S
with 5-7 support pts". On the 2/1 cards (`two_over_one.play`, where
the 1NT is 6-12, forcing, semi-forcing or not):

- The 1NT is now read as holding a three-card raise with 5-7 support
  points (6-7 HCP until Rick's 2026-11-07 ruling).
- Rusty's direct single raise with three trumps needs 8 support
  points (constructive), so a flat 6-7 bids 1NT. With four spades over
  1♥ there is no 1NT, so it still raises.
- Four trumps raise as before.
- A passed hand raises as before, since its 1NT is not forcing.
- The Brill card and `style=bba` keep their own raises.

The preference itself is in responder-rebids.bid (see its notes).

**Rick, 2026-11-07:** the band is support points: "support points.
with 9 support points a direct, constructive raise is correct." The
1NT now holds the three-card raise with `tp(M)<=7` (5-7 support
points; 6-7 in practice, the 1NT's floor is 6 HCP), and the single
raise is 8-10 support points. Hands with 8-9 support points that had
bid 1NT over 1♥ (the descriptiveness tie) now raise. The 1NT also
says `hcp<=11 | points<=12`, so a 12-count with a long suit bids its
2/1 rather than winning that tie for 1NT. Measured in
responder-rebids.notes.md ("Support points, not HCP").

**Measured:** see responder-rebids.notes.md, the #87 section.

files.rules/base/soloway.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Soloway jump shifts: the continuations. The jumps themselves are in
# responses.bid (`soloway_js`). GIB's system notes: opener rebids his
# suit with length, raises responder with three or more, bids a side suit
# without support to show at least KQ there, or bids notrump at the
# cheapest level with any other hand. Responder then rebids his suit
# (types 1 and 2), bids notrump (type 3) or raises opener (type 4). The
# auction is game forcing; keycard and control bids follow from the
# agreed suit (slam/). See soloway.notes.md.

module soloway "Soloway jump shifts"
  kind   convention
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/soloway
  param  soloway = bidding_conventions/soloway default false

# ── Opener's rebid ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1x (P) 2y (P) when soloway, !wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  3y  "Support for {y}: three with an honour, or four"   shows y>=4 | (y=3, quality(y)>=fair)
      sets  trump=y
      priority 1                                # support first
  3x  "Rebids {x}: five or more, no support"    shows x>=5, y<=3, quality(y)<=poor | y<=2
  cheapest(z)  "No support, a side suit with two of the top three honours"
      shows z>=4, quality(z)>=good, y<=3, quality(y)<=poor | y<=2
      when  z is not x, z is not y
      prefer 0 - cheapest_rank(z)
  2N  "No support, no strong side suit"        shows y<=3, quality(y)<=poor | y<=2
      priority -1

# ── Responder's second call (no fit agreed yet) ───────────────────────
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) | 1x (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) when soloway, !wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  cheapest(x)  "Type 4: support for {x}"        shows x>=4
      sets  trump=x
      priority 1
  cheapest(y)  "Type 1 or 2: a long, strong {y}"  shows y>=6, top5(y)>=4
  3N  "Type 3: balanced, 18+"                   shows balanced
      priority -1
  cheapest(y)  "Rebids {y}"                     shows y>=6
      priority -2
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) | 1x (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) when soloway, !wjs_on, y is not x, z is not x, z is not y, two_level_jump(y, x)
  cheapest(x)  "Type 4: support for {x}"        shows x>=4
      sets  trump=x
      priority 1
  cheapest(y)  "Type 1 or 2: a long, strong {y}"  shows y>=6, top5(y)>=4
  3N  "Type 3: balanced, 18+"                   shows balanced
      priority -1
  cheapest(y)  "Rebids {y}"                     shows y>=6
      priority -2
files.rules/base/soloway.notes.md:
# soloway (`soloway.bid`): notes

Soloway jump shifts (`general.soloway.play`): responder's jump to
two of a higher suit over 1♣, 1♦ or 1♥ is game forcing and shows one of
GIB's four hand types. The jumps are in `responses.bid` (`soloway_js`);
the continuations here. Cases: `soloway.test`. Scenarios:
Soloway_Jump_Shift and Soloway_Jump_Shift_Type-1..4 (21GF-SPECIALS2).

## Structure

- Types (4+ controls each): (1) six cards with four of the top five, 17+
  total points, no side four-card suit; (2) a solid suit (AKQJ), 17+;
  (3) five cards with three of the top five, 18+ HCP, 5-3-3-2 or 6-3-2-2;
  (4) five cards with three of the top five, four-card support for
  opener, 17+ support points. Suit tests as in the scenario's own script.
- Opener: raises with four, or three with an honour (priority); rebids
  his suit with five or more; shows a side suit with two of the top three
  honours; else 2NT.
- Responder: raises opener's suit (type 4), rebids his suit (types 1-2),
  or bids 3NT (type 3). From there the agreed suit leads to slam/.
- On a card with Soloway, strong jump shifts are off; weak ones win if
  both are set (no PBS card does).

## Corpus (Soloway_Jump_Shift*, 2026-10-05)

Same final contract as BBA on 38 of the first 250 boards (50 a
scenario) before (strong jump shifts), 76 after. With the jumps but
without the continuations calls agreed 73.1% (all 2,500 boards), with
them 78.3% (NS 48.1% to 58.4%). Remaining divergences at the jump, all
**BBA style**, not changed (GIB's definition is the spec):

- BBA never jumps 1♣-2♦ with 17 HCP (all 2♦ jumps have 18+), where GIB's
  "17+ total points" does.
- BBA does not jump with a balanced hand and a five-card major (type 3):
  1♦-1♥, then NMF/Roudi.
- BBA does not jump with a side four-card suit even with a solid suit
  (type 2), nor with a five-six two-suiter.
- With four clubs over 1♣ BBA raises (inverted 2♣) instead of type 4.
- Opener: BBA rebids a five-card minor (we do too; GIB says six) and
  raises three cards only with an honour (we follow BBA).

## Gaps

- After opener's 3♣ rebid and responder's 4♣, opener's keycard 4NT and a
  5♦ answer leave no sign-off below 5♦; we pass 5♦ (about 30 boards in
  these scenarios; a slam/ issue, rkcb-1430.bid).
- Soloway extended (`soloway_extended`) not built.

## Sources

- **GIB system notes, "Soloway Jump Shifts"**
  (https://www.bridgebase.com/doc/gib_system_notes.php#Soloway_Jump_Shift):
  the four types and both players' rebids. convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/soloway.toml` cites the same page.
- **BBA evidence:** the Soloway_Jump_Shift* corpus (2,500 boards): the
  BBA-style differences above; opener's raise needs an honour with three.

files.rules/base/strong-openings.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The strong openings above 1NT (Rick, 2026-09-23).
#
# Balanced hands have a ladder, and every rung is a place to stop:
#
#   2NT            20-21        2♣ then 3NT    24-25
#   2♣ then 2NT    22-23        3NT            26-27
#                               2♣ then 4NT    28+
#
# Unbalanced hands open 2♣ on **23 total points**, or on playing strength:
# within one trick of game, which is nine tricks with a major and ten with
# a minor, since game there is eleven. Playing tricks are counted as
# 13 - losers, and the hand needs a six-card suit or 5-5 to be counted
# that way at all (strong-openings.notes.md has BBA's own 2♣ hands).
#
# Responder: 2♦ waits, a suit at the cheapest level is a positive with a
# real suit, and after opener describes, the cheapest minor is the second
# negative — a bust, less than a jack and a queen.

module strong-openings "2♣ and 2NT openings"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/strong_2c
  skill  partnership_bidding/two_club
  param  two_c      = two_level.two_clubs.meaning default strong
  param  two_d_resp = two_level.two_clubs.2d_response default waiting
  param  bust_2h    = bidding_conventions/two_heart_bust default false
  param  kokish     = bidding_conventions/kokish default false   # 2♣–2♦–2♥ is the relay (openings/kokish.bid)
  # Off: no strong 2C, and strong hands open at the one level (base.bid
  # lifts its 21 HCP cap). A card whose forcing opening is 1C (Precision)
  # keeps 2C as the stand-in until a forcing 1C is built: without it the
  # strong hands open one of a suit and are passed out.
  param  forcing_2c = general.forcing_opening_2c default true
  param  forcing_1c = general.forcing_opening_1c default false
  param  two_nt_min = notrump.two_nt.range_min default 20
  param  two_nt_max = notrump.two_nt.range_max default 21
  param  three_nt_min = notrump.three_nt.range_min default 26
  param  three_nt_max = notrump.three_nt.range_max default 27
  param  gambling   = bidding_conventions/gambling_3nt default false
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  benjamin   = bidding_conventions/benjamin_2d default false
  # French 2♦ (openings/french-2d.bid) takes every 24+ hand: 2♣ stops at 23.
  param  french     = bidding_conventions/french_2d default false
  param  style      = general.style
  param  system     = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (3NT)

when opening
  2N  "{two_nt_min}-{two_nt_max} HCP, balanced"
      shows hcp=two_nt_min..two_nt_max, balanced
  3N  "{three_nt_min}-{three_nt_max} HCP, balanced"
      shows hcp=three_nt_min..three_nt_max, balanced
      shows S<=4 | system is not brill, H<=4 | system is not brill
      when  !gambling, !french
  # brill (the Brill card: 3NT 25-27): no five-card major in the 3NT
  # opening, which then opens 2C (below). Brill /explain, 2026-10-15,
  # "Balanced hand, 25-27 HCP": `(balanced or semibalanced) and hcp>= 25
  # and hcp<= 27 and H<= 4 and S <= 4`.
  # Three ways in, written apart because one condition for all of them
  # cannot be read. Any of them is a 2♣ opening.
  2C  "Strong 2♣: 22+ HCP"    alert
      shows hcp>=22, !balanced | (system is not brill, hcp<=25) | (system is brill, hcp<=24 | S>=5 | H>=5) | hcp>=28 | gambling   # balanced 26-27 opens 3NT, unless 3NT is Gambling (brill: 25-27 without a five-card major)
      when  two_c is strong | two_c is very_strong, forcing_2c | forcing_1c, !benjamin   # Benjamin: openings/benjamin.bid
      shows !french | hcp<=23
      sets  forcing=game, ask=strong_2c
      artificial
      priority 1                       # ahead of a one-level opening
  2C  "Strong 2♣: nine tricks with a major"  alert
      shows hcp>=17, losers<=4, hcp+length_points>=23
      shows (H>=6, quality(H)>=good) | (S>=6, quality(S)>=good) | (H>=5, S>=5)
      when  two_c is strong | two_c is very_strong, forcing_2c | forcing_1c, !benjamin   # Benjamin: openings/benjamin.bid
      shows !french | hcp<=23
      sets  forcing=game, ask=strong_2c
      artificial
      priority 1
  2C  "Strong 2♣: ten tricks with a long suit"  alert
      shows hcp>=17, losers<=3, hcp+length_points>=23
      shows (C>=6, quality(C)>=good) | (D>=6, quality(D)>=good) | (H>=6, quality(H)>=good) | (S>=6, quality(S)>=good) | shape 5-5-x-x
      when  two_c is strong | two_c is very_strong, forcing_2c | forcing_1c, !benjamin   # Benjamin: openings/benjamin.bid
      shows !french | hcp<=23
      sets  forcing=game, ask=strong_2c
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 2C (P)
  2D  "Waiting"                        artificial
      when  two_d_resp is waiting | two_d_resp is negative
      priority -1
  2H  "Positive: five or more hearts, 8+"
      shows H>=5, hcp>=8
      when  !bust_2h, (H>=6, top5(H)>=3) | quality(H)>=good
  2S  "Positive: five or more spades, 8+"
      shows S>=5, hcp>=8
      when  (S>=6, top5(S)>=3) | quality(S)>=good
  3C  "Positive: five or more clubs, 8+"
      shows C>=5, hcp>=8
      when  (C>=6, top5(C)>=3) | quality(C)>=good
      priority -1                      # balanced hands bid 2NT
  3D  "Positive: five or more diamonds, 8+"
      shows D>=5, hcp>=8
      when  (D>=6, top5(D)>=3) | quality(D)>=good
      priority -1
  2N  "Positive: balanced, 8+"         shows balanced, hcp>=8
  2H  "Bust: fewer than 3 HCP"         shows hcp<=2
      when  bust_2h
      sets  forcing=none                # opener may stop below game
      artificial
      priority 1

# ── Opener describes after the waiting bid ───────────────────────────
after 2C (P) 2D (P)
  2N  "22-23 HCP, balanced"            shows hcp=22..23, balanced
  # With a Gambling 3NT the balanced 26-27 opens 2C too, and rebids 3NT
  # (before 2026-10-05 it had no opening at all and passed: Kokish_Relay,
  # 10 of 50 boards). BBA rebids 3NT with 26-27 there.
  3N  "24-25 HCP, balanced"   shows balanced, hcp>=24, hcp<=25 | (gambling, hcp<=27)
      when  !kokish
  # With Kokish the 24-25 goes through the relay (kokish.bid, 2♣–2♦–2♥–
  # 2♠–2NT), so 3NT is the next rung up: 26-27 (BBA, Kokish_Relay with
  # Gambling: 85 boards, 59 at 26 and 26 at 27; the relay's 2NT 93 at 25).
  # Without a Gambling 3NT the 26-27 opens 3NT and we never rebid this,
  # but partner's 3NT reads the same (2026-11-07).
  3N  "26-27 HCP, balanced"   shows balanced, hcp>=26, hcp<=27
      when  kokish
  4N  "28+ HCP, balanced"              shows hcp>=28, balanced
  2H  "5+ hearts"                      shows H>=5
  2S  "5+ spades"                      shows S>=5
  3C  "5+ clubs"                       shows C>=5
  3D  "5+ diamonds"                    shows D>=5

# ── Opener after their overcall and partner's pass (2026-10-05) ──────
# The balanced hands rebid notrump as on the ladder, with a stopper in
# their suit; systems are on over the 2NT (one-nt.bid, `systems on`).
# Only the balanced rebids are written here so far.
after 2C (2x) P (P) | 2C (3x) P (P)
  2N  "22-23 HCP, balanced, a stopper in {x}"    shows hcp=22..23, balanced, stop(x)
  3N  "24-25 HCP, balanced, a stopper in {x}"    shows hcp=24..25, balanced, stop(x)

# ── Opener after a positive response ─────────────────────────────────
# Partner has a real suit and 8+, so the only questions left are the fit
# and the strain. `y is not D | partner.D>=5` is what tells the 3♦
# positive from the 2♦ waiting bid, which has its own block above.
# Responder after a positive and opener's suit: raise with three or more,
# agreeing the suit for the slam modules (2026-09-25: we bid 3NT with
# support and missed the slams BBA bid, To_Finesse_Or_Not_To_Finesse).
after 2C (P) 2N (P) 3S (P) | 2C (P) 3C (P) 3S (P) | 2C (P) 3D (P) 3S (P)
  4S  "Support: three or more spades"   shows S>=3   sets trump=S, forcing=game
      priority 1
after 2C (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) | 2C (P) 3C (P) 3H (P) | 2C (P) 3D (P) 3H (P)
  4H  "Support: three or more hearts"   shows H>=3   sets trump=H, forcing=game
      priority 1
# Opener's minor after a major positive: four-card support raises below
# game and agrees it, leaving the keycard ask to opener (2026-11-07,
# bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #94: 2C-2H-3D with J942 opposite AKT65
# bid 3NT, where 6D and 7D make).
after 2C (P) 2y (P) 3m (P) when y is H | y is S, m is C | m is D, !bust_2h | y is S
  4m  "Support: four or more {m}"       shows m>=4   sets trump=m, forcing=game
      priority 1

# The raise is the 22+ hand (Rick, 2026-10-01): the balanced 22-24 that
# was going to rebid 2NT, or any 22+ with three trumps, even with a suit
# of its own (BBA raises on all of them: probes/slam-2C-2H-opener.toml).
# A lighter 2C, opened on playing tricks, has a long suit and shows it.
# So responder counts the raise as 22, not the 2C floor of 17.
after 2C (P) 2y (P) | 2C (P) 3y (P) when y is not D | partner.D>=5, y is not H | !bust_2h
  cheapest(y) "Raise: three or more {y}, 22+"  shows y>=3, hcp>=22   sets trump=y
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades"           shows S>=5   when y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts"           shows H>=5   when y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"         shows D>=5   when y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"            shows C>=5   when y is not C
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, no fit for {y}"      shows balanced, hcp>=22   # every balanced 2C is 22+
      priority -1

# ── Responder's rebid over opener's 2NT (2026-09-28) ─────────────────
# Opener is balanced, 22+, with exactly two cards in my major (three
# would have raised). We are forced to game and hold 30+ between us, so
# every call here is a step towards slam (NT_Ladder 426: 2C P 2S P 2NT
# P, where six spades opposite two bid 3NT and BBA reached 6S).
# BBA, probes/strong2c-2S-2N-resp.toml and strong2c-2H-2N-resp.toml:
# a six-card suit rebids, a four-card side suit is shown, 5-3-3-2 bids a
# quantitative 4NT with 8-9 and 6NT with 10+.
# That is BBA's treatment (`general.style = bba`). By default systems are
# on over this 2NT (Rick, 2026-10-05; one-nt.bid, `systems on`): the 2NT
# system of two-nt-responses.bid answers it, Stayman and transfers.
after 2C (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) when y is H | y is S, y is not H | !bust_2h, style is bba
  3y  "Six or more {y}"      shows y>=6   sets trump=y
      priority 2                             # the fit first, before a side suit
  3S  "Four or more spades"                    shows S>=4
      when  y is H
      priority 1                             # a major fit before a minor suit
  3H  "Four or more hearts"                    shows H>=4
      when  y is S
      priority 1
  3C  "Four or more clubs"                     shows C>=4
  3D  "Four or more diamonds"                  shows D>=4
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 30, hcp + partner.hcp.min <= 32
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam in notrump"            shows balanced, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
  3N  "To play"
      priority -1

# Opener with four cards in responder's second major agrees it and asks
# for keycards at once: 30+ between us and a fit (BBA asks on almost
# every hand after 2C P 2S P 2NT P 3S P, probes/strong2c-2S-2N-3S-opener.toml).
# Without 1430 or 0314 on the card, game in the fit.
after 2C (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) 3z (P) when y is H | y is S, z is H | z is S, z is not y, y is not H | !bust_2h, style is bba
  4N  "Keycard ask in {z}: four-card support"  shows z>=4
      when  rkcb
      sets  trump=z, ask=keycards(z)
      artificial
  4z  "Four-card support: game in {z}"          shows z>=4
      when  !rkcb
      sets  trump=z

# After the balanced positive, opener shows a suit or raises the notrump.
after 2C (P) 2N (P)
  3S  "Five or more spades"                   shows S>=5
  3H  "Five or more hearts"                   shows H>=5
  3D  "Five or more diamonds"                 shows D>=5
  3C  "Five or more clubs"                    shows C>=5
  3N  "Balanced 22, no suit to show"         shows balanced, hcp>=22   # 23+ bids 4NT or 6NT
      priority -1
  4N  "Quantitative: 23-24 balanced, invites 6NT"  shows balanced, hcp=23..24
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam in notrump"            shows hcp>=25, balanced

# ── Responder's second call: the second negative ─────────────────────
# Having waited, responder shows a bust by bidding the cheapest minor;
# anything else is a positive and the auction is already game forcing.
# With the 2♥ bust (`parrish_bust`) the bust was shown at once: 2♦ has
# 3+ HCP and there is no second negative.
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2H (P)
  3C  "Second negative: fewer than 3 HCP"  shows hcp<=2  when !bust_2h  artificial  priority 1
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2S (P)
  3C  "Second negative: fewer than 3 HCP"  shows hcp<=2  when !bust_2h  artificial  priority 1
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 3C (P)
  3D  "Second negative: fewer than 3 HCP"  shows hcp<=2  when !bust_2h  artificial  priority 1

# ── Responder's second call over opener's major (2026-11-07) ─────────
# Rick, bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #92: 2♣–2♦–2♥ (natural, Kokish
# off) had no responder rules but the second negative, so every other
# hand fell through to the base "Game in notrump" (3NT with six good
# spades, or with a heart fit too weak for slam-entry's raise). Standard
# practice: a five-card suit of my own is shown (2♠ over 2♥ at the two
# level, a minor at three, each denying a fit), a raise is slam-entry's
# or base.bid's game in the fit, and 2NT
# waits with no fit and nothing to show, leaving room below 3NT for
# opener's second suit or six-card major. With Kokish on, 2♥ is the
# relay (kokish.bid) and these are off.
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2y (P) when y is S | !kokish, y is H | y is S, !bust_2h
  2S  "Five or more spades"               shows S>=5, hcp>=3, quality(S)>=fair, H<=2
      when  y is H
      priority 1
  3D  "Five or more diamonds"             shows D>=5, hcp>=3, quality(D)>=fair, y<=2
  2N  "No fit, nothing to show: waiting"  shows y<=2, hcp>=3
      priority -1

# Opener after the waiting 2NT: a six-card major rebids, a second suit
# is shown, 3NT with a five-card major and nothing more to say. Natural
# and forcing (the 2♣ game force).
after 2C (P) 2D (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) when y is S | !kokish, y is H | y is S, !bust_2h
  3y  "Six or more {y}"                     shows y>=6
      priority 1
  3S  "Four or more spades"                 shows S>=4
      when  y is H
  3D  "Four or more diamonds"               shows D>=4
  3C  "Four or more clubs"                  shows C>=4
  3N  "Five {y}, nothing more to show"     shows y=5
      priority -1

# ── Opener's new suit over responder's transfer (2026-11-07) ─────────
# Rick, bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #94: 2♣–2♥(positive)–2NT, systems
# on (Rick, 2026-10-05), 3♦ transfer, and opener bid 4♦ instead of
# completing. Opener's 2NT denied three hearts, so it cannot be a
# super-accept: it is natural, five or more of the minor, slam interest
# (we are forced to game with 30+ between us). Before, nothing read it
# (base.bid's runout fallback), responder took it as an answer to the
# transfer and bid a quantitative 4NT, and the 5♣ that followed was
# passed. The completion stays opener's own call (priority 0): these are
# here so the 4m is read, and answered.
after 2C (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) 3D (P) | 2C (P) 2S (P) 2N (P) 3H (P) when style is not bba, !bust_2h
  4C  "Five or more clubs: slam interest, no fit"     shows C>=5
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -1
  4D  "Five or more diamonds: slam interest, no fit"  shows D>=5
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -1

# Responder: with three or more of opener's minor the fit is found, and
# with 30+ between us the keycard ask agrees it (0314 or 1430 as the
# card and rkcb-1430.bid say); without RKCB, slam in the fit. No fit:
# back to my major, which opener may pass or bid on over.
after 2C (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) 3x (P) 4m (P) when y is H | y is S, x is D | y is S, x is H | y is H, m is C | m is D, style is not bba, !bust_2h
  4N  "Keycard ask in {m}: three or more {m}"   shows m>=3
      when  rkcb
      sets  trump=m, ask=keycards(m)
      artificial
      priority 2
  6m  "Slam: three or more {m}"                 shows m>=3
      when  !rkcb
      sets  trump=m
      priority 2
  4y  "No fit for {m}: my {y}"                   shows m<=2
      priority 1

# ── The 2♥ bust (`two_level.parrish_bust.play`) ─────────────────
# 2♣–2♥ shows fewer than 3 HCP (2♦ is then waiting with 3+, game
# forcing). Opener describes naturally; a suit at the two level is
# forcing one round, 2NT (22-23) and a three-level suit may be passed.
# Hearts are bid at the three level (2♥ was artificial).
after 2C (P) 2H (P) when bust_2h
  2N  "22-23 HCP, balanced"            shows hcp=22..23, balanced
  3N  "24-25 HCP, balanced"            shows balanced, hcp>=24, hcp<=25 | (gambling, hcp<=27)
  4N  "28+ HCP, balanced"              shows hcp>=28, balanced
  2S  "5+ spades: forcing one round"   shows S>=5
      sets  forcing=round
  3H  "5+ hearts"                      shows H>=5
  3C  "5+ clubs"                       shows C>=5
  3D  "5+ diamonds"                    shows D>=5
after 2C (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) when bust_2h
  3S  "Three or more spades"           shows S>=3
      sets  trump=S
      priority 1
  2N  "No spade support"
after 2C (P) 2H (P) 3H (P) when bust_2h
  4H  "Raise to game: three or more hearts"   shows H>=3
      sets  trump=H
      priority 1
  P   "No support"
after 2C (P) 2H (P) 3C (P) | 2C (P) 2H (P) 3D (P) | 2C (P) 2H (P) 2N (P) when bust_2h
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 1
# Opener after the bust's 2NT (no spade support): game with it in hand.
after 2C (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) 2N (P) when bust_2h
  4S  "Game in hand: six or more spades"   shows S>=6, losers<=3
      priority 1
  3S  "Six or more spades: to play"        shows S>=6
  3H  "Five or more hearts too"            shows H>=5
  3D  "Four or more diamonds too"          shows D>=4
  3C  "Four or more clubs too"             shows C>=4
  P   "No further bid"
      priority -1
