# Strong openings (`strong-openings.bid`): notes

2♣, 2NT and 3NT, and what follows them. Cases: `strong-openings.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-23)

**Balanced hands go up a ladder, and every rung is a place to stop:**

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2NT | 20-21 | 2♣ then 3NT | 24-25 |
| 2♣ then 2NT | 22-23 | 3NT | 26-27 |
| | | 2♣ then 4NT | 28+ |

So the 22+ HCP branch of 2♣ steps around the two notrump openings: a
balanced 26-27 opens 3NT, not 2♣.

**Unbalanced hands** open 2♣ on 23 total points (HCP plus one for each
card beyond four), or on playing strength — within one trick of game,
which is nine tricks with a major and ten with a minor, since game there
is eleven. Playing tricks are counted as 13 − losers.

**Responder**: 2♦ waits. A suit is a positive, 8+ with a real suit — five
cards with two of the top three honours, or six with three of the top
five. 2NT is the balanced positive. After opener describes, the cheapest
minor is the **second negative**: a bust, less than a jack and a queen.

French 2♦ (`two_level.french_2d.play`, openings/french-2d.bid) caps
every 2♣ opening at 23 and takes the 3NT opening's 26-27 as well.

Card fields: `two_level.two_clubs.2d_response` (waiting/negative/steps),
`parrish_bust` for the treatment where 2♥ shows the bust and 2♦ is game
forcing, `notrump.two_nt.range_min/max`, `notrump.three_nt.range_min/max`.

## Evidence, and one open question

BBA opened 2♣ eighteen times across the Basic_* scenarios, on 17-21 HCP
with big shape — `2.AQJ872.AKQJ83.`, `A2.AQJT7542.A.A3`,
`KQT43.AKQ32..AKT`. Its stated meaning is "19 to 37 total points". Every
one of the eighteen has a six-card suit or 5-5.

Rick's rule reads as two **alternative** triggers: 23 total points **or**
within a trick of game. Implemented that way it opens 2♣ on 17 of BBA's
18, but also on 14 of the 67 strong one-level hands BBA opens at the one
level, and it measures worse — the false positives cost more than the
true ones gain:

| unbalanced trigger | calls | auctions | contracts | IMPs vs par |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| playing strength alone | 84.2% | 39.3% | 50.3% | -8,542 |
| and 20 total points | 84.4% | 40.2% | 51.6% | -8,225 |
| and 21 | 84.7% | 40.9% | 52.7% | -7,821 |
| and 22 | 84.7% | 41.1% | 53.2% | -7,636 |
| **and 23** | **85.1%** | **41.3%** | **53.5%** | **-7,574** |

So the rules currently require **both**: 23 total points *and* within a
trick of game. **This is a question for Rick** — his wording says either
one is enough, and the measurement says both. The cost of following his
wording is about 1,000 IMPs over 11,656 boards.

A suit-quality guard came out of the same measurement: the long suit
needs two of the top three honours, or the losing-trick count flatters a
hand like `Q98765.AQ7.AK6.A` (four losers, a suit not worth bidding
twice). BBA opens that 1♠ and so do we.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- BBA opens 2♣ on hands of 20-22 total points that we open at the one
  level (8 of its 18): `AKQ654.AK9.J5.K5` (22), `2.AQJ872.AKQJ83.` (21).
- BBA opens 1♥/1♠ on some hands within a trick of game that we open 2♣.
- After 2C P 2M P 2NT P: BBA jumps to 4M with some weak seven-card
  suits, bids 4NT rather than a four-card minor with 8-9, and shows
  hearts before rebidding six spades; opener cues a control where BBA
  asks at once (see "After a positive and opener's 2NT" below).

## Gaps and open questions

- **The 2♥ bust treatment** (`parrish_bust`, written 2026-10-05): 2♥
  shows 0-2 HCP and lifts the game force (`sets forcing=none`); 2♦ then
  waits with 3+ and the second negatives are off. Opener rebids
  naturally: 2♠ forcing one round (responder 3♠ with three, else 2NT),
  2NT 22-23 and three-level suits passable, 3♥ for hearts, 3NT 24-25.
  The positive-response blocks skip 2♥ on that card. Kokish's relay
  (2♣–2♦–2♥) is unaffected: it follows the waiting 2♦. Bust_Over_Strong_2C
  with the field set: 5 boards, the divergence is our 2♥ where BBA (not
  playing it) waits. Sources: Larry Cohen, "Two Club Opening"
  (larryco.com: 2♥ as the immediate double negative); opener's rebids
  are standard practice, not yet cited.
- `two_clubs.2d_response = steps` is not modelled.
- Opener's second call after the second negative.
- Slam bidding after a positive: covered for opener's raise (responder
  4M, opener asks), for 2C P 2M P 2NT P (below) and for the balanced
  positive; not for a minor second suit (opener bids 3NT over 3C/3D, and
  4NT in the minor is not tried), nor for the grand: after 2C P 3D P 3S
  P BBA reaches 7S with all the keycards where we stop in 6S
  (To_Finesse_Or_Not_To_Finesse 1, 15, 38, 89), because `grand_try`
  counts responder at his 8 HCP floor and there is no king ask.

## Raising opener's major after a positive (2026-09-25)

To_Finesse_Or_Not_To_Finesse was the corpus's worst covered scenario by
par (-2,292 over 500 boards). After 2C-2NT-3S (or 3m-3M), responder
held three trumps and 8-11 and bid 3NT: there was no raise. BBA drives
to slam. Responder now raises to 4M with three or more, agreeing the
suit; opener with the values asks with 4NT.
- Distance from par: +774.
- To the bidding side: +1,556 (165 boards).

BBA's lighter positive responses (any five-card suit with 7+ total
points; 2NT with balanced 7+) are left alone: Rick's guidance (8+ and a
real suit) stands.
- Opening 1M rather than 2NT with 20-21 and a five-card major, as BBA
  sometimes does: -1,717 by distance, -3,432 to the bidding side (626
  boards). Rick's ladder (2NT with 20-21 balanced) stands.

## After a positive and opener's 2NT; the balanced positive (2026-09-28)

NT_Ladder 426 (Rick: "we should be in 6S here like BBA"): 2C P 2S P
2NT P with `AK9876.J4.T9653.` opposite `J4.AKT.AKQ2.AJ75`. BBA:
3S, 4NT, 5H, 6S. We bid 3NT: there were no rules for responder here,
and the notrump-ladder catch-all (responder-rebids.bid) took over.

Opener's 2NT after a major positive is balanced, 22+, with exactly two
cards in responder's major. Responder now (priority order):
- **3M with six or more**: the eight-card fit is known, so it agrees the
  suit (`sets trump`), and the keycard or control-bid machinery in
  slam/ takes over (opener's 22 is always 18 of its own).
- **The other major with four**, then **a minor with four**: natural.
  Opener with four in responder's other major agrees it and asks at once
  (4NT, `trump=z, ask=keycards(z)`; game in it without RKCB on the
  card). Over a minor opener bids 3NT (the base fallback).
- **5-3-3-2**: a quantitative 4NT with 30-32 between us (opener at 22),
  6NT with 33+.

Opener's notrump after 2C P 2NT P now splits the ladder as over 2D:
3NT is 22, a quantitative 4NT 23-24, 6NT 25+; and both of opener's
balanced rebids after a positive show `hcp>=22` (the 2C opening's own
reading starts at 17 because of the playing-strength openings), so
responder's slam arithmetic over them counts opener at 22. That is what
found 6NT on Benjamin_2D 25 and 151.

BBA, probed:
- `probes/strong2c-2S-2N-resp.toml`, `strong2c-2H-2N-resp.toml`
  (responder, 8-13 with five or more in the major, opener 22-24 with two):
  six-card suits rebid (we always do; BBA jumps to 4M with some weak
  7-card suits and 8-9), four-card side suits are shown (BBA, with a
  minor and 8-9, bids 4NT about half the time; we show the minor),
  5-3-3-2 bids 4NT with 8-9 and 6NT with 10+ (we bid 4NT with 10: 22+10
  is 32, one short). BBA shows hearts before rebidding six spades on
  6-4; we rebid the spades.
- `probes/strong2c-2S-2N-3S-opener.toml` (opener, 22-24 with two spades,
  after 3S): BBA asks with 4NT on 289 of 300 and bids 4S on 11; we agree
  on 256. The rest are control bids: with a side suit holding neither
  ace nor king we cue first (control-bids.bid, Rick 2026-09-25), where
  BBA asks straight away.
- `probes/strong2c-2N-opener.toml` (opener balanced 22-25 after
  2C P 2NT P): BBA 3NT with 22, 4NT with 23-24, 6NT with 25; we agree on
  295 of 300.

Measured (after the catch-all change in responder-rebids.bid):
- Responder's rebid over 2NT and the 4NT ask: distance from par +48,
  to the side +135 (22 boards).
- Opener after 2C P 2NT P (3NT 22, 4NT 23-24) and `hcp>=22` on the
  balanced rebids: distance from par +452, to the side +951 (132 boards).
- The 2C-opened boards over all scenarios (either auction opened 2C,
  5,401 boards): vs BBA -11,726 → -11,226.

## Opener's raise of a positive shows 22+ (2026-10-01)

Rick (2026-10-01): after 2C-2H (a natural positive) opener's 3H is the
balanced 22-24 hand that was going to rebid 2NT; with a long suit and
fewer HCP opener shows his own suit. BBA raises on every 22+ hand with
three hearts, even 75.AKQ.AKQ95.AT9 with five diamonds (272 of 272 in
`probes/slam-2C-2H-opener.toml`, alert "21+ total points"); with 18-21
it bids 3H or 4H ("19-20", fast arrival), never its own suit. We read
the raise at the 2C floor (17) and bid our own suit on a third of the
22+ hands. The raise now shows 22+ and outranks the own suit, for every
positive (`2C 2y` / `2C 3y`). Vanilla +60 IMPs vs BBA, corpus +97, 21GF
random +40, both halves positive; responder's slams after 2C-2H-3H are
slam-entry's (slam-entry.notes.md, "Declarer points and support
points").

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only 2h-bust`.
IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer;
"actor" is the side that made the first differing call. 2♥ bust
(`parrish_bust`), Bust_Over_Strong_2C (5 boards), Game_Forcing_2C and
Opps_Bid_Over_GF_2C: 174 boards changed; actor contract +180, other side
doubling +193, double-dummy +171, halves +94/+86 (z +2.6): gains.

## Systems on over opener's notrump (Rick, 2026-10-05)

Rick: 2♣–2♠–2NT and 2♣–2♥(positive)–2NT are systems on, like
2♣–2♦–2NT and 2♣ (2♠) P (P) 2NT (one-nt.notes.md, "Systems on"). So by
default responder answers opener's 2NT after a positive with the 2NT
system (Stayman, transfers: the six-card suit transfers and opener
declares). The natural rebids probed from BBA (2026-09-28, "After a
positive and opener's 2NT") are now BBA's treatment, `general.style =
bba` (strong-openings.test keeps their cases there). Measured on the
tripwire only: Grand_Slam_Invite 23 now stops in 4♥ after the transfer
where the natural 3♥ and keycard reached 7♥; slam continuations after a
transfer over a 22+ 2NT are the jacoby-transfers.bid ones.

**After their overcall and partner's pass** (2♣ (2x) P (P)) opener had
no rule at all. Added the balanced rebids only: 2NT with 22-23 and a
stopper (systems on over it), 3NT with 24-25 and a stopper. The suit
rebids and doubles there are still missing.

## Bridge-Classroom #94 and #92 (Rick, 2026-11-06; rules 2026-11-07)

**#94**, NT Ladder (Lev) board 38, dealer S, EW vul: North
`K973.AQT43.J942.-`, South (Rick) `AQJ.K8.AKT65.AK2`. Auction 2♣ P 2♥
(positive) P 2NT P 3♦ (transfer) P 4♦ (Rick) P 4NT (North:
"Quantitative, 5 ♥", alerted) P 5♣ (no rule) P P P: 5♣ in a 4-0 fit,
thirteen tricks in ♦, ♥, ♠ and NT. Rick: "Broken Rusty auction.
Strange 4NT alert."

1. **Systems stay on over 2♣–2♥(positive)–2NT.** Rick ruled this on
   2026-10-05 ("Systems on over opener's notrump" above), so the 3♦
   transfer is right: hearts are known, but the transfer makes the 22+
   hand declarer. Not reopened.
2. **Opener's 4♦ over the transfer is natural**: five or more diamonds,
   slam interest. Opener's 2NT denied three hearts (it would have
   raised), so a super-accept is impossible. It was unread (base.bid's
   runout fallback); responder still took it as "partner answered my
   transfer" and jacoby-transfers.bid's quantitative 4NT fired. Now
   read (`4C`/`4D` after 2♣–2M–2NT–transfer, priority -1: opener's own
   choice stays the completion).
3. **Responder over that 4m:** with three or more of the minor the fit
   is found and 4NT asks for keycards in it (`trump=m`), the card's RKCB;
   without RKCB, six of the minor; no fit, four of his major.
4. **The asker never passes an unread five-level answer to a
   quantitative 4NT** (base.bid, priority -40, above the game-reached
   pass): 6NT, taking the unread suit as an acceptance. The keycard
   answers already had their continuations (rkcb-1430.bid passes a
   5-of-trumps answer only with at most three keycards between us).
5. **Rusty's own auction on the board** went 2♣ 2♥ 3♦ (five diamonds)
   3NT: responder had no raise of opener's minor after a major
   positive. Responder now raises to 4m with four (agrees it), opener
   asks: 2♣ 2♥ 3♦ 4♦ 4NT 5♣ 6♦.

Calls on the board, before → after (stand-in card 21GF-GIB, modified
Jacoby 2NT, Kokish on): North over Rick's 4♦: Pass/4NT quantitative →
4NT keycard in ♦; over 5♣: Pass → 6♦. All-Rusty: 3NT → 6♦.

**#92** (kokish.notes.md has the diagnosis): with Kokish off, 2♣–2♦–2♥
is natural and responder had only the second negative, so the base
fallback bid 3NT on everything else. Responder now shows a five-card
suit without a fit (2♠ over 2♥, 3♦), waits with 2NT with no fit, and
opener over the 2NT rebids six of his major, shows a second suit or
bids 3NT. A natural 4♥ raise with few values was tried and dropped:
opener's 18+ asked for keycards over it (-81 IMPs on the actor's
contract errors over the strong-2♣ scenarios).

Measured (compare --limit 50 --par-all, Kokish_Relay, NT_Ladder,
Game_Forcing_2C, To_Finesse_Or_Not_To_Finesse, Bust_Over_Strong_2C,
Opps_Bid_Over_GF_2C; 255 boards): 13 changed, all at responder's call
over 2♣–2♦–2M (3NT → 2♠/2NT/3♦). `errors_diff.py` verdict, the actor's
contract errors: +10 IMPs (halves -5 / +15, they differ: small and
mixed), distance from par +13; vs BBA by par -185 → -172, by errors
-173 → -167. The 4m raise and the reading of opener's 4m over the
transfer did not occur in those 50-board samples (`.test` cases only).
All-scenario tripwire (`--limit 50`, 17,105 boards): 28 changed, every
one at responder's call over 2♣–2♦–2M or the new 4♦ raise after
2♣–2M–3♦ (+12 twice); nothing else moved. Actor's contract errors +22
(halves -5 / +27), distance from par +25; vs BBA by par -6,223 → -6,198,
by errors -7,734 → -7,716.

## 2♣–2♦–3NT with Kokish on (2026-11-07)

With Kokish (`two_level.kokish.play`) the 24-25 balanced goes through the
relay (2♣–2♦–2♥–2♠–2NT), so 2♣–2♦–3NT reads 26-27 there, not 24-25: the
ladder's next rung, and what BBA rebids on Kokish_Relay (85 boards: 59
at 26, 26 at 27; its relay 2NT 93 boards, all 25). Without a Gambling
3NT the 26-27 opens 3NT and our opener never rebids it, but a partner's
3NT reads 26-27 and over-3nt.bid counts from 26 (7 HCP: quantitative
4NT, where 24-25 passed). Kokish off: 24-25 as before. Rick (2026-11-07)
on transfers: "people playing jacoby transfers normally play them over
1NT, 2NT, 2C/2NT, and kokish relay, and sometimes 2C/3NT"; over 3NT
they are Texas (texas-transfers.notes.md). Details and measurements in
kokish.notes.md.

## Brill (general.system = brill, 2026-10-15)

Brill's treatment, played on the Brill card only (`cards/json/Brill.json`, `general.system = brill`: a stand-in until convention-card's `general.style` takes a `brill` value; cards/README.md "Brill"). Rusty plays the Brill dailies as South with three Brill robots, so it should read and bid what they do. Every other card is unchanged (a `.test` line on 21GF-GIB beside each Brill line; `compare --limit 50` tripwire against main: no board changed).

3NT is 25-27 (the card) with no five-card major ("Balanced hand, 25-27
HCP": `(balanced or semibalanced) and hcp>= 25 and hcp<= 27 and H<= 4 and S
<= 4`); a balanced 25-27 with a five-card major opens 2C. The 2C rule's
`hcp<=25` stays for every other card (their 3NT is 26-27 or the card's).

Measured with `probes/tools/brill_probe.py report --card Brill` over the top 2000 corpus auctions (calls of this group, board-weighted, our reading against Brill's): 0% -> 100% of 1,170 boards.

- **Rick's rulings (2026-09-23):** the balanced ladder (2NT 20-21, 2♣
  then 2NT 22-23, 2♣ then 3NT 24-25, 3NT 26-27, 2♣ then 4NT 28+); the
  unbalanced 2♣ on 23 total points or within a trick of game; responder's
  2♦ waiting, positives with a real suit and 8+, the second negative.
  Rick's guidance also stands against BBA's lighter positives and against
  opening 1M with 20-21 and a five-card major (2026-09-25).
- **Book practice:** the ladder, playing tricks as 13 minus losers, the
  second negative, and after 2C–positive–2NT rebidding a six-card suit,
  showing a four-card side suit and the quantitative 4NT are standard
  practice, not yet cited to a book or article.
- **BBA evidence:** BBA's eighteen 2♣ openings in the Basic_* scenarios

- **Where we differ from the source:** Rick's wording makes the two

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Transfer Walsh (Wikipedia, "Transfer Walsh"; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh): over partner's 1♣,
#
#   1♦   four or more hearts (with four of each major too)
#   1♥   four or more spades (longer than hearts, or 5-5)
#   1♠   no four-card major: four or more diamonds, or a game force
#        with longer diamonds
#   1NT  natural, 6-10 balanced (responses.bid)
#
# Opener accepts with three of responder's major (or four and a
# minimum), raises to two with four and 16-18, to game with 19+, and
# otherwise rebids naturally, the rebid denying three of the major. The
# natural rules that read the response as a suit stand aside under this
# card (`tw(x)` in rebids.bid). See transfer-walsh.notes.md.

module transfer-walsh "Transfer Walsh responses to 1♣"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh
  param  q4n = bidding_conventions/quantitative_4nt default true

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A game force with longer diamonds and a major starts with 1♠ (as Walsh
# bids 1♦ first with game values).
after 1C (P)
  1D  "Transfer: 4+ hearts, 6+ HCP"        alert
      shows H>=4, hcp>=6, H>=S, H>S | H=4, hcp<=11 | H>=D
      sets  forcing=round, ask=tw_accept(H)
      artificial
  1H  "Transfer: 4+ spades, 6+ HCP"        alert
      shows S>=4, hcp>=6, S>H | S>=5, S>=H, hcp<=11 | S>=D
      sets  forcing=round, ask=tw_accept(S)
      artificial
  1S  "Transfer Walsh: 4+ diamonds, no major unless 12+ HCP"   alert
      shows D>=4, hcp>=6, (H<=3, S<=3) | (hcp>=12, D>H, D>S)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=tw_nomajor
      artificial

# ── Opener after a transfer to a major ───────────────────────────────
when asked tw_accept(M)
  1{M}  "Accepts: three {M}, or four and a minimum"
        shows M>=3, M=3 | tp(M)<=15
        priority 3
  2{M}  "Raise: four {M}, 16-18"            shows M>=4, tp(M)=16..18   sets trump=M
        priority 3
  4{M}  "Game raise: four {M}, 19+"          shows M>=4, tp(M)>=19   sets trump=M
        priority 3
  # Without three of the major: natural, each denying the fit.
  1S    "4+ spades, not three hearts"        shows S>=4, H<=2, suit_points<=18
        when  M is H
        priority 2
  2H    "Reverse: 4+ hearts, longer clubs, 17+, not three spades"   shows H>=4, C>H, S<=2, suit_points>=17
        when  M is S
        sets  forcing=round
        priority 2
  1N    "12-14 HCP, balanced, not three {M}"   shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14, M<=2
        priority 1
  2N    "18-19 HCP, balanced, not three {M}"   shows balanced, hcp=18..19, M<=2
        priority 1
  2C    "6+ clubs, minimum, not three {M}"     shows C>=6, suit_points<=15, M<=2
  3C    "6+ clubs, 16-18, not three {M}"       shows C>=6, suit_points=16..18, M<=2
  2D    "Reverse: 4+ diamonds, longer clubs, 17+, not three {M}"   shows D>=4, C>D, suit_points>=17, M<=2
        sets  forcing=round
  3N    "18-21 with six or more clubs, not three {M}"   shows C>=6, hcp=18..21, M<=2
        priority 1
  1N    "Minimum, not three {M}"            shows hcp<=14, M<=2
        priority -3
  2C    "5+ clubs, not three {M}"   shows C>=5, M<=2
        priority -4

# ── Opener after 1♠ (no major) ───────────────────────────────────────
when asked tw_nomajor
  1N  "12-14 HCP, balanced"                  shows balanced | shape 5-4-2-2, hcp=12..14
      priority 1
  2N  "18-19 HCP, balanced"                  shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      priority 1
  2D  "Raise: 4+ diamonds, minimum"          shows D>=4, tp(D)<=15   sets trump=D
  3D  "Jump raise: 4+ diamonds, 16+"         shows D>=4, tp(D)>=16   sets trump=D
  2C  "6+ clubs, minimum"                    shows C>=6, suit_points<=15
  3C  "6+ clubs, 16-18"                      shows C>=6, suit_points=16..18
  3N  "18-21 with six or more clubs"         shows C>=6, hcp=18..21
  1N  "Minimum"             shows hcp<=14
      priority -3
  2C  "5+ clubs"               shows C>=5
      priority -4

# ── Responder's second call ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Opener accepted: three (or four, minimum) in responder's major.
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1H (P) | 1C (P) 1H (P) 1S (P)
  P   "Weak: to play"                        shows points<=10
      priority -5
  3N  "Game: 13+, four of the major"          shows points>=13
      priority -1
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12"                   shows points=11..12
      sets  ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1H (P)
  2H  "Five or more hearts, 8-10: competitive"   shows H>=5, points=8..10   sets trump=H, ask=signoff
  3H  "Invitational: five or more hearts, 11-12"  shows H>=5, tp(H)=11..12   sets trump=H, ask=invite(H)
  4H  "Game: five or more hearts, 13+"         shows H>=5, tp(H)>=13   sets trump=H
  1S  "Four spades as well, 6+"                 shows S>=4, H=4
      sets  forcing=round
      priority 1
after 1C (P) 1H (P) 1S (P)
  2S  "Five or more spades, 8-10: competitive"   shows S>=5, points=8..10   sets trump=S, ask=signoff
  3S  "Invitational: five or more spades, 11-12"  shows S>=5, tp(S)=11..12   sets trump=S, ask=invite(S)
  4S  "Game: five or more spades, 13+"         shows S>=5, tp(S)>=13   sets trump=S
  2H  "Four or more hearts as well, 8-10"      shows H>=4, S>=5, points=8..10   sets ask=signoff

# Opener raised to two (four, 16-18): game from 8.
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 2H (P) | 1C (P) 1H (P) 2S (P)
  P   "Weak: no game"                         shows points<=7
      priority -5
  4{trump}  "Game"                            shows points>=8

# Opener denied three of the major, or answered 1♠: natural.
# Slam and the second suit (2026-10-05, the self A/B against Walsh: every
# game force went 1NT-3NT, 19-21 HCP and a 4-4 fit in the other major
# included, -93 IMPs on 75 boards): a quantitative 4NT or 6NT, and the
# responder's reverses that natural Walsh has (responder-rebids.bid).
after 1C (P) 1x (P) 1N (P)
  P   "Weak: no game"                         shows points<=10
      priority -5
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12"                   shows points=11..12   sets ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 13+"                             shows points>=13
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      shows balanced, points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.min <= 32
      when  q4n
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam in notrump"                  shows balanced, points + partner.points.min >= 33
after 1C (P) 1S (P) 1N (P) | 1C (P) 1S (P) 2C (P)
  2H  "Game force: four hearts, longer diamonds"   shows H>=4, D>=5, D>S, points>=13   sets forcing=game
      priority 1
  2S  "Game force: four spades, longer diamonds"   shows S>=4, D>=5, H<=3, points>=13   sets forcing=game
      priority 1
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P)
  2S  "Responder's reverse: 4+ spades, 5+ hearts, game forcing"   shows S>=4, H>=5, points>=13   sets forcing=game
      priority 1
after 1C (P) 1H (P) 1N (P)
  3H  "Four hearts, five spades, game forcing"   shows H>=4, S>=5, points>=13   sets forcing=game
      priority 1

# Opener over responder's major after 1♣-1♠-1NT: the 1NT rebid did not
# deny a four-card major (responder had denied one), so raise with four.
after 1C (P) 1S (P) 1N (P) 2M (P) | 1C (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2M (P)
  3{M} "Four {M}: the fit"                    shows M>=4   sets trump=M
      priority 2
  2S   "Four spades, not four hearts"        shows S>=4, H<=3
      when  M is H
      priority 1
  3N   "No fit in {M}"
after 1C (P) 1S (P) 1N (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) | 1C (P) 1S (P) 2C (P) 2H (P) 2S (P)
  4S   "Four spades as well: game"           shows S>=4
      priority 1
  3N   "Game in notrump"
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P)
  2H  "Weak: six or more hearts"             shows H>=6, points<=10   sets ask=signoff
  3H  "Invitational: six or more hearts"     shows H>=6, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(H)
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"             shows H>=6, points>=13
after 1C (P) 1H (P) 1N (P)
  2S  "Weak: six or more spades"             shows S>=6, points<=10   sets ask=signoff
  3S  "Invitational: six or more spades"     shows S>=6, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(S)
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"             shows S>=6, points>=13

after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1S (P)
  P   "Weak: four spades too"                 shows S>=4, points<=10
      priority -4
  2S  "Raise: four spades, weak"              shows S>=4, points<=10   sets trump=S, ask=signoff
  3S  "Invitational raise: four spades"       shows S>=4, tp(S)=11..12   sets trump=S, ask=invite(S)
  4S  "Game: four spades"                     shows S>=4, tp(S)>=13   sets trump=S
  2H  "Weak: six or more hearts"              shows H>=6, points<=10   sets ask=signoff
  1N  "6-10, no spade fit"                    shows points<=10, S<=3   sets ask=signoff
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12, no spade fit"     shows points=11..12, S<=3   sets ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 13+, no spade fit"               shows points>=13, S<=3
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT, no spade fit"
      shows balanced, S<=3, points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.min <= 32
      when  q4n
      sets  ask=quant
  6N  "Slam in notrump, no spade fit"    shows balanced, S<=3, points + partner.points.min >= 33

after 1C (P) 1x (P) 2C (P)
  P   "Weak: no game"                         shows points<=10
      priority -5
  2N  "Invitational: 11-12"                   shows points=11..12   sets ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 13+"                             shows points>=13

# Opener's jump to 3♣ (six clubs, 16-18): game from 9 (2026-10-05, the
# self A/B: responder had no rule and passed it with 13-14).
after 1C (P) 1x (P) 3C (P)
  P   "Weak: no game"                         shows points<=8
      priority -5
  3N  "Game: 9+"                              shows points>=9
  5C  "Game in clubs: 9+, three clubs, a suit unstopped"   shows C>=3, points>=9, !balanced
      priority -1

after 1C (P) 1S (P) 2D (P)
  P   "Weak: no game"                         shows tp(D)<=10
      priority -5
  3D  "Invitational: 11-12"                   shows tp(D)=11..12   sets ask=invite(D)
  3N  "Game: 13+"                             shows points>=13

# Responder showed four spades as well after the heart transfer was
# accepted (1♣-1♦-1♥-1♠): opener raises with four, else describes.
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1H (P) 1S (P)
  2S  "Four spades, minimum"                  shows S>=4, tp(S)<=15   sets trump=S
  3S  "Four spades, 16-18"                    shows S>=4, tp(S)=16..18   sets trump=S
  4S  "Four spades, 19+"                      shows S>=4, tp(S)>=19   sets trump=S
  2H  "Four hearts, minimum"                  shows H>=4, S<=3, suit_points<=15   sets trump=H
  2C  "Six or more clubs, minimum"            shows C>=6, S<=3, H<=3, suit_points<=15
  2N  "18-19, balanced"                       shows balanced, hcp=18..19, S<=3
  1N  "Minimum, no four spades"               shows hcp<=14, S<=3
      priority -1
  3N  "15+, no four spades"                   shows hcp>=15, S<=3
      priority -2

# Opener reversed (17+, forcing one round) over the transfer.
after 1C (P) 1x (P) 2z (P) when we.forcing = round
  2N  "Forced: minimum, no fit"               shows points<=7
      priority -1
  3N  "Game: 8+"                              shows points>=8
      priority -2
  3C  "Three or more clubs, 8+: game forcing"  shows C>=3, points>=8   sets forcing=game
      priority -3
  3z  "Four {z}, 8+: game forcing"            shows z>=4, points>=8   sets forcing=game, trump=z
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 2z (P) when we.forcing = round
  2H  "Five or more hearts"                   shows H>=5   sets forcing=round
      when  z is D
after 1C (P) 1H (P) 2z (P) when we.forcing = round
  2S  "Five or more spades"                   shows S>=5   sets forcing=round
# Opener after responder's five-card major over the reverse.
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 2z (P) 2H (P) | 1C (P) 1H (P) 2z (P) 2S (P)
  2N  "No fit, minimum reverse"               shows hcp<=18
      priority -1
  3N  "No fit, 19+"                           shows hcp>=19
      priority -2
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 2z (P) 2H (P)
  3H  "Two hearts: the 5-2 fit"               shows H=2
after 1C (P) 1H (P) 2z (P) 2S (P)
  3S  "Two spades: the 5-2 fit"               shows S=2

# transfer-walsh (`transfer-walsh.bid`): notes

Transfer Walsh (`minor_openings.one_club.transfer_resp`): over 1♣, 1♦
shows hearts, 1♥ spades, 1♠ no four-card major (four diamonds, or a game
force with longer diamonds); 1NT stays natural. Cases:
`transfer-walsh.test`. Scenario: Transfer_Walsh (BBA plays it on
21GF-DEFAULT without the switch, so its auctions there are natural: only
our problems count, not agreement).

## Structure

- Responder bids hearts first with four of each major; spades first with
  five spades. Off over interference (the natural/negative-double rules).
- Opener: accepts with three of the major or four and a minimum (1M);
  raises to 2M with four and 16-18, 4M with 19+; else natural (1♠ over
  1♦, 1NT 12-14, 2♣ six clubs, 2NT 18-19, a reverse 17+), each denying
  three of the major.
- Responder's second call: after an acceptance, pass weak, 2M with five
  and 8-10, 3M invites with five, 4M game; 2NT/3NT with four. After a
  denial, natural (2M/3M/4M with six, 2NT/3NT). After a reverse: 2NT
  minimum, 3♣/3 of opener's suit game forcing, 3NT, or the five-card
  major.
- The natural rules that read the response as a suit (rebids.bid,
  responder-rebids.bid, checkback, NMF, Roudi, two-way NMF, XYZ, FSF,
  Wolff, NMF after 2NT) stand aside after 1♣ under this card: `define
  tw(x)` in rebids.bid.

## Corpus (Transfer_Walsh with the switch on, 50 boards, 2026-10-05)

Divergences at 1♣ P are all the transfer itself (BBA natural). Problems
in our auctions fixed: the reverse over a transfer and responder's
four spades after an acceptance had no rule. One remains in competition
(1♣ 2♦ 2♥ P 2♠, not ours).

## Gaps and questions for Rick

- The 1♠ response: Wikipedia has it as diamonds; convention-card's
  summary as "no four-card major". We take both: four diamonds and no
  major, or a game force with longer diamonds. A balanced 6-10 without a
  major bids 1NT.
- Opener's 1M acceptance with four and a minimum (as 1♣-1♥-2♥ would be
  for many): we chose 1M with any minimum, 2M with 16-18. Some play 2M
  as the minimum four-card raise.
- Slam auctions and the modules under slam/ and majors/ that read
  `after 1x (P) 1M (P)` literally (splinters by opener) are not gated.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only
transfer-walsh`. IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the
convention makes fewer; "actor" is the side that made the first
differing call. Against natural Walsh, Transfer_Walsh and 1C_WalshStyle:
711 boards changed. First -338 to the actor (z -3.2), three gaps: (1)
after 1♣-1x-1NT responder had only pass/2NT/3NT, so the game force with
longer diamonds and a major (1♠ first) never showed the major, and 19-21
balanced stopped in 3NT (-93 on 75 boards); now the responder's reverses
as in natural Walsh, opener raising with four, and a quantitative 4NT /
6NT (also after 1♣-1♦-1♠); (2) responder had no rule over opener's 3♣
(six clubs, 16-18) and passed it with 13-14; (3) opener's splinters
(splinters.bid) read 1♣-1♦/1♥ as natural and agreed the wrong major;
they now stand aside under Transfer Walsh. After: 703 changed; actor
contract -137, doubling 0; double-dummy -184; halves -172/+35 (z -1.4):
neutral. Left: no opener's splinter under Transfer Walsh (natural Walsh
found two slams by 1♣-1♥-4♦), and the game raise 4M with 19+ that
responder cannot judge for slam.

## Sources

- **Wikipedia, "Transfer Walsh"** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_Walsh):
  1♦ hearts, 1♥ spades, 1♠ diamonds, 1NT 6-9 balanced; opener accepts
  with three, jumps with extras. convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/transfer_walsh.toml` cites it.
- **Where we differ:** ranges (accept up to 15 support points, 2M 16-18)
  and responder's continuations follow our natural responder rebids
  (standard practice, not yet cited).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Two-way New Minor Forcing (xyNT): after 1x-1y-1NT, 2C relays to 2D
# (every invitational hand starts here, and a weak hand with diamonds
# passes 2D); 2D is an artificial game force; 2NT relays to 3C (a weak
# hand with clubs passes); jumps to three are natural slam tries. Played
# instead of NMF. See two-way-nmf.notes.md.

module two-way-nmf "Two-way New Minor Forcing (xyNT)"
  kind   convention
  needs  responder-rebids
  skill  bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf
  # On with its own switch, or with XYZ (xyz.bid), which plays the same
  # structure after every one-level rebid, 1NT included.
  param  twoway = bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf default false
  param  xyz    = bidding_conventions/xyz default false

after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1N (P) when twoway | xyz, !tw(x)
  2C  "xyNT: relay to 2♦, invitational or a diamond sign-off"   alert
      shows nt_rebid_invite | (D>=6, nt_rebid_signoff, y is not D, x is not D)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_relay
      artificial
      priority 1
  2D  "xyNT: artificial game force"   alert
      shows nt_rebid_game, y>=5 | (H>=4, S>=4) | !balanced
      sets  forcing=game, ask=xy_gf
      artificial
      priority 1
  2N  "xyNT: relay to 3♣, a club sign-off"   alert
      shows C>=6, nt_rebid_signoff
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_clubs
      artificial
  3y  "Slam try: six or more {y}"
      shows y>=6, points + partner.hcp.min >= 28
      sets  forcing=game, trump=y

when asked xy_relay
  2D  "Forced relay"                       alert   artificial
when asked xy_clubs
  3C  "Forced relay"                       alert   artificial

# ── After the 2♦ relay: weak with diamonds passes, every other call invites
after 1x (P) 1M (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when twoway | xyz, !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 2♦"                      shows D>=6, nt_rebid_signoff
  2M  "Invitational: five {M}"             shows M=5, nt_rebid_invite   sets ask=invite(M)
  3M  "Invitational: six {M}"              shows M>=6, nt_rebid_invite   sets ask=invite(M)
  2N  "Invitational, balanced"             shows nt_rebid_invite, M<=5   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
after 1C (P) 1D (P) 1N (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when twoway | xyz, !tw(C)
  P   "Weak"                               shows nt_rebid_signoff
      priority -5
  3D  "Invitational: six diamonds"         shows D>=6, nt_rebid_invite   sets ask=invite(D)
  2N  "Invitational, balanced"             shows nt_rebid_invite   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1N (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when twoway | xyz, !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 3♣"                      shows C>=6

# ── After the 2♦ game force: opener shows three of responder's major,
# then four hearts after a 1♠ response, else 2NT.
when asked xy_gf
  2H  "Three hearts"                       shows H=3        when partner.H>=4
  2S  "Three spades"                       shows S=3        when partner.S>=4
  2H  "Four hearts, not three spades"      shows H>=4, S<=2  when partner.S>=4
  2N  "No fit to show"
      priority -1
when answered xy_gf
  4H  "Game in the heart fit"              shows H>=5 | (H>=4, partner.H.min>=4)   when partner.H>=3   sets trump=H
  4S  "Game in the spade fit"              shows S>=5 | (S>=4, partner.S.min>=4)   when partner.S>=3   sets trump=S
  4H  "Game: six hearts"                   shows H>=6
  4S  "Game: six spades"                   shows S>=6
  3N  "Game, no major fit"
      priority -1

# two-way-nmf (`two-way-nmf.bid`): notes

Two-way New Minor Forcing (xyNT), card field
`other_conventions.two_way_nmf` (on in Precision and Precision-14-16).
Cases: `two-way-nmf.test`.

## Structure

After 1x-1y-1NT (every opening and response, uncontested):

- 2♣ relays to 2♦: every invitational hand (11-12), or a weak hand with
  six diamonds that passes 2♦. After the relay, 2M (five), 3M (six) and
  2NT invite; opener answers in rebids.bid.
- 2♦: artificial game force (13+, with a five-card major, both majors or
  an unbalanced hand; a balanced 13-15 bids 3NT). Opener: three of
  responder's major, four hearts after 1♠, else 2NT. Responder: four of
  the major with a fit, else 3NT.
- 2NT relays to 3♣, to play there with six clubs (weak).
- A jump to three of responder's suit is a slam try (six cards, 16+).
- On, it switches off NMF, the natural 2♣/2♦ and responder's natural
  2NT and three-level invitations (responder-rebids.bid).

## Corpus

The scenario Two-Way_New_Minor_Forcing_aka_xyNT plays 21GF-DEFAULT, which
has plain NMF, so BBA's auctions there are not xyNT. Run with
`--set other_conventions.two_way_nmf=true --set
other_conventions.new_minor_forcing.play=false`: no problems at the
convention's calls (2026-10-05). The Precision cards are the ones that
switch it on.

## Gaps and open questions

- Two-way NMF by a passed hand (`two_way_nmf_by_passed_hand`): not read;
  the relays apply by a passed hand too.
- The 2NT relay's shape-showing continuations (Bridge Winners' 3♦/3♥/
  3♠/3NT after 3♣) are not built; only the club sign-off.
- After 1♥-1♠-1NT, Bridge Winners reads 2♠ as 4-4 invitational; we keep
  our natural calls there.

## Played with XYZ (2026-10-05)

The module has no `card` line any more: its contexts hold when
`other_conventions.two_way_nmf` or `other_conventions.xyz` is set, since
XYZ (xyz.bid) is this structure extended to 1x-1y-1z. responder-rebids.bid
and new-minor-forcing.bid step aside for either switch.

## Sources

- **Bridge Winners, "Two-Way New Minor Forcing aka xyNT"**
  (https://bridgewinners.com/article/view/two-way-new-minor-forcing-aka-xynt):
  2♣ relay for invitations, 2♦ game force, 2NT relay to 3♣, three-level
  slam tries; off in competition. convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/two_way_nmf.toml` cites it.
- **Where we differ:** opener's answers to 2♦ follow NMF's (standard
  practice, not yet cited); the article leaves them open.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Weak jump shifts: opener's continuations and responder's answers. The
# jumps themselves are in responses.bid (two level 2-5 HCP and six cards,
# three level 2-6 and seven). Bridge Bum: opener may pass, rebid his own
# suit (not forcing), raise (not forcing), bid a new suit (forcing, extra
# strength) or bid 2NT, a forcing game try that implies at least two cards
# in responder's suit. See weak-jump-shifts.notes.md.

module weak-jump-shifts "Weak jump shifts"
  kind   convention
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts
  param  weak2 = bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts:two_level default false
  param  weak2_nc = bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts:not_in_comp default false
  param  weak3 = bidding_conventions/weak_jump_shifts:three_level default false

# Weak jump shifts with no interference: the two-level box, or the
# "not in competition" box other card formats have (#74). The modules
# that give way to a weak jump shift read this too.
define wjs_on = weak2 | weak2_nc

# A response of 2x to 1y is a jump when x ranks above y (else a two over
# one). responder-rebids.bid reads it to keep its 2/1 continuations away
# from a weak jump shift.
define two_level_jump(x, y) = y is C | (y is D, x is H | x is S) | (y is H, x is S)

# ── Opener after a weak jump shift at the two level ────────────────────
after 1x (P) 2y (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x), partner.jumped
  P   "To play: two of {y}"          priority -5
  4y  "Game: 18+ with two or more {y}"           shows y>=2, hcp>=18
      when  y is H | y is S
  3y  "Raise: 3+ {y}, 16-17, invitational"       shows y>=3, hcp=16..17
  2N  "Forcing game try: asks for a feature"     alert
      shows y>=3, hcp>=16, hcp<=17 | y is C | y is D
      sets  forcing=round, ask=wjs_feature
      artificial
  3x  "Rebids {x}: seven or more, not forcing"   shows x>=7, y<=1, hcp<=17
  # 18-21 with a long minor: rebids.bid's 3NT is off here (the conv-ab
  # run, 2026-10-07: 3NT opposite 2-5 and a misfit rarely makes).
  3x  "Rebids {x}: six or more, 18+, not forcing"   shows x>=6, y<=1, hcp>=18
      when  x is C | x is D
  4x  "Game in my own major: seven, or six good ones, 18+"
      shows x>=7 | (x>=6, quality(x)>=good), y<=1, hcp>=18
      when  x is H | x is S
  cheapest(z)  "New suit: 4+ {z}, 17+, forcing"  shows z>=4, hcp>=17, y<=1
      when  z is not x, z is not y
      sets  forcing=round

# Responder answers the 2NT game try: three of his suit with a minimum,
# 3NT with a maximum and two of the top three honours, else a feature
# (an ace or king) with a maximum.
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  3N  "Maximum: 4-5, two of the top three honours"   shows hcp>=4, quality(y)>=good
  3z  "Maximum: 4-5, a feature in {z}"
      shows hcp>=4, has(A,z) | has(K,z)
      when  z is not y
      prefer 0 - z
  3y  "Minimum: 2-3, or no feature"
      priority -1

after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  P   "Minimum: to play"             priority -5
  4y  "Game"                              shows hcp>=17, y>=3
      when  y is H | y is S
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) 3z (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x), z is not y
  4y  "Game in {y}"                              shows y>=2
      when  y is H | y is S
  3N  "Game in notrump"                          when  y is C | y is D
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2N (P) 3N (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  P   "No further bid"                             priority -5

# Responder after opener rebids his suit (not forcing): pass.
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  P   "Opener's suit: play here"                 priority -5

# Responder after opener's invitational raise: game with a maximum.
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 3y (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x)
  P   "Minimum: play three"                      priority -5
  4y  "Maximum: 4-5, game"                      shows hcp>=4
      when  y is H | y is S
# After opener's new suit (forcing): raise with four, else back to a
# known suit as cheaply as possible.
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) | 1x (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x), z is not x, z is not y
  3z  "Raise: four {z}"                          shows z>=4
  cheapest(y)  "Rebids {y}: no fit"              shows y>=6
      priority -1
  cheapest(x)  "Preference for {x}"              shows x>=2
      priority -2

# Opener after responder's answer to the new suit: game with a fit found
# (4 of a major, or 3NT), else stop.
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) * (P) | 1x (P) 2y (P) 3z (P) * (P) when wjs_on, y is not x, two_level_jump(y, x), z is not x, z is not y
  P   "No game: stop here"                       priority -5
  4z  "Game in the fit"                          shows z>=4, hcp>=19
      when  partner.z>=4, z is H | z is S
  3N  "Game in notrump: 22+"                     shows hcp>=22
      priority -1

# ── Opener after a weak jump shift at the three level ──────────────────
after 1x (P) 3y (P) when weak3, y is not x, partner.jumped
  P   "No further bid"                           priority -5
  4y  "Game: 17+ with two or more {y}"           shows y>=2, hcp>=17
      when  y is H | y is S
  3N  "To play: 18+, a fit for {y}, side suits stopped"
      shows y>=2, hcp>=18
      when  y is C | y is D
  4x  "Game in my own major: seven, or six good ones, 16+"
      shows x>=7 | (x>=6, quality(x)>=good), hcp>=16, y<=1
      when  x is H | x is S
files.rules/base/weak-jump-shifts.notes.md:
# weak-jump-shifts (`weak-jump-shifts.bid`): notes

Weak jump shifts by responder over a one-level suit opening. The jumps
are in `responses.bid` (card fields `general.jump_shifts.weak_2` and
`weak_3`); opener's continuations and responder's answers are here.
Cases: `weak-jump-shifts.test`. Scenario: Weak_Jump_Shift (21GF-WJS-MSS).

## Structure

- Two level (1♣-2♦/2♥/2♠, 1♦-2♥/2♠, 1♥-2♠): six cards, 2-5 HCP. Over
  1♥, 2♠ also denies three hearts (BBA passes those hands).
- Three level (1♦-3♣, 1♥-3♣/3♦, 1♠-3♣/3♦/3♥): seven cards, 2-6 HCP.
- Opener after a two-level jump: pass; 4 of a major with 18+ and two or
  more; 3y (16-17, three cards) invites; 2NT asks (16-17 with three, or any
  strong hand with a minor jump): responder bids 3y (minimum, or no
  feature), a feature with 4-5, 3NT with 4-5 and two of the top three;
  3x with seven of opener's suit, not forcing; a new suit 17+, forcing.
- Opener after a three-level jump: pass; 4M with 17+ and two cards; 3NT
  with 18+ and a fit for the minor; 4 of his own major with seven (or six
  good ones) and 16+.
- Card precedence: weak beats strong at two (21GF-WJS-MSS sets both;
  BBA plays weak), and weak beats invitational at three (21GF-MSS,
  -Multi, -NoInvertedMinor set both; not probed).
- `responder-rebids.bid`'s 2/1 continuations and `rebids.bid`'s answers
  to a 2/1 and to an invitational three-level jump are switched off after
  a weak jump shift (`two_level_jump(x, y)` here).

## Corpus (Weak_Jump_Shift, 2026-10-05)

Same final contract as BBA on 6 of the first 50 boards before (strong
jump shifts), 17 after; identical auctions 0 to 14. All 500: calls
agreeing 80.1% (NS 77.0%). BBA's
range is 3-5 HCP at two and up to 6 at three. Remaining divergences at
the convention's calls are mostly EW's (BBA's GIB card competes over the
jump, ours does not), and BBA passing where our opener rebids 3NT with a
long minor (rebids.bid's 18-21 3NT, not this module).

## Convention score (2026-10-07)

`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only weak-jump-shifts` (Weak_Jump_Shift, 500
boards): -0.62 IMPs per changed board before (Rusty +233, BBA +464, 372
boards), -0.02 after (Rusty +456, BBA +464; halves -68/+60), good.
What was wrong: **3NT opposite a weak jump shift.** rebids.bid's
"18-21 with six or more of my minor: 3NT" fired over the jump (1♣-2♠-3NT
with a singleton spade), and after opener's forcing new suit 3NT came
from 19. On the corpus deals 3NT opposite 2-5 HCP makes on about one
board in five even with 18-21; BBA almost never bids it. Now rebids.bid's
3NT is off after a weak jump shift (as its other rebids already were),
opener rebids a six-card minor at three with 18+ and a misfit (not
forcing), and 3NT after the new suit needs 22. About +220 of Rusty's
gain.

## Open questions

- Weak jump shifts by a passed hand and in competition: the jump is weak
  in both here (Bridge Bum: on in competition). The card has
  `competitive.weak_jump_shifts_in_comp`; competitive rules are elsewhere.
- Weak and invitational both set: weak wins at three. Not probed.

## Sources

- **Bridge Bum, "Weak Jump Shifts"**
  (https://www.bridgebum.com/weak_jump_shifts.php): ranges (2-5 and six,
  2-7 and seven) and opener's options. We take 2-6 at three (BBA's
  corpus maximum is 6).
- **BBA evidence:** the Weak_Jump_Shift corpus (500 boards): 2♠ over 1♥
  denies three hearts; opener rarely rebids a six-card suit.
- **Par on the corpus deals** (2026-10-07): no 3NT opposite the weak
  jump below 22; Bridge Bum's "rebid his own suit (not forcing)" covers
  the 18+ six-card minor.
- **Where we differ:** opener's 3y raise as invitational and the feature
  answers to 2NT are standard practice (as after a weak two), not yet
  cited.

files.rules/base/weak-two-responses.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responses to a weak two, and opener's answer to 2NT. Two treatments
# (card `two_level.weak_two_2nt_response`): `feature`, where opener shows a
# side ace or king with a maximum, and `ogust`, where opener's answer shows
# minimum or maximum and the suit's quality.

module weak-two-responses "Responses to a weak two"
  kind   system
  needs  preempts
  skill  bidding_conventions/weak_2s
  skill  bidding_conventions/ogust
  skill  partnership_bidding/weak_twos
  param  ask2nt = two_level.weak_two_2nt_response default feature
  param  two_c  = two_level.two_clubs.meaning default strong
  param  style  = general.style
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  aces   = bidding_conventions/blackwood default false

# Standard responder (the default until 2026-09-24): 2NT from 15, raises
# with four. The default is now BBA's, below: par preferred it (+453 IMPs
# on the corpus, +78 on Basic_*).
#
# The weak twos are 2♦, 2♥ and 2♠: 2♣ is the strong opening unless the
# card says it is natural. Without the guard, responder's 2NT over a
# strong 2♣ was read as the weak-two ask and opener answered with a
# feature (95 boards in the Basic_* scenarios, -478 IMPs).
after 2x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not N, x is not C | two_c is natural, style is standard
  2N  "Asks: how good is the weak two?"   alert
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  forcing=round, ask=weak_two(x)
      artificial
  3x  "Preemptive raise: four-card support"    shows x>=4, hcp<=14
  4x  "Game in the fit"                        shows x>=4, hcp>=14
      when  x is H | x is S                    # with three, ask first
  P   "No interest"                            shows hcp<=14
      priority -5

# The default, and bba (probed 2026-09-24, weak-two-responses.notes.md). BBA reads a weak
# two as lighter when we are not vulnerable, and lightest at favourable:
# game with three-card support from 15 vulnerable, 16 at equal
# vulnerability not vulnerable (15 with four), 18 at favourable, 13 with
# five; 5D with three-card support and 18-20. The 2NT ask: over a major
# from 13 with support when vulnerable (and with four at love all), from
# 14 with a doubleton unless at favourable; otherwise from 15 with two or
# more, 18 with a singleton, and always with 20. The
# preemptive raise stops at 11. A new major is natural and forcing: over
# 2D six cards from 13, five with exactly 14; over 2H five
# spades from 13 with at most one heart (with two, 2NT).
after 2x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not N, x is not C | two_c is natural, style is not standard
  2N  "Asks: how good is the weak two?"   alert
      shows hcp>=13
      when  hcp>=20 | (x>=2, hcp>=15) | (x<=1, hcp>=18) | (x is H | x is S, x=2, hcp>=14, vul | !they.vul) | (x is H | x is S, x>=3, vul) | (x is H | x is S, x>=4, !they.vul)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=weak_two(x)
      artificial
  # Probed 2026-09-24 (notes): flat 0-4 with four trumps raises only at
  # love all; with a singleton and four trumps, game unless vulnerable.
  3x  "Preemptive raise: four-card support"    shows x>=4, hcp<=11, hcp>=5 | shortest<=1
  3x  "Preemptive raise: four-card support"   shows x>=4, hcp<=4
      when  !vul, !they.vul
  4x  "Preemptive game raise: four trumps and a singleton"   shows x>=4, shortest<=1, hcp<=9
      when  !vul
  4x  "Game in the fit"                        shows x>=3, hcp=15..19
      when  x is H | x is S
      when  vul | (!they.vul, hcp>=16 | x>=4) | hcp>=18
  4x  "Game with five-card support"            shows x>=5, hcp=13..19
      when  x is H | x is S
  # 3NT before five of the minor (Rick, 2026-09-27, ticket
  # basic-weak-2-b104): nine tricks instead of eleven, and it scores
  # more even with an overtrick. Diamond help and the side suits held;
  # a six-card major is bid instead. From 16: with 15 the 2NT ask finds
  # the minimum (notes).
  3N  "To play: 16+, help in diamonds, the side suits stopped"
      shows hcp>=16, x>=2, stop(S), stop(H), stop(C), H<=5, S<=5
      when  x is D
      priority 1
  5x  "Game in diamonds: three-card support, 18-20"   shows x>=3, hcp=18..20
      when  x is D
  2H  "Natural, forcing: 5+ hearts, 13+"   shows H>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is D, H>=6 | hcp=14
      sets  forcing=round
  2S  "Natural, forcing: 5+ spades, 13+"   shows S>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is D, S>=6 | hcp=14
      sets  forcing=round
  2S  "Natural, forcing: 5+ spades, 13+"   shows S>=5, hcp>=13, H<=1
      when  x is H
      sets  forcing=round
  P   "No interest"                            shows hcp<=19
      priority -5

# Opener after a new suit (default and bba). Raise with three, else rebid the suit.
after 2x (P) 2y (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, style is not standard
  4y  "Three-card support: game"   shows y>=3
      when  y is H | y is S
  3y  "Three-card support"                 shows y>=3
  3x  "No fit: rebid the suit"             shows y<=2

# Responder after opener rebids the suit (no three-card support).
# Probed 2026-09-25 (w2-2H-2S-3H, w2-2D-2H-3D, w2-2D-2S-3D): BBA passes
# up to about 18 unless it has seven of its major (game from 13), bids
# three of the major with six and 19+, and 3NT or four of opener's major
# from 20.
after 2x (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, style is not standard, y is H | y is S
  4y  "To play: 7+ {y}"   shows y>=7
  4y  "To play: 6+ {y}, four top honours"      shows y>=6, top5(y)>=4, hcp>=16
  3y  "Six-card suit, 19+: forcing, asks for a doubleton"   shows y>=6, hcp>=19
      sets  forcing=round
  4x  "Game in partner's suit: 20+"   shows hcp>=20
      when  x is H | x is S
  3N  "Game in notrump: 20+, no fit"               shows hcp>=20
      when  x is D
  P   "No game"          shows hcp<=19

after 2x (P) 2y (P) 3x (P) 3y (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, style is not standard, y is H | y is S
  4y  "A doubleton: game in partner's suit"        shows y>=2
  3N  "A singleton or void: 3NT"                   shows y<=1

# ── Opener's answer to 2NT ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Standard (Rick, 2026-09-24): with a maximum show a feature, an ace or
# king; without one a queen; a jack only with AK of the suit. 3NT is kept for AKQ in the
# suit. The minimum, or a maximum with nothing outside, rebids the suit.
# (bba: 3NT is a maximum with no side honour; below.)
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is feature, style is not bba
  3N  "Solid suit: AKQ"                            shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(Q,t)
      priority 1
  3C  "Feature: the club ace or king, maximum"     shows has(A,C) | has(K,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
  3D  "Feature: the diamond ace or king, maximum"  shows has(A,D) | has(K,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
  3H  "Feature: the heart ace or king, maximum"    shows has(A,H) | has(K,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
  3S  "Feature: the spade ace or king, maximum"    shows has(A,S) | has(K,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
  3C  "Maximum: the club queen, no side ace or king"      shows has(Q,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
      priority -1
  3D  "Maximum: the diamond queen, no side ace or king"   shows has(Q,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
      priority -1
  3H  "Maximum: the heart queen, no side ace or king"     shows has(Q,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
      priority -1
  3S  "Maximum: the spade queen, no side ace or king"     shows has(Q,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
      priority -1
  3C  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the club jack"     shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,C), hcp>=8   when t is not C
      priority -2
  3D  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the diamond jack"  shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,D), hcp>=8   when t is not D
      priority -2
  3H  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the heart jack"    shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,H), hcp>=8   when t is not H
      priority -2
  3S  "Maximum: AK of the suit and the spade jack"    shows has(A,t), has(K,t), has(J,S), hcp>=8   when t is not S
      priority -2
  3{t}  "Minimum, or nothing outside the suit"     shows hcp<=10
        priority -3

# bba: a maximum is 8-10; it shows a side ace, king (not singleton) or
# queen third, and bids 3NT without one. A minimum (5-7) rebids the suit.
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is feature, style is bba
  3C  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in clubs"      shows hcp>=8, has(A,C) | (has(K,C), C>=2) | (has(Q,C), C>=3)   when t is not C
  3D  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in diamonds"   shows hcp>=8, has(A,D) | (has(K,D), D>=2) | (has(Q,D), D>=3)   when t is not D
  3H  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in hearts"     shows hcp>=8, has(A,H) | (has(K,H), H>=2) | (has(Q,H), H>=3)   when t is not H
  3S  "Feature: 8-10, A, Kx or Qxx in spades"     shows hcp>=8, has(A,S) | (has(K,S), S>=2) | (has(Q,S), S>=3)   when t is not S
  3N  "Maximum: 8-10, no side feature"               shows hcp>=8
  3{t}  "Minimum, 5-7"                                      shows hcp<=7

# Ogust (bridgebum.com/ogust.php): a minimum is 5-7, a maximum 8-10
# (the feature answers' maximum too); a good suit two of the top three
# honours; 3NT all three. Until 2026-10-07 the split was 6/7, which sent
# every 7-count to the maximum answers (BBA: 7 is a minimum on all 77
# corpus boards) and game opposite it (notes).
when asked weak_two(t), ask2nt is ogust
  3C  "Ogust: minimum, poor suit"   shows hcp<=7, quality(t)<=1   artificial
  3D  "Ogust: minimum, good suit"   shows hcp<=7, quality(t)>=2   artificial
  3H  "Ogust: maximum, poor suit"  shows hcp>=8, quality(t)<=1   artificial
  3S  "Ogust: maximum, good suit"  shows hcp>=8, quality(t)>=2   artificial
  3N  "Ogust: the top three honours"      shows quality(t)=3
      priority 1

after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3N (P) 4x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is C | x is D, style is bba
  5x  "A shortness: game in the minor"   shows shortest<=1
  P   "No shortness: play four"          shows shortest>=2

# ── Responder after the answer: place the contract, never pass an
# artificial answer.
# bba: facing a maximum (anything but three of the suit) the 2NT asker
# bids game: four of a major, 3NT over a minor-suit feature. Over a 3NT
# answer to 2D it passes with 17+ and bids 4D with 15-16; opener then
# bids 5D with a singleton or void, and passes without.
when answered weak_two(t), style is bba, !partner.last=3{t}
  4{t}  "Game: to play"   shows hcp>=13
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority 1
  3N    "Game: to play"   shows hcp>=13
        when  t is C | t is D, !partner.last=3N
        priority 1
  P     "To play: 3NT"          shows hcp>=17
        when  t is C | t is D, partner.last=3N
        priority 1
  4{t}  "Doubt about 3NT: 15-16"         shows hcp<=16
        when  t is C | t is D, partner.last=3N
        priority 1

# Slam values with opener's suit as trump: 33 HCP on partner's floor
# (2026-09-27), or slam-entry's count with no two bare side suits.
define w2_slam(t) = hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33 | (fit_slam_values(t), !two_bare_beside(t))

# Partner's 3NT answer showed AKQ of the suit (Ogust, or the standard
# feature answers; bba's 3NT is a maximum with no side honour).
define w2_solid = partner.last=3N, ask2nt is ogust | style is not bba

# The ask: two trumps and the values, or a singleton opposite AKQ with
# 21 of mine and no five-card major of my own (Ogust 45, 271: a minor
# slam one trick short where my major or notrump made twelve).
define w2_fit_slam(t) = (t>=2, w2_slam(t)) | (w2_solid, t>=1, hcp>=21, S<=4 | t is S, H<=4 | t is H)

when answered weak_two(t)
  # Slam values opposite the answer (2026-09-27, ticket b201: 26 HCP
  # opposite a maximum with a feature stopped in 4H): agree the suit and
  # ask for keycards, with 33 HCP between us counting partner at the
  # floor of his answer.
  #
  # Slam after the answer (2026-10-09, notes "Slam after the answer"):
  # the 2NT ask is artificial, so no notrump has been bid, and opener's
  # six-card suit is the public fit: 4NT is keycard in it (Rick,
  # 2026-10-03: 4NT with no notrump bid is keycard, for the last suit
  # bid). The values are slam-entry's count (`fit_slam_values`) with two
  # or more trumps; opposite the AKQ answer (3NT, Ogust or the standard
  # feature treatment) a singleton is fit enough, and 21 of mine with the
  # 9 of AKQ make the 30 a minor slam needs.
  4N    "Keycard ask in {t}"          shows w2_fit_slam(t)
        when  rkcb
        sets  trump=t, ask=keycards(t)
        artificial
        priority 2
  4N    "Blackwood: aces, {t} agreed"  shows w2_fit_slam(t)
        when  aces, !rkcb
        sets  trump=t, ask=aces
        artificial
        priority 2
  # My own major, with no fit for partner's suit and slam interest
  # (2026-10-09): natural and forcing at the three level, below 3NT
  # (bridgebum: "rebids by the Ogust bidder are natural"). 27 between us
  # on partner's floor: 22 facing a minimum, 19 facing a maximum.
  # Opener raises with three; the raise agrees it and the keycard ask
  # follows (rkcb-1430.bid).
  3S    "Natural: five or more spades, slam interest"   shows S>=5, S>=H, t<=1, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 27
        when  t is not S, partner.last=3C | partner.last=3D | partner.last=3H
        sets  forcing=game
        priority 3
  3H    "Natural: five or more hearts, slam interest"   shows H>=5, H>S, t<=1, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 27
        when  t is not H, partner.last=3C | partner.last=3D
        sets  forcing=game
        priority 3
  4{t}  "Game in the weak two suit"   shows hcp>=17
        when  t is H | t is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"             shows hcp>=17
        when  t is C | t is D
  # Opposite a maximum game needs less (Rick, 2026-09-28, ticket
  # basic-weak-2-b278: 16 opposite 3C, a maximum with a club feature,
  # signed off in 3H). The answers record partner's range: counting him
  # at its floor, game with 21 between us, so every asker (13+) facing
  # a feature or an Ogust maximum (both 8-10); facing a minimum (4)
  # the 17 above still rules. 21 beat 22 and 23 on both
  # yardsticks (notes).
  4{t}  "Game: to play"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 21
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority 1
  3N    "Game: to play"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 21
        when  t is C | t is D
        priority 1
  P     "To play"
        when  partner.last=3{t}
  4{t}  "Sign off in {t}"    shows hcp<=16
        when  partner.last=3N, t is H | t is S
  3{t}  "Sign off in {t}"             shows hcp<=16
  3N    "To play in 3NT"   shows hcp<=16
        priority -1
  4{t}  "Sign off in {t}"       shows hcp<=16
        when  t is H | t is S
        priority -2
  P     "No game"                     shows hcp<=16
        priority -5

# Opener after responder's three of the suit over a higher answer: a
# sign-off, passed. BBA bid on over 2♦-2NT-3♣-3♦ in four Basic_Weak_2
# boards (3NT twice, 4♦, 5♦); passing was closer to par in three of them
# (notes, 2026-09-25).
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, y is not x
  P   "No further bid"

# Opener after responder's own major over the answer (2026-10-09): raise
# with three, which agrees it; else 3NT.
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, z is H | z is S, z is not x, y is not z
  4z  "Three-card support: agrees {z}"   shows z>=3
      sets  trump=z
  3N  "No support for {z}"               shows z<=2

# Responder after opener's 3NT, no support for my major: slam in
# notrump on 33 between us, game in my suit with six, else pass.
after 2x (P) 2N (P) 3y (P) 3z (P) 3N (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural, z is H | z is S, z is not x, y is not z
  6N  "Slam in notrump"   shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
  4z  "Six-card suit: game in it"        shows z>=6
  P   "To play"

# Opener after the preemptive raise: pass.
after 2x (P) 3x (P) when weak_two_suit(x), x is not C | two_c is natural
  P   "No further bid"

# weak-two-responses (`weak-two-responses.bid`): notes

Responses to a weak two, and opener's answer to the 2NT ask. Cases:
`weak-two-responses.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

Both treatments of the 2NT ask, chosen by the card field
`two_level.weak_two_2nt_response`:

- **feature** (the default): opener bids a side suit with the ace or king
  and a maximum, else three of the trump suit;
- **ogust**: 3♣ minimum/poor suit, 3♦ minimum/good suit, 3♥ maximum/poor,
  3♠ maximum/good, 3NT the top three honours.

BBA's import sets `ogust` when its Ogust switch is on (`[[derived]]`).

## Other choices

Responder: 2NT asks with 15+; four-card support raises (preemptive with a
minimum, game with 14+); with three-card support and a strong hand, ask
first. After the answer responder places the contract and never passes an
artificial one: game with 17+, otherwise three of the suit, 3NT when the
answer was higher, or four of a major.

## Gaps

- A new suit by responder at the four level after the answer (over
  3♠ or 3NT), and over a minor answer the other minor; slam with a
  singleton facing any answer but AKQ (2026-10-09, "Slam after the
  answer").

## BBA treatment (2026-09-24)

`general.style = bba`. Evidence: the Basic_* boards (responder's and
opener's hands against BBA's call) and `rbb probe` with the responder's
hand fixed, `--prefix "2H Pass"`, dealer South, two random layouts each
(both layouts always agreed), at each vulnerability; opener's answers
with both hands fixed, `--prefix "2S Pass 2NT Pass"`. Basic-Bridge card,
where the 2NT answer is the feature treatment.

**Responder over 2♥ depends on vulnerability** (probes; P pass, 2N the
ask, 4H game). "Vul" is responder's side:

| North | HCP | ♥ | love all | we vul, they not | favourable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AQ52.K95.J932.Q6 | 12 | 3 | P | P | P |
| AQ52.K95.Q932.Q6 | 13 | 3 | P | 2N | P |
| AQ52.K95.K932.Q6 | 14 | 3 | P | 2N | P |
| AQ52.K95.KJ93.Q6 | 15 | 3 | 2N | 4H | 2N |
| AQ52.K95.KJ93.K6 | 16 | 3 | 4H | 4H | 2N |
| AQ52.K95.KQ93.K6 | 17 | 3 | 4H | 4H | 2N |
| AQ52.A95.KQ93.K6 | 18 | 3 | 2N | 4H | 2N |
| AQ5.K952.J932.Q6 | 12 | 4 | P | P | P |
| AQ5.K952.Q932.Q6 | 13 | 4 | 2N | 2N | P |
| AQ5.K952.K932.Q6 | 14 | 4 | 2N | 2N | P |
| AQ5.K952.KJ93.Q6 | 15 | 4 | 4H | 4H | 2N |
| AQ5.K952.KJ93.K6 | 16 | 4 | 4H | 4H | 2N |
| AQ5.K952.KQ93.K6 | 17 | 4 | 4H | 4H | 2N |
| AQ52.K9.KJ932.Q6 | 15 | 2 | 2N | 2N | 2N |
| AQ52.K9.KQ932.K6 | 17 | 2 | 2N | 2N | 2N |
| AQ52.9.KQ932.KJ6 | 15 | 1 | P | P | P |
| AQ52.9.AQ932.KJ6 | 16 | 1 | 2N | 2N | 2N |

The first corpus boards that showed it: AK95.Q83.AK92.76,
AQ52.K95.KJ93.K6 and AJ94.AT6.K95.A62 bid 2NT at favourable and 4♥ at
love all, vulnerable and all vulnerable (10 layouts each). BBA plays the
weak two as lighter the less it risks, so responder needs more for game.

Corpus, responses to 2♥/2♠ (Basic_*): with a singleton, 15-17 passes 11
times and asks 5; four-card support raises to three at 10-11 (3 of 3)
and passes at 12 (5 of 5); five-card support bids game 4 times (13, 13,
16, 19 HCP) and asks 3 times (13, 14, 14). Over 2♦: 5♦ with three-card
support and 18-20 (4 boards); 13-14 with support passes where our 2NT
rule would ask (5 of 5, all with responder vulnerable); a six-card major
with 13+ is bid (18 of 19, the other 5♦); a five-card major with 15+
asks 24 times and is bid 3 times, with 13-14 passes 7 times and is bid
3 times.

**Opener's answer to 2NT** (Basic_*, all three suits, 131 boards): 5-7
rebids the suit (29 of 29, and no 8-10 hand rebids it); 8-10 shows a
side ace, a king that is not singleton, or a queen third (3♣/3♦/3♥/3♠;
55 answers, every one in such a suit), and bids 3NT without one (47
answers, none holding one: queen doubletons and a singleton king do not
count). Probes over 2♠: KQ7543.52.87.K32 3♣,
KQ7543.52.K7.832 3♦, AQ7543.53.87.Q32 3♣, AQ7543.53.Q87.32 3♦,
KQ7543.K.872.832 3NT, AK7543.52.87.832 (7) 3♠, KQ7543.52.87.832 (5) 3♠.

Responder then: facing a maximum in a major, game or a slam try 48
times, pass 5, three of the suit 4 (58 boards without a double); over
2♦-2NT-3NT it bids 4♦ with 15-16 (8 of 9, the ninth passes) and passes
with 17+ (10 of 11, the other 4NT with 22). Over 4♦ opener bids 5♦ with
a singleton or void (3 of 3) and passes 3 of the 5 hands without one
(Q8.98.AK9632.J92 and 93.JT5.AK9754.93 bid 5♦).

**The rules** (weak-two-responses.bid, style bba):
- after 2♦/2♥/2♠: 4M with three-card support and 15-19 vulnerable, 16
  at love all (15 with four), 18 at favourable; 4M with five from 13 (the
  corpus is split there); 5♦
  with three and 18-20; the 2NT ask over a major from 13 with support
  vulnerable, with four at love all, with a doubleton from 14 unless at
  favourable; otherwise 15 with two or more, 18 with a singleton, and
  always 20; the raise to three with four and up to 11; a new major
  natural and forcing (over 2♦ six cards from 13 or five with 14; over
  2♥ five spades from 13 and at most one heart); pass up to 19.
- after a new suit: raise with three (4M with 9+), else rebid the suit.
- the 2NT answer: 3{t} 5-7, a feature 8-10, 3NT 8-10 without one.
- after the answer: game facing a maximum; over 3NT (minor) pass 17+,
  4♦ 15-16; opener's 5♦ with a shortness.

All the probed responder hands agree with the engine except two:
AQ52.A95.KQ93.K6 (18 with three: BBA 2NT at love all, we bid 4♥; the
corpus has 18 with three bidding 4M 7 times of 8) and AQ52.9.AQ932.KJ6
(16 with a singleton: BBA 2NT, we pass, as BBA does on most corpus
singletons).

**Measured**, Basic_Weak_2 under the bba style, openings and responses
together (500 boards): calls agreeing 79.3% → 86.5%, identical auctions
22.2% → 45.0%, same contract 35.2% → 54.8%, par net −497 → −277 IMPs;
with NS bidding alone 82.0% → 89.3%, 26.4% → 53.0%, 40.1% → 61.3%. The
Basic_* and corpus totals are in preempts.notes.md; the responses took
Basic_* identical auctions from 37.9% to 39.8% and same contract from
47.7% to 49.0% after the opening rules.

The default is unchanged (the default contexts gained only `style is not
bba`; the bba rules keep the style in their context, and hand conditions
never share a `when` with it). Board-by-board check in preempts.notes.md.

**Gaps and open questions**
- Opener after a new-suit response: BBA uses the cheapest calls for
  hands with a doubleton (2♦-2♥-2♠ six times, 3♣ three), 3♦ with a
  void or singleton, and raises with three. Our rule only raises or
  rebids the suit; the corpus is too small (35 boards) to pin the
  meaning of 2♠ and 3♣ down.
- Over 2♦-2NT-3♥ (a heart feature) BBA bid 4♦ three times where we bid
  3NT; not modelled.
- Vulnerable, BBA's six-four minor preempts need a better suit
  (preempts.notes.md).
- **Question for Rick**: BBA asks with 13-14 and a fit when vulnerable
  and bids game with 15-16 and three trumps, but at favourable needs 18.
  Our default asks from 15 and bids game only with four. Worth a par
  test of the vulnerability split?

## Rick's rulings and more probes (2026-09-24)

**Feature answer, standard (now the default).** With a maximum (8-10 of
the 4-10 range) show a side ace or king; without one a queen; a jack only
with AK of the suit. 3NT is kept for AKQ in the suit. A minimum, or a
maximum with nothing to show, rebids the suit. BBA's "3NT = maximum with
no side honour" stays as the `bba` treatment. Ogust is the card's other
choice (`ask2nt`), to be filled in later.

**Vulnerability and scoring**, probed over 2H (South 73.KQJ964.853.72,
West's pass forced), responder 3-3-4-3 with three hearts:

| North | HCP | love all MP | love all IMP | we vul (MP = IMP) | favourable (MP = IMP) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K94.A85.KQ64.Q93 | 14 | P | P | P | P |
| K94.A85.KQ64.K93 | 15 | P | 2NT | 2NT | P |
| A94.A85.KQ64.K93 | 16 | 2NT | 2NT | 4H | 2NT |
| AQ4.A85.KQ64.K93 | 18 | 2NT | 4H | 4H | 2NT |
| AQ4.A85.AQ64.K93 | 19 | 4H | 4H | 4H | 4H |

Both the 2NT ask and the raise to game move with vulnerability; at love
all IMPs make BBA about a point bolder, otherwise MP and IMP agree. The
corpus is all matchpoints.

**Preemptive raises exist**, and move with vulnerability too (scoring
matters only on the last hand):

| North | HCP | love all | we vul | favourable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9852.T85.KQ64.J9 (3 trumps) | 6 | P | P | 3H |
| 985.T875.J642.98 (4, flat) | 1 | 3H | P | P |
| 9.T8752.K642.985 (5, singleton) | 3 | 3H | P | 3H |
| 9.T875.KQ64.J985 (4, singleton) | 6 | 4H | 3H | 4H |

| A9.T875.KQ64.J98 (4) | 10 | 3H | 3H | 4H MP / 3H IMP |

With four trumps and a singleton BBA preempts to game unless we are
vulnerable. The flat 1-count raising at love all and passing at
favourable is one probe and odd; to be checked with more hands before
the bba rules use it.

## Weak preemptive raises, more probes; BBA's responses become the default (2026-09-24)

Rick found the flat 1-count strange; nine more flat four-trump hands, 0-4
HCP, over the same 2H:

| North (four hearts, flat) | HCP | love all | we vul | favourable | both vul |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 985.T875.J642.98 | 1 | 3H | P | P | P |
| 986.T875.9642.98 | 0 | 3H | P | P | P |
| 9865.T875.964.98 | 0 | 3H | P | P | P |
| 986.T875.J64.985 (4-3-3-3) | 1 | P | P | P | P |
| Q86.T875.964.985 (4-3-3-3) | 2 | P | P | P | P |
| 986.T875.Q964.J8 | 3 | 3H | P | P | P |
| K86.T875.964.985 (4-3-3-3) | 3 | 3H | P | P | P |
| 9865.T875.J64.98 | 1 | 3H | P | P | P |
| 986.A875.964.985 (4-3-3-3) | 4 | 3H | P | P | P |

and with shortness:

| North | HCP | love all | we vul | favourable | both vul |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9.T875.KQ64.J985 (4, singleton) | 6 | 4H | 3H | 4H | 4H |
| 9.AT875.9642.985 (5, singleton) | 4 | 4H | 3H | 4H | 3H |
| 9.T8752.K642.985 (5, singleton) | 3 | 3H | P | 3H | P |
| 9.T875.9642.J985 (4, singleton) | 1 | 4H | 3H | 3H | 3H |
