It is real: flat four-trump weak hands raise only at love all (4-3-3-3
with 1-2 HCP excepted), and pass at every other vulnerability, even
favourable. A singleton with four trumps always raises; the level is
not a clean function of HCP and vulnerability. Modelled simply: flat
0-4 raises at love all; a singleton and four trumps, up to 9 HCP, goes
to game unless vulnerable; 5+ HCP with four trumps raises to three as
before. Few corpus hands are affected (+1 IMP).

**Par test of BBA's responses as the default** (the 2NT ask, raises and
game by vulnerability, forcing new suits; opener's answers stay the
standard feature ones): corpus -168,198 -> -167,745 (+453), Basic_* +78,
uncontested +75, Basic_Weak_2 -439 -> -361. Adopted; the previous
responses (2NT from 15, raises with four) are the `standard` treatment.

## Responder after 2x-2M-3x (2026-09-25)

The most frequent "no rule" position in Basic_* N/S auctions (27 of 203
positions): opener rebid the suit over responder's forcing major, and
responder had nothing to say. Probed with 300 random responders each
(5+ in the major, 13-21 HCP; opener six of its suit, at most two of the
major), at love all and all vulnerable: `probes/w2-2H-2S-3H.toml`,
`w2-2D-2H-3D.toml`, `w2-2D-2S-3D.toml`.

BBA passes most hands up to 18-19 HCP. It bids game with a seven-card
major from 13 (and a six-card suit with four of the top five honours
from about 16), three of the major with six and 19+ (forcing: opener
bids 4M with a doubleton, 3NT without), and 3NT or four of opener's
major with 20+. Over 3♦ it sometimes raises to 4♦ with 16-20 and a
doubleton, which opener mostly passes; not modelled.

Our rules follow that. Agreement with BBA on the grids: 92-95%, the rest
mostly BBA passing a few 19-counts where we bid. Basic_* N/S: no-rule
positions 203 -> 176, vs BBA +21 IMPs, +47 to the side that changed its
call (7 boards).

## Opener after responder signs off following the answer (2026-09-25)

2x-2NT-3y-3x (y above x's three-level) is a sign-off, and opener now
passes it explicitly (it passed before by default, with no rule). BBA
bid on over 2♦-2NT-3♣-3♦ in four Basic_Weak_2 boards (73: 5♦, 109 and
431: 3NT, 282: 4♦); against par, passing 3♦ was better on 109, 282
and 431 (+370, +210, +330 NS) and worse on 73 (150 against 400). Par
decides: kept as a sign-off. No-rule positions 176 -> 143.

## 3NT before 5♦ over a weak 2♦ (Rick, 2026-09-27; ticket basic-weak-2-b104)

Basic_Weak_2 board 104: 2♦ P with AK.AK985.JT2.A74 bid 5♦ (the
BBA-derived "three-card support, 18-20") and went down; 3NT makes ten
tricks. Rick: over a weak 2♦ strongly prefer 3NT to 5m, with something
in diamonds and the unbid suits stopped. Now 3NT with 16+, two or more
diamonds, every side suit stopped and no six-card major, ranked above
5♦.

| variant | full corpus (par / side) | Basic_* (par / side) |
|---|---|---|
| 14+ | +79 / +58 | |
| 15+ | +138 / +167 | -13 / -10 |
| 15+, no six-card major | +139 / +181 | +2 / +11 |
| 16+, no six-card major | +126 / +202 | +10 / +26 |
| 17+, no six-card major | +59 / +119 | +2 / +18 |

16 kept: better on three of the four figures, 13 IMPs behind 15 by par
on the corpus. The Basic_* losses at 15 were hands where the 2NT ask
would have found opener's minimum and stopped in 3♦, and hands with a
six-card heart suit.

On the same board BBA answered the 2NT ask with 3NT on KQ8764 and Q3:
BBA's maximum with no side honour (the `bba` treatment), which our
default reads as AKQ. Our default answer is 3♥, the heart queen with a
maximum, and responder then bids 3NT. No change needed there.

## Slam after the 2NT ask (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-weak-2-b201: 2H 2NT 3S (maximum), North AKJT86.AJ.AK8.AQ
bid 4H. Responder now agrees the weak-two suit and asks with 4NT
(keycards on 1430/0314 cards, aces on standard-Blackwood cards) when
his HCP plus partner's floor reach 33: +308 par, +832 side IMPs (70
boards). The board now reaches 6H.

**Open, for Rick: counting tricks for the grand.** BBA reached 7H via
5NT; Rick counts 14 top tricks for 7NT. `grand_try` is still the
placeholder "35 HCP between us, partner at his floor" (34 here). A
real evaluator would count sure tricks: my suits' top cards with
partner's known honours and length, plus the aces and kings the asks
have located. That wants a design (what partner's answers pin down,
how a long suit with a known fit counts), not a one-off rule.

## Game opposite a maximum answer (Rick, 2026-09-28; ticket basic-weak-2-b278)

Basic_Weak_2 board 278: 2H P 2NT P 3C P, North AJ94.AT6.K95.A62 (16)
signed off in 3H; BBA bid 4H. Rick: with 16 and opener showing a
maximum, responder should normally bid game. The only game rule was
`hcp>=17` whatever the answer, which is right opposite a minimum (4-10)
and too much opposite a feature (8-10).

Now responder counts partner at the floor of his answer: game with
`hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 21` (four of the major, 3NT over a minor),
ranked above the sign-offs. Facing a feature (8+) every 2NT asker (13+)
bids game, and facing an Ogust maximum (8+ since 2026-10-07; it was 7+,
so game from 14); facing a minimum (4)
the old 17 is unchanged.

| combined threshold | full corpus vs BBA | side IMPs | par-distance (sideimps) | boards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | -115,452 | | | |
| 20 (also 16 facing a minimum) | -114,591 (+861) | +1051 | +861 | 330 |
| **21** | **-114,604 (+848)** | **+1054** | **+848** | 284 |
| 22 | -114,659 (+793) | +975 | +793 | 261 |
| 23 | -114,976 (+476) | +550 | +476 | 128 |

21 adopted: 20 is 13 IMPs better by par and 3 worse by side IMPs, so
the yardsticks disagree on lowering the minimum case to 16; not taken.
The gains are over 2H (+472 side, 119 boards) and 2S (+559, 158).

**BBA probes** (`probes/w2-2H-2N-3C.toml`, `probes/w2-2H-2N-3H.toml`:
200 responders each, 13-17 HCP with two or three hearts, opener 6-card
hearts, 8-10 or 4-7; love all and NS vulnerable, MP and IMP). Over the
3C feature BBA bids 4H with 15+ almost always, with 14 about half the
time and with 13 about a quarter (MP 12 of 63, IMP 19 of 63); heart
length does not split it. So BBA wants about 14 opposite a feature;
the corpus par says game from 13, and par decides. Over the 3H minimum
BBA passes up to 14, and with 15-17 bids game about a quarter of the
time at love all and half or more with NS vulnerable, where our rule
waits for 17: left alone here (not part of the ticket; a candidate for
a later par test).

## Ogust ranges (2026-10-07, convention score)

The convention score (`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only ogust`, the Ogust
scenario, NS with Ogust on and off) was poor: Rusty's gain -79, BBA's
+229, net -0.81 per changed board (379 boards). Cause: our Ogust split
minimum and maximum at 6/7 HCP, so every 7-count answered 3♥/3♠
(maximum), and responder, counting partner at 7, bid game opposite a
minimum (Ogust 394: J3.T5.AJT874.J76 answered 3♥ and North bid 3NT,
down; BBA 3♦, passed). The source (bridgebum.com/ogust.php) says bad
hand 5-7, good hand 8-10, a good suit two of the top three honours,
3NT the good hand with all three; BBA, Ogust corpus: 7 HCP minimum on
all 77 boards, 8+ maximum on all 140, every AKQ suit 3NT (61). Now
minimum `hcp<=7`, maximum `hcp>=8` (as the feature answers' maximum),
and 3NT ranked above 3♠ for AKQ. Game facing a maximum (21 between us)
now comes from 13 again, as facing a feature.

| | Rusty's gain | BBA's gain | net / changed board | halves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | -79 | +229 | -0.81 (379) | agree |
| after | -22 | +229 | -0.67 (373) | agree (-157/-94) |

Background (Ogust scenario, vs BBA by par): +17 -> +24. Most of what is
left is BBA's own off run (its feature answers) doing worse than ours:
on the changed boards where our auction did not change BBA gains +190.
BBA counts AJT as a good suit (3♠/3♦, 17 boards) and KJT/QJT as poor;
the source counts only A, K, Q, so AJT stays poor here.

## Slam after the answer (2026-10-09, Rick: "start on the 4NTs")

The Ogust convention score's worst boards (45, 102, 114) stopped in
3NT after the answer with 22-25 HCP opposite. After the 2NT ask our
responder never went past game: the only slam rule asked with 33 HCP on
opener's floor and two trumps (25 opposite a maximum, 28 opposite a
minimum), and on the Ogust corpus no 2NT auction reached slam at all.
The big responder hands are short in opener's suit (the scenario's
weak twos are mostly 2♦), so most of the missed slams (46 boards where
twelve tricks made) need either the solid suit or responder's own suit.

**Decisions**
- **4NT is keycard in opener's suit.** The 2NT ask is artificial, so
  our side has bid no notrump, and opener's six-card suit is shown
  (`shown_fit`); Rick's rule (2026-10-03, rkcb-1430.notes.md "The
  keycard suit") makes 4NT keycard for it. So 4NT here is never
  quantitative; there is no quantitative 4NT after the ask. No source
  found that says otherwise (bridgebum's Ogust page only says "rebids
  by the Ogust bidder are natural"; Neil Timm's Ogust handout covers
  game only).
- **With two or more trumps** the ask needs slam-entry's count
  (`fit_slam_values`: 31 on opener's floor for the support hand, or 32
  on his maximum with four losers or fewer, his range seven wide or
  less) and no two bare side suits, or the old 33 HCP on his floor.
- **A singleton opposite the AKQ answer** (3NT, Ogust or the standard
  feature answer; not bba's 3NT, which is a maximum without a feature):
  the ask with 21 HCP, the 9 of AKQ making the 30 a minor slam needs.
  Corpus, 3NT answer and a singleton: twelve tricks in the suit on 7 of
  8 boards at 21+, 3 of 7 at 19-20. Not with a five-card major of my
  own: on 45 and 271 the minor slam made eleven where the major or
  notrump made twelve.
- **No ask with a singleton facing any other answer**: at 19-23 HCP
  opposite 3♥/3♠ twelve tricks made on about half the boards.
- **Responder's own major**: natural and forcing at the three level
  over a lower answer (3♥ over 3♣/3♦, 3♠ over 3♣/3♦/3♥), with five or
  more, a singleton or void in opener's suit, and 27 HCP on opener's
  floor (22 facing a minimum, 19 facing a maximum). Opener raises to
  four with three (which agrees the suit; the keycard ask follows from
  rkcb-1430.bid), else bids 3NT; responder then bids 6NT on 33 HCP,
  four of his suit with six, else passes.
- **No-fit quantitative slam by HCP**: not written. On 102 (25 HCP
  opposite a maximum, a singleton queen) 6NT makes ten tricks: a weak
  two's values are in a suit responder cannot reach. Only the 6NT
  after opener's 3NT denial above.

**Measured** (`conv_ab.py --only ogust --reuse-bba`, contract errors
for NS):

| | Rusty's gain | BBA's gain | net / changed board | halves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | -22 | +229 | -0.67 (373) | agree (-157/-94) |
| after | -50 | +229 | -0.75 (373) | agree (-157/-122) |

The convention score falls because the continuations serve both of our
runs: our Ogust run gains 83 IMPs of contract errors (13 boards changed:
13, 76, 109, 114, 121, 212, 278, 302 to slam), our feature run 111 (19
boards; with the feature answers 3♠ stays free for responder's spades
over a 3♥ feature, 415 reaching 6♠). The Ogust background (our side
against par) improves by those amounts; what the score measures, Ogust
against the feature ask, does not.

**Random deals** (BBA-bid Pavlicek 100,000, 21GF both sides, so the
feature ask; `.rbb-cache/random/`, base rules from main against these):
25 boards changed, contract errors on them 287 -> 139 (NS 108 -> 23, EW
179 -> 116), +148 IMPs, halves +93/+55. 21 better (missed slams bid,
mostly after a keycard ask in a major), 1 level, 3 worse: 93382 (6♠
down, -14: 15 HCP and a doubleton facing 3♥, two quick club losers),
41375 (-3), 31728 (0).

**Tripwire** (`compare --limit 50`, all scenarios): 6 of 17,105 boards
changed, all in the weak-two scenarios and Preempt_Keycard (Weak_2_Bids
32 and Preempt_Keycard 49 to 6♥, Lax_Leveled 39 to 6♦, Ogust 10 and 13).

## Sources

- **The conventions:** the 2NT feature ask, standard practice, not yet
  cited. Ogust: bridgebum.com/ogust.php (3♣ 5-7 one top honour, 3♦ 5-7
  two, 3♥ 8-10 one, 3♠ 8-10 two, 3NT 8-10 all three; "rebids by the
  Ogust bidder are natural"); the PBS Ogust scenario's chat cites the
  same page. Neil H. Timm, "OGUST and Modified OGUST"
  (bridge-tips.co.il, 2022): the answers, game decisions only.
- **Slam after the answer** (2026-10-09): 4NT keycard in opener's suit
  from Rick's keycard-suit rule (2026-10-03) and the fit-vs-agreement
  rule (opener's six-card suit is public); thresholds from slam-entry
  (`fit_slam_values`) and the Ogust corpus (21 opposite AKQ); the
  natural new major below 3NT and opener's raise, standard practice,
  not yet cited.
- **Rick's rulings:** both treatments of the 2NT ask, chosen by the card
  (2026-09-22); the standard feature answer as the default (2026-09-24);
  BBA's responses become the default after a par test, the old ones kept
  as the `standard` treatment (2026-09-24); 3NT before 5♦ over a weak 2♦
  (2026-09-27, ticket basic-weak-2-b104); game opposite a maximum answer
  (2026-09-28, ticket basic-weak-2-b278). Ticket basic-weak-2-b201
  (slam after the ask, 2026-09-27).
- **BBA probes:** `rbb probe` with responder's hand fixed over 2♥ and with
  both hands fixed over `2S Pass 2NT Pass`, at each vulnerability
  (2026-09-24, hands in the tables); `probes/w2-2H-2S-3H.toml`,
  `probes/w2-2D-2H-3D.toml`, `probes/w2-2D-2S-3D.toml` (2026-09-25);
  `probes/w2-2H-2N-3C.toml`, `probes/w2-2H-2N-3H.toml` (2026-09-28).
- **BBA evidence:** the Basic_* boards, Basic_Weak_2 in particular.
- **Corpus measurements:** the par test of BBA's responses (+453), the
  sign-off pass, slam after the ask (+308), the game threshold table
  (21 adopted), judged by par and by side IMPs.
- **Where we differ:** AJT is a poor suit for our Ogust answers (the
  source), a good one for BBA's; we pass 2x-2NT-3y-3x, where BBA sometimes bids on
  (par decides); game opposite a feature from 13 where BBA wants about 14;
  the vulnerability split for asking is a question for Rick.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# XYZ (Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge #587; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/xyz): after three one-level bids, 1x-1y-1z,
# responder's 2♣ relays to 2♦ (every invitational hand starts here, and a
# weak hand with diamonds passes 2♦), 2♦ is an artificial game force, and
# 2NT relays to 3♣ (weak with clubs). Other calls are natural and weak or
# as before (responder-rebids.bid). After 1x-1y-1NT the same structure is
# two-way New Minor Forcing, which two-way-nmf.bid plays when this card
# field is on. The relay and game-force answers are two-way-nmf.bid's
# (`xy_relay`, `xy_clubs`, `xy_gf`). See xyz.notes.md.

module xyz "XYZ: 2♣ relay and 2♦ game force after three one-level bids"
  kind   convention
  card   bidding_conventions/xyz
  needs  two-way-nmf
  skill  bidding_conventions/xyz

after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) when !tw(x)
  2C  "XYZ: relay to 2♦, invitational or a diamond sign-off"   alert
      shows points=11..12 | (points<=10, D>=6 | (x is D, D>=4, z<=2))
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_relay
      artificial
      priority 2
  2D  "XYZ: artificial game force"   alert
      shows points>=13
      sets  forcing=game, ask=xy_gf
      artificial
      priority 2
  2N  "XYZ: relay to 3♣, a club sign-off"   alert
      shows points<=10, C>=6 | (x is C, C>=5, z<=2)
      sets  forcing=round, ask=xy_clubs
      artificial
      priority 2

# ── After the 2♦ relay: weak with diamonds passes, every other call invites
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) 2C (P) 2D (P) when !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 2♦"                      shows points<=10
  2y  "Invitational: five {y}"             shows y=5, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(y)
      when  y is H | y is S
  3y  "Invitational: six {y}"              shows y>=6, points=11..12   sets ask=invite(y)
  3z  "Invitational raise: four {z}"       shows z>=4, tp(z)=11..12   sets ask=invite(z)
  2N  "Invitational, balanced"             shows points=11..12, z<=3   sets ask=nt_invite
      priority -1
  3x  "Invitational: four {x}"             shows x>=4, points=11..12, z<=3   sets ask=invite(x)
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority -2
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when !tw(x)
  P   "To play in 3♣"                      shows C>=4

# xyz (`xyz.bid`): notes

XYZ (`other_conventions.xyz`): after three one-level bids responder's
2♣ relays to 2♦ (invitations, or weak with diamonds), 2♦ is an
artificial game force, 2NT relays to 3♣ (weak with clubs). After
1x-1y-1NT the same structure is two-way NMF: `two-way-nmf.bid` now has
no `card` line and plays when either `other_conventions.two_way_nmf` or
`other_conventions.xyz` is set (NMF, its natural 2♣/2♦ and the direct
invitations stand aside for both). Cases: `xyz.test`. Scenario: XYZ
(BBA on 21GF-DEFAULT without XYZ; with `--set other_conventions.xyz=true`
no problems in our auctions at the convention's calls, 50 boards,
2026-10-05).

## Structure

- 2♣ relay: 11-12, or weak with six diamonds (or four diamonds and a
  doubleton in opener's second suit after 1♦-1♥-1♠). Opener always
  answers 2♦ (two-way-nmf.bid's `xy_relay`); responder passes, or
  invites: 2y with five (a major), 3y with six, 3z with four of opener's
  second suit, 2NT balanced, 3 of opener's minor with four.
- 2♦ game force: answered as two-way NMF's (`xy_gf`): three of
  responder's major, else 2NT; responder places the contract.
- 2NT: weak with six clubs (or five and a doubleton in opener's second
  suit after 1♣); responder passes 3♣.
- Natural calls kept: 1NT, the raises of opener's second suit (2z weak,
  3z invitational), 2y with a weak six-card major, 1♠ over 1♣-1♦-1♥.
  Taken by XYZ: 2♣ and 2♦ (preference, the weak diamonds, the natural 2♣
  after 1♦-1♥-1♠), 2NT, the direct 3y invitation.
- Priority 2: ahead of fourth suit forcing (fourth-suit-forcing.bid),
  which still applies after a two-level rebid.

## Gaps and questions for Rick

- Todd lets opener break the 2♣ relay with a good 15-17; we always
  answer 2♦ (as two-way NMF). Decision: keep the relay forced.
- Every game-forcing hand goes through 2♦, even with four of opener's
  second major (4z directly would be natural); the answers find the fit.
- Some play XYZ's 2NT as natural invitational (Todd); we use the 3♣
  relay, matching two-way NMF and the convention-card summary
  ("extending two-way checkback").

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only xyz-vs-nmf`.
IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer;
"actor" is the side that made the first differing call. Against New
Minor Forcing (on in both runs), XYZ: 248 boards changed; actor contract
-28, double-dummy -15, halves +15/-43 (z -0.7): neutral.

## Sources

- **Robert S. Todd, "XYZ", Adventures in Bridge #587**
  (https://www.advinbridge.com/this-week-in-bridge/587): the four
  auctions, 2♣ relay (invitational), 2♦ game forcing, continuations after
  the relay. convention-card `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/xyz.toml`
  cites it.
- **Where we differ:** 2NT is the clubs relay (as two-way NMF, Bridge
  Winners "xyNT") rather than Todd's natural 2NT; the relay cannot be
  broken.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Advancer: partner has overcalled, and it is our turn.
#
# Ranges follow BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which are the usual ones.
# Over a one-level overcall a raise is 7-11 total points with three-card
# support, a new suit 8+ with four cards at the one level and 9+ with
# five at the two, 1NT 8-11 balanced with a stopper in their suit, and
# the cue bid of their suit a limit raise or better (12+ with three).
# The jump raise is weak. With `overcalls.responses.jump_cuebid_mixed`
# the jump cue bid is a mixed raise: four trumps, 7-9 support points.
#
# An overcall is not forcing, so advancer passes with less; there is no
# forced bid here as there is after a takeout double.
#
# The file then covers, in order: advancer when RHO does not pass, the
# balancing overcall (partner is 8-15 there, so everything costs about
# two points more), the two-level overcall — simple or a weak jump, and
# they need different answers — advancer over RHO's 1NT, and the
# overcaller's reply to the cue-bid raise.
#
# Not written yet (beyond the rebid after a new suit, at the end):
# advancer's continuations once the overcaller has
# rebid, and the support cue bid.
#
# Advancing a 1NT overcall needs nothing here: systems are on, and the
# notrump modules carry the `(1x) 1N (P)` spelling of their patterns.

module advances "Advancing partner's overcall"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/advancing_overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/support_cuebids
  skill  competitive_bidding/mixed_raise
  param  jump_raise = overcalls.responses.jump_raise default weak
  param  mixed      = competitive_bidding/mixed_raise default false

after (1x) 1y (P)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
      when  jump_raise is weak
  1S  "8+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  1N  "8-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      when  y<=2 | y is C | y is D
  cheapest(C) "9+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(D) "9+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(H) "9+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  2{x} "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  # A five-card major that can be shown at the one level comes first
  # (Rick, 2026-11-09: the Brill field bid 1H, 8 of 8, with
  # QT6.A8643.J9.KJ5 over 1C 1D Pass). Over a 1S overcall 2NT stays:
  # 2H there measured worse (3 boards, -24 IMPs).
  2N  "12-15 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp+length_points<=15, H<=4 | y is S, S<=4
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  3{x} "Mixed raise: 4+ {y}, 7-9 support points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=4, tp(y)=7..9
      when   mixed, !vul
      sets   ask=mixed_raise(y)
      priority 2                        # ahead of the raise to two and the preemptive raise, which these hands also fit
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancing a balancing overcall ───────────────────────────────────
# Partner reopened, so he is 8-15 rather than 8-17 and some of his values
# are borrowed from us: everything costs about two points more than in
# the direct seat. BBA's Balancing meanings: the raise 9-11, 1NT 10-11,
# a new suit at the one level 7-9, the cue bid 13+.
after (1x) P (P) 1y (P)
  2{y} "Raise: 9-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp+length_points<=11
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: four-card support, under 9 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=8
      when  jump_raise is weak
  1S  "7+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  1N  "10-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      when  y<=2 | y is C | y is D
  cheapest(C) "11+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(D) "11+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(H) "11+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  2{x} "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=13
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  2N  "13-15 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  P   "Not enough to advance a reopening bid"  priority -10

# ── Advancer when RHO does not pass ──────────────────────────────────
# RHO has doubled or bid over the overcall. Support is still the first
# thing to show, and raising at once takes bidding room from them.
after (1x) 1y (X) | (1x) P (P) 1y (X)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

after (1x) 1y (1z) | (1x) P (P) 1y (1z)
  2{y} "Raise: 8-11 with three {y}, up to 11 with four"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=11, hcp+length_points>=8 | y>=4
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: five {y}, four at favourable; under 8 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(y)          # one trump more than the Law for a weak hand (total-tricks.bid)
      priority 1                        # before the raise to two, which a weak four-card hand also fits
  1N  "8-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  cheapest(S) "Free bid: 9+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not S, y is not S, z is not S
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: 9+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H, z is not H
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# The mixed raise holds over RHO's double or one-level bid too (BBA's
# `Mixed raise` switch plays it there and only there: advances.notes.md,
# "Mixed raise"). The direct seat only: a balancing
# overcall's ranges are two points higher. Not vulnerable only, in both
# places: BBA's limit, and the jump to three vulnerable drew the
# penalty doubles (contract errors -100 -> +4 in the self A/B).
after (1x) 1y (X) | (1x) 1y (1z)
  3{x} "Mixed raise: 4+ {y}, 7-9 support points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=4, tp(y)=7..9
      when   mixed, !vul
      sets   ask=mixed_raise(y)
      priority 2                        # ahead of the raise to two and the preemptive raise, which these hands also fit

after (1x) 1y (2z) | (1x) P (P) 1y (2z)
  2{y} "Raise: 7-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=11
  3{y} "Raise: four-card support, 8-11 total points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancing a two-level overcall ───────────────────────────────────
# `(*)` is any call by RHO, so this covers the seat however he has
# answered the overcall, and passing is much the commonest advance.
#
# `y is not x` throughout: their opening bid repeated by partner would
# be a cue bid (Michaels), not an overcall.
after (1x) 2y (*) | (1x) P (P) 2y (*) when y is not x
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# Advancer bids only while RHO has left him room: his pass, his double,
# or his simple raise of their own suit. Once RHO has bid a suit of his
# own, or notrump, or jumped, BBA's advancer passes, and so do we — the
# context above is then the only one that matches. A two-level overcall
# in the balancing seat is passed out for the same reason.

# A weak jump overcall is a six-card suit, so three-card support is nine
# trumps and the raise is a further preempt: partner is not invited to
# do anything. The `when` is the complement of the simple-overcall one
# below: "y could have been bid at the one level over x".
after (1x) 2y (P) | (1x) 2y (X) | (1x) 2y (2x) when y is not x, x is C | (x is D, y is not C) | (x is H, y is S)
  4{y} "Raise to game: four-card support, 11+"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: three-card support, under 11 points"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Preemptive raise: four-card support, under 11 points"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  y is C | y is D

# The rest only when the overcall was a *simple* two-level overcall,
# where partner has 12-17 and an opening hand to go with it. The `when`
# spells out "y could not have been bid at the one level over x": over
# 1C every two-level suit is a jump, over 1D only clubs is simple, over
# 1H everything but spades, and over 1S all three.
after (1x) 2y (P) | (1x) 2y (X) | (1x) 2y (2x) when y is not x, x is S | (x is H, y is not S) | (x is D, y is C)
  4{y} "Raise to game in partner's major: four-card support, 13+"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  y is H | y is S
  3{y} "Raise: 7-10 total points, four-card support"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=10
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(x), y<=2
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "12+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "12+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C

# ── Advancer over RHO's 1NT ──────────────────────────────────────────
# `after (1x) 1y (1z)` binds a suit, so RHO's 1NT left advancer with no
# rule at all. Support is still the first thing to show.
after (1x) 1y (1N) | (1x) P (P) 1y (1N)
  2{y} "Raise: 9-11 total points, three-card support"
      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp+length_points<=11
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  y>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=round, ask=cue_raise(y)
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── The overcaller answers advancer's cue bid ────────────────────────
# The cue showed three-card support and a limit raise or better, so the
# overcall's own range decides: a minimum signs off in the suit, and
# 13+ total points bids the game. Written against the question, so it is
# the same rule whatever level the cue was made at.
when asked cue_raise(t)
  4{t} "Accepts: game in {t}"
      shows hcp+length_points>=13
      when  t is H | t is S
  3N  "Accepts: 13+ balanced, game in notrump"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  t is C | t is D
  cheapest(t) "Minimum: signs off"
      priority -1

# Over the mixed raise (7-9 support points, four trumps): game wants
# about 25, so 16 or more bids it; else three of the suit, which the jump
# cuebid always leaves room for over a one-level overcall.
after (1x) 1y (P) 3x (P) | (1x) 1y (X) 3x (P) | (1x) 1y (1z) 3x (P)
  4{y} "Accepts: game in {y}"
      shows hcp+length_points>=16
      when  mixed, y is H | y is S
  3N  "Accepts: 16+ balanced, game in notrump"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=16, stop(x)
      when  mixed, y is C | y is D
  3{y} "Minimum: signs off"
      when  mixed
      priority -1

# ── The overcaller's rebid after a new suit (2026-09-25) ──────────────
# Advancer's new suit is not forcing. No rules existed (~90 corpus
# boards where BBA bid). BBA: raise with four, rebid a six-card suit,
# 1NT with 11-14 balanced and their suit held; otherwise pass.
after (1x) 1y (P) 1z (P)
  2{z} "Four-card support"                   shows z>=4
  2{y} "Six or more {y}"                     shows y>=6, z<=3
      priority -1
  1N  "11-14 balanced, {x} held"             shows balanced, hcp>=11, hcp<=14, stop(x), z<=3
  P   "No further bid"                  priority -5
after (1x) 1y (P) 2z (P)
  3{z} "Four-card support"                   shows z>=4, hcp>=11
  2{y} "Six or more {y}"                     shows y>=6, z<=3
      when  y is not C
      priority -1
  P   "No further bid"                  priority -5

# The overcaller again after (1x) 1y (2x) P (P): BBA rebids a six-card
# suit with 12+ (2026-09-25). It also doubles for takeout with a
# singleton in their suit and 13+; that double cost IMPs against par.
# The rebid is at the two level: a one-level overcall outranks their
# suit, so 2{y} is always there, and 3{y} was a jump. On bare SAYC BBA
# rebids 2{y} with six from 10 HCP (2026-10-02, 88 hands).
after (1x) 1y (2x) P (P)
  2{y} "Competes: six or more {y}"           shows y>=6, hcp>=10
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5

# ── Advancing from the sandwich seat ─────────────────────────────────
# Partner came in after (1x) P (1y) (overcalls.bid, 2026-10-07). I have
# passed once, and both of them have bid: raise with support, compete to
# the three level with four, preempt with four and a weak hand. A new
# suit or notrump is not written: a passed hand with neither support
# nor a fit passes.
after (1x) P (1y) 1z (*) | (1x) P (1y) 2z (*) when z is not x, z is not y
  cheapest(z) "Raise: three-card support, 7+ total points"
      shows z>=3, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  cheapest_rank(z)<=13                 # the two level
  cheapest(z) "Competitive raise to three: four-card support"
      shows z>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  cheapest_rank(z)>=15, cheapest_rank(z)<=18
  jump(z) "Preemptive raise: four-card support, weak"
      shows z>=4, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows weak_jump_raise(z)                   # total-tricks.bid
      when  cheapest_rank(z)<=13, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
      priority 1
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# Partner's takeout double of the two suits they have not bid: answer in
# the longer (a major with equal length), a jump with 9-11 and four
# cards, 1NT with both their suits stopped and nothing to bid, else the
# longer unbid suit however short.
after (1x) P (1y) X (P) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Answers the double: four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H | y is H, S>=D | x is D | y is D, S>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Answers the double: four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, H>S | x is S | y is S, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Answers the double: four or more diamonds"
      shows D>=4, D>S | x is S | y is S, D>H | x is H | y is H, D>=C | x is C | y is C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Answers the double: four or more clubs"
      shows C>=4, C>S | x is S | y is S, C>H | x is H | y is H, C>D | x is D | y is D, hcp<=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  jump(S) "Jump answer: four or more spades, 9-11"
      shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H | y is H, hcp>=9
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Jump answer: four or more hearts, 9-11"
      shows H>=4, H>S | x is S | y is S, hcp>=9
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(D) "Jump answer: four or more diamonds, 9-11"
      shows D>=4, D>S | x is S | y is S, D>H | x is H | y is H, hcp>=9
      when  x is not D, y is not D, cheapest_rank(D)<=13
  jump(C) "Jump answer: four or more clubs, 9-11"
      shows C>=4, C>S | x is S | y is S, C>H | x is H | y is H, C>D | x is D | y is D, hcp>=9
      when  x is not C, y is not C, cheapest_rank(C)<=13
  1N  "6-10, both their suits stopped"
      shows hcp>=6, hcp<=10, stop(x), stop(y)
      priority -1
  # The forced answer without four cards: the longer unbid suit.
  cheapest(S) "Answers the double: three spades"
      shows S>=3, S>=H | x is H | y is H, S>=D | x is D | y is D, S>=C | x is C | y is C
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Answers the double: three hearts"
      shows H>=3, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      priority -3
  cheapest(D) "Answers the double: the longer unbid suit"
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      priority -4
  cheapest(C) "Answers the double: the longer unbid suit"
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      priority -5

after (1x) P (1y) X (*) when y is not x, !rho.last=P
  cheapest(S) "Free bid: four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not S, y is not S, cheapest_rank(S)<=13
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, S<=H | x is S | y is S, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not H, y is not H, cheapest_rank(H)<=13
  cheapest(D) "Free bid: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not D, y is not D, cheapest_rank(D)<=13
  cheapest(C) "Free bid: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=7
      when  x is not C, y is not C, cheapest_rank(C)<=13
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── Advancer after partner's overcall of their 1NT ───────────────────
# The overcall is five cards and 12+ total points (overcalls.bid); RHO
# has 15-17. Advancer passes (added 2026-09-25: no rule matched).
# Competitive raises were tried and lost 26 IMPs to the advancing side
# over the corpus, par neutral (nt-interference.notes.md).
after (1N) 2y (*) | (1N) 3y (*)
  P   "Not enough to advance"  priority -10

# ── The defending side once the opening side bids on ─────────────────
# They opened; we have overcalled, advanced or raised, and they have bid
# again. Each of us has described his hand once, so with nothing new to
# say the call is a pass. A fallback below every real rule (2026-09-25:
# 63 no-rule positions in the Basic_* N/S boards came from here, e.g.
# 1S (2D) 2S (P) 4S and 1S (2D) X (3D) 3H). Positions where the
# defending side has more to say need rules of their own above this.
when lho.opened | rho.opened
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20

# Advancing an overcall (`advances.bid`): notes

Advancer's call after partner's overcall, direct or balancing, at the
one level or the two. Cases: `advances.test`.

## Guidance

Rick has not ruled on the advance yet; the ranges are BBA's Basic-Bridge
meanings, which are the usual ones:

- **raise** 7-11 total points with three-card support;
- **new suit** 8+ with four cards at the one level, 9+ with five at the
  two level;
- **1NT** 8-11 balanced with a stopper in their suit, denying an unbid
  four-card major and three-card support for partner's major;
- **jump raise** weak: four-card support and less than 8
  (`overcalls.responses.jump_raise`);
- an overcall is not forcing, so advancer **passes** with less.

## Evidence

From `bba-cli --all-meanings`, grouped over all four opening suits:

| call | BBA's meaning |
|---|---|
| raise | "calculated bid", 7-12 total points, 3+ support |
| new suit, one level | "bidable suit", 8-21, 4+ |
| new suit, two level | "bidable suit", 9-21, 5+ |
| pass | 0-12 total points (0-16 over a one-level overcall) |

## Advancing a two-level overcall (2026-09-23)

The advance of a two-level overcall was the largest no-rule cluster in
the corpus after the first round (`(1x) 2y (P)` and `(1x) 2y (2x)`
together, about 200 boards of the Basic-Bridge subset alone). It is now
written, and it splits on **what the two-level overcall was**:

- **a simple two-level overcall** (y could not have been shown at the
  one level: 2♣ over anything, 2♦ over 1♥/1♠, 2♥ over 1♠) is 12-17 with
  five cards, so advancer can invite. The raise to three is 7-10 with
  **four**-card support, the cue bid of their suit is a limit raise or
  better (11+ with three), 2NT is 11-12 and 3NT 13+ with a stopper, and
  a new suit is 10+ with five (12+ where it has to go to the three
  level). 4M is 13+ with four-card support, so that a limit raise cues
  rather than blasting;
- **a weak jump overcall** (everything else) is a six-card suit and 4-9,
  so the raise is a further preempt: three-card support in a major or
  four in a minor, under 11 total points, and 4M with four-card support
  and 11+, there being no cue bid worth making opposite a weak hand.

The `when` on each context spells the distinction out in `is` tests
(`x is C | (x is D, y is not C) | (x is H, y is S)` is "y is a jump"),
because the language has no operator for suit rank.

Advancer only bids while RHO has left him room — his pass, his double,
or his simple raise of their own suit. Over RHO's free bid, his notrump
or his jump the corpus says advancer passes, and trying to bid there
cost 130 calls across the corpus, so those auctions get the bare
`(*)` pass rule that covers the seat and nothing else.

**The overcaller answers the cue bid.** The cue `sets ask=cue_raise(y)`
and the answer is written `when asked cue_raise(t)`, once, whatever
level the cue was made at: 13+ total points bids the game, a minimum
signs off in the suit. Without it the cue bid was passed out and the
comparison flagged 30 boards whose contract was an artificial call.

### Evidence

`bba-cli --all-meanings`, grouped by abstracted prefix:

| prefix | call | BBA's meaning | hands |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1x) 2y (P), simple | 3y | "calculated bid", 7-10 tp, 3+ | all had **four** |
| (1x) 2y (P), simple | 2x | "limit raise or better" / "strength cue bid", 9-10+ | 3+ support |
| (1x) 2y (P), simple | new suit, 2 level | "bidable suit", 9-10 tp, 5+ | |
| (1x) 2y (P), simple | new suit, 3 level | "bidable suit", 12-17 tp, 5+ | |
| (1x) 2y (P), jump | 3y | "preemptive", 4-14 tp | 2-4 support |
| (1x) 2y (P), jump | 4y | "calculated bid", 3+ support | |
| (1x) 2y (2x) | 3y | "calculated bid", 6-12 tp, 3+ | |
| (1x) 2y (*) | P | 0-12 tp | 73 of 99 simple, 206 of 264 jump |

BBA's 2NT over a weak jump overcall is artificial (a feature ask); we do
not play it, and our natural 2NT is gated to the simple overcall.

## Advancer's cue-bid raise (2026-09-23)

`(1x) 1y (P) 2x` is a limit raise or better: three-card support and 12+
total points. BBA's meaning is "limit raise or better in !y", 20 calls
in the corpus on 12-18 HCP. 2NT with a stopper is 12-15 there, which is
BBA's 14-15 widened a little to meet the 1NT advance at 11.

The cue bid carries **no `priority`**, so descriptiveness ranks it: a
five-card suit of our own is still bid first, which is what the existing
case `K8.J72.Q93.AQT87 | 1D 1H P | 2C` requires.

## Advancer over RHO's 1NT (2026-09-23)

`after (1x) 1y (1z)` binds a suit, so RHO's 1NT left advancer with no
rule at all. The raise is 9-11 with three-card support (two points more
than over a pass — 1NT may be preparing a penalty double, and BBA passes
these hands out to 16 total points) and the cue bid 12+.

## Advancing a balancing overcall (2026-09-23)

Partner reopened, so he is 8-15 rather than 8-17 and part of his values
are borrowed from us. The direct-seat block no longer carries the
`(1x) P (P) 1y (P)` spelling; there is a separate balancing block with
everything about two points dearer: the raise 9-11, 1NT 10-11, 2NT
13-15, a new suit at the one level 7+ and at the two level 11+, the cue
bid 13+. Those are BBA's own `Balancing` meanings (raise 9-11 HCP, 1NT
10-11, one-level suit 7-9, cue bid 13).

Effect on the three balancing scenarios (Balancing,
Too_Strong_for_Overcall4th, Trap_Pass_Opener): calls +5, contracts
11.7% → 12.1%, par +98 IMPs, identical auctions 8.7% → 8.1%.

## Measured effect of the whole slice (2026-09-23)

Basic-Bridge subset (`compare --min-coverage 50`, 24 scenarios, 11,656
boards) and the whole corpus, before → after the second-call work in
this module and in `after-interference.bid`:

| | subset before | subset after | corpus before | corpus after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calls | 85.1% (89437) | 85.1% (89481) | 74.9% (1331086) | 74.9% (1331913) |
| identical auctions | 41.3% | 41.4% | 14.9% | 14.9% |
| same contract | 53.5% | 53.6% | 27.0% | 27.2% |
| par, net IMPs | -7574 | -7431 | -244279 | -239918 |
| no rule in a live auction | 5989 | 5692 | 165221 | 156762 |

## 2NT and a five-card major (2026-11-09)

Over 1♣ (1♦) P, Rusty advanced 2NT with QT6.A8643.J9.KJ5 in a Brill
daily, and all 8 other entrants bid 1♥ with the same hand. Rick agreed
that the major comes first. The 2NT advance now denies a five-card major
when that major can be bid at the one level (`H<=4 | y is S, S<=4`).
Over a 1♠ overcall 2NT stays: a first version that denied five hearts
there too bid 2♥ instead on 3 corpus boards and cost 24 IMPs of contract
errors. No corpus board reaches the one-level case.

## Gaps and open questions

- Advancer's **continuations** after the overcaller rebids, and after
  the cue-bid answer: `when asked cue_raise(t)` is answered once and
  then the auction has no more rules.
- Advancer over RHO's free bid, notrump or jump: we pass by rule. BBA
  passes most of them too, but not all, and a responsive double is the
  proper tool (off on this card).
- The **support cue bid** (`overcalls.responses.support_cuebid`) is
  still unwritten; the cue here is always a limit raise.
- Advancing a **1NT overcall** needs nothing here: systems are on, and
  the notrump modules carry the `(1x) 1N (P)` and `(1x) P (P) 1N (P)`
  spellings of their patterns (see `overcalls.notes.md`).
- **For Rick.** Over a simple two-level overcall the raise to three now
  asks for four-card support, because every BBA hand that raised had
  four even though its stated meaning allows three. With three and 7-10
  we pass. Is that right, or should three-card support raise?
- **For Rick.** 4M by advancer is 13+ with four-card support over a
  simple overcall (so that 11-12 cues first) but 11+ over a weak jump
  (where there is no cue worth making). The split is a judgment call.

## Fallback: the defending side after they bid on (2026-09-25)

Once our E/W overcalled in boards BBA bid N/S alone, the overcaller and
advancer had no rule whenever the opening side bid again (63 of the
remaining no-rule positions in Basic_* N/S). A pass at priority -20
under `when lho.opened | rho.opened` now closes them: each of us has
described his hand once. It changes no call (the engine passed anyway)
but it hides the defending side from the no-rule count, which falls
from 95,896 to 28,594 over the corpus. **A real gap on the defending
side (a big fit worth competing on, a second suit) now shows only as a
divergence from BBA, not as a problem.** A narrower form (partner
passed last) closed about two thirds as many; say if you want that one
instead.

Advancer over our E/W's overcall of their 1NT also passes (see
nt-interference.notes.md for the raises that were tried).

## Systems on after they double our 1NT overcall (2026-09-27)

Rick: systems are on after a 1NT overcall, and by default also after a
penalty double of it (some play escapes there, as over 1NT (X)). Every
notrump context spelled `(1x) 1N (P)` now also takes `(1x) 1N (X)`,
still gated by `nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on`. Ticket
basic-takeout-double-b160: North, Q9.JT942.932.J84, transfers with 2♦
(BBA too) instead of passing 1NT doubled.

## Raising a one-level overcall: trumps and points (2026-10-02)

Over a one-level overcall (RHO passing, doubling or bidding at the one
level) the raises now count trumps the way BBA does:

- **three-card support** raises to two with 8-11 total points (was
  7-11);
- **four-card support** raises to two at any strength up to 11;
- the **weak jump** (under 8) needs five trumps, or four at favourable
  vulnerability (`weak_jump_raise(y)` in `total-tricks.bid`); it took
  four at any vulnerability.

Unchanged over a two-level bid by RHO (`(1x) 1y (2z)`): letting the weak
four-card hand raise to two there lost (−34 and −20 IMPs on the two
commonest auctions), so that block keeps 7-11 with three.

**Evidence** (vanilla SAYC random set, BBA on bare SAYC, the advancer of
a one-level major overcall, any RHO action up to 2♦): with three hearts
BBA raises to 2♥ from about 8 HCP and passes 5-7 (we raised 495 such
hands); with four it raises to 2♥ with 2-11 HCP (169 hands where we
jumped) and jumps mostly with five or at favourable. On the boards
where this was the first difference, BBA's pass beat our raise by 729
IMPs and its 2M beat our 3M by 362 (errors yardstick).

**Measured** against the two previous changes (errors yardstick, IMPs;
even / odd boards):

| set | boards | errors | contract / doubling | distance from par | side IMPs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla SAYC random | 690 | +582 (+328 / +254) | +88 / +494 | −100 | +215 |
| corpus | 844 | +342 (+152 / +190) | +18 / +324 | −156 | +265 |
| 21GF random | 630 | +715 (+377 / +338) | +178 / +537 | +56 | −42 |

Most of the gain is in the doubling errors (the opponents, also us,
missing a penalty double of the light raise), but the contract errors
gain on all three sets as well, so the change is kept. Distance from
par is mixed (for Rick, below).

## The overcaller's rebid over their raise (2026-10-02)

After `(1x) 1y (2x) P (P)` the six-card rebid was written as 3{y}, a
jump: a one-level overcall always outranks their suit, so 2{y} is
there. BBA on bare SAYC rebids 2{y} with six from 10 HCP (88 hands, 66
of them where we jumped). Now 2{y}, 10+. Small and positive everywhere
(errors yardstick): vanilla +43 over 38 boards, corpus +23 over 24,
21GF +31 over 33; distance from par +7 / +2 / +1.

## Advancing from the sandwich seat (2026-10-07)

Partner came in after (1x) P (1y) (overcalls.bid, same date). I am a
passed hand and both of them have bid, so the advance is short: raise
with three at the two level, compete at three with four, preempt with
four and a weak hand (`weak_jump_raise`); otherwise pass. After the
takeout double: the longer unbid suit (a major with equal length), a
jump with four and 9-11, 1NT with both their suits stopped, else the
longer unbid suit however short; a free bid over their call with four
(a major) or five (a minor). Standard practice, not yet cited; not
probed against BBA.

## Never pass out our own artificial bid (2026-10-12)

Brill round robin 2026-10-09, board 90000102: `1S 2S X 3S X P P P`,
-1,700. South's Michaels 2♠ and North's cue 3♠ were both artificial;
after E's double both our passes came from "Defending: nothing more to
say" (priority -20), and the auction ended in our cue bid, doubled.

The guard, in the rules with one new engine term:

- `artificial_contract` (engine 0.7.0, CONTRACT.md): our side made the
  auction's last bid, the rule that explained it says `artificial`, and
  it did not answer partner's question. Answers (Lebensohl's and other
  relay completions, keycard answers) are left out: the asker may choose
  to play them, and does (418 corpus boards pass "Lebensohl: as asked"
  with clubs, 165 keycard answers in our suit are passed at the slam).
- `passes_out_artificial` (base.bid, a `define`):
  `artificial_contract, rho.last=P`: RHO has passed our artificial bid,
  so my pass leaves LHO to end the auction, or ends it. After RHO's
  double my pass is allowed (it gives partner another turn: opener's
  pass of a doubled Stayman 2♣ means something), and partner runs.
- The catch-all passes carry `when !passes_out_artificial`: this file's
  "Defending: nothing more to say", base.bid's "Game reached",
  after-interference.bid's two "nothing new to say", and two transfer
  fallbacks with the same hole: jacoby-transfers.bid's "Weak: play here"
  (responder passed his own transfer, doubled and passed back) and
  nt-interference.bid's "Nothing more to show".
- The runout (base.bid, priority -60, below every real rule): the
  cheapest bid in our best known fit (my length plus partner's shown
  minimum), never in a suit they have bid naturally.

For the Michaels case the Michaels bidder now describes instead of
passing (two-suited-overcalls.notes.md, 2026-10-12); were he to pass,
North would run to 4♥.

**Measured** (full corpus, 170,633 boards, against main; the boards
where our auction changed):

- Boards whose final contract was our artificial bid, passed by a
  catch-all: 76 → 9 (the 9 are doubled Lebensohl completions the asker
  had chosen to play: answers, left alone). The runout fires on 48
  boards, the game-force fallbacks take over on 25 more (the force of
  the cue bid now applies once the pass is gone).
- Most of it is the advancer's game-forcing cue of their preempt
  (`3x X P 4x P`), which the doubler passed out: 67 boards before, 0
  after; We_X_Opps_Preempt alone 51 boards.
- 77 boards changed. Errors yardstick +583 IMPs (halves +341 / +242),
  contract errors +450, doubling +133; distance from par +402 (+242 /
  +160); side IMPs +698. Whole set vs BBA, net errors -101,747 →
  -101,164.
- The tripwire: no change outside the guard's own positions and the
  Michaels scenarios.

## Mixed raise: the jump cuebid (2026-10-28)

Switched on by `overcalls.responses.jump_cuebid_mixed` (Rick asked for
it, 2026-10-28: "a jump cue bid of opener's suit, showing 4+ card
support for partner's overcall, and 7-9 support points"). Over a
one-level overcall, advancer's `3{x}` shows four or more trumps and
7-9 support points (`tp(y)`), ahead of the raise to two and the
preemptive raise (priority 2). The plain cue bid stays the limit raise
or better. The overcaller bids game with 16+ total points (25 opposite
9), 3NT over a minor with 16+ balanced and their suit stopped, else three
of his suit. Cases: `advances.test`, "Mixed raise".

**Where:** over RHO's pass, double or one-level bid, in the direct
seat. Not over a two-level overcall: there their suit outranks ours
(`(1♠) 2♥ (P) 3♠`), so the jump cuebid would force four of ours. Not
after a balancing overcall, whose ranges are two points higher.

**BBA plays it in competition only** (probe 2026-10-28, `rbb probe
--ns-card 21GF-SPECIALS --set "Mixed raise=1|0" --dealer W`, four
hands with four spades and 7-9 support points over 1♣–1♠):

| prefix | `Mixed raise = 1` | `Mixed raise = 0` |
|---|---|---|
| 1♣ 1♠ X | 3♣ 3♣ 3♣ (the 6-count passes) | 2♠ 2♠ 2♠ |
| 1♣ 1♠ P | P P 2♠ P | the same |

The corpus agrees: in Mixed_Raise_In_Comp BBA's advancer jump-cuebids
43 times over a double and 16 times over a one-level bid, never over a
pass. And the key does not touch 1M–3M: over `1♠ P` on 21GF-DEFAULT
(no Bergen) BBA bids the same five hands either way. So BBA's `Mixed
raise` key is this convention; convention-card mapped it to
`major_openings.jump_raise.mixed`, which made our responder play 1M–3M
as a mixed raise on the cards with it on (21GF-GIB, 21GF-SPECIALS) and
our advancer not play this. Remapped to
`overcalls.responses.jump_cuebid_mixed` (convention-card v0.22.1,
Rick, 2026-10-28). Over a pass we play it as Rick defined it; BBA there
raises or passes.

**Not vulnerable only.** In Mixed_Raise_In_Comp BBA's jump cuebid after
their double is almost all non-vulnerable (none vul 24, EW vul 14, both
4, NS vul 1); vulnerable it passes or raises. Measured on that scenario
(500 boards, vs BBA, errors):

| | errors | contract | doubling | par distance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old mapping (convention off) | −129 | −160 | +31 | −151 |
| remapped, any vulnerability | −217 | −156 | −61 | −98 |
| remapped, not vulnerable | **−78** | **−80** | **+2** | **−85** |

So `!vul`, over the pass too. BBA's choice between pass, raise and the
jump cuebid at equal vulnerability does not follow length or HCP (the
same 4-card 6-9 hands do all three); not modelled. Not played either:
over a 1♥ overcall and their double (spades shown), BBA cuebids 2♠ as
the raise (22 boards); the cue of the doubler's suit is a separate
treatment.

**Self A/B** (`probes/self-ab.toml`, `mixed-raise`: Mixed_Raise_In_Comp,
We_Overcall, Basic_Overcall, After_Partner_Overcalls; 500 boards each,
both sides). First version, any vulnerability: 304 boards changed,
contract errors −100, doubling +25, distance from par +61, z −1.4,
**leans loss**: three-level contracts going down vulnerable opposite a
light overcall (board 34: 3♠−2), against their game shut out (19 boards
from their 4♥ to our 3♠). Not vulnerable: 147 boards changed, contract
errors **+4**, doubling −10, distance from par +51, halves differ,
z −0.2, **neutral**.

## Sources

- **The ranges:** BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which are the usual ones,
  from `bba-cli --all-meanings` ("Evidence"). Rick has not ruled on the
  advance; the usual ranges are standard practice, not yet cited to a
  book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** a five-card major the one level allows is bid
  before 2NT (2026-11-09, from the Brill field PBNs: 8 of 8 entrants
  bid 1♥);
  systems on after a 1NT overcall, and by default
  after a penalty double of it (2026-09-27, ticket
  basic-takeout-double-b160).
- **BBA evidence:** BBA's advances of two-level and balancing overcalls
  and its cue-bid raise (2026-09-23 sections). No `probes/*.toml` spec
  yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** the whole slice (2026-09-23) and the
  defending-side fallback (2026-09-25).
- **Brill round robin 2026-10-09, board 90000102**
  (`probes/brill-90000102.pbn`): the guard against passing out our own
  artificial bid (2026-10-12).
- **Where we differ from BBA's stated meanings:** the raise of a
  two-level overcall asks for four trumps, as every BBA hand that raised
  had, although its meaning allows three (for Rick).
- **Raising a one-level overcall** (2026-10-02): BBA's raises on the
  vanilla SAYC random set (95,558 deals, bare SAYC) and the measurements
  in that section; the Law of Total Tricks (Cohen, *To Bid or Not to
  Bid*, 1992) hedged a trump for a weak hand, which is BBA's practice,
  not the book's.
- **Mixed raise** (2026-10-28): Rick's definition (above); the BBA probe
  and corpus count in that section. The usual statements of the
  convention (Bridge World Standard and others) are not yet cited; the
  convention-card summary (`spec/conventions/competitive_bidding/mixed_raise.toml`)
  matches.
