# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responder's call when RHO has overcalled or doubled partner's one-level
# opening (Rick, 2026-09-22): negative doubles through 3S, and natural
# bids otherwise.
#
# The uncontested rules in responses.bid are written as `after 1x (P)`
# patterns, so none of them fire once the opponents come in; everything
# responder needs over interference is here.
#
# Negative double: 6+ total points with four or more cards in each unbid
# major, so a suit bid in the only unbid major promises five. Where both
# majors are bid (1H-(1S)) the double shows the minors instead.
#
# Opener's answer to the negative double is written once with relative
# calls, so it is right at every level they push us to, and there is a
# separate block for the auctions where they compete over the double.
#
# Not written yet: their 1NT overcall, jump shifts, opener's rebid after
# anything but a negative double, and responder's second call once the
# auction has been contested.

module after-interference "Our side once the opponents come in"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/negative_doubles
  skill  partnership_bidding/negative_doubles
  skill  competitive_bidding/support_cuebids
  param  neg = competitive_bidding/negative_doubles default true
  param  cue_raise = competitive_bidding/support_cuebids default true
  param  new_suit_forcing = competitive.new_suit_after_overcall_forcing default true
  param  js = competitive.jump_shift_after_overcall default weak
  param  fsj = competitive_bidding/fit_showing_jumps default false
  param  tfr = bidding_conventions/transfers_after_double default false

# ── They overcalled at the one level ─────────────────────────────────
after 1x (1y) when neg
  X   "Negative double: 6+ total points, the unbid suits"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=6
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  ((D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)) | S>=4 | H>=4
      when   (S<=4 | x is S | y is S), (H<=4 | x is H | y is H | (y is S, hcp<=7))
      when   x<=2 | x is C | x is D     # support for a major: raise first (2026-09-25)
      priority 1
  # (the y-is-S clause) Five hearts over 1S and too weak for 2H: BBA
  # doubles (probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml: 12 of 12 with 6 HCP).

# ── Trap pass ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# With negative doubles on, responder cannot double their overcall for
# penalty. With length and strength in their suit he passes instead and
# hopes opener reopens with a double (rebids.bid), which he then passes
# (responder-rebids.bid). The holding: four or more with two of the top
# three or three of the top five (Rick's penalty-double standard,
# 2026-09-23), and 8+ HCP. The condition is `when`, not `shows`: a pass
# still says nothing, so opener does not read every pass as a trap. Not
# disclosed as a possible trap either: it is the same "No suitable bid" as
# every other pass here, and usually is one (Rick, 2026-10-29).
after 1x (1y) | 1x (2y) when y is not x, neg
  P   "No suitable bid"
      when  y>=4, quality(y)>=good | top5(y)>=3, hcp>=8, x<=2
      priority 2

after 1x (1y)
  1S  "6+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  S>=5 | (x is not H, y is not H, H<=3)
  1H  "6+ total points, four or more hearts"
      shows H>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not H, y is not H, y is not S
      when  H>=5 | (x is not S, y is not S, S<=3)
  1N  "6-10 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  2{x} "Raise: 6-9 total points, support for partner's suit"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      shows minor_raise(x)                # eight trumps: five over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  # BBA's 1C (1S) 3C (2026-09-27, ticket b469): the jump raise over an
  # overcall is preemptive, as over the double.
  jump(x) "Preemptive raise: five-card support, six in a minor, under 8"
      shows x>=5, hcp+length_points<=7
      shows minor_preempt(x)              # nine trumps: six over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
  cheapest(C) "8+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(D) "8+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  2H  "8+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  y is S, x is not H, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  # Not forcing (Basic-Bridge): limited to 12, and 13+ jumps, forcing to
  # game, as over a two-level overcall (below).
  cheapest(C) "8-12 total points, five or more clubs, not forcing"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C, !new_suit_forcing
  cheapest(D) "8-12 total points, five or more diamonds, not forcing"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D, !new_suit_forcing
  2H  "8-12 total points, five or more hearts, not forcing"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=12
      when  y is S, x is not H, !new_suit_forcing
  jump(C) "13+ total points, five or more clubs: forcing to game"
      shows C>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not C, y is not C, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      when  H<=4 | y is not S | x is H     # 5-5 with hearts: the higher suit
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(D) "13+ total points, five or more diamonds: forcing to game"
      shows D>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not D, y is not D, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      when  H<=4 | y is not S | x is H     # 5-5 with hearts: the higher suit
      sets  forcing=game
  3H  "13+ total points, five or more hearts: forcing to game"
      shows H>=5, hcp>=13
      when  y is S, x is not H, !new_suit_forcing, js is strong
      sets  forcing=game
  # Limit raise or better, and the notrump responses (2026-09-26: over a
  # one-level overcall these existed only over two-level ones, so 11-16
  # counts with a fit or a stopper passed; 40 corpus boards with 25+ HCP
  # and game on).
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {x}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  x>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      when   cue_raise, x is H | x is S | x>=4
      sets   forcing=round
      priority 1
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(y)
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# Opener when they raise over the one-level cue bid: game in a major
# with 16+, else let it go (the cue bid is no longer forcing).
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) when y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 16+"   shows hcp>=16
       when  x is H | x is S
  3N   "Game: 16+ with a stopper in {y}"       shows hcp>=16, stop(y)
       when  x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Game: 16+, no stopper in {y}"          shows hcp>=16
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -1
  # The minor cue bid promised four, so a fifth card is nine trumps:
  # compete at the four level (2026-09-27: these hands passed once the
  # round force ended with their raise, -159 IMPs by side on 57 boards).
  4{x} "Competes: five or more {x}"
       shows x>=5
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -4
  P    "No game"
       priority -5

# Responder once opener has passed their raise, or competed in his
# minor: the cue bid was 11+ with no upper limit, so with 13+ responder
# bids the game himself.
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) P (P) when y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 13+"   shows hcp+length_points>=13
       when  x is H | x is S
  3N   "Game: 13+ with a stopper in {y}"       shows hcp+length_points>=13, stop(y)
       when  x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 14+"                shows hcp+length_points>=14
       when  x is C | x is D
       priority -1
  P    "Limit raise only"
       priority -5
after 1x (1y) 2y (3y) 4x (P) when x is C | x is D, y is not x
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 13+"  shows hcp+length_points>=13
  P    "Limit raise only"
       priority -5

# ── Weak jump shifts over their one-level overcall ───────────────────
# `competitive.jump_shift_after_overcall` = weak (the 21GF cards): a
# jump in a new suit is preemptive, a six-card suit and little else
# (ACBL convention card, "Jump shift in competition: weak"; BBA alerts
# it "1X-(1Y)-2Z weak", 1-10 HCP, median 6, six cards, and only at the
# two level: a three-level jump it never makes, it passes). With
# support for partner's major a raise comes first. A passed hand's jump
# is fit-showing when the card plays those (fit-showing-jumps.bid).
# With `strong`, the 13+ jumps above (when a new suit is not forcing).
after 1x (1y) when y is not x, js is weak, !passed_hand | !fsj
  jump(S) "Weak jump shift: six or more spades, 2-7 HCP"
      shows S>=6, hcp=2..7
      when  x is not S, y is not S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 8
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      priority 2
  jump(H) "Weak jump shift: six or more hearts, 2-7 HCP"
      shows H>=6, hcp=2..7
      when  x is not H, y is not H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 8
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      priority 2
# Opener passes the weak jump unless something else fits better.
after 1x (1y) 2z (P) when partner.jumped, js is weak, z is not x, z is not y
  P   "No further bid"             priority -5

# ── They overcalled at the two level or jumped ───────────────────────
# Rick: over a two-level overcall a new suit is 10+ total points with five
# cards and forcing, and the negative double is 8+ with four. At the three
# level the free bid needs another point.
after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x
  X   "Negative double: 8+ total points, the unbid suits"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=8
      shows  (S>=4 | x is S | y is S), (H>=4 | x is H | y is H)
      shows  ((D>=4 | x is D | y is D), (C>=4 | x is C | y is C)) | S>=4 | H>=4
      when   (S<=4 | x is S | y is S), (H<=4 | x is H | y is H)
      when   neg
      priority 1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: limit raise or better in {x}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  x>=3, hcp+length_points>=11
      when   cue_raise
      sets   forcing=round
      priority 1
  cheapest(x) "Raise: 7-10, three-card support, five in a minor"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=7, hcp+length_points<=10
      shows minor_raise(x)                # eight trumps: five over a minor (total-tricks.bid)
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not S, y is not S, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not H, y is not H, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(D) "10+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not D, y is not D, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round
  cheapest(C) "10+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10
      when  x is not C, y is not C, new_suit_forcing
      sets  forcing=round

# The same bids where the card says a new suit is not forcing
# (Basic-Bridge sets `1X-(Y)-2Z forcing` off). The free bid is then
# limited, up to 12 HCP (BBA: 8-13 total points), and with 13+ HCP
# responder jumps,
# forcing to game (BBA: 13-21; probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml, 2026-09-25).
# Before, a 14-count made the non-forcing bid and was passed.
after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x, !new_suit_forcing
  cheapest(S) "10+ total points, five or more spades, not forcing"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "10+ total points, five or more hearts, not forcing"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "10+ total points, five or more diamonds, not forcing"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "10+ total points, five or more clubs, not forcing"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=12
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  jump(S) "13+ total points, five or more spades: forcing to game"
      shows S>=5, hcp>=13
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(H) "13+ total points, five or more hearts: forcing to game"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(D) "13+ total points, five or more diamonds: forcing to game"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      sets  forcing=game
  jump(C) "13+ total points, five or more clubs: forcing to game"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      sets  forcing=game

# Opener after the forcing jump: game in a major with three-card support,
# else 3NT with their suit stopped; the game force does the rest.
after 1x (1y) 2z (P) | 1x (1y) 3z (P) | 1x (2y) 3z (P) when partner.jumped, z is not x, z is not y, we.forcing = game
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game"         shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "No fit, a stopper in {y}"         shows stop(y)
        priority -1

after 1x (2y) | 1x (3y) when y is not x
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(y)
  3N  "13+ total points, balanced, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  stop(y)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# ── They doubled for takeout ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Redouble shows the balance of the strength; everything else is what it
# would have been, a level lower in ambition.
after 1x (X)
  XX  "Redouble: 10+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp+length_points>=10
      when  S<=4 | x is S | hcp>=12        # BBA: a five-card spade suit with 10-11 bids 1S
      when  H<=4 | x is H | x is S | hcp>=12   # and five hearts over a minor bid 1H
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "6-9 total points, four or more spades, or 10-11 with five"
      shows S>=4, S>H, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9 | (S>=5, hcp<=11)
      when  x is not S
  cheapest(H) "6-9 total points, four or more hearts, or 10-11 with five"
      shows H>=4, H>=S, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9 | (H>=5, hcp<=11)
      when  x is not H, x is not S
  cheapest(D) "6-9 total points, four or more diamonds"
      shows D>=4, S<=3, H<=3, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is not D, x is not H, x is not S
  2{x} "Raise: 4-9 total points, support for partner's suit"
      shows x>=3, hcp+length_points>=4, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is H | x is S | x>=5
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | x is H), (H<=3 | x is H | x is S)   # over a major, support first (BBA)
  3{x} "Preemptive raise: five-card support for a major, less than 8"
      shows x>=5, hcp+length_points<=7
      when  x is H | x is S
  1N  "6-9 total points, balanced"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=6, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  (S<=3 | x is S), (H<=3 | x is H)
      when  x<=2 | x is C | x is D
      when  !tfr | x is C | x is D          # a transfer to clubs (transfers-after-double.bid)
  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# ── Opener answers a negative double ─────────────────────────────────
# Partner has shown four or more cards in each unbid major and 6+ total
# points (8+ over a two-level overcall), so opener names the major he
# has (counted in support points, as an uncontested raise is: with a
# singleton, 16 HCP and four trumps is game, 2026-09-25), bids notrump with a stopper, or rebids his own suit. A negative
# double is forcing: opener always bids something, and jumps with 16-18.
# Relative calls keep one set of rules right at every level.
after 1x (1y) X (P) | 1x (2y) X (P) | 1x (3y) X (P)
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, minimum"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(S) "Four spades, 16-18"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=16..18
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Four hearts, 16-18"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)=16..18
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "12-14 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp<=14
      when  stop(y), !weak_nt
  # With a weak notrump the balanced hands above it, up to 17 (Rick,
  # 2026-11-07; one-nt.bid, `weak_nt`).
  cheapest(N) "Balanced, above the weak notrump: up to 17, a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, above_weak_nt
      when  stop(y), weak_nt
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)
  # A major rebid is read as six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16, Brill daily
  # board 8): the five-card rebid below with nothing better to say is the
  # least lie and is read by this rule (a read-as call by design). A
  # minor's rebid stays five or more (2026-10-09, read as the hand holds).
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: six or more, minimum"
      shows x>=6, hcp<=15
      when  x is H | x is S
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: five or more, minimum"
      shows x>=5, hcp<=15
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  x>=6
  jump(x) "Six cards in {x}, 16-18"
      shows x>=6, hcp=16..18
  # Partner promised four, so three is an eight-card fit and BBA bids it:
  # `1D (1S) X (P) 2H` on KQ6.832.KT84.A64. Below the four-card bids and
  # the notrump rebid, above naming a minor.
  4S  "Game: four spades, 19+"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)>=19
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  4H  "Game: four hearts, 19+"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)>=19
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  # Where both majors are bid the double showed the minors, and where
  # opener has no major, no stopper and no six-card suit he still has to
  # bid. An unbid four-card minor comes before rebidding his own suit,
  # which is what BBA does: `1D (1S) X (P) 2C` on 754.AQ.AQ52.QT74.
  cheapest(D) "Four diamonds, minimum"
      shows D>=4, hcp<=15
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      priority -1
  cheapest(C) "Four clubs, minimum"
      shows C>=4, C>=D, hcp<=15
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      when  (S<=3 | x is S | y is S), (H<=3 | x is H | y is H)
      priority -1
  # Partner promised four, so three is an eight-card fit and BBA bids it
  # once it has nothing else: `1D (1S) X (P) 2H` on KQ6.832.KT84.A64.
  cheapest(S) "Three spades, minimum"
      shows S>=3, hcp<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S, partner.S>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(H) "Three hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=3, hcp<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H, partner.H>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: five cards, minimum"
      shows x>=5, hcp<=15
      priority -2
  # Strong hands with no fit and no balanced notrump (2026-09-25: 19-20
  # counts rebid their suit as "nothing better" and were passed). From
  # 17 since 2026-09-26: 19/17/16 tried, 17 best (+192 by par distance).
  # Not over a three-level overcall: there it lost (-131 IMPs over 1S (3H)).
  3N  "Game: 17+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=17, stop(y)
      when  lho.last=1{y} | lho.last=2{y}
      priority -1
  cheapest(y) "Cue bid: 17+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=17
      when  lho.last=1{y} | lho.last=2{y}
      sets  forcing=game
      priority -2
  cheapest(x) "Rebids {x}: no better bid"
      priority -5

# ── Opener answers the cue-bid raise ─────────────────────────────────
# The cue bid showed three-card support and 11+ total points, so opener
# accepts with more than a minimum and signs off otherwise.
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) | 1x (3y) 4y (P) when y is not x   # their bid in our suit is a two-suiter (two-suited-overcalls.bid)
  # In support points (2026-09-26): 16 HCP left 14-15 with shortness in
  # a partscore. 14/15/16 support points: +750/+697/+519 by par distance.
  4{x} "Accepts: game in {x}"
      shows tp(x)>=14
      when  x is H | x is S
  # With a minor, 3NT is the game: from 14 with their suit held, any
  # shape, else five of the minor from 16 (2026-09-25: 16-20 counts
  # signed off, 668 corpus boards with 25+ HCP between us and 3NT on).
  3N  "Accepts: 14+ with a stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=14
      when  stop(y), x is C | x is D
  5{x} "Accepts: 16+, no stopper in {y}"
      shows hcp>=16
      when  x is C | x is D
      priority -1
  cheapest(x) "Minimum: signs off"
      priority -2

# Responder after opener's sign-off: the cue bid was 11+ with no upper
# limit, so with 13+ responder bids the game himself.
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 4x (P) when x is C | x is D, y is not x
  3N  "Game: 13+ with a stopper in {y}"   shows hcp+length_points>=13, stop(y)
  5{x} "Game in the minor: 14+"          shows hcp+length_points>=14
      priority -1
  P   "Limit raise only"
      priority -5
after 1x (2y) 3y (P) 4x (P) when x is H | x is S, y is not x
  P   "Game reached"
after 1x (1y) 2y (P) 2x (P) | 1x (1y) 2y (P) 3x (P) | 1x (2y) 3y (P) 3x (P) when x is H | x is S, y is not x
  4{x} "Game: 13+"  shows hcp+length_points>=13
  P   "Limit raise only"
      priority -5

# ── Opener when they compete over the negative double ────────────────
# They have bid again, so the double is no longer forcing and opener may
# pass. He still names a four-card major at the cheapest level, bids
# notrump with a stopper, or rebids a six-card suit with extras; with a
# minimum and nothing to say he lets them have it, which is what BBA
# does on most of these hands. Only where they have merely competed to
# the next level: over a jump by them BBA passes almost always, and we
# leave that to the pass below.
after 1x (1y) X (2z) | 1x (2y) X (3z) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, minimum"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)<=15
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, minimum"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)<=15
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  jump(S) "Four spades, 16-18"
      shows S>=4, tp(S)=16..18
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  jump(H) "Four hearts, 16-18"
      shows H>=4, tp(H)=16..18
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "12-15 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp<=15
      when  stop(y)
  jump(N) "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      when  nt_jump_to_game                  # 3NT at most (rebids.bid)
      shows balanced, hcp=18..19
      when  stop(y)
  cheapest(x) "Six or more {x}, 13+"
      shows x>=6, hcp>=13
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# They jumped over the double. Most of these hands pass in the corpus,
# so opener only bids on with real extras: a four-card major for the one
# partner promised, or a stopper, and 13+ HCP to go with it.
after 1x (1y) X (3z) | 1x (1y) X (4z) | 1x (2y) X (4z) | 1x (3y) X (4z) when y is not x
  cheapest(S) "Four spades, 13+"
      shows S>=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts, 13+"
      shows H>=4, hcp>=13
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(N) "13+ balanced with a stopper in {y}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=13
      when  stop(y)
  P   "No further bid"  priority -10

# ── Fallback: a player on the opening side who passed last time ──────
# They have come in, and I passed at my last turn: with nothing new to
# say I pass again. Below every real rule (2026-09-25: six no-rule
# positions in Basic_* N/S boards, e.g. 1C P P X P 2N and
# 1D (2C) P (2S) 3D (P), where responder had passed with 0-5 or 8).
when they.bid, !lho.opened, !rho.opened, me.last=P   # our side opened
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20
# And when partner passed at his last turn: he has nothing more, and I
# have described my hand (2026-09-25: 1S (X) 2S (3C) P (P), the raiser).
when they.bid, !lho.opened, !rho.opened, partner.last=P
  P   "No further bid"
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out our own artificial bid (base.bid)
      priority -20

# ── Opener after partner answered the reopening double ───────────────
# Partner was forced to bid; opener goes on only with game values.
after 1x (1y) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) | 1x (1y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (2y) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) | 1x (2y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (3y) P (P) X (P) 3z (P) | 1x (3y) P (P) X (P) 4z (P) when y is not x, z is not y
  3N  "Game: 18+ with a stopper in {y}"    shows hcp>=18, stop(y)
  P   "No game"
      priority -10
files.rules/competitive/after-interference.not:
# Our side once they come in (`after-interference.bid`): notes

Responder's call when RHO has overcalled or doubled partner's one-level
opening, and opener's answer to a negative double. Cases:
`after-interference.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **Negative doubles through 3♠**, plus natural bids.
- The double shows **6+ total points with four or more cards in each
  unbid major**, so a suit bid in the only unbid major promises five.
  Where both majors have been bid (1♥-(1♠)) it shows the minors.
- **Redouble is 10+** and says we own the hand.
- Raises are 6-9 with support over an overcall. **Over a double the raise
  starts at 4 total points**: BBA raises on 5 HCP with three trumps, and
  taking the level away from a doubler is worth it. The jump raise is
  five-card support for a major with less than 8; a minor raises to two,
  which is what BBA does with the same hands.
- 1NT denies an unbid four-card major (partner would hear about it from
  the double) and denies three-card support for partner's major.

## Evidence

From `bba-cli --all-meanings` on the two Basic scenarios:

- **(1x 1y) X** — "negative double", 6-21 total points, 4-6 cards in the
  unbid major. A one-level suit bid in the only unbid major showed 5+
  (1♣-(1♥)-1♠), but only 4+ when both majors were still unbid
  (1♣-(1♦)-1♠ and 1♣-(1♦)-1♥), which is what the rules do.
- **(1x X)** — responder over a double: pass 0-5; a new suit at the one
  level 6+ with 4+; a raise "calculated bid" 7-9 with 3+; redouble
  "penalty" 10+; a jump raise of a minor "preemptive" 3-7 with five.

Effect: call-2 agreement over the two scenarios went from 49.5% to 62.8%,
and Basic_Takeout_Double from 60.4% to 71.3% of calls.

Two rules were wrong until the `.test` cases caught them: the negative
double outranked a five-card major (it now denies one), and 1NT outranked
a raise with three-card support for partner's major.

## Over a two-level or jump overcall (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **a new suit is 10+ total points with five cards, and forcing**
  (`competitive.new_suit_after_overcall_forcing`, default on; Basic-Bridge
  turns it off, and then the same bids are made without the force);
- **the negative double is 8+ with four cards** in each unbid major;
- **the cue bid of their suit is a limit raise or better**: 11+ with
  three-card support (`competitive.cue_bid_raise.play`, default on).
  Opener accepts with 16+ and signs off in the suit otherwise.

Their bid **in our suit** is a cue bid, not an overcall (Michaels and the
like), so these rules are gated on `y is not x`. Without that they fired
over a Michaels cue bid and cost about a point of agreement in each of
the six Michaels scenarios. Since 2026-09-28 our answers to their
Michaels and Unusual 2NT are in `two-suited-overcalls.bid`; opener's
answer to the cue-bid raise got the same `y is not x` guard, since
1♦ (2♦) 3♦ (our competitive raise over Michaels) was being read as
"1x (2y) 3y", the cue-bid raise.

Opener's answer to the negative double is written once with relative
calls (`cheapest(S)`, `jump(N)`, `cheapest(x)`), so it is right at every
level the opponents push us to. Before that it only covered a one-level
overcall, and a two-level negative double was left to die: the corpus
lost 12 points of identical auctions in McCabe_after_WJO and 11 in
Opps_Preemptive_Overcall until opener could answer.

Across the corpus this slice is worth +36.6 points of call agreement and
+75.6 points of contract agreement summed over the 90 scenarios it moved.

## Opener's answer to the negative double, completed (2026-09-23)

The block only bid majors, notrump with a stopper, and a six-card suit
of its own, so 1♥-(1♠)-X — where the double shows the **minors** — and
every minimum with no major and no stopper died on the spot: `1x 1y X P`
was 665 boards of "no rule in a live auction" across the corpus and the
largest second-call gap in the module. Opener now has, below the
four-card major and the notrump rebid and in this order:

1. an **unbid four-card minor** (`cheapest(D)` with four, `cheapest(C)`
   with four and at least as many as diamonds, so 4-4 bids the cheaper);
2. **three cards in the major partner promised** — an eight-card fit,
   which is what BBA does (`1D (1S) X (P) 2H` on KQ6.832.KT84.A64);
3. **five cards in his own suit** (the old rule needed six);
4. `cheapest(x)` with nothing shown at priority -5, so the forcing
   double always gets an answer.

Two more holes at the top of the range: with **19+** and a four-card
major opener bids the game (`1C (1S) X (P) 4H` on A63.AT92.A.AQJ43), and
the jump in a major stops at 18 as before.

Effect on the corpus: `1x 1y X P` gained 255 calls, and the whole
module's slice took no-rule from 165,221 to 156,762 boards.

## Opener when they compete over the negative double (2026-09-23)

`1x (1y) X (2y)` was the second-largest second-call gap (225 boards
across the corpus). They have bid again, so the double is no longer
forcing and **pass is BBA's commonest answer** (it passes 11-18 there).
Opener competes only with something to say: a four-card major at the
cheapest level, a jump in it with 16-18, notrump with a stopper, or a
six-card suit with 13+. Everything else passes, by rule rather than by
having no rule.

Over a **jump** by them (`1x (1y) X (3y)` and higher) even that is too
much: BBA passes almost everything, and bidding there cost 43 calls.
That context keeps only a four-card major or a stopper **with 13+**,
and passes otherwise.

`when y is not x` on both contexts: their bid in our suit is a cue bid,
not an overcall. Without it these rules fired over Michaels and cost
about 20 calls in the `1x (2x) X (4y)` auctions alone.

## Measured effect (2026-09-23)

Before → after, for the whole second-call slice in this module and
`advances.bid` together:

| | subset before | subset after | corpus before | corpus after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calls | 85.1% (89437) | 85.1% (89481) | 74.9% (1331086) | 74.9% (1331913) |
| identical auctions | 41.3% | 41.4% | 14.9% | 14.9% |
| same contract | 53.5% | 53.6% | 27.0% | 27.2% |
| par, net IMPs | -7574 | -7431 | -244279 | -239918 |
| no rule in a live auction | 5989 | 5692 | 165221 | 156762 |

252 scenarios moved: +827 calls, +358 boards with the same contract,
-8,459 no-rule points. The biggest movers are Double_double (+82 calls),
Maximal_Double (+55), McCabe_after_WJO (+49 calls, -560 no-rule),
After_Partner_Overcalls (+41 calls, +26 contracts) and
After_Opp_Overcalls (+35). Two scenarios gain no-rule points because
their auctions now live longer than they used to
(After_Partner_Overcalls +174, Double_by_Advancer +115); both gained 26
contracts in exchange.

Accepted cost: 13 more boards flagged **trump fit under 7 cards** on the
Basic-Bridge subset (176 → 189), nearly all opener naming a minor for a
negative double whose `shows` is a disjunction, so the engine cannot
know partner really holds it.

## Gaps and open questions

- **Their 1NT overcall**: `after 1x (1y)` binds a suit, so nothing fires
  after `1x (1N)` and responder passes. It is the largest single no-rule
  point left in the corpus — about 3,700 boards (`1D 1NT`, `1C 1NT`) —
  and the `Opps_Overcall_1NT` scenario is 500 of them.
- **Opener's rebid in a contested auction generally** is now the biggest
  remaining cluster of dead auctions, and it is not written anywhere:
  `1x (1y) 2z (P)` 68 boards, `1x (X) 1y (P)` 65, `1x (X) P (2y)` 60,
  `1x (1y) 1z (2y)` 55, `1x (X) P (2x)` 51, `1x (X) XX (1y)` 50,
  `1x (1y) 1z (P)` 48 on the Basic-Bridge subset alone, over 500 boards
  in all. It sits between this module and `base/rebids.bid`; a decision
  on where it belongs would unblock it.
- **Responder's second call in a contested auction**: `1x (1y) X (P) 2x`
  is 54 boards on the subset, and it is the next turn after the rules
  added here.
- **Jump shifts**: done 2026-10-05 (below). Lebensohl over an overcall
  of 1m (BBA plays it on the 21GF card) is still open.
- **Trap passes**: BBA passes with length and strength behind the
  overcaller where we double or cue. Trap_Pass loses 3.0 points of call
  agreement, and its contracts gain 2.6.
- Opener's rebid after our side has been doubled
  (`competitive.jordan_2nt`, support redoubles).
- **For Rick.** Opener's answer to a negative double now names an unbid
  four-card minor before rebidding a four-card suit of his own, and bids
  a three-card major for partner's promised four before a five-card
  minor. BBA is not consistent about this (it bids 2♦ on one 4-5 minor
  hand and 2♣ on another identical one); the order above is what
  measured best.

## After their takeout double (2026-09-25)

Basic_Takeout_Double was the weakest Basic scenario against par (-434).
- **Support first over a major.** The raise was blocked by four cards in
  the other major, so 1S (X) with three spades and four hearts passed:
  hearts can't be bid at the one level over 1S. BBA raises. +338.
- **Five-card major with 10-11 bids it.** BBA bids 1S (or 1H over a
  minor) with five and 10-11; we redoubled. The suit now covers five
  cards up to 11, and the redouble waits for 12 with such a hand. +418
  (spades), +34 (hearts).

Corpus: -160,381 -> -159,591.
- **Re-checked from the acting side** (probes/tools/sideimps.py,
  overcalls.notes.md "For Rick: which yardstick"):
  - Support first over a major: both measures agree (+338 distance, +541
    to the side).
  - Five-card major before the redouble: they disagree. +452 by distance,
    but the redouble is better for the side that acts by 654. For Rick.

## Fallback: a player on the opening side who passed last time (2026-09-25)

`when they.bid, !lho.opened, !rho.opened, me.last=P`: pass, priority
-20. Six Basic_* N/S positions had no rule, all a responder who passed
with 0-5 (or 8) and an opener who had let them have it, facing a
balancing sequence. No call changes. Written with the negations because
there is no self form of `opened` (`me.opened` and bare `opened` are
unknown terms, which evaluate false without an error from `bid check`).

## Trap pass (2026-09-25)

Prerequisite for judging the one-level overcall quality test
(overcalls.notes.md, "For Rick: which yardstick"): our opening side had
no way to punish a light overcall, so the side yardstick flattered
overcalling. With negative doubles responder cannot double for penalty.
He now passes with four or more of their suit, two of the top three or
three of the top five (Rick's penalty standard), 8+ HCP and at most two
of opener's suit; opener's reopening double (rebids.bid) and
responder's pass of it (responder-rebids.bid) already existed. The
trap condition is a `when`, so a pass still promises nothing: a
higher-priority `shows` would have made every pass read as a trap.

Full corpus: +82 by par distance, +1,122 to the side that trapped (253
boards). Basic_* competitive: -3 / +20 (4 boards).

## Opener's answer to the negative double in support points (2026-09-25)

Found while re-running the overcall quality A/B with the trap pass in:
most of what an overcall "gained" by the side yardstick (1,815 boards,
+3,234) was our opening side bidding worse after it, 839 times
dropping from game to a partscore. The main cause: opener answered the
double in HCP (minimum up to 15, jump 16-18, game 19+), so 16 HCP with
a singleton and four trumps jumped to 2♠ and responder passed, where
uncontested it raised to 4♠ on 19 support points. The major answers
now count `tp(M)`, and responder bids game over the jump with 8+
(responder-rebids.bid, `partner.jumped`). Full corpus +730 by par
distance, +836 by side (420 boards); Basic_* competitive +8 / -2.

## Strong hands after the negative double (2026-09-25)

Opener with 19+ and no fit or balanced notrump rebid his suit as
"nothing better to say", and responder with 13+ unbalanced had no call
over a minimum answer; both were passed out in partscores that reach
game uncontested. Now: opener 3NT with a stopper, else a cue bid of
their suit (game forcing); responder 3NT with a stopper, else the cue
bid. Only over one- and two-level overcalls: over three-level ones it
lost (-131 over 1♠ (3♥)). Full corpus +644 by par distance, +875 by
side (257 boards).

## Free bids where a new suit is not forcing (2026-09-25)

On cards with `1X-(Y)-2Z forcing` off (Basic-Bridge and the 21GF
cards in the corpus), the free new suit was "10+" (8+ over a one-level
overcall) with no ceiling, so 14-counts made a non-forcing bid and
opener passed. BBA on Basic (`probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml`, 300
responders with five hearts over 1♦ (1♠)): 2♥ is 8-13 total points,
not forcing; 3♥ is 13-21, forcing; with five hearts and 6-7 it doubles.
Now: the free bid up to 12 HCP, a jump with 13+ HCP forcing to game
(opener raises a major with three, else 3NT with their suit stopped,
else the game force), and the negative double over 1♠ allows five
hearts under 8 HCP. Grid agreement 59% -> 69%. Full corpus +139 by par
distance, +255 by side, in two steps.

## More opening-side gaps in competitive auctions (2026-09-25)

Basic_* competitive no-rule positions 103 -> 15: a pass fallback when
partner passed at his last turn (the raiser after 1♠ (X) 2♠ (3♣) P
(P)); opener after partner's forced answer to the reopening double
(3NT with 18+ and a stopper, else pass); 1m (3x) 4m: 5m with 16+
(rebids.bid); and 1NT (3x) (nt-interference.bid). Basic_* competitive
+18 / +30, full corpus +189 / +262.

## Support first, and forcing free bids at the two level (2026-09-25)

- The negative double's shape clause (`| S>=4 | H>=4`) let a hand with
  four-card support for opener's major double instead of raising;
  after opener's rebid of the suit it then passed, missing the fit
  (1♥ (1♠) X 2♥ with Kxxx). With three or more of opener's major the
  raise now comes first. Full corpus +179 by par distance, +368 by side
  (965 boards).
- Over a one-level overcall, the two-level free bids on cards where a
  new suit is forcing (the 21GF cards) did not set `forcing=round`, so
  opener could pass them. Fixed; +4 / +36, but the minor openings lose
  (1♣ (1♠) 2♦ -89 by side): opener's forced rebids there need work.

## The cue-bid raise of a minor (2026-09-26)

New work queue for the invitational tail: contested boards where our
opening side stops in a partscore with 25+ HCP between the hands and
game makes double dummy (`probes/tools/missed_games.py FILE missed 25 25`). Top of it, 668
boards: 1m (2x) 3x, opener signing off "no game opposite a limit raise"
with 16-20, because with a minor he accepted only balanced with a
stopper. Now 3NT from 14 with their suit held (any shape), else 5m from
16; responder, whose cue bid has no upper limit, bids 3NT (13+,
stopper) or 5m (14+) over the sign-off. The first try lost on the
majors: the forced-rebid rules for free bids (rebids.bid) also matched
the cue bid, their suit read as partner's; they now need
`partner.z>=5`. Full corpus +1,006 by par distance, +2,269 by side.
The same with a major: over opener's sign-off in three, responder with
13+ bids game (240 boards in the queue). Full corpus +919 by par
distance, +1,865 by side.

## Cue-bid raise and notrump over a one-level overcall (2026-09-26)

Over a one-level overcall responder had the negative double, one-level
suits, 1NT and a simple raise, but no limit raise and no 2NT/3NT: those
existed only over two-level overcalls, so 11-16 counts with a fit or a
stopper passed (1♥ (1♠) P with three hearts and 11-16). Added the cue
bid (three-card major support or four of a minor, 11+), 2NT 11-12
(asks the notrump invitation) and 3NT 13+, both balanced with their
suit stopped; opener's answers and responder's follow-ups now include
the one-level cue. When they raise over the cue, opener bids game with
16+ or competes in his suit (the engine keeps the round force, so pass
is not available). Full corpus +1,100 by par distance, +2,660 by side
(1,511 boards).

## Accepting the major limit raise in support points (2026-09-26)

Opener accepted the cue-bid raise of a major with 16 HCP, so 14-15
with a doubleton or singleton stayed in three (52 boards in the
missed-games queue). Now `tp(x)>=14`. Tried: 16 HCP -> 15 HCP +61;
16 / 15 / 14 support points +519 / +697 / +750 by par distance
(+1,339 / +1,723 / +1,905 by side). 14 kept, par deciding; it accepts
12 HCP with a singleton, a normal acceptance.

Opener's strong answers to the negative double (3NT with a stopper,
else the cue bid) now start at 17 rather than 19: 17 +192 by par
distance, +278 by side; 16 +158 / +192. A case in the test file that
recorded BBA's 2♣ on K964.K4.AT.AQJT9 (17, spades held) now expects
3NT.

## A round force ends when they act over it (2026-09-27)

The engine kept a `forcing=round` in force after the forcer's LHO bid,
doubled or redoubled, so partner could not pass (hence the "engine keeps
the round force" workaround above). Now the force holds only when RHO
passes; a game force is unchanged. The compare tool's broken-force check
uses the same rule.

- The workaround after `1x (1y) 2y (3y)` (opener's `cheapest(x)` at -6)
  is gone. With the force released it was dead code: the pass at -5
  already outranked it, and removing it changed no board.
- The engine change alone was neutral: 230 boards changed, -1 IMP by
  side, +0 by par distance. It hid two things. With the cue raise of a
  minor, opener now passed their raise with a fifth trump and responder
  passed with game values: -159 by side on 57 boards. Added opener's 4m
  with five (nine trumps opposite the cue's four), 5m with 16+ and no
  stopper, and responder's game with 13+ after opener's pass or 4m:
  +290 by side, +176 by par. Opener's 18+ raise of a forcing free bid
  (rebids.bid) was gated on `we.forcing = round` and now used the card
  field instead: +33 by side.
- Doubles: takeout, negative, responsive and reopening doubles never
  set `forcing=round`. They are forcing because their blocks have no
  pass when RHO passes, and every block where RHO has bid has one.
  They stay that way: a round force would remove the explicit penalty
  passes (`1x (1y) P (P) X (P)` responder with four of theirs,
  `1N (2y) X (P)` and `1N (3y) X (P)` opener).
- Total, full corpus: vs BBA -142,200 -> -142,024; 213 boards, +358 by
  side, +176 by par distance; no rule 4,639 -> 4,587; broken forces 83
  both; contested missed games (`missed 10 25`) 996 -> 971, failed games
  (`over 10`) 2,210 -> 2,196. Basic_* competitive one board -2 (par -1),
  N/S one board +10 (par +2).
- Still losing: `1H (1S) 2m (2S)` with a minimum now passes where the
  forced opener used to find 3H or 3m, about -54 by side on 55 boards.
  Most of these are responder bidding a minor with three hearts where
  BBA raised to 2H, so the fix belongs in responder's choice, not here.
- For Rick: the 18+ raise on every card (not only where the free bid
  is forcing) was +99 by side and +27 by par, but it turns rebids.test's
  1H (2C) 2D (P) 2H (Basic-Bridge, 64.AK8432.AK86.9) into 3D. Kept to
  the forcing cards.

## Raising opener's minor counts the trumps (2026-10-02)

Responder's raises of a minor over an overcall now count the trumps the
way the Law of Total Tricks does (`minor_raise(x)`, `minor_preempt(x)`
in `total-tricks.bid`). One of a minor promises three, so:

- the simple raise (`1m (1y) 2m`, and `1m (2y) 3m` with 7-10) needs five,
  eight trumps; it took three over a two-level overcall (six trumps at
  the three level) and passed with four or fewer only over a one-level
  one;
- the preemptive jump (`1m (1y) 3m`) needs six, nine trumps; it took
  five (eight trumps at the three level).

Major raises are unchanged (three-card support; a third-seat 1♥ may be
four cards, and requiring eight known trumps there lost IMPs).

**Evidence.** BBA on bare SAYC (Random_Pavlicek_SAYCvanilla, 95,558
deals) at `1C (1x)` with five clubs and under 8: pass 108, 3♣ 26; with
six, 3♣ 12, pass 2. At `1D (1x)`, five diamonds: pass 109, 3♦ 2; six:
3♦ 12. Over a two-level overcall, BBA's 3♣/3♦ raise has five cards (28 +
25 hands); it passes with three or four (about 190 hands each), where
we raised. Counting opener's minor as four (raising 1♣ with four at the
two level, as BBA sometimes does) lost 158 IMPs over 1♣ and was neutral
over 1♦, so it is not done.

**Measured** (errors yardstick, IMPs; even / odd boards):

| set | boards changed | errors | contract / doubling | distance from par | side IMPs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla SAYC random | 975 | +1,010 (+396 / +614) | +537 / +473 | +115 | +215 |
| corpus | 747 | +951 (+329 / +622) | +531 / +420 | +245 | +190 |
| 21GF random | 856 | +1,043 (+397 / +646) | +513 / +530 | +190 | +283 |

The largest single gains: `1D (2S) 3D` → pass (+142 vanilla, +251
corpus), `1C (2H/2D) 3C` → pass, `1C/1D (1H) 3m` → pass. The largest
loss: `1C (2S) 3C` → pass with four clubs (−65 vanilla).

The ticket test from Basic_Overcall 469 (1♣ (1♠) 3♣ with five clubs,
Basic-Bridge card) now passes; the case is rewritten with six clubs, and
the five-club hand expects a pass. One consequence in `rebids.test`:
after `1D (2S) 3D (P)` the raise now shows five, so opener with five
holds ten trumps and the Law bids 4♦ (it passed before; still not 5♦).

## Jump shifts over their overcall, from the card (2026-10-05)

`competitive.jump_shift_after_overcall` (`1X-(1Y)-2Z weak/strong` in
`.bbsa`): weak on every 21GF and Precision card, strong on Basic-Bridge.

- **weak**: `1x (1y)` and a jump to 2H/2S is preemptive, six or more
  cards, 2-7 HCP, not with three-card support for partner's major;
  opener passes it unless another rule (a strong balanced hand) bids.
  Only at the two level: BBA alerts "1X-(1Y)-2Z weak" at 2H/2S only
  (all 63 corpus alerts), and passes the weak six-card hands a three-level
  jump would show; our first version also jumped at three and diverged
  on about 20 boards, so it was cut back.
- **strong**: the existing 13+ game-forcing jumps (where a new suit is
  not forcing).
- A passed hand's jump is a fit-showing jump when the card plays those
  (`fit-showing-jumps.bid`).

Tripwire (all scenarios, --limit 50): the weak jump shift now fires in
Negative_Free_Bid, Dealing_with_Overcalls_Strong, Game_Overcalls and
single boards elsewhere, all on cards that set it. BBA bids 1S rather
than 2S with 8 HCP and six spades, and over 1D (1S) bids a forcing 2H
with six hearts and 7-9 HCP: hence the 2-7 range.

**For Rick:** with `weak` and a new suit not forcing (the Precision
cards), a 13+ responder with a long suit now has no jump; he bids the
non-forcing new suit or doubles. Fine, or should the jump stay strong
there? **Rick, 2026-10-08: deferred to the Precision project**, which
needs research first. Options then: the non-forcing new suit or a
double (today), or a cue bid of their suit as the forcing route.

## Opener's five-card rebid after the negative double (2026-10-09)

`1S (2H) X (P) 2S` on QJT63.QJ.972.AK9 (no stopper, no second suit) was
bid by "Five cards in {x}" and read as "Six cards, minimum" (Brill
report, own-misdescribed). Standard practice: with no four-card major,
no stopper and no second suit opener rebids a five-card suit. The
minimum rebid now reads "five or more (usually six)" (`shows x>=5`,
`when x>=6`: six-card hands still bid it first), and the five-card
fallback is a minimum too (it went to 18; 16-18 now falls to "nothing
better"). Case in after-interference.test. Measured with the rest of
the read-as work: rebids.notes.md, "Read as the hand holds".

The cue-bid raise's sign-off (`1D (1H) 2H (P) 3D` on four diamonds) read
as rebids.bid's "Rebids diamonds: six or more": that block now takes
only natural free bids (`partner.named(z)`), so the sign-off reads as
it is meant.

Still open here (rebids.notes.md, work queue): the three-card major for
partner's double read as four (6 misdescribed at --limit 50), the
"nothing better" 1S/2S read as four spades (9), 5m after the cue-bid
raise read as 16+ (8).

## Opener's major rebid is six or more (Rick, 2026-10-16)

Brill daily, Rick 2026-10-16, board 8 (dealer W, None; Rusty South,
Brill North): P 1♠ (3♥) X (P) 3♠ (P) 3NT, all pass, on
93.875.AK42.AKQ8 opposite AKJT85.Q9.J9.T32 (6 spades). Par is 4♠ NS;
3NT had no heart stopper. Rick: "North has promised 6+ spades here, so
we have a spade fit, and also we don't have a heart stopper. The lack of
a stopper prohibits the 3NT bid, and the spade fit indicates a 4S bid."
And, widening it: "When opener opens 1M and rebids that M, it should be
treated as 6+ in any context, even though there will be some times
where it's the 'least lie' and there isn't a 6th card in the suit."

- Opener's minimum rebid of his **major** over the negative double now
  reads six or more (`shows x>=6`), at the two and three level. The
  five-card "nothing better to say" rebid below it is kept as the least
  lie and is read by the six-card rule: a read-as call by design, not a
  bug in compare's count. A minor's rebid keeps the 2026-10-09 honest
  "five or more (usually six)".
- Responder's raise and game after the double count the fit from what
  opener showed (`z>=8-partner.z.min`, responder-rebids.bid): two cards
  opposite the six-card rebid, four opposite a four-card answer.
- Responder's notrump after the double (2NT invitation, 3NT game) needs
  their suit stopped (`stop(they.strain)` when their last bid was a
  suit); a 13+ hand with no fit and their suit stopped may bid 3NT
  unbalanced. The fit comes first (4M at priority 0, 3NT below).

The rest (rebids.bid's other major rebids, measurements): rebids.notes.md,
"A major rebid is six or more".

## Sources

- **Jump shifts in competition** (2026-10-05): the ACBL convention card's
  "Jump shift in competition: weak / strong"; BBA's alerts
  ("1X-(1Y)-2Z weak") for the range and the two-level limit. Weak jump
  shifts by responder: standard practice, not yet cited to a book.

- **The conventions:** negative doubles, the redouble, the cue-bid raise
  (limit raise or better) and free bids. Standard practice, not yet
  cited to a book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** negative doubles through 3♠ and what the double,
  redouble, raises and 1NT show; over a two-level or jump overcall, the
  forcing new suit, the 8+ double and the cue-bid raise (2026-09-22);
  "Rick's penalty standard" for the trap pass (two of the top three or
  three of the top five).
- **BBA evidence:** `bba-cli --all-meanings` on the two Basic scenarios
  ("Evidence").
- **BBA probes:** `probes/free-bid-1D-1S.toml` (2026-09-25).
- **Corpus measurements:** each section, judged by par distance and by
  side IMPs (`probes/tools/sideimps.py`); the invitational work queue
  from `probes/tools/missed_games.py` (2026-09-26).
- **Where we differ:** opener's answer to the negative double names an
  unbid four-card minor first, where BBA is inconsistent (for Rick);
  the redouble after their takeout double, where the two yardsticks
  disagree (2026-09-25, for Rick).
- **The Law of Total Tricks** for the minor raises (2026-10-02): Larry
  Cohen, *To Bid or Not to Bid* (1992); BBA's bare-SAYC raises on the
  vanilla random set, and the measurements in that section.
- **Opener's five-card rebid after a negative double** (2026-10-09):
  standard practice, not yet cited to a book.
- **Rick, 2026-10-16** (Brill daily board 8): opener's major rebid is six
  or more in any context, a five-card one the least lie; no stopper, no

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The balancing seat: they opened, partner passed, and RHO passed too.
# Partner is marked with values, so everything is lighter than in the
# direct seat (Rick, 2026-09-22, following BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings):
#
# - the reopening double is 8+ total points with three or more cards in
#   every unbid suit, or 18+ with any shape;
# - a suit at the one level is 8-15 total points with five cards, at the
#   two level 10-15;
# - 1NT is 12-15 balanced with a stopper, not the 15-18 of the direct
#   seat, and 2NT is 19-21.
#
# Systems are on over the balancing 1NT: the notrump modules carry the
# `(1x) P (P) 1N (P)` spelling of their patterns.

module balancing "The balancing seat"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/balancing
  param  one_min = overcalls.one_level_min default 8
  param  two_min = overcalls.two_level_min default 12
  param  nt_min  = nt_overcalls.balance.range_min default 12
  param  nt_max  = nt_overcalls.balance.range_max default 15
  param  oc_max  = overcalls.one_level_max default 17

# ── Reopening ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (1x) P (P)
  X   "Reopening double: 8+ total points and the unbid suits"
      shows hcp+length_points>=8
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C)) | hcp+length_points>=oc_max+1
  1S  "Reopening: five spades, 8-15 total points"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not S
  1H  "Reopening: five hearts, 8-15 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not H
  1D  "Reopening: five diamonds, 8-15 total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not D
  2C  "Reopening: five clubs, 10-15 total points"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not C
  2D  "Reopening: five diamonds, 10-15 total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not D, x is not C
  2H  "Reopening: five hearts, 10-15 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=two_min-2, hcp+length_points<=15
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
  1N  "Balancing notrump: {nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max
      when  stop(x)
  2N  "19-21 balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp=19..21
      when  stop(x)
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"  priority -10

# The balancing seat (`balancing.bid`): notes

They opened, partner passed, RHO passed. Cases: `balancing.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

Follow BBA's meanings, which are the usual lighter balancing ranges:

- **reopening double** 8+ total points with three or more cards in every
  unbid suit (or 18+ with any shape, as in the direct seat);
- **a suit at the one level** 8-15 total points with five cards, **at the
  two level** 10-15;
- **1NT** 12-15 balanced with a stopper — `nt_overcalls.balance.range_min`
  and `_max`, not the 15-18 of the direct seat — and **2NT** 19-21.

A balanced 16+ is too strong for the balancing notrump and doubles first.

## Evidence

`bba-cli --all-meanings` on the `Balancing` scenario (21GF cards, 5,197
calls). Grouped by the opening they reopened over:

| call | BBA's meaning |
|---|---|
| X | "reopening double", 8-37 total points, 3+ in each unbid suit |
| 1NT | "NT style", 12-15 total points, 2-5 in every suit |
| 2NT | "NT style", 19-21 |
| suit, one level | "bidable suit", 8-15, 5+ |
| suit, two level | "bidable suit", 10-15, 5+ |
| cue bid | Michaels (not on our card) |

Advancer over the reopening **double** needs no new rules: those
contexts in `takeout-double.bid` carry the balancing spelling of their
patterns (`(1x) P (P) X (P)` beside `(1x) X (P)`), and the notrump
modules carry `(1x) P (P) 1N (P)`, so systems are on over the balancing
notrump too.

Advancer over the reopening **suit bid** now has its own block in
`advances.bid` (2026-09-23): partner is 8-15 rather than 8-17, so the
raise is 9-11 rather than 7-11, 1NT is 10-11, 2NT 13-15, a new suit at
the one level 7+ and at the two level 11+, and the cue bid 13+. Those
are BBA's own `Balancing` meanings. The direct-seat block no longer
carries the `(1x) P (P) 1y (P)` spelling. Effect over the three
balancing scenarios: calls +5, contracts 11.7% → 12.1%, par +98 IMPs,
identical auctions 8.7% → 8.1%.

A two-level overcall in the balancing seat is left to the bare pass rule
in `advances.bid`: BBA's advancer passed 32 of the 33 in the corpus.

Effect: the `Balancing` scenario gained 6.7 points of call agreement,
11.0 of identical auctions and 13.4 of contracts; Too_Strong_for_Overcall4th
+4.1 calls; Trap_Pass_Opener +1.9 calls and +6.2 auctions. Summed over
the 46 scenarios that moved: calls +29.8, contracts +11.0, auctions -6.8
(a handful of weak-notrump scenarios where BBA passes the hand out).

## Gaps and open questions

- **Jump overcalls in the balancing seat** are not written: a jump there
  is natural and intermediate, not the weak jump of the direct seat.
- Reopening over a **two-level or preemptive opening**, and the balancing
  double of 1NT.
- Michaels and the unusual notrump in balancing (the direct-seat ones are
  in `two-suited-overcalls.bid`, 2026-09-28; Basic-Bridge plays neither).
- Partner should read a reopening **double** as lighter than a direct
  one; those advance rules still use the direct-seat ranges (the suit
  overcall no longer does).

## Sources

- **Rick's rulings:** follow BBA's meanings, which are the usual lighter
  balancing ranges (2026-09-22).
- **BBA evidence:** `bba-cli --all-meanings` on the Balancing scenario
  (21GF cards, 5,197 calls), tabled in "Evidence"; advancer's ranges over
  a balancing suit bid are BBA's own Balancing meanings. No
  `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Book practice:** the lighter balancing ranges are standard practice,
  not yet cited to a book or article.
- **Corpus measurements:** the three balancing scenarios and the 46 that
  moved (2026-09-23).
- **Where we differ:** advancer still reads a reopening double with the
  direct-seat ranges (Gaps).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Cappelletti (Hamilton) and Modified Cappelletti over their 1NT, direct
# and balancing (vs-1nt.notes.md has the sources and the BBA probes).
#
#   X    penalty, 15+ HCP                     (both)
#   2♣   one long suit, six or more            (Cappelletti)
#        a long minor, or a major and a minor  (Modified)
#   2♦   both majors, 5-4 or longer            (both)
#   2♥/2♠ that major (5) and a minor (4)       (Cappelletti)
#        that major, six or more, one-suited   (Modified)
#   2NT  both minors, 5-5 or longer            (both)
#
# Strength (BBA on 21GF-DEFAULT, probes/vs-1N-capp.toml, 1,500 hands):
# BBA doubles from 15 HCP, shows a six-card suit from 9-10 HCP and a
# two-suiter from 9; it passes a 5-4 major-minor hand whose four-card
# minor has no top honour. We count HCP plus a point a card beyond four
# in each suit: 12 for a one-suiter (10 HCP with six cards, 9 with
# seven), 10 for a two-suiter (9 HCP with 5-4, 8 with 5-5), 8 for the
# minors (6 HCP with 5-5 minors, as BBA at 6-7 with 6-5). With 18+ HCP
# the double comes first whatever the shape.

module cappelletti "Cappelletti and Modified Cappelletti over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/cappelletti
  skill  competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (below)

# ── Direct and balancing: the calls both versions share ──────────────
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti | def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  X   "Penalty: 15+ HCP"
      shows hcp>=15
      sets  ask=nt_penalty
  2D  "Cappelletti: both majors, 5-4 or longer"   alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      when  system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_majors
  2N  "Cappelletti: both minors, 5-5 or longer"   alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=17
      when  system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# brill (the Brill card): every Cappelletti bid has 10+ HCP, and 2D is
# 5-5 in the majors. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "Cappelletti - majors":
# `H >= 5 and S >= 5 and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - minors": `C >= 5 and
# D >= 5 and totalpoints >= 15 and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - single
# suited": `totalpoints >= 10 and lengthlongestsuit >= 6 and singlesuited
# and hcp >= 10`; "Cappelletti - S and a minor": `S >= 5 and (C >= 4 or D
# >= 4) and loserlevel >= 2 and totalpoints >= 12 and hcp >= 10`.
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti | def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti, system is brill
  2D  "Cappelletti: both majors, 5-5 or longer, 10+ HCP"   alert
      shows H>=5, S>=5, hcp>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_majors
  2N  "Cappelletti: both minors, 5-5 or longer, 10+ HCP"   alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# ── Cappelletti ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/cappelletti
  2C  "Cappelletti: one long suit, six or more"   alert
      shows longest>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17 | (system is brill, hcp<=18)
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=capp_one
  2H  "Cappelletti: five hearts and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows H>=5, S<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Cappelletti: five spades and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows S>=5, H<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      shows hcp>=10 | system is not brill
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)

# Advancer over 2♣: the 2♦ relay asks for the suit. BBA and GIB pass with
# six clubs and bid a six-card major of their own, not forcing
# (probes/vs-1N-capp-2C-adv.toml: 526 relays, 32 2♥, 21 2♠, 21 passes).
when asked capp_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2D  "Relay: bid your suit"                      alert
      sets  ask=capp_relay
  P   "Long clubs: to play"                       shows C>=6
  2H  "Six or more hearts: to play"               shows H>=6, hcp<=12
  2S  "Six or more spades: to play"               shows S>=6, hcp<=12

when asked capp_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My suit is diamonds"                       shows D>=6
  2H  "My suit is hearts"                         shows H>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
  2S  "My suit is spades"                         shows S>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)
  3C  "My suit is clubs"                          shows C>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(C)

# ── Modified Cappelletti ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2♣ is a long minor or a major-minor two-suiter; 2♥/2♠ one-suited.
after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/modified_cappelletti
  2C  "Modified Cappelletti: a long minor, or a major and a minor"   alert
      shows ((C>=6 | D>=6), second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12) | (((H>=5, S<=3) | (S>=5, H<=3)), (C>=4 | D>=4), hcp+length_points>=10)
      shows hcp<=17
      sets  ask=mcapp_one
  2H  "Modified Cappelletti: six or more hearts"  alert
      shows H>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(H)
  2S  "Modified Cappelletti: six or more spades"  alert
      shows S>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)

# Advancer relays: 2♣ may be diamonds or a major, so it is not passed.
when asked mcapp_one, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2D  "Relay: show your hand"                     alert
      sets  ask=mcapp_relay

when asked mcapp_relay, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "Long diamonds"                             shows D>=6
  2H  "Hearts and a minor"                        shows H>=5, C>=4 | D>=4
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Spades and a minor"                        shows S>=5, C>=4 | D>=4
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)
  3C  "Long clubs"                                shows C>=6

# Cappelletti (`cappelletti.bid`): notes

Cappelletti (Hamilton) and Modified Cappelletti over their 1NT, direct
and balancing seat. Cases: `cappelletti.test`. The answers every defence
shares (the majors, a major and a minor, the minors, the penalty double)
are in `vs-1nt.bid`; the comparison of the defences, the corpus figures
and how the opponents' calls are read are in `vs-1nt.notes.md`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-28)

"People play all of these, we'd like our bot to be compatible with their
cards." The card's `competitive.vs_1nt_strong.system` decides
(`cappelletti` from the `.bbsa` key `Cappelletti`, on for 21GF-DEFAULT,
21GF-GIB and eight other cards; `modified_cappelletti` is a new option
with no `.bbsa` key).

## The calls

| Call | Cappelletti | Modified Cappelletti |
|---|---|---|
| X | penalty, 15+ HCP | the same |
| 2♣ | one long suit, six or more (advancer relays 2♦) | a long minor, or 5-4 in a major and a minor (advancer relays 2♦) |
| 2♦ | both majors, 5-4 or longer | the same |
| 2♥/2♠ | that major (5+) and a four-card minor | that major, six or more, one-suited |
| 2NT | both minors, 5-5 or longer | the same |

After the Cappelletti relay the overcaller passes with diamonds and bids
2♥, 2♠ or 3♣; after the Modified relay he passes with diamonds, bids
2♥/2♠ with that major and a minor (then the 2♥/2♠ answers of vs-1nt.bid
apply) or 3♣ with clubs. The Cappelletti advancer may pass 2♣ with six
clubs or bid a six-card major of his own (BBA and GIB both do); the
Modified advancer always relays, since 2♣ may be diamonds or a major.

## BBA (probes, 21GF-DEFAULT, 2026-09-28)

`probes/vs-1N-capp.toml` (1,500 hands, direct seat): BBA's meanings are
exactly the table above: "Cappelletti, strong" X from 15 HCP, "any 6+
suit" 2♣, "both majors" 2♦ (4-4 or longer in its alert, 5-4 in practice),
"5M-4m" 2♥/2♠, "Unusual 2NT" 5-5 minors. The strength it needs:

- 2♣ from 9 HCP (half the hands at 9, 60% at 10, nearly all from 11);
- the two-suiters from 9 (5-5 at 9-10 always, 5-4 majors half the time
  at 9);
- 2♥/2♠ with 5-4 only about a third of the time at 9-14: it passes when
  the four-card minor has no ace, king or queen (AKQ73.KQ5.9.8732,
  72.AJT32.K4.J743 pass; K3.QT874.KJT8.54 bids). We ask for a top honour
  in the minor;
- 2NT from 6 HCP with 6-5.

We count HCP plus a point a card beyond four in each suit: 12 for the
one-suited 2♣, 10 for the two-suiters, 8 for 2NT. After the rules,
**1,302 of the 1,500 hands agree with BBA** (87%). The differences: BBA
passes 159 hands we bid (a 15-HCP double 42 times, where BBA passes 16 of
51 at 15; 2♣ 51 times at the bottom of the range), and we pass 18 it bids.

`probes/vs-1N-capp-bal.toml` (800 hands, balancing seat): the same
meanings, a point or two stronger (2♣ from 11 HCP). We use the direct
thresholds; balancing 2♣ lost 137 IMPs to the side that bid it (par
distance +99): see Gaps.

Advancer (`probes/vs-1N-capp-2C-adv.toml`, `-2D-adv`, `-2H-adv`,
`-2S-adv`, `-2N-adv`, `-X-adv`) and the overcaller's rebids
(`-2C-2D`, `-2H-2N`): recorded in vs-1nt.notes.md, where those rules
live.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- X at 15 HCP: BBA passes a third of the 15-counts. We double all of
  them (the side that doubled gained 2,186 IMPs over 1,367 boards on the
  corpus, par distance -1,286: vs-1nt.notes.md).
- A 5-4 major-minor hand with a poor minor passes, as BBA; with 15-17
  and no call it passes too (the double wants 15, so 15-17 doubles).
- The advancer after a one-suited answer raises a major with two cards
  (11-12 invites, 13+ bids game); BBA's continuations there were not
  probed.

## Brill (general.system = brill, 2026-10-15)

Brill's treatment, played on the Brill card only (`cards/json/Brill.json`, `general.system = brill`: a stand-in until convention-card's `general.style` takes a `brill` value; cards/README.md "Brill"). Rusty plays the Brill dailies as South with three Brill robots, so it should read and bid what they do. Every other card is unchanged (a `.test` line on 21GF-GIB beside each Brill line; `compare --limit 50` tripwire against main: no board changed).

Every Cappelletti bid has 10+ HCP, 2D is five-five in the majors, and the
2C one-suiter goes to 18 ("Cappelletti - majors": `H >= 5 and S >= 5 and hcp
>= 10`; "- minors": `C >= 5 and D >= 5 and totalpoints >= 15 and hcp >= 10`;
"- single suited": `totalpoints >= 10 and lengthlongestsuit >= 6 and
singlesuited and hcp >= 10`; "- S and a minor": `S >= 5 and (C >= 4 or D >=
4) and loserlevel >= 2 and totalpoints >= 12 and hcp >= 10`). With five-four
in the majors brill passes. Brill marks the calls artificial and so should
we, on every card (our Cappelletti rules carry `alert` but not
`artificial`): left for Rick, as it changes the default cards' reading.

Measured with `probes/tools/brill_probe.py report --card Brill` over the top 2000 corpus auctions (calls of this group, board-weighted, our reading against Brill's): 0% -> 0% of 3,456 boards, all of it the artificial flag (39% -> 100% ignoring it).

## Sources

- Brill /explain, 2026-10-15 (Thorvald Aagaard's public Brill service, answers cached in `.rbb-cache/brill-service/explain/`): the rule text quoted in the `brill` section and in the `.bid` comments. Applies to the Brill card only (`general.system = brill`, cards/README.md "Brill").
- Bridge Bum, "Cappelletti (Hamilton)", https://www.bridgebum.com/cappelletti.php
  (the calls; advancer's 2♦ relay, pass with long clubs, 2♥/2♠ natural;
  and its "Modified Cappelletti" section: 2♣ "a minor one-suiter, or at
  least 5-4 or 4-5 in a major and a minor", relay 2♦, then pass with
  diamonds, 2♥/2♠ with that major and a minor, 3♣ with clubs; 2♥/2♠
  "6+").
- Wikipedia, "Cappelletti convention", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappelletti_convention
  (penalty double 15+; 2♦ majors "traditionally 5-5 but often 5-4").
- ACBL Unit 390 (Simon), "Modified Cappelletti",
  https://www.acblunit390.org/Simon/modcapp.htm (a variant where 2♣ is a
  *diamond* one-suiter or a major-minor two-suiter and 3♣ is natural; we
  follow Bridge Bum's "either minor", which is what the relay answers
  3♣ with clubs imply in both).
- GIB (BBO's robot, what the GIB corpus in Practice-Bidding-Scenarios
  plays), queried through https://netbridge.dk/gib.html (its bidding
  database, sequences `1N-*`, `1N-2C-P-*`, `1N-2C-P-2D-P-*`, `1N-2D-P-*`,
  `1N-2H-P-*`, `1N-2N-P-*`, `1N-D-P-*`, `1N-P-P-*`): X "Penalty double --
  16+ HCP"; 2♣ "Cappelletti - single suited -- 14- HCP; 10+ total
  points"; 2♦ "majors -- 5+ ♥; 5+ ♠"; 2♥/2♠ "hearts/spades and a minor";
  2NT "minors -- 5+ ♣ 5+ ♦"; the same in the balancing seat; advancer
  passes 2♣ with long clubs, 2♦ relay, 2♥/2♠ six-card suits, 2NT over
  2♥/2♠ "Show me your other suit".

## Gaps and open questions

- **Balancing 2♣** lost on both yardsticks (vs-1nt.notes.md). BBA wants
  11+ HCP there; we use the direct 12-with-length. Worth a probe-driven
  threshold of its own.
- The advancer's invitational 2NT over 2♣ (GIB: 11-14 balanced) is not
  written: a strong advancer relays and then raises.
- Nothing after the opponents compete over our call (the answers need
  RHO to pass or double); the fallback is pass.
- Cappelletti over a weak notrump: played the same (the card's field is
  "vs strong NT"; BBA and GIB do not change it either).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Maximal doubles (`doubles.maximal`). We have bid and raised a major,
# 1M .. 2M, and they bid three of the suit directly below ours (3D under
# hearts, 3H under spades): there is no room left for a game try, so the
# double is the game try and three of our major is only competitive.
# Partner signs off in 3M with a minimum or bids game with a maximum.
# (Bridge Bum, "Maximal Double"; Todd, "Non-Takeout Doubles", Advancing
# in Bridge 357.) Alertable.
#
# Applies to the opener after 1M (any) 2M and to the overcaller after
# (1x) 1M (any) 2M. Against any other three-level bid (not the suit just
# below ours) the double stays what it was.

module maximal-doubles "Maximal doubles"
  kind   convention
  card   competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/maximal_doubles

# ── The opener or the overcaller ─────────────────────────────────────
# The game try is the opener's usual invitation over a single raise,
# 17-18 support points (rebids.bid); 3M competes with six trumps (five and
# a shape) and no game interest.
after 1M (*) 2M (3x) | (1y) 1M (*) 2M (3x) when (M is H, x is D) | (M is S, x is H)
  X   "Maximal double: a game try in {M}"
      alert  artificial
      shows  tp(M)=17..18
      sets   trump=M, ask=maximal(M)
      priority 2
  3{M} "Competitive: no game interest"
      shows M>=6 | (M>=5, !balanced), tp(M)<=16
      sets  trump=M
      priority 1
  4{M} "Game: 19+"
      shows tp(M)>=19
      sets  trump=M
      priority 1
  P   "No further bid"  priority -5

# ── Partner answers the game try ─────────────────────────────────────
# The raise was 6-10: the top of it (9+ support points) accepts.
when asked maximal(t)
  4{t} "Accepts the game try: a maximum raise"
      shows tp(t)>=9
      priority 1
  3{t} "Declines: a minimum raise"
      priority 1

# ── Partner after the competitive 3M ─────────────────────────────────
after 1M (*) 2M (3x) 3M (P) | (1y) 1M (*) 2M (3x) 3M (P) when (M is H, x is D) | (M is S, x is H)
  P   "No further bid"  priority 1
# Maximal doubles (`maximal-doubles.bid`): notes

Switched on by `doubles.maximal` (21GF-WJS-MSS, Precision,
Precision-14-16). Cases: `maximal-doubles.test`.

## What it plays (2026-10-05)

After 1M (any) 2M or (1x) 1M (any) 2M, when they bid three of the suit
directly below ours (3D under hearts, 3H under spades):

- X: the game try, 17-18 support points (the opener's usual invitation
  over a single raise in rebids.bid), alerted;
- 3M: competitive, six trumps or five with an unbalanced hand, 16 or
  less;
- 4M: 19+;
- partner answers the double with 4M on a maximum raise (9+ support
  points), else 3M; after the competitive 3M he passes.

Over any other three-level bid the double keeps its old meaning.

## BBA (fast-lane compare, 2026-10-05)

The scenarios' corpus (Maximal_Double, Maximal_After_Overcall) was bid
on 21GF-SPECIALS, which has `Maximal Doubles = 0` although the scenario
asks for them, so BBA's 3M there is invitational and its doubles are
penalty. With `--set doubles.maximal=true` call agreement 73.3% ->
74.1% (100 boards); the one remaining divergence at the maximal call is
the convention itself (our X game try where BBA bids 3M).

## Open questions

- Partner's penalty pass of the maximal double (a trump stack in their
  suit) is not written; the sources say partner signs off or bids game.
- Not applied when the responder, rather than the opener, is the one
  to act over their 3x (1M P 2M P P 3x), nor to minor-suit raises.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only
maximal-doubles`. IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the
convention makes fewer; "actor" is the side that made the first
differing call. Maximal_Double and Maximal_After_Overcall: 85 boards
changed; actor contract +10, doubling +39; other side contract +42,
doubling -54; double-dummy +63 to the actor; halves +4/+45 (z +1.3):
leans gain.

## Sources

- Bridge Bum, "Maximal Double" (https://www.bridgebum.com/maximal_double.php):
  when it applies, X a game try, 3M competitive, partner signs off or
  bids game; alertable. Bridge Bum lists it after the opponents bid
  *and raise* the suit below ours; we also apply it when they introduce
  it at the three level (as the scenarios' filters do), where the lack
  of room is the same.
- Robert S. Todd, "Non-Takeout Doubles: Card-Showing, Maximal, Penalty,
  Lead-Directing", Adventures in Bridge 357 (cited by convention-card;
  not read here).
- Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `btn/Maximal_Double.btn`,
  `btn/Maximal_After_Overcall.btn`.
