# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Landy and Multi-Landy over their 1NT, direct and balancing
# (vs-1nt.notes.md). BBA plays Multi-Landy on seven cards (21GF-Multi,
# 21GF-SPECIALS2 and others) as Woolsey describes it; its meanings,
# from probes/vs-1N-mlandy.toml (1,000 hands, 21GF-Multi):
#
#   X    a four-card major and a longer minor, 12+ HCP
#   2♣   both majors
#   2♦   one major, six or more (the "multi")
#   2♥/2♠ that major (5) and a minor (4)
#   2NT  both minors
#
# Landy is 2♣ for the majors, everything else natural (overcalls.bid).

module multi-landy "Landy and Multi-Landy over their 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  vs-1nt
  skill  competitive_bidding/multi_landy
  skill  competitive_bidding/landy
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/multi_landy | def is competitive_bidding/landy
  2C  "Landy: both majors, 5-4 or longer"          alert
      shows H>=4, S>=4, H+S>=9, hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_majors

after (1N) | (1N) P (P) when def is competitive_bidding/multi_landy
  X   "Multi-Landy: a four-card major and a longer minor"   alert
      shows H=4 | S=4, C>=5 | D>=5, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=ml_x
  2D  "Multi-Landy: six or more in one major"      alert
      shows H>=6 | S>=6, second_longest<=4, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=ml_multi
  2H  "Multi-Landy: five hearts and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows H>=5, S<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_mm(H)
  2S  "Multi-Landy: five spades and a four-card minor"   alert
      shows S>=5, H<=3, ((C>=4, quality(C)>=fair) | (D>=4, quality(D)>=fair))
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_mm(S)
  2N  "Multi-Landy: both minors, 5-5 or longer"    alert
      shows C>=5, D>=5, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp<=17
      sets  ask=nt_minors

# Advancer over the double bids 2♣, pass or correct to the minor.
when asked ml_x, rho.last=P | rho.last=X | rho.last=XX
  2C  "Pass or correct: bid your minor"            alert
      sets  ask=ml_minor
when asked ml_minor, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My minor is clubs"                          shows C>=5
  2D  "My minor is diamonds"                       shows D>=5

# Advancer over the multi 2♦ bids 2♥, pass or correct.
when asked ml_multi, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  2H  "Pass or correct: bid your major"            alert
      sets  ask=ml_major
when asked ml_major, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My major is hearts"                         shows H>=6
  2S  "My major is spades"                         shows S>=6
      sets  ask=nt_one(S)

# Landy and Multi-Landy (`multi-landy.bid`): notes

Landy and Multi-Landy over their 1NT, direct and balancing seat. Cases:
`multi-landy.test`. Shared answers: `vs-1nt.bid`; the comparison of the
defences: `vs-1nt.notes.md`.

Not in Rick's list of 2026-09-28 (Cappelletti, Modified Cappelletti,
Meckwell, DONT), but seven BBA cards turn `Multi-Landy` on (21GF-Multi,
21GF-SPECIALS2, 21GF-MSS, 21GF-NoInvertedMinor, 21GF-PolishTwoSuiters,
21GF-GIB-Bergen, Precision), and until now the key only switched our
natural overcalls off, so those cards passed every hand over 1NT. The
module costs little once the shared answers exist. `.bbsa` keys
`Multi-Landy` and `Landy` were already mapped.

## The calls

Multi-Landy as BBA plays it on 21GF-Multi (`probes/vs-1N-mlandy.toml`,
1,000 hands; its alerts in quotes), which is Woolsey's version:

| Call | Shows | BBA | Advancer |
|---|---|---|---|
| X | a four-card major and a longer minor | "4M-5m", 12+ HCP | 2♣ pass or correct to the minor |
| 2♣ | both majors | "both majors", 9+ | preference |
| 2♦ | one major, six or more | "Multi", 9-17 | 2♥ pass or correct |
| 2♥/2♠ | that major and a four-card minor | "5M-4m", 9+ | as Cappelletti's 2♥/2♠ |
| 2NT | both minors | "Unusual 2NT" | the longer minor |

Landy: 2♣ both majors, the rest natural (overcalls.bid).

## Sources

- Bridge Bum, "Multi-Landy (Woolsey)", https://www.bridgebum.com/multi_landy.php
- Wikipedia, "Cappelletti convention", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappelletti_convention
  (Multi-Landy as "reverse Cappelletti": 2♣ and 2♦ swapped).
- BBA on 21GF-Multi, `probes/vs-1N-mlandy.toml`.

Bridge-Classroom's `ntDefenses.js` lists Multi-Landy with a penalty
double and natural 2♥/2♠; that is closer to plain Landy. We follow BBA
(and Woolsey) because the BBA cards that carry the key play it that way.

## Gaps

- Woolsey's double also covers a six-card minor and strong hands
  (Bridge Bum); BBA's alert names only the 4M-5m hand, and so do we.
- The advancer's continuations were not probed; the preference and
  pass-or-correct answers are the shared ones.
- Over their Landy/Multi-Landy 2♣ (majors) our side still plays
  systems on (Stayman by double: nt-interference.bid); a cue-bid
  structure would suit it better.

files.rules/competitive/overcalls.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Overcalls of a one-level opening on our right (Rick, 2026-09-22):
#
# - a simple overcall is always a five-card suit: 8-17 total points at the
#   one level, 12-17 at the two level (BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which
#   Rick adopted). No four-card overcalls on this card;
# - too strong to overcall (18+ total points) is a takeout double first and
#   the suit afterwards, whatever the shape (takeout-double.bid); the
#   overcall's own ceiling is 16 HCP (17 from 2026-09-25, 16 from
#   2026-09-27 so that 17+ is the power double), so a six-card suit with
#   16 still overcalls, as BBA does;
# - a jump overcall follows the weak-two rules: six cards, 4-10 HCP (10
#   as BBA, 2026-09-25), and vulnerable two of the top three or three of
#   the top five honours;
# - a direct 1NT overcall is 15-18 balanced with a stopper in their suit,
#   a point wider than our 1NT opening.
#
# With two five-card suits the higher-ranking one is bid, as in base.bid:
# each rule requires its suit to be at least as long as the suits above it
# and longer than the suits below it, so only one of them can fire.

module overcalls "Suit and notrump overcalls"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/overcalls
  skill  partnership_bidding/overcalls
  param  one_min = overcalls.one_level_min default 8
  param  one_max = overcalls.one_level_max default 16
  param  two_min = overcalls.two_level_min default 12
  param  two_max = overcalls.two_level_max default 17
  param  jump    = overcalls.jump default weak
  param  nt_min  = nt_overcalls.direct.range_min default 15
  param  nt_max  = nt_overcalls.direct.range_max default 18
  param  system  = general.system   # `brill`: the Brill card's treatments (1NT overcall)
  param  nt_def  = defence_to_1nt.strong
  param  raptor  = competitive_bidding/raptor default false
  param  sandwich = competitive_bidding/sandwich_nt default false

# ── Simple overcalls at the one level ────────────────────────────────
# `(1x)` binds x to the suit they opened; the rules below never bid it.
#
# The suit has to be worth bidding (Rick, 2026-09-23): two of the top
# three or three of the top five honours, **or else an opening hand** --
# it takes 12 total points to overcall on a ten-high suit. Without that
# we overcalled 1♠ on J8753 with 10 HCP and pushed the auction up for
# the opponents.
after (1x)
  1S  "Overcall: five spades, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not S
      when  quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  1H  "Overcall: five hearts, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not H
      when  quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  1D  "Overcall: five diamonds, {one_min}-{one_max} total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not D
      when  quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12

# ── Simple overcalls at the two level ────────────────────────────────
# Only where the suit cannot be shown at the one level: clubs over any
# opening, diamonds over a major, hearts over 1S. A two-level bid in a
# suit that could have been shown more cheaply is a jump, below.
# Up to the one-level maximum in HCP as well (ticket b400, 2026-10-02):
# a 16-count with a good six-card suit is 18 total points, over the
# two-level maximum but short of the power double's 17 HCP, and it used
# to pass. Now no direct-seat pass holds more than 16 HCP.
# The minimum is in HCP, a point less with six cards (ticket b238,
# 2026-10-04; probes/oc-2C-over-1D.toml): BBA overcalls 2C over 1D from
# 12 HCP with five clubs, 11 with six or seven, never on less (a weak
# hand with seven clubs preempts at 3C). 12 total points let 10 HCP and
# six clubs overcall, and partner read the overcall as 3+ HCP.
after (1x)
  2C  "Overcall: five clubs, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D
      shows hcp>=two_min | (C>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not C
      when  C>=6 | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=4
  2D  "Overcall: five diamonds, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (D>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not D, x is not C
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=4
  2H  "Overcall: five hearts, {two_min}-{two_max} total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (H>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp+length_points<=two_max | hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=4

# ── Notrump overcall ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# With a five-card major we show the major instead, which is what BBA
# does: every 1NT overcall in the corpus had four cards or fewer in both.
after (1x)
  1N  "{nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x), !raptor             # Raptor 1NT shows two suits (raptor.bid)
      when  system is not brill
# brill (the Brill card, 15-17): balanced or semi-balanced, so a five-card
# major will do. Brill /explain, 2026-10-15, "Overcalling 1Mi with 1N" and
# "Overcalling 1Ma with 1N", "15-17": `stopper('C') and hcp>= 15 and hcp<=
# 17 and (balanced or semibalanced)`.
after (1x) when system is brill
  1N  "{nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced or semi-balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced | semibalanced, C=2..5, D=2..5, H=2..5, S=2..5, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max
      when  stop(x), !raptor

# Advancer when their partner raises over our 1NT overcall: nothing was
# written (~160 corpus boards). BBA, 2026-09-25: a five-card suit at the
# two level to play; a six-card minor at the three level; 3NT with 9+
# and their suit held. BBA also doubles for takeout short in their suit;
# the double cost 449 IMPs against par here, so it is left out.
after (1x) 1N (2x)
  2S  "To play: five or more spades"          shows S>=5, hcp<=8
      when  x is H
  3C  "To play: six or more clubs"            shows C>=6, hcp<=8, H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
  3D  "To play: six or more diamonds"         shows D>=6, D>C, hcp<=8, H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
  3N  "Game: 9+, {x} held"                    shows hcp>=9, stop(x)
  P   "Not enough to advance"                        shows hcp>=0
      priority -5

# ── Over their 1NT, natural (2026-09-25, probes/vs-1N.toml) ───────────
# No rules existed. BBA on Basic-Bridge (no conventional defence): a
# five-card suit at the two level with 12+ total points (six cards from
# about 10 HCP), the longest suit and the higher of two equal; a
# preemptive three-level bid with seven cards and 4-10. (BBA also doubles
# with 13+ and 4-3-3-3; neutral, left out.) Judged from the overcalling
# side: +1,007 IMPs over 237 changed boards (par distance says -825, but
# par distance counts a successful overcall against us: overcalls.notes.md).
# The pass is shared by every defence, and the conventional defences
# preempt in a narrower range (vs-1nt.bid). Landy keeps the natural 2♦/2♥/2♠ and uses 2♣ for the majors
# (multi-landy.bid).
# `natural` is the card's explicit word for it (convention-card 0.43; it used to load as `other`).
after (1N) when nt_def is none | nt_def is competitive_bidding/landy
  2S  "Natural: five spades, 12+ total points"    shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  2H  "Natural: five hearts, 12+ total points"    shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  2D  "Natural: five diamonds, 12+ total points"  shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
after (1N) when nt_def is none
  2C  "Natural: five clubs, 12+ total points"     shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
  3S  "Preemptive: seven spades, 4-10"            shows S>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1
  3H  "Preemptive: seven hearts, 4-10"            shows H>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1
  3D  "Preemptive: seven diamonds, 4-10"          shows D>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1
  3C  "Preemptive: seven clubs, 4-10"             shows C>=7, hcp=4..10
      priority 1

# ── Weak jump overcalls ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# The weak-two rules of preempts.bid: six cards and 4-10 HCP, and
# vulnerable two of the top three or three of the top five honours.
# A jump is only a jump where the suit was biddable more cheaply, so
# each rule names the openings it applies to.
after (1x) when jump is weak
  2D  "Weak jump overcall: six diamonds, 4-10"   shows D=6, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is not D, x is not H, x is not S
      when  !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3
  2H  "Weak jump overcall: six hearts, 4-10"     shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when  x is not H, x is not S
      when  !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  2S  "Weak jump overcall: six spades, 4-10"     shows S=6, hcp=4..10
      when  x is not S
      when  !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3

# Seven-card suits jump to the three level, as they open at the three
# level uncontested.
after (1x) when jump is weak
  3C  "Jump overcall: seven clubs, 4-10"    shows C=7, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is not C
      when  !vul | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3
  3D  "Jump overcall: seven diamonds, 4-10" shows D=7, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is not D
      when  !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3
  3H  "Jump overcall: seven hearts, 4-10"   shows H=7, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when  x is not H
      when  !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  3S  "Jump overcall: seven spades, 4-10"   shows S=7, hcp=4..10
      when  x is not S
      when  !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3

# ── The sandwich seat: (1x) P (1y) ───────────────────────────────────
# Fourth hand after opener's partner has responded one of a suit
# (2026-10-07). Nothing was written here, so this hand always passed
# ("Defending: nothing more to say"): 78% of the positions where BBA
# acted and that rule passed were such first entries (total-tricks.notes.md),
# and conventions that answer this interference (support doubles and
# redoubles) never arose in our own auctions. The same overcalls as in
# the direct seat, in the suits they have not bid, and the same weak
# jumps; 1NT is natural and stops both their suits; the double is for
# takeout of the two unbid suits. BBA, 21GF-DEFAULT
# (probes/oc4-1D-P-1H.toml, oc4-1H-P-1S.toml): overcalls 8-17 total
# points at the one level and 12-17 at the two, 1NT 15-17, the double
# 12+ with three or more in both unbid suits, weak jumps as in the
# direct seat. Our double wants eight cards in the two suits (or 15+):
# BBA passes most 12-14 hands with four-three. A five-card suit
# overcalls first. Partner has passed, so there is no power double
# here: strong hands overcall (up to 18 HCP) or double. Not written:
# BBA's 2NT for the two lowest unbid suits and its natural bids in
# responder's suit (2H, 3H over 1D P 1H with six or seven hearts).
after (1x) P (1y) when y is not x
  1S  "Overcall: five spades, {one_min}-18 total points"
      shows S>=5, S>=H | x is H | y is H, S>=D | x is D | y is D, S>=C | x is C | y is C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=18
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  1H  "Overcall: five hearts, {one_min}-18 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S | x is S | y is S, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C
      shows hcp+length_points>=one_min, hcp<=18
      when  x is not H, y is not H, y is not S
      when  quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3 | hcp+length_points>=12
  2C  "Overcall: five clubs, {two_min}-18 total points"
      shows C>=5, C>S | x is S | y is S, C>H | x is H | y is H, C>D | x is D | y is D
      shows hcp>=two_min | (C>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp<=18
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      when  C>=6 | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=4
  2D  "Overcall: five diamonds, {two_min}-18 total points"
      shows D>=5, D>S | x is S | y is S, D>H | x is H | y is H, D>=C | x is C | y is C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (D>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp<=18
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=4
  2H  "Overcall: five hearts, {two_min}-18 total points"
      shows H>=5, H>S | x is S | y is S, H>=D | x is D | y is D, H>=C | x is C | y is C
      shows hcp>=two_min | (H>=6, hcp>=two_min-1), hcp<=18
      when  x is not H, y is S
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=4
  1N  "{nt_min}-{nt_max} balanced, both their suits stopped"
      shows balanced, hcp>=nt_min, hcp<=nt_max, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x), stop(y), !passed_hand, !sandwich   # Sandwich 1NT shows the two unbid suits
  # The takeout double of the two suits they have not bid.
  X   "Takeout: hearts and spades, 12+"   shows H>=3, S>=3, H+S>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is C, y is D
      priority -1
  X   "Takeout: diamonds and spades, 12+" shows D>=3, S>=3, D+S>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is C, y is H
      priority -1
  X   "Takeout: diamonds and hearts, 12+" shows D>=3, H>=3, D+H>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is C, y is S
      priority -1
  X   "Takeout: clubs and spades, 12+"    shows C>=3, S>=3, C+S>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is D, y is H
      priority -1
  X   "Takeout: clubs and hearts, 12+"    shows C>=3, H>=3, C+H>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is D, y is S
      priority -1
  X   "Takeout: both minors, 12+"         shows C>=3, D>=3, C+D>=8 | hcp>=15, hcp>=12
      when  x is H, y is S
      priority -1
  # With 15+, four or more in both and not balanced (1NT), the double
  # comes before an overcall.
  X   "Takeout: hearts and spades, 15+"     shows H>=4, S>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is C, y is D
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout: diamonds and spades, 15+"   shows D>=4, S>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is C, y is H
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout: diamonds and hearts, 15+"   shows D>=4, H>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is C, y is S
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout: clubs and spades, 15+"      shows C>=4, S>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is D, y is H
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout: clubs and hearts, 15+"      shows C>=4, H>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is D, y is S
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout: both minors, 15+"           shows C>=4, D>=4, hcp>=15, !balanced
      when  x is H, y is S
      priority 1
  P   "No overcall"  priority -10

after (1x) P (1y) when y is not x, jump is weak
  2S  "Weak jump overcall: six spades, 4-10"   shows S=6, hcp=4..10
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3
  2H  "Weak jump overcall: six hearts, 4-10"   shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when  x is not H, y is not H, y is not S
      when  !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  3C  "Jump overcall: seven clubs, 4-10"    shows C=7, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is not C, y is not C
      when  !vul | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3
  3D  "Jump overcall: seven diamonds, 4-10" shows D=7, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is not D, y is not D
      when  !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3
  3H  "Jump overcall: seven hearts, 4-10"   shows H=7, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when  x is not H, y is not H
      when  !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  3S  "Jump overcall: seven spades, 4-10"   shows S=7, hcp=4..10
      when  x is not S, y is not S
      when  !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3

# ── Over their raise: (1x) P (2x), (1x) P (3x) ─────────────────────
# Direct seat after opener's partner raised (2026-10-20, Brill daily
# board 4: 1C P 2C with AKQJ85.QT8732.5.- passed twice, every other
# entrant bid). Nothing was written here, so the seat fell through to
# advances.bid's "Defending: nothing more to say". Standard practice,
# the direct-seat overcalls one level up: a natural suit at the cheapest
# level, five or more (a good suit or six) with 10+ total points at the
# two level; at the three level six cards from 10 HCP, or five with 14+
# and not balanced (the tripwire: five-card 3C overcalls on 11-13, and a
# balanced 15, went down where the pass defended); up to 16 HCP;
# a jump with six (seven at the four level is not written) and 4-10,
# weak as over their opening. The takeout double of the raise is
# takeout-double.bid's, the cue bid and 2NT two-suiters
# two-suited-overcalls.bid's. Higher of equal-length suits, as above.
after (1x) P (2x)
  2S  "Overcall over their raise: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H | x is H, S>=D | x is D, S>=C | x is C
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not S
      when  S>=6 | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3
  2H  "Overcall over their raise: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D | x is D, H>=C | x is C
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  2D  "Overcall over their raise: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C | x is C
      shows hcp+length_points>=10, hcp<=one_max
      when  x is C
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3
  3H  "Overcall over their raise: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>=D, H>=C
      shows (H>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is S
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=4
  3D  "Overcall over their raise: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S | x is S, D>H | x is H, D>=C
      shows (D>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is H | x is S
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=4
  3C  "Overcall over their raise: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, C>S | x is S, C>H | x is H, C>D | x is D
      shows (C>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not C
      when  C>=6 | quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=4
  P   "No overcall over their raise"  priority -10

after (1x) P (2x) when jump is weak
  3S  "Weak jump over their raise: six spades, 4-10"   shows S=6, hcp=4..10
      when  x is not S
      when  !vul | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3
  3H  "Weak jump over their raise: six hearts, 4-10"   shows H=6, hcp=4..10, S<=3
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  !vul | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3
  3D  "Weak jump over their raise: six diamonds, 4-10" shows D=6, hcp=4..10, H<=3, S<=3
      when  x is C
      when  !vul | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3

# Over the jump raise only the three level is left below game: a natural
# suit with the three-level overcall's values; four of a suit is not
# written.
after (1x) P (3x)
  3S  "Overcall over their jump raise: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H | x is H, S>=D | x is D, S>=C | x is C
      shows (S>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is not S
      when  S>=6 | quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=4
  3H  "Overcall over their jump raise: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D | x is D, H>=C | x is C
      shows (H>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is C | x is D
      when  H>=6 | quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=4
  3D  "Overcall over their jump raise: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C | x is C
      shows (D>=6, hcp>=two_min-2) | (hcp>=14, !balanced), hcp<=one_max
      when  x is C
      when  D>=6 | quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=4
  P   "No overcall over their jump raise"  priority -10

# ── Nothing to say ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# An explicit pass, so that the seat is covered and partner can draw the
# negative inference that we had no overcall.
# A strong hand doubles first (takeout-double.bid), so the pass caps the
# hand at the one-level overcall maximum. A trap pass is not assumed until
# it shows (Rick, ticket b400, 2026-10-02): BBA's direct-seat passers
# over a one-level opening, vanilla set, 99% at most 14-16 HCP.
after (1x)
  P   "No overcall"  shows hcp<=one_max  priority -10
files.rules/competitive/overcalls.notes.md:
# Overcalls (`overcalls.bid`): notes

Simple overcalls of a one-level opening, the weak jump overcall, and the
direct 1NT overcall. Cases: `overcalls.test`. Advancer is in
`advances.bid`; the takeout double is in `takeout-double.bid`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **A simple overcall is always a five-card suit.** No four-card
  overcalls on this card (`overcalls.often_4_cards` is off).
- **8-17 total points at the one level, 12-17 at the two level**, taken
  from BBA's Basic-Bridge meanings, which Rick adopted.
- **Too strong to overcall is a double first, then the suit**: 18+ total
  points doubles whatever its shape (`takeout-double.bid`).
- **A jump overcall follows the weak-two rules**: six cards, 4-9 HCP, and
  vulnerable two of the top three or three of the top five honours. A
  seven-card suit jumps to the three level, as it opens there.
- **The direct 1NT overcall is 15-18 balanced with a stopper**, a point
  wider than our 1NT opening.

## The suit has to be worth bidding (Rick, 2026-09-23)

A one-level overcall needs **two of the top three or three of the top
five honours**, or else **an opening hand**: it takes 12 total points to
overcall on a ten-high suit.

Found from board 120 of Basic_Major, where we overcalled 1♠ on
`J8753.QJ8.A63.Q3` — ten HCP and a jack-high suit. BBA passed, we pushed
the auction and they played 2♥ instead of our 3♦.

It is worth far more than that one board: **+4,520 IMPs against par**
across the corpus, identical auctions 15.4% → 15.6%, same contract 30.1%
→ 30.5%. Two `.test` cases had to change, both of which had encoded the
old behaviour on suits like `AT852` (nine HCP, two of the top five) and
`J87654` (seven HCP).

## Evidence

`bba-cli --all-meanings` on `Basic_Overcall.pbn` and
`Basic_Takeout_Double.pbn` with the Basic-Bridge card on both sides
(4,520 and 4,942 calls with their meanings), grouped by auction prefix:

| call | BBA's meaning | hands it made it on |
|---|---|---|
| (1x) 1y | "bidable suit", 8-17 total points, 5+ | 8-16 HCP, five or six cards |
| (1x) 2y | "bidable suit", 12-17 total points, 5+ | 11-16 HCP |
| (1x) 1N | "NT style", 15-17 total points, 2-5 in every suit | 15-17 HCP, never a five-card major |
| (1x) 2M jump | "Weak natural 2M", 4-10 total points, 6-7 cards | 8-10 HCP, six cards |

Two-level overcalls also want a suit: BBA passes plenty of 11-14 HCP
hands with a ragged five-card suit (A7632, K9865, J9543) at the two
level. We ask for **six cards, or two of the top three honours, or four
of the top five**; that gained a little on calls and more on contracts
(auctions matching 7.8% → 8.8% in Basic_Overcall).

**1NT with a five-card major**: every 1NT overcall in the corpus had four
cards or fewer in both majors, so the rule denies a five-card major and
we show the suit instead. BBA does the same (board 1 of Basic_Overcall
overcalls 1♠ on a balanced 16-count with AJ972).

Scenario effect (Basic-Bridge card, 500 boards each):

| | before | after this module | after the whole competitive slice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic_Overcall, calls | 66.1% | 72.0% | 74.1% |
| Basic_Takeout_Double, calls | 59.6% | 60.4% | 71.3% |

## Systems on over the 1NT overcall

`nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on` (default on, which is what BBA plays).
Rather than copy the 1NT family into a competitive module, the `after`
line now takes alternatives (`docs/LANGUAGE.md` section 4), so every
notrump context reads

```
after 1N (P) | (1x) 1N (P) | (1x) P (P) 1N (P) when !they.bid | systems_on
```

and Stayman, Jacoby and Texas transfers, minor-suit transfers,
super-accepts and the natural 2NT/3NT responses all apply after our
overcall, direct or balancing. The continuations were already written
against state (`when answered transfer(M)`), so they needed nothing.

BBA's meanings confirm it plays the same way: over `(1x) 1N (P)` the
corpus has 2♣ "Stayman" (7+), 2♦/2♥ "transfer", 3♣ "1N-3C transfer to
diamonds", 4♦ "Texas", 2NT "8-9" and 3NT "9-15".

| scenario | calls | auctions | contracts |
|---|---|---|---|
| We_Overcall_NT_then_Stayman | 75.3% → **87.3%** | 10.6% → 46.6% | 11.4% → 65.8% |
| We_Overcall_NT_then_Texas | 70.5% → **80.8%** | 0.0% → 18.6% | 0.0% → 22.8% |
| We_Overcall_NT_then_Jacoby | 70.0% → **79.5%** | 0.4% → 20.2% | 1.4% → 26.6% |
| We_Overcall_1N | 74.2% → **80.4%** | 15.0% → 26.2% | 15.4% → 33.4% |
| After_1x_1N | 73.3% → **75.7%** | 13.6% → 16.2% | 13.6% → 19.6% |

## Accepted differences from BBA

- BBA passes some 12-14 HCP hands with a five-card minor over a major
  opening that we overcall at the two level, and overcalls some that we
  pass. The line is not a rule in BBA; it evaluates the hand.
- BBA's weak jump overcall runs to 10 total points; ours stops at 9, the
  same as our weak two.
- BBA sometimes preempts to the three level on a six-card suit.

## Gaps and open questions

The balancing seat is `balancing.bid`; responsive doubles are
`responsive-doubles.bid`.

- Overcalls of a 1NT opening, of a weak two, and of two-level openings.
- Two-suited overcalls (Michaels, the Unusual 2NT) are in
  `two-suited-overcalls.bid` (2026-09-28), when the card plays them
  (Basic-Bridge does not).

## The sandwich seat: (1x) P (1y) (2026-10-07)

No rule covered the fourth hand after opener's partner responded one
of a suit, so it always passed (advances.bid's "Defending: nothing more
to say"), and the conventions that answer an overcall there (support
doubles and redoubles) never came up in our own auctions: the
convention score found switching support doubles off changed 0 boards.

BBA, 21GF-DEFAULT, 600 random 6-17 hands each
(`probes/oc4-1D-P-1H.toml`, `probes/oc4-1H-P-1S.toml`): BBA acts on 186
and 133 of 600: overcalls ("bidable suit": 8-17 at one level, 12-17 at
two), the double ("takeout double": 12+, three or more in both unbid
suits), 1NT 15-17, weak jumps and preempts as in the direct seat, the
Unusual 2NT, and natural bids in responder's suit with six or seven.

What we play: the direct seat's overcalls in the suits they have not
bid (the length tests ignore their suits; up to 18 HCP, since partner
has passed and there is no power double), the weak jumps, 1NT 15-18
with both their suits stopped (not with Sandwich 1NT on, nor by a
passed hand), and the takeout double: eight cards in the two unbid
suits (or 15+), after a five-card suit's overcall; with 15+, four of
each and an unbalanced hand the double comes first. Agreement with
BBA's call 414 -> 525 of 600 and 467 -> 528 of 600 (it was every pass).
Advancing (advances.bid): raise with three (two level) or four (three
level), preempt with four; answer the double in the longer unbid suit.

Not written: the Unusual 2NT there, BBA's natural bids in responder's
suit, and BBA's double on four-three with 12-14 (BBA passes most of
those hands too; we pass all).

Tripwire (`compare --limit 50`, 17,105 boards): 370 changed, all at the
new calls, Impossible 2♠ (impossible-2s.notes.md) and the inverted-minor
gaps. By the errors yardstick on our changed boards (errors_diff.py,
344 scored): contract errors +24 (actor +26), doubling errors -386
(-133 the actor's, -253 the other side's), distance from par -302. The
loss is doubling: overcalls that go down undoubled count against the
side that did not double them, and our penalty doubles of overcalls
are weak (CLAUDE.md: our engine plays both sides). Worst context
1C P 1D 1S (-93 over 38 boards). For Rick: keep the contract-error
gain and look at the opener's side's penalty doubles, or tighten the
one-level overcall here?

## Probed over 1C (2026-09-25, `probes/overcall-1C.toml`)

2,500 hands with a five-card or longer suit and 5-17 HCP over 1C
(Basic-Bridge, default style): 78% agreement before, 82% after.
- **Light overcalls.** BBA overcalls a five-card suit with 8-10 HCP
  whatever its quality (KT853, T976 in hearts...). Dropping our quality
  test, Rick's 2026-09-23 rule, costs **-4,835 IMPs** on the corpus.
  Rick's rule stands, strongly.
- **Weak jump overcalls:** BBA jumps with 10 HCP too. 4-10 instead of
  4-9: +258 (-167,116 -> -166,858).
- **The ceiling:** a six-card suit with 16 HCP has 18 total points, so
  we doubled; BBA overcalls. Capping the overcall at 17 HCP instead of
  17 total points: +229 (-166,858 -> -166,629). The strong any-shape
  double keeps 18 total points: moving it to HCP too cost 971 IMPs.

## Over their 1NT, natural; and judging competitive calls (2026-09-25)

We had no rules over an opposing 1NT. BBA on Basic-Bridge
(`probes/vs-1N.toml`, 2,500 hands) overcalls naturally:
- a five-card suit at the two level with 12+ total points;
- a seven-card preempt at the three level with 4-10.

Our rules now do the same when the card names no conventional defence:
91% agreement.

**Distance from par is the wrong yardstick here.** The corpus par figure
treats both sides alike: a competitive call that works (an overcall that
buys the contract, a preempt that pushes them too high) moves the
result away from par and counts as a loss. On the 237 boards this
change touches:

| Measure | IMPs |
|---|---|
| Distance from par | -825 |
| Double-dummy result to the side that overcalled | +1,007 |

`probes/tools/sideimps.py BASE.json VARIANT.json` computes the second.
Use it for competitive decisions; distance from par stays right for
uncontested auctions.

## For Rick: which yardstick for competitive calls? (2026-09-25)

Today's competitive A/B tests, re-run with both measures. Each row is a
variant against the rules as committed:

| Variant | Distance from par | IMPs to the side that acted |
|---|---|---|
| Reopening takeout double, (1x) X (2x) P P X | -1,741 | -2,478 |
| Advancer's takeout double after (1x) 1N (2x) | -449 | -555 |
| Overcaller's takeout double after (1x) 1y (2x) P P | -203 | -497 |
| Takeout double on 12 HCP (10 with a singleton) | -314 | +232 |
| Ours plus 10 HCP with a singleton | -380 | +163 |
| Two-level overcalls on three of the top five honours | -285 | +768 |
| **One-level overcalls without the quality test (your rule)** | **-4,924** | **+7,429** |
| Weak jump overcalls back to 4-9 (from 4-10) | -229 | +312 |
| One-level overcall cap back to 17 total points | -60 | -620 |
| Natural overcalls of 1NT (committed) | -825 | +1,007 |
| Undo "five-card major before the redouble" after (X) | -452 | +654 |
| Undo "support first over a major" after (X) | -338 | -541 |
| Undo the doubler's rebid when opener competes | -405 | -860 |
| Undo the preempt responses' vulnerability split | -57 | -204 |

Neither measure is clean:
- **Distance from par** counts any move away from par against us,
  including a competitive call that gains.
- **IMPs to the side that acted** plays our engine on both sides. Our
  engine rarely doubles for penalty, so a light overcall is seldom
  punished here as it would be at the table. That flatters bidding.

Kept where both measures agree: the three doubles are rejected, and the
17-HCP cap stays. The rest are for you, above all the quality test on
one-level overcalls: +7,429 by the second measure, -4,924 by the first.
A fair test probably needs penalty doubles on the defending side first.

With a strong hand, N will normally double then show what they have ...
run a scan on BBA auctions where there is 1M (pass) and see what the max
HCP is for the passer ... if there is an outlier, we shouldn't keep that
in our inference" (also for 1m); "for something where there could be a
trap pass, we should assume it's not a trap pass hand unless and until

BBA's direct-seat passer over a one-level opening, vanilla SAYC set:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1♣ | 11,473 | 16 | 18 | 19 |
| 1♦ | 13,759 | 15 | 18 | 19 |
| 1♥ | 9,519 | 15 | 17 | 18 |
| 1♠ | 11,380 | 14 | 17 | 18 |

## Two-level overcalls: the minimum in HCP (ticket b238, 2026-10-04)

Rick: "on the 2C overcall, how can West have 3 HCP possibly? With a weak
hand and long clubs, they would make a 3C overcall. So this normally
would be a 12-18 total points overcall - preempt when weaker, double
first when stronger. Can we see how BBA judges to make this bid based
on club length, club strength and points?"

BBA over 1D, 1,500 made hands (`probes/oc-2C-over-1D.toml`, Basic-Bridge):

at the margin (six clubs, 9-12 HCP: 25% with no top honour, 80% with
all three). So BBA reads the card's "2-level overcall: minimum 12" as
HCP, a point less with six cards.

2C/2D/2H now show `hcp>=two_min | (suit>=6, hcp>=two_min-1)` (was 12

## Over their raise: (1x) P (2x), (1x) P (3x) (2026-10-20)

Brill daily 2026-10-20, board 4 (IMP, all vul, dealer W): 1C P 2C
(inverted, 10+) and South, AKQJ85.QT8732.5.-, passed ("Defending:
nothing more to say", advances.bid) and passed again over 2NT-3NT.
Every other entrant bid (4S doubled made +1, 2S, 3C for the majors, 3S);
par NS 5HX/5SX -1, they make 3NT. Nothing was written for the direct
seat over a raise, so it fell to advances.bid.

Now, standard practice (not yet cited): a natural suit at the cheapest
level, five or more (six, or a good suit) with 10+ total points at the
two level, up to 16 HCP; at the three level six cards from 10 HCP, or
five with 14+ and not balanced; weak jumps with six and 4-10 as over
the opening; over the jump raise the three-level natural calls only.
The takeout double of the raise stays takeout-double.bid's; the cue bid
and 2NT are two-suited-overcalls.bid's (that hand now bids 3C, Michaels,
and 4S over partner's 3S: 4SX= +790 when our engine bids all four seats).

The first try allowed a five-card three-level overcall from 11 HCP
(the two-level overcall's minimum less one): on the tripwire the 3C
overcalls lost 25 contract IMPs and 29 against par (five-card suits on
11-13, a balanced 15 doubled for -800), so the three level needs six
or 14+ unbalanced. By rule after that (changed boards, IMPs gained in
contract errors / doubling errors / par distance): 2S 20 boards
-2/-10/0, 2H 6 +13/-5/+10, 2D 3 +4/+3/+1, 3C 26 +1/-28/-7, 3D 10
+16/+3/+17, 3H 25 +5/-11/-7, weak jumps 10 +14/+14/+4, over the jump
raise 7 +7/-8/+3. The doubling losses are mostly the opponents' (our
engine on both sides) not doubling a failing overcall. Several 2S
overcalls over an inverted minor raise were passed out or doubled
because opener has no rule after (1m) P (2m) 2S: a gap on the opening
side, not written here.

Tripwire (`compare --limit 50`, all scenarios, against main 2358856):
145 of 17,105 boards changed in 50 scenarios, all at the new calls.
Against BBA: errors -8,497 -> -8,461 (contract -7,228 -> -7,148,

# Penalty doubles by judgment (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md, Phase 3).
#
# Draft: see penalty-doubles.notes.md.

module penalty-doubles "Penalty doubles: they are too high"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base

# The contract is theirs and undoubled: RHO has just bid (direct), or LHO
# bid and both partner and RHO have passed since (passed round to me).
define direct = !rho.last=P, !rho.last=X, !rho.last=XX
define passed_round = rho.last=P, partner.last=P, !lho.last=P, !lho.last=X, !lho.last=XX

# Their suit, natural, and not one we have shown (a bid in our suit is a
# cue bid; Stayman, a strong 2C or a transfer shows no length in the suit).
define natural_theirs(x) = they.strain is x, they.fit(x).min>=4, partner.x.min<=2, shown.x.min<=2

# Where they will play: passed round to me, or a fit found, or game.
# Directly over a new suit the auction may be forcing.
define settled(x) = passed_round | they.fit(x).min>=7 | they.game_reached

# Rick's penalty-double standard (2026-09-23): four or more with two of
# the top three, or three of the top five.
define good_trumps(x) = x>=4, quality(x)>=good | top5(x)>=3

# They have bid game and I hold 17 or more: they have 23 at most between
# them, whatever partner's silence hides (2026-10-02; 18 doubles fewer
# contracts that make but gains less, notes).
define big_hand_vs_game = they.game_reached, hcp>=17

# What I hold in their suit against what we have shown between us
# (we.hcp.min: my HCP and the bottom of partner's range). Good four at
# 17 and any four at 20 since partner's floor is known more often
# (2026-10-03, after PRs #44/#45; notes, "Retuned on the higher floors").
# The big hand doubles their game on strength, but not short in their
# suit (a void or a singleton) with six or more of its own: that hand
# declares (vs-preempts.bid; Brill daily 2026-10-14 board 4, 5D doubled
# with a void and six hearts made, 6H on; 2026-10-15). A void and five
# still doubles (2026-10-14 board 7, 4S doubled went down). The
# takeout doubler keeps the old count: his pass of their game still
# denies 17+ (else the advancer loses the shape the double showed).
define pen_suit(x) = (good_trumps(x), we.hcp.min>=17) | (x>=4, we.hcp.min>=20) | (x>=3, we.hcp.min>=21) | we.hcp.min>=22 | (big_hand_vs_game, x>=2 | longest<=5 | me.last=X)

# Responder's first call over their overcall: the double is negative.
define responder_first = partner.opened, me.bids=0, !passed_hand, !me.last=X, !me.last=XX

# Partner need not have shown values: with 22 known in my own hand (or
# 17-21 with their trumps) the double stands alone. A condition that
# partner had shown 4+ was a par artefact: it lost on the errors
# yardstick on all three sets (penalty-doubles.notes.md, 2026-10-01).

# Not over partner's notrump opening (one bid, a range of four points or
# less): they came in with shape against a balanced hand, and the double
# lost (21GF random set, 2026-10-01).
define partner_nt = partner.opened, partner.bids=1, partner.hcp.min>=12, partner.hcp.max - partner.hcp.min <= 3

define pen_spot(x) = natural_theirs(x), settled(x), !partner_nt

when they.bid, direct | passed_round, !asked, they.level>=2, !responder_first
  X   "Penalty double of their spades"
      shows pen_suit(S)
      when  pen_spot(S)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their hearts"
      shows pen_suit(H)
      when  pen_spot(H)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their diamonds"
      shows pen_suit(D)
      when  pen_spot(D)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their clubs"
      shows pen_suit(C)
      when  pen_spot(C)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6

# Their notrump after they have both bid (not an opening 1NT or 2NT,
# which vs-1nt.bid and the defences answer).
when they.bid, passed_round | (direct, they.game_reached), !asked, !responder_first, they.strain is N, lho.bids + rho.bids >= 2
  X   "Penalty double of their notrump"
      shows we.hcp.min>=21 | big_hand_vs_game
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6

# They bid over our game: the side that bid game owns the hand, so the
# player with values (12+ in my hand, or 20 known between us) and two of
# their trumps doubles (2026-10-02). After partner's signoff too: the
# signoff's "nothing to add" pass (rebids.bid, priority -5) would
# otherwise sell out, so this double sits at -5.
define our_game_bid = me.last=3N | me.last=4H | me.last=4S | me.last=5C | me.last=5D | me.last=5H | me.last=5S | partner.last=3N | partner.last=4H | partner.last=4S | partner.last=5C | partner.last=5D | partner.last=5H | partner.last=5S
define over_our_game(x) = x>=2, hcp>=12 | we.hcp.min>=20

  X   "Penalty double of their spades"
      shows over_our_game(S)
      when  natural_theirs(S), !partner_nt
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -5
  X   "Penalty double of their hearts"
      shows over_our_game(H)
      when  natural_theirs(H), !partner_nt
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -5
  X   "Penalty double of their diamonds"
      shows over_our_game(D)
      when  natural_theirs(D), !partner_nt
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -5
  X   "Penalty double of their clubs"
      shows over_our_game(C)
      when  natural_theirs(C), !partner_nt
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -5

# (2026-10-09): the redouble said we hold the balance (10+ opposite an
# opening), a penalty double the same, and what they bid now is a
# rescue, not forcing. The hand behind the rescuer doubles it with four
# or more of their suit (penalty-doubles.notes.md, "Doubling errors
# after the convention batches").
# The redouble is mine, of their takeout double of partner's opening
# (not a support, SOS or McCabe redouble: those show a holding), and
# the doubler has run from it, directly in front of me. Opener's double
# of the advance (1x X XX 1y/2y X) and mine of a forced one-level
# advance passed round to me lost on the random sets: left out.
define we_redoubled = me.last=XX, partner.opened, me.bids=0, partner.hcp.min>=10, direct
define they_ran = we_redoubled | asked nt_penalty | asked penalty
# After partner's penalty double of their suit, a run is a new suit:
# the runner's partner has not bid it. A raise of the doubled suit is
# not a rescue (Brill daily 2026-10-08 board 2: 1NT 2D 2H (X) 4H,
# doubled on T764 and made; 2026-10-15). After our redouble or a
# penalty double of their notrump every bid of theirs is a run (the
# doubler's side raising the rescue included).
define ran_to(x) = !(asked penalty) | (direct, !lho.named(x)) | (passed_round, !rho.named(x))
define ran_into(x) = x>=4

when they.bid, direct | passed_round, they_ran
  X   "Penalty: four or more spades"
      shows ran_into(S)
      when  natural_theirs(S), ran_to(S)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority 0
  X   "Penalty: four or more hearts"
      shows ran_into(H)
      when  natural_theirs(H), ran_to(H)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority 0
  X   "Penalty: four or more diamonds"
      shows ran_into(D)
      when  natural_theirs(D), ran_to(D)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority 0
  X   "Penalty: four or more clubs"
      shows ran_into(C)
      when  natural_theirs(C), ran_to(C)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority 0

# overcalled: partner's hand is described and has little defence, so my
# double is for penalty (Berkowitz-Cohen, low-level doubles: penalty
# "after 2♦, 2M openings"), on my own strength and their trumps
# (2026-10-09, notes).
define partner_preempted = partner.opened, partner.bids=1, partner.hcp.max<=11
define vs_overcall_of_preempt(x) = (x>=2, hcp>=15) | (x>=4, hcp>=12) | (x>=3, hcp>=12, quality(x)>=good | top5(x)>=3) | (x>=5, hcp>=9)

when they.bid, direct | passed_round, !asked, partner_preempted, me.bids=0
  X   "Penalty double of their spades"
      shows vs_overcall_of_preempt(S)
      when  natural_theirs(S)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their hearts"
      shows vs_overcall_of_preempt(H)
      when  natural_theirs(H)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their diamonds"
      shows vs_overcall_of_preempt(D)
      when  natural_theirs(D)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6
  X   "Penalty double of their clubs"
      shows vs_overcall_of_preempt(C)
      when  natural_theirs(C)
      sets  ask=penalty
      priority -6

# opener's pass denied a fit and extras, so the hand is a misfit for
# them and ours on strength; the double is for penalty (2026-10-09,
# notes).
define one_level_pen(x) = (x>=3, we.hcp.min>=19) | (x>=2, we.hcp.min>=22)

when they.bid, passed_round, !asked, they.level=1, me.has_bid, partner.has_bid

when asked penalty, rho.last=P

Phase 3 of docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md: a penalty double as a judgment rule
keyed on auction state, not on a sequence, so it keeps working as
conventions are added. First version 2026-10-01.

## The rule

When the contract is theirs and undoubled (RHO has just bid, or it has
been passed round to me), at the two level or higher, I double for
penalty when, with `we.hcp.min` my HCP plus the bottom of partner's
shown range:

| my holding in their suit | we.hcp.min |
|---|---|
| four or more with two of the top three or three of the top five (Rick's standard, 2026-09-23) | 17 (20 until 2026-10-03) |
| four or more | 20 (2026-10-03) |
| three or more | 21 |
| anything | 22 |
| their notrump (after they have both bid) | 21 |

Only where it is a contract:
- their suit is natural (`they.fit(x).min >= 4`: not Stayman, a strong
  2♣, a transfer, or an overcall the engine cannot read) and not one we
  have shown (a cue bid);
- it will stand: passed round to me, or they have a fit (seven or more
  shown), or they have bid game. Directly over a new suit the auction
  may be forcing;
- not over partner's notrump opening (one bid, a range of four points
  or less): they came in with shape against a balanced hand;
- not responder's first call over their overcall (the double is
  negative there).

Partner need not have shown values: a condition that he had
(`partner.hcp.min >= 4`) was dropped on 2026-10-01, when the errors
yardstick found it a par artefact (below, "Re-judged by errors").

Priority -6: above the silence passes (-10, -20), below every sequence
rule and the LoTT (-4). It sets `ask=penalty`; partner sits (priority
-1, so a sequence pass or bid does not answer it instead).

Two more doubles (2026-10-02, below "Doubling more"):
- **their game, my 17**: once they have bid game, 17 HCP in my own hand
  is enough on its own (any holding in their suit, and their notrump
  game too): they have 23 at most between them (`big_hand_vs_game`);
- **they bid over our game** (`our_game_bid`: my or partner's last call
  was 3NT, 4M or five of a suit, and they bid on at the four level or
  higher): 12+ in my hand or 20 known between us, and two or more of
  their trumps (`over_our_game(x)`). Priority -5, and also when partner's
  game was a signoff (`asked signoff`): the signoff's "nothing to add"
  pass (rebids.bid, -5) otherwise sold out to them.

And one penalty pass in responder-rebids.bid: responder leaves opener's
reopening double in with four of their suit only when they are good
(two of the top three, three of the top five), five long, or he has
8 HCP.

Three more (2026-10-09, below "Doubling errors after the convention
batches"):
- **they ran** (`they_ran`): the redoubler doubles the doubler's rescue
  from our redouble (`1x (X) XX (P) P (2y) X`), and partner of a
  penalty double (ours, or a 1NT defence's `nt_penalty`) doubles their
  runout, with four or more of their suit (`ran_into(x)`), priority 0;
- **partner preempted** (`partner_preempted`: one bid, 11 HCP at
  most) and they overcalled: my double is for penalty with 15+ and two
  of their trumps, 12+ and four (or three good), 9+ and five
  (`vs_overcall_of_preempt(x)`);
- **their one-level overcall, we have both bid**, passed round to me:
  three of their suit and 19 known between us, or two and 22
  (`one_level_pen(x)`).
Partner sits only when RHO has passed (`asked penalty, rho.last=P`):
when they run, the double of the runout answers it.

  there.

  declarers are vulnerable and 3.4 when not (BBA 4.5 and 3.3).
- **Seat:** in the undoubled chances where the defenders held 20+ HCP,
  both decisive passes were replayed. Half of them are "Defending:
  nothing more to say" (advances.bid), then after-interference.bid's
  "Passed last time" and "Partner passed", rebids.bid's "Partner has
  nothing", responder-rebids.bid's "Partner had no reopening bid
  either".

### What the defenders know

The decisive passes of the undoubled chances where the defenders held
20+ HCP were replayed through `rbb call --json` (19,632 positions),
then a sample of 15,000 contested final contracts, made or not (30,000
positions), and 8,000 uncontested ones (16,000), to cost a double
(double dummy, no runout: an upper bound, see below).
- **Partner's shown minimum is 0 in most positions.** A pass is a true
  0, but so is most of what partner bids: in 53% of the positions where
  partner had made a bid his `hcp.min` was 0, and in 93% after a
  two-level bid. The rules describe overcalls, raises and new suits in
  total points (`hcp+length_points>=8`), and the knowledge ranges do
  not narrow `hcp` (or `points`) from a sum: a simple raise "6-9 total
  points" reads as 0-30 HCP, an overcall "8-16 total points" as 0-16.
  So `we.hcp.min` is my own HCP in most contested positions, and
  `they.hcp.max` is near 40 (their raises are 0-30 too): the deck bound
  (40 minus their maximum) adds to it in only a fifth to a quarter of
  contested positions. This is the knowledge limit, and it is in the
  engine (For Rick 7).
- **The inference from a pass is lost twice.** "No overcall" over their
  one-level opening should deny 17+ (the power double takes every hand
  of 17+), but reads 0-30: the takeout double's third `shows` line uses
  `has(A,x)` about the doubler's own hand, which cannot be resolved for
  another seat, so the whole denial is skipped (engine.rs, negative
  inference); and without that line the denial is kept as a constraint
  but the range summary cannot see that `hcp>=17` implies the rest of
  it. A lower maximum would not help a penalty double anyway: the
  doubles read minimums.
- **Their suit is known**: their length was read in 99.7% of contested
  positions. Unread bids (no rule: the balancing 2S of 1H P 2H 2S)
  still block `natural_theirs` there.
- **Doubling what is not known loses.** The contested sample loses
  63,444 IMPs doubled whole; with the actual 22+ HCP and three trumps
  it would gain about 2 a board. With what is known (`we.hcp.min` 20,
  three trumps) a double gains 1.8 a board on 275 positions; lower
  thresholds and trump stacks look good statically (five trumps and 10
  HCP, +4.6 a board) but lost when measured on 2026-10-01 (stacks,
  above): they run, and the static cost ignores it. "Our fit, they
  compete at the three level", BBA's largest class, loses statically at
  every HCP threshold tried (-1.6 to -3.1 a board): with a fit on both
  sides the three level often makes.
- **Uncontested**: with 15+ HCP against their game +1.6 a board
  statically (85 of 8,000 sampled contracts), 17+ against 3NT more;
  against partscores everything lost. Hence the game double below.

A small block in self-play: our declarers bid over our game on 369
final contracts of the vanilla set (BBA's opponents 1,884), and 74 of

sacrifices. A forcing-pass treatment is not needed for these numbers;
the rule above lets the side that bid game double with values.

| `1x P 1y 1z` | 693 (127, 4) | 19 (5, 3) | responder, "Minimum: they have bought it" (responder-rebids.bid) |
| `1N X 2x` | 486 (128, 16) | 37 (7, 0) | partner of the penalty double of 1NT, "Defending: nothing more to say" |
| `1x X XX P P 1y` | 456 (56, 0) | 0 (1, 1) | the redoubler |
| `3x 4y`, `3x 3y` | 510, 389 (77, 0; 71, 0) | 141, 144 | responder to the preempt |

In `1x X XX P P 2y` and `1N X 2x` the penalty double was blocked by
"the contract will stand" (a run is not forcing, but the rule only
knew passed-round, a fit or game); over partner's preempt by "not
responder's first call" (meant for the negative double). Neither rule
said anything about one-level contracts.

### Rules added

1. **They ran** (`they_ran`, priority 0): the redoubler's double of the
   doubler's rescue, directly over it (`1x (X) XX (P) P (2y) X`), and
   partner's double of their runout from a penalty double (ours, or a
   1NT defence's), with four or more of their suit. "After our
   redouble, any subsequent doubles are penalty" (Larry Cohen, "Over
   opps' takeout double"); Berkowitz-Cohen's "already penalized".
2. **Partner preempted** (`partner_preempted`, priority -6): their
   overcall of a weak two or a three-level opening, doubled for
   penalty by responder with 15+ and two of their trumps, 12+ and four
   (or three good), 9+ and five. Berkowitz-Cohen, penalty "after 2♦,
   2M openings". Thresholds from a static count first (every undoubled
   overcall of our preempt in the three sets, the double's double-dummy
   value by responder's HCP and holding: 15+ gains with two trumps
   (+3.40 a board), 12-14 with four (+2.94) or three good (+4.33),
   9-11 only with five (+5.47 good, +0.73 poor); under 9 loses
   everywhere), then measured.
3. **Their one-level overcall, we have both bid** (priority -6):
   `1x P 1y (1z) P (P) X` and alike, passed round to me: three of
   their suit and 19 known between us, or two and 22. Opener's pass
   denied a fit and extras; the sandwich overcall is alone against
   the balance of strength. Static count first (responder 12-14: +3.21
   a board with two trumps, +4.67 with three; 9-11: +0.67 with three,
   +2.82 with four; under 9 loses but for four).
4. Partner sits for my penalty double only when RHO passed: when they
   run, rule 1 answers it.

## Brill dailies: a raise is not a run; the big hand with a suit (2026-10-15)

Two doubles from the Brill dailies (Rusty South, 21GF-GIB):

- **Brill daily 2026-10-08 board 2** (MP): (P) P (1NT) P (2D) P (2H) X
  (4H), South K87.T764.87.J742 doubled "they ran into my hearts" and 4H
  made (-590 against -420). Partner's double of the transfer completion
  read as a penalty double (`asked penalty`), so `they_ran` held; but
  East raised the doubled suit, he did not run from it. After
  partner's penalty double of a suit, `ran_to(x)` now asks for a new
  suit: the runner's partner has not bid it (`!lho.named(x)` directly,
  `!rho.named(x)` passed round). After our redouble or a penalty double
  of 1NT every bid is still a run (the doubler's side raising its
  rescue, 1C X XX 1D 2C 2D, included), and four small still doubles
  (measured below).
- **Brill daily 2026-10-14 board 4** (IMP): (2D) P (5D), South
  AQJ7.AKQT94.-.K84 doubled on strength (`big_hand_vs_game`); 5DX made,
  6H and 6S were on. The strength double now stands aside with a void
  or singleton in their suit and six or more of my own: that hand
  declares (vs-preempts.bid's new block for their raised preempt bids
  5H). A void and only five still doubles: Brill daily 2026-10-14
  board 7 (1H 1S P 2H P 2S P 4S, .AKJT7.A854.AJ63) doubled and 4S went
  down; a first version that excluded every void lost it.

  The takeout doubler keeps the old count (`me.last=X`): without it
  his pass of their game no longer denied 17+, the advancer lost the
  shape the double showed and stopped bidding 4S in 1H X 3H P 4H P P
  (9 boards, contract -25, par -20 on the full corpus).

Measured against main a12e72e, `compare --par`, errors_diff, together
with the vs-preempts.bid blocks (2026-10-15), split by the rule that
changed. Full corpus: 210 boards, errors +235 (+129 / +106), contract
+108, doubling +127, par +234. The strength doubles given up: 144
boards, contract +7, doubling +34, par +70; the new bids in their
place and over their raised preempts (vs-preempts.bid): 66 boards,
contract +101, doubling +93, par +164. "They ran" changes no corpus
board (only the Brill one). An earlier version that also limited the
runs after our redouble and wanted an honour in four trumps lost 284
doubling IMPs on the corpus (the redoubler's AT7.AQ75.Q9.8762 over 2C
and alike): not kept. Tripwire (`--limit 50`): 18 boards, errors +20
(+3 / +17), contract +5, doubling +15, par +7.

## Sources

- **Standard practice, not yet cited:** double when they are too high
  and the balance of strength is ours; trump length and honours behind
  or in front of the declarer; the combined-strength thresholds are
  calibrated here, not quoted.
- **Rick's rulings:** the penalty-double holding, four or more with two
  of the top three or three of the top five (2026-09-23,
  after-interference.bid trap pass, responder-rebids.bid); thresholds in
  the rules as named conditions (JUDGMENT-LAYER.md decisions, 2026-09-30).
- **BBA evidence:** its doubled final contracts on the vanilla random
  set (above); issue #448 on not letting them play undoubled.
- **BBA's issues** on its own penalty doubles (github.com/EdwardPiwowar/BBA):
  #83 "Another terrible penalty double", #86 "Yet another wrong penalty
  double", #731, #797, #578 "This is not a penalty double - just a
  strong hand", #1092 "Mad doubles are still with us": its count of
  doubles that made is a known cost, not one to copy.
- **2026-10-02:** the game and over-our-game doubles and the reopening
  pass are standard practice, not yet cited (a game bid against 17 in
  my hand; the side that bid game doubles their bid over it; leaving a
  takeout double in needs trump tricks); thresholds calibrated here on
  the three sets (tables above); `probes/tools/double_chances.py`.
- **Measurements:** the tables above, from `rbb compare` on
  Random_Pavlicek_SAYCvanilla with the vanilla `--set` list, the
  `rbb call` replay of 15,000 positions, `probes/tools/sideimps.py`,
  `probes/tools/par_blame.py`, `probes/tools/penalty_x.py`, and
  `probes/tools/errors_diff.py` for the re-judgment by errors
  (Rick's yardstick, 2026-10-01).
- **2026-10-03:** the test hand and the counts above, from
  `rbb compare` on the three sets and `probes/tools/errors_diff.py`.
- **2026-10-03, retune:** the variant tables and the three-set table,
  from `rbb compare` on main 53f1d3a (after PRs #44 and #45) and
  `probes/tools/errors_diff.py`, `probes/tools/penalty_x.py`; the
  thresholds are calibrated here, not quoted.
- **2026-10-09, after the convention batches:**
  - Larry Cohen, "Over Opps' T/O Double"
    (larryco.com/bridge-articles/over-opps-to-double): "After our
    redouble, any subsequent doubles are penalty." The rule takes only
    the redoubler's double of the doubler's rescue; opener's double
    lost here (For Rick 16).
  - David Berkowitz and Larry Cohen, "Berk-Co Exceptions to Low-Level
    Doubles" (larryco.com/bridge-articles/berk-co-exceptions-to-low-level-doubles):
    doubles below 2NT are takeout except, among others, when "the
    opponents have already been 'left in' or doubled for penalties"
    (their runout from our penalty double) and after our 2♦ and 2M
    openings (the preempt rule). Their list is one partnership's
    style; JUDGMENT-LAYER.md question 6 stays open.
  - The one-level double after we have both bid: standard practice,
    not yet cited; thresholds from the static count and the three-set
    measurement above.
  - Measurements: `rbb compare` on the three sets at main 3342483 and
    with each rule (rule copies under `--rules`), `probes/tools/errors_diff.py`,
    `probes/tools/par_blame.py`, and `probes/tools/double_context.py`
    (new) for the context tables.
- **2026-10-15, the Brill dailies:** after a penalty double of a suit,
  a rescue is a new suit, not a raise; the big hand short in their
  suit with a long suit of its own bids it. Standard practice, not yet
  cited; the boards named above and the measurement there.
