# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Rubensohl (convention-card competitive_bidding/rubensohl; Wikipedia,
# "Rubinsohl"; Larry Cohen, "Transfer Lebensohl"): a transfer version of
# Lebensohl. Every bid from 2NT up is a transfer to the next strain.
#
# 1. After a natural two-level overcall of our 1NT (2♦, 2♥, 2♠;
#    `notrump.rubensohl.play`, which switches Lebensohl off):
#
#    - two of a suit: natural, to play; the double: as the card says
#      (nt-interference.bid);
#    - 2NT clubs, 3♣ diamonds, 3♦ hearts, 3♥ spades, 3♠ notrump;
#    - the transfer to their suit is Stayman: game values, four cards in
#      an unbid major;
#    - the transfer to notrump (3♠, or 3♠ over 2♠: their suit) is game
#      values with no stopper and no four-card major; 3NT is game with a
#      stopper;
#    - a transfer to a minor: six or more, weak (to play) or with game
#      values (then 3NT); to a major: five or more, invitational or
#      better (Wikipedia: "at least invitational").
#
#    Opener completes a transfer with a minimum; with a maximum (17) and
#    three-card support for the major he bids game, with a maximum and
#    no fit 3NT. He answers Stayman with the major, else 3NT with a
#    stopper, else completes to their suit. Responder then places it.
#
# 2. After partner's takeout double of their weak two
#    (`competitive.rubensohl_after_double.play`, which switches
#    Lebensohl there off: vs-preempts.bid): the same transfers from 2NT
#    up (Wikipedia: "the same transfer structure applies"), with the
#    doubler in opener's place. A transfer shows four or more (five in
#    a major below their suit when it jumps past two of it) and either a
#    weak hand to play at three or 9+; the transfer to their suit is
#    Stayman-like (game values, four of an unbid major), the transfer to
#    notrump game values without a stopper.
#
# Notes: rubensohl.notes.md.

module rubensohl "Rubensohl: transfers after interference over 1NT and after doubling a weak two"
  kind   convention
  needs  nt-interference
  needs  vs-preempts
  skill  competitive_bidding/rubensohl
  param  over_nt  = competitive_bidding/rubensohl:over_1nt_interference default false
  param  after_x  = competitive_bidding/rubensohl:after_double default false

define rub_nt(y) = over_nt, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
define rub_nt_opener(y) = over_nt, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)

# ════ 1. After they overcall our 1NT ═════════════════════════════════

# ── Responder over 2♦ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1N (2D) when rub_nt(D)
  2N  "Rubensohl: transfer to clubs, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows C>=6, C>D, H<=3, S<=3
      priority 3
  3C  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, a four-card major"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: transfer to hearts, invitational or better"
      alert  artificial
      shows H>=5, H>=S, hcp>=8
      priority 3
  3H  "Rubensohl: transfer to spades, invitational or better"
      alert  artificial
      shows S>=5, S>H, hcp>=8
      priority 3
  3S  "Rubensohl: game values, no stopper in {y}"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(D), H<=3, S<=3
      priority 3
  3N  "Game with a stopper in diamonds"
      shows hcp>=10, stop(D), H<=3, S<=3
      priority 3

# ── Responder over 2♥ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1N (2H) when rub_nt(H)
  2N  "Rubensohl: transfer to clubs, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows C>=6, C>=D, S<=3
      priority 3
  3C  "Rubensohl: transfer to diamonds, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows D>=6, D>C, S<=3
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, four spades"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, S=4
      priority 3
  3H  "Rubensohl: transfer to spades, invitational or better"
      alert  artificial
      shows S>=5, hcp>=8
      priority 3
  3S  "Rubensohl: game values, no stopper in hearts"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(H), S<=3
      priority 3
  3N  "Game with a stopper in hearts"
      shows hcp>=10, stop(H), S<=3
      priority 3

# ── Responder over 2♠ ───────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1N (2S) when rub_nt(S)
  2N  "Rubensohl: transfer to clubs, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows C>=6, C>=D, H<=3
      priority 3
  3C  "Rubensohl: transfer to diamonds, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows D>=6, D>C, H<=3
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: transfer to hearts, invitational or better"
      alert  artificial
      shows H>=5, hcp>=8
      priority 3
  3H  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, four hearts"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, H=4
      priority 3
  3S  "Rubensohl: game values, no stopper in spades"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=10, !stop(S), H<=3
      priority 3
  3N  "Game with a stopper in spades"
      shows hcp>=10, stop(S), H<=3
      priority 3

# ── Opener ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) when rub_nt_opener(y)
  3C  "Completes the transfer to clubs"           artificial
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3C (P) when rub_nt_opener(y), y is not D
  3D  "Completes the transfer to diamonds"        artificial
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3D (P) when rub_nt_opener(y), y is not H
  4H  "A maximum and three or more hearts: game"  shows H>=3, hcp>=17
      priority 4
  3N  "A maximum, two hearts"                     shows H<=2, hcp>=17
      priority 4
  3H  "Completes the transfer: a minimum"         artificial
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3H (P) when rub_nt_opener(y), y is not S
  4S  "A maximum and three or more spades: game"  shows S>=3, hcp>=17
      priority 4
  3N  "A maximum, two spades"                     shows S<=2, hcp>=17
      priority 4
  3S  "Completes the transfer: a minimum"         artificial
      priority 3
# Stayman (the transfer to their suit): the major, else 3NT with a
# stopper, else their suit (no stopper, no major).
after 1N (2D) 3C (P) when rub_nt_opener(D)
  3H  "Four hearts"                               shows H>=4
      priority 4
  3S  "Four spades"                               shows S>=4, H<=3
      priority 4
  3N  "No four-card major, diamonds stopped"      shows stop(D)
      priority 3
  3D  "No four-card major, no stopper"            artificial
      priority 2
after 1N (2H) 3D (P) when rub_nt_opener(H)
  3S  "Four spades"                               shows S>=4
      priority 4
  3N  "No four spades, hearts stopped"            shows stop(H)
      priority 3
  3H  "No four spades, no stopper"                artificial
      priority 2
after 1N (2S) 3H (P) when rub_nt_opener(S)
  4H  "Four hearts"                               shows H>=4
      priority 4
  3N  "No four hearts, spades stopped"            shows stop(S)
      priority 3
  3S  "No four hearts, no stopper"                artificial
      priority 2
# Game values without a stopper.
after 1N (2y) 3S (P) when rub_nt_opener(y)
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                          shows stop(y)
      priority 3
  4C  "No stopper: clubs"                         shows C>=D
      priority 2
  4D  "No stopper: diamonds"                      shows D>C
      priority 2

# ── Responder after the completion ──────────────────────────────────
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) 3C (P) when rub_nt(y)
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                    shows hcp<=9
      priority 3
  3N  "Game values with clubs"                    shows hcp>=10
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3C (P) 3D (P) when rub_nt(y), y is not D
  P   "Weak: to play in diamonds"                 shows hcp<=9
      priority 3
  3N  "Game values with diamonds"                 shows hcp>=10
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3D (P) 3H (P) when rub_nt(y), y is not H
  P   "Invitational: no more"                     shows hcp<=9
      priority 3
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"                  shows H>=6, hcp>=10
      priority 3
  3N  "Game: five hearts, choice of games"        shows H=5, hcp>=10
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3H (P) 3S (P) when rub_nt(y), y is not S
  P   "Invitational: no more"                     shows hcp<=9
      priority 3
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"                  shows S>=6, hcp>=10
      priority 3
  3N  "Game: five spades, choice of games"        shows S=5, hcp>=10
      priority 3
after 1N (2y) 3D (P) 3H (P) 3N (P) when rub_nt_opener(y), y is not H
  4H  "Three hearts: the major"                   shows H>=3
      priority 3
  P   "Two hearts: notrump"                       priority 2
after 1N (2y) 3H (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) when rub_nt_opener(y), y is not S
  4S  "Three spades: the major"                   shows S>=3
      priority 3
  P   "Two spades: notrump"                       priority 2
# After the Stayman answer.
after 1N (2D) 3C (P) 3H (P) | 1N (2D) 3C (P) 3S (P) | 1N (2H) 3D (P) 3S (P) | 1N (2S) 3H (P) 4H (P) when over_nt
  4H  "The heart fit: game"                       shows H>=4
      when  partner.H>=4
      priority 3
  4S  "The spade fit: game"                       shows S>=4
      when  partner.S>=4
      priority 3
  3N  "No fit: notrump"
      priority 2
  P   "Game reached"
      priority 1
after 1N (2D) 3C (P) 3D (P) | 1N (2H) 3D (P) 3H (P) | 1N (2S) 3H (P) 3S (P) when over_nt
  4C  "No stopper: clubs"              shows C>=4, C>=D
      priority 2
  4D  "No stopper: diamonds"           shows D>=4, D>C
      priority 2
  3N  "To play in 3NT"
      priority 1

# ════ 2. After partner doubles their weak two ═══════════════════════
# Advancer. Their suit x is 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠. Two of a suit is natural and
# weak (vs-preempts.bid).
after (2x) X (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) when after_x, x is not C
  2N  "Rubensohl: transfer to clubs, to play or invite"
      alert  artificial
      shows C>=4, C>=D, hcp<=12 | C>=5, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      priority 3
  3C  "Rubensohl: transfer to diamonds, to play or invite"
      alert  artificial
      shows D>=4, D>C, hcp<=12 | D>=5, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not D
      priority 3
  3C  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, a four-card major"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=13, H=4 | S=4, H<=4, S<=4
      when  x is D
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: transfer to hearts, four or more"
      alert  artificial
      shows H>=4, H>=S | x is S, hcp<=12
      when  x is S
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: transfer to hearts, five or more, 9-12"
      alert  artificial
      shows H>=5, H>=S, hcp>=9, hcp<=12
      when  x is D
      priority 3
  3D  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, four spades"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=13, S=4
      when  x is H
      priority 3
  3H  "Rubensohl: transfer to spades, five or more, 9-12"
      alert  artificial
      shows S>=5, hcp>=9, hcp<=12
      when  x is D | x is H
      priority 3
  3H  "Rubensohl: Stayman, game values, four hearts"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=13, H=4
      when  x is S
      priority 3
  3S  "Rubensohl: game values, no stopper in {x}, no four-card major"
      alert  artificial
      shows hcp>=13, !stop(x), H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
      priority 3
  3N  "Game with {x} stopped"
      shows hcp>=13, stop(x), H<=3 | x is H, S<=3 | x is S
      priority 3

# The doubler completes the transfer (with 17+ and four-card support for
# a major he bids game); answers the Stayman transfer with a major, else
# 3NT with a stopper, else their suit; over 3♠, 3NT with a stopper.
# With 19+ and their suit stopped the doubler bids 3NT instead, as over
# Lebensohl's relay (vs-preempts.bid); the self A/B (2026-10-05) lost
# the games that relay found, partner's transfer passed with 20-22.
after (2x) X (P) 2N (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) when after_x, x is not C
  3N  "19+ with {x} stopped: game"               shows hcp>=19, stop(x)
      priority 4
  3C  "Completes the transfer"                    artificial
      priority 3
after (2x) X (P) 3C (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3C (P) when after_x, x is not C, x is not D
  3N  "19+ with {x} stopped: game"               shows hcp>=19, stop(x)
      priority 4
  3D  "Completes the transfer"                    artificial
      priority 3
after (2x) X (P) 3D (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3D (P) when after_x, x is not C, x is not H
  4H  "17+ and four hearts: game"                 shows H>=4, hcp>=17
      priority 5
  3N  "19+ with {x} stopped, two hearts or fewer: game"   shows hcp>=19, stop(x), H<=2
      priority 4
  3H  "Completes the transfer"                    artificial
      priority 3
after (2x) X (P) 3H (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3H (P) when after_x, x is not C, x is not S
  4S  "17+ and four spades: game"                 shows S>=4, hcp>=17
      priority 5
  3N  "19+ with {x} stopped, two spades or fewer: game"   shows hcp>=19, stop(x), S<=2
      priority 4
  3S  "Completes the transfer"                    artificial
      priority 3
after (2x) X (P) 3C (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3C (P) when after_x, x is D
  3H  "Four hearts"                               shows H>=4
      priority 4
  3S  "Four spades"                               shows S>=4, H<=3
      priority 4
  3N  "No four-card major, diamonds stopped"      shows stop(D)
      priority 3
  3D  "No four-card major, no stopper"            artificial
      priority 2
after (2x) X (P) 3D (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3D (P) when after_x, x is H
  3S  "Four spades"                               shows S>=4
      priority 4
  3N  "No four spades, hearts stopped"            shows stop(H)
      priority 3
  3H  "No four spades, no stopper"                artificial
      priority 2
after (2x) X (P) 3H (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3H (P) when after_x, x is S
  4H  "Four hearts"                               shows H>=4
      priority 4
  3N  "No four hearts, spades stopped"            shows stop(S)
      priority 3
  3S  "No four hearts, no stopper"                artificial
      priority 2
after (2x) X (P) 3S (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3S (P) when after_x, x is not C
  3N  "A stopper in {x}"                          shows stop(x)
      priority 3
  4C  "No stopper: clubs"                         shows C>=D
      priority 2
  4D  "No stopper: diamonds"                      shows D>C
      priority 2

# Advancer after the completion: pass when weak, else game.
after (2x) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) | (2x) X (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3C (P) 3D (P) when after_x, x is not C
  P   "Weak: to play"                             shows hcp<=8
      priority 3
  3N  "9+ with {x} stopped"                       shows hcp>=9, stop(x)
      priority 3
  P   "To play"                            priority 1
after (2x) X (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3D (P) 3H (P) when after_x, x is not C, x is not H
  4H  "Game: 11+ with five, or 12+"               shows hcp>=11, H>=5 | hcp>=12
      priority 3
  P   "Weak or invitational: no more"             priority 1
after (2x) X (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) when after_x, x is not C, x is not S
  4S  "Game: 11+ with five, or 12+"               shows hcp>=11, S>=5 | hcp>=12
      priority 3
  P   "Invitational: no more"                     priority 1
files.rules/competitive/rubensohl.notes.md:
# Rubensohl (`rubensohl.bid`)

Two switches: `notrump.rubensohl.play` (after they
overcall our 1NT) and `competitive.rubensohl_after_double.play` (after
partner's takeout double of their weak two). Both are on in the
Precision and Precision-14-16 cards, with Lebensohl off. Cases:
`rubensohl.test`.

## What it plays (2026-10-05)

Over a natural 2♦/2♥/2♠ overcall of our 1NT: two of a suit natural, the
double as the card says; 2NT clubs, 3♣ diamonds, 3♦ hearts, 3♥ spades,
3♠ notrump. Transfers to a minor: six or more (weak to play, or game
values then 3NT). To a major: five or more, invitational or better. The
transfer to their suit is Stayman (game values, four of an unbid
major); the transfer to notrump is game values without a stopper and
without a four-card major; 3NT game with a stopper. Opener completes
with a minimum (15-16); with 17 bids game with three of the major, 3NT
without. Responder after the completion: pass weak or invitational,
game with six of the major, 3NT with five (opener corrects with three).

After our double of their weak two the same transfers from 2NT, the
doubler in opener's place: four-card minors (weak to play at three, or
9+ with five), majors 9-12 (over 2♠ the heart transfer is any hand up to
12), the transfer to their suit Stayman with 13+, 3♠ game without a
stopper, 3NT with one.

Switching it on turns off Lebensohl over 1NT (notrump/lebensohl.bid,
`!rub` on its contexts), the natural 2NT invitation over their
overcall (notrump/nt-interference.bid, `!rub`), and Lebensohl and the
natural three-level replies after the double (vs-preempts.bid,
`!(leb | rub)`). The natural three-level forcing bids of
nt-interference.bid stay, outranked by the transfers (priority 3).

## Deviations and open questions

- Over their 2♣ (natural) nothing changes: like our Lebensohl, Rubensohl
  reads only 2♦/2♥/2♠.
- "Rubensohl after 1m" (BBA key, on in the Precision cards) has no card
  field; not written.
- Sources disagree in detail: Wikipedia's Rubinsohl (2NT clubs and up,
  3♣ over 2♦ is Stayman) is what we play; Larry Cohen's and Todd's
  "Transfer Lebensohl" keep a 2NT relay. Question for Rick if the
  Precision partnership plays the other.

## Compare (2026-10-05)

Lebensohl and Lebensohl2 with `--set notrump.rubensohl.play=true`
(84.8% agreement), Lebensohl_vs_Opps_W2_* with
`--set competitive.rubensohl_after_double.play=true` (85.2%): the
divergences at our calls are the transfers against BBA's Lebensohl
(1NT 2♠: our 3♦ transfer where BBA bids a natural 3♥, our 3♥ Stayman
where BBA makes a negative double). No forced passes or contradictions.
Tripwire: three boards in Weak_NT_11-16, SCS_Two_Clubs and
Weak_NT_14-15 (Precision cards); in the last, 1NT 2♥ 2NT (natural
invitation) became a pass, since Rubensohl has no natural 2NT.
Question for Rick: invite in notrump by double, or keep it as is.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only
rubensohl-vs-lebensohl-nt, rubensohl-vs-lebensohl-x`. IMPs by the errors
yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer; "actor" is the side
that made the first differing call. Against Lebensohl (both on in the
base, Rubensohl added). Over their overcall of 1NT, Lebensohl and
Lebensohl2: 258 boards changed; actor contract -44, doubling -12,
double-dummy -82, halves -6/-50 (z -0.9): neutral. After our double of a
weak two (Lebensohl_vs_Opps_W2_*): first -251 to the actor (z -1.6),
three bugs: (1) advancer with 9-12 and only a four-card minor had no
call and passed the double for penalty (2♥ X P P, -670); the minor
transfers now take 4+ up to 12; (2) vs-preempts.bid's natural 3M
invitational jump stayed on, and the doubler read 3♠ as Rubensohl's "no
stopper" (4♣ in a 5-3 spade fit); it is now off under Rubensohl over a
two-level preempt; (3) the doubler had no 3NT with 19+ over the
transfer, as Lebensohl's relay has. After: 741 boards changed; actor
contract +181, doubling -43; other side contract +120, doubling -153;
double-dummy +63; halves +31/+107 (z +1.0): leans gain.

## Sources

- Wikipedia, "Rubinsohl" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubinsohl):
  the transfer scheme over 2♦, "at least invitational" major transfers,
  3♠ game without a stopper, the same scheme after the double of a weak
  two.
- Larry Cohen, "Transfer Lebensohl"
  (https://www.larryco.com/bridge-articles/transfer-lebensohl), and
  Robert S. Todd, Adventures in Bridge 548: opener completes with a
  minimum, any other bid is forcing.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Takeout doubles of a one-level opening, and advancer's replies
# (Rick, 2026-09-22):
#
# - a takeout double is 12 total points with three or more cards in every
#   unbid suit;
# - it is also the call with 17+ HCP and any shape, including a long
#   strong suit: too strong to overcall is double first, then bid the suit
#   (overcalls.bid stops at 16 HCP). In HCP since 2026-09-27: BBA's power
#   doubles step up at 17 HCP (takeout-double.notes.md), and an HCP
#   threshold lets the deck and the auction rule the power hand out;
# - advancer answers on the standard ladder: a suit at the cheapest level
#   is 0-8, a jump 9-11, and the cue bid of their suit 12+;
# - advancer bids his longest suit, majors first, and the cheaper of two
#   equal suits.
#
# Not written yet: responsive doubles (off on this card), advancer over
# RHO's bid, and doubles of anything but a one-level suit opening.

module takeout-double "Takeout doubles"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  needs  overcalls
  skill  competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles
  param  oc_max = overcalls.one_level_max default 16

# ── The double ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after (1x)
  X   "Takeout: the unbid suits and 12+, or any 18+"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C)) | hcp>=oc_max+1
      # A queen or jack, alone, in a doubleton of their suit is marked
      # down: 12 with Qx or Jx there passes, 13 doubles. BBA does this at
      # every vulnerability (probes/td-1S-shape.toml; ticket b60); we only
      # at unfavourable, the one where it gains on both yardsticks (notes).
      shows hcp+length_points>=13 | x>=3 | has(A,x) | has(K,x) | (!has(Q,x), !has(J,x)) | !vul | they.vul

# ── Advancer, when RHO passes ────────────────────────────────────────
# The double is forcing: advancer names his suit however weak he is.
# A suit at the cheapest level says nothing beyond 0-8 total points.
after (1x) X (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P)
  1H  "0-8 total points, four or more hearts"   shows H>=4, H>=S | x is S, hcp+length_points<=8 | (H=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not H, x is not S
  1S  "0-8 total points, four or more spades"   shows S>=4, S>H | x is H, hcp+length_points<=8 | (S=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not S
  1D  "0-8 total points, four or more diamonds" shows D>=4, D>C, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H, hcp+length_points<=8 | (D=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not D, x is not H, x is not S
  2C  "0-8 total points, four or more clubs"    shows C>=4, C>=D, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H, hcp+length_points<=8 | (C=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not C
  2D  "0-8 total points, four or more diamonds" shows D>=4, D>C, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H, hcp+length_points<=8 | (D=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not D, x is not C
  2H  "0-8 total points, four or more hearts"   shows H>=4, H>=S | x is S, hcp+length_points<=8 | (H=4, hcp<=9)
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
  1N  "7-10 HCP, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp>=7, hcp<=10
      when  stop(x)

# Jumps invite: 9-11 total points with the same suits.
after (1x) X (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P)
  2H  "9-11 total points, four or more hearts"   shows H>=4, H>=S | x is S, hcp+length_points=9..11, H>=5 | hcp>=10
      when  x is not H, x is not S
  2S  "9-11 total points, four or more spades"   shows S>=4, S>H | x is H, hcp+length_points=9..11, S>=5 | hcp>=10
      when  x is not S
  3C  "9-11 total points, four or more clubs"    shows C>=4, C>=D, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H, hcp+length_points=9..11, C>=5 | hcp>=10
      when  x is not C
  3D  "9-11 total points, four or more diamonds" shows D>=4, D>C, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H, hcp+length_points=9..11, D>=5 | hcp>=10
      when  x is not D, x is not C
  3H  "9-11 total points, four or more hearts"   shows H>=4, H>=S | x is S, hcp+length_points=9..11, H>=5 | hcp>=10
      when  x is not H, x is not D, x is not C
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points=11..12
      when  stop(x)

# BBA (probes/advance-1S-X.toml, 2026-09-25): 12+ with their suit held
# and no four-card unbid major bids 3NT; with no four-card suit to name,
# the cheapest three-card suit.
after (1x) X (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P)
  3N  "Game: 12+, a stopper in {x}"  shows hcp>=12, stop(x), (H<=3 | x is H), (S<=3 | x is S)
      priority 2
  1D  "0-8, no four-card suit to show: three diamonds"  shows D>=3, H<=3, S<=3, hcp<=8
      when  x is C
      priority -2
  1H  "0-8, no four-card suit to show: three hearts"   shows H>=3, S<=3, hcp<=8
      when  x is not H, x is not S
      priority -3
  2C  "0-8, no four-card suit to show: three clubs"    shows C>=3, H<=3, S<=3, hcp<=8
      when  x is not C
      priority -2
  2D  "0-8, no four-card suit to show: three diamonds" shows D>=3, H<=3, S<=3, hcp<=8
      when  x is not D, x is not C
      priority -3

# The cue bid is the only game force: 12+ with no clear suit to jump in.
after (1x) X (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P)
  2{x} "Cue bid: 12+ total points, asks for a description"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=game
      priority 1

# ── The doubler's rebid ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Advancer's cheapest suit said 0-8, so a minimum double passes. The
# hands too strong to overcall show themselves now: 18+ total points
# bids its own suit, raises with support, or bids notrump with a
# stopper. This is the second half of "double first, then bid the suit".
after (1x) X (P) 1y (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P) 1y (P)
  P   "Minimum takeout double"
      shows hcp<=16
      priority -5
  2{y} "18-19 total points, four-card support"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points=17..19
  3{y} "20-21 total points, four-card support"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points=20..21
  4{y} "22+ total points, four-card support for partner's major"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=22
      when  y is H | y is S
  1N  "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp=17..19
      when  stop(x)
  cheapest(S) "18+ total points and a five-card spade suit"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "18+ total points and a five-card heart suit"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "18+ total points and a five-card diamond suit"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "18+ total points and a five-card club suit"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not C, y is not C

after (1x) X (P) 2y (P) | (1x) P (P) X (P) 2y (P)
  P   "Minimum takeout double"
      shows hcp<=16
      priority -5
  3{y} "Strong raise: four-card support, 18+"
      shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
  3{y} "Strong raise: three-card support, 20+"
      shows y=3, hcp>=20
  cheapest(S) "18+ total points and a five-card spade suit"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "18+ total points and a five-card heart suit"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "18+ total points and a five-card diamond suit"
      shows D>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "18+ total points and a five-card club suit"
      shows C>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  2N  "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp=17..19
      when  stop(x)

# The doubler again when they compete (2026-09-25; no rules before). BBA:
# after (1x) X (2x) P P a five-card suit with 16+, or double again with
# 12+ short in their suit; when opener competes over the advance, raise
# with four and 16+, or show a five-card suit with 16+ (+645 with the
# suit bids). The second double first cost ~1,500 IMPs against par
# because advancer had no answer and left it in; with the takeout
# answers below it gains (2026-09-27, ticket b89, notes).
after (1x) X (2x) P (P)
  cheapest(S) "16+ and five spades"                 shows S>=5, hcp>=16
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "16+ and five hearts"                 shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp>=16
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  X   "Takeout again: short in {x}"                 shows x<=1, hcp>=12
  P   "No further bid"                                priority -5

# Advancer after the second double: it is still for takeout. Bid the
# longest unbid suit, a major first; pass only with a trump stack.
after (1x) X (2x) P (P) X (P)
  cheapest(S) "Takeout: four or more spades"        shows S>=4, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Takeout: four or more hearts"        shows H>=4, H>=D, H>=C
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Takeout: my longest, diamonds"       shows D>=C
      when  x is not D
  cheapest(C) "Takeout: my longest, clubs"          shows C>=3
      when  x is not C
      priority -1
  P   "Penalty: five of their suit"                 shows x>=5, hcp>=5
      priority 2

after (1x) X (P) 1y (2x) | (1x) X (P) 2y (2x)
  3{y} "16+, four-card support"                     shows y>=4, hcp+length_points>=16
  cheapest(C) "16+ and five clubs"                  shows C>=5, hcp>=16, y<=3
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  cheapest(D) "16+ and five diamonds"               shows D>=5, D>C, hcp>=16, y<=3
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  # The strong balanced double, as without their bid (2026-10-05, the
  # Raptor self A/B: 1♣ X P 1♥ 2♣ passed with 18 HCP; BBA bids 2NT).
  2N  "18-19 balanced with a stopper in {x}"       shows balanced, hcp=17..19
      when  stop(x)
  P   "No further bid"                                priority -5

# The doubler when their responder bid over the double, partner passed
# and opener bid again (2026-09-25: 1H (X) 1S (P) 1NT, where 18+ with a
# long suit passed). The strong double shows its suit now.
after (1x) X (1y) P (*) | (1x) X (2y) P (*) when y is not x, !rho.last=P
  cheapest(S) "18+ total points and five spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "18+ total points and five hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "18+ total points and five diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "18+ total points and five clubs"
      shows C>=5, D<=4, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=18 | hcp>=17
      when  x is not C, y is not C

# The doubler after advancer's cue bid when opener bids again
# (2026-09-27; Basic_Takeout_Double 193, 1H (X) P (2H) 3H). The cue bid
# forced to game and asked for a description. The power double (17+
# HCP) doubles; anything less describes itself, or passes where the
# force allows it. So not doubling denies the power hand, and partner can
# count the double's shape (the Law of Total Tricks, total-tricks.bid).
after (1x) X (P) 2x (*) when !rho.last=P
  X   "Power double: 17+ HCP"
      shows hcp>=17
      priority 1
  P   "No extras: 16 or less"                   shows hcp<=16
      priority -5
  # Below the pass: where the game force rules the pass out, the
  # minimum describes itself; a pass (BBA's forcing pass) denies only
  # the power hand, not every four-card suit.
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades, no extras"   shows S>=4, hcp<=16
      when  x is not S
      priority -6
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts, no extras"   shows H>=4, S<=3, hcp<=16
      when  x is not H
      priority -6
  cheapest(N) "A stopper in {x}, no extras"     shows stop(x), hcp<=16
      priority -7
  # Four-card minors up the line (Rick, ticket b455): clubs with 4-4.
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds, no extras" shows D>=4, D>C | x is C, hcp<=16
      when  x is not D
      priority -8
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs, no extras"    shows C>=4, C>=D | x is D, hcp<=16
      when  x is not C
      priority -8

# ── Advancer when RHO does not pass ──────────────────────────────────
# The double is no longer forcing: advancer passes with nothing and bids
# his own suit freely. Over a one-level bid a four-card major is enough;
# higher up he needs five cards and more values.
after (1x) X (1y) | (1x) P (P) X (1y)
  1S  "Free bid: 6+ total points, four or more spades"
      shows S>=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: 6+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Free bid: 6+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=3, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Free bid: 6+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=3, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=6
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  1N  "8-11 total points, balanced, a stopper in both their suits"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=8, hcp+length_points<=11
      when  stop(x), stop(y)
  2{x} "Cue bid: 12+ total points"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=12
      sets   forcing=game
      priority 1
  P   "No free bid"  priority -10

after (1x) X (2y) | (1x) P (P) X (2y)
  cheapest(S) "Free bid: 8+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Free bid: 8+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not H, y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Free bid: 8+ total points, five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not D, y is not D
  cheapest(C) "Free bid: 8+ total points, five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=8
      when  x is not C, y is not C
  2N  "11-12 total points, balanced, a stopper in {x}"
      shows balanced, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp+length_points<=12
      when  stop(x)
  P   "No free bid"  priority -10

# RHO redoubled: partner still wants to hear a suit, so advancer names
# his cheapest four-card suit however weak he is.
after (1x) X (XX) | (1x) P (P) X (XX)
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades"   shows S>=4, S>H
      when  x is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts"   shows H>=4, H>=S
      when  x is not H
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds" shows D>=4, D>C, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not D
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs"    shows C>=4, C>=D, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not C
  P   "No four-card suit to name"  priority -10

# The doubler when advancer passed the redouble (2026-09-27, ticket b197:
# 1S X XX P P P was -520). Advancer had no four-card suit to name, so the
# doubler runs to his cheapest four-card suit and advancer corrects;
# leaving it in needs four of their suit.
after (1x) X (XX) P (P)
  cheapest(C) "Rescue: four or more clubs, the cheapest"     shows C>=4
      when  x is not C
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Rescue: four or more diamonds, the cheapest"  shows D>=4, C<=3 | x is C
      when  x is not D
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Rescue: four or more hearts, the cheapest"    shows H>=4, C<=3 | x is C, D<=3 | x is D
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Rescue: four or more spades"                  shows S>=4, C<=3 | x is C, D<=3 | x is D, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
  P   "Leaves it in: four or more of their suit"             shows x>=4
      priority 2


# ── The double of their raise (2026-10-05) ───────────────────────────
# (1x) P (2x) X: they have found a fit, so the double is for takeout,
# not penalty (penalty-doubles.bid read it as penalty, priority -6):
# a singleton or void in their suit, three or more in each unbid suit,
# 13+ HCP (BBA mostly passes there: a first try at 12+ total points
# with a doubleton doubled on 95 of the tripwire's boards, BBA agreed
# on 14; scrambling-2nt.notes.md). Written with Scrambling 2NT (scrambling-2nt.bid), whose
# scenario starts here (PBS btn/Scrambling_2NT.btn: 13+, 4-4-4-1 or
# 5-4-4-0 short in their major).
after (1x) P (2x)
  X   "Takeout of their raise: short in {x}, the unbid suits, 13+ HCP"
      shows hcp>=13, x<=1
      shows (S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C)

# Advancer must bid (they have a fit; partner is short there): his
# longest unbid suit, majors first; four of a major or 3NT with game
# values opposite the double; a pass only with their suit stacked.
after (1x) P (2x) X (P)
  4S  "Game: four or more spades, 11+"
      shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
  4H  "Game: four or more hearts, 11+"
      shows H>=4, H>S | x is S, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  3N  "Game: 11+ with {x} stopped"
      shows hcp>=11, stop(x), S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      priority 1
  P   "Penalty: five or more {x} with two top honours"
      shows x>=5, quality(x)>=good
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades"     shows S>=4, S>=H | x is H
      when  x is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts"     shows H>=4, H>S | x is S
      when  x is not H
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds"   shows D>=4, D>C, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not D
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs"      shows C>=4, C>=D, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not C
  # No four-card suit: the longest unbid suit, cheapest first.
  cheapest(C) "No four-card suit: clubs"    when x is not C, C>=D | x is D
      priority -5
  cheapest(D) "No four-card suit: diamonds" when x is not D, D>C | x is C
      priority -5
  cheapest(H) "No four-card suit: hearts"   when x is not H
      priority -6
  cheapest(S) "No four-card suit: spades"   when x is not S
      priority -7

# Takeout doubles (`takeout-double.bid`): notes

The direct double of a one-level opening, advancer's replies, and the
doubler's rebid. Cases: `takeout-double.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-22)

- **12 total points with three or more cards in every unbid suit.**
- **18+ total points doubles whatever the shape**, including with a long
  strong suit: too strong to overcall is double first, then bid the suit.
  That is why the double's second branch starts one point above the
  overcall maximum (`overcalls.one_level_max` + 1).
- **Advancer answers on the standard ladder**: the cheapest suit is 0-8,
  a jump 9-11, and the cue bid of their suit 12+ and forcing to game.
  (BBA's own ladder is 0-10 / 7-12 / 10+, which we did not copy.)
- Advancer bids his longest suit, majors first, and the cheaper of two
  equal suits.
- **The doubler passes a minimum** and shows his extra values afterwards:
  18-19 raises one level, 20-21 two, 22+ bids the major game, and a
  five-card suit of his own is bid at the cheapest level.

## Evidence

From `bba-cli --all-meanings` on the two Basic scenarios:

- **(1x) X** — "takeout double", 12-37 total points, 3+ in each unbid
  suit and at most four of theirs. The hands were 10-18 HCP, median 13,
  and typically 4-4-3 or 4-3-3 in the unbid suits.
- **(1x) X (P)** — advancer: a minimum suit bid 0-10 total points with
  4+; a jump 7-12; the cue bid "strength cue bid", 10+.

The double is what BBA does with most 12-17 balanced-ish hands short in
their suit: it is the single largest divergence in these two scenarios
(424 of the 1,000 boards diverged at call 2 with BBA doubling and us
passing). Adding it took call-2 agreement from 46.6% to 87.5%.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- Our ladder starts the jump at 9 and the cue bid at 12; BBA's bands
  overlap (7-12 for a jump, 10+ for the cue bid), so boundary hands
  differ.
- BBA doubles some 10-11 HCP hands with shape that we pass, and passes
  some 12-counts with a five-card suit that we double.
- We require three cards in every unbid suit; BBA's meaning allows a
  doubleton in an unbid minor on stronger hands.

Advancer when RHO does not pass is written too: a free bid needs 6+ at
the one level and 8+ higher, the cue bid is still 12+, and over a
redouble advancer names his cheapest four-card suit however weak. That
alone took Basic_Takeout_Double from 71.3% to 72.5% of calls and its
contracts from 5.6% to 7.4%.

## Gaps and open questions

- **Responsive doubles** are in `responsive-doubles.bid`, switched on by
  `doubles.responsive.play` — the 21GF cards play them, Basic-Bridge does
  not, so on this card a double by advancer over their raise still has no
  rule.
- The **penalty pass** of a takeout double with length in their suit.
- Doubles of anything but a one-level suit opening: weak twos, preempts,
  1NT, and the **balancing double**.
- Advancer's rebid after the cue bid (the cue sets `forcing=game`, so the
  base rule bids game in the agreed suit or 3NT).

## Advancer, probed (2026-09-25, `probes/advance-1S-X.toml`)

2,000 random advancer hands after 1S X P (Basic-Bridge). Agreement
before: 45%; after: 55%. Corpus: -162,699 -> -162,394 (+305).
- **3NT with 12+ and their suit stopped** (no four-card unbid major),
  where we cue-bid. Worth +72 alone. **For Rick:** this overrides "the
  cue bid is 12+" for hands with a stopper. Test 19 now expects 3NT.
- **No four-card suit to name** (four of their suit, say): BBA bids the
  cheapest three-card suit. We had no call.
- **1NT is 7-10 HCP** with a stopper. Total points put 5-3-3-2 hands
  with nine or ten out of range, leaving them no call.
- **Jumps:** BBA does not jump with four cards and 9 HCP. It jumps with
  five from about 8, or four with 10-11. Four cards and 9 now bid at the
  cheapest level.

Not done: BBA's penalty pass with long strong trumps; the rest of the
disagreement is mostly the level with 9-11 (2S cue vs 3H...).
- **Their suit is not an unbid major** (2026-09-25). The advances in a
  minor said S<=3, H<=3, meant to prefer an unbid major. That left four
  of their suit (spades over 1S) with no call: 177 corpus boards. The
  guards now read `S<=3 | x is S`. The heart advance says the same about
  spades. Corpus: -162,394 -> -162,157.

## The double itself, probed over 1S (2026-09-25, `probes/tod-1S.toml`)

2,500 hands with three or fewer spades and 9-19 HCP over 1S: 80%
agreement. BBA's threshold is HCP by shortness. With a singleton in
their suit it doubles from 10-11 HCP (and prefers the double to a
two-level minor overcall at 11-14). With a doubleton it doubles from
12 HCP; 11 with a five-card suit passes, where our total points double.
Tried against par:

| Change | IMPs |
|---|---|
| 12 HCP, or 10 with a singleton | -314 |
| Our 12 total points, plus 10 HCP with a singleton | -380 |
| Two-level overcalls on three of the top five honours instead of four | -285 |

Ours stays in all three.

## The power double in HCP (2026-09-27)

Step a of the Law of Total Tricks work (Basic_Takeout_Double 193). The
double's second meaning was "18+ total points, any shape". Length
points can add nine to an unknown hand, so no HCP limit could ever rule
the power hand out, and the double never collapsed to "three or more
in the unbid suits". BBA (`probes/tools/takeout_shape.py` and a scan
of 913 auctions where the doubler, free to pass, then bids a new suit
or notrump): its power double steps up at 17 **HCP** (12-14: 103
hands, the competitive minimum; 15: 9; 16: 5; 17: 129; 18: 268), and
counted as HCP plus length the same hands show no step. Rick: treat it
as a likelihood, accepting the rare distributional power double below
17 that the inference will misread.

| power branch | full corpus (par / side) | Basic_* competitive |
|---|---|---|
| 18+ HCP, overcall to 17 | -937 / -2,176 | -3 / -26 |
| 17+ HCP, overcall to 17 (overlap) | +13 / -171 | -11 / -11 |
| 17+ HCP, overcall to 16 | +1 / +154 | -11 / -11 |

Kept: 17+ HCP with the overcall to 16 (`one_level_max` default 16),
neutral on its own; its value is the inferences it allows. **For
Rick:** this lowers the overcall ceiling from 17 to 16 HCP; the
fallback is the overlap version (overcall to 17), -171 by side.

## Step c: the doubler's pass denies the power double (2026-09-27)

For the double to collapse to its shape, a pass must deny 17+ HCP.

- The doubler's rebids after an advance: the "minimum" pass is now 16
  HCP or less (was 17 total points); the strong actions are "18 total
  points, or 17 HCP". Moving the ladder wholly to HCP lost (-38 by par
  distance, -327 by side: 15-16 counts with a long suit stopped bidding
  it); the mixed version is neutral (+1 / -58).
- After advancer's cue bid and opener's rebid (1♥ (X) P (2♥) 3♥, board
  193) there was no rule. Now: double with 17+; pass with 16 or less
  (BBA's forcing pass, and ours where the force allows it); where the
  game force rules the pass out, a four-card suit or notrump. The suit
  bids rank **below** the pass, so a pass denies only the power hand:
  ranked above it, the pass also denied every four-card suit and read
  South as exactly 3-4-3-3. Full corpus +100 / +139, Basic_*
  competitive +17 / +24.

On board 193, North now reads South's pass as 0-16 HCP with three or
more spades, diamonds and clubs.

## The second double, (1x) X (2x) P (P) X (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b89: our West raised 1♠–X–2♠ at once
(BBA passed and bid 2♠ a round later), and Rick asked whether that shut
North–South out of their club fit. It did not in BBA's hands: given
`1S X 2S`, bba-cli goes on `P P X P 3C`, the same +130 as its own
auction. What shut us out was our doubler's pass. The second double
(12+, short in their suit) had been left out on 2026-09-25 as costing
~1,500 IMPs against par, but advancer had no rule after it and left
every one in for penalty. With takeout answers (longest unbid suit, a
major first; pass with five trumps and 5+):

| doubler shows | full corpus (par / side) | boards |
|---|---|---|
| **x<=1, 12+ (kept)** | **+169 / +377** | 212 |
| x<=2, 12+ | +159 / +515 | 372 |
| x<=1, 14+ | +136 / +244 | 124 |

Both yardsticks agree on all three; the singleton version is best by
par. Advancer with 4-4 in the minors bids 3♦ (3♣ measured 6 IMPs
worse on both, noise). Board 89 now goes `1S X 2S P P X P 3D`, +110
against BBA's +130.

## Wasted honours in their suit (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b60: South doubled 1♠ with
QT.J95.KJ95.KQT2 (12 HCP, NS vulnerable), BBA passed. Rick asked how
BBA values such hands: his instinct was that the QT is not worth two
points, that the tens and nines should help, and that a shape double
wants 13+ dummy points.

`probes/td-1S-shape.toml`: 500 hands, 10-15 HCP, a doubleton spade and
three or more in the other suits, over 1♠, all four vulnerabilities.
Without a five-card minor:

| spade holding | 12 HCP | 13 HCP |
|---|---|---|
| no honour | X 12 | X 13 |
| A or K (with or without J) | X 10 | X 13 |
| Q or J alone | **P 10** | X 7 |

So BBA marks a lone queen or jack in a doubleton of their suit down by
about a point, and the same at every vulnerability. It gives no
visible credit for tens and nines here (QT passes like Q2), and a 12
count with a doubleton and nothing wasted doubles: it does not ask for
13 dummy points.

Played at every vulnerability the discount splits the yardsticks: +418
par, −218 side IMPs (360 boards). By the doubler's vulnerability:

| doubler / opponents | boards | side | par |
|---|---|---|---|
| nv / nv | 82 | −78 | +94 |
| nv / vul | 83 | −104 | +137 |
| **vul / nv** | 96 | **+3** | **+101** |
| vul / vul | 99 | −39 | +86 |

Only at unfavourable do both agree, which is where Rick's "especially
vulnerable" pointed. Kept there: +103 par, +23 side (108 boards).
Elsewhere the light double wins by side IMPs (it gets us into the
auction). Board 60 now passes 1♠ as BBA does.

## After the redouble (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b197: `1S X XX P P P`, −520. Two holes:

- Advancer's rules after the redouble kept `S<=3, H<=3` on the minor
  suits, meant to send four-card majors to the major but also blocking
  a minor when the four spades were *their* suit. North,
  J975.JT.KQ972.87, had to pass; BBA bids 2♦ (`rbb probe`, prefix
  `1S X XX`). Now `S<=3 | x is S`, like the other advance rules.
- The doubler had no rule after `(1x) X (XX) P (P)` and sat in the
  redouble. Advancer's pass there says no four-card suit to name, so
  the doubler now runs to his cheapest four-card suit (partner
  corrects), and leaves it in only with four of their suit.

Full corpus: +2,567 par, +4,771 side IMPs (604 boards).

## Game in a known fit; minors up the line (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b455: `1H X P 2H 3H 4D P`, and North, with
five spades opposite a double that promised three, had no rule in a
game force. The game-force fallback in base.bid knew only the agreed
suit and 3NT; it now also bids game in an eight-card fit that has been
shown but not agreed (a major ahead of 3NT, a minor after it). The
doubler shows four-card minors up the line (clubs with 4-4).
Full corpus: +1,392 par, +1,698 side IMPs (1,049 boards). One test
changed: 2C 2D 2H with three hearts and 8 HCP now bids 4♥, not the
fallback 3NT.

## The strong balanced double when they raise (2026-10-05)

`(1x) X (P) 1y (2x)`: the doubler with 18-19 balanced and their suit
stopped bids 2NT, as without their raise (BBA bids it: We_Overcall_1N
board 343). Found by the Raptor self A/B (raptor.notes.md), where the
strong balanced hands double instead of overcalling 1NT; before, the
doubler passed.

## Sources

- **Rick's rulings:** the double (12 total points and three cards in
  every unbid suit, or 18+ any shape), advancer's standard ladder (0-8,
  9-11, cue bid 12+), the doubler's rebids (2026-09-22); the power double
  as a likelihood from 17 HCP (2026-09-27). Tickets
  basic-takeout-double-b89 (the second double) and -b60 (wasted honours
  in their suit, "especially vulnerable"), 2026-09-27.
- **Book practice:** the advancer ladder is the "standard ladder" in
  Rick's words, as opposed to BBA's 0-10 / 7-12 / 10+. Standard practice,
  not yet cited to a book or article.
- **BBA evidence:** `bba-cli --all-meanings` on the two Basic scenarios;
  the scan of 913 auctions with `probes/tools/takeout_shape.py`.
- **BBA probes:** `probes/advance-1S-X.toml` and `probes/tod-1S.toml`
  (2026-09-25), `probes/td-1S-shape.toml` (2026-09-27), and `rbb probe`
  after the redouble.
- **Corpus measurements:** the power-branch table and the later steps,
  judged by par distance and by side IMPs.
- **Where we differ:** our ladder bands against BBA's overlapping ones;
  boundary doubles; three cards in every unbid suit ("Accepted
  differences from BBA"). The overcall ceiling moved from 17 to 16 HCP,
  pending Rick.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responder after RHO overcalls partner's one-level opening with 1NT.
#
# `after-interference.bid` writes every one-level context as `after 1x (1y)`,
# and `1y` binds a suit, so nothing there fires over a notrump overcall and
# responder passed whatever he held. `1D (1N)` and `1C (1N)` were the two
# largest no-rule points in the corpus.
#
# Their 1NT is 15-18 balanced with a stopper, so partner's opening plus our
# own hand locates the rest of the deck: with 10+ total points we own the
# balance and double for penalty. Otherwise it is a competitive auction one
# level up, and the calls are natural. Nine total points is the floor for
# bidding a suit of our own: they have 15-18 and a stopper, so entering at
# the two level on less runs into their strength. BBA declares the bid as
# 7-12 but only makes it from 9 up (366 of the 406 `Opps_Overcall_1NT`
# decisions match at 9; the declared 7 matches 344).
#
# See their-1nt-overcall.notes.md for the BBA meanings this is built from.

module their-1nt-overcall "Responder over their 1NT overcall"
  kind   system
  needs  base

after 1x (1N)
  X   "Penalty: 10+ total points, no long suit of our own"
      shows hcp+length_points>=10
      when  (S<=4 | x is S), (H<=4 | x is H)
      when  C<=5, D<=5
      priority 1

  2{x} "Raise: 6-9 total points, support for partner's suit"
      shows x>=3, tp(x)>=6, tp(x)<=9
      when  x is H | x is S | x>=5
      priority 1                      # a fit first, even holding a suit of our own

  2H  "9+ total points, five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not H

  2S  "9+ total points, five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not S

  2C  "9+ total points, six or more clubs"
      shows C>=6, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not C

  2D  "9+ total points, six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6, hcp+length_points>=9
      when  x is not D

  # Seven cards and too little to bid them at the two level and be
  # raised: jump instead and take the room away. At nine total points
  # both this and the 2-level bid fit, and the seven-card suit says more.
  3C  "Preemptive: seven or more clubs, 5-9 total points"
      shows C>=7, hcp+length_points>=5, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is not C
  3D  "Preemptive: seven or more diamonds, 5-9 total points"
      shows D>=7, hcp+length_points>=5, hcp+length_points<=9
      when  x is not D

  # No preemptive jump raise: BBA's 4M over their 1NT is a shapely 11
  # count, not a weak five-card raise, and jumping to game on a raise
  # this side of their 15-18 loses contracts.

  P   "No suitable bid"  priority -10

# Opener after partner's penalty double of their 1NT (2026-09-27, ticket
# b160: no rule). With 10+ opposite and an opening here, the double is
# theirs to escape: sit, and pull only a minimum with a six-card suit and
# a singleton, where 1NT doubled may make on our missing entries. When
# advancer runs, partner doubled and acts next: pass.
after 1x (1N) X (P)
  2{x} "Pulls: six or more {x}, a minimum with a singleton or void"
       shows x>=6, hcp<=13, shortest<=1
  P    "Leaves the double in"
       priority -5
after 1x (1N) X (*) when !rho.last=P
  P    "No further bid"
       priority -5

# Opener after partner's preemptive jump over their 1NT (2026-09-27,
# ticket b326: 1H 1NT 3D P 3H with a singleton diamond). Partner has
# seven cards and 5-9: that is the trump suit. Pass, and bid game in it
# only with 19+ and support. (BBA plays 3D here as 13-14 and forcing,
# so it never passes: probes/pull-preempt-1H-1N-3D.toml.)
after 1x (1N) 3z (P) when z is C | z is D, z is not x
  5{z} "Game in partner's suit: 19+ and support"   shows z>=2, hcp>=19
       priority 3
  P    "No game"
       priority 2

# their-1nt-overcall (`their-1nt-overcall.bid`): notes

Responder when RHO overcalls partner's one-level opening with 1NT.
Cases: `their-1nt-overcall.test`.

## Why it is here and not in `competitive/`

`after-interference.bid` writes every one-level context as
`after 1x (1y)`, and `1y` binds a *suit*, so no rule in it matched a
notrump overcall: responder passed whatever he held. `1D (1N)` and
`1C (1N)` were the two largest no-rule points in the whole corpus
(1,862 and 1,790 boards), and the four `1x (1N)` points together were
5,464 boards of dead auction, 20,461 with everything downstream.

The module sits in `notrump/` because that is the slice this piece of
work owned. **It arguably belongs beside the other contested-auction
rules in `competitive/after-interference.bid`** — it is responder's
first call over interference, which is exactly that module's subject.
Moving it is a copy of one `after` block; nothing here reads a notrump
card field. (For Rick.)

## Guidance

Their 1NT is 15-18 balanced with a stopper. Partner opened, so the deck
is accounted for: with 10+ total points we own the balance of the
strength and double for penalty. Below that it is an ordinary
competitive auction, one level higher than usual.

- **X is penalty, 10+ total points**, and denies a five-card major or a
  six-card minor — with one of those, bid it.
- **A raise of partner's suit is 6-9 support points** with three-card
  support for a major, five for a minor. It comes before naming a suit
  of our own.
- **A new suit at the two level is 9+ total points**, five cards in a
  major, six in a minor.
- **3♣ / 3♦ with seven cards and 5-9** total points: a preempt.
- Everything else passes.

## Evidence

`bba-cli --all-meanings` on `Opps_Overcall_1NT` (NS play 21GF-DEFAULT,
which is the card on 199 of the 342 corpus scenarios), 406 decisions at
`1x (1N)`:

| BBA's call | boards | its stated meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Pass | 287 | |
| 2♠ / 2♥ | 75 | "bidable suit", 7-12 total points, 5+ cards |
| 2♠ / 2♥ in partner's major | (of those) | "calculated bid", 6-9 total points, 3+ cards |
| X | 21 | "penalty", 10-37 total points |
| 2♣ / 2♦ | 12 | "bidable suit", 7-12 total points, **6+** cards |
| 3♣ / 3♦ | 5 | "bidable suit", 5-7 total points, 7+ cards |
| 4♠ / 4♥ / 3♥ / 3♠ | 6 | preemptive |

**The declared range is not the range BBA bids.** The note on the suit
bid says 7-12 total points, but BBA passes most 7s and 8s: a grid search
over the 406 decisions puts the floor at **9**.

| new-suit floor | decisions matched (of 406) |
|---|---|
| 7 (BBA's stated range) | 344 |
| 8 | 363 |
| **9** | **366** |
| 10 | 363 |

The raise band and the double threshold were searched the same way:
raise 6-9 and X at 10+ give 366; a wider raise (4-11) gives 371, two of
which are boards where BBA raises on four points. 6-9 is what BBA
declares and what the rule promises, so that is what is written.
Passing everything, the state before this module, matched 287.

## Accepted differences from BBA

- **BBA sometimes bids a poor five-card suit on 7-8 total points and
  sometimes passes an eleven-count with five spades** (`AQ753.K732.Q.932`
  over 1♦: BBA passes). Nothing in shape, suit quality (top honours) or
  vulnerability separated the two groups in the 406 decisions. The 9-point
  floor is the best single cut; it costs about 12 boards where BBA bids
  and we pass.
- **No preemptive jump raise.** BBA's 4♠ over their 1NT was a shapely
  11-count, not a weak five-card raise, so there is no `4{x}` rule. Three
  boards.

## Measured effect (2026-09-23, whole corpus)

At the `1x (1N)` decision itself: **72.8% → 86.5%** of calls agree
(3,240 → 3,850 of 4,452). Corpus-wide this module plus the 1NT
interference work is +1,991 calls, +186 boards with the same contract,
+209 identical auctions and −4,476 no-rule points; `1x (1N)` alone
accounts for the 5,464 dead second calls, and the whole `1x 1N…`
subtree drops from 20,461 no-rule points to 16,092.

## Gaps and open questions

- **Opener's rebid is now the dead end.** Responder bidding creates a
  new no-rule point one call later: `1H (1N) 2H` +168 boards,
  `1S (1N) 2S` +148, `1D (1N) 2S` +140, `1C (1N) 2S` +126,
  `1D (1N) 2H` +110, `1C (1N) 2H` +109 — about 800 boards in all,
  every one of them opener with nothing written for him. This is the
  same "opener's rebid in a contested auction" gap
  `after-interference.notes.md` already lists as the biggest remaining
  cluster, and it is not ours to write.
- **Their 1NT overcall is not interpreted as 15-18 with a stopper.** We
  have no rule for the opponents' 1NT overcall either, so the engine
  reads it as an unknown call and `partner`/`rho` knowledge stays wide.
  The point counts here are ours alone; a rule for their overcall (in
  `competitive/overcalls.bid`) would let responder count the deck
  properly.
- **A balancing 1NT overcall** (`1x P P 1N`) is a different animal and is
  not covered: the pattern here is only the direct seat.
- **Their 1NT over a two-level or higher opening** is not covered.

## After our penalty double (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b160: `1C 1NT X P` had no rule for opener
(nor over advancer's run). Opener now sits, pulling only a minimum with
six of his suit and a singleton; over a run, partner doubled and acts
next, so opener passes. Measured together with systems on over the
doubled 1NT overcall (advances): +149 par, +654 side IMPs (98 boards);
no-rule positions 3,265 → 3,060.

## Sources

- **The approach:** penalty double with 10+ once they overcall 1NT over
  our opening, and otherwise competitive bidding one level higher.
  Standard practice, not yet cited to a book or article.
- **Rick's rulings:** ticket basic-takeout-double-b160 (2026-09-27): the
  opener's rules after our penalty double.
- **BBA evidence:** `bba-cli --all-meanings` on Opps_Overcall_1NT
  (21GF-DEFAULT, 406 decisions), with a grid search over those decisions
  for the new-suit floor, the raise band and the double threshold. No
  `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** 2026-09-23 (72.8% to 86.5% at the decision)
  and 2026-09-27 (+149 par, +654 side IMPs).
- **Where we differ:** BBA's stated 7-12 for a new suit against the 9
  floor it actually bids; no preemptive jump raise ("Accepted differences
  from BBA").

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# The Law of Total Tricks (Rick, 2026-09-27; Basic_Takeout_Double 193).
# When both sides are bidding and the hand is not clearly ours, compete
# to the level where the tricks needed equal our trumps: eight trumps,
# the two level; nine, three; ten, four. No higher.
#
# Our trumps are my length plus what partner has shown. A takeout double
# of a major counts as four in the unbid suits once it is known to be the
# shape double (the power branch collapses when the deck or the auction
# rules out 17 HCP): BBA's doubler holds four of the other major 68% of
# the time and four of a minor 73% (probes/tools/takeout_shape.py).
# Elsewhere partner counts for what he has shown.
#
# At unfavourable vulnerability we hedge a trick: one level lower.
#
# Three rules, one per level: the doubler's bonus and the hedge are terms
# in the count (a condition counts 1 when it holds). Until 2026-09-30 the
# file spelled each combination out, twelve rules (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md,
# Phase 0).
#
# A fallback: below every rule that describes a hand, above the passes
# that only say "nothing more to say".

module total-tricks "The Law of Total Tricks"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/law_of_total_tricks

# Partner's three cards in x count as four when his takeout double of
# their major is known to be the shape double.
define doubler_four(x) = ((lho.H>=5 | rho.H>=5), partner.S>=3, partner.D>=3, partner.C>=3) | ((lho.S>=5 | rho.S>=5), partner.H>=3, partner.D>=3, partner.C>=3), partner.x.min = 3

# Raises of opener's minor in competition count the trumps the same way.
# One of a minor promises three (the engine reads 1♣ as 1+, so the test is
# what partner opened): a raise needs five for eight trumps, a preemptive
# jump six for nine. BBA on bare SAYC raises 1m over an overcall with five
# and jumps with six, not five; counting opener's minor as four (raising
# with four) lost 158 IMPs over 1♣ (2026-10-02). A major opening is raised
# with three as before (in third seat it may be four cards).
define opened_minor(x)  = (x is C | x is D), partner.opened, partner.x.min <= 3
define minor_raise(x)   = !opened_minor(x) | x >= 5
define minor_preempt(x) = !opened_minor(x) | x >= 6

# Advancer's weak jump raise of a one-level overcall: the overcall is
# often a bare five, and a weak hand has no defence to spare, so it jumps
# with five trumps, or four at favourable. BBA on bare SAYC raises to two
# with four and 5-9 HCP (169 hands where we jumped) and jumps mostly with
# five or at favourable (2026-10-02).
define weak_jump_raise(y) = y >= 5 | favourable

# Our trumps as the Law counts them, a trick fewer at unfavourable.
define lott_trumps(x) = we.fit(x).min + doubler_four(x) - unfavourable

# They are competing: the last bid or double at the table is theirs, made
# over our side's last bid (RHO's call, or LHO's when partner and RHO have
# both passed since). A lone overcall or opening that we have bid over,
# and that neither of them has backed, is not competition (2026-10-02).
define they_compete = !rho.last=P | (partner.last=P, !lho.last=P)

when they.bid, they.still_bidding, !game_reached   # not once we have bid game (ticket b100)
  2x  "Competes: to play"
      shows lott_trumps(x) = 8
      when  doubler_four(x) | !doubler_four(x)       # known either way: not while the double may be the strong one
      when  partner.x>=3, hcp>=5, we.hcp.min <= 24   # not clearly our hand
      when  they_compete                             # the weak raise to two only against a bid (2026-10-02)
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -4
  3x  "Competes: to play"
      shows lott_trumps(x) = 9
      when  doubler_four(x) | !doubler_four(x)
      when  partner.x>=3, hcp>=5, we.hcp.min <= 24
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -4
  4x  "Competes: to play"
      shows lott_trumps(x) >= 10
      when  doubler_four(x) | !doubler_four(x)
      when  partner.x>=3, hcp>=5, we.hcp.min <= 24
      sets  ask=signoff
      priority -4
files.rules/competitive/total-tricks.notes.md:
# total-tricks (`total-tricks.bid`): notes

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-27)

From Basic_Takeout_Double 193 (1♥ (X) P (2♥) 3♥ P P, North
T3.J.AJ8763.KJ87; BBA 4♦, our engine had no rule):

- When both sides are actively bidding and the HCP look roughly equal,
  compete to the level where the tricks needed equal our total trumps:
  South's double nominally shows four diamonds, North has six, so 4♦.
- The double can be counted because South cannot hold the power
  double: after North's cue bid a power double would have acted, and
  the deck (North 10, East about 16) leaves South too little. These
  are likelihoods, not certainties: play for the 19 hands in 20.
- Treat the double's three-card minimum as more likely four: a double
  of a major nearly always has the other major, of a minor less so.
- Vulnerability tempers it: at unfavourable, hedge by a trick.

## How it is built (steps a-d, each measured)

- a. The double's power branch in HCP (17+), the overcall to 16
  (takeout-double.notes.md): BBA's power doubles step up at 17 HCP.
- b. Engine: the 40-HCP deck caps every seat, publicly and from the
  chooser's own hand; the cap collapses the double to its shape.
- c. The doubler's pass denies the power double (takeout-double.bid).
- d. This module: my length plus partner's shown minimum, plus one
  when partner's three is a takeout double of their major (four is the
  norm there: other major 68%, a minor 73%;
  `probes/tools/takeout_shape.py`), bid exactly that level less six, at
  most the four level, one lower vulnerable against not. Needs 5+ HCP
  of my own and not clearly our hand (my HCP plus partner's minimum at
  most 24). A sign-off (`ask=signoff`): partner passes. Priority -4,
  below every rule that describes a hand.

## Measured (full corpus, par distance / side; Basic_* competitive)

| variant | full corpus | Basic_* comp. |
|---|---|---|
| any time they have bid, no floor | +1,723 / +16,098 | +98 / +280 |
| still bidding, no floor | +468 / +17,438 | +84 / +346 |
| still bidding, 5+ HCP | +1,996 / +12,084 | +79 / +237 |
| still bidding, 7+ HCP | +1,673 / +8,818 | +103 / +224 |
| any time, 5+ HCP, sign-off | +3,486 / +11,559 | +101 / +182 |
| **still bidding, 5+ HCP, sign-off (kept)** | **+2,052 / +12,162** | **+79 / +237** |

"Still bidding" = one of the opponents' last calls was not a pass,
Rick's "both sides actively bidding". Without it the rule scores more
par (+3,486) but fires once they have gone quiet: a minimum doubler
raised advancer's 0-8 1♠ to 2♠, and responder overrode opener's
decline of the limit raise. Those are wrong bridge, so the restriction
stays. Basic_* N/S: -1 / +6. Failed games in contested auctions rose
(2,133 -> about 2,488 in the unrestricted run), expected from a
competitive rule; par still gains.

Two cases in the test files that expected a pass now compete, as the
rule says: 1♠ (2♦) X (3♦) 3♥ with six diamonds, 4♦; 1♠ (X) 2♠ (3♣) P P
with four spades, 3♠.

## Open

- **For Rick:** the unrestricted version's extra par (+1,434) comes
  from contested partscore auctions where the opponents paused for a
  round (raising partner's balancing bid, the doubler raising
  advancer). Some of that may be worth a narrower rule.
- The hedge is one level at unfavourable only; favourable is the plain
  count.

## Not after our game (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-takeout-double-b100: `1H X P 2H 3H 3NT P 4C`, the LoTT
pulling partner's 3NT to four of a six-card minor. Rick: we do not pull
partner's 3NT to a minor unless looking for slam; the six clubs are
tricks in notrump and 3NT promised the heart stopper. The context now
requires `!game_reached`. Tiny on the corpus (5 boards: +20 par, −12
side IMPs), adopted on Rick's ruling. Keeping the LoTT out of the whole
game force was worse: it sent a hand with a singleton heart jack to 3NT
(the 4♦ case in total-tricks.test).

## Three rules instead of twelve (2026-09-30)

The judgment layer's Phase 0 (docs/JUDGMENT-LAYER.md) rewrote the file
with named conditions: `doubler_four(x)` (partner's three counts four
after a shape takeout double of their major) and `lott_trumps(x)`
(`we.fit(x).min + doubler_four(x) - unfavourable`, a condition counting 1
or 0). One rule per level, with a guard, `doubler_four(x) |
!doubler_four(x)`, that keeps the old behaviour of firing only once the
double's shape is known either way. On the full corpus our calls did not
change (170,633 boards, identical auctions and replays); only the
explanations did: the "a trick hedged vulnerable" and "partner's double
counted as four" wordings are gone from 577 calls, which now read as the
plain level. The context uses `they.still_bidding` for `!lho.last=P |
!rho.last=P` (the same test).

Measuring it exposed a cache bug in the engine: descriptiveness was
cached by rule and calls only, so a `shows` reading the vulnerability
(`unfavourable`) took whichever board filled the cache first when boards
are bid in parallel. The key now carries the values of such terms.

## The weak raise to two only against a bid (2026-10-02)

"Still bidding" (one of their last calls is not a pass) let the
two-level rule raise partner's one-level overcall on 5-6 HCP and three
trumps after `(1D) 1S (P)`: opener had bid once and responder passed,
so nobody was competing. BBA on bare SAYC passes these (raises from
about 9 HCP with three trumps, 7 with four). The two-level rule now also
needs `they_compete`: the last bid or double at the table is theirs,
made over our side's last bid (RHO's call, or LHO's when partner and RHO
have passed since).

Measured on top of the minor-raise change (errors yardstick, IMPs; even
/ odd boards):

| set | boards | errors | contract / doubling | distance from par | side IMPs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla SAYC random | 218 | +152 (+114 / +38) | +19 / +133 | −16 | +200 |
| corpus | 272 | +126 (+45 / +81) | +101 / +25 | +94 | +60 |
| 21GF random | 189 | +152 (+121 / +31) | +29 / +123 | −5 | +175 |

**The same restriction on all three levels was tried and not kept.** It
gained on the errors line (+393 vanilla, +383 corpus, +426 21GF, both
halves) but only through the doubling errors (+1,482 doubling against
−1,089 contract on vanilla), and distance from par lost 753 / 916 / 679.
By level: the two level gained on every count; the three and four levels
lost on contract errors and par everywhere and gained only because our
defenders, who double 3.4% of the chances against BBA's 13.8%, were no
longer given a chance to miss a penalty double. A gain that depends on
our weak doubling is not one to bank (penalty-doubles.notes.md), so the
three and four levels stay as they were (e.g. (2♠) 3♥ (P) 4♥ with ten
trumps, a raise they have not bid over yet, gained under both).

## Diagnosis: where "did not compete" comes from (2026-10-02)

Vanilla SAYC random set (95,558 deals, BBA on bare SAYC), "how each
table met par", class *did not compete or bid on (the side with par)*:
ours 10,922 boards / 91,512 IMPs against BBA's 8,266 / 64,882 at main
52174cf. `probes/tools/compete_diag.py` splits it (figures after the
commits of this date; the split barely moved):

| the side that should have bid | ours bds / IMPs | BBA bds / IMPs | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| never came in | 3,717 / 28,894 | 2,533 / 18,480 | 10,414 |
| came in only with a double | 548 / 4,929 | 400 / 3,281 | 1,648 |
| had bid (opened or overcalled) | 6,759 / 58,327 | 5,333 / 43,121 | 15,206 |

By the level of their last bid, where we had bid: one level 841 / 6,023
against 262 / 1,612; **two level 3,066 / 24,557 against 1,541 /
10,815**; three and four levels at parity; five level BBA worse.

**The decisive pass is rarely the call that differs.** On 7,368 of our
11,024 boards BBA's auction never reached our last pass at all; where
it did, BBA passed too in most cases ("Defending: nothing more to say":
BBA passes 2,174 of 2,833, bids 504, doubles 155). The first call where
our auction left BBA's, on these boards (our errors minus BBA's):
both sides in +10,227 (4,573 boards; mostly responder's and advancer's
first call over interference: the negative double, free bids, raises);
our first entry over their opening +6,523 (3,113); the opening +2,372
(957).

**par_blame's "Defending: nothing more to say"** ("W outbid, did not
compete", 3,825 boards / 28,694 IMPs at main; 3,814 after): the rule is
also the pass of the fourth seat at its *first* call, after (1x) P (1y),
(1x) P (1NT) or (1x) P (2x), because `overcalls.bid` covers only the
direct seat. Where BBA acted at a position this rule passed, 78% of
the boards (5,187 of 6,609) and of the IMPs were such first entries.
That is the one-level overcall decision, out of scope here (Rick's
separate probe).

**BBA's balancing over their fit loses on the errors yardstick.** At
(1x) P (2x) P (P) BBA balances in 353 of 1,938 boards (X 128, a suit
225), we never do; on the boards where that was the first difference
BBA's balance did worse than our pass (X −142, 3♣ −68, 3♦ −13, 3♥ −27
IMPs). No balancing rule was written.

## Tried and not kept (2026-10-02)

Each measured with `probes/tools/errors_diff.py` against the kept
changes before it.

- **Pushing a trick at favourable** (`lott_trumps` + favourable):
  errors −2,756 on vanilla (both halves), but contract errors +1,805 and
  distance from par +1,803. The whole loss is doubling errors (−4,561):
  our defenders, who double 3.4% of the chances, failing to double the
  extra level. For Rick: under competent doubling the push looks right.
- **Opener over their balancing double**, 1x (P) P (X): the redouble with
  17+ and the jump rebid with six and 17+ gained on vanilla (+433) and
  21GF (+319) but not on the corpus (+9, halves +83 / −74), and distance
  from par lost on all three (−254 / −170 / −259). BBA's lighter actions
  (a six-card rebid at two, a second suit) lost 586 IMPs on 2♣ alone.
- **Responder's raise over their takeout double from 6 total points**
  (was 4; BBA passes 3-5): +65 on vanilla, contract −39, side IMPs −283.
- **The two-level Law rule from 8 HCP** (was 5): +6 on vanilla,
  contract −278, side IMPs −1,373.

## Sources

- **The principle:** the Law of Total Tricks (LoTT), compete to the level
  of the total trumps. Standard practice, not yet cited to a book or
  article in these notes.
- **Rick's rulings:** the guidance from Basic_Takeout_Double 193
  (2026-09-27): compete when both sides are bidding, count the double as
  four in the other major, play for the 19 hands in 20, hedge a trick at
  unfavourable; do not pull partner's 3NT to a minor unless looking for
  slam (2026-09-27, ticket basic-takeout-double-b100).
- **BBA evidence:** BBA's 4♦ on the ticket board; the takeout double's
  shape from `probes/tools/takeout_shape.py`; BBA's power doubles from 17
  HCP (`takeout-double.notes.md`).
- **Corpus measurements:** the variant table, judged by par distance and
  by side IMPs; "still bidding" is kept although the unrestricted rule
  scores more par, because the extra cases are wrong bridge.
- **The two-level restriction** (2026-10-02): BBA's raises of a one-level
  overcall on the vanilla SAYC random set (`(1x) 1S (P)`: 2♠ 196 hands
  with three spades from about 9 HCP, pass 198 with 5-8), and the
  measurements in its section.
- **The diagnosis** (2026-10-02): `probes/tools/compete_diag.py` on the
  vanilla SAYC compare JSON; par_blame (`probes/tools/par_blame.py`) on
  the same; the variants in "Tried and not kept", by
  `probes/tools/errors_diff.py`.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

# Transfer responses after their takeout double of our major
# (`vs_to_double.new_suit_forcing_tfr`; convention-card
# bidding_conventions/transfers_after_double; Robert S. Todd, "1-Major
# (X) Transfers", Adventures in Bridge 598; PBS btn/Transfers_after_1M_X.btn,
# after the ACBL Bulletin, June 2025, p. 66). Over 1M (X), from 1NT up
# to the suit below opener's major, each bid transfers to the next suit:
#
#   over 1♥: 1♠ natural (as before), 1NT clubs, 2♣ diamonds, 2♦ hearts
#   over 1♠: 1NT clubs, 2♣ diamonds, 2♦ hearts, 2♥ spades
#
# - a transfer to a new suit: five or more cards (six when weak), fewer
#   than three of opener's major, a weak two or better;
# - the transfer to opener's major: a constructive raise, three trumps,
#   8-10; the direct raise to 2M is 4-7 with three;
# - the jump to three of the suit below the major (1♥-3♦, 1♠-3♥): four
#   trumps, 8-10; 3M stays preemptive (vs-takeout-double.bid);
# - 2NT: a fit (three or more) and 11+ (Jordan 2NT, extended to three
#   trumps);
# - the redouble: 10+ without three trumps.
#
# Opener completes the transfer (with the raise: 2M on a minimum, 3M
# with 15-16, game with 17+); responder then passes when weak, raises
# his suit to invite, or bids 3NT with game values. Notes:
# transfers-after-double.notes.md. Only after a major: transfers over
