# Michaels cue bids and the Unusual 2NT (`two-suited-overcalls.bid`): notes

Two-suited overcalls of a one-level suit opening on our right, advancer's
answers, the two-suiter's rebid, and the opening side's answer when
they make one. Cases: `two-suited-overcalls.test`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-28)

- **Michaels**: (1m) 2m shows both majors; (1M) 2M the other major and a
  minor. Strength conventions (for example weak or strong, not
  intermediate) and vulnerability.
- **Unusual 2NT**: the two lowest unbid suits (over a major, both minors).
- **Advancer**: preference, jump preference (invitational), asking for
  the minor after a major-minor Michaels, cue bids with game interest,
  passing.
- **The two-suiter's rebids** (the strong variety bids again), and the
  opening side's actions over them.
- Card fields under Bridge-Classroom's paths.

## Card fields

| Field | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `direct_cuebids.nat_minors_michaels` | our cue of a natural 1♣/1♦ is Michaels | Bridge-Classroom's DirectCuebidsMatrix (new here) |
| `direct_cuebids.quasi_michaels` | the same over a 1♣/1♦ that may be short | the matrix (new) |
| `direct_cuebids.nat_majors_michaels` | our cue of 1♥/1♠ is Michaels | the matrix (new) |
| `direct_cuebids.{art,quasi,nat_minors,nat_majors}_{michaels,natural,other}`, `direct_cuebids.description` | the rest of the matrix and its notes | recorded, not read |
| `competitive.michaels.play` | Bridge-Classroom's catalog switch: Michaels over both | existing |
| `competitive.michaels.strength` | `wide_range` (default) or `weak_or_strong` | was free text; now an enum. `weak_or_strong` is the value Bridge-Classroom's seed card writes |
| `competitive.michaels.minor_advance` | advancing a major-suit Michaels with a hand for partner's minor: `ask_2nt` (default) or `pass_or_correct` | convention-card PR #55 (2026-10-13); no `.bbsa` key, so every imported card plays `ask_2nt` |
| `competitive.unusual_2nt.play`, `nt_overcalls.jump_2nt_lowest_unbid` | the Unusual 2NT (catalog switch, and the card's NT-overcall box) | existing; either turns the rules on |
| `competitive.unusual_vs_unusual.play` | the opening side's cue bids over their 2NT, Bridgebum's way | existing |

The matrix's columns are the kind of opening (artificial ♣/♦, quasi-
natural ♣/♦, natural ♣/♦, natural ♥/♠) and its rows what our cue bid
means (Michaels, natural, other). The rules read the Michaels cells of
the natural columns and of quasi (a possibly short minor is treated like
a natural one: our rules cannot see the opponents' minimum length when
we choose). The artificial column is recorded only; there are no
strong-club rules yet.

**`.bbsa`**: `Michaels Cuebid` now sets the matrix
(`nat_minors_michaels` and `nat_majors_michaels`) instead of
`competitive.michaels.play`. The meaning is certain from the probes
below: over 1♣/1♦ BBA's alert is "5+ hearts, 5+ spades", over 1♥/1♠
"5+ in the other major, 0-3 in theirs", and BBA's minor openings are
natural. `Unusual 2NT` keeps its mapping (`competitive.unusual_2nt.play`),
whose meaning the probes confirm (the two lowest unbid suits, five-five).
Nothing about short or artificial minors is mapped.

Rick's own card (a Bridge-Classroom export) sets `nat_minors_michaels`,
`nat_majors_michaels` and `nt_overcalls.jump_2nt_lowest_unbid`, which the
rules now read, and says "minimax Mich, Leaping Michaels" in
`direct_cuebids.description`. Free text is not parsed: **for Rick**, set
`competitive.michaels.strength = weak_or_strong` on the card for
mini-maxi. Leaping Michaels is not written.

## What BBA does (probes, 2026-09-28, 21GF-DEFAULT, IMPs)

Specs in `probes/`, made with `probes/gen_hands.py`, dealer E opening,
columns None / NS (we vulnerable) / EW.

**The overcall** (`michaels-1C`, `-1D`, `-1H`, `-1S`, `unusual-2n-1C`,
`-1D`, `-1H`, `-1S`: 200-300 five-five hands each, 5-19 HCP):

- Michaels: BBA's alert is "8 to 29 total points" not vulnerable, "12 to
  29" vulnerable. In HCP: not vulnerable about half the 7-counts bid it,
  almost all from 8 (singletons and voids in their suit count); up to 17
  HCP; 18-19 double. Vulnerable, 8-10 overcalls the higher suit, 11-12
  split, 13+ Michaels. Same over all four openings.
- Unusual 2NT: "9 to 29 total points" at every vulnerability, from about
  7 HCP, and still 2NT on 19. Over 1♣ diamonds and hearts, over 1♦ clubs
  and hearts. With six-six in the minors BBA sometimes bids 4NT (Unusual
  4NT: not written).

**Advancer** (`michaels-adv-1C`, `michaels-adv-1H`, `unusual-2n-adv-1H`):

- BBA never passes the cue. Preference "to the partner's longer" with
  two or more; with equal length it prefers spades over hearts and
  diamonds over clubs.
- The jump preference is **preemptive** in BBA ("4 to 9 total points,
  3+"), the jump to game "preemptive" 4-11 with four trumps (and with
  more it bids game too).
- 2NT after a major Michaels: "to the partner's longer", asking for the
  minor.
- The cue bid is a "strength cue bid" with 17+ (16+ after 2NT).
- 3NT with their suit held, 15-16+.
- After 2NT: preference at the three level, 4m "preemptive" 4-8 with
  four, 5m to play.

**The opening side** (`vs-michaels-1H`, `vs-michaels-1C`,
`vs-unusual-2n-1H`; BBA's cards play no Unusual vs Unusual):

- 1♥ (2♥): 2♠ limit raise or better (10+, three hearts); X "support"
  6-9 with three; 3♥/4♥ preemptive; 2NT/3NT natural with spades held;
  3m natural 13+.
- 1♣ (2♣): 2♥ limit raise or better in clubs (12+, four); 2♠ "strength
  cue" 11+; X "support" 6-9 with four clubs; 2♦ natural, forcing;
  3NT with both majors held.
- 1♥ (2NT): 3♣ limit raise or better; 3♦ "strength cue" 14+; 3♥ 7-10
  with three; 4♥ preemptive; 3♠ natural; X penalty, 10+.

## What we play, and where we differ from BBA

- **The overcall**: as BBA, in our count: `hcp+length_points` 9+ not
  vulnerable (7 HCP five-five), 11+ vulnerable (9 HCP), up to 17 HCP
  (the power double above). BBA waits for about 11 HCP vulnerable;
  **11 beat 13 on both yardsticks** (+93 IMPs par distance, +231 to the
  overcalling side, 334 boards). Not vulnerable, 10 and 8 were tried:
  the yardsticks disagreed both times (10: par +81, side −146; 8: par
  −51, side +94), so 9 stays.
- **weak_or_strong** (mini-maxi, Bridgebum and Wikipedia): weak 9-11
  HCP-ish (`hcp+length_points` 9+, 11+ vulnerable, HCP 11 at most), or
  16+ and bids again. Played on both sides of the whole corpus it lost
  on both yardsticks (par −603, side −430, 1,283 boards), which only
  says it is not BBA's method: the corpus auctions were bid with a wide
  range. It stays an option for cards that ask for it.
- **The jump preference is invitational** (Rick; Wikipedia: "preference
  bids or jump preferences"); BBA's is preemptive, and Bridgebum's jump
  is preemptive too. BBA's way measured +3 par, +65 side IMPs (312
  boards): a wash. Rick's ruling stands; **for Rick** if he wants BBA's.
- **The cue bid** by advancer is 16+, game or slam interest, forcing
  (BBA 17+, Bridgebum "game or slam interest"); over 1♠ (2♠), where the
  hearts can only be shown at the three level, the cue is 12+ (game
  interest), since there is no room for an invitational jump. Since
  2026-10-13 the cue of a major promises three of partner's major (a
  strong raise); a hand that wants partner's minor asks with 2NT
  instead, and three of a minor is natural (section "2NT asks for the
  minor", below).
- **The opening side**: the cue of their known suit (after Michaels) or
  of their lower suit (after 2NT) is the limit raise, as BBA; the
  raise itself is competitive (BBA uses a double for the 6-9 raise and
  keeps 3♥ preemptive); four of our major with four trumps is
  preemptive. **Not written**: BBA's doubles (the 6-9 raise double after
  Michaels, the penalty double after 2NT), because opener would need
  answers to them. With Unusual vs Unusual on we play Bridgebum's
  version (3♣ game force in the other major, 3♦ the limit raise, 3♠
  natural 7-10).
- **Opener** accepts the limit raise with 14+ support points (a major)
  or 14+ HCP (3NT; five of the minor from 16); after the competitive
  raise bids game with 17+ support points; after responder's 2NT bids
  3NT with 14+; once responder has raised or bid notrump and they bid on,
  passes, or doubles with 15+.
- `after-interference.bid`: two contexts that read our raise over their
  cue bid as a cue-bid raise now say `y is not x` (1♦ (2♦) 3♦ was taken
  for "1x (2y) 3y": opener accepted a "limit raise" that was a 6-9
  raise).

## Corpus (2026-09-28)

Before and after, whole corpus and the boards where both sides bid in
BBA's auction (`--auctions competitive`). "vs BBA" is distance from par
against BBA; "side" is `probes/tools/sideimps.py BASE NEW`.

| | calls agreeing | vs BBA (par distance) | side IMPs | no rule in a live auction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| whole corpus | 76.7% → 77.0% | −114,531 → −113,454 (**+1,077**) | **+3,480** (4,351 boards) | 2,835 → 2,800 |
| competitive auctions | 71.1% → 71.9% | −40,830 → −39,732 (**+1,098**) | **+3,268** (4,181 boards) | |

The two yardsticks agree. By opening (side IMPs): over 1♣ +1,084, 1♥
+941, 1♦ +776, 1♠ +680.

The two-suited scenarios (calls agreeing with BBA; vs BBA in IMPs):

| scenario | calls | vs BBA |
|---|---|---|
| Michaels_Cuebid | 62.5% → 72.9% | −410 → −391 |
| Michaels_after_1m | 58.5% → 69.2% | −598 → −352 |
| Michaels_and_Unusual | 60.5% → 74.1% | −204 → −126 |
| Unusual_2N | 62.6% → 77.9% | −280 → −195 |
| Two-Suited_Overcalls | 63.0% → 73.7% | −48 → −83 |
| Opps_Michaels_Cuebid | 60.3% → 75.2% | −429 → −20 |
| Opps_Michaels_and_Unusual | 60.4% → 73.0% | −307 → −206 |
| Opps_2-Suited_Overcalls | 63.7% → 72.8% | −363 → −350 |
| Leaping_Michaels, Non_Leaping_* | unchanged (not written) | |

Probe agreement with BBA after the change (None / we vulnerable):
Michaels over 1♣ 260/300 and 205/300 (we bid it lighter vulnerable, by
design), over 1♥ 273/300 and 193/300; Unusual 2NT over 1♥ 256/300 and
262/300; advancer after 1♣ (2♣) 151/300, after 1♥ (2♥) 157/300, after
1♥ (2NT) 177/300 (the differences are the invitational jump, our
preemptive four-level raise with four trumps and 9 HCP or less where
BBA bids game from 12, and our 4m preempt after 2NT); the opening side
216/300 over Michaels of 1♥, 171/300 over Michaels of 1♣, 209/300 over
2NT (mostly BBA's doubles).

## Gaps and open questions

- Michaels and the Unusual 2NT in the **balancing seat**
  (`(1x) P (P) 2x`), by a passed hand over a second-seat opening only
  through the same rules; after two suits bid (`1x P 1y 2NT`): written
  2026-10-30 (below).
- **Leaping Michaels** (Rick's card) and non-leaping Michaels over weak
  twos; Unusual 1NT and 4NT (BBA bids 4NT with six-six).
- The opening side's **doubles** (above), and "unusual over unusual"
  over a minor opening and over Michaels (we play BBA's natural-ish
  structure there whatever the card says).
- Advancer when opener's partner bids more than a preference allows
  (a jump, notrump): pass unless a simple competitive preference fits.
- A two-suiter that is 6-5: no special treatment.

## Two-suiters over preempts and at the four level (2026-10-05)

Fast lane (CLAUDE.md "Pace"): written from the sources below, then
`compare` of Jordan_2N, Leaping_Michaels, Non_Leaping_Michaels_After_2-Bid
and _3-Bid, Unusual_2N (`--limit 50`) read at the conventions' own calls.
Call agreement there 71.7% -> 78.8%.

- **Unusual 1NT** (`competitive.unusual_1nt.play`, on in every PBS
  21GF card): a passed hand's 1NT over their opening shows the two lowest
  unbid suits; in the sandwich seat (`(1x) P (1y) 1NT`) the two unbid
  suits. Five-four or better, 6+ HCP. Advancer: the longer suit (lower
  with equal length) at the cheapest level, a jump with four and 11+.
  **BBA hardly plays it**: in GIB_Sandwich_NT_BPH it overcalls 1S with
  five spades (five-five included), bids 2NT with six-five, and passes
  most five-four and five-five hands of 9-10 HCP; its only 1NTs in the
  corpus are five-four minors with 10 HCP. We bid the convention as
  defined (-14 agreeing calls in that scenario). Gating it off with five
  spades only made us pass: a passed hand has no 1-level overcall rule.
- **Unusual 4NT** (`competitive.unusual_4nt.play`, on in every 21GF
  card): the jump to 4NT over their one-level opening or their raise
  shows the two lowest unbid suits, six-six or seven-five (six-five goes
  through the Unusual 2NT, which has no upper limit: BBA bids 2NT there,
  and our first try at six-five took 20 of its 2NTs); over a weak two or
  three-level preempt five-five with four losers; over four of a major
  the minors, five-five, five losers. Advancer: the longer suit at the
  five level.
- **Michaels over their preempt** (BBA's reading of its Michaels switch,
  no separate card field): the cue of a weak two (13+ total points), in
  the balancing seat or over their raise (11+), and of a three-level
  preempt (16+): both majors over a minor, the other major and a minor
  over a major. BBA's thresholds are not probed; 15 at the four level
  overcalled BBA's 3S on 5-5 hands, so 16. Advancer: game in a known
  major with three and 8+ HCP (or four), else the cheapest preference
  with three, 3NT with their suit held, else pass or correct (4♣ for the
  unknown minor, 4♥ for the unknown major). **BBA style**: over 2♥/2♠ 3M
  it asks with 3NT ("to the partner's longer"); we bid 4♣ pass or correct
  and keep 3NT natural.
- **Leaping Michaels** (`competitive.leaping_michaels.play`; 21GF-WJS-MSS
  and Precision only, not the cards of the Leaping_Michaels scenario,
  where BBA plays the cue instead): Rosen's table. 5-5, at most five
  losers. With it the direct cue of a weak two is not Michaels (Rosen: a
  stopper ask, not written). After (2♦) 4♣ advancer bids 4♥ pass or
  correct, not Bridge Bum's 4♦ ask.
- **Non-Leaping Michaels** (`competitive.non_leaping_michaels.play`; no
  PBS card plays it): Rosen's table over a three-level preempt, five
  losers; the cue of a minor is both majors (shared with the Michaels
  rule).
- **Direct jump cue bids** (`competitive.direct_jump_cuebid_major`,
  `_minor`; no PBS card turns them on, BBA plays none): as the PBS
  scenarios Jump_Cuebid_Strong and _Weak define them. Gambling: a solid
  seven-card suit, no stopper in theirs, asks for 3NT; strong: the same
  with six controls; majors: five-five, up to 10 HCP; preempt: seven of
  their minor, up to 10 HCP, two top honours. Advancer: 3NT with a
  stopper, else 4♣ pass or correct. Not written: over a major the
  `minor` option (meaning unknown), and the strong variety's 4♣/4♦
  control answers.
- All of these over a preempt require the opener's suit to be shown
  (`rho.x>=5`), so a Multi 2♦ is not cue-bid as diamonds.

Questions for Rick (decisions taken):
- Unusual 1NT against BBA's near-silence: we play it as defined.
- What does `direct_jump_cuebid_major = minor` mean? Not written.
- Michaels-over-preempt strength (13 / 11 / 14 / 16 total points) is
  ours, not probed; worth a grid if the Leaping scenarios matter.

## Cue-bid raises are artificial (2026-10-09)

The seven "Cue bid: limit raise or better" rules carried a bare `alert`,
so `partner.named(z)` counted them as natural bids of their suit and
rebids.bid's free-bid block read opener's sign-off as "six or more"
(rebids.notes.md, "Read as the hand holds"). They are now `alert
artificial`, as the cue bids in after-interference.bid are.

## Answering advancer's cue bid; Michaels is artificial (2026-10-12)

Brill round robin 2026-10-09, board 90000102 (Rusty N/S on 21GF-GIB,
BBA E/W; E/W vulnerable): `1S 2S X 3S X P P P`, North in 3♠ doubled
down eight, -1,700. South (`.QT953.AJ854.86`, Michaels) passed the
doubled cue bid with advances.bid's catch-all "Defending: nothing more
to say", and North passed it out the same way. Two holes: no rule for
the Michaels bidder after a cue of a major (the old `(1x) 2x (P) 3x (P)`
block was written for both majors: over 1♠ (2♠) 3♠ its "minimum: spades"
was 4♠, their suit), and nothing kept a catch-all pass from leaving our
cue bid as the contract (advances.notes.md, "Never pass out our own
artificial bid").

What we play now:

- **Every Michaels-family call is `artificial`**, not only alerted: the
  cue bids over one-level openings and preempts, the Unusual 1NT, 2NT
  and 4NT, advancer's cue bids and 2NT ask, the opening side's cue
  bids, the jump cue bids (but the preempt in their minor, which is a
  place to play) and Leaping Michaels' 4♦ over 2♦. Leaping and
  Non-Leaping Michaels' minor bids and the pass-or-correct bids stay
  bare alerts: they name a suit we may play in. `partner.named(S)` no
  longer reads a Michaels 2♠ as spades.
- **The cue of a minor** (both majors known): as before, a minimum names
  the longer major cheaply, 13+ bids its game, now also when RHO doubles
  the cue (`(1m) 2m (*) 3m (P|X)`).
- **The cue of a major**: over 1♥ (2♥) 3♥ a minimum (up to 12) bids 3♠,
  a maximum names the minor at the four level (below 4♠), or bids 4♠
  with six. Over 1♠ (2♠) 3♠ (12+, game interest) there is no room below
  4♥, so the Michaels bidder names the minor at the four level whatever
  his strength; advancer places the contract: game in the major with
  three, five of the minor with four and 13+, else pass the minor with
  four, or the major's five-two fit.
- **RHO doubles the cue**: the Michaels bidder still describes (a pass
  is not "nothing extra, you choose": the cue bidder could not choose
  without knowing the minor). The same over a doubled 2NT ask.
- On the board: South now bids 4♦ (makes ten tricks double dummy;
  E/W make 4♠ +1, par N/S -300 in 6♦X/6♥X). Had South passed, North
  would run to 4♥ (the runout, base.bid).

Measured: the Michaels convention score (`probes/tools/conv_ab.py
--only michaels --reuse-bba`, main's rules against these) -105 → -90
(Rusty's gain +210 → +225, halves -60/-45 → -45/-45); the Unusual 2NT
unchanged (-497). On the full corpus the four Michaels_Cuebid boards
whose 1♠ (2♠) 3♠ answer changed gained 27 IMPs (errors); the opening
side's 3♦ "game force without a fit" over their 2NT, now artificial,
moved three boards from opener's 3♥/3♠ rebid to the game-force 3NT
(-4 IMPs): opener has no rebid rule over the artificial cue (gap).

Not written: BBA's double of our Michaels (W,
7 HCP, a spade void) and its double of the cue bid (E) read as "no
rule". Writing them means a meaning for our own side too (the 6-9 raise
double BBA plays, or values) with opener's answers; left as a gap.

Sources: Bridgebum's "Michaels Cuebid" covers the 2NT ask and the
minimum rebid after the raise of the cue, not the cue of a major or a
doubled cue; Larry Cohen's "Michaels Cue Bid"
(<https://www.larryco.com/bridge-articles/michaels-cue-bid>) says the
meaning of pass and redouble after their double "requires discussion".
Naming the minor at the four level is the extension of the 2NT ask,
standard practice, not yet cited.

## 2NT asks for the minor; the cue raises the major (2026-10-13)

**Rick (2026-10-13)**: "If partner wants to play in the cue bidder's
minor, they bid 2NT to ask 'which minor'. Normally bidding the minor
says 'I have a 6+ card suit of my own'." On board 90000102 (above)
North, `864.K7.KQT9.A942`, 12 HCP with both minors and a doubleton
heart, had cue-bid 3♠ ("12+, describe your hand"); by the ruling he
asks with 2NT and places the contract after South's 3♦.

What we play after (1M) 2M, both majors:

- **2NT asks for the minor** at any strength, with a doubleton or less
  in partner's major (still priority −1: the fallback for every hand
  without a major fit that has no better call). The Michaels bidder
  names it at the three level over a pass or a double. When RHO bids
  over the ask the force is off: he names it at the four level with 13+
  or a six-card minor, else passes (naming it with any hand lost 23
  IMPs on 14 corpus boards; the restriction about broke even).
- **After the answer** advancer counts HCP (shortness in partner's
  major is no value: support points made two invitations with a void
  in it go down): pass up to 9, four of the minor invites (10-12 with
  three-card support, 10-11 with four; the Michaels bidder accepts with
  14+, or 12+ and a sixth card), 3NT with 13+ and their major held,
  five of the minor with 13+ (12 with four trumps), and with 17+ and
  four-card support the cue of their major as a slam try (the Michaels
  bidder bids six with 13+, else five). The same over RHO's bid, where
  a pass is the weak hand's.
- **Three of a minor by advancer is natural**: six or more of his own,
  at most two of partner's major, up to 12 HCP, to play; the Michaels
  bidder passes.
- **3NT direct** (13+, their major held, no fit) only without three
  cards in both minors; with three of each, 2NT first.
- **The cue bid is the strong raise of partner's major**: three-card
  support, 16+ over 1♥ (2♥), 12+ over 1♠ (2♠). The Michaels bidder's
  answers follow from the known fit: over 1♥ (2♥) 3♥ a minimum bids 3♠
  (the cue bidder then bids 4♠, or 3NT without a fit after a minor cue),
  a maximum names the minor at the four level or bids 4♠ with six; over
  1♠ (2♠) 3♠ a minimum bids 4♥, a maximum (13+) names the minor at the
  four level. Once the minor is named the cue bidder bids game in the
  major (slam bidding after it is a gap).
- **Minor-suit Michaels and the Unusual 2NT**: both suits are known, so
  no ask is needed; their cue bids stay "16+, game or slam interest".
  Nothing changed there.
- The guard of 2026-10-12 stays: no passing out our own artificial bid.

On the board North now bids `1♠ 2♠ X 2NT`, South 3♦, and North 5♦
over a pass or over 4♠ (13 support points, four diamonds; 5♦ takes ten
tricks double dummy, -100 or -300 doubled, against E/W's 4♠ +1, -650;
par N/S -300). E/W's calls after 2NT are BBA's and not reproduced here
(our own West raises to 3♠ instead of doubling).

Measured (`probes/tools/conv_ab.py --only michaels,unusual-2nt
--reuse-bba`): the Michaels convention score -90 -> **-78** (Rusty's
gain +225 -> +237, halves -45/-45 -> -43/-35); the Unusual 2NT
unchanged (-497). Tripwire (`compare --limit 50`, all scenarios): 16
boards changed, every one an auction after a major-suit Michaels (11
of them in other scenarios: Opps_Michaels_*, Namyats, Goulash and
such). Full Michaels_Cuebid, Michaels_and_Unusual, Unusual_2N and
Opps_2-Suited_Overcalls against main (`errors_diff.py`, 36 changed
boards): errors **+34** (halves +28/+6), contract -16, doubling +50;
distance from par -27. By first call: natural 3♦ +43 (6 boards),
natural 3♣ over 1♥ -14 (4), the four-level answer over RHO's bid
4♣ +18 / 4♦ -18 (5 each). The natural three of a minor is Rick's
definition and stays.


Questions for Rick (decisions taken):
- After the cue raise of a major and the Michaels bidder's maximum
  (naming the minor), slam is not explored: the cue bidder bids game.
- Advancer's natural three of a minor is capped at 12 HCP; a stronger
  hand with its own suit asks with 2NT, or bids 3NT.
- With a weak hand that fits only one minor, advancer still asks and
  passes the answer (no pass-or-correct correction). Pass or correct is
  now the card's other treatment (below).

Sources: Bridgebum, "Michaels Cuebid": after (1♥) 2♥, 2NT "asks the
overcaller to bid his minor suit at the 3-level", three of a minor
"natural, showing a very good club suit (usually 6+)", non-forcing;
after the raise of the cue the Michaels bidder bids his cheapest suit
with 0-10, everything else game forcing (we: a minimum up to 12, the
cue of a major as a raise is ours). Larry Cohen, "Michaels Cue Bid":
3♣ pass or correct to play in partner's minor, 2NT as an ask among
"sophisticated methods"; we follow Rick and Bridgebum (natural 3m).
The invite / slam-try structure after the answer is ours: standard
practice, not yet cited.

## Two treatments: `competitive.michaels.minor_advance` (2026-10-13)

After a Michaels cue bid of a major (1♥ (2♥), 1♠ (2♠): the other major
and a minor), advancer who wants to play in partner's minor has two
treatments, chosen by the card field (convention-card PR #55):

- **`ask_2nt`** (default; Rick 2026-10-13, Bridge Bum): everything in
  the section above. 2NT asks for the minor at any strength; 3♣ and 3♦
  are natural (six of advancer's own, up to 12 HCP, to play); the cue
  raises partner's major.
- **`pass_or_correct`** (Larry Cohen, "Michaels Cue Bid": "If you want
  to play in the minor, you should bid 3♣ to allow partner to pass or
  correct (don't guess!)", and as the "advanced method", "2NT with
  invitational hands"):
  - **3♣ pass or correct**: up to 9 HCP, at most two of partner's major
    (the fallback, as the 2NT ask is under `ask_2nt`). The Michaels
    bidder passes with clubs and bids 3♦ with diamonds, also over a
    double; when RHO bids, the force is off as over the 2NT ask (the
    minor at the four level with 13+ or a six-card minor, else pass).
    Advancer passes the correction: he chose a partscore.
  - **2NT asks with 10+** (invitational or better), at most two of
    partner's major; the answer and everything after it are
    `ask_2nt`'s (invite with four of the minor, 3NT, five, the slam
    try).
  - **3♦ natural**: six of advancer's own, as under `ask_2nt`; the
    Michaels bidder passes. Cohen's article does not say how advancer
    shows a long minor of his own; 3♦ stays natural because 3♣ is the
    only call pass or correct needs. **There is no natural 3♣**: with
    long clubs of his own advancer bids 3♣ (partner passes with clubs,
    else plays 3♦ in a probable misfit) or, with 13+ and their major
    held, 3NT. A gap, recorded rather than invented.
  - Unchanged: the preferences, the jump preference, game in the
    major, the cue raise, 3NT.

**Which BBA plays** (`probes/michaels-minor-advance.toml`, 1♠ (2♠) P,
21GF-DEFAULT, 14 hands, none and NS vulnerable): **2NT on every hand
without a heart fit**, from 3 HCP with both minors to 12 HCP, and with
advancer's own seven-card minor too; its alert is "to the partner's
longer", 0-37 total points. So BBA's style is `ask_2nt` with no natural
three of a minor (our `ask_2nt` keeps 3m natural: Rick's definition).
With 12 HCP vulnerable BBA bids 3NT. With three hearts it prefers 3♥.

**Self A/B** (`probes/tools/self_ab.py --name michaels-minor-advance
--scenarios Michaels_Cuebid Michaels_and_Unusual --base
competitive.michaels.minor_advance=ask_2nt --variant
...=pass_or_correct --side ns`, 1,000 boards): 40 changed (2NT -> 3♣
on 35 of them); actor errors contract -4, doubling +3 (halves -5/+4,
differ), z -0.1: **neutral**. Distance from par +22. The worst board
(Michaels_Cuebid 121, -6) is the four-level answer over RHO's bid.
It is the card's choice; neither treatment is better on these deals.

Tests: `two-suited-overcalls.test`, the "pass or correct" section
(card override `competitive.michaels.minor_advance=pass_or_correct`)
and two `ask_2nt` cases on the same hands.

Questions for Rick (decisions taken):
- `pass_or_correct` has no natural 3♣ (above); should a long club suit
  of advancer's own have a route (e.g. 3♣ then 4♣ over the correction)?
- 3♣ pass or correct is capped at 9 HCP and 2NT starts at 10 (Cohen:
  "invitational hands"); a 10-12 hand that only wants a partscore asks
  and passes the answer.

Sources: Larry Cohen, "Michaels Cue Bid"
(<https://www.larryco.com/bridge-articles/michaels-cue-bid>), fetched
2026-10-13: the pass-or-correct 3♣ and the invitational 2NT; it does
not cover 3♦, advancer's own minor or the cue raise. Bridge Bum and
Rick for `ask_2nt` (above). The BBA probe above.


## Over their raise (2026-10-20)

Brill daily 2026-10-20, board 4: 1C P 2C, AKQJ85.QT8732.5.- passed; one
entrant bid 3C for the majors. Now the cue of their raised minor,
(1m) P (2m) 3m, shows both majors (five-five or better, the wide-range
values of the direct cue bid: 9+ total points not vulnerable, 11+
vulnerable, up to 17 HCP; at either `competitive.michaels.strength`),
and 2NT over a raise the two lowest unbid suits (over a major the
minors, over 1C diamonds and hearts, over 1D clubs and hearts) when the
card plays the Unusual 2NT. Advancer: the longer major at the three
level (spades with equal length), game with four-card support or three
and 10+, 3NT with 13+ and their minor held; over a bid by RHO a
preference with three cards, else pass. After 2NT: the preference, 4H
with four (or three and 10+), five of a minor with four and 12+. The
two-suiter bids game over the preference with 16+ or four losers or
fewer (six-six, six-five: the board's hand has three), else passes.
Standard practice, not yet cited; the cue of a raised major is not
written. Tripwire: 9 boards changed by these rules, +14 contract
errors, +2 doubling, +15 against par.

## After both opponents have bid; 4NT balancing (2026-10-30)

Found by comparing Brill's convention files with our rules (Brill's
service reads these calls; Rusty had no rule for any of them). Brill's
definitions were hints only: the rules follow the sources below.

- **2NT after opener and responder have both bid** (card
  `competitive.unusual_2nt.play` or `nt_overcalls.jump_2nt_lowest_unbid`):
  (1x) P (1y) 2NT and (1x) P (2y) 2NT (a new suit, not a jump shift)
  show five-five in the two suits they have not bid: 1H P 1S 2NT the
  minors, 1C P 1D 2NT the majors, 1C P 1H 2NT diamonds and spades,
  1H P 2C 2NT diamonds and spades. Bridge Bum: the Unusual 2NT "is also
  in effect if both opponents have bid up to 2♠" (1H 2D 2NT = clubs and
  spades), and after their two-over-one it promises extra; 12+ total
  points. After a 1NT response, (1x) P (1N) 2NT, only one suit is bid:
  the two lowest unbid, 11+. First written as 10 and 9 (the direct 2NT's
  9 by analogy, which came from BBA's "9 to 29 total points" alert);
  the whole corpus (all scenarios, 500 boards each, 2026-10-31) chose
  two more. Judged by the 2NT bidder's contract errors (Rick,
  2026-10-31: the side bidding the change, taken as doubled):
  +2 everywhere +93 IMPs on 107 boards (halves +45/+48), +2 only
  vulnerable +72 on 58 (halves +24/+48); the non-vulnerable step
  between them +21 (halves +21/0). Distance from par +166 beside it.
  Balancing after their raise, (1x) P (2x) P (P) 2NT, the same as the
  direct 2NT over the raise (standard practice, not yet cited: Bridge
  Bum's "not Unusual" balancing 2NT is over a weak two, not over a
  raise). Above the takeout double with 15+ (overcalls.bid): the
  five-five is the exact description, and the Unusual 2NT has no upper
  limit (BBA).
- **Sandwich seat with a 1NT two-suiter on**: with the Sandwich 1NT
  (sandwich-nt.bid, five-four or five-five) or a passed hand's Unusual
  1NT, the one-level sandwich seat stays theirs and 2NT is not bid
  there. The first version took 30 of GIB_Sandwich_NT_BPH's 1NT boards
  (21GF-GIB plays the passed-hand Unusual 1NT). BBA itself bids 2NT
  there with some six-five hands (boards 4, 35, 37): open question.
- **Advancer** after any of these 2NTs: the longer of partner's suits at
  the cheapest level (the lower with equal length), game in a major with
  four-card support and 10+ HCP, five of a minor with four and 13+ (when
  partner has no major); over a double the same; when RHO bids, the
  cheapest preference with four, else pass. The 2NT bidder passes a
  three-level preference, or bids game in a major with 16+ or four
  losers. One named pattern (`u2n_two_bid`) holds the four entries.
- **The Unusual 4NT, balancing and over their raised preempt** (card
  `competitive.unusual_4nt.play`, on the Brill card): 4NT over (3x) P (P)
  and (2x) P (3x) as the direct jump over three (five-five, four losers);
  over (4M) P (P), (3M) P (4M), (2M) P (4M) and the balancing seat after
  their raise to game, (3M) P (4M) P (P), the minors, five-five with
  five losers, as the direct 4NT over 4M; over (3m) P (4M) the two unbid
  suits. Advancer: the longer suit at the five level (spades added for
  the last case). Wikipedia: a 4NT overcall shows the same two suits as
  2NT and is "an extreme two suiter", usually six-five; our five-five
  with few losers over a preempt is the existing deviation (above).
- **Kept: our 4NT over their 4♠ shows both minors.** Brill reads it as a
  three-suited takeout; Wikipedia's 4NT overcall is the two-suiter, and
  no source we have says otherwise. Recorded, not changed.
- Opps_Preempt board 6 (3H P P, KQ.T.AK742.KQT87): 4NT, 5C made with
  par 6C; BBA doubled and played 4C. 11 contract errors to BBA's 13.
- **Tripwire** (all scenarios, `--limit 50`, against HEAD): 33 boards
  changed, every one first at one of these calls (2NT 26, the rest
  1NT-response 2NT and 4NT). The side that bid them: contract errors -2,
  doubling -5 (fewer). The other side: contract +5, doubling +52, almost
  all undoubled sacrifices and partscores of ours going down (our weak
  doubling, as both sides are ours). Totals: errors -50 IMPs to us
  (contract -3, doubling -47), par distance -10. Judged as a bidding
  change on its contract errors: neutral to slightly better. The worst
  boards are light two-suiters doubled or set (Gavin_Transfers_after_2N
  board 33, 1D P 1N 2N on 9 HCP five-five: 3C doubled, 12 IMPs;
  1m-1N 45; SCS16_1or2C 29 the best, -12).

Open questions (not written):
- Brill's **jump to 3NT and 4NT after (1x) P (1y)** as two-suiters
  (1H P 1S 3NT, 1C P 1H 4NT, ...): exotic, no standard source.
- **Unusual NT over a weak two after responder raises** (2M P 3M 3NT /
  4NT, 2D P 3H 3NT): Brill reads them as two-suiters; not written.
- (3M) X (4M) 4NT, after partner's takeout double: advancer's two-suiter
  (Brill), a different module (advances), not written.
- BBA's passed-hand 2NT in the sandwich seat with six-five (above).

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Over their 1NT opening: what every defence shares (vs-1nt.notes.md).
#
# The convention the card plays for `defence_to_1nt.strong` is the
# defence, and each has its own module for the calls that differ:
# natural (overcalls.bid), Cappelletti and Modified Cappelletti
# (cappelletti.bid), DONT (dont.bid), Meckwell (meckwell.bid), Landy and
# Multi-Landy (multi-landy.bid). Their calls say what they show and set
# a question for partner (`sets ask=...`); the answers that are the same
# whichever defence asked are written here, once, against the question:
#
#   nt_majors       partner has both majors: pick one, invite or bid game
#   nt_mm(M)        partner has five M and a four-card minor
#   nt_which_minor  I asked for that minor: partner names it
#   nt_minors       partner has both minors: pick one
#   nt_pc(x)        partner has x and another suit: pass, or ask which
#   nt_other        I asked for the other suit: partner names it
#   nt_one(x)       partner has shown one long suit x
#   nt_penalty      partner doubled for penalties
#
# Advancer's strength is measured in support points (tp) once a major
# fits. BBA (21GF-DEFAULT, probes/vs-1N-capp-*-adv.toml) raises a
# five-card major with 3+ support: to three with 8-14 total points and
# to game from about 11. The overcaller has 9-17, so we invite with 10-12
# support points and bid game from 13.

module vs-1nt "Over their 1NT: what every defence shares"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_1nt
  param  def = defence_to_1nt.strong

# ── Preempts and the pass ────────────────────────────────────────────
# With a conventional defence a seven-card suit jumps to the three level
# only when it is too weak for the one-suited call: BBA on 21GF-DEFAULT
# preempts with 6-8 HCP and bids 2♣ (Cappelletti) from 9 with seven cards
# (probes/vs-1N-capp.toml). We preempt up to 11 counting a point a card
# beyond four, one below the one-suiter's 12: 4-8 HCP with seven cards.
# The natural defence keeps its own 4-10 (overcalls.bid).
after (1N) when !(def is none)
  3S  "Preemptive: seven spades"                  shows S>=7, hcp>=4, hcp+length_points<=11
      priority 1
  3H  "Preemptive: seven hearts"                  shows H>=7, hcp>=4, hcp+length_points<=11
      priority 1
  3D  "Preemptive: seven diamonds"                shows D>=7, hcp>=4, hcp+length_points<=11
      priority 1
  3C  "Preemptive: seven clubs"                   shows C>=7, hcp>=4, hcp+length_points<=11
      priority 1
after (1N) | (1N) P (P)
  P   "No overcall"             priority -10

# ── Partner has both majors ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Cappelletti 2♦, Landy and Multi-Landy 2♣, DONT 2♥, Meckwell X then 2♥.
# Preference to the longer major (hearts when equal, as BBA and GIB),
# a jump to invite with four, game from 13 support points; a long minor
# with at most two cards in either major plays there.
when asked nt_majors, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "Hearts: to play"                  shows H>=S
      when  partner.last=2H
  2H  "Preference: hearts"               shows H>=S
  2S  "Preference: spades"               shows S>H
  3H  "Invitational: four hearts"        shows H>=4, H>=S, tp(H)=10..12
  3S  "Invitational: four spades"        shows S>=4, S>H, tp(S)=10..12
  4H  "Game in hearts"                   shows H>=3, H>=S, tp(H)>=13
  4S  "Game in spades"                   shows S>=3, S>H, tp(S)>=13
  P   "Long clubs: to play"              shows C>=6, H<=2, S<=2
      when  partner.last=2C
  P   "Long diamonds: to play"           shows D>=6, H<=2, S<=2
      when  partner.last=2D
  3C  "Long clubs: to play"              shows C>=6, H<=2, S<=2
      when  !partner.last=2C
  3D  "Long diamonds: to play"           shows D>=6, H<=2, S<=2
      when  !partner.last=2D

# ── Partner has five of a major and a four-card minor ────────────────
# Cappelletti and Multi-Landy 2♥/2♠, Modified Cappelletti 2♣ then 2♥/2♠.
# Pass with two or more; raise with three; 2NT asks for the minor with a
# singleton or void; a six-card suit of my own is to play.
when asked nt_mm(M), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P    "{M} to play"                            shows M>=2
  3{M} "Invitational raise"                     shows M>=3, tp(M)=10..12
  4{M} "Game in {M}"                            shows M>=3, tp(M)>=13
  2N   "Which is your minor?"                   alert  artificial
       shows M<=1
       sets  ask=nt_which_minor
  2S   "Six or more spades: to play"            shows S>=6, M<=2
       when  M is H
  3H   "Six or more hearts: to play"            shows H>=6, M<=2
       when  M is S
  3C   "Six or more clubs: to play"             shows C>=6, M<=1
  3D   "Six or more diamonds: to play"          shows D>=6, M<=1

when asked nt_which_minor, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  3C  "My minor is clubs"                       shows C>=4, C>=D
  3D  "My minor is diamonds"                    shows D>=4, D>C

# ── Partner has both minors ──────────────────────────────────────────
# 2NT in Cappelletti, Meckwell and Multi-Landy. The longer minor, and
# diamonds when equal (BBA, probes/vs-1N-capp-2N-adv.toml: 98 of 98);
# game with a fit and 14 support points.
when asked nt_minors, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  3C  "Preference: clubs"                       shows C>D
  3D  "Preference: diamonds"                    shows D>=C
  5C  "Game in clubs"                           shows C>=4, C>D, tp(C)>=14
  5D  "Game in diamonds"                        shows D>=4, D>=C, tp(D)>=14
  3H  "Six or more hearts: to play"             shows H>=6, C<=2, D<=2
  3S  "Six or more spades: to play"             shows S>=6, C<=2, D<=2

# ── Partner has a known suit and another ─────────────────────────────
# DONT 2♣/2♦ (and a higher suit), Meckwell 2♣/2♦ (and a major). Pass
# with three of the known suit; otherwise the next step asks for the
# other one, which partner passes or corrects.
when asked nt_pc(x), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "Support for {x}: to play"                shows x>=3
  2D  "Which is your other suit?"               alert
      shows x<=2
      when  x is C
      sets  ask=nt_other
  2H  "Pass or correct: which is your other suit?"   alert
      shows x<=2
      when  x is D
      sets  ask=nt_other

when asked nt_other, rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  P   "My other suit is diamonds"               shows D>=4
      when  partner.last=2D
  P   "My other suit is hearts"                 shows H>=4
      when  partner.last=2H
  2H  "My other suit is hearts"                 shows H>=4
  2S  "My other suit is spades"                 shows S>=4

# ── Partner has shown one long suit ──────────────────────────────────
# After a relay answer, a natural 2♥/2♠ (Meckwell, DONT 2♠) or the
# Multi-Landy 2♦. Raise a major with two or more: invite with 11-12,
# game from 13.
when asked nt_one(x), rho.last=P | rho.last=X
  3{x} "Invitational raise"                     shows x>=2, hcp=11..12
       when  x is H | x is S
  4{x} "Game in {x}"                            shows x>=2, hcp>=13
       when  x is H | x is S
  P    "No further bid"                    priority -5

# ── Partner doubled for penalties ────────────────────────────────────
# Cappelletti and Modified Cappelletti: 15+ HCP. Sit with five or more
# HCP, or with nowhere to go; run to a five-card suit with less.
when asked nt_penalty, rho.last=P | rho.last=XX
  P   "Leaves the double in"          priority -1
  2C  "Weak: five or more clubs"                shows C>=5, hcp<=4
  2D  "Weak: five or more diamonds"             shows D>=5, hcp<=4
  2H  "Weak: five or more hearts"               shows H>=5, hcp<=4
  2S  "Weak: five or more spades"               shows S>=5, hcp<=4
files.rules/competitive/vs-1nt.notes.md:
# Defences to their 1NT (`vs-1nt.bid`): notes

The shared part of the defences to the opponents' 1NT opening: the
three-level preempts, the pass, and the answers every defence uses
(partner has both majors, a major and a minor, both minors, a suit and
another, one long suit; the penalty double). Cases: `vs-1nt.test`. The
defences themselves: `cappelletti.bid` (Cappelletti and Modified
Cappelletti), `dont.bid`, `meckwell.bid`, `multi-landy.bid` (Landy and
Multi-Landy); the natural defence stays in `overcalls.bid`. How our side
reads their calls: `nt-interference.notes.md`.

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-28)

"Implement the common defences against the opponents' 1NT opening, so
our bot is compatible with the cards people play: Cappelletti (a.k.a.
Hamilton), Modified Cappelletti, Meckwell, and DONT. We can do
comparisons to see which appears most effective, but since people play
all of these, we'd like our bot to be compatible with their cards."
Each partnership's card chooses; a card that sets nothing keeps the
natural defence of before.

## The card

`competitive.vs_1nt_strong.system` is the field, the path Bridge-
Classroom's editor writes (`VsNtDefense.vue`: a system name, picked from
`ntDefenses.js` or typed, and one text cell per call). The older
`competitive.defense_vs_strong_nt.convention` loads into it as an alias.
Options: `cappelletti`, `modified_cappelletti`, `landy`, `multi_landy`,
`dont`, `meckwell`, `other` (natural). Since the editor stores display
names, the field has `value_aliases` (a new field attribute, 2026-09-28):
an enum value matches ignoring case, spaces and hyphens ("Meckwell",
"Multi-Landy", "DONT", "Modified Cappelletti"), and "Hamilton" /
"Pottage" load as `cappelletti`, "Penalty" / "Natural" / "Standard" as
`other`. The per-call cells (`.dbl`, `.2c`, `.2d`, `.2h`, `.2s`, `.2nt`,
`.other`) and the whole `vs_1nt_weak` block are text fields: they load
and round-trip, the rules do not read them. `competitive.dont.play`
(the editor's catalog switch for DONT) plays DONT when the system is
unset or `other`.

`.bbsa`: `Cappelletti`, `Landy` and `Multi-Landy` were mapped already
and now write the new path. BBA has no key for DONT, Meckwell or
Modified Cappelletti. No new key was mapped and none was guessed.

## The shared answers

- **Both majors** (Cappelletti 2♦, Landy/Multi-Landy 2♣, DONT 2♥,
  Meckwell X then 2♥): the longer major, hearts when equal (BBA and GIB
  both); a jump with four and 10-12 support points; game from 13; a
  six-card minor with at most two of either major plays there.
  BBA (`probes/vs-1N-capp-2D-adv.toml`): 2♥ 183, 2♠ 191, 3♥/3♠ invites
  90 (11-14 total points), 4♥/4♠ 87, pass with long diamonds 17.
- **A major and a minor** (Cappelletti and Multi-Landy 2♥/2♠, Modified
  2♣ then 2♥/2♠): pass with two or more; 3M invites with three (10-12
  support points), 4M from 13; 2NT asks for the minor with a singleton or
  void; a six-card suit of one's own is to play. BBA
  (`-2H-adv`, `-2S-adv`): pass 328/342, 3M 88/94 (8-14), 4M 99/87
  (from 11), 2NT "ask for minor" 46/55. It raises more than we do.
  The overcaller answers 2NT with his minor (`-2H-2N`: all 300).
- **Both minors** (2NT): the longer minor, diamonds when equal (BBA,
  `-2N-adv`: 98 of 98), 5♣/5♦ with a fit and 14.
- **A suit and another** (DONT 2♣/2♦, Meckwell 2♣/2♦): pass with three,
  else the next step asks, and partner passes or bids his other suit.
- **One long suit shown**: raise a major with two, 11-12 invites, 13+
  game.
- **The penalty double** (Cappelletti): sit with 5+ HCP or no five-card
  suit; run to a five-card suit with 0-4. BBA (`-X-adv`) runs more
  (0-7 total points, to any four-card suit) and passes from about 8;
  running with four-card suits was not tried.
- Every answer needs RHO to pass or double (the relays also allow a
  redouble); when they bid, the fallback is a pass.
- **Preempts**: with a conventional defence a seven-card suit jumps to
  the three level only below the one-suited call (4-8 HCP), as BBA on
  21GF-DEFAULT (6-8 HCP; 2♣ from 9 with seven). The natural defence keeps
  its 4-10 (overcalls.bid).

## Measured (2026-09-28, full corpus, 170,633 boards)

Baseline (this branch before the change): vs BBA **-114,604** IMPs.
After: **-116,953** (-2,349 by par distance), with the cards as they are
(21GF-DEFAULT, NS in 208 scenarios, and 21GF-GIB, EW in 316, both play
Cappelletti; seven cards play Multi-Landy). By the competitive yardstick
(`probes/tools/sideimps.py base.json final.json 3`): **5,106 boards
changed, +6,027 IMPs to the side that changed its call** (the direct
seat +5,454 on 4,309 boards, balancing +579 on 793), par distance -2,349.
The two yardsticks disagree, as they did for the natural overcalls
(overcalls.notes.md, "For Rick: which yardstick"): the defending side
gains, and par distance counts its gains as losses. No-rule positions
in live auctions 2,835 → 2,779; artificial contracts 133 → 133.

By call (base → final, side IMPs / par distance): X +2,186 / -1,286
(1,367 boards); 2♣ +396 / +271 (955); 2♦ +690 / -202 (601); 2♠ +739 /
-92; 2♥ +399 / -287; 2NT +326 / +30; balancing 2♣ -137 / +99 (261),
balancing X +627 / -407. Only the balancing 2♣ loses on the side
yardstick (cappelletti.notes.md, Gaps). By side: EW (mostly 21GF-GIB)
+4,137 / -2,026 over 3,006 boards, NS +1,890 / -323 over 2,100.

Replay agreement with BBA: 76.6% → 76.9% of calls (NS 63.6 → 63.9, EW
89.5 → 89.8); identical auctions 16.4% → 16.9%.

## Comparison of the defences (for Rick: information, not a choice)

Each defence forced on for both sides (`compare --set
competitive.vs_1nt_strong.system=X`), against the natural defence forced
the same way (`=other`). "Side" is sideimps from the natural run to the
defence's run, from the side that made the first differing call; "par"
the change in distance from par over the same boards (positive: closer).
"vs BBA" is the full-corpus total of each run.

| Defence | vs BBA | boards changed | side IMPs | par distance | EW side / par | NS side / par |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| natural (`other`) | -115,733 | | | | | |
| Cappelletti | -117,155 | 5,141 | **+2,963** | -1,422 | +1,951 / -1,338 | +1,012 / -84 |
| Meckwell | -117,321 | 4,058 | +2,676 | -1,588 | +2,442 / -1,982 | +234 / +394 |
| Modified Cappelletti | -116,607 | 5,014 | +2,401 | -874 | +1,362 / -925 | +1,039 / +51 |
| Multi-Landy | -116,689 | 4,188 | +1,694 | -956 | +1,268 / -1,084 | +426 / +128 |
| DONT | -117,082 | 4,758 | +726 | -1,349 | +798 / -1,497 | -72 / +148 |
| Landy | -115,591 | 1,317 | -58 | +142 | -94 / +18 | +36 / +124 |

Reading it:

- Every defence except Landy gains for the side that uses it, by the
  side yardstick; every one loses by par distance, which counts a
  successful intervention against it. Landy is close to natural (only
  2♣ differs) and is the one par favours.
- Most of Cappelletti's, Modified Cappelletti's and Meckwell's gain is
  the penalty double (Cappelletti: X over a natural pass +1,464 on 908
  boards, balancing X +654) and, for Meckwell, its double (+775 over a
  pass, +707 where natural bid 2♠). DONT has no penalty double and gains
  least; its passes where natural overcalled 2♠/2♦/2♣ lose (-306, -193,
  -124): our DONT has a 15 HCP ceiling, so a 16-17 overcall now passes.
- Cappelletti's one-suited 2♣ where natural bid 2♦ or 2♠ loses (-258
  over 379 boards, -240 over 218): showing the suit a round later costs.
  Modified Cappelletti's 2♣ loses the same way over 2♥ (-125).
- These boards were dealt for other scenarios, with our engine on both
  sides; the corpus has no BBA reference for DONT, Meckwell or Modified
  Cappelletti, so only the two double-dummy yardsticks judge them.

Runs: local `rbb compare --json` outputs (`base.json`, `final.json`,
`f-<defence>.json`, one per defence forced on with `--set`), not kept.

## `natural` (2026-11-03)

convention-card 0.43 added `natural` to the defence options; "Natural"
used to load as `other`. Both play the natural defence in overcalls.bid,
and `natural` also says no DONT, whatever `dont.play` says.

## Sources

- Bridge Bum: "Cappelletti (Hamilton)", https://www.bridgebum.com/cappelletti.php
  (with its Modified Cappelletti section); "DONT",
  https://www.bridgebum.com/dont.php; "Meckwell Defense to 1NT",
  https://www.bridgebum.com/meckwell_defense_to_1nt.php; "Multi-Landy
  (Woolsey)", https://www.bridgebum.com/multi_landy.php.
- Wikipedia: "Cappelletti convention",
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappelletti_convention; "DONT",
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DONT; "Meckwell convention",
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meckwell_convention.
- ACBL Unit 390 (Simon): "Modified Cappelletti",
  https://www.acblunit390.org/Simon/modcapp.htm; "Meckwell defense to
  1NT", https://www.acblunit390.org/Simon/meckwellnt.htm.
- GIB (what the GIB corpus plays): its bidding database, as browsed at
  https://netbridge.dk/gib.html (sequences `1N-*`, `1N-P-P-*`,
  `1N-D-P-*`, `1N-2C-P-*`, `1N-2C-P-2D-P-*`, `1N-2D-P-*`, `1N-2H-P-*`,
  `1N-2N-P-*`): Cappelletti, X penalty 16+, the same in the balancing
  seat.
- Bridge-Classroom `src/utils/ntDefenses.js` and
  `src/components/conventionCard/VsNtDefense.vue` (the card paths and
  the editor's meanings).
- BBA, as a black box: the probes listed under each module.

## Probes (all `our = []`, 21GF-DEFAULT unless named)

`probes/vs-1N-capp.toml` (direct, 1,500 hands), `vs-1N-capp-bal.toml`
(balancing, 800), `vs-1N-capp-2C-adv`, `-2D-adv`, `-2H-adv`, `-2S-adv`,
`-2N-adv`, `-X-adv` (advancer, 600 each), `-2C-2D` and `-2H-2N` (the
overcaller's answers), `vs-1N-mlandy.toml` (21GF-Multi, 1,000).

## Gaps and open questions

- **Which yardstick** decides the thresholds (the penalty double at 15,
  the minimum for the two-suiters)? The card decides the defence; the
  thresholds follow BBA and the sources where they agree.
- **Their weak notrump**: `vs_1nt_weak.system` loads but is not read;
  the strong-notrump scheme is played against every range. Reading it
  needs the opener's range in the context (their 1NT's `hcp.max`).
- Competitive continuations when the opener's side bids over our call
  are not written (the fallback is pass).
- Systems (Stayman, transfers) by the advancer of a 1NT *overcall* are
  unrelated and unchanged.
- Suction and Hello (in the editor's list) are not options: a card
  naming them loads with the field reported invalid and plays natural.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Defence against their preempts (2026-09-27). The par attribution
# (probes/tools/par_blame.py) showed our side passing out their weak twos
# and three-level preempts: over anything but a one-level opening there
# were no rules at all.
#
# Natural, as the Basic-Bridge card plays it, and as BBA bids it there
# (probes/vs-w2-2D.toml, vs-w2-2H.toml, vs-w2-2S.toml): the one-level
# structure a level higher.
#
# - a takeout double: 12+ total points, two or fewer of theirs and three
#   or more in each unbid suit, or 17+ HCP with three or fewer of theirs
#   (the power double, then bid again);
# - a new suit: five or more, 12-16 HCP; at the three level 13 total
#   points; a suit worth bidding (two of the top three, three of the top
#   five, six cards, or an opening hand of 13 total points);
# - a jump to three of a major: six or more, 15-16;
# - 2NT: 15-17 balanced, their suit stopped, no five-card major;
# - four of a major: seven or more, game;
# - otherwise pass.
#
# A weak two is told from a strong 2C by what the opener has shown: at
# most 12 HCP.

module vs-preempts "Defence against preempts"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  competitive_bidding/defense_vs_preempts
  skill  competitive_bidding/takeout_doubles
  skill  competitive_bidding/lebensohl
  param  leb = competitive_bidding/lebensohl:after_weak_two_double default false
  param  rub = competitive_bidding/rubensohl:after_double default false

# ── Direct seat over their weak two ──────────────────────────────────
after (2x) when x is not N, rho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Takeout: the unbid suits and 12+, or any 17+"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=2) | (hcp>=17, x<=3)
  cheapest(S) "Overcall: five or more spades, 12-16"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=16
      when  x is not S
      when  quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3 | S>=6 | hcp+length_points>=13
      when  cheapest_rank(S) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(H) "Overcall: five or more hearts, 12-16"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=16
      when  x is not H
      when  quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3 | H>=6 | hcp+length_points>=13
      when  cheapest_rank(H) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(D) "Overcall: five or more diamonds, 12-16"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=16
      when  x is not D
      when  quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3 | D>=6 | hcp+length_points>=13
      when  cheapest_rank(D) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(C) "Overcall: five or more clubs, 12-16"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=16
      when  x is not C
      when  quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3 | C>=6 | hcp+length_points>=13
      when  cheapest_rank(C) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=13
  jump(S) "Strong jump overcall: six or more spades, 15-16"
      shows S>=6, hcp=15..16
      when  x is not S
  jump(H) "Strong jump overcall: six or more hearts, 15-16"
      shows H>=6, H>S, hcp=15..16
      when  x is not H, x is not S
  cheapest(N) "15-17 balanced, {x} stopped, no five-card major"
      shows balanced, hcp=15..17, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x)
  4S  "Seven or more spades: game"
      shows S>=7, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  x is not S
  4H  "Seven or more hearts: game"
      shows H>=7, H>S, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  x is not H
  P   "No overcall"
      priority -10

# ── Balancing over their weak two: (2x) P (P) ───────────────────────
# BBA (probes/vs-w2-2H-bal.toml): lighter than direct. A reopening double
# with two or fewer of theirs and 12+; a new suit from 9 total points at
# the two level, 11 at the three; 2NT 16-18; a jump to three of a major
# with six and 15+.
after (2x) P (P) when x is not N, lho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Reopening double: 12+, short in {x}, the unbid suits"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=2) | (hcp>=17, x<=3)
  cheapest(S) "Balancing: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=16
      when  x is not S
      when  cheapest_rank(S) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=11
  cheapest(H) "Balancing: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=16
      when  x is not H
      when  cheapest_rank(H) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=11
  cheapest(D) "Balancing: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=16
      when  x is not D
      when  cheapest_rank(D) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=11
  cheapest(C) "Balancing: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=9, hcp<=16
      when  x is not C
      when  cheapest_rank(C) <= 13 | hcp+length_points>=11
  jump(S) "Six or more spades, 15-16"
      shows S>=6, hcp=15..16
      when  x is not S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 13
  jump(H) "Six or more hearts, 15-16"
      shows H>=6, H>S, hcp=15..16
      when  x is not H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 13, !rub | cheapest_rank(x) > 18
  cheapest(N) "16-18 balanced, {x} stopped"
      shows balanced, hcp=16..18, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x)
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"
      priority -10

# ── Direct seat over their three-level preempt ───────────────────────
# BBA (probes/vs-p3-3{C,D,H,S}.toml): a takeout double from 12; a new
# suit at the three level from 12 total points, at the four level from
# 14; 3NT 17-21 with their suit stopped; four of a major with seven.
after (3x) when x is not N, rho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Takeout: 12+, short in {x}, the unbid suits, or 17+"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=2) | (hcp>=17, x<=3)
  cheapest(S) "Overcall: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      when  x is not S
      when  quality(S)>=good | top5(S)>=3 | S>=6 | hcp+length_points>=14
      when  cheapest_rank(S) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=14
  cheapest(H) "Overcall: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      when  x is not H
      when  quality(H)>=good | top5(H)>=3 | H>=6 | hcp+length_points>=14
      when  cheapest_rank(H) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=14
  cheapest(D) "Overcall: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      when  x is not D
      when  quality(D)>=good | top5(D)>=3 | D>=6 | hcp+length_points>=14
      when  cheapest_rank(D) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=14
  cheapest(C) "Overcall: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=12, hcp<=17
      when  x is not C
      when  quality(C)>=good | top5(C)>=3 | C>=6 | hcp+length_points>=14
      when  cheapest_rank(C) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=14
  3N  "17-21 with {x} stopped"
      shows hcp=17..21, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x)
  4S  "Seven or more spades: game"
      shows S>=7, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  x is not S
  4H  "Seven or more hearts: game"
      shows H>=7, H>S, hcp+length_points>=13
      when  x is not H
  P   "No overcall"
      priority -10

# ── Balancing over their three-level preempt: (3x) P (P) ─────────────
# BBA (probes/vs-p3-3H-bal.toml): a reopening double with 12+ and at most
# one of theirs; a new suit at the three level from 11 total points, at
# the four from 13; 3NT 17-20 with their suit stopped.
after (3x) P (P) when x is not N, lho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Reopening double: 12+, short in {x}, the unbid suits"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12
      shows ((S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=1) | (hcp>=17, x<=3)
  cheapest(S) "Balancing: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  x is not S
      when  cheapest_rank(S) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(H) "Balancing: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  x is not H
      when  cheapest_rank(H) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(D) "Balancing: five or more diamonds"
      shows D>=5, D>S, D>H, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  x is not D
      when  cheapest_rank(D) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(C) "Balancing: five or more clubs"
      shows C>=5, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=11, hcp<=17
      when  x is not C
      when  cheapest_rank(C) <= 18 | hcp+length_points>=13
  3N  "17-20 with {x} stopped"
      shows hcp=17..20, S<=4, H<=4
      when  stop(x)
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"
      priority -10

# ── Their four-level preempt ─────────────────────────────────────────
# BBA (probes/vs-p4-4H.toml, vs-p4-4S.toml, vs-p4-4H-bal.toml). Over 4H a
# takeout double from 14 and 4S with five from 14 total points; over 4S
# the double is for penalty, 17+ (values: partner leaves it in unless
# his shape says otherwise); five of a minor from 16. Balancing over 4H:
# the double from 12 with no hearts, 4S from 13, five of a minor from 15.
after (4x) when x is H, rho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Takeout: 14+, short in hearts"
      shows hcp+length_points>=14, x<=2, S>=3
  4S  "Five or more spades, 14+"
      shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=14
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds, 16+"   shows D>=5, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=16
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, 16+"      shows C>=5, C>D, hcp+length_points>=16
  P   "No overcall"
      priority -10
after (4x) when x is S, rho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Values: 17+, for penalty"
      shows hcp>=17, x>=2
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds, 16+"   shows D>=5, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=16
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts, 16+"     shows H>=5, H>=D, H>=C, hcp+length_points>=16
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, 16+"      shows C>=5, C>D, hcp+length_points>=16
  P   "No overcall"
      priority -10
after (4x) P (P) when x is H, lho.hcp.max <= 12
  X   "Reopening double: 12+, no hearts"
      shows hcp+length_points>=12, x<=1
  4S  "Five or more spades, 13+"             shows S>=5, hcp+length_points>=13
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds, 15+"   shows D>=5, D>=C, hcp+length_points>=15
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, 15+"      shows C>=5, C>D, hcp+length_points>=15
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"
      priority -10
# Advancer after our double of their four-level preempt: over 4H take
# it out into five or more spades; otherwise leave it in.
after (4x) X (P) | (4x) P (P) X (P) when x is H | x is S
  4S  "Five or more spades"                  shows S>=5
      when  x is H
  P   "Leaves the double in"
      priority -5

# ── Their four-level minor preempt (2026-10-15) ──────────────────────
# Brill daily 2026-10-14 board 5: (4C) passed round with 16 HCP,
# 4-2-4-3; there was no rule over 4C or 4D. Standard practice (doubles
# of preempts below 4S are for takeout, Bridge World Standard; partner
# converts with length in their suit): the double is takeout of the
# minor, short in it with both majors, or 16+ with any shape (at the
# four level it is the strong hand's only call); four of a major is
# natural, five or more; a five-card other minor from 16. As over 4H,
# a little more than over a three-level preempt: 14 total points. A 4m
# opening no rule reads (cards without one) counts as natural; Namyats
# is artificial and stays out.
after (4x) when x is C | x is D, rho.hcp.max <= 12 | rho.named(x)
  X   "Takeout: 14+, short in {x}, or 16+"
      shows ((S>=3, H>=3, (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=2, hcp+length_points>=14) | (hcp>=16, x<=3))
  4S  "Five or more spades, 14+"             shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp+length_points>=14
  4H  "Five or more hearts, 14+"             shows H>=5, H>S, hcp+length_points>=14
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds, 16+"   shows D>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=16
      when  x is C
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs, 16+"      shows C>=5, S<=4, H<=4, hcp+length_points>=16
      when  x is D
  P   "No overcall"
      priority -10
after (4x) P (P) when x is C | x is D, lho.hcp.max <= 12 | lho.named(x)
  X   "Reopening double: 12+, short in {x}, or 16+"
      shows ((S>=3, H>=3, (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C), x<=2, hcp+length_points>=12) | (hcp>=16, x<=3))
  4S  "Five or more spades, 13+"             shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp+length_points>=13
  4H  "Five or more hearts, 13+"             shows H>=5, H>S, hcp+length_points>=13
  P   "Nothing to reopen with"
      priority -10
# Advancer: a four-card major, the longer (hearts with four of each:
# the cheaper), a five-card other minor, else leave it in.
after (4x) X (P) | (4x) P (P) X (P) when x is C | x is D
  4H  "Four or more hearts"                  shows H>=4, H>=S
  4S  "Four or more spades"                  shows S>=4, S>H
  cheapest(D) "Five or more diamonds"        shows D>=5, S<=3, H<=3, x<=2
      when  x is C
  cheapest(C) "Five or more clubs"           shows C>=5, S<=3, H<=3, x<=2
      when  x is D
  P   "Leaves the double in"
      priority -5

# ── Their preempt raised to the four or five level (2026-10-15) ──────
# Brill daily 2026-10-14 board 4: (2D) P (5D) with AQJ7.AKQT94.-.K84;
# the "they are too high" penalty double (penalty-doubles.bid) was the
# only call, and 5DX made with 6H/6S on. With a void in their suit and
# a long suit the hand is for declaring: bid it; the double is takeout
# (as over their four-level preempt, a level higher). The long suit
# first: its own strain is the one partner cannot find.
after (2x) P (4x) | (2x) P (5x) | (3x) P (4x) | (3x) P (5x) when x is not N, lho.hcp.max <= 12
  cheapest(S) "Six or more spades, 16+"
      shows S>=6, S>=H, hcp+length_points>=16
      when  x is not S
      when  cheapest_rank(S) <= 23 | hcp+length_points>=18
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Six or more hearts, 16+"
      shows H>=6, H>S, hcp+length_points>=16
      when  x is not H
      when  cheapest_rank(H) <= 23 | hcp+length_points>=18
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Six or more diamonds, 18+"
      shows D>=6, D>S, D>H, hcp+length_points>=18
      when  x is not D
  cheapest(C) "Six or more clubs, 18+"
      shows C>=6, C>S, C>H, C>D, hcp+length_points>=18
      when  x is not C
  X   "Takeout: 16+, short in {x}"
      shows hcp+length_points>=16, x<=1
      shows (S>=3 | x is S), (H>=3 | x is H), (D>=3 | x is D), (C>=3 | x is C)
# Advancer: the double is takeout but high; pull it only with a
# five-card major and at most one of theirs, else leave it in.
after (2x) P (4x) X (P) | (2x) P (5x) X (P) | (3x) P (4x) X (P) | (3x) P (5x) X (P) when x is not N
  cheapest(S) "Five or more spades and no defence"   shows S>=5, S>=H, x<=1
      when  x is not S
  cheapest(H) "Five or more hearts and no defence"   shows H>=5, H>S, x<=1
      when  x is not H
  P   "Leaves the double in"
      priority -5

# ── Advancer after our double of their weak two ──────────────────────
# BBA (probes/vs-w2-2H-X-adv.toml, vs-w2-2S-X-adv.toml): the cheapest
# suit with four, 0-10 (majors first); a jump in a major with five, 8-11;
# 2NT 11-12 and 3NT 12+ with their suit stopped; the cue bid of their
# suit, 13+, forcing to game; four of a major with four and game values;
# a pass with length and strength in their suit.
after (2x) X (P) | (3x) X (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) | (3x) P (P) X (P) when x is not C
  P   "Penalty: five of their suit with two top honours"
      shows x>=5, quality(x)>=good | top5(x)>=3
      priority 2
  P   "Penalty: four of their suit, a flat hand and 10+"
      shows x=4, hcp>=10, stop(x), S<=4, H<=4, D<=4, C<=4
      priority 2
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: 13+, forcing to game"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp+length_points>=13
      sets   forcing=game
      when   !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18
  4S  "Game: four or more spades, 11+"
      shows S>=4, S>=H, hcp+length_points=11..12
      when  x is not S
  4H  "Game: four or more hearts, 11+"
      shows H>=4, H>S, hcp+length_points=11..12
      when  x is not H
  jump(S) "Invitational: five or more spades, 8-10"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp+length_points=8..10
      when  x is not S, cheapest_rank(S) <= 13, !rub | cheapest_rank(x) > 18     # a jump to three, not to game; Rubensohl transfers there
  jump(H) "Invitational: five or more hearts, 8-10"
      shows H>=5, H>S, hcp+length_points=8..10
      when  x is not H, cheapest_rank(H) <= 13, !rub | cheapest_rank(x) > 18
  cheapest(N) "11-12 with {x} stopped"
      shows hcp+length_points=11..12, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  stop(x), cheapest_rank(x) < 14, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game with {x} stopped, no four-card major"
      shows hcp+length_points>=13 | (hcp+length_points>=11, cheapest_rank(x) >= 14), S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  stop(x), !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades, 0-10"
      shows S>=4, S>=H, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  x is not S, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(S) <= 13
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts, 0-10"
      shows H>=4, H>S, hcp+length_points<=10
      when  x is not H, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(H) <= 13
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds, 0-10, no four-card major"
      shows D>=4, D>=C, hcp+length_points<=10, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not D, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(D) <= 13
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs, 0-10, no four-card major"
      shows C>=4, C>D | x is D, hcp+length_points<=10, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not C, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(C) <= 13
  # Nothing fits: the longest suit that is not theirs, cheapest first.
  cheapest(S) "No four-card suit: spades"   when x is not S, S>=H, S>=D, S>=C, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(S) <= 13
      priority -5
  cheapest(H) "No four-card suit: hearts"   when x is not H, H>=D, H>=C, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(H) <= 13
      priority -5
  cheapest(D) "No four-card suit: diamonds" when x is not D, D>=C, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(D) <= 13
      priority -6
  cheapest(C) "No four-card suit: clubs"    when x is not C, !(leb | rub) | cheapest_rank(x) > 18 | cheapest_rank(C) <= 13
      priority -7

# ── The doubler's rebid ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# A pass denies the power double (17+ HCP); the strong hand raises,
# shows its own suit, or bids notrump.
after (2x) X (P) 2y (P) | (2x) X (P) 3y (P) | (3x) X (P) 3y (P) | (3x) X (P) 4y (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2y (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3y (P) when y is not x, x is not C
  P   "Minimum double"          shows hcp<=16
      priority -5
  4{y} "Game: four-card support, 17+"      shows y>=4, hcp>=17
      when  y is H | y is S
  cheapest(y) "Raise: four-card support, 17+"                 shows y>=4, hcp>=17
      priority -1
  3N  "18+ with {x} stopped"                         shows hcp>=18, stop(x)
  cheapest(S) "17+ and five or more spades"          shows S>=5, hcp>=17
      when  x is not S, y is not S
  cheapest(H) "17+ and five or more hearts"          shows H>=5, S<=4, hcp>=17
      when  x is not H, y is not H
after (2x) X (P) 2N (P) when x is not C, !leb, !rub
  3N  "Accepts the invitation: 14+"                  shows hcp>=14
  P   "Declines"                                     shows hcp<=13
      priority -5

# ── Lebensohl after our double of their weak two ─────────────────────
# `competitive.lebensohl_weak_twos.play` (the 21GF cards). Bridge Bum,
# "Lebensohl over weak two bids"; Larry Cohen, "Lebensohl". Advancer:
#
# - a new suit at the two level: natural, weak (the rules above);
# - 2NT: a relay to 3C, with a weak hand that must bid at the three
#   level (pass or correct), or game values with their suit stopped
#   ("slow shows": then the cue bid or 3NT);
# - a new suit at the three level directly: constructive, 8-11;
# - the cue bid directly: game values, four of an unbid major, no stopper;
# - 3NT directly: game values, no stopper, no four-card major;
# - jumps to three of a major (invitational) and to game: as before.
#
# The natural replies above step aside at the three level when this is
# on (their `!leb` clauses); over a three-level preempt nothing changes.
# Tried 2026-09-27 and reverted on par; built again from the card
# 2026-10-05 (vs-preempts.notes.md).
after (2x) X (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) when x is not C, leb, !rub
  2N  "Lebensohl: relay to 3C, weak or game values"
      alert  artificial
      shows  (hcp<=8, C>=4 | (D>=4, x is H | x is S) | (H>=4, x is S), S<=3 | x is S | cheapest_rank(S) >= 15, H<=3 | x is H | cheapest_rank(H) >= 15) | (hcp>=13, stop(x), S<=4 | x is S, H<=4 | x is H)
      sets   ask=leb_relay
      priority 1
  cheapest(x) "Cue bid: game values, a four-card major, no {x} stopper"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=13, (S=4, x is not S) | (H=4, x is not H), S<=4 | x is S, H<=4 | x is H
      when   !stop(x)
      sets   forcing=game, ask=leb_cue
      priority 1
  3N  "Game values, no four-card major, no stopper in {x}"
      shows hcp>=13, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  !stop(x)
      priority 1
  cheapest(S) "Constructive: four or more spades, 9-12"
      shows S>=4, S>=H, hcp=9..12
      when  x is not S, cheapest_rank(S) >= 15
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Constructive: four or more hearts, 9-12"
      shows H>=4, H>S, hcp=9..12
      when  x is not H, cheapest_rank(H) >= 15
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Constructive: four or more diamonds, 9-12"
      shows D>=4, D>=C, hcp=9..12, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not D, cheapest_rank(D) >= 15
      priority 1
  cheapest(C) "Constructive: four or more clubs, 9-12"
      shows C>=4, C>D | x is D, hcp=9..12, S<=3 | x is S, H<=3 | x is H
      when  x is not C, cheapest_rank(C) >= 15
      priority 1
  # A five-card unbid major and game values: bid the game (BBA too).
  4S  "Game: five or more spades"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not S
      priority 1
  4H  "Game: five or more hearts"
      shows H>=5, H>S, hcp+length_points>=11
      when  x is not H
      priority 1
  # Five of their suit and a weak hand: nowhere to go, pass (BBA).
  P   "Leaves the double in: five or more {x}"
      shows x>=5, hcp<=8
      priority 1
  # Nothing else fits: the relay, then the best of what is left.
  2N  "Lebensohl: relay to 3C"
      alert  artificial
      sets   ask=leb_relay
      priority -8

# The doubler: 3C as asked; with 19+ and their suit stopped, 3NT.
after (2x) X (P) 2N (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) when x is not C, leb, !rub
  3N  "Game: 19+ with {x} stopped"    shows hcp>=19, stop(x)
      priority 2
  3C  "Lebensohl: as asked"
      alert  artificial
      priority 1

# Advancer after the relay.
after (2x) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) when x is not C, leb, !rub
  P   "Weak, clubs"                                  shows C>=4, hcp<=8
      priority 1
  cheapest(D) "Weak, diamonds: to play"              shows D>=4, D>C, hcp<=8
      when  x is not D
      priority 1
  cheapest(H) "Weak, hearts: to play"                shows H>=4, H>D, H>C, hcp<=8
      when  x is S
      priority 1
  cheapest(x) "Slow cue: game values, four of an unbid major, {x} stopped"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=13, stop(x), (S=4, x is not S) | (H=4, x is not H)
      sets   forcing=game, ask=leb_cue
      priority 1
  3N  "Slow 3NT: game values with {x} stopped, no four-card major"
      shows hcp>=13, stop(x)
      priority 1
  P   "Weak: to play in clubs"                          priority -10

# The doubler answers either cue bid: an unbid four-card major, else
# 3NT, else his longer minor.
after (2x) X (P) 3x (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 3x (P) | (2x) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3x (P) | (2x) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) 3C (P) 3x (P) when x is not C, leb, !rub
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts"                          shows H>=4
      when  x is not H
      priority 2
  cheapest(S) "Four spades"                          shows S>=4
      when  x is not S
      priority 2
  3N  "No four-card major"                           priority 1
  cheapest(D) "No major, no stopper: diamonds"       shows D>=4, D>=C
      when  x is not D
      priority -1

# ── Advancer after our overcall of their weak two ────────────────────
after (2x) 2y (P) | (2x) 3y (P) | (3x) 3y (P) | (3x) 4y (P) | (2x) P (P) 2y (P) | (2x) P (P) 3y (P) when y is not x, x is not C
  4{y} "Game: three-card support, 12+"               shows y>=3, hcp+length_points>=12
      when  y is H | y is S
  cheapest(y) "Raise: three-card support, 8-11"      shows y>=3, hcp+length_points=8..11
  3N  "Game: 12+ with {x} stopped"                   shows hcp+length_points>=12, stop(x), y<=2
  P   "Nothing to add"                               priority -10

# ── Advancer after our 2NT (15-17) ───────────────────────────────────
after (2x) 2N (P) when x is not C
  3N  "Game: 9+"                                     shows hcp>=9, S<=5, H<=5
  4S  "Game: six or more spades, 8+"                 shows S>=6, hcp>=8
      when  x is not S
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts, 8+"                 shows H>=6, hcp>=8
      when  x is not H
  P   "No game"                                      shows hcp<=8
      priority -10

# ── Their side after our action over the weak two ───────────────────
# The weak-two responses assume a pass on the right. Over our double or
# overcall the responder competes with a fit (total-tricks.bid) or
# passes; the opener has described his hand.
after 2x (X) | 2x (2y) | 2x (3y) | 2x (2N) | 3x (X) | 3x (3y) | 3x (4y) | 3x (3N) | 4x (X) | 4x (4y) | 4x (5y) when x is not N
  P   "No further bid"                 priority -10
after 2x (X) P (*) | 2x (2y) P (*) | 2x (3y) P (*) | 2x (2N) P (*) | 3x (X) P (*) | 3x (3y) P (*) | 3x (4y) P (*) | 4x (X) P (*) | 4x (4y) P (*) | 4x (5y) P (*) when x is not N
  P   "No further bid"      priority -10
