# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module minor-transfers "Minor-suit responses to 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  notrump-base
  skill  bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers
  param  mtp   = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:over_1nt default true    # a silent card plays relay, as before the switch (2026-10-30)
  param  style = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:style default relay
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_2c = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_2c default false

# One card field chooses the treatment (see notes). Only the calls that
# start the sequence and opener's answer differ; responder's next call is
# written once, for every treatment, against `answered transfer(m)`.
#
# The transfers are for weak and invitational hands with no five-card major
# (with one, transfer to the major first). With game values, bid 3NT.

# ── relay (the default): 2S relays to 3C; pass with clubs, 3D with diamonds.
after nt1 when (!they.bid | systems_on), mtp, style is relay
  2S  "Relay to 3♣: a weak hand with a long minor"  alert
      shows C>=6 | D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, strength=signoff
      sets forcing=round, ask=relay
      artificial
after nt1 2S (P) when mtp, style is relay
  3C  "Completes the relay"  artificial
when answered relay
  P   "Clubs: play here"       shows C>=6
  3D  "Diamonds: play here"    shows D>=6

# ── four-way: 2S transfers to clubs, 2NT to diamonds. Opener shows good
# support (Kxx or better) by bidding the step below the suit (four_way) or the
# suit itself (four_way_reversed); the other call denies it.
after nt1 when (!they.bid | systems_on), mtp, style is four_way | style is four_way_reversed
  2S  "Transfer to clubs"      alert  shows C>=6, H<=4, S<=4, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(C)  artificial
  2N  "Transfer to diamonds"   alert  shows D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(D)  artificial

after nt1 2S (P) when mtp, style is four_way
  2N  "Good club support: Kxx or better"   alert  shows C>=3, has(A,C) | has(K,C)  artificial
  3C  "No good club support"
after nt1 2N (P) when mtp, style is four_way
  3C  "Good diamond support: Kxx or better"   alert  shows D>=3, has(A,D) | has(K,D)  artificial
  3D  "No good diamond support"

after nt1 2S (P) when mtp, style is four_way_reversed
  3C  "Good club support: Kxx or better"   shows C>=3, has(A,C) | has(K,C)
  2N  "No good club support"                alert  artificial
after nt1 2N (P) when mtp, style is four_way_reversed
  3D  "Good diamond support: Kxx or better"   shows D>=3, has(A,D) | has(K,D)
  3C  "No good diamond support"                alert  artificial

# ── bba: 2S transfers to clubs, 3C to diamonds; opener always completes.
after nt1 when (!they.bid | systems_on), mtp, style is bba
  2S  "Transfer to clubs"      alert  shows C>=6, H<=4, S<=4, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(C)  artificial
  3C  "Transfer to diamonds"   alert  shows D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(D)  artificial
after nt1 2S (P) when mtp, style is bba
  3C  "Completes the transfer"
after nt1 3C (P) when mtp, style is bba
  3D  "Completes the transfer"

# ── two_nt_three_c: 2NT transfers to clubs, 3C to diamonds; opener always
# completes. 2S stays free for Minor Suit Stayman (21GF-MSTandMSS). Any
# strength: with game values responder goes on after the completion.
after nt1_undoubled when (!they.bid | systems_on), mtp, style is two_nt_three_c
  2N  "Transfer to clubs: six or more clubs"  alert
      shows C>=6, D<=3, H<=3, S<=3
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(C)
      artificial
      priority 1
  3C  "Transfer to diamonds: six or more diamonds"  alert
      shows D>=6, C<=3, H<=3, S<=3
      sets  forcing=round, ask=transfer(D)
      artificial
      priority 1                         # ahead of the natural 3♦ slam try
after nt1_undoubled 2N (P) when mtp, style is two_nt_three_c
  3C  "Completes the transfer"
after nt1_undoubled 3C (P) when mtp, style is two_nt_three_c
  3D  "Completes the transfer"

# ── Responder after any minor transfer. Game values: 3NT. Opposite good
# support the long minor should run, so invitational values bid 3NT too.
# Otherwise play the minor at the three level.
when answered transfer(m)
  P   "Play here"                          shows strength<=invite   when partner.last=3{m}
  3m  "Sign off in {m}"                    shows strength<=invite
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"       shows strength>=game
  3N  "To play: invitational values, a long {m}"   shows strength=invite    when partner.m>=3

# ── Over a 2♣ overcall of our 1NT (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c`). Every
# treatment keeps its own calls: 2♣ was not one of them, so nothing
# moves. The minor transfer picks up the same five-HCP floor as the
# major ones: below that BBA leaves their 2♣ alone.
after 1N (2C) when vs_2c, mtp, style is relay
  2S  "Relay to 3♣: a weak hand with a long minor"  alert
      shows C>=6 | D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=5, strength=signoff
      sets forcing=round, ask=relay
      artificial
after 1N (2C) 2S (P) when vs_2c, mtp, style is relay
  3C  "Completes the relay"  artificial

after 1N (2C) when vs_2c, mtp, style is four_way | style is four_way_reversed
  2S  "Transfer to clubs"      alert  shows C>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=5, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(C)  artificial
  2N  "Transfer to diamonds"   alert  shows D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=5, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(D)  artificial

after 1N (2C) when vs_2c, mtp, style is bba
  2S  "Transfer to clubs"      alert  shows C>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=5, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(C)  artificial
  3C  "Transfer to diamonds"   alert  shows D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=5, strength<=invite  sets forcing=round, ask=transfer(D)  artificial
after 1N (2C) 2S (P) when vs_2c, mtp, style is bba
  3C  "Completes the transfer"
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) when vs_2c, mtp, style is bba
  3D  "Completes the transfer"

# minor-transfers (`minor-transfers.bid`): notes

Responses to 1NT with a long minor. One card field,
`notrump.minor_transfers`, chooses the treatment. Cases:
`minor-transfers.test` (a section per treatment).

## Guidance (Rick, 2026-09-21)

- **relay** is the default: 2S relays to 3C, and responder passes or
  corrects to 3D.
- **four_way**: 2S shows clubs and 2NT diamonds. Opener shows good support
  (Kxx or better) by bidding the step below the suit (2NT over 2S, 3C over
  2NT); bidding the suit denies it. This is how Rick plays it.
- **four_way_reversed**: the same, with the two answers swapped (the suit
  shows good support).
- **bba**: BBA's own treatment (below).
- **two_nt_three_c** (2026-10-13): 2NT transfers to clubs, 3♣ to
  diamonds, any strength, opener always completes; 2♠ stays free for
  Minor Suit Stayman. BBA's 21GF-MSTandMSS, derived on import from its
  `1N-2N transfer to clubs` and `1N-3C transfer to diamonds` keys
  (convention-card PR #55). The rules moved here unchanged from
  minor-suit-stayman.bid, which had read the two `notrump.transfers.*`
  switches while the field had no value for the pair. Not offered over
  a 2♣ overcall (`vs_2c`): it never was; open question.
- Treatments are card choices, not separate conventions; only the calls
  that differ are written per treatment (LANGUAGE.md, "Treatments").
- Another variant Rick mentioned, not built: a 2S range ask, where 2S is
  weak with clubs or a notrump invitation, and opener bids 3C with a maximum
  and 2NT otherwise.

What we build on top:

- The transfers are for weak and invitational hands with no five-card
  major. With a five-card major, transfer to the major first; with game
  values, bid 3NT.
- After a minor transfer, responder plays the minor at the three level, or
  bids 3NT: with game values, or with invitational values opposite good
  support (the minor should run).
- With four-way transfers 2NT is not natural. Invitational hands without a
  major go through Stayman and bid 2NT next (`stayman.bid`), and the natural
  2NT (`one-nt.bid`) is off.

## Evidence from BBA

BBA's cards set the treatment through several switches: 21GF-DEFAULT
and 13 other PBS cards have `1N-2S transfer to clubs` and
`1N-3C transfer to diamonds`, which import as `bba`. In the corpus BBA's
opener always completes (3C or 3D, no super-accept). Responder passes when
weak (43 and 56 deals) and bids 3NT when invitational or better (22, 23).
With a five-card major and a six-card minor BBA transfers to the major
(616 calls).

Other switch combinations (Minor Suit Stayman over 1NT, 3C Puppet
Stayman, 2S clubs alone) import as `none`: we do not know how BBA plays
them.

Corpus, when this module was added: +752 calls agree with BBA, 1 fewer.

## Gaps (not built yet)

- Slam tries and game-forcing hands with a long minor.
- The 2S range ask.
- Interference over the transfers.

## Under interference (2026-09-23)

A 2♣ overcall of our 1NT takes none of these calls away, so
`after 1N (2C) when vs_2c` repeats each treatment's opening call and
opener's answer. The only change is a **five-HCP floor**, the same one
the major transfers picked up: BBA does not enter at the two level over
their 2♣ with nothing.

Over a *double* there is no minor transfer written. On the cards that
keep transfers on over a double (Basic-Bridge, 21GF-GIB) the minor
transfers are off, so a weak hand with a long minor has nowhere to run
and passes, which is what BBA does. A card with both on would want
these rules here too.

Evidence and numbers: `nt-interference.notes.md`.

## Length points (2026-09-23)

With `points` counting length a six-card minor adds two points, so
`5.K73.QJ9542.J83` (7 HCP) is 9 — invitational, no longer weak:

- **relay / none**: the relay stays for weak hands (0–7 total points);
  invitational hands with a long minor bid the natural 2NT
  (`one-nt.bid`, see its notes). Before, this hand had no rule at all.
  9 HCP and six diamonds (11) bids 3NT.
- **four_way**: Stayman's "invitational without a major" clause (for
  2NT) now excludes a six-card minor, `C<=5, D<=5`: that hand transfers,
  as designed, and bids 3NT opposite good support.
- Test hands for the weak sequences were changed to genuinely weak ones
  (`5.J73.QJ9542.832`); the 8-HCP `5.Q73.J83.AQ9542` is now 10 and bids
  3NT directly.

The corpus has no `relay` or `four_way` card, so these are measured only
through the `none` cards, where every option was within 10 IMPs.

## Convention score: the switch (2026-10-07)

The conv-ab run reported the convention unmeasured: only 9 of our
auctions changed with it "off". The rules were not at fault; the off
switch was. `probes/conv-ab.toml` set `notrump.minor_transfers=none`
and `notrump.minor_transfers.over_2nt=false`, but `minor_transfers` is
derived on import from BBA's `1N-2S/2N/3C transfer` keys
(`notrump.minor_transfers.two_s_clubs`, `two_nt_clubs`, `two_nt_diamonds`,
`three_c_diamonds`) and already reads `none` on 21GF-MSTandMSS
(Minor_Suit_Transfer's card), whose 2NT/3♣ transfers
minor-suit-stayman.bid reads from those keys. Setting it to `none`
changed nothing there, and the exported off card kept the keys, so
BBA went on transferring too (only its 2NT key changed). The off list
now also clears the four `transfers.*` keys, which switches both
engines. (Since 2026-10-13 21GF-MSTandMSS reads `two_nt_three_c`, and
`minor_transfers=none` alone switches our side off.)

Measured (Minor_Suit_Transfer, 2N_and_1_Minor): **+0.60 IMPs per
changed board** (Rusty's gain +378, BBA's +59; 528 changed boards, 499
of ours; halves +54/+265, agree): good.

## Card schema 2.0

- (2026-10-30) Card schema 2.0 (convention-card ADR-0002): the enum became
  `notrump.minor_transfers.play` and `.style` (no `none`; off is `play =
  false`). The modules read `mtp` with default **true**, so a card silent on
  minor-suit transfers still plays relay, as before. 0 calls changed on
  `compare --limit 50`.

## Sources

- **The treatments:** `relay`, `four_way` and `four_way_reversed` as Rick
  described them (2026-09-21; `four_way` is how Rick plays it). Beyond
  that description, standard practice, not yet cited to a book or
  article.
- **`bba`:** BBA's `1N-2S transfer to clubs` and `1N-3C transfer to
  diamonds` keys, as BBA plays them in the corpus ("Evidence from BBA").
  How BBA plays its other switch combinations (Minor Suit Stayman over
  1NT, 3♣ Puppet Stayman, 2♠ clubs alone) is unknown, so they import as
  `none`.
- **Rick's rulings:** the treatments and the default (2026-09-21); the 2♠
  range ask he mentioned is not built.
- **BBA evidence:** the corpus figures above, and the interference
  evidence in `nt-interference.notes.md`. No `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** when the module was added; length points
  (2026-09-23), measured only through the `none` cards, since no corpus
  card plays `relay` or `four_way`.

N 5.K73.J83.QJ9542      | 1NT P 2S P 2NT P | 3NT    | 7 HCP + 2 length = 9 opposite good support: the clubs should run
N 5.K73.J83.QJ9542      | 1NT P 2S P 3C P  | P      | 9 without good support: play 3C
N 5.Q73.J83.AQ9542      | 1NT P            | 3NT    | 8 HCP + 2 length = 10: game, no transfer
N Q82.K73.J83.K954      | 1NT P            | 2C     | invitational, no major: Stayman, then 2NT
N Q82.K73.J83.K954      | 1NT P 2C P 2D P  | 2NT    | the invitation

# ── four_way_reversed: the suit itself shows good support.
card    21GF-DEFAULT bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:style=four_way_reversed
S AK5.KJ7.Q94.K832      | 1NT P 2S P       | 3C     | good club support
S AK5.KJ72.Q94.QJ3      | 1NT P 2S P       | 2NT    | not good support
S AK5.KJ72.A94.QJ3      | 1NT P 2NT P      | 3D     | good diamond support

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Responder when RHO acts over our 1NT opening.
#
# Stayman and the transfers keep their own calls in `stayman.bid` and
# `jacoby-transfers.bid`, gated by the two card switches
# `notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_double` and `notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c`. What is
# left, and lives here, is what only exists because they bid: the
# redouble, the weak escapes when the transfers are off, and the pass.
#
# See nt-interference.notes.md for the BBA meanings behind the ranges.

module nt-interference "Our 1NT when RHO acts"
  kind   system
  needs  notrump-base
  param  vs_double = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_double default false
  param  vs_2c     = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_2c default false
  param  leb       = competitive_bidding/lebensohl:over_1nt_interference default false
  param  rub       = competitive_bidding/rubensohl:over_1nt_interference default false

# ── They doubled, transfers on ───────────────────────────────────────
# 2♣ is Stayman and 2♦/2♥ are the transfers (see the other modules).
# Everything else with values redoubles: partner has 15-17 and they have
# opened their mouth on the rest, so the hand is ours.
after 1N (X) when vs_double
  XX  "Values: 6+ HCP, no suit to show"
      shows hcp>=6
      priority -1
  P   "Not enough to act over the double"
      shows hcp<=5
      priority -10

# ── They doubled, transfers off ──────────────────────────────────────
# Without the transfers the two-level calls are natural escapes: a weak
# hand runs to its own long suit and everything else passes. The cut is
# four HCP, measured against BBA on the cards that leave the switch off
# (see the notes): at five and up BBA sits for the double whatever the
# shape, and running there loses more calls than it wins. There is no
# redouble here for the same reason — BBA redoubles only about one hand
# in twenty-five, and no condition we can write picks those out.
after 1N (X) when !vs_double
  2H  "Weak: five or more hearts, running from the double"
      shows H>=5, H>=S, hcp<=4
  2S  "Weak: five or more spades, running from the double"
      shows S>=5, hcp<=4
  2C  "Weak: six or more clubs, running from the double"
      shows C>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp<=4
  2D  "Weak: six or more diamonds, running from the double"
      shows D>=6, H<=4, S<=4, hcp<=4
  P   "Sitting for the double"
      priority -10

# Opener after responder's escape over the double: partner's suit is
# where we play (2026-09-28: 179 no-rule boards once the opponents'
# Cappelletti doubled for penalties).
after 1N (X) 2y (P) when !vs_double, y is not N
  P   "Partner's escape: to play"

after 1N (X) XX (P)
  P   "Playing 1NT redoubled"

# Our redouble, and they run: opener passes, leaving it to responder,
# who doubles for penalties with four of their suit or 9+ HCP.
after 1N (X) XX (*) when !rho.last=P
  P   "Partner redoubled: his decision"
after 1N (X) XX (2y) P (P)
  X   "Penalty"                                  shows y>=4 | hcp>=9
  P   "No further bid"                             priority -5

# Over a 2♣ overcall with `vs_2c` on nothing new is needed: the double
# is Stayman (stayman.bid), the transfers keep their calls
# (jacoby-transfers.bid, minor-transfers.bid, texas-transfers.bid) and
# the natural notrump calls and the pass are in one-nt.bid. With it off,
# a natural 2♣ has its own rules below.

# ── They overcalled 2♦, 2♥ or 2♠ ─────────────────────────────────────
# Their natural two-level overcall (2026-09-25; nt-interference.notes.md,
# probes/nt-2D-resp, nt-2H-resp, nt-2S-resp). No Lebensohl on the Basic
# card, so everything is natural except the double, which BBA plays as
# negative: four cards in an unbid major and 5+ HCP (over 2♠ five hearts
# with a weak hand too). A new suit at the two level is weak and to play,
# a non-jump at the three level forcing to game (BBA bids 3NT rather than
# jump in a five-card major); 2NT invites with 8-9 and 3NT is game from
# 10 (BBA does not insist on a stopper); four of a major is six cards
# and 10+.
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  X   "Negative double: four cards in an unbid major, 5+ HCP"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=5, S>=4 | H>=4
      when   y is D, S<=4, H<=4
      priority 1
  # Five hearts below 10 points double too: with 10+ they bid 3♥.
  X   "Negative double: four hearts, 5+ HCP"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=5, H=4 | (H=5, points<=9)
      when   y is S
      priority 1
  X   "Negative double: four spades, 5+ HCP"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=5, S=4
      when   y is H
      priority 1
  2H  "Natural, to play: five or more hearts"   shows H>=5, hcp>=4, points<=9
      when  y is D
  2S  "Natural, to play: five or more spades"   shows S>=5, hcp>=4, points<=9
      when  y is D | y is H
  cheapest(C) "Natural, forcing to game: five or more clubs"      shows C>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  cheapest(D) "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      when  y is not D
      sets  forcing=game
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"   shows H>=5, points>=10
      when  y is S
      sets  forcing=game
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"   shows H>=6, hcp>=10
      when  y is not H, !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"   shows S>=6, hcp>=10
      when  y is not S, !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  2N  "Invitational: 8-9 HCP, a stopper in {y}"   shows hcp=8..9, stop(y)
      when  !leb, !rub                  # 2NT is a relay or a transfer
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                           shows hcp>=10
      when  !leb
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10

# Opener answers the negative double: a four-card major at the cheapest
# level, 2NT with a stopper, a four-card minor, or a pass for penalties
# with four of their suit.
after 1N (2y) X (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  cheapest(H) "Four hearts for partner's double"   shows H>=4   when y is not H
  cheapest(S) "Four spades for partner's double"   shows S>=4   when y is not S
  2N  "No four-card major, a stopper in {y}"       shows stop(y)
      priority -1
  P   "Four of their suit: defends"                shows y>=4
      priority -2
  cheapest(C) "No major, no stopper: four clubs"   shows C>=4
      priority -3
  cheapest(D) "No major, no stopper: four diamonds"   shows D>=4
      when  y is not D
      priority -3
  cheapest(N) "No four-card major"
      priority -5

# Responder after opener's answer: game with 10+, an invitation in the
# major with 8-9, else pass.
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2M (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3M (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  4M  "Game in the fit: 10+"          shows M>=4, points>=10
  3M  "Invitational in the fit: 8-9"  shows M>=4, points=8..9
      when  partner.last=2M
  3N  "Game, no fit: 10+"             shows M<=3, points>=10
  P   "No game"                       shows points<=9
      priority -5
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2M (P) 3M (P) when y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  4M  "Accepts the invitation: a maximum"        shows hcp>=16
  P   "Declines: a minimum"                      shows hcp<=15
after 1N (2y) X (P) 2N (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3C (P) | 1N (2y) X (P) 3D (P) when y is not C, rho.y>=4, (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  3N  "Game: 10+"                     shows points>=10
  P   "No game"                       shows points<=9
      priority -5

# Opener after responder's other calls.
after 1N (2y) 3z (P) when y is not C, z is not y, z is not N, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"   shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1
after 1N (2y) 2z (P) when y is not C, z is not N, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2y) 2N (P) when !leb, !rub, y is not C, lho.y>=4, (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3)
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1

# ── Their natural 2♣, transfers off (2026-09-30) ─────────────────────
# With `vs_2c` off there is no Stayman by double and no transfer, and a
# natural 2♣ (five or more clubs: `rho.C>=5`, which DONT, Meckwell,
# Cappelletti and Landy 2♣ never show) is met as BBA meets it on bare
# SAYC (nt-interference.notes.md, probes/nt-2C-nat-resp.toml): no
# negative double. A five-card suit at the two level is to play, 2NT
# invites with a club stopper, 3NT is game with one. A weak hand with
# four of a major passes and leaves it to opener's reopening double.
# Game values are ours, not BBA's (which passes some 13-16 counts): a
# five-card suit at the three level forces to game, and the cue-bid is
# Stayman forcing to game, with a four-card major or no club stopper.
after 1N (2C) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  2S  "Natural, to play: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, S>=H, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2H  "Natural, to play: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, H>S, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2D  "Natural, to play: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, H<=4, S<=4, hcp>=4, points<=9
  2N  "Invitational: 8-9 HCP, a club stopper"     shows hcp=8..9, stop(C), H<=4, S<=4
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP, a club stopper"             shows hcp>=10, stop(C), H<=3, S<=3
  3C  "Stayman cue-bid: a four-card major or no club stopper"
      alert  artificial
      shows  hcp>=10, H<=4, S<=4, H=4 | S=4 | !stop(C)
      sets   forcing=game
      priority 1
  3D  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, H>S, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  3S  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, S>=H, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
      priority 2
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"   shows H>=6, H>S, points>=9
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 3
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"   shows S>=6, S>=H, points>=9
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 3
  P   "No bid over their 2♣: weak, or length in clubs"
      priority -10

# Opener after responder's call.
after 1N (2C) 2z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not N
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2C) 2N (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1
after 1N (2C) 3z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not C
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"   shows z>=3
        when  z is H | z is S
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1
# The cue-bid: a four-card major, else 3NT with a club stopper, else 3♦.
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3H  "Four hearts"                         shows H>=4
  3S  "Four spades, not four hearts"        shows S>=4, H<=3
  3N  "No four-card major, a club stopper"  shows H<=3, S<=3, stop(C)
  3D  "No four-card major, no club stopper" shows H<=3, S<=3
      priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3M (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  4M  "Game in the fit"                     shows M>=4
  3S  "Four spades, not four hearts"        shows S>=4
      when  M is H
  3N  "No fit: game in notrump"
      priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3H (P) 3S (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  4S  "Four spades too: game in the fit"    shows S>=4
  3N  "Game in notrump"                     priority -1
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3D (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  3N  "Game in notrump"
after 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3N (P) | 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3H (P) 3N (P) | 1N (2C) 3C (P) 3S (P) 3N (P) when !vs_2c
  P   "No further bid"

# They raised their clubs: compete in partner's major with four, accept
# the invitation with a maximum, otherwise pass.
after 1N (2C) 2M (3C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3M  "Four-card support: competing"   shows M>=4
  P   "No further bid"            priority -5
after 1N (2C) 2N (3C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            priority -5
# Any other raise of their clubs over partner's two-level call, and
# their next club bid after we compete: we have said what we have.
after 1N (2C) 2z (3C) | 1N (2C) 2z (4C) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  P   "No further bid"   priority -10
after 1N (2C) 2M (3C) 3M (4C) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  P   "No further bid"         priority -10

# Responder passed: with two clubs opener reopens with a double (BBA,
# 32 of 32 two-club openers in the vanilla corpus; none with three).
# Responder passes for penalties with four clubs, else names a suit.
after 1N (2C) P (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  X   "Reopening double: two clubs or fewer"   shows C<=2
      priority 1
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) when !vs_2c, rho.C>=5
  P   "Four or more clubs: defends"             shows C>=4
      priority 1
  2N  "8-9 HCP, a club stopper"                 shows hcp>=8, stop(C), H<=3, S<=3
  2H  "Four or more hearts"                     shows H>=4, H>=S
  2S  "Four or more spades"                     shows S>=4, S>H
  2D  "Four or more diamonds"                   shows D>=4
      priority -1
  2D  "Nothing better"                          priority -5
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) 2z (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5, z is not N
  P   "Partner's suit, to play"
after 1N (2C) P (P) X (P) 2N (P) when !vs_2c, lho.C>=5
  3N  "Accepts: a maximum"             shows hcp>=16
      priority 1                       # ahead of one-nt.bid's answer to the invitation
  P   "Declines: a minimum"            shows hcp<=15
      priority 1

# ── Their conventional overcalls (2026-09-28, vs-1nt.notes.md) ───────
# The rules above read 2♦/2♥/2♠ as natural: they apply when the
# overcaller has shown four or more of the suit bid and not both majors.
# The opponents' defence (their card: cappelletti.bid, dont.bid,
# meckwell.bid, multi-landy.bid) can show something else:
#
# - both majors (Cappelletti 2♦, DONT 2♥): the double shows values and
#   says we can defend; a minor at the three level is natural and forcing
#   to game; 3NT is game with both majors held. Afterwards a double of
#   their major is for penalties.
# - an unknown major (Multi-Landy 2♦): the double shows values; 3NT game.
# - their 2♣ is left to the systems-on rules (Stayman by double), and
#   their double to the rules at the top.
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3C  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more clubs"      shows C>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3D  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more diamonds"   shows D>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3N  "Game: 10+, both majors held"                   shows hcp>=10, stop(H), stop(S)
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10
after 1N (2y) when y is not C, (maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                                shows hcp>=10
  P   "No bid over their overcall"
      priority -10

# Responder after a transfer that they interrupted (2026-09-28): with a
# hand no transfer continuation describes (5-4 in the majors and a
# singleton, which uncontested goes through Stayman first) he passes.
# A gap to fill, not a treatment: nt-interference.notes.md.
when answered transfer(M), they.bid
  P   "No further bid"                         priority -10
      when  !passes_out_artificial   # never pass out my own transfer, doubled (base.bid)

# Their relay over our Stayman double (Cappelletti 2♣, X, 2♦): opener
# still shows a major, doubles 2♦ with four of them, else passes.
after 1N (2C) X (2D) when vs_2c
  2H  "4+ hearts"                                shows H>=4
  2S  "4 spades, not 4 hearts"                   shows S>=4, H<=3
  X   "Penalty: four or more diamonds, no major"  shows D>=4, H<=3, S<=3
  P   "No 4-card major"                          shows H<=3, S<=3
      priority -1

# Opener after responder's game-forcing minor over their majors: 3NT,
# the game our side can make with both majors held by one of us.
after 1N (2y) 3z (P) when y is not C, lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4, z is C | z is D
  3N  "Game in notrump"

# Opener after the value-showing double: pass unless they run; a double
# of the suit they run to is for penalties. Responder the same after
# opener's pass: game with 10+ and their suit held.
after 1N (2y) X (P) when y is not C, (lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4) | ((maybe lho.y<=3), (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3))
  P   "Defending their artificial overcall"

# Whatever their overcall, once their advancer bids over our double
# opener has said what he has; the rules above add what he can (a
# penalty double). 2026-09-28: 110 no-rule boards, 1N 2♠ X 2NT and alike.
after 1N (2y) X (*) when !rho.last=P, !rho.last=X
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -10
after 1N (2y) X (2z) when y is not C, (lho.H>=4, lho.S>=4) | ((maybe lho.y<=3), (maybe lho.H<=3) | (maybe lho.S<=3))
  X   "Penalty: four or more {z}"                    shows z>=4
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5
after 1N (2y) X (2z) X (P) when y is not C, (rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4) | ((maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3))
  P   "Partner doubled for penalties: defend"
after 1N (2y) X (2z) P (P) when y is not C, (rho.H>=4, rho.S>=4) | ((maybe rho.y<=3), (maybe rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3))
  X   "Penalty: four or more {z}"                    shows z>=4
  3N  "Game: 10+, {z} held"                          shows hcp>=10, stop(z)
  P   "No further bid"                          priority -5

# ── Their 2NT: both minors (Cappelletti, Meckwell, Multi-Landy) ─────
after 1N (2N)
  X   "Values: 8+ HCP"                shows hcp>=8
  3H  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more hearts"     shows H>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  3S  "Natural, forcing to game: five or more spades"     shows S>=5, points>=10
      sets  forcing=game
  4H  "Game: six or more hearts"                     shows H>=6, hcp>=10
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  4S  "Game: six or more spades"                     shows S>=6, hcp>=10
      when  !texas_1nt
      priority 1
  3N  "Game: 10+ HCP"                                shows hcp>=10
  P   "No bid over their 2NT"
      priority -10
after 1N (2N) 3z (P) when z is H | z is S
  4{z}  "Three-card support: game in the major"      shows z>=3
  3N    "Game in notrump"
        priority -1

# Responder passed their overcall: opener has shown his hand.
after 1N (2y) P (P)
  P   "No further bid"

# ── They preempted over our 1NT (a three-level suit) ─────────────────
# No rule existed (2026-09-25: 1NT (3H) in Basic_NT and What_To_Open).
# Game in notrump with their suit held, four of a five-card major, a
# double with game values and no stopper, short in their suit (opener
# passes it with four of theirs); otherwise pass.
after 1N (3y) when y is not N
  3N  "Game: 9+, a stopper in {y}"         shows hcp>=9, stop(y)
  4H  "Game: five or more hearts, 9+"      shows H>=5, hcp>=9
      when  y is not H, !texas_1nt | y is S   # over 3♣/3♦ 4♥ is Texas
  4S  "Game: five or more spades, 9+"      shows S>=5, hcp>=9
      when  y is not S
  X   "Takeout: 9+, no stopper in {y}"     shows hcp>=9, y<=2
      priority -1
  P   "No bid over their preempt"
      priority -10
after 1N (3y) X (P) when y is not N
  P   "Four of their suit: defends"        shows y>=4
      priority 1
  3N  "A stopper in {y}"                   shows stop(y)
  cheapest(S) "Four or more spades"        shows S>=4   when y is not S
  cheapest(H) "Four or more hearts"        shows H>=4   when y is not H
  cheapest(D) "Four or more diamonds"      shows D>=4   when y is not D
      priority -1
  cheapest(C) "Four or more clubs"         shows C>=4   when y is not C
      priority -1
  3N  "Game in notrump"
      priority -5
after 1N (3y) P (P) when y is not N
  P   "No further bid"
files.rules/notrump/nt-interference.notes.md:
# nt-interference (`nt-interference.bid`): notes

Responder when RHO doubles our 1NT or overcalls 2♣. Cases:
`nt-interference.test`.

This module holds only the calls that exist *because* they bid — the
redouble, the natural escapes, the pass. Stayman, the transfers, Texas
and the natural notrump calls keep their own calls and live in their own
modules, in `after 1N (X)` and `after 1N (2C)` contexts next to the
uncontested ones (`stayman.bid`, `jacoby-transfers.bid`,
`minor-transfers.bid`, `texas-transfers.bid`, `one-nt.bid`).

## The two card switches

`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_double` ("Transfers if RHO doubles") and
`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c` ("Transfers if RHO bids clubs") were both in
the coverage report's *ignored* list: every notrump pattern we had was
`after 1N (P)` or a competitive spelling of it, so a double or a 2♣
overcall switched the whole structure off and responder passed. On the
corpus that was 1,331 decisions after a double and 1,243 after 2♣.

The switches really do change the system, and the corpus lets both
halves be measured: **21GF-DEFAULT** (199 of 342 scenarios) has
`vs_double = 0` and `vs_2c = 1`; **21GF-GIB** and **Basic-Bridge** have
both on.

Note that `after A | B` takes one `when` for the whole line, so the
double and the 2♣ overcall are written as two contexts rather than two
alternatives. That is also what keeps the uncontested
`after 1N (P) | (1x) 1N (P) | …` line — with its
`when !they.bid | systems_on` — untouched.

## Over a double

**Transfers on** (`vs_double`). The 1NT structure is unchanged and
responder is very active. From a 150-board `rbb probe --prefix "1NT X"`
on Basic-Bridge: 2♣ Stayman 42, redouble 48, 2♦/2♥ transfer 35, pass 12.

- 2♣ is **Stayman one point below the uncontested floor** — 7 opposite
  15-17, written `hcp>=24-partner.hcp.max` so it follows the card.
  Finding the 4-4 fit is also somewhere to run to.
- Stayman **denies a five-card major** here, unlike the uncontested 2♣:
  with 5-4 BBA transfers rather than looking for the other major first,
  and with 5-5 it transfers to **spades**. (Uncontested, Stayman keeps
  priority with 5-4 for Smolen.)
- **XX is 6+ HCP with nothing else to say** — partner has 15-17 and they
  have doubled into it, so the hand is ours. BBA passes 0-5 and
  redoubles from 6.

Agreement on the probe: **142/150**.

**Transfers off.** A different game: BBA passes 170 of 252 decisions in
`Opps_Double_1_NT` (21GF-DEFAULT). The two-level calls are natural
escapes — 2♥/2♠ with five, 2♣/2♦ with six — and the cut is **four HCP**:

| escape cap | decisions matched (of 252) |
|---|---|
| 3 | 193 |
| **4** | **205** |
| 5 | 186 |
| 6 | 168 |
| pass everything (before) | 170 |

**There is no redouble in this branch.** BBA redoubles 10 times in 252,
on 6-9 counts that are indistinguishable from the fifty 6-9 counts it
passes, and a `hcp>=6` redouble cost 77 boards on its own (205 → 138).
Passing them is both closer to BBA and the safer bid.

## Over a 2♣ overcall

One structure on every corpus card that sets `vs_2c`, and it is simply
"systems on with the double standing in for 2♣":

- **X is Stayman**, 8+ with a four-card major and no five-card one.
- **2♦ / 2♥ are the transfers**, with a **five-HCP floor**: below that
  BBA leaves their 2♣ alone rather than push to the two level with
  nothing. (Over a double there is no floor — running is the point.)
- **2♠ / 3♣ are the minor transfers**, same floor, same treatment field.
- **2NT is the natural invitation and 3NT the natural game**; 2♣ takes
  neither away.
- **Texas is on**, and over interference it doubles as a preempt: with
  **seven** cards in a major and no values BBA transfers straight to
  game rather than to the two level (`A9.JT87432.2.T65` → 4♦).

Agreement at `1N (2C)`: **45.8% → 87.1%** (571 → 1,086 of 1,247).

## Accepted differences from BBA

- **The 2♣ escape with a long minor over a double, transfers on.** With
  2♣ Stayman and 2♦ a transfer there is nowhere to run, and BBA passes.
  So do we. A card with minor transfers on would want `2♠`/`3♣` here;
  not written.
- **Stayman over 2♣ with game values.** BBA's X is 8-9 only: with 10+
  and a four-card major it bids 3NT and never looks for the 4-4 fit.
  We keep `strength>=invite`, so we double with game values too. It
  costs 11 boards of agreement and looks like better bridge; flagged
  for Rick.
- **Super-accepts are not written for these auctions.** Opener simply
  completes the transfer.
- **BBA's 2NT over a double** (8-9 balanced, `vs_double` off) is bid on
  two boards and passed on fifty like it; not written.

## Measured effect (2026-09-23)

At the two decisions: `1N (X)` 59.8% → 76.3% (798 → 1,018 of 1,334),
`1N (2C)` 45.8% → 87.1% (571 → 1,086 of 1,247). The scenarios that
moved most are Lebensohl (+212 calls), Suction (+155), Cappelletti
(+148), Mitchell_Stayman (+118 calls, +71 contracts), Opps_Double_1_NT
(+105) and Exit_Transfers (+105) — all of them scenarios built around
an action over 1NT.

## Gaps and open questions

- **Opener after the interference.** `1N (X) XX (2y)` and the rest of
  the auctions where they bid again have no rules: opener passes.
- **Lebensohl** (`notrump.lebensohl.play`) is on for
  21GF-DEFAULT and is not built. That is the structure over a 2♦ or
  higher overcall of our 1NT, which is untouched here: only 2♣ and the
  double are covered, because those are the two the card switches name.
- **Runout / exit transfers over the double.** The remaining
  disagreements at `1N (X)` are dominated by cards that play something
  else again: "BBA 2♠, ours P" 56 boards and "BBA 3♣, ours P" 46 come
  from the Exit_Transfers and Runout_after_1N_X scenarios, which are
  treatments we have no field for.
- **Their double is not interpreted.** We have no rule for a double of
  a 1NT opening, so the engine does not know it shows 15+ (BBA calls it
  "Cappelletti, strong" on these cards). The redouble's 6-HCP floor is
  therefore a flat number rather than a count of the deck.

## Length points (2026-09-23)

- `AT9.J6.K2.976532` over their 2♣ (Cappelletti, any six-card suit;
  Opps_Double_1_NT) is now 8 HCP + ½ + 2 = 10½, game, and bids 3NT; BBA
  transfers to clubs (2♠). Accepted: by Rick's count it is a game hand.
  On that one board 3NT takes 7 tricks double-dummy, and BBA's auction
  ended in 3♦X by West, one down — a single board, not evidence either
  way. The minor transfer case moved to
  `AT9.J6.Q2.976532` (9½).
- The Texas preempt over 2♣ (`A9.JT87432.2.T65`) now reads
  `suit_strength=signoff`, see `texas-transfers.notes.md`.

## Their natural 2♦/2♥/2♠ overcall (2026-09-25)

Since our East-West overcall 1NT naturally (overcalls.bid, "Over their
1NT, natural"), boards that BBA bid N/S alone now reach 1NT-(2x), and
three seats had no rule: responder, the advancer, and opener in the
pass-out seat (20 of the 110 remaining no-rule positions in Basic_* N/S).

**Decision: add simple natural rules** rather than leave the seats
empty. BBA on the Basic card (`probes/nt-2D-resp.toml`,
`nt-2H-resp.toml`, `nt-2S-resp.toml`, 250 random responders each):

| call | BBA's meaning (its own `--all-meanings`) |
|---|---|
| X | negative: 5+, four cards in an unbid major (over 2♠ 4-6 hearts) |
| 2♥/2♠ | natural, to play, 4-9 |
| 3♣/3♦/3♥ (non-jump) | natural, 5+, 9-13, forcing |
| 2NT | 8-9 |
| 3NT | 9-15, no stopper required (3NT on a diamond void over 2♦) |
| 4♥/4♠ | six cards, game |
| Pass | 0-8 |

Our rules follow that, in HCP where BBA's boundaries are HCP-like; with
a five-card major and game values over 2♦/2♥ we bid 3NT as BBA does
rather than jump. Agreement on the grids: 83-87%; most of the rest is
2NT or 3NT with 9. Opener answers the double with a four-card major,
2NT with a stopper, a pass with four of their suit, or a four-card
minor; responder then bids game with 10+, invites with 8-9. Opener
raises a three-level major with three, else 3NT; passes a two-level
suit; accepts 2NT with 16-17.

The advancer (partner of the 1NT overcaller) passes. Competitive raises
(three-card support, 6-10) were tried: -26 IMPs to the advancing side
over the corpus, par distance neutral, so they were dropped.

**Measured**, both yardsticks, as the competitive-yardstick rule asks:
full corpus +188 IMPs by par distance and +170 to the side that changed
its call (74 boards); Basic_* N/S flat (8 boards, -4 / -6). No-rule
positions in Basic_* N/S 110 -> 87.

## Their preempt over our 1NT (2026-09-25)

1NT (3x) had no rules (Basic_NT and Basic_What_To_Open, 7 positions
with the follow-ups). Now: 3NT with 9+ and a stopper, four of a five-
card major with 9+, a takeout double with 9+ short in their suit (opener
defends with four of theirs, else 3NT with a stopper or a four-card
suit), otherwise pass. BBA's calls in the corpus: pass, 3NT and one
double. Full corpus: 1NT (3♦) +105, (3♣) +90, (3♥) +80 by side, part of
a +189 / +262 change with the fallbacks below.

## Their conventional defences (2026-09-28)

The opponents' calls over our 1NT are now read with their card's defence
(`competitive.vs_1nt_strong.system`: cappelletti.bid, dont.bid,
meckwell.bid, multi-landy.bid; vs-1nt.notes.md). 21GF-GIB, the EW card
of 316 scenarios, plays Cappelletti, so from now on EW double 1NT with
15+, bid 2♣ with a one-suiter, 2♦ with the majors and so on, where
before they passed every hand. What changed here:

- **The natural-overcall rules** (`after 1N (2y)` and their
  continuations) now apply only when the overcaller has shown four or
  more of the suit bid and not both majors: `rho.y>=4, (maybe
  rho.H<=3) | (maybe rho.S<=3)` (`lho.` from opener's seat). Cappelletti
  2♥/2♠ (five of the major and a minor), Meckwell 2♥/2♠, DONT 2♦ and 2♠
  pass; Cappelletti 2♦ and DONT 2♥ (both majors) do not.
- **Both majors shown** (Cappelletti 2♦, DONT 2♥): X shows 8+ HCP and
  says we can defend; 3♣/3♦ natural and forcing to game (opener bids
  3NT); 3NT with both majors held. When they run, a double is for
  penalties (four of the suit), and opener leaves a penalty double in.
- **An unknown major** (Multi-Landy 2♦): X values, 3NT game.
- **Their 2NT** (minors): X values; 3♥/3♠ natural and forcing, four of
  a major with six; 3NT with 10+; opener raises a major with three.
- **Their 2♣ relay over our Stayman double** (Cappelletti 2♣ X 2♦):
  opener still shows a major, doubles 2♦ with four and no major.
- **Their penalty double**: opener passes partner's escape
  (`vs_double` off), passes a redouble left in, and after our redouble
  and their run leaves it to responder, who doubles with four of their
  suit or 9+.
- After a transfer they interrupted, a responder with no continuation
  (5-4 in the majors with a singleton, which goes through Stayman
  uncontested) passes: a fallback, not a treatment.

These took the no-rule positions they had caused (821 more at the first
run) back below the baseline (2,835 before, 2,795 after). Still open:
Lebensohl (on for 21GF-DEFAULT) over their two-level calls; a cue-bid
structure over Landy/Multi-Landy 2♣ (we keep Stayman by double);
opener's rebids when their advancer bids over our double (a pass).

## Their natural 2♣, transfers off (2026-09-30)

With `notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c` off (the vanilla SAYC card; no stock
corpus card) nothing applied after a natural 2♣: the 2♦/2♥/2♠ rules are
gated `y is not C` and the 2♣ systems-on rules need the switch. On the
95,558 vanilla SAYC deals that was 156 no-rule boards at `1NT (2C)` and
54 more at `1NT (2C) 2NT (P)`.

The rules apply only when the 2♣ showed five or more clubs
(`rho.C>=5`): DONT and Meckwell 2♣ promise only four, Cappelletti's 2♣
an unknown suit, Landy the majors, so their 2♣ is untouched (a test
holds this for Cappelletti on 21GF-DEFAULT).

**What BBA plays** (bare SAYC, `probes/nt-2C-nat-resp.toml`, 400 random
responders, with BBA's own meanings from the grid's `bba_alert`):

| call | BBA |
|---|---|
| X | never bid (0 of 400; 0 of 270 in the vanilla corpus): no negative double |
| 2♦/2♥/2♠ | five or more, "4 to 9 total points", to play |
| 2NT | 8-9, a club stopper |
| 3NT | 9-15, a club stopper |
| 3♦ | five or more diamonds, 9-13 |
| 4♥/4♠ | six or more, "6 to 13 total points" |
| 3♣ | artificial, two 16-counts |
| Pass | 0-9, but also 10-16 counts with no club stopper (QT.Q862.AKQ8.Q95, 15, passes) and long clubs |

Opener (vanilla corpus): after responder's pass he **reopens with a
double holding two clubs** (32 of 32 two-club hands; never with three),
and responder passes it with four or more clubs or names a four-card
suit. After 2NT he bids 3NT with 16 (2 of 2) and passes 15 (4 of 4).
After a two-level suit he passes; after 3♦ he bids 3NT.

**Ours.** BBA's low end, as it is: two-level suits from 4 HCP and at
most 9 points, 2NT 8-9 with a club stopper, 3NT from 10 with one, a weak
hand with a four-card major passes and relies on the reopening double,
and the reopening double itself. BBA's high end we do not copy: it has
no forcing call short of game, so it passes or bids a non-forcing 2♠
with 13-16 counts. Ours, standard practice rather than BBA:

- a five-card suit at the three level forces to game (3♦ non-jump, 3♥/3♠
  jumps); opener raises a major with three, else 3NT;
- **3♣ cue-bid: Stayman, forcing to game**, with a four-card major or
  without a club stopper. Opener shows a four-card major (hearts first),
  else 3NT with a club stopper, else 3♦; responder raises a fit, shows
  four spades over 3♥, else 3NT;
- four of a major with six cards and 9+ points (BBA from about 6-7 HCP;
  our cut is a judgment call, between BBA's and the natural block's 10);
- when they raise clubs over a two-level call opener competes in a major
  with four and accepts 2NT with 16-17; otherwise passes.

**Measured** (baseline main 16e3f68, same binary):

| set | vs BBA before | after | no-rule before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla SAYC (95,558) | -42,209 | -42,106 (+103) | 1,641 | 1,425 |
| PBS corpus | -93,855 | -93,855 | 2,607 | 2,607 |
| 21GF random | -43,948 | -43,948 | 1,378 | 1,378 |

Calls agreeing on vanilla 798,209 → 798,399. The corpus and the 21GF set
do not move: every card there keeps `vs_2c` on or plays an artificial
2♣. `sideimps.py` on the vanilla runs: 266 boards changed, **+548 IMPs
to the side that changed its call**, +103 by par distance. By call:

| change | boards | side IMPs | par distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| opener's reopening double (P → X) | 53 | +172 | -90 |
| responder's 2♦/2♥/2♠ (from pass, 2NT or a 3-level preempt) | 136 | +190 | +12 |
| 2NT / 3NT / 3♣ / three-level suits / 4M | 66 | +182 | +168 |
| opener accepts 2NT (P → 3NT) | 11 | +4 | +13 |

The yardsticks disagree on the **reopening double** (and, mildly, on
the two-level diamonds: +58 side, -45 par): it often ends in 2♣ doubled
beaten by more than our par contract, or pushes them, which par distance
counts as a loss. It is the competitive call the side yardstick exists
for, and BBA's call. **Rick, 2026-09-30: keep it.**

Still open: a weak six-card major (5-6 HCP) bids 2♥/2♠ where BBA jumps
to game; a five-card major with 9 HCP and 10 points forces with 3♥ where
BBA bids 3NT (5 boards, -9).


## The answer to 2NT outranks one-nt.bid's (2026-10-03)

After 1NT (2♣/2♦/...) 2NT, opener's "Accepts: a maximum" (16+) and
"Declines: a minimum" (15-) here and one-nt.bid's general answer to
`asked nt_invite` (by strength) are candidates for the same calls at
the same priority, so descriptiveness chose between them. With the
engine's narrower knowledge of opener (2026-10-03) the general Pass
measured 0.445 against this 3NT's 0.435 and 16 HCP declined (the test
at 1NT (2C) 2NT). These pairs are now priority 1: the specific answer
to the invitation over their interference comes first.

## Sources

- **The structure over interference:** standard practice, not yet cited
  (Stayman by double and transfers over 2♣ follow the card's switches,
  BBA's play on every corpus card that sets them). Over a natural 2♣
  with the switch off: natural two-level suits to play, the cue-bid as
  game-forcing Stayman, three-level suits forcing: standard practice,
  not yet cited; the reopening double with shortness in their suit is
  BBA's (vanilla corpus).
- **BBA probes:** `rbb probe --prefix "1NT X"` on Basic-Bridge (not kept);
  `probes/nt-2D-resp.toml`, `nt-2H-resp.toml`, `nt-2S-resp.toml` (natural
  2♦/2♥/2♠, Basic-Bridge); `probes/nt-2C-nat-resp.toml` (natural 2♣,
  bare SAYC), meanings from the grid's `bba_alert`.
- **Corpus measurements:** Opps_Double_1_NT (escape cut), the full corpus
  (2026-09-23, -25, -28), the vanilla SAYC random set (2026-09-30).
- **Where we differ from BBA:** Stayman over 2♣ with game values; game
  forcing calls over a natural 2♣ where BBA passes or bids 2♠; 4♥/4♠ with
  six from 9 points ("Accepted differences", the 2026-09-30 section).
- **2026-10-03:** priority of the 2NT answers, nt-interference.test
  (1NT 2C 2NT P, transfers off).

files.rules/notrump/nt-splinter.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Splinters over 1NT (nt-splinter.notes.md): 1NT–3♦ with
# `notrump.three_d_response = splinter`, 1NT–3♥/3♠ with
# `notrump.three_major_splinter`. The bid suit is a singleton or void,
# with four or more in each other suit (4-4-4-1, 5-4-4-0 and alike,
# no five-card major) and game values; not with a singleton A, K or Q
# (BBA bids Stayman with those). Opener bids game in a four-card
# major he shares, else 3NT.

module nt-splinter "Splinters over 1NT"
  kind   convention
  needs  notrump-base
  param  three_d  = notrump.three_d_response default natural
  param  major_splinter = notrump.three_major_splinter default false

after 1N (P)
  3D  "Splinter: 0-1 ♦, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows D<=1, !has(A,D), !has(K,D), !has(Q,D), H=4, S=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  three_d is splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2                           # ahead of Stayman
  3H  "Splinter: 0-1 ♥, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows H<=1, !has(A,H), !has(K,H), !has(Q,H), S=4, D>=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  major_splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2
  3S  "Splinter: 0-1 ♠, 4+ in each other suit, game values"  alert
      shows S<=1, !has(A,S), !has(K,S), !has(Q,S), H=4, D>=4, C>=4, strength>=game
      when  major_splinter
      sets  forcing=game, ask=nt_splinter
      artificial
      priority 2

when asked nt_splinter
  4S  "Four spades: game in the fit"        shows S>=4
      when  partner.last=3D | partner.last=3H
      sets  trump=S
  4H  "Four hearts: game in the fit"        shows H>=4, S<=3 | partner.last=3S
      when  partner.last=3D | partner.last=3S
      sets  trump=H
  3N  "No major fit: 3NT"
      priority -1

# nt-splinter (`nt-splinter.bid`): notes

Splinters over 1NT: 1NT–3♦ with `notrump.three_d_response = splinter`
(BBA "1N-3D splinter"), 1NT–3♥/3♠ with `notrump.three_major_splinter`
("1N-3M splinter"); both on for 21GF-GIB. Cases: `nt-splinter.test`.

## What is played (2026-10-05)

The splinter suit is a singleton or void, the other three suits are
four or more each with no five-card major (4-4-4-1, 4-4-5-0, ...), and
game values. It outranks Stayman. Opener bids four of a major he holds
four of (spades first over 3♦), else 3NT. Nothing is written for slam:
responder passes the game (slam/ may add a try later).

**Not with a singleton A, K or Q.** The PBS NT_Splinter text says GIB
splinters with one; BBA does not (it bids 2♣ Stayman: 20 boards in 100),
and the standard advice is the same (an honour singleton is a stopper
for notrump, not shortness to show). We follow BBA.

## Scenario check (2026-10-05)

`compare NT_Splinter --limit 100`, responder's call over 1NT and
opener's answer: **24 → 162 of 166**.

## Sources

- PBS `btn/NT_Splinter.btn` chat text (shape and strength: a stiff or
  void, four in each other suit, 12+ total points).
- BBA's own auctions in `bba/NT_Splinter.pbn` (black box): the
  singleton honour exception and opener's answers.
- Standard practice for the stiff-honour exception, not yet cited.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.

module notrump-base "1NT opening and natural responses"
  kind   system
  needs  base
  skill  basic_bidding/notrump_openings
  skill  partnership_bidding/basic_notrump
  param  nt_min   = notrump.one_nt.range_min default 15
  param  nt_max   = notrump.one_nt.range_max default 17
  param  nt_min_plus  = notrump.one_nt.range_min_plus default false
  param  nt_max_minus = notrump.one_nt.range_max_minus default false
  param  alt_min  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_min
  param  alt_max  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_max
  param  alt_min_plus  = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_min_plus default false
  param  alt_max_minus = notrump.one_nt_alt.range_max_minus default false
  param  alt_where = notrump.one_nt_alt.seat_vul
  param  one_less = notrump.one_nt.allow_one_less default false
  param  minors   = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:style default relay
  param  mtp      = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:over_1nt default true
  param  three_c_transfer = bidding_conventions/minor_suit_transfers:three_c_diamonds default false
  param  three_d  = notrump.three_d_response default natural
  param  systems_on = nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on default true
  param  vs_2c   = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:vs_2c default false
  param  style   = general.style
  param  five_major = notrump.one_nt.five_card_major default sometimes
  param  jacoby  = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers default true
  param  puppet_1nt = bidding_conventions/puppet_stayman:over_1nt default false
  param  allow_5422 = notrump.one_nt.allow_5422 default false
  param  allow_4441 = notrump.one_nt.allow_4441 default false

# ── Systems on (Rick, 2026-10-05) ────────────────────────────────────
# One notion: partner's last call is a natural notrump showing a
# balanced range, and our notrump system answers it at that level: at
# 1NT the two-level structure (Stayman, transfers, ...), at 2NT the
# three-level one (two-nt-responses.bid, two-nt-minors.bid). Each piece
# only as the card plays it. Opener's range is whatever the auction
# showed (1NT 15-17, 2NT 20-21, 2♣–2♦–2NT 22-23, Kokish 24-25, a 1NT
# overcall 15-18 ...), and the responses count strength bands against it.
#
# Where (Rick, 2026-10-05; one-nt.notes.md, "Systems on"): our side has
# not bid a suit naturally before the notrump. Artificial calls do not
# count (2♣ strong, 2♦ waiting, the 2♥ bust, Kokish's relays: rules mark
# them `artificial`), nor do the opponents' calls (2♣ (2♠) P (P) 2NT is
# on). One exception, Rick's list: a positive response to our artificial
# opening (2♣–2♠–2NT, 2♣–2♥–2NT) is on too; BBA's treatment
# (`general.style = bba`) keeps its natural rebids there instead. Not
# when the notrump answers partner's opening (1♥–1NT, 2♣–2NT), or when it
# is our second natural notrump. Our notrump overcall or balancing
# notrump: as the card says (`nt_overcalls.direct.systems_on`).
systems on when call = 1N | call = 2N, maybe shown.balanced, shown.second_longest.min <= 4
  !me.named(C), !me.named(D), !me.named(H), !me.named(S), !me.named(N)
  !partner.opened, !partner.named(N), !(lho.opened | rho.opened) | systems_on
  (me.opened, style is not bba) | (!partner.named(C), !partner.named(D), !partner.named(H), !partner.named(S))

# The 1NT system's ways in (LANGUAGE.md §4, named auction patterns):
# our 1NT where the system came on, RHO passing; with `nt1` also RHO's
# double of our 1NT overcall or balancing 1NT (a double of the 1NT
# opening has its own rules: `after 1N (X)` in stayman.bid and
# jacoby-transfers.bid). A context that starts `after nt1` reaches the
# responses from all of them.
define auction nt1_undoubled = systems 1N (P)
define auction nt1 = nt1_undoubled
  systems 1N (X)   when lho.opened | rho.opened

# The range is in HCP, as BBA plays it (15-17 HCP exactly, whatever the
# tens or length). With the card option "1NT may be 1 HCP light", a hand one
# HCP short opens 1NT when its extras bring it to the range in total points.
# A five-card major only as the card allows (`one_nt.five_card_major`):
# BBA opens 1NT with one only with "1NT opening shape 5 major"; its bare
# SAYC card (probe 2026-09-30) opens the major.
#
# The card's qualifiers (one-nt.notes.md, "Range qualifiers"). A plus on
# the minimum ("14+") is a good 14: the range is judged, in total points,
# so 14 HCP opens only with a point more (a five-card suit, two tens) and,
# the same judgment at the top, a 17 that is worth 18 does not. A minus on
# the maximum ("15-17-", a poor 17) judges the top only. The plus on the
# maximum and the minus on the minimum change nothing: the HCP range
# already takes every hand at those counts. Partner reads the judged range
# (total points 15-17 for "14+-17") and counts against it.
#
# The alternate range (`notrump.one_nt_alt`) is in force where its
# seat/vulnerability text covers the opener's seat and vulnerability
# (`seat_vul`: "Not Vul", "3rd/4th", "NV 1st/2nd"), the main range
# everywhere else. Partner and the opponents read the 1NT by the same
# rules, so every count against opener's range (responses, slam, our
# defence's reading) sees the range in force. The responses are the same
# either way (`one_nt_alt.same_responses`; a separate system for the
# other range is not modelled).
define nt_alt = alt_min is not none, alt_max is not none, seat_vul(alt_where)
define nt_main_range = hcp=nt_min..nt_max, points>=nt_min+1 | !nt_min_plus, points<=nt_max | !(nt_min_plus | nt_max_minus)
define nt_alt_range = hcp=alt_min..alt_max, points>=alt_min+1 | !alt_min_plus, points<=alt_max | !(alt_min_plus | alt_max_minus)
# Opener has shown more than the 1NT range in force (a 2NT, 2♣ then
# notrump): the quantitative answers below.
define above_1nt = (!nt_alt, shown.hcp.min>=nt_max+1) | (nt_alt, shown.hcp.min>=alt_max+1)
# A weak notrump in force (the range in force tops at 14 or less: Rick's
# 11+-14 not vulnerable). Opener's balanced hands too strong for it open
# a suit, and the rebids show them (Rick, 2026-11-07; rebids.bid, "With
# a weak notrump"): after a one-level response 1NT from the top of the
# range up to 17 (`above_weak_nt`: a good 14 to 17 opposite 11+-14),
# 2NT 18-19; after a 2/1 the jump to 3NT the same, 2NT 12-14 or 18+.
# The opener's own seat and vulnerability decide it (`seat_vul` reads
# the actor).
define weak_nt = (!nt_alt, nt_max <= 14) | (nt_alt, alt_max <= 14)
# The top of the weak range judged out of it (a 14 worth 15 total points
# where the range is "11+-14", one-nt.notes.md "Range qualifiers")
# belongs with the hands above the range. Partner reads the 14 in: a
# 14-17 reading measured better than 15-17 (rebids.notes.md).
define weak_nt_top_out = (!nt_alt, hcp=nt_max, points>=nt_max+1) | (nt_alt, hcp=alt_max, points>=alt_max+1)
define above_weak_nt = (!nt_alt, hcp>=nt_max+1, hcp<=17) | (nt_alt, hcp>=alt_max+1, hcp<=17) | weak_nt_top_out
when opening, !nt_alt
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows hcp=nt_min-1, points>=nt_min, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
      when one_less
  # The card's shape options (one-nt.notes.md, "5-4-2-2 and 4-4-4-1").
  # 5-4-2-2 with a five-card minor and four hearts or four of the other
  # minor, both doubletons headed by the ace or king (BBA: never with
  # four spades, always with both doubletons stopped). 4-4-4-1 only with
  # a singleton ace or king.
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, 5-4-2-2"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, shape 5-4-2-2, C=5 | D=5, S=2, H>=2, D>=2, C>=2, has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=3 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=3 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=3 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_5422
  1N  "Notrump opening: {nt_min}-{nt_max} HCP, 4-4-4-1"  announce "{nt_min} to {nt_max}"
      shows nt_main_range, shape 4-4-4-1, S>=2 | has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=2 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=2 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=2 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_4441
# The alternate range, where it is in force: the same rules on its range.
when opening, nt_alt
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, balanced"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, balanced, five_major is not never | (H<=4, S<=4)
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, 5-4-2-2"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, shape 5-4-2-2, C=5 | D=5, S=2, H>=2, D>=2, C>=2, has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=3 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=3 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=3 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_5422
  1N  "Notrump opening: {alt_min}-{alt_max} HCP, 4-4-4-1"  announce "{alt_min} to {alt_max}"
      shows nt_alt_range, shape 4-4-4-1, S>=2 | has(A,S) | has(K,S), H>=2 | has(A,H) | has(K,H), D>=2 | has(A,D) | has(K,D), C>=2 | has(A,C) | has(K,C)
      when allow_4441

# Responder. Strength bands are total points measured against opener's
# range, so they follow the card: with 15-17, invite is 8-9 and game 10-15.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  6N  "To play: slam values"
      shows balanced, points>=32-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # with five, transfer first
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, points<=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is not bba
      sets  ask=quant
      # Rick: 17 opposite 15-17 jumps to 6NT (BBA: 10 of 12 hands; 16
      # mostly invites). BBA's choices at 16-17 do not follow controls.
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows strength=game, H<=4, S<=4                   # with five, transfer first
      when  style is not bba
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5     # a long suit has its own route
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), style is not bba   # 2NT is a transfer
      when  !(mtp, minors is two_nt_three_c)                # 2NT is a transfer
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points, a long minor"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, (C>=6 | D>=6)
      when  !mtp | minors is relay         # no minor route for invitations
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  # A slam try in the minor: six cards, or five in an unbalanced hand
  # (2026-09-27: 15-18 counts with a five-card minor bid 3NT opposite
  # 15-17; a nine-card fit makes slam double dummy 72% of the time at 29
  # HCP between the hands, an eight-card fit 71% at 30).
  3C  "Slam try: six or more clubs, or five and unbalanced"
      shows C>=6 | (C>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  !three_c_transfer, !(mtp, minors is bba), !puppet_1nt
  3D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds, or five and unbalanced"
      shows D>=6 | (D>=5, !balanced), strength>=slam_invite, H<=4, S<=4
      when  three_d is natural
  3N  "No better call: {game} total points or more"
      shows strength>=game
      priority -5                      # a strong hand never passes 1NT
  P   "No game interest: {signoff} total points"
      shows strength=signoff
      when  style is not bba
      priority -10                     # only if nothing else fits

  # The BBA treatment (probed 2026-09-24, one-nt.notes.md). Total points
  # are HCP + ½ per ten (the `bba` valuation), with two exceptions: with
  # 4-4 in the minors the tens do not count, and 8 HCP 4-3-3-3 without a
  # ten passes. At IMPs game comes a point earlier (9 opposite 15-17).
  # The slam invitation needs 16 HCP: 15 and tens bids 3NT.
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite, hcp>=33-partner.hcp.max, points<=31-partner.hcp.min, H<=4, S<=4
      when  style is bba
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, bba_nt_game_points>=10, strength<=game
      when  matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
  3N  "To play: game values"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, bba_nt_imp_game_points>=10, strength<=game
      when  imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
  # Opposite a 1NT that is not 15-17 (Precision, our 1NT overcall), the
  # earlier rules, measured against partner's range: the counts below were
  # fitted opposite 15-17.
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (strength=game, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=32-partner.hcp.max)
      when  matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
  3N  "To play: game values"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, (points>=24-partner.hcp.min, points<=32-partner.hcp.max, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=24-partner.hcp.min, hcp<=32-partner.hcp.max)
      when  imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, (strength=invite, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5, !shape 4333 | hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max | hcp>=26-partner.hcp.max | has(T,S) | has(T,H) | has(T,D) | has(T,C)) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.min)
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, (points>=25-partner.hcp.max, points<=23-partner.hcp.min, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5, !shape 4333 | hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max | hcp>=26-partner.hcp.max | has(T,S) | has(T,H) | has(T,D) | has(T,C)) | (C=4, D=4, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=23-partner.hcp.min)
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  P   "No game interest"
      shows (strength=signoff, C<=3 | D<=3 | C>=5 | D>=5) | (C=4, D=4, hcp<=24-partner.hcp.max) | (shape 4333, hcp>=25-partner.hcp.max, hcp<=25-partner.hcp.max, !has(T,S), !has(T,H), !has(T,D), !has(T,C))
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min<=14 | partner.hcp.max>=18
      priority -10
  # At matchpoints BBA's lines between pass, 2NT and 3NT are its own
  # counts (bba_nt_points, bba_nt_game_points: one-nt.notes.md, "BBA's
  # count"): shape-dependent weights, a ten worth 0-0.9, a doubleton major
  # without A or K charged. Calibrated opposite 15-17.
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, bba_nt_points>=8, bba_nt_game_points<=9, points>=25-partner.hcp.max
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), matchpoints
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  2N  "Invitational"
      shows H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5, bba_nt_imp_points>=8, bba_nt_imp_game_points<=9, points>=24-partner.hcp.max
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed), imps
      when  style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  P   "No game interest"
      shows bba_nt_points<=7
      when  matchpoints, style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      priority -10
  P   "No game interest"
      shows bba_nt_imp_points<=7
      when  imps, style is bba, partner.hcp.min>=15, partner.hcp.max<=17
      priority -10

# Natural major-suit responses when the card plays no transfers
# (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.play` off; one-nt.notes.md, "Natural majors
# without transfers", probes/nt-van-*.toml). 2M is to play with five or
# more and no game interest; 3M is five or more and game values, forcing:
# opener raises to 4M with three or more, else bids 3NT. With 5-5 the
# higher suit. 5-4 in the majors goes through Stayman (stayman.bid), and
# bids 3M over the 2♦ denial.
after nt1 when !they.bid | systems_on
  3S  "Five or more spades, game forcing"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, strength>=game
      when  !jacoby
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(S)
  3H  "Five or more hearts, game forcing"
      shows H>=5, H>S, strength>=game
      when  !jacoby
      sets  forcing=game, ask=choose_game(H)
  4S  "To play: seven or more spades, short of a game force"
      shows S>=7, S>=H, strength=invite
      when  !jacoby
      priority 1                       # ahead of the invitational Stayman (stayman.bid)
  4H  "To play: seven or more hearts, short of a game force"
      shows H>=7, H>S, strength=invite
      when  !jacoby
      priority 1
  2S  "To play: five or more spades, no game interest"
      shows S>=5, S>=H, strength=signoff | (strength=invite, hcp<=6)
      when  !jacoby
  2H  "To play: five or more hearts, no game interest"
      shows H>=5, H>S, strength=signoff | (strength=invite, hcp<=6)
      when  !jacoby

# Opener after the signoff: pass (BBA passed 641 of 642 on the vanilla set).
after nt1 2H (P) | nt1 2S (P) when !jacoby
  P   "Partner's signoff"

# Opener chooses the game: four of the major with three or more (an
# eight-card fit), 3NT with two, whatever the strength (BBA, every one of
# 800 probe hands: probes/nt-van-3h-opener.toml, nt-van-3s-opener.toml).
when asked choose_game(M)
  4M  "Three or more {M}: game in the fit"   shows M>=3
  3N  "Two {M}: 3NT"                         shows M<=2

# Responder after the choice: with six, 3NT goes back to the major (an
# eight-card fit again); slam values bid it.
when answered choose_game(M), partner.last=3N
  6M  "Slam: six or more {M}, slam values"   shows M>=6, strength>=slam
  6N  "Slam values, no fit"                  shows M<=5, strength>=slam
  4N  "Quantitative, no fit"                 shows M<=5, balanced, strength=slam_invite
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      sets  ask=quant
  4M  "Six or more {M}: game in the fit"     shows M>=6, strength<=slam_invite
  P   "No fit: play 3NT"                     shows M<=5, strength<=slam_invite
when answered choose_game(M), partner.last=4{M}
  6M  "Slam in the fit"                      shows strength>=slam
  # The same slam, counting shortness (support points).
  6M  "Slam in the fit"  shows tp(M)>=33-partner.points.min
  P   "Game in the fit"                      shows strength<=slam_invite
      priority -1

# Opener answers the natural 3m slam try (six of the minor, slam-invite
# values): slam with a fit and a maximum, else 3NT (it had no rule;
# Basic_What_To_Open 320).
after 1N (P) 3C (P) when !three_c_transfer, !(mtp, minors is bba), !puppet_1nt
  6C  "Accepts: a club fit and a maximum"   shows C>=3, hcp>=17
  4C  "A club fit, not a maximum: responder decides"   shows C>=3, hcp<=16
      sets  trump=C, forcing=game
  3N  "Declines: no club fit"               shows C<=2
after 1N (P) 3D (P) when three_d is natural
  6D  "Accepts: a diamond fit and a maximum"   shows D>=3, hcp>=17
  4D  "A diamond fit, not a maximum: responder decides"   shows D>=3, hcp<=16
      sets  trump=D, forcing=game
  3N  "Declines: no diamond fit"               shows D<=2
# Responder after the answer: with the fit known, slam from 17 total
# points (32+ between the hands); without it, 6NT only with slam values.
after 1N (P) 3C (P) 4C (P) | 1N (P) 3D (P) 4D (P)
  6{trump} "Slam in the fit: 17+"          shows points>=17
  5{trump} "Game in the fit"               shows points<=16
after 1N (P) 3C (P) 3N (P) | 1N (P) 3D (P) 3N (P)
  6N  "No fit, but slam values: {slam} total points"   shows strength>=slam
  P   "No fit: 3NT"
      priority -5

# Opener answers the invitation: accept only when game is certain (17
# opposite 8-9). With a 4-4 major fit found through Stayman, play there.
when asked nt_invite
  4H  "Accepts, in the 4-4 heart fit"   shows H>=4, strength>=game    when partner.H>=4
  4S  "Accepts, in the 4-4 spade fit"   shows S>=4, strength>=game    when partner.S>=4
  3H  "Declines, in the 4-4 heart fit"  shows H>=4, strength<=invite  when partner.H>=4
  3S  "Declines, in the 4-4 spade fit"  shows S>=4, strength<=invite  when partner.S>=4
  3N  "Accepts the invitation"          shows strength>=game
  P   "Declines: not a maximum"         shows strength<=invite

# Responder after a decline in the fit: the invitation was answered.
# (bba: over 3S responder bids game with the top of the invitation;
# stayman.bid.)
when answered nt_invite, partner.last=3H | partner.last=3S, style is not bba
  P   "Partner declined: play three of the major"

# Opener answers the quantitative 4NT: slam with 32 combined.
when asked quant
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows points>=32-partner.points.min
      when  style is not bba | above_1nt
  P   "Declines: not enough for slam"   shows points<=31-partner.points.min
      when  style is not bba | above_1nt
  # BBA, over its 1NT: 17 HCP accepts, 16 declines whatever its tens
  # (1N_Balanced_Raise, Basic_NT).
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation"     shows hcp>=33-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba, !above_1nt
  P   "Declines: not enough for slam"   shows hcp<=32-partner.hcp.min
      when  style is bba, !above_1nt

# Responder over a 2♣ overcall of our 1NT, when the card keeps the
# structure on (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.vs_2c`). The natural notrump calls
# are unchanged — 2♣ takes nothing away from them — and the double
# replaces the 2♣ Stayman call (stayman.bid). BBA plays it this way on
# every card in the corpus that sets the switch.
after 1N (2C) when vs_2c
  6N  "To play: {slam} total points"
      shows balanced, strength=slam, H<=4, S<=4
  4N  "Quantitative: {slam_invite} total points, invites 6NT"
      when  quant_4nt   # slam.quantitative_4nt.play (slam-entry.bid)
      shows balanced, strength=slam_invite
      sets  ask=quant
  3N  "To play: {game} total points"
      shows strength=game, H<=4, S<=4                   # with five, transfer first
  2N  "Invitational: {invite} total points"
      shows strength=invite, H<=4, S<=4, C<=5, D<=5     # a long suit has its own route
      when  !(mtp, minors is four_way), !(mtp, minors is four_way_reversed)
      sets  ask=nt_invite
  3N  "No better call: {game} total points or more"
      shows strength>=game
      priority -5
  P   "No bid over their 2♣"
      priority -10
