# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Reverse Flannery (Dural Bridge, "Flannery and Reverse Flannery";
# Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `Reverse_Flannery`): responder's jumps to
# 2♥ and 2♠ over partner's 1♣/1♦ show five spades and four or five
# hearts, below a game try:
#
#   1m–2♥   5♠ and 4-5♥, 5-8 HCP     (card `two_level.reverse_flannery.two_h`)
#   1m–2♠   5♠ and 4♥, 9-10 HCP      (card `two_level.reverse_flannery.two_s`)
#
# Over 2♥ opener passes or bids 2♠ to play, or asks with 2NT: 3♣ 5-4 and
# 5-6, 3♦ 5-4 and 7-8, 3♥ 5-5 and 5-6, 3♠ 5-5 and 7-8. Both outrank a
# jump shift of either kind. See reverse-flannery.notes.md.

module reverse-flannery "Reverse Flannery"
  kind   convention
  needs  responses
  skill  bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery
  param  rf_2h = bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery:two_h default false
  param  rf_2s = bidding_conventions/reverse_flannery:two_s default false

# Read by responses.bid: a jump Reverse Flannery takes is not a strong jump
# shift, which is only what the jump means when nothing else claims it.
define rf_2h_on = rf_2h
define rf_2s_on = rf_2s

# ── Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P)
  2H  "Reverse Flannery: five spades, four or five hearts, 5-8 HCP"   alert
      shows S=5, H=4..5, hcp=5..8
      when  rf_2h
      priority 2
  2S  "Reverse Flannery: five spades, four hearts, 9-10 HCP"   alert
      shows S=5, H=4, hcp=9..10
      when  rf_2s
      priority 2

# ── Opener after 2♥ (5-8) ────────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P) 2H (P) when rf_2h
  P   "To play in hearts: hearts longer than spades"
      shows H>S, S<=2, hcp<=15
  2S  "To play in spades"
      shows hcp<=15
      priority -1
  3m  "Six or more of my minor: to play"
      shows m>=6, S<=1, H<=2, hcp<=15
  2N  "Asks: which shape and which half of the range?"   alert
      shows hcp>=16
      sets  forcing=round, ask=reverse_flannery
      artificial
      priority 1
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, hcp>=18
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, H>S, hcp>=18
      priority 1

when asked reverse_flannery
  3C  "5-4 in the majors, 5-6 HCP"   shows H=4, hcp<=6   artificial   priority 2
  3D  "5-4 in the majors, 7-8 HCP"   shows H=4, hcp>=7   artificial   priority 2
  3H  "5-5 in the majors, 5-6 HCP"   shows H=5, hcp<=6   priority 2
  3S  "5-5 in the majors, 7-8 HCP"   shows H=5, hcp>=7   priority 2

# Opener places the contract: game with 23 between us counting partner
# at the floor of his answer, else the cheapest call in the better major.
when answered reverse_flannery
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, S>=H | partner.H.max<=4, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, H>S, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: no major fit"   shows S<=2, H<=3, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 23
  P   "Partner's 3♠: play there"
      when  partner.last=3S
  3S  "Sign off in spades"
      when  !partner.last=3S
      priority -1
  4H  "Sign off: hearts are the fit"   shows H>=4, H>S
      when  partner.last=3S
      priority -1

# ── Opener after 2♠ (9-10) ───────────────────────────────────────────
after 1m (P) 2S (P) when rf_2s
  P   "A minimum with two spades: play 2♠"
      shows S=2, hcp<=14
  3S  "Three or more spades, a minimum: invites game"
      shows S>=3, tp(S)<=14
  2N  "Short spades, a minimum: no fit"
      shows S<=1, hcp<=14
      priority -1
  3H  "Four hearts, short spades: to play"
      shows H>=4, S<=1, hcp<=14
  3m  "Six or more of my minor, short spades: to play"
      shows m>=6, S<=1, hcp<=14
  4S  "Game in spades"   shows S>=3, tp(S)>=15
      priority 1
  4H  "Game in hearts"   shows H>=4, S<=2, hcp>=15
      priority 1
  3N  "Game in notrump: no fit"   shows S<=2, H<=3, hcp>=15

# Responder after opener's invitation: game with the top of the range.
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 3S (P) when rf_2s
  4S  "Accepts: 10 HCP"   shows hcp>=10
      priority 1
  P   "Declines: 9 HCP"
      priority 1

# Responder after opener's sign-offs: pass.
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 3x (P) when rf_2s, x is not S
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 1
after 1m (P) 2S (P) 2N (P) when rf_2s
  # Partner is minimum without a fit: 2NT is high enough.
  P   "No game: play 2NT"   shows hcp<=9
      priority 1
  3N  "10 HCP: game"
      priority 1
after 1m (P) 2H (P) 3m (P) | 1m (P) 2H (P) 2S (P) when rf_2h
  P   "No further bid"
      priority 1

# Reverse Flannery: notes

## Decisions

- Responses, not openings: 1m–2♥ (5♠ 4-5♥, 5-8 HCP) and 1m–2♠ (5♠ 4♥,
  9-10), as the Dural Bridge page and the PBS scenario define it. The
  convention-card summary calls it "an opening of 2♥ (or 2♦)"; the card
  fields `two_level.reverse_flannery.two_h/.two_s` come from BBA's
  `Reverse Flannery 2H/2S`, which BBA plays as these responses.
- Priority 2: they outrank the one-level response and any jump shift
  (strong or weak) on the same call.
- Over 2♥ opener passes only with longer hearts and at most two spades,
  else 2♠; 2NT asks from 16; game in a major from 18.
- Over 2♠ (BBA, scenario): pass with two spades and a minimum; 3♠ with
  three or more and a minimum (a game try, responder accepts with 10);
  4♠ with 15 support points.

## BBA (compare Reverse_Flannery --limit 50, 2026-10-05: 92% of calls agree)

- BBA bids 2♠ over 2♥ with three-card hearts too: BBA style.
- Thresholds for 3♠ vs 4♠ over 2♠ differ by a point: don't care.
- The 1m–2♥–3♦ divergences are the opponents' (EW) calls.

## Open questions

- None. The definition now says it is a response to one of a minor, and
  the `two_d` treatment left from the opening is retired (2026-11-14).

## Sources

- Dural Bridge, "Flannery and Reverse Flannery",
  https://duralbridge.com/flannery.ing.htm: the two responses and the 2NT
  ask (3♣/3♦/3♥/3♠). Opener's ranges for game and the 2♠ continuations
  are ours (from the scenario's BBA auctions).
- Practice-Bidding-Scenarios `btn/Reverse_Flannery.btn` and `bba/`.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Defence to their Multi 2♦ (Bridge Bum, "Defense to Multi 2D", option
# 2). Their 2♦ is read with their card: when it is a Multi, the opener
# may hold six hearts or six spades (`maybe lho/rho.H>=6, maybe ...S>=6`;
# `maybe ...D<=3`; a natural weak 2♦ shows six diamonds and Flannery
# five hearts, so neither matches). In the direct seat:
#
#   X     13-15 balanced, or 16+ any shape
#   2♥/2♠ natural, five or more, not forcing
#   2NT   16-18 balanced
#   3♣/3♦ natural, six or more
#   3♥/3♠ natural, six or more, better than a two-level overcall
#
# After (2♦) P (2♥/2♠), pass or correct: a double is takeout of the suit
# bid, other calls natural, 2NT 15-18. Everything else passes. These
# outrank the defence to a natural 2♦ (competitive/vs-preempts.bid).
# See vs-multi.notes.md.

module vs-multi "Defence to a Multi 2♦"
  kind   defence
  needs  base

after (2D) when maybe rho.H>=6, maybe rho.S>=6, maybe rho.D<=3

  2H  "Natural: five or more hearts, not forcing"   shows H>=5, hcp=10..15

  2S  "Natural: five or more spades, not forcing"   shows S>=5, hcp=10..15

# Defence to a Multi 2♦: notes

## Decisions

- Their 2♦ is recognised by what their card made it show: six hearts and
  six spades both possible, and diamonds possibly short. That holds for a
  Multi, and also for any other artificial 2♦ that shows no suit
  (Benjamin's game force, for example); not for a weak 2♦ or Flannery.
- Direct seat (Bridge Bum, option 2): X 13-15 balanced or 16+; 2♥/2♠
  natural 10-15; 2NT 16-18 balanced; 3m natural six+; 3M six+, 13-16.
  Anything else passes (priority 1: above the defence to a natural 2♦).
- Fourth seat after (2♦) P (2♥/2♠): X takeout of the suit bid (13+),
  natural suits, 2NT 15-18. Leaping Michaels 4m is not written.
- Advancer's calls are left to the general competitive modules: they
  read the double as 13+.

## BBA (compare Opps_Multi_2D --limit 50, 2026-10-05: 78% of calls agree)

- BBA's direct 3♦ (a few boards where we double or bid 2NT) and its
  passes with a five-card heart suit and 10-11 HCP: BBA style.

## Sources

- Bridge Bum, "Defense to Multi 2D (B)",
  https://www.bridgebum.com/defense_to_multi_2d_b.php. Point ranges for
  the natural overcalls are ours.

# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# DOPI and ROPI: answering an ace or keycard ask after the opponents
# interfere. The answers keep their steps, the first two replaced:
#
#   they bid a suit (DOPI)    double = first step, pass = second step,
#                             then the next two bids are steps three
#                             and four;
#   they double (ROPI)        redouble = first step, pass = second step,
#                             then 5♣ and 5♦.
#
# So with 1430 a double shows one or four keycards and a pass none or
# three; with standard Blackwood a double shows none or four aces, a pass
# one. The asker then places the contract, and with two keycards (aces)
# missing defends: passes partner's double, or doubles himself over
# partner's pass. Notes: dopi-ropi.notes.md.

module dopi-ropi "DOPI and ROPI: answering an ace or keycard ask over interference"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi
  param  dopi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:dopi default false
  param  ropi   = bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi:ropi default false
  param  depo   = bidding_conventions/depo default false
  param  gstyle = general.style
  param  rkcb   = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard default false
  param  rstyle = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:style default 1430
  param  m0314  = bidding_conventions/roman_keycard:minor_0314 default false

# The first step of the keycard answers is "1 or 4" (1430) unless the
# card plays 0314 (`slam.rkcb.style`), or its `minor_0314` treatment
# applies with a minor as trumps (Rick, 2026-11-09: follow the card's
# keycard order). Shared by rkcb-1430.bid and minorwood.bid.
define kc_first_14(t) = !(rkcb, rstyle is 0314), !m0314 | t is H | t is S

# They bid a suit over the ask, below six (DOPI); they doubled it (ROPI).
# A bid, not a pass, double or redouble: checked first, as only bids can
# be ordered (`<=` on a pass is an error).
define rho_bid = !(rho.last = P), !(rho.last = X), !(rho.last = XX)
define lho_bid = !(lho.last = P), !(lho.last = X), !(lho.last = XX)
define partner_bid = !(partner.last = P), !(partner.last = X), !(partner.last = XX)
define dopi_bid  = rho_bid, rho.last <= 5S
define ropi_dbl  = rho.last = X

# ── Keycards ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

when dopi, !depo, asked keycards(t), dopi_bid
  X   "DOPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  X   "DOPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5

when ropi, asked keycards(t), ropi_dbl
  XX  "ROPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  XX  "ROPI: 0 or 3 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 1 or 4 keycards"              shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial
      when  !kc_first_14(t)
      priority 5
  5C  "ROPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      priority 5
  5D  "ROPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      priority 5

# Steps three and four over their bid: the next two bids.
when dopi, !depo, asked keycards(t)
  5D  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5C
      priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5C
      priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5D
      priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5D
      priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5H
      priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5H
      priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 keycards, no {t} queen"     shows keycards(t)=2, !has(Q,t)   artificial
      when  rho.last = 5S
      priority 5
  6C  "DOPI: 2 keycards and the {t} queen" shows keycards(t)=2, has(Q,t)    artificial
      when  rho.last = 5S
      priority 5

# ── DEPO (`slam.depo`) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Played instead of DOPI: over their suit bid a double shows an even
# number (0, 2 or 4), a pass an odd number (1 or 3), of keycards or aces.
# No steps above: with the values for slam, partner's even or odd and my
# own count decide.
when depo, asked keycards(t), dopi_bid
  X   "DEPO: 0, 2 or 4 keycards"   shows keycards(t) in 0|2|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DEPO: 1 or 3 keycards"       shows keycards(t) in 1|3|5   artificial
      priority 5

when depo, asked aces, dopi_bid
  X   "DEPO: 0, 2 or 4 aces"       shows keycards(N) in 0|2|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DEPO: 1 or 3 aces"           shows keycards(N) in 1|3     artificial
      priority 5

# ── Aces (standard Blackwood) ─────────────────────────────────────────

when dopi, !depo, asked aces, dopi_bid
  X   "DOPI: 0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "DOPI: 1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
      priority 5

when ropi, asked aces, ropi_dbl
  XX  "ROPI: 0 or 4 aces"   shows keycards(N) in 0|4   artificial
      priority 5
  P   "ROPI: 1 ace"         shows keycards(N)=1        artificial
      priority 5
  5C  "ROPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2        artificial
      priority 5
  5D  "ROPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3        artificial
      priority 5

when dopi, !depo, asked aces
  5D  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5C   priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5C   priority 5
  5H  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5D   priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5D   priority 5
  5S  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5H   priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5H   priority 5
  5N  "DOPI: 2 aces"        shows keycards(N)=2   artificial   when rho.last = 5S   priority 5
  6C  "DOPI: 3 aces"        shows keycards(N)=3   artificial   when rho.last = 5S   priority 5

# ── The asker over a DOPI or ROPI answer ─────────────────────────────
#
# Two keycards (aces) missing: defend rather than bid on. Partner's double
# was the answer and also penalty: pass it. Over partner's pass, double.
# Over ROPI's redouble the asker always bids: 4NT redoubled is ours.
# With the values the slam rules of the ask's own module apply.
define kc_two_missing(t) = we.keycards(t).max <= 3

when (dopi | ropi | depo), answered keycards(t), rho.last = P
  P   "Defend doubled: two keycards missing"
      when  partner.last = X, kc_two_missing(t), lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
  # Over partner's pass a count still open ("0 or 3" facing my two) is
  # read low, as the sign-off in rkcb-1430.bid is: partner bids six over
  # the double with the higher count.
  X   "Penalty: two keycards missing"
      when  partner.last = P, we.keycards(t).min <= 3, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      sets  ask=keycard_correct(t)
      priority 5

when (dopi | ropi | depo), answered aces, rho.last = P
  P   "Defend doubled: two aces missing"
      when  partner.last = X, we.keycards(N).max <= 2, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
  X   "Penalty: two aces missing"
      when  partner.last = P, we.keycards(N).max <= 2, lho_bid, lho.last <= 5S
      priority 5
files.rules/slam/dopi-ropi.notes.md:
# dopi-ropi (`dopi-ropi.bid`): notes

Answering an ace or keycard ask after the opponents interfere
(2026-10-05). Gated on `slam.dopi` (they bid a suit) and `slam.ropi`
(they double 4NT). Every PBS card plays both except Basic-Bridge (ROPI
only).

## What the rules do

- **DOPI** (their suit bid over 4NT, up to 5♠): double = the first
  step, pass = the second, the next two bids = steps three and four.
  With 1430 a double is "1 or 4", a pass "0 or 3"; the card's 0314
  treatments swap them as `rkcb-1430.bid` does. Standard Blackwood:
  double 0 or 4 aces, pass 1, then 2 and 3.
- **ROPI** (they double 4NT): redouble = first step, pass = second, 5♣
  and 5♦ steps three and four.
- **The asker** with two keycards (aces) missing defends: passes
  partner's double, or doubles over partner's pass. An open count
  ("0 or 3" facing my two) is read low and the double sets
  `keycard_correct`, so partner bids six with the higher count (as the
  5-level sign-off does). Over ROPI's redouble the asker always bids.
- **Reading 4NT in competition** (`rkcb-1430.bid`, `read_only`): the
  asks there are off once they have bid ("in competition it cost"), so
  BBA's contested 4NT read as nothing and we never answered it. A
  read-only copy now makes it keycard for the suit we play in, and for
  the trump after total-tricks.bid's `ask=signoff` jump to game
  (1H-2NT-(3C)-4H-4NT). We still never ask in competition ourselves.

## Corpus (DOPI_ROPI, Exclusion_*, --limit 50, 21GF cards)

At the answer to BBA's 4NT: 24/36 agreed on DOPI_ROPI before the reading
rules (most misses "no rule" for BBA's contested 4NT), 34/44 over the
three scenarios after. What is left is reading: 4NT after a strong 2♣
and their overcall, and 5♥/5♠ answers where BBA counts the queen
differently. The asker's next call differs mostly outside DOPI: BBA's
5NT king ask (now built), BBA passing a 5♠ answer with a keycard
missing, and grand slam judgment.

The reading rules are `read_only` (rkcb-1430.bid): a first version
ranked them at -60 only, below "every pass", but in a game force no pass
is offered and we bid them (25 boards in the tripwire, contract errors
136 -> 291). Now never chosen.

**Engine change (2026-10-05):** a pass a rule marks `artificial` is
allowed in a force (engine.rs `choose_from`). Without it DOPI's pass was
impossible in any game-forcing auction (Jacoby 2NT, a splinter): the
engine forbids a pass while the opponents hold the contract below our
game.

## Open questions

- **DEPO** (`slam.depo`, 2026-10-05): double an even number of
  keycards (aces), pass an odd number, over their suit bid. The spec
  says "played instead of DOPI", so with `slam.depo` on it replaces DOPI
  at every level (some pairs play DOPI low and DEPO high; the card has
  no field for that split). ROPI is unchanged. The asker's DOPI rules
  apply as they are: over an even double facing two of mine the count
  stays open (2 or 4) and we sign off, and partner's correction to six
  needs three keycards, so the slam with two and two is missed.
  **Question for Rick:** worth a DEPO-specific correction? Decision
  taken: no, rare.
- Interference at the six level is not answered by DOPI (the rules stop
  at 5♠); a double there is whatever the competitive rules say.
- The asker's continuation over an open "1 or 4" double (asker with no
  keycard) passes; a correction structure there is not written.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only
depo-vs-dopi`. IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the
convention makes fewer; "actor" is the side that made the first
differing call. DEPO against DOPI (`slam.depo` on, `slam.dopi` on in
both runs), DOPI_ROPI: 0 boards changed. Our 4NT came up on 394 boards
and the opponents never bid over it: our defenders do not interfere over
keycard, so the scenario's interference exists only in BBA's auctions.
No self verdict possible; the `.test` cases are the check.

## Convention score (2026-10-07)

Still unmeasurable. The module is gated by `slam.dopi`/`slam.ropi`; the
switch changes nothing because our defenders never bid over our 4NT
(0 of our 394 4NT auctions on DOPI_ROPI). BBA's interference there comes
mostly from an overcall of Jacoby 2NT followed by a raise over 4NT
(1H P 2N 3C ... 4N 5C), and BBA's own switch changes only 17 of 472
boards: the scenario has few chances even for BBA. Writing defenders'
bids over their keycard ask (a sacrifice or lead-directing bid at the
five level) and overcalls of Jacoby 2NT would make the position arise;
not done here. With 17 boards the score would not mean much anyway.

## Sources

- **The convention:** ACBL Unit 390, "DOPI and ROPI"
  (https://www.acblunit390.org/Simon/dopi-ropi.htm): double/redouble the
  first step, pass the second, then the steps; convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/dopi_ropi.toml` (Kantar, *25 More
  Bridge Conventions You Should Know*, ch. 15; Todd, Adventures in Bridge
  #536). Where we differ from Unit 390: its 1430 table lists a "3rd
  cheapest = three keycards", which repeats the pass; we use four steps.
- **DEPO:** convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/depo.toml` (Kantar, *25 More
  Bridge Conventions You Should Know*, ch. 15): double even, pass odd,
  instead of DOPI.
- **BBA:** DOPI_ROPI corpus notes ("A=1/5 or 4/5" for a double over 1430)
  agree with the step order.

files.rules/slam/kickback.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Kickback: with a suit agreed, the keycard ask is the bid one step above
# four of the trump suit instead of 4NT: 4♦ with clubs, 4♥ with
# diamonds, 4♠ with hearts. With spades it is 4NT, which rkcb-1430.bid
# already is. The answers are the four 1430 steps above the ask (0314 by
# `slam.kickback.rkcb_0314`), so the fourth step is five of the trump
# suit and every answer leaves the sign-off in five. Notes:
# kickback.notes.md.

module kickback "Kickback: the step above four of the trump suit asks for keycards"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/kickback
  param  kbplay = bidding_conventions/kickback default false
  param  kb1430 = bidding_conventions/kickback:rkcb_1430 default false
  param  kb0314 = bidding_conventions/kickback:rkcb_0314 default false
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# The card plays Kickback when any of its three fields is on.
define kickback_on = kbplay | kb1430 | kb0314

# The ask is four of the next suit, while the auction is below it
# (`cheapest_rank`: 4♦ 21, 4♥ 22, 4♠ 23). Once
# the auction has passed it, 4NT is the ask again (rkcb-1430.bid).
define kb_room(t) = (t is C, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21) | (t is D, cheapest_rank(H) <= 22) | (t is H, cheapest_rank(S) <= 23)
define kb_asks(t) = kickback_on, kb_room(t)

# Hearts as trumps: 4♠ is the ask, not a control bid (control-bids.bid).
define kb_spade_ask = kb_asks(H), trump is H

# The first step: "1 or 4" (1430), else "0 or 3".
define kb_first_14 = !kb0314

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The values are rkcb-1430.bid's: 33 facing a limited partner's maximum
# with no two bare side suits, or 33 on a game-forcing partner's floor.
# Priority 11: the call must read as the ask whatever else could claim
# it (the engine reads a call by its highest-ranked rule), so it ranks
# above the descriptive calls, but below a control bid (12), which comes
# first when a side suit is uncontrolled.

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4D  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, kb_room(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4H  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, kb_room(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is H, kb_room(H)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control
  4D  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, kb_room(C)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4H  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, kb_room(D)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  trump is H, kb_room(H)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

# After a control-bid exchange in hearts (control-bids.bid), as the 4NT
# ask there: once every side suit is covered.
when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, asked control(t), trump is H
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  kb_room(H), all_covered
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when kickback_on, we.trump is suit, answered control(t), partner.last = 4H, trump is H
  4S  "Kickback: keycard ask in ♥"  alert
      when  kb_room(H), all_covered_by_us
      sets  ask=kickback(trump)
      artificial
      priority 15

# ── The answers: four steps above the ask ─────────────────────────────

when kickback_on, asked kickback(t), rho.last = P
  4H  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, kb_first_14
  4H  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, !kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, !kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C
  5C  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C

  4S  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, kb_first_14
  4S  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, !kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, !kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D
  5D  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D

  4N  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is H, kb_first_14
  4N  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is H, !kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is H, kb_first_14
  5C  "Kickback: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is H, !kb_first_14
  5D  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is H
  5H  "Kickback: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is H

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The queen: mine, or partner's fourth step, which is always five of our
# suit (`partner.has(Q,t)` is never known: the engine does not track
# another hand's honours; 2026-10-07, as rkcb-1430.bid's 5♠).
#
# As after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid): `we.keycards(t)` combines my count with
# the answer, within the deck's five. The fourth step is five of our
# suit: pass it with two keycards missing.

when kickback_on, answered kickback(t)
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  # The king ask, as after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid answers it); the self A/B
  # (2026-10-05) lost the grands that 4NT-5NT found.
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)>=4
  # The count that fits (rkcb-1430.bid, `kc_high`): with 30 HCP between
  # us the low count of an open answer is impossible.
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}, grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | partner.last = 5{t}
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  kc_high(t)
  P     "To play"
        when  partner.last=5{t}, we.keycards(t).max<=3
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  we.keycards(t).max<=3
        sets  ask=kb_correct(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  maybe we.keycards(t)>=4
        sets  ask=kb_correct(t)

when kickback_on, asked kb_correct(t)
  6{t}  "Corrects to six: the higher count"   shows keycards(t) in 3|4|5
  P     "Accepts the sign-off"
files.rules/slam/kickback.notes.md:
# kickback (`kickback.bid`): notes

Kickback (2026-10-05). Gated on `slam.kickback.play`, `.rkcb_1430` or
`.rkcb_0314` (any of the three; the `.bbsa` keys "Kickback 1430" and
"Kickback 0314" set the last two). No stock card plays it.

## What the rules do

- **The ask:** with a suit agreed, the step above four of the trump
  suit: 4♦ for clubs, 4♥ for diamonds, 4♠ for hearts; spades keep 4NT
  (rkcb-1430.bid). The values are rkcb-1430.bid's (33 on partner's
  maximum when he is limited, with no two bare side suits; 33 on his
  floor in a game force). After a heart control-bid exchange, as the 4NT
  ask there. Available while the auction is below the ask; once past
  it, 4NT is keycard again.
- **Priority 11:** the engine reads a call by its highest-ranked rule,
  so the ask must outrank anything else that could claim 4♦/4♥/4♠. It
  stays below a control bid (12): a hand with an uncontrolled suit
  control-bids first, as with 4NT.
- **Answers:** four steps, 1430 (0314 with `rkcb_0314`): first step "1
  or 4", second "0 or 3", third two without the queen, fourth two with
  it. The fourth step is always five of the trump suit.
- **The asker:** as after 4NT: grand with every keycard and the queen,
  six with at most one missing, sign off in five otherwise (a pass when
  the answer is five of our suit), partner correcting to six with the
  higher count of an open answer (`ask=kb_correct`).
- rkcb-1430.bid's trump-agreed asks and control-bids.bid's past-game 4♠
  control bid (hearts trumps) step aside when Kickback applies
  (`kb_asks`, `kb_spade_ask`).
- This is also the cure for the club problem in rkcb-1430.notes.md (an
  answer past 5♣ leaves no sign-off): with Kickback every answer leaves
  five of the minor.

## Gaps and open questions

- No queen ask (the next step over a "1 or 4"/"0 or 3" answer) and no
  king ask; DOPI/ROPI over interference with the Kickback ask is not
  written (the ask is simply lost).
- A fit known but not agreed (rkcb-1430.bid's `kc_open`, `shown_fit`)
  still asks with 4NT, also in a minor. **Question for Rick:** should
  Kickback extend there? Decision taken: no, to keep 4NT unambiguous
  where nothing set the trump suit.
- Kickback for hearts as well as the minors follows the convention-card
  summary and Todd. Some partnerships play it in the minors only
  ("Redwood"). **Question for Rick:** minors only? Decision taken: all
  three, as the card's source.

## Corpus

No PBS scenario plays Kickback, and BBA's 21GF cards have it off. Checked
with `--set slam.kickback.play=true` on Minor_Game_Or_Slam and
Slam_After_Major_Fit (`--limit 50`): the ask came up 3 times in the
minors and 8 times in hearts, answered and placed as written; no final
contract changed (same par scores as without Kickback).

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only kickback`.
IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer;
"actor" is the side that made the first differing call.
Minor_Game_Or_Slam and Slam_After_Major_Fit: 154 boards changed; first
-11 to the actor (contract), the grands that 4NT-5NT found and Kickback
could not: its asker had no king ask. With the 5NT king ask added
(rkcb-1430.bid answers it): actor contract +8, double-dummy +26, halves
-8/+16 (z +0.2): neutral. What is left is the price of the step ask
itself: with diamonds agreed 4♥ is the ask, so a heart fit found later
cannot be bid there (Slam_After_Major_Fit 445).

## Five keycards and the count that fits (2026-10-07)

As in rkcb-1430.bid (rkcb-1430.notes.md, same date): five keycards
answer with the third/fourth step, as two (the steps wrap 0/3, 1/4,
2/5; before, a five-keycard answerer had no answer and passed the
ask), and the asker settles an open count by the high cards
(`kc_high`): with 30 HCP between us the low count is impossible, so six
(or the king ask with all five and the queen) instead of the sign-off.
With the king ask on the card the asker asks before the 35-HCP grand.
The correction to six now shows `keycards in 3|4|5`, which the engine
can combine with the first answer. `.test` cases: the five-keycard
answers.

## Sources

- **The convention:** Robert S. Todd, "Kickback Keycard Ask",
  Adventures in Bridge #582
  (https://www.advinbridge.com/this-week-in-bridge/582): 4♦ asks in
  clubs, 4♥ in diamonds, 4♠ in hearts; 1430 step answers. Convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/kickback.toml`.
- **Where we differ:** no queen or king ask yet.

files.rules/slam/minorwood.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Minorwood: with a minor agreed, four of that minor asks for keycards
# instead of 4NT, so every answer stays below five of the minor: over
# 4♣ the steps are 4♦ 4♥ 4♠ 4NT, over 4♦ they are 4♥ 4♠ 4NT 5♣ (1430,
# or 0314 as the card's keycard treatment says). Kickback, when the card
# plays it, is the ask instead (kickback.bid). Notes: minorwood.notes.md.

module minorwood "Minorwood: four of the agreed minor asks for keycards"
  kind   convention
  needs  base
  skill  bidding_conventions/minorwood
  param  mwplay = bidding_conventions/minorwood default false
  param  kstyle = slam.king_ask.style default five_nt   # five_nt | next_step | none (convention-card 0.28); a card that is silent plays 5NT (2026-10-29)

# Four of the minor is still available (`cheapest_rank`: 4♣ 20, 4♦ 21).
define mw_room(t) = (t is C, cheapest_rank(C) <= 20) | (t is D, cheapest_rank(D) <= 21)
define mw_asks(t) = mwplay, !kickback_on, mw_room(t)

# ── The ask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A game force with the minor agreed, or (uncontested) a forcing or
# limited auction where four of the minor cannot be weak: "if there is
# any question, 4m is Minorwood" (the source). The values are the 4NT
# ask's (rkcb-1430.bid). Priority 11, as Kickback's: the call must read
# as the ask whatever else could claim it.

when mwplay, !kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, we.forcing = game, !answered control
  4C  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, mw_room(C)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4D  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, mw_room(D)
      when  slam_values
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

when mwplay, !kickback_on, we.trump is suit, !minor_given_way, !asked, !they.bid, we.forcing = none | we.forcing = round
  4C  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♣"  alert
      when  trump is C, mw_room(C)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11
  4D  "Minorwood: keycard ask in ♦"  alert
      when  trump is D, mw_room(D)
      when  slam_values_limited, !two_bare_suits
      sets  ask=minorwood(trump)
      artificial
      priority 11

# ── The answers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The first two steps as the card's keycard ask has them in a minor
# (`kc_first_14`, dopi-ropi.bid: 1430 unless the card says 0314 or its minor treatment applies).

when mwplay, asked minorwood(t), rho.last = P
  4D  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, kc_first_14(t)
  4D  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, !kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is C, kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is C, !kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C
  4N  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is C

  4H  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, kc_first_14(t)
  4H  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, !kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 0 or 3 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 0|3   artificial   when t is D, kc_first_14(t)
  4S  "Minorwood: 1 or 4 keycards"             shows keycards(t) in 1|4   artificial   when t is D, !kc_first_14(t)
  4N  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards, no {t} queen"    shows keycards(t) in 2|5, !has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D
  5C  "Minorwood: 2 or 5 keycards and the {t} queen"  shows keycards(t) in 2|5, has(Q,t)   artificial   when t is D

# ── The asker places the contract ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The queen: mine, or partner's fourth step (4NT in clubs, 5♣ in
# diamonds); `partner.has(Q,t)` is never known (2026-10-07).

when mwplay, answered minorwood(t)
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C), grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  # The king ask, as after 4NT (rkcb-1430.bid answers it; 2026-10-05).
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, we.keycards(t)=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C)
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  we.keycards(t)>=4
  # The count that fits (rkcb-1430.bid, `kc_high`): with 30 HCP between
  # us the low count of an open answer is impossible.
  7{t}  "Grand slam"
        when  kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C), grand_try, kstyle is not five_nt   # with the king ask, ask first (2026-10-07)
  5N    "King ask: all keycards and the {t} queen held"
        when  kstyle is five_nt, kc_high(t), we.keycards(t).max=5, has(Q,t) | (t is C, partner.last = 4N) | (t is D, partner.last = 5C)
        sets  ask=kings(t)
        artificial
  6{t}  "Small slam"
        when  kc_high(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  we.keycards(t).max<=3
        sets  ask=mw_correct(t)
  5{t}  "Signoff"
        when  maybe we.keycards(t)>=4
        sets  ask=mw_correct(t)

when mwplay, asked mw_correct(t)
  6{t}  "Corrects to six: the higher count"   shows keycards(t) in 3|4|5
  P     "Accepts the sign-off"
files.rules/slam/minorwood.notes.md:
# minorwood (`minorwood.bid`): notes

Minorwood (2026-10-05). Gated on `slam.minorwood.play`; off when the card
also plays Kickback (kickback.bid is then the ask). No stock card plays
it and the `.bbsa` format has no key for it.

## What the rules do

- **The ask:** with a minor agreed, four of it while the auction is
  below that: in a game force with rkcb-1430.bid's values (33 on
  partner's floor), or uncontested in a forcing or limited auction (33
  on partner's maximum, no two bare suits). The source: "if there is any
  question about what is going on, 4m is forcing and we should usually
  treat it as Minorwood". Priority 11, as Kickback, so 4m reads as the
  ask whatever else could claim it.
- **Answers:** four steps above the ask, 1430 or 0314 as the card's
  keycard ask has them in a minor (`kc_first_14`, dopi-ropi.bid: the
  `slam.rkcb.minor_0314` treatment, or `general.style=bba` with
  0314). Over 4♣: 4♦ 4♥ 4♠ 4NT; over 4♦: 4♥ 4♠ 4NT 5♣.
- **The asker:** grand, six, or five of the minor (partner corrects to
  six with the higher count of an open answer, `ask=mw_correct`).
- rkcb-1430.bid's trump-agreed 4NT asks step aside while Minorwood
  applies (`mw_asks`).

## Gaps and open questions

- With Minorwood on, any uncontested 4m in a minor-agreed auction reads
  as the ask, so the natural 4m calls other modules make (a raise to
  four, "game try in the minor") become unavailable in meaning. That is
  the convention's price; the source accepts it.
- Not in competition below a game force (the source: "not in
  non-forcing competitive auctions").
- No queen ask, and no 5m+1 king ask (the source's follow-ups).

## Corpus

Minor_Game_Or_Slam `--limit 50 --set slam.minorwood.play=true`: 7 asks,
7 boards changed, +26 IMPs against BBA by par (-243 against -269
without). Mostly 1m-2m(inverted)-4m, which our base bid as a natural
non-forcing raise and partner passed; as Minorwood it reached slams that
make.

## Self A/B (2026-10-05)

BBA does not play it, so it is judged against ourselves (CLAUDE.md,
"Pace"): the same deals with the card field off and on, every board,
`probes/tools/self_ab.py --batch probes/self-ab.toml --only minorwood`.
IMPs by the errors yardstick, positive when the convention makes fewer;
"actor" is the side that made the first differing call.
Minor_Game_Or_Slam: 96 boards changed; actor contract +492 (with the 5NT
king ask added, +478 before), double-dummy +641, halves +236/+256 (z
+8.5): gains. Mostly the 1m-2m-4m auctions our base passed out in four
(Corpus, above).

## Five keycards and the count that fits (2026-10-07)

As in rkcb-1430.bid (rkcb-1430.notes.md, same date): five keycards
answer with the third/fourth step, as two (the steps wrap 0/3, 1/4,
2/5; before, a five-keycard answerer had no answer and passed the
ask), and the asker settles an open count by the high cards
(`kc_high`): with 30 HCP between us the low count is impossible, so six
(or the king ask with all five and the queen) instead of the sign-off.
With the king ask on the card the asker asks before the 35-HCP grand.
The correction to six now shows `keycards in 3|4|5`, which the engine
can combine with the first answer. `.test` cases: the five-keycard
answers.

## Sources

- **The convention:** Robert S. Todd, "Slam Bidding: Minorwood",
  Adventures in Bridge #405
  (https://www.advinbridge.com/this-week-in-bridge/405): when 4m is
  Minorwood (game forcing with a minor fit and no major fit; jumps that
  are clearly not weak), the 1430 step answers over 4♣ and 4♦, the queen
  and king asks. Convention-card
  `spec/conventions/bidding_conventions/minorwood.toml`.
- **Where we differ:** no queen or king ask.

files.rules/slam/over-3nt.bid:
# Syntax: docs/LANGUAGE.md. Check with `rbb bid check`.
#
# Slam after partner's 3NT (2026-09-27). The slam work's third group:
# 1,433 boards where BBA bid slam and our auction stopped in a 3NT that
# one partner bid with 15-18 balanced while the other, often with 15-17
# and a long suit, passed. Nothing looked past 3NT.
#
# Partner's 3NT has shown a range, and I add my HCP to his minimum: 6NT
# with 34 or more; a quantitative 4NT with 32-33 (answered by `when asked
# quant`, one-nt.bid); with a six-card minor and 31+, four of it as a
# slam try. Counting partner at his minimum, one point above the
# textbook 33/31 measured best (notes).

module over-3nt "Slam after partner's 3NT"
  kind   judgement
  needs  base
  skill  partnership_bidding/slam_bidding
  param  q4n   = bidding_conventions/quantitative_4nt default true
  param  tu    = bidding_conventions/texas:two_under default false
  param  o23   = bidding_conventions/jacoby_transfers:over_2c_3nt default true
  param  system = general.system   # `brill`: Gerber here instead (gerber.bid)

# After 2♣–2♦–3NT (24+ shown, opener's second bid) Texas uses 4♦/4♥, or
# 4♣/4♦ for 2-under (texas-transfers.bid): the tries and natural bids
# below give way there, or partner would read them as transfers. Only
# when the card plays transfers there (`notrump.jacoby_transfers.over_2c_3nt`,
# default on, Rick 2026-11-07); off, 4♦ and 4♥ are natural.
define big_3n = partner.hcp.min>=24, partner.bids>=2
define texas_3n = big_3n, o23

when partner.last=3N, !they.bid, we.trump is none
  # Without Texas over 2♣–2♦–3NT, a six-card major goes to game
  # naturally: the same hands that Texas carries there (texas-transfers.bid).
  4H  "To play: six or more hearts"
      shows H>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when  big_3n, !(texas_2nt, o23)
      priority -10
  4S  "To play: six or more spades"
      shows S>=6, points>=25-partner.points.min, suit_points<=32-partner.points.min
      when  big_3n, !(texas_2nt, o23)
      priority -10
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
      priority -10
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 32, hcp + partner.hcp.max <= 35
      sets  ask=quant
      priority -10
  4C  "Slam try: six or more clubs"
      shows C>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      when  !(texas_3n, tu)
      sets  ask=slam_try(C)
      priority -10
  4D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      when  !(texas_3n, texas_2nt | tu)
      sets  ask=slam_try(D)
      priority -10

  # A standalone major, six to the AKQJ or seven to the AKQ, plays in
  # game without help from partner, and a short suit with no stopper is
  # a risk in notrump (Rick, 2026-09-27, ticket b194: 1S 2D 2S 3NT with
  # AKQJ63 and 32 in hearts; BBA bids 4S).
  4S  "To play: a self-sufficient ♠ suit"
      shows (S>=6, quality(S)=3, top5(S)>=4) | (S>=7, quality(S)=3)
      shows (H<=2, !stop(H)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      priority -10
  4H  "To play: a self-sufficient ♥ suit"
      shows (H>=6, quality(H)=3, top5(H)>=4) | (H>=7, quality(H)=3)
      shows (S<=2, !stop(S)) | (D<=2, !stop(D)) | (C<=2, !stop(C))
      when  !(texas_3n, texas_2nt, !tu)
      priority -10

# The same after their overcall of our 2♣ (2♣ (2♥) P (P) 3NT, 2♣ P 2♦
# (2♥) 3NT), where the block above stops at `!they.bid`. 4♣ is not a
# jump over 3NT, so it is the club slam try, not Gerber (Rick,
# 2026-10-31: Gerber needs a jump; without one 4♣ is a slam try).
# Texas is off after interference, so the tries do not give way to it.
after 2C (*) P (P) 3N (P) | 2C (P) 2D (*) 3N (P) when they.bid, system is not brill
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
      priority -10
  4C  "Slam try: six or more clubs"
      shows C>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      sets  ask=slam_try(C)
      priority -10
  4D  "Slam try: six or more diamonds"
      shows D>=6, hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31
      sets  ask=slam_try(D)
      priority -10

when asked slam_try(m), partner.last=4{m}, we.trump is none
  6{m}  "Small slam: a fit"                       shows m>=3
  4N    "No fit"                            shows m<=2
when answered slam_try(m), partner.last=4N
  6N  "Small slam"    shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 34
  P   "To play"
      priority -5

# The same count for responder when opener's rebid is a new suit
# (2026-09-27): responder bid 3NT with 33+ between the hands
# (1a–1b–2c–3NT, 772 boards short of slam). Counted in points: after a
# jump shift the HCP floor is only 10 (it shows suit points), the
# points floor 18. The textbook 33/31 is kept although lower thresholds
# score better on the slam-rich corpus (notes).
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
after 1x (P) 1y (P) 1z (P)
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
after 1x (P) 2y (P) 2z (P) when z is not x, z is not y
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 33, !shortest<=1
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows points + partner.points.min >= 31, points + partner.points.max <= 36, !shortest<=1
      when  no_ask                         # with Blackwood or RKCB, keycard in the last suit (Rick, 2026-10-03)
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1

# Opener over responder's 15-17 jump to 3NT after a game-forcing 2/1
# and opener's two-level rebid (responder-rebids.bid; Rick, 2026-11-06,
# #91). The count above (34 / 32 on partner's minimum) lost slams
# opener had bid over the old 16+ 2NT; Rick, 2026-11-07: opener should
# be more aggressive here. The textbook 33/31 on responder's minimum, in
# HCP: 18+ bids 6NT, 16-17 a quantitative 4NT. Counting points or
# partner at mid-range lost (notes).
after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 3N (P) when x is not y, we.gf
  6N  "Small slam"
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 33
      priority 1
  4N  "Quantitative: invites 6NT"
      when  q4n                            # the card plays a quantitative 4NT
      shows hcp + partner.hcp.min >= 31, hcp + partner.hcp.min <= 32
      sets  ask=quant
      priority 1
# Responder answers it in HCP too: 16-17 accepts, 15 declines (31-32
# between the hands). one-nt.bid's answer counts points on opener's
# floor, and his five-card suit made it accept with every 15.
after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 3N (P) 4N (P) when x is not y, we.gf
  6N  "Accepts the slam invitation: 16-17"   shows hcp>=16
      priority 1
  P   "Declines: 15"                          shows hcp<=15
      priority 1
files.rules/slam/over-3nt.notes.md:
# over-3nt (`over-3nt.bid`): notes

## Why (2026-09-27)

Slam work, third group. Over the corpus BBA bid slam on 14,834 boards
where we did not (78% make double dummy). After the minor slam tries
over 1NT and 2NT, the largest remaining shapes were suit openings that
reached 3NT: 1a-2b-3NT (876 boards), 1a-1b-2c-3NT (557) and others,
where one partner bid 3NT with 15-18 balanced and the other passed with
15-17 and often a long suit. Nothing looked past partner's 3NT.

## Calibration (all double-dummy tables in the corpus)

P(a small slam makes), by HCP between the hands and longest fit:

| HCP | fit 7 (suit / 6NT) | fit 8 | fit 9 | fit 10+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 29 | 32% / 19% | 55% / 28% | 72% / 37% | 83% / 39% |
| 30 | 53% / 39% | 71% / 47% | 83% / 56% | 89% / 59% |
| 31 | 65% / 59% | 80% / 66% | 90% / 76% | 95% / 80% |
| 32 | 79% / 75% | 89% / 83% | 94% / 89% | 99% / 95% |
| 33 | 91% / 92% | 94% / 92% | 98% / 98% | 99% / 97% |

Double dummy flatters slams; treat these as upper bounds.

## Rules and thresholds

When partner has just bid 3NT, no suit is agreed and they are silent:
6NT, a quantitative 4NT (answered by `when asked quant`), or 4♣/4♦
with six as a slam try (partner bids six with three-card support, else
4NT; then 6NT with the values). My HCP plus partner's shown minimum:

| 6NT / 4NT / minor try | full corpus (par / side) | ours-only slams make |
|---|---|---|
| 33 / 31-32 / 30 | +2,298 / +5,352 | 59% |
| **34 / 32-33 / 31 (kept)** | **+2,516 / +5,193** | 64% |
| 35 / 33-34 / 32 | +2,137 / +4,432 | |

Counting partner at his minimum, one point above the textbook numbers
is best.

## Responder after opener's new suit (2026-09-27)

The biggest group short of slam was responder's 3NT after opener's
second suit: 1a–1b–2c–3NT (772 boards), 1a–1b–1c–3NT (489),
1a–2b–2c–3NT (556). BBA reaches slam on well over half of them. The
same 6NT / quantitative 4NT now apply at responder's second call
after 1x–1y–2z, 1x–1y–1z and 1x–2y–2z (new suits).

It counts **points**, not HCP: a jump shift shows 19+ suit points, which
leaves opener's HCP floor at 10, so an HCP count never saw it. The
first try (34/32 HCP, the numbers used over 3NT) changed 10 boards.

| 6NT / 4NT, in points | full corpus (par / side) | boards |
|---|---|---|
| 34 / 32 | +189 / +515 | 48 |
| **33 / 31 (kept)** | **+504 / +1,133** | 108 |
| 32 / 30 | +993 / +1,892 | 196 |
| 31 / 29 | +1,624 / +2,886 | 342 |

The lower thresholds keep winning, and I do not trust it: the scenarios
are dealt for slam (Soloway, Minor_Game_Or_Slam, Fourth_Suit_Forcing).
On the boards where 6NT fires, at 33 it almost always holds 32+ real
HCP between the hands, and makes double dummy every time; at 31 it
fires on 29-31 HCP, where 6NT makes 17-69%. The textbook 33 stays.
**For Rick:** the rest of the gap is that opener's strength after a
simple new-suit rebid is 12-18, too wide to count on. BBA gets there by
exploring (3m, fourth suit, then 4NT); we have no slam try below 3NT
yet in these auctions.

A first attempt put the rule in one context for every uncontested
position below game. It overrode the notrump auctions' own slam
counting (Stayman, transfers, 1NT–4NT): −11,422 par, −14,314 side. The
contexts are now named auctions.

## A standalone major over partner's 3NT (2026-09-27)

Ticket basic-weak-2-b194 (Rick): 1S 2D 2S 3NT with AKQJ63.32.6.T542
should go back to 4S: the suit needs no help to keep trump control, and
the weak heart doubleton is a risk in notrump. Standalone: six to the
AKQJ or seven to the AKQ; plus a doubleton or shorter without a
stopper. +615 par, +969 side IMPs (420 boards). Without the unguarded
condition: +601 / +942 on 603 boards, so it stays.

## With Blackwood or RKCB, 4NT is keycard here (Rick, 2026-10-03)

> A 4NT with no prior NT bids is normally keycard regardless, and if
> there hasn't been suit agreement, it's for the last bid suit.

The quantitative 4NT after 1x-1y-1z, 1x-1y-2z and 1x-2y-2z (no notrump
bid) now needs `no_ask`: on cards with an ace or keycard ask, 4NT there
is the ask in z (rkcb-1430.notes.md, "The keycard suit"); on cards with
neither (bare SAYC) it stays quantitative. The 6NT beside it is
unchanged. Measured with the rest of that change.

## The card's quantitative 4NT (2026-10-05)

The quantitative 4NT rules here read `slam.quantitative_4nt.play`
(default on; every PBS card has it on): with it off, 4NT is not bid
quantitatively and the hand passes or bids on as the other rules say.
Only the slam/ modules are gated so far; the quantitative 4NTs in
notrump/ (one-nt, stayman, jacoby-transfers, two-nt-responses) and
base/ (rebids, responder-rebids, strong-openings) still ignore the
field (they belong to other work in flight).

## After their overcall of our 2♣ (Rick, 2026-10-31)

2♣ (2♥) P (P) 3NT and 2♣ P 2♦ (2♥) 3NT: the 6NT count and the 4♣/4♦
slam tries as without interference (the main block stops at
`!they.bid`). 4♣ is not a jump over 3NT, so it is the slam try, not
Gerber: Rick, "generally Gerber requires a jump". Not on the Brill card,
where gerber.bid plays Gerber here for Brill partners.

## After 5-4 shown over 1NT (Rick, 2026-11-06)

Bridge-Classroom #85 (1NT–2♥–2♠–3♣–3NT, 16 HCP opposite 17, 6NT
makes): the count here is HCP and missed it. The fix lives in
jacoby-transfers.bid (its notes, "Slam after 5-4 shown"): there
responder counts total points, and that 4NT takes over this one in
that auction. The balanced-hand thresholds here are unchanged.

## Opener over responder's 15-17 3NT after a 2/1 (Rick, 2026-11-07)

Since 2026-11-06 (#91, responder-rebids.notes.md) responder's jump to
3NT after a game-forcing 2/1 and opener's two-level rebid is 15-17
HCP; the 16+ hands used to bid 2NT, where opener counted slam in
points on the 16 floor (rebids.bid). Moved to this module's general
count (34 / 32-33 HCP on partner's minimum), opener lost slams: -50
IMPs on 21 boards (actor contract errors, last round's split). Rick,
asked whether opener should be more aggressive opposite a 15-17 3NT:
"yes".

Now `after 1y (P) 2x (P) 2z (P) 3N (P)` (game force) counts the
**textbook 33 / 31-32 in HCP on responder's minimum**: 18+ bids 6NT,
16-17 a quantitative 4NT. Responder answers the 4NT in HCP: 16-17
accepts, 15 declines. The general count elsewhere is unchanged.

**Measured** (compare `--par-all`, 35 scenarios, 17,500 boards: 2/1,
forcing 1NT, major raises, misfits, slam; errors_diff.py on the item's
own run, the bidding side's contract errors; the auction is rare, so
few boards change):

| opener's count | boards | actor contract errors (halves) | par |
|---|---|---|---|
| points, 33 / 31-32 on the minimum | 181 | -378 (-103 / -275) | -280 |
| points, partner at mid-range (32 / 30-31) | 281 | -666 (-221 / -445) | -542 |
| HCP, partner at mid-range (32 / 30-31) | 14 | +24 (+29 / -5, differ) | +27 |
| HCP, 33 / 31-32, `!shortest<=1` | 5 | +24 (+13 / +11) | |
| HCP, 33 / 31-32, one-nt.bid's answer | 8 | +31 (+26 / +5) | +32 |
| **HCP, 33 / 31-32, answered in HCP (kept)** | 8 | **+18 (+13 / +5)** | +19 |

Points were a disaster: after a 2/1 misfit opener's long suits count
length points his partner cannot use in notrump (6-5 and 6-4 hands
bid 6NT on 30 HCP). one-nt.bid's answer counts points on opener's
floor, and opener here always has a five-card suit, so it accepted
with every 15: the 4NT was a 6NT bid by 16-count. It scored one board
better (Misfit_13-Plus 402, 16 opposite 15 made 6NT) but is the 31-HCP
slam this module's calibration rejects, so the HCP answer is kept.

## Without transfers over 2♣–2♦–3NT (Rick, 2026-11-07)

`notrump.jacoby_transfers.over_2c_3nt` (default on: "default to on") says
whether Texas runs over 2♣–2♦–3NT. Off, 4♦ and 4♥ there are natural:
`texas_3n` reads the field, so the minor tries and the self-sufficient
4♥ come back, and a six-card major with game values below the slam band
bids four of it to play (the hands texas-transfers.bid carries there).
The same natural game bids serve a card with Texas off. Cases in
`notrump/texas-transfers.test`.

## Sources

- **The thresholds:** the textbook combined counts for 6NT and a
  quantitative 4NT (33 HCP for slam) are standard practice, not yet cited
  to a book or article. The numbers in the rules are calibrated on the
  corpus's double-dummy tables ("Calibration"), one point above the
  textbook where partner is counted at his minimum.
- **Rick's rulings:** ticket basic-weak-2-b194 (2026-09-27): a
  standalone major goes back to four of it over partner's 3NT.
- **BBA evidence:** the 14,834 corpus boards where BBA bid slam and we
  did not, and BBA's exploring sequences after a new-suit rebid ("For
  Rick"). No `probes/*.toml` spec yet.
- **Corpus measurements:** the threshold tables (2026-09-27) and the
  rejected single-context version (-11,422 par).
- **Where we differ:** responder's thresholds stay at the textbook 33,
  although lower ones score better on the slam-dealt scenarios.
- **Rick's ruling, 2026-10-03:** 4NT with no notrump bid is keycard
  for the last suit on cards that play an ask.
- Rick, 2026-10-31: Gerber needs a jump; 4♣ over 3NT is a slam try.
- Rick, 2026-11-06 (bridge-classroom-bug-artifacts #85): invite slam
  after 5-4 shown; built in jacoby-transfers.bid.
- **Rick, 2026-11-07** (#91 follow-up): opener should be more
  aggressive about slam opposite responder's 15-17 3NT after a 2/1.
  The textbook 33/31 HCP count there is standard practice, not yet
  cited.
- Rick, 2026-11-07: the `over_2c_3nt` field on the Jacoby Transfer card, default on; off, 4♦/4♥ natural (the field's description).
